headline: Carter (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
story: Carter was designated for return from injured reserve 16 days ago, so Arizona will need to make a decision on him next week. Carter has yet to play in a game this season after being injured back in August.

headline: Carter (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Carter opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a knee injury he picked up in training camp in early August. He logged a trio of full practices during Week 11 prep but is not quite ready to return, so his next chance to make his 2026 debut is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Carter (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Rams, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Carter will remain on IR for Week 10 and will not suit up for Sunday's divisional contest against the Rams. The defensive tackle logged three consecutive limited practices after being designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday.

headline: The Cardinals designated Carter (knee) to return from injured reserve Wednesday.
story: Carter opened the season on injured reserve due to a knee injury that he sustained during training camp. He was a limited practice participant in Wednesday's session, but he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's NFC West tilt against the Rams.

headline: Gaines (ankle) is out for Sunday's game versus Washington, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Gaines will miss his sixth straight game in Week 12 due to an ankle injury. With Gaines being on the sidelines again, 2025 sixth-rounder Hayden Conner will project as the Cardinals' top option off the bench on the interior of the offensive line Sunday.

headline: Gaines (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Gaines will miss a fourth consecutive game while recovering from an ankle injury, and his next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29. Hjalte Froholdt has cleared the league's concussion protocol and is slated to start at center against Kansas City.

headline: Gaines (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Rams, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
story: Gaines was set to start at center due to the absence of Hjalte Froholdt (concussion). With Gaines also unable to suit up due to an ankle injury, Hayden Conner will make his first career start at center against Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett.

headline: Gaines (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 9 matchup versus the Seahawks, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
story: Gaines continues to battle a knee injury and will miss his third straight game. Hayden Conner may make another start at right guard, though Isaiah Adams (ankle) -- who has been deemed questionable -- could take on that role if he's activated from IR on Saturday.

headline: Gaines (ankle) did not participate at the Cardinals' practice Thursday, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports.
story: Gaines has missed back-to-back practices to open the week as he continues to nurse an ankle injury that he suffered in mid-October. The offensive lineman appears to be on track to miss a third game in a row Sunday versus the Seahawks.

headline: Gaines (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
story: Gaines will miss a second consecutive game due to an ankle injury, and his next chance to play is Week 9 against the Seahawks on Sunday, Nov. 8. Hayden Conner should start at right guard in Gaines' absence.

headline: Gaines (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Broncos, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Gaines remains sidelined with a bad ankle. Hayden Conner is set to start at right guard against the Broncos in the 27-year-old's place.

headline: Long (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
story: The tight end returned from injured reserve two weeks ago and has two grabs for 18 yards on three targets in two games since suffering a knee injury. Long is now dealing with an ankle issue. Teagan Quitoriano would see an uptick in snaps behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins if Long is unable to play.

headline: Long hauled in his lone target for an 11-yard reception in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Long ranked third among Cardinals tight ends in playing time, logging 23 of 56 offensive snaps while Trey McBride (45 snaps) and Elijah Higgins (32) paced the position group. In his first two contests back in action since being reinstated from injured reserve Nov. 14 following a five-game absence, Long has notched two receptions for 18 yards on three targets.

headline: Long (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Rams, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Long was activated from injured reserve Saturday, and the sixth-year pro has been cleared to return from a five-game absence due to a knee injury. He will operate in a rotational role at tight end behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins.

headline: Arizona activated Long (knee) from injured reserve Saturday, and he remains questionable for Sunday's battle against the Rams.
story: Long had been on IR since Oct. 6 after suffering a knee injury during Week 4 against the Giants. He was limited in all three of the Cardinals' practice sessions this week but could suit up Sunday. If Long plays, he'll work as a depth tight end behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins, though Long could still have some pass-catching opportunities given how depleted the team's wideout corps is.

headline: The Cardinals designated Long (knee) for return from injured reserve Wednesday.
story: The tight end was injured in Week 4 against the Giants but had his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday. Elijah Higgins and Teagan Quitoriano have been soaking up the snaps at the position behind Trey McBride in recent weeks.

headline: The Cardinals placed Long (knee) on injured reserve Tuesday.
story: Long left Sunday's game against the Giants due to a knee injury, which is severe enough for the sixth-year pro to go on injured reserve. As such, Long will be required to miss at least the next four games, so Week 9 against the Seahawks on Sunday, Nov. 8 is the earliest he is eligible to return. In order to add more depth at tight end behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins, the Cardinals signed 2022 fifth-rounder Teagan Quitoriano from the practice squad to the active roster.

headline: Long (knee) is questionable to return against the Giants on Sunday.
story: In Long's absence, Elijah Higgins is the lone depth option at tight end behind Trey McBride. Long is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game.

headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that he has no update on Love (ankle), who is eligible to come off injured reserve following Sunday's game against the Commanders, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
story: Love will miss a fourth consecutive game Sunday but will then be eligible to come off injured reserve ahead of Week 13 against the Eagles. LaFleur previously said Love will be reevaluated Monday once eligible to return, and the coach added Friday that he expects to know more Wednesday once the Cardinals return to practice. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight are still the leading in-house backfield options in the meantime.

headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that the Cardinals will evaluate Love (ankle) again Monday to hone in on a return date for the running back, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
story: Love must miss at least one more game due to the right high-ankle sprain that he picked up in a Week 8 win at Dallas, but the Cardinals have a decision to make next week, as they have a Week 13 matchup with the Eagles on tap before a Week 14 bye. For as long as Love is sidelined, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will continue to man Arizona's backfield.

headline: Coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that the Cardinals are still evaluating the status of Love (ankle), with the running back's earliest possible return from IR on the horizon, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
story: "I'll know a little bit more as this week goes," LaFleur noted of Love, who will miss at least one more game before potentially being activated ahead of, and available for, Week 13 action. Love sustained a right high-ankle sprain Nov. 1, and at the time he was thought to be facing a projected recovery timeline of 4-to-5 weeks. However, for this coming weekend's game against the Commanders at least, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will continue to handle Arizona's backfield duties.

headline: Arizona placed Love (ankle) on injured reserve Tuesday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Love's move to IR was fully expected, after Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported earlier Tuesday that the rookie first-round pick was diagnosed with a right high-ankle sprain and was facing a projected recovery timeline of 4-to-5 weeks. While Love is on the mend, Tyler Allgeier is expected to step into a lead role out of the Arizona backfield beginning with the team's Week 9 game against Seattle.

headline: Love was diagnosed Tuesday with a right high-ankle sprain, which is expected to send him to injured reserve and keep him out for 4-to-5 weeks, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Love was available to play Week 8 after missing the Cardinals' previous two games due to a left ankle issue, but he ended up exiting Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys late in the first quarter after tweaking his opposite ankle. Though the No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft was cleared to play in advance of Week 1 after previously sustaining a right high-ankle sprain in the preseason, he won't be as fortunate this time around now that he's sprained the same ankle for the second time in less than three months. The projected 4-to-5-week recovery timeline gives Love a chance at returning to action when first eligible to return from IR on Dec. 6 against the Eagles, but at least for the next four games, Tyler Allgeier looks poised to serve as Arizona's lead back. The Cardinals could also look to bring James Conner (foot) back from IR at some point during that four-game stretch.

headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that Love suffered a "new" ankle injury during Sunday's overtime win at Dallas, and that he'll have an update on the running back later this week, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Prior to having his right ankle rolled up on while getting tackled Sunday, Love was dealing with a left ankle issue, so this is a bit of a non-update from LaFleur. Having said that, LaFleur's last comment indicates that he may touch on the nature of Love's injury and also its prognosis in the near future. Fellow RB Bam Knight has entered the concussion protocol in the wake of Week 8 action, leaving Tyler Allgeier as the unquestioned healthy lead back for the Cardinals at the moment.

headline: Love (ankle) was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cowboys to begin the second half, Alex Weiner of ArizonaSports.com reports.
story: Love had sat out the Cardinals' prior two contests due to a left ankle injury, but he appeared to tweak the opposite ankle on a carry late in the first quarter of Sunday's game. After a brief visit to the medical tent on the Arizona sideline, Love retreated to the locker room, where he remained to begin the third quarter before the Cardinals ruled him out. Prior to his departure, Love carried nine times for 23 yards and didn't draw any targets. His status will warrant monitoring leading up to the Cardinals' Week 9 game against the Seahawks on Nov. 8.

headline: Love (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game at Dallas, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: Love missed the previous two contests due to a left ankle injury, but after having his right ankle rolled up on in the second quarter Sunday, he visited the medical tent and then the locker room before the Cardinals clarified the nature of his injury. For as long as Love is off the field, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will man Arizona's backfield.

headline: Love headed into the locker room during the second quarter of Sunday's game against the Cowboys to be further evaluated for an apparent lower-body injury, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Love had been sidelined for the Cardinals' previous two games due to a left ankle injury, but he appeared to check out of Sunday's contest after taking a hit to his right ankle/leg in the final minute of the first quarter. The Cardinals will examine him more thoroughly in the locker room before providing an update on the nature of his injury as well as his status for the remainder of the contest. Love carried nine times for 23 yards prior to departing.

headline: Love (undisclosed) went to the sideline during Sunday's contest in Dallas, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Love appeared to get his right ankle rolled up on in the second quarter and remained on the turf for a spell before jogging to the sideline and going into the medical tent. He's been dealing with a left ankle injury that sidelined him the last two games, so this appears to be a new health concern.

headline: Love (ankle) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Dallas, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Head coach Mike LaFleur told Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site Friday that Love was expected to play in Week 8, and the running back's lack of designation confirms as much. After opening the week with back-to-back limited listings, Love capped it with a full session Friday, indicating that he's ready for close to a normal workload Sunday after a two-game absence. Speaking of the time off, Love relayed to Urban that "two weeks for anybody will get people feeling how they want to feel." As a result, Love will rejoin a backfield that previously was a near-even split between Tyler Allgeier (toe) and Bam Knight the last two weeks.

headline: Coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that Love (ankle) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Cowboys, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: In his return to drills this week following a two-game absence, Love has managed a pair of limited practices as he seeks to put an ankle injury behind him. It's unclear if Love will enter the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Dallas, something that'll be revealed on Friday's practice report. As for the rest of Arizona's backfield, Tyler Allgeier is tending to a toe issue, leaving just Bam Knight as a healthy option at the position.

headline: Love (ankle) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: Love maintained his activity level from Wednesday, which followed two weeks off due to a lingering ankle injury. Head coach Mike LaFleur hasn't indicated if Love actually has a chance to return to action Sunday at Dallas, but Friday's practice report will reveal his chances to do so.

headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Love (ankle) will practice in a limited fashion Wednesday, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
story: This doesn't come as a surprise, as LaFleur told Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic on Monday that Love was slated to practice Wednesday. Now that Love's activity level is known, he'll have two more chances to get back to full this week before the Cardinals potentially make a ruling on his status ahead of Sunday's game at Dallas. Love has missed the last two games due to a lingering ankle injury, which has allowed Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to split the backfield reps during that span.

headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that Love (ankle) will take part in Wednesday's practice, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: Love has missed the last two games due to a lingering ankle issue, which allowed Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight to split backfield reps during that span. More likely than not, Love will need to string together multiple practices in a row to put himself in a position to return to action this coming Sunday at Dallas.

headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that Love (ankle) won't play Sunday against the Broncos, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Love thus will miss a second consecutive contest as he tends to a lingering ankle injury. With Love again sidelined, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will man Arizona's backfield, as they did during last Sunday's win at the Rams. In that contest, Allgeier out-snapped Knight, 40-32, but the latter had 17 touches for 98 yards from scrimmage, while the former recorded 19 touches for just 48 total yards. Love's next chance for game action is Sunday, Nov. 1, in Dallas.

headline: Love (ankle) remained sidelined at Thursday's practice, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Love has logged back-to-back DNPs to begin the practice week and appears well on his way to missing a second straight contest Sunday against the Broncos. With Love sidelined for Week 6 against the Rams, Tyler Allgeier narrowly out-snapped Bam Knight 40 to 32, but it was Knight who was far more effective in the box score. While Allgeier out-carried him 15 to 13, Knight picked up 80 rushing yards to Allgeier's 38. Knight added two catches for 18 yards on two targets and would be a worthwhile RB2/flex option in fantasy if Love does miss Sunday's game.

headline: Love (ankle) worked on the side with trainers during the open portion of Thursday's practice, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
story: Love was listed as a non-participant Wednesday and could be headed for the same fate Thursday, unless he's able to take part in drills later in Thursday's practice. Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reported earlier Thursday that Love will likely miss Sunday's game against the Broncos, and Love working on a side field Thursday has done nothing to dispel that notion. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight are poised to lead Arizona's backfield again.

headline: The Cardinals expect their backfield to remain without Love (ankle) for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports Thursday.
story: Love didn't practice Wednesday after sitting out this past Sunday's win over the Rams. He still has two more opportunities to resume practicing and give himself a chance to return Sunday against the Broncos, but the report suggests that the Cardinals are pessimistic regarding the rookie third overall pick's availability. If Love misses a second consecutive game, Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight would be in line for additional opportunities against a Denver run defense that has been surprisingly weak this season.

headline: Love (ankle) will not practice Wednesday, per Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site.
story: Love is working his way back from an ankle injury that kept him out for Week 6 but is still not ready to ramp up to practice participation. He'll have a chance to get back in the mix Thursday or Friday, but if Love is unable to do so, it'll be a mix of Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight on Sunday against the Broncos.

headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that Love (ankle) is expected to do some running Tuesday, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
story: The Cardinals shut Love down for Week 6 as he tends to a lingering ankle injury, so Tuesday's activity from the rookie will help determine where he stands in his recovery. It's unclear if Love has a chance to return to action Sunday against the Broncos, but Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will handle the backfield until the former is ready.

headline: Love (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at the Rams, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Love thus will miss the first game of his career due to the ankle injury that has bothered him in recent weeks. So far, the third overall pick in this year's draft is sitting on 3.7 yards per carry and has been targeted just 14 times through five contests. Head coach Mike LaFleur noted to Urban on Friday that Love will be used more in the passing game once he's able to adequately make cuts, which requires his current health concern to be a thing of the past.

headline: Love (ankle) remained sidelined at practice Thursday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Love now has just one more chance to mix into drills this week Friday before the Cardinals potentially make a decision on his status for Sunday's game at the Rams. Considering head coach Mike LaFleur told Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic on Wednesday that the team wants to "get this ankle right and do it the right way," there's a chance that means missed games and not just missed practices for Love. In the event Arizona opts to sit Love this weekend, Tyler Allgeier will stand to step in as the lead runner, with Bam Knight in reserve.

headline: Love (ankle) wasn't present at the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: With back-to-back absences under his belt this week, Love may be in danger of missing the first game of his career Sunday at the Rams, especially after head coach Mike LaFleur told Mackie on Wednesday that the Cardinals want to "get this ankle right and do it the right way." What exactly that entails remains to be seen, but the team could make a ruling on Love's status for Week 6 as soon as it posts Friday's injury report. If Love is inhibited or sidelined this weekend, Tyler Allgeier is next in line to pace Arizona's backfield, with Bam Knight backing him up.

headline: Love (ankle) won't practice Wednesday, as head coach Mike LaFleur said the Cardinals want to "get this ankle right and do it the right way," Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: Love emerged from Week 4 at the Giants with an ankle injury, and while he was able to play through it this past Sunday against the Lions, he mustered just 12 carries for 22 yards and didn't haul in his only target. Considering LaFleur's comments were murky, it's unclear if Love's practice reps are the only thing that will be managed this week, or if the rookie running back is in danger of missing an actual game. Nonethelees, Love's status will be monitored closely as the week continues to get a sense of the overall situation ahead of Sunday's road matchup with the Rams.

headline: Love rushed 12 times for 22 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Cardinals' 45-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
story: Love's meager rushing yardage total actually led the Cardinals on the afternoon, and game script had essentially turned away from the run by halftime with Arizona already down 24-7 at that point. The rookie first-round pick was on the sideline by the final drive of the afternoon, and Love finished with a new career low in rushing yards. The downturn on the ground was particularly drastic when compared to Love's previous two games, when he'd gained 153 yards on 35 carries against the 49ers and Giants. Love and the Cardinals will have an uphill battle to bounce back in Week 6 as well, as Arizona pays a visit to the Rams next Sunday.

headline: Love (ankle) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest versus the Lions, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: Love emerged from Week 4 action with an ankle injury that limited him at practice Wednesday and Thursday, but he didn't have any restrictions at Friday's session before getting the all clear for Week 5. He touched on his health afterward, telling Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com that he's feeling "really, really good this week" and that he "found a way I really want to do things just consulting with the training staff and throughout my outside stuff." On Sunday, Love will look to build upon the 259 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs on 66 touches that he's racked up through the first four games of his career.

headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Friday that Love (ankle) is "trending in the right direction" ahead of Sunday's game against the Lions, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
story: Love so far has been limited at practice this week due to an ankle injury that he sustained in a Week 4 loss at the Giants. Despite LaFleur's comments, the Cardinals' final Week 5 injury report Friday may reveal that Love enters the weekend with a game designation.

headline: Love (ankle) stayed limited at Thursday's practice, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
story: Love emerged from a Week 4 loss at the Giants with a new ankle injury that's not related to the high-ankle sprain that he tended to in August. Friday's practice report will reveal whether or not he heads into the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.

headline: Love (ankle) was in uniform and participating during the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
story: Love is dealing with the second ankle injury of his young career in the wake of this past Sunday's loss at the Giants. He was able to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday and appears as if he'll be listed as at least that one day later. Thursday's practice report will reveal his activity level.

headline: Love (ankle) practiced on a limited basis Wednesday, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
story: On Monday, coach Mike LaFleur said that Love emerged from Week 4 action with an ankle injury that's not related to the high-ankle sprain he tended to in August. Prior to Wednesday's session, LaFleur added more context, telling Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com that the issue shouldn't impact Love's practice reps this week. With a capped session to begin Week 5 prep, Love is experiencing practice restrictions, so the status of the Cardinals' No. 1 RB will be monitored closely as the weekend approaches.

headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that Love's ankle injury shouldn't impact him during Week 5 prep, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
story: The Cardinals have yet to post Wednesday's injury report, but LaFleur previously told Dani Sureck of the team's official site on Monday that Love has a new ankle issue that's unrelated to the high-ankle sprain he tended to in August. LaFleur's most recent comments imply that Love may not have practice restrictions this week, or if he does he could be listed as "not-injury related, rest."

headline: Coach Mike LaFleur said Monday that Love is dealing with an ankle issue that's not related to the high-ankle sprain he tended to in August, Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Love came out of preseason Week 1 with the previous ankle issue and missed the rest of exhibition season. Through four games to begin his career, the third overall pick in this year's draft has had an oscillating workload from week-to-week, with his 66 touches going for 259 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs. Love did cede the Cardinals' last four offensive snaps of Sunday's loss at the Giants to fellow RB Tyler Allgeier, which came after the former limped off the field after one of QB Jacoby Brissett's three interceptions, according to Darren Urban of the team's official site. Wednesday's practice report should provide a sense of where Love stands with the current health concern.

headline: Coach Mike LaFleur has ruled out Carson Beck (back) for Sunday's game against the Commanders, which sets the stage for Johnson to start the contest, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Johnson, who completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown in a 34-7 loss to Kansas City in Week 11, thus is set to make his second straight start for the Cardinals. With no teams on bye this week, Johnson's Week 12 fantasy utility is limited to Superflex formats and to fantasy managers scrambling for a short-term injury replacement at the QB position.

headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that Johnson is preparing to start Sunday's game versus the Commanders due to Carson Beck's back injury, Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Beck won't practice Wednesday due to continued issues with back spasms, which held him out of this past Sunday's loss in Kansas City. In place of Beck, Johnson completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and one touchdown while also taking two carries for five yards. Friday's injury report will reveal if Beck has a chance to play in Week 12, and by proxy if Johnson will get another spot start.

headline: Johnson completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City. he added five yards on two carries.
story: The 40-year-old QB was pressed into duty with rookie Carson Beck (back) on the shelf, and Johnson unsurprisingly wasn't really up to the task after the Cardinals fell into a 14-0 hole before the first quarter was over. Johnson spent most of his afternoon finding Trey McBride for short gains, and he did hit Simi Fehoko for a two-yard score in the second quarter. Beck doesn't figure to miss much time, but if Johnson gets another start in Week 12, he'll be taking on a much less formidable Commanders defense.

headline: Johnson will start Sunday's game against the Chiefs with Carson Beck (back) having been downgraded to out for Week 11, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Coming out of his first NFL start in a Week 10 loss to the Rams, Beck was added to the injury report Thursday due to back spasms. He was listed questionable after failing to practice Friday before the Cardinals offically ruled him out for Week 11 a day later. With Beck set to sit out, the 40-year-old Johnson will pick up his 12th career NFL start while seeing action for his eighth different team since entering the league in 2008 as a fifth-round pick of the Buccaneers. He most recently started in the final two games of the 2025 season as a member of the Commanders, completed 64.4 percent of his passes for 329 yards, one touchdown and one interception while turning 11 carries into 55 yards and a score.

headline: Johnson is expected to start Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: With Carson Beck (back) not expected to practice Friday or play Sunday, Johnson appears in line to step into the starting quarterback role for Arizona. Johnson has a career 14:18 TD:INT across 50 regular-season appearances. The entire Arizona offense is one to avoid when making fantasy lineup decisions for Week 11.

headline: The Cardinals signed Johnson off the Bengals' practice squad Monday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Johnson will head to Arizona in what will mark the 15th different NFL organization that he's been a part of since entering the league as a fifth-round pick in 2008. The 40-year-old is expected to operate as the primary backup option behind rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who is poised to make his first NFL start Week 10 versus the Rams in place of the injured Gardner Minshew (elbow). With Minshew at risk of missing the remainder of the 2026 campaign while he recovers from a torn UCL, Johnson will likely stick around Arizona until the season concludes.

headline: Beck (back) will not play Sunday against the Commanders, coach Mike LaFleur said Friday, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Beck has yet to resume practicing and will miss a second consecutive game Sunday due to back spasms, paving the way for Josh Johnson to start against Washington. LaFleur added that a Week 13 return against the Eagles is in play for Beck, who made his first regular-season NFL start in a 34-6 Week 10 loss to the Rams. Beck's practice participation level leading up to that game will provide an indication regarding his potential availability, and LaFleur added that the team will know more about Beck's status "early in the week," per Weinfuss.

headline: Beck (back) was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's injury report, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Beck thus appears to be trending toward a second straight absence Sunday against the Commanders due to the back spasms that flared up late last week. If the Cardinals ultimately rule out Beck on Friday's practice report, Josh Johnson again will be under center for Arizona this weekend.

headline: Beck (back) wasn't spotted during the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Beck hasn't practice since last Thursday, when his back spasms flared up, and he's now in danger of missing a second consecutive game Sunday against the Commanders. Ultimately, Friday's session and the Cardinals' ensuing injury report will dictate if Beck has a chance to play this weekend. Josh Johnson is waiting in the wings if Beck can't suit up.

headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Beck (back) won't practice Wednesday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Beck continues to deal with back spasms that sidelined him this past Sunday at Kansas City. LaFleur told Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site Wednesday that the team is preparing Josh Johnson to start Sunday's game against the Commanders, so Beck seemingly is in danger of missing a second straight contest.

headline: Beck (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Kansas City, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: The Cardinals were already preparing for Josh Johnson to operate as the starting quarterback Sunday, as Beck entered the weekend with the questionable tag due to back spasms. Joey Aguilar will operate as Johnson's backup, and Beck's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Beck (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Kansas City, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: Beck showed up on the Cardinals' Week 11 injury report Thursday as limited due to back spasms that have flared up, per Darren Urban of the team's official site. Beck then didn't practice Friday, but Arizona still is giving him a chance to play Sunday. If Beck isn't able to go, though, Josh Johnson is lined up to be under center in his place.

headline: Beck (back) will not practice Friday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: After being listed as limited Thursday, Beck's looming absence from Friday's practice -- the result of back spasms flaring up -- per Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site, clouds his status for Sunday's game at Kansas City. For now, coach Mike LaFleur said the team will proceed as if Josh Johnson will make the start at quarterback, though the door hasn't been completely closed on the possibility of Beck being available. It's a situation to avoid in most fantasy formats.

headline: Beck was listed as limited on Thursday's injury report due to a back issue, Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Per Sureck, Beck dealt with back spasms a "few weeks ago," so his sudden appearance on Arizona's Week 11 injury report has a reasonable explanation. In any case, his status now will be monitored in advance of Sunday's game at Kansas City, with Friday's practice report potentially providing clarity in that regard.

headline: Beck was 11-for-18 passing for 108 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions and had one rush for one yard during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
story: The Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens after Week 8, and then Gardner Minshew tore the UCL in his right elbow in Week 9, setting the stage for the first appearance (a start) of Beck's career. Beck, a rookie third-rounder, generated just two drives of 30-plus yards among his nine possessions overall, and two others ended in interceptions in Rams territory. He also didn't find much success with his top available skill-position talent, TE Trey McBride, who gathered in all five of his targets for 37 yards. They'll look to improve their rapport next Sunday in Kansas City.

headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that Beck will start Sunday's game against the Rams, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Arizona first dealt Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore last Friday, and then Gardner Minshew suffered a torn UCL in his right elbow during this past Sunday's game at Seattle and will undergo season-ending surgery. That series of events precedes Beck taking over as the Cards' No. 1 signal-caller, and with eight other skill-position players on reserve lists at the moment, the top talents available to the offense will be TE Trey McBride and RB Tyler Allgeier.

headline: Beck is expected to start Sunday's contest against the Rams, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
story: With Gardner Minshew (elbow) having emerged from the Cardinals' Week 9 loss to the Seahawks with a torn UCL that will likely require season-ending surgery, Beck looks set to make his NFL debut Sunday and could wind up starting the final eight games of the 2026 campaign. The rookie third-round pick out of Miami had been inactive as the Cardinals' emergency No. 3 quarterback for much of the first half of the regular season after he completed 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown in his lone preseason appearance. Lead running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is still on injured reserve for at least three more contests and top wide receiver Michael Wilson (neck) suffered a season-ending injury in Week 9, so Beck will have to make do with limited skill-position talent around him while facing off against the Rams.

headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur said that Beck will serve as the Cardinals' No. 2 quarterback behind starter Gardner Minshew in Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports.
story: Beck had been a healthy inactive through each of the Cardinals' first eight games of the season as the emergency No. 3 quarterback, but he'll get the chance to dress for the first time in Week 9 after Arizona removed the struggling Jacoby Brissett from the starting role and dropped him down two spots on the depth chart. Like Brissett, the 30-year-old Minshew is a journeyman who isn't viewed as the team's long-term solution under center, so it wouldn't be surprising if Beck eventually received a look as the starter before the end of the season if Arizona eventually fades from playoff contention. A rookie third-round pick out of Miami, Beck completed 15 of 19 pass attempts for 188 yards and a touchdown during his lone preseason appearance.

headline: Beck (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game in Dallas, though he will be available as the team's QB3, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports.
story: Beck has been battling a back injury. While the rookie is seemingly healthy, he will be inactive for the Week 8 meeting with the Cowboys. However, Beck will be eligible to play if Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew leave the game due to illness, injury or ejection.

headline: Beck (back) practiced in full Thursday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: Beck has been battling a back injury, though it hasn't prevented him from being the team's emergency QB3. While it appears the worst of the injury is behind the rookie signal-caller, that still likely won't improve his chances of getting on the field anytime soon, at least while Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew are healthy.

headline: Beck (back) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Broncos on Sunday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Beck was unable to practice Thursday and Friday due to back spasms. He's inactive for Sunday's contest, but as the emergency third quarterback, he would be allowed to play in the event that both Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew left the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Beck (back) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Beck was unable to practice Thursday and Friday while working through back spasms, per Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com. He's been the emergency QB3 in each of the Cardinals' first six games of the season, and since Arizona doesn't have another quarterback on the practice squad, the team could just roll with starter Jacoby Brissett and backup Gardner Minshew for Sunday's contest.

headline: Beck (back) did not participate at practice Thursday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Beck popped up on the Cardinals' injury report with a back issue Wednesday, and he's now trending in the wrong direction ahead of a Week 7 matchup versus the Broncos. If he can't get back on the practice field Friday, it's unlikely he'll be available in any capacity come Sunday.

headline: Beck (back) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Beck has not played this regular season, as he's been designated as the Cardinals' emergency third quarterback for all six of their games so far. If he can get over the problem with his back by Friday, there's a good chance he'll fill that role again in Week 7 versus the Broncos.

headline: Beck (coach's decision) is inactive and is designated as Arizona's emergency third quarterback for Sunday's matchup versus the Rams, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Beck remains the third option behind Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew. The rookie third-rounder will only enter Sunday's contest if both Brissett and Minshew are unable to continue playing.

headline: Beck (coach's decision) is inactive and is designated as Arizona's emergency third quarterback for Sunday's matchup versus the Lions.
story: Beck remains the third option behind Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew. The rookie third-rounder will only enter the game if both Brissett and Minshew are unable to continue playing.

headline: Beck (coach's decision) is inactive and is designated as Arizona's emergency third quarterback for Sunday's matchup versus the Giants.
story: Beck has now been inactive as the emergency third quarterback for each of Arizona's first four games this season. He'll be able to enter Sunday's matchup only if both Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew need to exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Slovis was claimed off waivers by the Cardinals on Wednesday, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN reports.
story: Slovis had been waived by the Ravens earlier in the week, and while the team hoped to bring him back, the equally quarterback-embattled Cardinals swooped in and claimed him. With that, Slovis returns to the team he played for in 2025.

headline: The Ravens waived Slovis on Tuesday, Ryan Mink of the team's official site reports.
story: Baltimore seemingly plans to add depth at another position after clearing a spot on the 53-man roster by cutting Slovis, who had served as the team's emergency No. 3 quarterback in each of the last three contests. If Slovis clears waivers, the Ravens will look to re-sign him to their practice squad.

headline: Slovis (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Panthers but will serve as the Ravens' emergency quarterback.
story: Slovis will be inactive once again. However, if Jacoby Brissett and Joe Fagnano exit Sunday's meeting with Carolina due to an injury, illness or ejection, Slovis will be available to play.

headline: Slovis (coach's decision) is inactive but serving as the Ravens' emergency No. 3 quarterback Monday night versus the Chargers.
story: Slovis will operate as Baltimore's third option at QB for the second straight week. He will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Jacoby Brissett and backup Joe Fagnano are removed from the contest.

headline: Slovis (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against Jacksonville but will serve as the team's emergency quarterback.
story: Practice-squad elevation Austin Reed moved up to the No. 2 spot on the depth chart ahead of the Week 9 meeting with the Jaguars. While Slovis is inactive, he will be available if Reed and starter Joe Fagnano exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: The Ravens signed Slovis off the Packers' practice squad Tuesday, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
story: Slovis immediately becomes the healthiest quarterback on the Baltimore roster, as all of Lamar Jackson (thumb), Tyler Huntley (toe) and Joe Fagnano (ankle) emerged from Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills with injuries. Jackson is ticketed for injured reserve and Huntley is considered unlikely to play Thursday against the Jaguars, leaving Fagnano as the likely Week 9 starter after he was listed as a limited participant for Monday's walk-through practice. While the Ravens could elevate Austin Reed from the practice squad to provide another option at quarterback Thursday, Slovis -- who appeared in two games with Arizona in 2025 -- may be the preferred option to serve as Fagnano's top backup.

headline: Gibbens registered 10 total tackles (six solo) during Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Gibbens was able to lead the team in takedowns in Week 11, recording double-digit tackles for the second time in four weeks. The linebacker has now compiled 76 total tackles (33 solo), including 0.5 sacks, while also notching a pass defensed over 11 contests so far this season.

headline: Gibbens recorded seven tackles (four solo) in a 30-16 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
story: Gibbens' 41 defensive snaps were a season low, but the fifth-year linebacker still led the Cardinals in tackles. He's posted at least seven stops in six of seven regular-season games and is up to 49 tackles (21 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and one pass defense in 2026.

headline: Baker recorded six total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City.
story: Baker was able to register at least six stops for the fourth week in a row and seventh time overall this year. The safety is about as steady as they come, compiling 74 total tackles (36 solo), including a career-high 3.5 sacks, while also adding an interception and a forced fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 season.

headline: Baker posted six tackles (two solo) during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams in Week 10.
story: It was the third consecutive week that Baker recorded at least six stops (and the sixth time this season). The veteran safety is up to 68 tackles (31 solo), including a career-high 3.5 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception) and one forced fumble through 10 regular-season games. Baker was held out of Wednesday's practice for rest purposes, so he should be available for Sunday's road game against the Chiefs.

headline: Baker recorded 11 tackles (three solo) in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Cardinals.
story: The star safety has now logged three 11-tackle games this season, and Baker remains one of the bright spots for a Cardinals team that doesn't have many in 2026. The 10th-year pro was mentioned in trade rumors prior to Tuesday's deadline, but he'll finish out the campaign in Arizona. He's up to 62 tackles (29 solo), including a career-high 3.5 sacks, four pass breakups, including an interception, and a forced fumble across nine starts this season. Baker appears headed for an eighth straight Pro Bowl selection.

headline: Baker logged two tackles (one solo) during Sundays' 30-16 loss to Denver.
story: Baker was cleared to play against the Broncos after nursing a groin injury and an illness during Week 7 prep. He was on the field for 59 of the Cardinals' 61 defensive snaps (96.7 percent), but his two stops were a season low. The veteran safety is up to 44 tackles (25 solo), including a career-best 3.5 sacks, and four pass defenses (including one interception) through seven regular-season games.

headline: Baker (groin) is active against the Broncos on Sunday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Baker has been working through both a groin injury and an illness, but the veteran safety has been given the green light by medical staff to play Sunday. He has 42 tackles (24 solo), including a career-best 3.5 sacks, and four pass defenses (one interception) through six regular-season games.

headline: Baker (groin) is listed as questionable but expected to play against the Broncos on Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Baker missed the first two practices of the week due to both an illness and a groin injury before logging a limited session Friday. That was enough for him to draw the questionable tag for Week 7, and it appears the veteran safety will suit up against Denver.

headline: Baker (groin/illness) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Baker was held out of each of the first two practices due to an illness and groin injury, but he earned the questionable tag after logging a limited session Friday. Wydett Williams and Dadrion Taylor-Demerson would be the top candidates to start at safety if Baker cannot play.

headline: Baker (groin/illness) did not participate at practice Thursday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Baker played through a groin issue in the Cardinals' contest against the Rams in Week 6, but he has now missed two straight practice sessions after an illness was added to his status on the injury report. If he can't practice Friday, he'll be facing an uphill battle to be available Sunday versus the Broncos.

headline: Baker, who sat out Wednesday's practice due to a groin injury as well as an illness, logged six tackles (four solo), including 1.0 sacks, and a pass defensed in the Cardinals' 18-16 win over the Rams on Sunday.
story: The veteran strong safety did it all in Sunday's contest while playing all 57 of the Cardinals' defensive snaps. Baker sacked Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford for a loss of eight yards on first down in the second quarter, leading to a Rams punt. The defensive back regularly blitzes the quarterback and has accumulated 3.5 sacks through six regular-season games in 2026.

headline: Baker (groin/illness) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Baker was able to play through his groin issue in Week 6 against the Rams, but now he's also dealing with an illness, and his status for Week 7 is in question. He'll probably have to manage a full practice Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Baker (groin) is active for Sunday's game against the Rams.
story: Baker did not participate in Friday's practice after sustaining a groin injury. The safety appears to be gutting his way through the new issue to suit up for Sunday's divisional matchup with the Rams.

headline: Baker (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Rams, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
story: Baker did not participate in Friday's practice with a new groin injury. The veteran strong safety is a durable defensive back, so he may be able to play through the issue for Sunday's divisional bout. If Baker cannot suit up, Dadrion Taylor-Demerson will likely start at strong safety.

headline: Baker tallied five tackles (two solo) and an interception during Arizona's loss versus the Giants on Sunday.
story: Baker had a strong outing despite the loss, as he managed to record one of the team's two interceptions of Jameis Winston. The 2017 second-round pick has now compiled 25 tackles (14 solo), including 1.5 sacks, and an interception across his first four outings, and will look to keep producing next week versus the Lions.

headline: Wilson recorded eight total tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Wilson was able to register at least eight stops for the second straight week and fifth time overall this season. The linebacker has now compiled 80 total tackles (35 solo), two passes defensed and a forced fumble over 11 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Wilson registered 10 tackles (six solo) during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams in Week 10.
story: The Cardinals were blown out at home in Week 10, but Wilson came away from the loss with a season-high 10 stops while playing every single defensive snap. The veteran linebacker is up to 72 total tackles through 10 regular-season games, and he is three stops shy from matching his career-high that he set in 2024 with the Cardinals (over 16 regular-season contests).

headline: Wilson (knee) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Cowboys, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Wilson's practice reps were limited due to a knee injury, but the veteran linebacker's full practice Friday was enough for him to fade an injury tag for Sunday's road game. The 2019 fifth-rounder has 47 tackles (20 solo), one pass defense and one forced fumble through seven regular-season games.

headline: Wilson (knee) was limited in Thursday's practice, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: Wilson didn't practice Wednesday, but he was out there Thursday in a limited capacity. He'll likely need another limited session Friday to avoid an injury designation ahead of the Week 8 meeting with the Cowboys.

headline: Wilson (knee) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Wilson's absence Wednesday was marked not injury related, but there does seem to be a knee issue. His activity at practice Thursday and Friday should offer more insight into whether he's truly in danger of sitting out in Week 8.

headline: Wilson (thumb) was a full participant at the Cardinals' practice Thursday, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
story: Wilson was added to the injury report with a thumb injury Wednesday, ultimately logging a limited practice. The linebacker now appears to be good to go for Sunday's matchup with the Giants after increasing his participation Thursday.

headline: Wilson (thumb) was a limited participant in Arizona's practice Wednesday, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
story: Wilson popped up on the injury report Wednesday due to a thumb issue, putting his status for Sunday's matchup versus the Giants up in the air. If he ends up being unable to play, Cody Simon would be in line to start at middle linebacker.

headline: Duvernay logged 81 kickoff-return yards in the Cardinals' 34-7 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
story: Duvernay played two offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver took a step back after drawing three targets in Week 10, as both Simi Fehoko and Harrison Wallace were clearly ahead of him Sunday.

headline: Duvernay caught two of three targets for 35 yards during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
story: Duvernay was on the field for only 10 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (28.6 percent), but the veteran wide receiver connected with rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck on passes of four and 31 yards on back-to-back plays late in the first quarter. Duvernay finished the contest second in catches, targets and receiving yards behind Trey McBride, and he's caught two passes in each of his last three outings. With Michael Wilson (neck) out for the year, the Cardinals' top wideouts for the rest of the season appear to be Duvernay, Simi Fehoko and rookie fifth-rounder Reggie Virgil, which doesn't inspire much confidence heading into Week 11 against Kansas City on Nov. 22.

headline: Duvernay registered two catches for eight yards on two targets, returned three kickoffs for 64 yards and brought back two punts for 21 yards in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks.
story: A two-time Pro Bowl return man, Duvernay played exclusively on special teams over the Cardinals' first seven games of the season, but he's seen his role on offense expand out of necessity following the trade of Marvin Harrison to the Texans along with the season-ending injuries to Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Jalen Brooks (wrist). For the second straight week, Duvernay logged just under half of the offensive snaps, with his 45 percent share placing him behind only Michael Wilson (83 percent) and Simi Fehoko (49 percent) among the team's wideouts. Head coach Mike LaFleur announced Monday that Wilson was diagnosed with a neck fracture that will bring an end to his season, so Duvernay could be in line for an even more pronounced role heading into next Sunday's game against the Rams. However, with starting quarterback Gardner Minshew (elbow) also sustaining a likely season-ending injury in the loss to the Seahawks, Duvernay will be on the receiving end of passes from rookie third-round pick Carson Beck, who will make his NFL debut in Week 10.

headline: Duvernay caught both of his targets for 14 yards while also adding 75 yards as a kick returner and 12 punt-return yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime win against the Cowboys.
story: Duvernay reeled in his first two passes of the year while playing 34 offensive snaps in the victory. Fellow wideout Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) fractured his right tibia during the contest, and he is likely set to miss the rest of the 2026 campaign. Duvernay will likely see an increased role on offense in Bourne's absence, but he will remain an unappealing fantasy option ahead of the team's Week 9 matchup against Seattle.

headline: Virgil wasn't targeted in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
story: The 22-year-old wide receiver played just two offensive snaps, the same amount as Devin Duvernay, as the duo played behind all three of Simi Fehoko (52 snaps), Harrison Wallace (36) and Zay Jones (32) in the Cardinals' injury-ravaged wideout depth chart. Virgil has three catches for 54 yards on 11 targets across seven games this season and therefore doesn't possess any fantasy relevance at the moment.

headline: Virgil was on the field for 16 of the Cardinals' 35 offensive snaps (45.7 percent), but the rookie fifth-rounder didn't get a target during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
story: The Cardinals' offense struggled in its first game this season with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center, finishing with just 17:37 in time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Virgil and the rest of the pass catchers, and even star tight end Trey McBride finished with only five catches on as many targets for 37 yards. It's hard to put much trust into Virgil and the rest of the pass catchers, especially with the team heading into a tough Week 11 road tilt against Kansas City.

headline: Virgil will take over a larger role after teammate Michael Wilson suffered a season-ending neck injury last week, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: A 2026 fifth-round pick, Virgil started his career buried on the depth chart before moving up due to injuries and trades. It's not quite the same as earning a starting job, but he should see routes and targets all the same in the coming weeks. Virgil has been targeted on 11 of 56 routes (19.6 percent) and caught just three passes for 54 yards in five appearances. He should get plenty of playing time this Sunday against the Rams in what will be the first career start for rookie QB Carson Beck.

headline: Virgil caught one of four targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
story: Gardner Minshew found Virgil for a 25-yard pass early in the first quarter, but the duo failed to connect for the rest of Sunday's contest. The Cardinals' offense took some big hits in Week 9, with Minshew sustaining a torn UCL and wide receiver Michael Wilson suffering a fracture in his neck, and those injuries will keep both players on the shelf for the rest of the 2026 season. Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) and Jalen Brooks (wrist) are both also on season-ending IR, which leaves Virgil, Simi Fehoko, Devin Duvernay and superstar tight end Trey McBride as the top targets for rookie third-round quarterback Carson Beck heading into Week 10 against the Rams.

headline: Virgil failed to reel in either of his targets during Sunday's 33-30 overtime victory against Dallas.
story: Virgil played a season-high 38 offensive snaps, but he went without a reception for the third straight week. The Cardinals placed Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) on injured reserve Tuesday after the wide receiver fractured his right tibia in Week 8, so more opportunities could come Virgil's way moving forward. Regardless of an increase in workload, the team's Week 9 matchup versus Seattle will be a challenging one for the 22-year-old.

headline: Virgil recorded two receptions for 29 yards on five targets in Sunday's 45-21 loss to the Lions.
story: A healthy inactive for the first four games of the season, Virgil ended up suiting up for the first time after the Cardinals opted to hold Marvin Harrison out in Week 5 before trading him to the Texans shortly after Sunday's contest concluded. Virgil served as the Cardinals' No. 4 receiver, logging just 13 of 73 offensive snaps but seeing ample involvement during his limited time on the field. While the rookie fifth-round pick out of Texas Tech should be active for the Cardinals on a regular basis moving forward, he's likely to rank behind Michael Wilson, Trey McBride and Kendrick Bourne in the pecking order for targets.

headline: Virgil (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's battle against the Giants.
story: Virgil has yet to log a snap so far during his rookie campaign. The fifth-round pick in April's NFL Draft may need an injury (or other absence) ahead of him on the wideout depth chart in order to garner playing time for Arizona.

headline: Higgins caught his lone target for four yards during the Cardinals' 34-7 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
story: The Cardinals offense struggled Sunday with Josh Johnson as the starter in the absence of Carson Beck (back). Of Johnson's 31 pass attempts, 26 of them were split between Trey McBride (14), Harrison Wallace (seven) and Simi Fehoko (five), leaving very little for Higgins and the other Cardinals pass catchers. Higgins has only one catch over his last two outings and a 19-166-1 line on 21 targets through 11 regular-season games.

headline: Higgins played 24 of 35 offensive snaps (68.6 percent) but didn't get a target during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
story: Week 10 was Higgins' first game since signing a three-year contract extension worth up to $26.8 million. He didn't have much to show for it during Sunday's loss, although the Cardinals finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession, and the offense struggled as a whole with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center. Higgins will take an 18-162-1 receiving line on 20 targets through 10 games into Arizona's Week 11 tilt against Kansas City on Nov. 22.

headline: Higgins is signing a contract extension with the Cardinals through 2029, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Higgins was scheduled for free agency after this season, and he's taken on a larger role as the year has progressed, helping the Cardinals get by with limited talent at wide receiver. Higgins has 18 catches for 162 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets, serving as a complementary receiving option alongside Trey McBride when the Cardinals use multi-TE formations. Higgins figures to stick in that role long-term and won't be of much fantasy interest unless McBride misses time.

headline: Higgins caught both of his targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks.
story: With all of the injuries at wide receiver for Arizona, Higgins played a season-high 66 percent of the offensive snaps in Seattle. It still didn't translate to an elevated role in the pass game. Higgins has 18 grabs for 162 yards and a touchdown on 20 targets across nine games this season.

headline: Higgins tallied two catches for 10 yards on four targets Sunday in a 33-30 overtime win over Dallas.
story: Wideout Michael Wilson missed a portion of the contest due to an injury to his ribs, and Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) exited for good late in the first half. That resulted in a need for other Cardinals pass catchers to step up, and Higgins ended up getting targeted a season-high four times. However, he didn't do much with the opportunity, finishing with his lowest yardage total since he was shut out in Week 2. Meanwhile, No. 1 tight end Trey McBride had another big game with seven catches for 72 yards and a touchdown on eight targets. McBride's elite status will likely continue to make Higgins an afterthought most weeks.

headline: Higgins caught all three of his targets for 17 yards and made one tackle on kick coverage in the Cardinals' 30-16 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
story: Higgins played 39 offensive snaps and 17 special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The versatile tight end continues to fill a moderate role in the passing game, allowing the Cardinals to continue playing 12- and 13-personnel packages.

headline: Higgins caught all three of his targets for 28 yards during the Cardinals' 18-16 win over the Rams on Sunday.
story: Higgins has caught exactly three passes in three of his last four games, and, over that span, he has an 11-124-1 receiving line on 11 targets. Trey McBride is the focal point of the Cardinals' offense, but Higgins has been on the field for at least 40 percent of the team's offensive snaps in three games this season. The Cardinals will stay home for Week 7 against the Broncos, whose defense has given up 329 receiving yards to opposing tight ends this season, which ranks 21st in the NFL.

headline: Higgins caught both of his targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's loss to the Giants.
story: As usual, most of Arizona's tight-end targets went to Trey McBride, who posted a 7-31-0 line on 12 looks. However, Higgins actually had a better fantasy score in some formats due to his two-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter. Higgins didn't log any receptions or targets over the first two weeks of the campaign, but he's ticked up his production a bit over the past two weeks with a 5-39-1 receiving line on five targets.

headline: Fehoko caught one of five targets for a two-yard touchdown in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
story: The wideout led his position group by playing 52 of 56 offensive snaps, and he ran a team-high 34 routes on Josh Johnson's 37 dropbacks. It didn't translate to much production outside of the short touchdown, as Fehoko has consistently shown he can't win enough as an NFL receiver. He's been thrust into heavy snaps due to a litany of injuries in Arizona. Fehoko can mostly be ignored in fantasy until he shows something more in the box score.

headline: Fehoko finished Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams with one catch on two targets for 21 yards. He also recorded a tackle.
story: Week 10 was the Cardinals' first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck as the starting quarterback. The offense struggled to move the ball and logged only 35 snaps as a whole while finishing with 17:37 in time of possession. That meant less opportunities for Fehoko and the rest of the Cardinals' skill-position players, although the sixth-year pro did connect with Beck on a 21-yard pass early in the first quarter. Fehoko's 26 offensive snaps led all Arizona wide receivers, and with Michael Wilson (neck) out for the rest of the season, he should continue to operate in an elevated role heading into Week 11 against Kansas City on Nov. 22.

headline: Fehoko will take over a larger role after teammate Michael Wilson suffered a season-ending neck injury last week, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Fehoko is a 2021 fifth-round pick who turned 29 earlier this month and has been targeted on just two of 37 routes for the Cardinals this year. He mostly seems to have stuck around the league because his size is useful for special teams and blocking, but Fehoko now has a chance to get more snaps on offense, if only because Arizona's WR depth chart has been decimated. He has a chance to start this Sunday against the Rams in QB Carson Beck's first career start.

headline: Fehoko was unable to haul in his lone target in Sunday's 17-3 loss to the Seahawks.
story: Fehoko has already climbed way up the wideout pecking order over the past two weeks, logging a 49 percent offensive snap share in both games after not exceeding a 12 percent snap share through the first seven weeks. However, the veteran wideout hasn't been able to do much with the recent opportunity, and he's stuck on one catch for 17 yards on two targets through nine contests. With that said, somebody is going to have to step up in the wideout corps to try to replace the production of Michael Wilson (neck), Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Jalen Brooks (wrist), all of whom have been lost to season-ending injuries over the past two weeks. Fehoko is a candidate to take on some of that responsibility along with Reggie Virgil, Devin Duvernay and Harrison Wallace. The Cardinals will also be working with a new quarterback moving forward, as rookie Carson Beck is lined up to claim the starting role from Gardner Minshew (elbow), who landed on injured reserve Tuesday.

headline: Fehoko is listed as a starting receiver on the Cardinals' unofficial depth chart heading into Sunday's game at Seattle, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports.
story: Buried on the depth chart at receiver to begin the season, Fehoko mostly served as a special-teams contributor through the Cardinals' first seven games. However,the Cardinals have since traded away Marvin Harrison before losing Jalen Brooks (wrist) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) to season-ending injuries within the past two weeks, so Fehoko suddenly finds himself in a position to contribute. Fehoko played double-digit snaps for the first time in 2026 on Sunday, coincidentally against his former teams the Cowboys. He wasn't much of a factor in a comeback win, however, earning just one target for a 17-yard reception while taking the field for 40 of the team's 81 offensive play. While Fehoko could see his playing time climb even higher in Week 9, tight ends Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins, wideout Michael Wilson (ribs) and running back Tyler Allgeier may be better bets to command targets from quarterback Gardner Minshew.

headline: Jones reverted to the Cardinals' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: Jones' 32 snaps on offense during Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs were ahead of both Devin Duvernay and Reggie Virgil (two each) and behind Simi Fehoko (52) and Harrison Wallace (36). Jones finished the game with a one-yard carry and a 17-yard catch on two targets, and that reception ended up being the second-longest offensive play for the Cardinals. Given his usage in Week 11, Jones stands a good chance of being brought up for Week 12 against the Commanders on Nov. 29, although his next elevation from the practice squad is the last one he is eligible for this season.

headline: The Cardinals elevated Jones from the practice squad Saturday.
story: The veteran wideout played seven offensive snaps in Arizona's loss to the Rams last Sunday. With a boatload of injuries at the position, Jones figures to have a role for the foreseeable future. He has no fantasy appeal in this injury-ruined offense.

headline: Jones reverted to the Cardinals' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: Jones was elevated to the Cardinals' active roster for Week 10 against the Rams on Sunday. He played seven offensive snaps and failed to haul in his lone target from Carson Beck, and Jones also recorded a tackle on linebacker Wesley Bailey midway through the third quarter in what was a 34-6 loss for Arizona. Michael Wilson (neck), Kendrick Bourne (lower leg) and Jalen Brooks (wrist) are all on season-ending IR, so Jones could be elevated to the Cardinals' active roster for Week 11 against the Chiefs on Sunday.

headline: Jones was elevated from Arizona's practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
story: Jones signed with the Cardinals' practice squad Oct. 28, and this is his first elevation since joining the organization. The veteran wideout could immediately slide into a major role in Arizona's passing game among a depleted wideout corps that has lost Michael Wilson (neck) and Kendrick Bourne (tibia) for the season. Jones spent the past two campaigns with the Cardinals, and he caught 12 passes (on 18 targets) for 182 yards over eight games last year.

headline: The Cardinals signed Jones to the practice squad Wednesday.
story: Jones spent the final week of training camp with the Texans but was unable to crack the 53-man roster. He's now with the Cardinals as a member of the practice squad and would be a candidate for elevation to the active roster if Arizona was in need of depth at wide receiver. Jones played in eight regular-season games for the Cardinals in 2025 before being placed on injured reserve in mid-November due to an Achilles injury.

headline: Wallace finished Sunday's loss to Kansas City with four catches for 57 yards on seven targets.
story: Wallace began the season on the Cardinals' practice squad and didn't play in his first NFL game until Week 9 versus Seattle. After logging a total of seven offensive snaps and one catch across his first two contests, the rookie paced Arizona wideouts in targets, receptions and receiving yards. Wallace also ranked second among the wideout corps with 36 offensive snaps, so it appears there was a conscious effort to involve him in the team's passing game. The Cardinals' wide-receiver room has lacked a reliable option since Michael Wilson went down with a season-ending neck injury, so the door is wide open for Wallace to claim a prominent role with continued production.

headline: Wallace recorded a nine-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
story: Though he played just five of the Cardinals' 35 snaps on offense, Wallace was able to come away with his first NFL reception in the third quarter. Even if Wallace earns more playing time in future weeks, he'll likely struggle to produce meaningful fantasy lines while rookie third-round pick Carson Beck continues to direct the offense behind a shaky offensive line.

headline: The Cardinals signed Wallace from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
story: Wallace signed to Arizona's practice squad in August and has yet to play in a regular-season game. Week 9 will be the undrafted free agent's NFL debut should he be active for Sunday's matchup against Seattle. He will likely act as a depth piece should he play.

headline: Ryland made his lone extra-point attempt in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Playing with their third- and fourth-string quarterbacks, the Cardinals have mustered a total of 13 points over their last two games. Ryland has minimal fantasy appeal in an offense struggling to simply move the ball. On the season, he's 22-for-24 on field-goal tries and 17-for-18 on PATs across 11 games.

headline: Ryland went 2-for-2 on field-goal tries during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
story: Ryland provided all of the offense for Arizona in Week 10, making multiple field goals in a contest for the fourth time in the last five weeks. The kicker has rebounded well in 2026 after a challenging 2025 campaign, converting 22 of 24 field-goal tries over 10 contests so far this season.

headline: Ryland made his lone field-goal attempt during Arizona's loss versus the Seahawks on Sunday.
story: Ryland played just three snaps during the loss, though he managed to convert his only kick, which came from 28 yards and also served as the team's only points in the game. He now has converted 20 of his 22 field-goal attempts and 16 of his 17 extra-point tries across nine games this season.

headline: Ryland converted both of his field-goal attempts and three of four PATs in Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Cowboys.
story: Ryland's missed PAT came in the fourth quarter with 1:03 remaining after Michael Wilson's touchdown knotted the game at 30-30. Arizona was lucky to get to overtime, but Ryland made the winning kick with 4:09 remaining, drilling a 42-yard field goal. On the season, he's made 19 of 21 field-goal tries and 16 of 17 extra-point attempts.

headline: Ryland went 3-for-3 on field-goal tries and converted his only extra-point attempt during Sunday's 30-16 loss to Denver.
story: Ryland remained a busy man in Week 7, making field goals from 30, 26 and 41 yards against the Broncos. The kicker has now registered three or more field-goal makes in four contests this season while attempting one or zero field goals in Arizona's other three games. Ryland and the Cardinals' unpredictable offense will have a chance to be more productive in Week 8 against the Cowboys' putrid defense.

headline: Ryland converted all six of his field-goal attempts during Arizona's win over the Rams on Sunday.
story: Ryland had a dominant outing during the victory, scoring all 18 points for the Cardinals, including a game-winning 43-yard field goal as time expired. The 27-year-old now has made 14 of his 16 field-goal tries to start the season and will look to keep producing next week versus the Broncos.

headline: Ryland made all three of his extra-point attempts but missed his lone field-goal try during the Cardinals' 45-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
story: Ryland failed to connect on a 53-yard field goal early in the third quarter, and the miss set the Lions up at mid field and ultimately led to a 39-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff to Jameson Williams five plays later. Ryland has attempted one field goal or zero in three of Arizona's last four games, and both of his missed kicks this season have come from 50-plus yards. The Cardinals will travel to Los Angeles for a Week 6 NFC West showdown against the Rams on Oct. 18.

headline: Ryland made his only field-goal attempt and went 3-for-3 on extra-point tries during Sunday's 36-24 loss to the Giants.
story: Ryland got the chance to attempt only one field goal, but he made the most of it. The kicker converted a 60-yard try as time expired in the first half, notching the longest field goal of his career. Ryland has now gone 8-for-9 on field-goal tries, including 2-for-3 from 50-plus yards, over four contests to open the 2026 campaign.

headline: Quitoriano played all 13 of his snaps on special teams in Sunday's 34-7 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Since coming out of nowhere to post two receiving touchdowns in his Cardinals debut back in Week 5 against the Lions, Quitoriano has fallen out of the mix for playing time on offense. After the two-score effort, Quitoriano logged double-digit snaps on offense in four straight contests, but he drew just one target over that stretch. In the subsequent two games, Quitoriano has played just three total snaps on offense while Trey McBride, Elijah Higgins and Hunter Long have been prioritized ahead of him at tight end.

headline: Quitoriano caught both of his targets for 15 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 45-21 loss to Detroit.
story: Quitoriano entered Sunday having recorded just two receptions since the beginning of the 2023 campaign. The tight end made the most of his two chances in Week 5, reeling in a two-yard touchdown pass from Jacoby Brissett in the first quarter before later connecting with the quarterback again for a 13-yard score in the third quarter. Quitoriano's performance figures to be an anomaly, and he carries little fantasy value moving forward.

headline: The Cardinals signed Quitoriano from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday.
