story: The move gives the Cardinals extra depth at tight end on the 53-man roster after Hunter Long (knee) was placed on injured reserve, with Kenny Yeboah taking Quitoriano's place on Arizona's practice squad. Quitoriano has yet to take the field this season, but he's now slated in as the TE3 behind Trey McBride and Elijah Higgins. Quitoriano played in 17 regular-season games for the Falcons in 2025, when he contributed on both special teams and offense but did not see a target.

headline: Knight carried the ball seven times for 35 yards and caught his only target for 10 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City.
story: Although he split the backfield workload nearly equally with Tyler Allgeier, Knight was the more productive RB, although he still failed to reach 50 rushing yards for a fourth straight game. The 25-year-old running back gets a more favorable matchup in Week 12 against the Commanders, but Knight and Allgeier could face additional competition for touches if Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is cleared to return.

headline: Knight turned five carries into 19 yards, failed to haul in either of his two targets and recorded a tackle during the Cardinals' 34-6 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
story: Knight was cleared to return for Week 10 from a one-game absence while in the league's concussion protocol. His 19 snaps were actually ahead of fellow running back Tyler Allgeier (16), with the duo each logging five carries. The Cardinals logged only 35 offensive snaps for the entire game and finished with a measly 17:37 time of possession, however. It was Arizona's first game with rookie third-rounder Carson Beck under center, and Knight and the offense will have its hands full in Week 11 against Kansas City, whose defense ranks eighth in the NFL in yards allowed per game (314.8).

headline: Knight (concussion) is cleared to play Sunday against the Rams, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Knight figures to split backfield work with Tyler Allgeier, who played 96 percent of snaps last week when Knight was inactive for a 17-3 loss at Seattle. Knight suffered the concussion in Week 8, shortly after Jeremiyah Love injured his ankle -- an issue that sent the rookie to injured reserve not long after. Love is out for at least three more games, leaving Allgeier and Knight to split backfield work again.

headline: Knight (concussion) practiced in full Thursday, Zach Gershman of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Knight was limited Wednesday after donning a yellow non-contact jersey in practice, but after ditching it one day later, he was able to handle every on-field rep. That's not to say he's gained clearance from the concussion protocol, which requires an evaluation from an independent neurologist, but he's likely on the precipice of doing so. Friday's injury report will determine if Knight heads into the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game against the Rams.

headline: Knight (concussion) practiced Thursday without a yellow non-contact jersey, Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Knight didn't practice last week before being ruled out for this past Sunday's game at Seattle due to a concussion that he suffered one week prior, but he got back on the practice field as limited Wednesday while wearing the non-contact jersey. His ability to ditch it one day later indicates he's making progress through the protocol for head injuries, but Thursday's practice report will unveil whether or not he was full.

headline: Knight (concussion) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: This marks Knight's first on-field work since suffering a concussion during a Week 8 win at Dallas. According to Mackie, Knight was wearing a yellow non-contact jersey at Wednesday's session, so the running back likely still has a few phases to go to complete his time in the protocol for head injuries.

headline: Knight (concussion) practiced Wednesday in a non-contact jersey, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: After suffering a concussion in Week 8 at Dallas, Knight wasn't able to practice last week before the Cardinals ruled him out ahead of this past Sunday's game in Seattle. With his return to drills this week, he's made progress through the protocol for head injuries, but the presence of the non-contact jersey indicates he's a few steps away from meeting with an independent neurologist.

headline: Knight (concussion) is out for Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
story: After being concussed early in last Sunday's game against Dallas, Knight will miss at least one contest, as he remains in the league's protocol. With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) also sidelined, Tyler Allgeier projects to handle most of the backfield work, though it's a really tough road draw against a strong run defense.

headline: Knight (concussion) officially didn't practice Thursday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Since exiting Week 8 action with a concussion, Knight hasn't been able to log any practice reps, which generally isn't a good sign that he'll be available Sunday at Seattle. Arizona may make a ruling on Knight's status once it posts Friday's injury report, and if he's indeed sidelined for that contest, Tyler Allgeier stands to serve as the team's workhorse running back this weekend, with Evan Hull likely backing him up.

headline: Knight (concussion) wasn't present for Thursday's practice, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: Assuming Knight goes down as a non-participant Thursday, his lack of activity so far this week doesn't give him a good chance to gain clearance from the concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's game at Seattle. With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) hitting IR on Tuesday, Tyler Allgeier is poised to lead the Cardinals backfield until Knight is back in action, at which point there's expected to be more of a even split between the two.

headline: Knight (concussion) did not practice Wednesday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: Knight is in concussion protocol after playing just 18 offensive snaps in last Sunday's overtime win over the Cowboys. With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) headed to injured reserve and out for at least the next four weeks, Knight figures to have a key backfield role alongside Tyler Allgeier, but it might be a challenge for Knight to gain clearance for Sunday's game against Seattle.

headline: Coach Mike LaFleur said Wednesday that the Cardinals planned on Knight (concussion) being one of their top two backs before he and Jeremiyah Love (ankle) suffered injuries in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: Love will have to spend at least the next four games on IR, and Knight's availability for Week 9 is in doubt with him being in concussion protocol, but his coach's words signal a prominent role in Arizona's backfield may be waiting for him whenever he's ready to play again. Until then, free-agent acquisition Tyler Allgeier figures to be the primary beneficiary of Love's extended absence, but Knight should also eventually see an increased workload, especially in the passing game. Recent signee Evan Hull is also in the mix, but he has not played an offensive snap yet in 2026.

headline: Head coach Mike LaFleur revealed Monday that Knight is in the concussion protocol following Sunday's overtime win in Dallas, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Knight took a shoulder to the helmet from a Cowboys defender in the third quarter of Sunday's game, and after a visit to the locker room, he was ruled out with a concussion. It marked the second Cardinals RB to exit and not return in Week 8 -- Jeremiyah Love suffered a "new" ankle injury, per LaFleur -- so at the moment Tyler Allgeier is the top healthiest member of the team's backfield.

headline: Knight (concussion) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
story: With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) also dealing with an injury, Tyler Allgeier will see added backfield opportunities against Dallas. Knight will now need to advance through the NFL's concussion protocol in order to be available for next Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

headline: Knight headed to the locker room during Sunday's game against the Cowboys after sustaining an unspecified injury, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
story: With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) also having previously departed the contest, Tyler Allgeier is left to handle the Cardinals' RB duties. Before his exit, Knight carried three times for eight yards.

headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) has been cleared to return from a two-game absence to face the Cowboys on Sunday, so Knight is expected to revert to rotational role in the Cardinals' backfield.
story: The rookie first-rounder was a full participant in Friday's practice, which was enough for him to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's contest. Love could operate on a snap count in his return, so Knight and Tyler Allgeier -- who have co-led the Cardinals' backfield for each of the last two games -- could both still see a fair amount of involvement in Arizona's offensive gameplan. Over his last two outings, Knight has turned 22 carries into 128 yards (5.8 YPC) and caught five passes on seven targets for 33 yards.

headline: Knight accrued seven carries for 48 yards and reeled in three of five targets for 15 yards during Sunday's 30-16 defeat to the Broncos.
story: With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined for a second consecutive contest, Tyler Allgeier and Knight again were tasked with manning the Cardinals backfield. Allgeier earned 11 touches to Knight's 10 on Sunday, but the latter out-gained him by 14 yards from scrimmage (63 versus 49). It was the second week in a row in which Knight churned out more yardage than Allgeier on fewer touches, and even if Love is able to return in Week 8 at Dallas, Knight could begin to put himself in position for regular snaps moving forward, if he hasn't already.

headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will be sidelined for Sunday's game against the Broncos, so Knight and Tyler Allgeier will be used in tandem in Love's absence, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: It was an 18-15 split in carries between Allgeier and Knight during the Cardinals' Week 6 win over the Rams, but Knight was far more efficient with his touches, finishing with 80 yards compared to Allgeier's 38. Knight is averaging 6.2 yards per carry this season, and he and Allgeier are facing a Denver defense Sunday that ranks 31st in the league in rushing yards allowed per game (139.8).

headline: Knight rushed 15 times for 80 yards and caught both of his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 18-16 win over the Rams.
story: Knight got an extended opportunity in the absence of Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and was far more efficient than Tyler Allgeier, who mustered just 38 rushing yards on 18 rushing attempts. Love figures to reclaim the lead role in Arizona's backfield upon his return, which could come as soon as Week 7 against the Broncos, but Knight could get a sizable workload should Love remain sidelined. Prior to Sunday's win, Knight had just three carries and no targets all season.

headline: Knight will bump up the Cardinals' RB depth chart in Week 6 with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) ruled out, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
story: Knight still will be situated behind Tyler Allgeier, but the former nonetheless is the No. 2 back for as long as Love is sidelined. For his career, Knight has tallied 173 carries for 614 yards (3.5 YPC) and five touchdowns and hauled in 36 of 46 targets for 268 yards and another TD in 26 games.

headline: Allgeier carried the ball seven times for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City.
story: Game script fairly quickly put the Cardinals' running game in mothballs, and Allgeier wound up splitting the backfield workload nearly equally with Bam Knight, who picked up 45 scrimmage yards on eight touches. Allgeier has gone three straight games without reaching 50 rushing yards or getting into the end zone, but those games were also against very tough opponents (the Seahawks in Week 9 and the Rams in Week 10). The fifth-year RB could find a little more running room in Week 12 against the Commanders, but Jeremiyah Love (ankle) might also be ready to rejoin the lineup by then.

headline: Allgeier mustered five carries for 14 yards and didn't gather in his only target during Sunday's 34-6 defeat to the Rams.
story: With Bam Knight back in the lineup in Week 10 after one absence due to a concussion, Allgeier didn't reach double-digit touches for the first time since Week 5, a span in which the latter's 65 touches went for 334 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs. Knight himself found a similar lack of success Sunday with just 19 yards on his five rushes. Because the Cardinals racked up just 123 yards of offense in rookie QB Carson Beck's first NFL start, it's tough to envision worse outcomes moving forward, though the team does take on the surging Chiefs next Sunday on the road.

headline: Allgeier compiled 17 carries for 46 yards and caught two of three targets for no yards during Sunday's 17-3 defeat at Seattle.
story: Allegeier has reeled off 10-plus touches in four straight contests, a span in which he's turned 65 touches into 334 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs. He's been the beneficiary of repeated ankle injuries to rookie first-round pick Jeremiyah Love, who must remain on IR for at least three more outings after Sunday's matchup, and the other current top RB on the active roster (Bam Knight) is in the concussion protocol, which will require clearance from an independent neurologist for his next game action. As a result, Allgeier is set up to retain a significant workload until Knight gets the all clear to return.

headline: Allgeier is slated to work as Arizona's No. 1 running back beginning with Sunday's game at Seattle after Jeremiyah Love (ankle) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, Darren Urban of the team's official site reports.
story: After previously leading the Cardinals backfield when Love was sidelined due to a different ankle injury Weeks 6 and 7, Allgeier is now slated for a longer run atop the depth chart while Love is projected to miss 4-to-5 weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain. Love sustained his latest ankle injury late in the first quarter of Sunday's overtime win over the Cowboys, with his early exit clearing the way for Allgeier to run wild. Allgeier finished with a career-high 147 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries along with 44 yards and another score on five receptions. In addition to Love getting hurt, Bam Knight sustained a concussion and is uncertain to play Week 9 against Seattle, so the backfield could belong to Allgeier, Evan Hull and a practice-squad signee (likely Jerome Ford). Though Allgeier found substantial success in Week 8, he came into the contest averaging just 2.9 yards per carry on 61 totes. He'll also be facing a Seattle defense that is tied for the second-fewest yards per carry (3.8) allowed to running backs this season, so a repeat performance by Allgeier would be surprising.

headline: Allgeier reeled off 147 yards and one touchdown on 11 carries and gathered in all five targets for 44 yards and one more TD during Sunday's 33-30 overtime win in Dallas.
story: Fellow RBs Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion) left in the second and third quarters, respectively, and were unable to return, leaving Allgeier as the only healthy and available backfield option the rest of the way. Allgeier didn't really get going until QB Gardner Minshew took over for Jacoby Brissett late in the third quarter, as the running back recorded a 63-yard touchdown run, another 52-yard carry and a five-yard TD grab on the next two drives to account for most of his output. Considering Love has been dealing with ankle issues for most of the season and already has missed two games, and Knight is subject to the protocol for head injuries, Allgeier may be in line for a boost in workload in the short term.

headline: Allgeier (toe) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest at Dallas, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Allgeier kicked off Week 8 prep as a non-participant due to a toe injury, but he was able to log back-to-back limited sessions to end it, which was enough to get the all-clear for Sunday's matchup. He'll be welcoming back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) to the Cardinals backfield after a two-game absence, so the breakdown of reps between those two and potentially Bam Knight remains to be seen.

headline: Allgeier (toe) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports.
story: After Allgeier sat out Wednesday's session due to a toe injury, his ability to mix into drills one day later generally is a good sign as the Cardinals go through Week 8 prep. Friday's practice report will unveil if Allgeier enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's contest at Dallas, and also whether or not rookie RB Jeremiyah Love has a chance to put an end to a two-game absence. Currently, Bam Knight is the only healthy backfield option on Arizona's active roster.

headline: Allgeier (toe) didn't practice Wednesday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Allgeier wasn't present for the media-access portion of Wednesday's session, and a toe injury was the reason for his absence. Fellow RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) returned to drills Wednesday as a limited participant, so question marks abound in the Cardinals backfield as the team kicks off Week 8 prep.

headline: Allgeier was not present during the portion of Wednesday's practice open to the media, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
story: It's unclear if Allgeier is dealing with a health concern or merely getting the day off, but Wednesday's practice report will reveal as much. Fellow RB Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is returning as a limited participant to begin Week 8 prep, throwing the Cardinals backfield in a bit of flux.

headline: Allgeier rushed eight times for 19 yards and caught all three of his targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 30-16 loss to the Broncos.
story: For a second consecutive game, Allgeier led the Cardinals in carries in the absence of Jeremiyah Love (ankle) but was far less efficient on the ground than Bam Knight. Allgeier has 57 rushing yards on 26 carries (2.2 YPC) during this two-game span compared to 128 rushing yards on 22 carries (5.8 YPC) for Knight over the same stretch. Love should reclaim his spot as the top option in Arizona's backfield once he's cleared to return, and even if that doesn't happen in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Allgeier could start to cede more opportunities to Knight if Allgeier remains inefficient.

headline: Allgeier and Bam Knight will be the Cardinals' top backs for Sunday's game against the Broncos due to the absence of Jeremiyah Love (ankle), Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
story: Love is set to miss a second consecutive game while working through a lingering ankle injury. Allgeier logged 18 carries in Week 6 against the Rams, but he turned that into only 38 yards while adding one catch (on two targets) for 10 yards. Knight, on the the other hand, was more efficient, turning 17 touches into 98 yards. It could be a 50-50 split in the Cardinals backfield for Sunday's contest against a Broncos defense that gives up 139.8 rushing yards per game, which is second-worst in the NFL behind the Cowboys (149.8).

headline: Allgeier rushed 18 times for 38 yards and caught one of two targets for 10 yards in Sunday's 18-16 win over the Rams.
story: Allgeier racked up 19 touches in the absence of Jeremiyah Love (ankle), but the former struggled to find running room and was outplayed by third-string running back Bam Knight, who turned 17 touches into 98 yards in Arizona's unlikely victory. Allgeier's season averaged dipped below 3.0 yards per carry with Sunday's inefficient outing. Love would likely reclaim the lead role if he returns in Week 7 against the Broncos, and Knight could also earn touches at Allgeier's expense moving forward in a crowded Cardinals backfield that may also welcome James Conner (foot) back from injured reserve in the coming weeks.

headline: Allgeier is poised for a leading role out of the Cardinals backfield Sunday at the Rams with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined in Week 6, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
story: Despite Love being active for each of the first five contests of the season, Allgeier's snap share ranged from 36 to 64 percent weekly, and he averaged 9.4 touches for 32.6 yards from scrimmage per game while scoring one rushing TD. The overall workload thus will increase with Love out, and Allgeier's primary competition for RB reps will be Bam Knight, who has just three carries in 2026.

headline: Allgeier rushed three times for seven yards and caught both of his targets for nine yards during Sunday's 45-21 loss to the Lions.
story: Allgeier was on the field for 32 offensive snaps, but he only had five touches in the contest. In comparison, rookie running back Jeremiyah Love turned 12 carries into 22 yards over his 34 offensive snaps in the defeat. Allgeier has rushed 35 times for 119 yards and a touchdown while reeling in all 12 of his targets for 44 yards over five contests this season, and he remains a valuable insurance policy for fantasy managers with Love on their roster.

headline: Allgeier rushed eight times for 42 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the Giants. He added two catches for seven yards on two targets.
story: After Jeremiyah Love appeared to distance himself from Allgeier in Week 3 against the 49ers, Allgeier ended up out-snapping the rookie running back against the Giants. Love out-carried Allgeier 14 to eight Sunday, but it was Allgeier who found the end zone with a 22-yard score in the first quarter to give Arizona a 14-3 lead. Through four games, Allgeier has rushed 32 times for 112 yards and a touchdown, adding 10 catches for 35 yards on 10 targets. Splitting time with Love, Allgeier is touchdown-or-bust fantasy option most weeks.

headline: Allgeier rushed twice for minus-1 yard and caught all four of his targets for 10 yards in the Cardinals' 36-30 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
story: Rookie first-round pick Jeremiyah Love worked as the clear lead back for the first time in his nascent career Sunday, relegating Allgeier to a minor role. Allgeier was thus limited to screen passes and checkdowns, catching everything thrown his way for minimal gains. It remains to be seen if Sunday's notable shift in workload will have carryover into a Week 4 road matchup against the Giants on Sunday.

story: Why Dopp is still in on 'target monster' Trey McBride

headline: How should fantasy managers handle Trey McBride?

headline: Is Trey McBride a sell-high candidate in fantasy?

headline: McBride caught nine of 14 targets for 54 yards in Sunday's 34-7 loss to Kansas City. He added four yards on his only carry.
story: Working with his fourth quarterback of the season in Josh Johnson, McBride dominated the 40-year-old's attention, as no other Cardinal got more than seven targets or hauled in more than four passes. The star tight end wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, as his longest gain went for a mere nine yards. Carson Beck (back) could be back under center in Week 12 against the Commanders, but that might not improve McBride's outlook, as he saw only five targets in Week 10 during the rookie QB's first NFL start.

headline: McBride tallied five catches on as many targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 34-6 loss to the Rams.
story: McBride's streak of at least seven catches ended at 11 games, and his receiving yardage total marked his second-fewest of the campaign in what doubled as rookie QB Carson Beck's first NFL start. Better days likely are ahead for the duo, but as McBride works with his third signal-caller this season -- and the least experienced one at that after Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew -- there may be more lows than highs for the tight end over the final seven contests. McBride will look to bounce back next Sunday at Kansas City.

headline: McBride recorded seven catches (on eight targets) for 54 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss at Seattle.
story: With QB Jacoby Brissett getting traded to Baltimore this past week, McBride was on the receiving end of passes from Gardner Minshew, and the result was the tight end's fourth-fewest receiving yards in a game this season and also the fourth time he didn't reach the end zone through nine contests. On a positive note, McBride extended his streak with at least seven receptions to 11 outings, which matches the second-longest streak in NFL history, trailing only the 14 Antonio Brown put together from 2014-2015. McBride may have a tough task on his hands next Sunday against the Rams' surging defense.

headline: McBride hauled in seven of eight targets for 72 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 33-30 overtime victory at Dallas.
story: The Cardinals offense experienced a QB change from Jacoby Brissett to Gardner Minshew late in the third quarter, but McBride was undeterred, extending his streak of seven-plus catches to eight consecutive contests to begin the season while also scoring his fifth TD of 2026 on a 14-yard connection with Minshew with 2:11 remaining in regulation. Overall, McBride has a 66-544-5 line on 86 targets just shy of the midpoint of the campaign, putting him on pace to surpass most of his career-high marks (126-1,239-11 on 169 targets) from a season ago. It's unclear who between Brissett and Minshew will be under center next Sunday at Seattle, but McBride and WR Michael Wilson (ribs), assuming the latter suits up, will be the top options in the passing game.

headline: McBride caught 10 of 13 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-16 loss to the Broncos.
story: McBride became the first tight end in NFL history to record 400 regular-season catches in his first five campaigns, bolstering his career total to 406 with 10 grabs Sunday. He scored Arizona's lone touchdown of the game on a seven-yard catch in the third quarter while setting season highs in catches and receiving yards. McBride has recorded at least seven receptions in all seven games this season while scoring four times heading into a Week 8 matchup with a weak Dallas pass defense.

headline: McBride caught seven of nine targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 18-16 win over the Rams.
story: McBride led the Cardinals in catches, receiving yards and targets as Arizona pulled off the upset on the back of six field goals. The star tight end led the NFL with 42 catches through five weeks and has at least seven receptions in every game this season. McBride is up to 49 catches for 361 yards and three touchdowns on 65 targets as the top option in the passing game for the Cardinals heading into a Week 7 home game against the Broncos.

headline: McBride brought in nine of 10 targets for 66 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals' 45-21 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
story: McBride was in the familiar position of leading the Cardinals in receptions and targets, and he was narrowly second to Kendrick Bourne in receiving yards. The star tight end's touchdown reception was also a thing of beauty despite the fact it came when the game was completely out of reach, as McBride somehow secured the pass inbounds after tapping it twice to himself while swarmed by two defenders. McBride already has three nine-catch tallies in the first five games of the season, and he's also opened the campaign with five consecutive double-digit target totals. McBride has amassed 42 receptions in 2026, putting him well on pace for a third straight 100-catch season heading into a Week 6 home matchup against the Rams next Sunday.

headline: McBride caught seven of 12 targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the Giants.
story: White the star tight end saw double-digit targets for a fourth straight game to begin the season, McBride couldn't turn the volume into meaningful production, with backup TE Elijah Higgins instead connecting with Jacoby Brissett on a two-yard score in the third quarter. McBride will carry a 33-242-2 line on a whopping 46 targets into a Week 5 clash at home with the Lions.

headline: Bergeron (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Bergeron has started all 10 games this season and played all 631 offensive snaps. It's unclear when he suffered the injury, but Kyle Hinton and Andrew Vorhees are options to replace Bergeron at left guard against Minnesota.

headline: Hellams (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
story: Hellams played a season-high 62 defensive snaps against the Chiefs in Week 10 and logged 11 tackles (seven solo) in the loss. He apparently suffered an injury in the contest and will miss his first game of the season. Hellams' main contributions have come on special teams.

headline: Hellams logged 11 tackles (seven solo) in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
story: Hellams racked up tackles in what ended up being a disastrous night for the Falcons' defense. It's typically not a good thing when your third-level defender has to make all the plays, but make them, Hellams did, saving several explosive plays from the Chiefs' offense from becoming house calls.

headline: Bowman (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Bowman was unable to participate in practice all week due to a hamstring injury that will sideline the second-year defensive back for the fourth time in the Falcons' last five games. Sydney Brown will operate in an elevated role in the secondary in the absence of Bowman, whose next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Lions on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Bowman is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
story: Bowman practiced fully all week and was eligible to return from a two-game absence with a hamstring injury, but per Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com, he was left off the roster "not for an injury or performance reason" but rather because of a "numbers game" involving other healthy players.

headline: Bowman was estimated as a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Bowman hasn't played since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 6 against Chicago. Now with a full practice, the 23-year-old is on track to play Sunday against the Bengals. The second-year pro has six tackles (five solo) and two pass deflections in four games this season.

headline: Bowman (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Bowman was initially tagged as questionable after stringing together consecutive limited practices Thursday and Friday. However, he hasn't progressed enough in his recovery from a hamstring injury to play Sunday, so he'll end up being sidelined for a second consecutive game. Sydney Brown figures to see an uptick in defensive snaps in the absence of Bowman, whose next chance to play is Week 9 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Bowman (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Bowman was removed from the Falcons' Week 6 loss against the Bears and did not return due to a hamstring injury, which also prevented him from practicing during Week 7 prep. His absence means Sydney Brown should see an uptick in defensive snaps during Sunday's contest, and Bowman's next chance to play is Week 8 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Bowman (hamstring) is doubtful to return to Sunday's game against Atlanta, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Bowman suffered a hamstring injury in the second half of Sunday's contest and is not expected to return. If Bowman can't get back on the field in Week 6, Dee Alford should fill most of the void the rest of the way.

headline: Daniels (Achilles) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Vikings, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Daniels has been working through an Achilles injury since October, but his full practice participation Friday was enough for the rookie fourth-rounder to avoid an injury tag for Week 12. He has accumulated 69 tackles (43 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including an interception) and one fumble recovery across 10 games.

headline: Daniels (Achilles) was limited during Thursday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Daniels has been dealing with an Achilles issue since late October, but is hasn't yet caused him to miss any games. With that in mind, unless he's suffered a setback, Daniels seems likely to suit up Sunday in Minnesota. He's had a solid rookie season, tallying 69 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, two defensed passes (including an interception) and one fumble recovery through 10 contests.

headline: Daniels (Achilles) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Daniels popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to an Achilles injury, but his full session Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's home game. The rookie fourth-rounder has accumulated 61 tackles (41 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

headline: Daniels (Achilles) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Daniels was also limited by an Achilles injury during the Thursday of Week 8 prep. He ultimately avoided an injury designation for that game against the Buccaneers and played without limitations in Week 9 against the Bengals as well. The rookie fourth-round pick's availability for Sunday's game against the Chiefs will be clarified on Friday's injury report.

headline: Daniels logged eight tackles (four solo) during Atlanta's loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
story: Daniels continues to produce for the Falcons, as he's now recorded seven or more tackles in five consecutive games. Across nine appearances this season, the 23-year-old has racked up 60 tackles (41 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception. He will look to maintain this level of production during the team's Week 10 matchup versus the Chiefs.

headline: Daniels (Achilles) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Daniels popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to an Achilles injury, but he was able to avoid an injury designation for Week 8 after logging a full session Friday. The rookie fourth-rounder has logged at least seven combined tackles in each of his last three outings, and through seven regular-season games he has accumulated 40 tackles (31 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception) and one fumble recovery.

headline: Daniels (Achilles) was limited in Thursday's practice, Will McFadden of the team's official site reports.
story: Daniels practiced in full Wednesday, though after being downgraded to limited Thursday, there is concern he won't be on the field in Week 8 versus Tampa Bay. The 23-year-old is coming off the best performance of his career in the Week 7 win over the 49ers, garnering 11 tackles (nine solo) and one interception. His services will be needed even more if Divine Deablo (forearm) can't suit up once again. However, if Deablo and Daniels are both sidelined, Harold Perkins, Christian Harris and Josh Woods would likely be more involved.

headline: Daniels recorded 11 tackles (nine solo), an interception and a fumble recovery Sunday in a 29-20 victory versus San Francisco.
story: That Daniels was even on the field Sunday was a victory in itself after he was carted off the field and transported to the hospital due to a neck injury one week prior. The talented rookie not only suited up against San Francisco, he was a central part of sending the 49ers to their first loss, as he led Atlanta in tackles and essentially sealed the win in the fourth quarter by intercepting Brock Purdy with less than three minutes remaining and then recovering a George Kittle fumble with less than a minute left. The memorable effort included Daniels' first career interception, first career recovered fumble and career-high single-game tackle tally.

headline: Daniels (neck) is active for Sunday's game against the 49ers,  Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Daniels has recovered from a scary neck injury that sent him to the hospital during the Week 6 showdown with the Bears. The linebacker has managed to recover in just one week and is all set to suit up next to Harold Perkins at inside linebacker for Sunday's game against the 49ers.

headline: Daniels (neck) is questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Daniels suffered a scary neck injury in Week 6 against the Bears, when he was stretchered off the field and transported to a local hospital. He was cleared to practice in Week 7 prep and ended up finishing with a FP-LP-FP log. Daniels is understandably not in the clear just yet, but he could be given the green light by medical staff once he goes through pregame warmups Sunday.

headline: Daniels (neck) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Daniels spent a night in the hospital after being carted off the field in the third quarter of the Falcons' Week 6 loss to the Bears. The linebacker has improved greatly since the collision and is already back to full participation in practice. If Daniels can continue to string full practices together, he should have no problem suiting up for Sunday's game against the 49ers.

headline: The Falcons announced after Sunday's 31-23 loss to the Bears that Daniels (neck) was alert and had movement in all his extremities after being carted off the field in the third quarter and transported to Grady Memorial Hospital.
story: The rookie linebacker will likely remain in the hospital overnight to receive further evaluation after exiting Sunday's game following a helmet-to-knee collision with the Bears' Colston Loveland. Daniels has recorded 29 tackles, a sack and a pass breakup through Atlanta's first six contests.

headline: Daniels won't return to Sunday's game against Chicago after being carted off the field in the third quarter due to a neck injury, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: After Daniels appeared to lay motionless for a few moments following a helmet-to-knee collision with the Bears' Colston Loveland, medical staff cut off the rookie linebacker's jersey and pads before transporting him off the field with a neck brace in place. Daniels recorded seven tackles prior to his departure.

headline: Daniels (Achilles) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Monday's game against the Saints, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Daniels popped up on Friday's injury report as a limited practice participant due to an Achilles issue, but he shed an injury designation for Week 4 after logging a full practice Saturday. The rookie fourth-rounder has 10 tackles (six solo) through the first three games of the regular season.

headline: Branch (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Minnesota, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Branch will join Jahan Dotson (hamstring) on the sidelines in Week 12. Drake London, Olamide Zaccheaus, Beaux Collins and Chris Blair are Atlanta's available options at wide receiver, while Zaccheaus and Khalil Herbert are the top candidates to handle punt and kickoff returns in Branch's absence. Branch's next opportunity to suit up will be Sunday, Dec. 6, against Detroit.

headline: Branch (hamstring) didn't participate in Wednesday's practice, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: After being sidelined for the Falcons' previous two games, Branch isn't yet back to full health coming out of a Week 11 bye. The Falcons will see what, if anything, Branch is able to do at practices Thursday and Friday before deciding whether he'll carry a designation into Sunday's game against the Vikings. The rookie third-round pick out of Georgia has been a regular presence on the Falcons' return units but hasn't seen much involvement on offense when healthy; he's recorded 10 catches for 64 yards on 12 targets through his first eight NFL appearances.

headline: Branch (hamstring) went through warmups during the media-viewing portion of Monday's unofficial practice session, Daniel Flick of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
story: It's unclear how much work Branch was able to get in Monday, but his presence alone opens the door for a Week 12 return. The Falcons will provide an official update on his status when they release their first injury report of the week Wednesday.

headline: Branch (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Branch missed a Week 9 loss to the Bengals and didn't practice this week. Olamide Zaccheaus and Chris Blair took on extra snaps in Branch's absence last week. The good news for Branch is that Atlanta has a bye coming up after Sunday's game.

headline: Branch (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
story: The rookie wideout was injured in the Week 8 loss to the Bucs and missed last Sunday's loss to the Bengals in Spain. Olamide Zaccheaus and Chris Blair picked up extra snaps behind Drake London and Jahan Dotson.

headline: Coach Kevin Stefanski noted Monday that Branch (hamstring) won't play Sunday against the Bengals, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: The same applies to LB Samson Ebukam, with Josh Kendall of The Athletic relaying via Stefanski that either or both of the injured players could face multi-game absences. Through eight games thus far, Branch has caught 10 of his 12 targets for 64 yards. In the 2026 third-rounder's looming absence, Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus will continue to lead Atlanta's WR corps, with Chris Blair in reserve.

headline: Branch (hamstring) was forced out Sunday's game against the Buccaneers with a hamstring injury, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Prior to that, Branch wasn't targeted in the contest. In his absence versus Tampa Bay, Drake London, Jahan Dotson, Olamide Zaccheaus and Chris Blair are available to handle Atlanta's WR duties.

headline: Branch brought in one of two targets for nine yards, logged an eight-yard carry and returned his lone kickoff for 61 yards during the Falcons' 29-20 win over the 49ers on Sunday.
story: Branch saw minimal usage offensively, but he made an impact early with a 61-yard kickoff return in the first quarter, with the Falcons' offense converting that opportunity into a 39-yard field goal five plays later. It was a solid bounce back from his Week 6 performance against the Chicago, when he lost two fumbles. The rookie third-rounder has a 10-64-0 line on 12 targets through seven regular-season games, and Branch's role will continue to be a complementary one while he's situated behind Drake London, Kyle Pitts and Bijan Robinson in the pecking order. The Falcons will hit the road for Week 8 against the Buccaneers on Nov. 1.

headline: Branch caught both of his targets for nine yards while adding 85 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 31-23 loss to Chicago.
story: Branch has now caught exactly two passes in three straight games, but he has only compiled 34 total yards on those receptions. The wide receiver is merely a depth option behind the likes of Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus, and he's much more valuable as a return specialist for Atlanta. On the season, Branch has reeled in nine of 10 targets for 55 yards over six contests so far.

headline: Branch caught both of his targets for 10 yards while also adding 65 kickoff-return yards and 25 yards as a punt returner during Monday night's 45-24 win over the Saints.
story: Branch garnered exactly two targets for the third game in a row as he played 13 snaps on offense. The wide receiver is primarily a special-teams asset, making him an unappealing fantasy option. As long as Drake London, Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus are available, Branch has little to no offensive upside.

headline: Smith (neck) is active for Sunday's game against the 49ers,  Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Smith missed the Falcons' Week 6 loss to the Bears due to a neck injury. The outside linebacker is set to suit up after a one-game absence. The veteran pass rusher's return will boost the rotational efficiency of the Falcons' defensive line as he goes in when Samson Ebukam or Cameron Thomas need to rest.

headline: Smith (neck) is questionable but expected to play against the 49ers on Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Smith earned the questionable tag for Week 7 after an LP-LP-FP practice log, but it looks like the veteran pass rusher will return from a one-game absence due to a neck injury. His return would give the Falcons a boost at the edge rusher position, especially if Samson Ebukam (hamstring) is not cleared to play.

headline: Smith (neck) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Smith opened the week with back-to-back limited practices before logging a full session Friday. He's working through a neck injury that forced him to be sidelined for Week 6 against the Bears, and his status for Sunday's contest may not be officially known until the Falcons announce their list of inactive players about 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. Smith's return would bolster the Falcons' depth at the edge rusher position behind Samson Ebukam (hamstring) and Cameron Thomas.

headline: Smith (neck) is active for Sunday's game against the Bears.
story: Smith was limited in Friday's practice with a neck injury after clearing concussion protocol Thursday. The outside linebacker seems to have recovered in time for Sunday's contest and is all set to suit up on the edge against the Bears.

headline: Smith (neck) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bears, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Smith cleared concussion protocol Thursday, but his practice reps have been limited by a neck issue. The veteran pass rusher will continue to get treatment over the weekend, but if he's not cleared to play Sunday, then Jared Ivey would be the lone rotational option behind starters Samson Ebukam and Cameron Thomas.

headline: Smith (neck) was a limited participant at practice Thursday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Smith's status on Atlanta's official injury report changed from "concussion/neck" to just "neck" Thursday, signaling he has cleared league concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's game versus the Bears. With that said, his availability for Week 6 is still up in the air due to the neck issue, and he may have to log a full practice Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Smith (concussion/neck) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Smith entered the league's concussion protocol during the Falcons' Week 4 win over the Saints on Monday. He drew the questionable tag after practicing in a limited capacity Friday, but it looks like he won't clear protocol before Sunday's game. Samson Ebukam (hamstring) is also listed as questionable, so Jared Ivey, Bralen Trice and Cameron Thomas are all in line for more defensive snaps against Baltimore. Smith's next chance to play is Week 6 against the Bears on Sunday, Oct. 18.

headline: Smith (concussion/neck) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site  reports.
story: Smith was a limited participant in Friday's practice as he continues to deal with a concussion he suffered in the Falcons' win over the Saints on Monday. The linebacker still needs to be cleared for full contact by an independent neurologist. If the 34-year-old still has concussion symptoms Saturday, he will not be able to suit up for Sunday's game.

headline: Smith (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Monday night's game against the Saints, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Smith exited the contest in the first quarter after being down on the field for several minutes. An independent neurologist ruled that the outside linebacker had sustained a concussion, and he will not be allowed to return to the game. Smith will now enter the league's five-step protocol, and his status for a Week 5 matchup against the Ravens on Sunday night will remain in question for the time being.

headline: Smith (neck) is being evaluated for a possible concussion and is questionable to return to Monday's game against the Saints, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Smith took a knee to the helmet early in the first quarter and was down on the field for several minutes, but the veteran pass rusher was able to jog off the field and into the blue medical tent. Cameron Thomas and Yasir Abdullah should both see more defensive snaps for as long as Smith is on the sidelines being evaluated by medical staff.

headline: Thomas and the Falcons agreed to a three-year extension worth up to $33 million Friday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: The extension means Thomas -- a third-round selection of the Cardinals in the 2022 NFL Draft -- will be under contract with the Falcons through the 2029 season. The fifth-year pro has stepped into a larger role defensively this year due to the absences of James Pearce (back) and Jalon Walker (knee, IR), the former of whom missed the first eight games of the 2026 campaign while serving a suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy. Thomas has accumulated 25 tackles (nine solo), including 2.0 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

headline: Dotson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Minnesota, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Coming off Atlanta's Week 11 bye, Dotson was a listed DNP on all three of the team's Week 12 practice reports due to a hamstring injury, which will force his first missed game of the season. With fellow WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring) also out Sunday, the Falcons' depth at the position is a bit thin behind Drake London and Olamide Zaccheaus, as Beaux Collins and Chris Blair are the other options on the active roster. As a result, Dylan Drummond, Antwane Wells and Vinny Anthony will be candidates to be brought up from the practice squad.

headline: Dotson (hamstring) wasn't spotted at practice Friday, Daniel Flick of the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
story: Dotson hasn't practiced all week, so it wouldn't be surprising if he's ultimately ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings once the Falcons release game designations Friday. Zachariah Branch (hamstring) also remained sidelined at Friday's practice, so Olamide Zaccheaus, Beaux Collins and Chris Blair may be Atlanta's only healthy and available wide receivers behind Drake London against Minnesota.

headline: Dotson (hamstring) did not participate in Thursday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: It's the second straight missed practice for Dotson, who is dealing with a hamstring issue. That's not a good sign ahead of Sunday's Week 12 clash against Minnesota, but Dotson will have one more chance to get on the practice field Friday. If he ends up being sidelined Sunday, Olamide Zaccheaus could take on a larger offensive snap share, as could Zachariah Branch, though he's also looking iffy to suit up due to a hamstring issue of his own.

headline: Dotson was a non-participant in Wednesday's practice due to a hamstring injury, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Dotson was a spectator for the Falcons' first Week 12 practice along with rookie Zachariah Branch (hamstring), making the activity of both receivers worth tracking the next two days to get a sense of whether either has a chance to play Sunday in Minnesota. Up until the Falcons' Week 11 bye, Dotson has been a picture of health during his first season in Atlanta, appearing in all 10 games while recording 19 receptions for 416 yards and two touchdowns on 39 targets.

headline: Dotson caught three passes for 63 yards on six targets in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Dotson has yet to hit 100 receiving yards in a game this season and has just two touchdowns, but he leads the league averaging 21.9 yards per catch, turning his 19 grabs into 416 yards through 10 games. He's fighting for leftover opportunities behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta's offense. Dotson isn't a reliable fantasy option down the stretch and headed into the Falcons' Week 11 bye.

headline: Dotson caught two passes for 16 yards on two targets in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.
story: Despite playing 84 percent of the offensive snaps, Dotson's two targets were a distant sixth on the team against Cincinnati. He has 16 catches for 33 yards and two touchdowns on 33 targets through nine games this season and isn't a particularly exciting fantasy option fighting for scraps behind Drake London, Bijan Robinson and Kyle Pitts in Atlanta.

headline: Dotson caught two of five targets for 95 yards during Sunday's 16-0 loss to Tampa Bay.
story: Dotson and the rest of the Falcons offense were held in check for the majority of Sunday's loss. The wide receiver did provide Atlanta's biggest highlight play of the day, connecting with quarterback Michael Penix for a 76-yard gain on the team's final possession of the day in the fourth quarter. Dotson's 95 yards were a season high, and he has now reeled in 14 of 31 targets for 337 yards and two touchdowns over eight contests to open the 2026 regular season.

headline: Dotson caught one pass on three targets for six yards during Sundays' 29-20 win over San Francisco.
story: Dotson's lone catch came late in the second quarter as part of a 14-play, 56-yard drive that ended with a 33-yard field goal by Nick Folk as time expired. Dotson also drew a defensive pass interference penalty late in the third quarter, but it was an otherwise quiet night for the fifth-year pro, whose 38 offensive snaps were second-most among Falcons wide receivers behind Drake London (55). Dotson has two catches or fewer in six of the first seven games of the regular season for a 12-242-2 line on 26 targets. The Falcons hit the road in Week 8 for an NFC South tilt against the Buccaneers, whose defense stifled Panthers QB Bryce Young in a Week 7 win for Tampa Bay.

headline: Dotson caught three of five targets for 87 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 31-23 loss to Chicago.
story: Dotson led the team in receiving yards, and his most notable moment of the game came in the second quarter when he connected with quarterback Michael Penix for a 13-yard touchdown. The wide receiver has now reeled in multiple passes in three straight contests, exceeding 50 receiving yards in each of those games, and he appears to have distanced himself as the team's No. 2 option behind Drake London at his position.

headline: Dotson caught two of four passes for 54 yards during the Falcons' 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens on Sunday.
story: Dotson was responsible for the Falcons' second-longest play of the game, when he connected with Michael Penix (ribs) on a 36-yard pass late in the second quarter that led to a five-yard touchdown pass from Penix to Kyle Pitts three players later. Dotson finished as the Falcons' second-leading receiver behind Drake London (118), though Dotson's four targets were fourth-most on Atlanta behind London (11), Bijan Robinson (seven) and Pitts (six). Dotson is up to an 8-149-1 receiving line on 18 targets through five regular-season games, although the scoring ceilings for the Falcons pass catchers would be lower if Tua Tagovailoa is under center instead of Penix for Week 6 against the Bears on Oct. 18.

headline: Dotson caught two of three passes for 54 yards and a touchdown during the Falcons' 45-24 win over the Saints on Monday.
story: Falcons running backs Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson were responsible for five of the team's six offensive touchdowns during Monday's blowout win, with the duo combining for 207 yards on 33 carries. Dotson was the only pass catcher to get in on the scoring action, with the fifth-year wideout connecting with Michael Penix on a 31-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter to extend Atlanta's lead to 38-17. It was Dotson's first touchdown since Week 8 of the 2025 season, and he's up to a 6-95-1 receiving line (on 14 targets) through the first four games of the 2026 regular season. Up next for the Falcons is a Week 5 home tilt against the Ravens, whose secondary could be without veteran outside cornerback Marlon Humphrey (calf).

headline: Pearce (back) practiced in full Thursday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Pearce was listed as a limited participant Wednesday but was able to practice without limitations one day later. As such, he should be good to go for Sunday's matchup in Minnesota.

headline: Pearce (back) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Pearce was dealing with a back injury in early November but has played in each of the Falcons' last two games. He has two more chances to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's road game against the Vikings.

headline: Pearce (back) is listed as active Sunday versus the Bengals in Madrid, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Pearce completed his eight-game suspension for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy this week, but after being listed as a full participant on the Falcons' first two Week 9 injury reports, he was limited by a back injury Friday and thus entered the weekend as questionable to play. With his status now clarified for Sunday's matchup, he seems likely to resume his role as one of Atlanta's top pass rushers, which equated to 10.5 sacks among his 26 tackles in 17 regular-season games as a first-round rookie in 2025.

headline: The Falcons listed Pearce (back) as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Pearce was reinstated by the NFL on Monday after serving an eight-game suspension. The 23-year-old is expected to play a big role at edge for the Falcons' defense but may be eased back into the lineup to start out.

headline: The NFL reinstated Pearce on Monday after he served his eight-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy, Darius Hayes of Sports Illustrated reports.
story: Pearce had to miss the first eight games of the season following an arrest back in February, but he's now back with the Falcons' active roster for Week 9. He projects to eventually play a big role on the edge during the second half of the campaign, but he might get eased back into things to start out.

headline: Deablo (forearm) was not listed on Wednesday's injury report, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo aggravated a forearm injury against the Bengals in Week 9, which prevented him from playing against the Chiefs in Week 10. He's had additional time to recover courtesy of the bye, and given his absence from Wednesday's injury report, Deablo is on track to play against the Vikings on Sunday.

headline: Deablo (forearm) was downgraded from doubtful to out Saturday ahead of Sunday's clash against Kansas City, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo suffered a forearm injury in Week 6 against Chicago and missed Atlanta's subsequent two games. He returned to face the Bengals last Sunday but apparently aggravated the issue, and he didn't practice Thursday or Friday this week. With Deablo now ruled out against the Chiefs, Harold Perkins should get a healthy dose of defensive snaps at linebacker.

headline: Deablo (forearm) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Deablo was cleared to return for Week 9 against the Bengals after missing the Falcons' two prior games due to a forearm injury. He may have aggravated the injury against Cincinnati, and he logged consecutive DNPs to end Week 10 prep. He hasn't been ruled out yet, but assuming Deablo doesn't play, Harold Perkins would be the top candidate to start alongside Kendal Daniels at inside linebacker.

headline: Deablo (forearm) is active for Sunday's game against the Bengals in Madrid, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Since suffering a forearm injury during a Week 6 loss to the Bears, Deablo has missed the last two contests, and while he capped Week 9 prep with a questionable designation, his full session Friday signaled that he was closing in on a return to action. With that confirmed, he's a good bet to retake one of the starting inside linebacker spots in the Falcons defense, despite Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins holding down the fort in Deablo's absence.

headline: The Falcons listed Deablo (forearm) as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo was a limited participant in practice both Wednesday and Thursday. The 28-year-old has missed back-to-back games after suffering a forearm injury in Week 6 against Chicago. The sixth-year pro has 30 tackles (15 solo) and one pass breakup in six games this season.

headline: Deablo (forearm) was considered to be a limited participant at the Falcons' walkthrough practice Wednesday, Tori McElhaney of the team's official website reports.
story: Deablo has missed back-to-back games while nursing a forearm injury that he suffered in Week 6 against Chicago. The linebacker's ability to be limited Wednesday is a step in the right direction, but he will have two more opportunities to log a full practice and move past the forearm issue before Sunday's contest versus the Bengals.

headline: Deablo (forearm) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo was initially tagged as questionable after ending Week 8 prep with consecutive limited practices. He'll end up missing a second straight game due to a forearm injury, and his next chance to suit up is Week 9 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 8. Harold Perkins is the top candidate to start alongside Kendal Daniels at inside linebacker in Deablo's absence.

headline: Deablo (forearm) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo ended Week 8 prep with back-to-back limited practices, and he has a chance to return from a one-game absence due to a forearm injury. If he's not cleared to play Sunday, then Harold Perkins would likely start alongside Kendal Daniels at inside linebacker.

headline: Deablo (forearm) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Will McFadden of the team's official site reports.
story: Deablo injured his forearm during the Week 6 loss to the Bears, which ultimately kept him off the field for Sunday's win over the 49ers. The 28-year-old didn't practice Wednesday, and while he was limited Thursday, he likely has more hurdles to clear before suiting up Sunday versus Tampa Bay. If Deablo can't get out there in Week 8, Harold Perkins and Kendal Daniels (Achilles) could be in line for more snaps.

headline: Deablo (forearm) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo has not practiced since sustaining a forearm injury in the Falcons' Week 6 loss to the Bears. The starting inside linebacker does not appear to have progressed in his recovery and will need to upgrade to at least limited participation by Friday's practice to have any chance of suiting up for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.

headline: Deablo (forearm) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo was held out of practice all week due to a forearm injury that he picked up in a Week 6 loss to Chicago. Harold Perkins and Josh Woods figure to be the top candidates to start alongside Kendal Daniels (neck) at inside linebacker in the absence of Deablo, whose next chance to play is Week 8 against Tampa Bay on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Deablo (arm) did not participate at the Falcons' practice Wednesday, Daniel Flick of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
story: Deablo suffered an arm injury in the first half of the team's 31-23 loss to the Bears in Week 6, and he was ultimately unable to return to action before the conclusion of the contest. The linebacker will have two more chances to return to practice before Sunday's contest against San Francisco.

headline: Deablo (arm) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Bears, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo exited the first half of Sunday's contest with an arm injury. The injury is severe enough to rule out the linebacker for the remainder of the contest, meaning the Falcons will need to turn to Harold Perkins at inside linebacker against this Bears offense.

headline: Deablo (arm) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bears, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo exited the first half of Sunday's contest with an arm injury. While the starter is absent, Harold Perkins is set to fill in at inside linebacker next to Kendal Daniels.

headline: Deablo (hamstring) was a full participant at practice Thursday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo was limited by a lingering hamstring injury at Wednesday's practice, but it appears he's now finally back up to full speed. He's on the fringe of IDP consideration in some formats going into Sunday's matchup versus the Bears.

headline: Deablo (hamstring) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo was able to play through his hamstring injury in Sunday's game versus the Ravens, but it still appears to be bothering him as Atlanta begins its preparations for Week 6. With that said, barring any setbacks, it still seems at this point that he's on track to play come Sunday versus the Bears.

headline: Deablo (hamstring) is active for Sunday night's game against the Ravens, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo was a limited participant in Friday's practice and was listed as questionable for Sunday night's game. The inside linebacker overcame his hamstring issue in time and is all set to suit up for Sunday Night Football next to fellow inside linebacker Kendal Daniels.

headline: Deablo (hamstring) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Ravens, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site  reports.
story: Deablo was a limited participant in Friday's practice with a hamstring injury. The linebacker played through the injury during the Falcons' blowout win over the Saints on Monday Night Football. Diablo played 81 percent of the Falcons' defensive snaps in the contest and will likely suit up for a similar snap share in Sunday's game against the Ravens.

headline: Deablo (hamstring) is active for Monday night's game against the Saints, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Deablo was limited throughout the Falcons' Week 4 prep and was listed as questionable ahead of Monday's contest, but his availability has now been confirmed. If Deablo were to suffer an in-game setback, Harold Perkins would be the next man up at linebacker for Atlanta.

headline: Deablo (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Saints, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: A hamstring injury limited Deablo's practice participation all week, so the sixth-year pro will have the questionable tag heading into Monday's NFC South showdown. Rookie sixth-rounder Harold Perkins would likely start next to Kendal Daniels at inside linebacker if Deablo is not cleared to play against New Orleans.

headline: Zaccheaus caught two of his four targets for 17 yards and returned five punts for 81 yards during Atlanta's loss Sunday versus the Chiefs.
story: Zaccheaus recorded a season-high 17 receiving yards during the loss while playing 29 snaps on offense and 14 on special teams. The 29-year-old has hauled in eight passes for 43 yards in addition to amassing 231 kick-return yards and 81 punt-return yards across nine games this season.

headline: Zaccheaus caught one of three targets for five yards during the Falcons' 34-17 loss to the Bengals on Sunday in Madrid. He also returned one kickoff for 28 yards and returned two punts for minus-three yards.
story: Zaccheaus briefly left Sunday's game and was evaluated for a possible concussion, but the veteran wide receiver was quickly cleared to return. He has only six catches (on 16 targets) for 26 yards through eight regular-season games, and he's caught one pass or zero in seven of those contests. Zaccheaus isn't a key piece in the Falcons' offense, and that's unlikely to change heading into Week 10 against the Chiefs on Nov. 15.

headline: Zaccheaus (head) has returned to Sunday's matchup against Cincinnati in Madrid, Spain, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Zaccheaus was pulled from the game in the third quarter to be evaluated for a concussion. He cleared protocol relatively quickly and returned during the same period. He'll try to help Atlanta's offense rally back from a fourth-quarter deficit.

headline: Zaccheaus is being evaluated for a possible concussion and is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bengals in Madrid, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Zaccheaus exited the third quarter of Sunday's international contest with a head injury. The wide receiver will be evaluated by one of the NFL's independent neurologists, and if he is deemed to have a concussion will be out for the remainder of the game. While Zaccheaus is absent, Chris Blair and Beaux Collins could see more snaps with the offense.

headline: Zaccheaus (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
story: Zaccheaus didn't play in the Week 7 meeting with the 49ers due to a shoulder injury. He was limited during practice throughout the week, though it wasn't enough to avoid a questionable designation for Sunday's divisional clash with Tampa Bay. While the wideout was in danger of missing this contest, he will avoid a second consecutive absence. Zaccheaus has only four catches (11 targets) for 17 yards in six regular-season games in 2026. He also holds a role on special teams as a return man.

headline: Zaccheaus (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Zaccheaus was limited in practice all week due to a shoulder injury, which prevented him from playing against the 49ers in Week 7. His status may not be officially known until approximately 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, when the Falcons announce their list of inactive players. Zachariah Branch would continue to operate in an elevated role both offensively and on special teams as a returner if Zaccheaus is held out for a second consecutive week.

headline: Zaccheaus (shoulder) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Will McFadden of the team's official site reports.
story: Zaccheaus didn't play in the 29-20 win over San Francisco on Sunday. While his limited participation in the Falcons' previous two practices is a positive sign, he still may be heading for an injury designation for the Week 8 meeting with Tampa Bay. The 29-year-old hasn't been overly involved this season, catching four passes (11 targets) for 17 yards. However, Zaccheaus plays a role as a return man on special teams, so if he's not cleared to play Sunday, Jahan Dotson and Zachariah Branch may see more action in that capacity, even more so if Brian Robinson (hamstring) is also unavailable.

headline: Zaccheaus (shoulder) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Zaccheaus continues his streak of limited practices from Week 7 prep into Week 8 prep. The wide receiver was inactive for the Falcons' Week 7 win over the 49ers despite logging three consecutive limited sessions. This contest shows Wednesday's participation level is nothing new and does not yet move the needle for Zaccheaus' potential to suit up Sunday against the Buccaneers.

headline: Zaccheaus (shoulder) is inactive for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Zaccheaus battled a shoulder injury throughout Week 7 prep, logging limited practice participation in all three sessions. The wide receiver ultimately lost the battle and will need additional time to recover from the injury, leaving Zachariah Branch as the Falcons' No. 3 wide receiver for Sunday's contest against the 49ers.

headline: Zaccheaus (shoulder) is trending toward not being available for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Zaccheaus was limited by a shoulder issue in all three practices of Week 7 prep. That earned him the questionable tag for Sunday's game, but it looks like the veteran wide receiver will miss his first game of the 2026 season. Zachariah Branch would take on a larger role offensively and on special teams as a returner if Zaccheaus is unable to play.

headline: Zaccheaus (shoulder) is questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Zaccheaus' practice reps were limited during Week 7 prep due to a shoulder issue, which he may have picked up during the Falcons' Week 6 loss to the Bears. If he cannot play Sunday, then rookie third-rounder Zachariah Branch would be in line for more work both on offense and on special teams as a returner, with running back Brian Robinson also in the mix for return duties.

headline: Zaccheaus (shoulder) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: It's the second straight limited practice to begin the week for Zaccheaus, who is dealing with a shoulder injury. He may need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid being tagged with a designation heading into the weekend. Zaccheaus had four catches on six targets through three weeks but hasn't caught any of his five targets over Atlanta's past three contests.

headline: Zaccheaus (shoulder) was a limited participant at the Falcons' practice Wednesday, Daniel Flick of The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
story: Zaccheaus appears to have picked up a shoulder injury during the team's 31-23 loss to the Bears in Week 6. The fact that he was able to practice in any capacity Wednesday would suggest that it is a minor issue, but the wide receiver will have two more chances to prove his health before Sunday's matchup with the 49ers.

headline: Zaccheaus failed to haul in his lone target during the Falcons' 45-24 win over the Saints on Monday.
story: The Falcons relied more heavily on the running game Monday, with Michael Penix attempting only 20 passes while Bijan Robinson and Brian Robinson combined for 203 yards and five touchdowns on 33 carries. That left few targets to go around for the Falcons' pass catchers, with none other than Drake London (six) seeing more than three targets from quarterback Michael Penix. Zaccheaus' 21 offensive snaps were third-most among Falcons wide receivers behind London (51) and Jahan Dotson (36). However, despite entering the season as the team's WR3, Zaccheaus has just four catches (on seven targets) for 17 yards through the first four games of the regular season, and rookie wideout Zachariah Branch has seemingly taken over as Atlanta's primary returner on kickoffs and special teams. Up next for the Falcons is a Week 5 home showdown against the Ravens.

headline: Herbert caught two of his three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 35-13 loss versus the Chiefs. He also returned six kickoffs for 168 yards.
story: Herbert was targeted three times for the second straight game in Week 10, but he continued to make a bigger impact on special teams. His first kickoff return of the day went for 39 yards to Atlanta's 45-yard line, but the offense promptly went three and out. He'll be hoping to keep up the momentum as a returner following the Falcons' bye in Week 11.

headline: Herbert carried the ball once for seven yards and caught two of his three targets for two yards during Atlanta's loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
story: Herbert continued to serve a limited role in his first game since being signed to the active roster from the practice squad, as he played just 11 snaps on offense and nine on special teams. With Brian Robinson (hamstring) set to miss at least another three games, Herbert will likely continue to serve as the team's backup running back behind Bijan Robinson.

headline: The Falcons signed Herbert from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday.
story: Herbert was elevated for both Week 7 and Week 8, turning six carries into 21 yards and two catches (on two targets) into 22 yards while also working as a kick returner. He could take on a bigger role Sunday versus Cincinnati and potentially beyond, as No. 2 RB Brian Robinson was placed on injured reserve Saturday due to a hamstring injury. That means Herbert is the Falcons' only healthy running back behind workhorse Bijan Robinson

headline: Herbert reverted to the Falcons' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: With Brian Robinson (hamstring) missing a second straight contest Sunday against the Bucs, Herbert played 10 offensive snaps behind Bijan Robinson's 43. Herbert carried the ball four times for 12 yards and caught his only target for three yards against Tampa Bay.

headline: The Falcons elevated Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Tori McElhaney of the team's official site reports.
story: Herbert will serve as the Falcons' RB2 behind Bijan Robinson for a second consecutive week due to the absence of Brian Robinson (hamstring). Herbert turned three touches into 28 yards against the 49ers in Week 7 and figures to see a similar workload Sunday against the Buccaneers, whose defense is second-best in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing running backs.

headline: Herbert reverted to the Falcons' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
