story: Herbert was elevated to the active roster for Sunday's 29-20 win against the 49ers, when he served as Bijan Robinson's backup due to the absence of Brian Robinson (hamstring). Herbert was on the field for only 11 of the Falcons' 68 snaps (16.2 percent), although he nearly nearly found the end zone early in the second half on a 19-yard catch but was ruled out of bounds just short of the goal line. The sixth-year running back added two carries for nine yards and turned two kickoff returns into 65 yards, and he could be elevated for Week 8 against the Buccaneers on Nov. 1 depending on the health of the Falcons' backfield.

headline: The Falcons elevated Herbert from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Tori McElhaney of the team's official site reports.
story: Herbert is set to suit up for his 2026 regular-season debut as the No. 2 running back behind Bijan Robinson for Sunday's game against the 49ers. The 28-year-old will take relief snaps in place of Brian Robinson (hamstring), who has been ruled out due to injury.

headline: After Brian Robinson (hamstring) was ruled out, Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said Friday that Herbert will be Bijan Robinson's backup against the 49ers on Sunday, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Herbert has been on the practice squad for the past month but will be elevated for RB2 duties against San Francisco. He carried the ball 16 times for 52 yards (3.3 YPC) across seven appearances with the Jets last season but hasn't been a productive rusher since 2023 with the Bears.

headline: Moody went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Moody was signed by the Falcons off the Ravens' practice squad Tuesday, and he was able to put together a perfect debut with the team in Week 10. The kicker converted a 28-yard field-goal try in the second quarter before later adding a 38-yard make in the fourth. With Atlanta's bye week in Week 11, Moody's next chance to build on Sunday's performance will come in Week 12 against the Vikings.

headline: The Falcons signed Moody off the Ravens' practice squad Tuesday, according to NFL reporter Jordan Schultz.
story: Atlanta will move on from Nick Folk and hand its kicking job to Moody, after Folk missed five field-goal and one extra-point attempts through the team's first nine games. Cut by Washington during the preseason, Moody caught on with the Ravens as a member of the practice squad shortly thereafter and made his 2026 debut in a loss to the Jaguars this past Thursday, when he converted a 53-yard field goal along with his lone point-after attempt. With Tyler Loop (groin) set to miss at least three more games, the Ravens will need to break in a new kicker in advance of Monday's game against the Chargers after losing Moody.

headline: Moody reverted to Baltimore's practice squad Friday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: Moody made his only field-goal try and converted his only extra-point attempt during Thursday's 33-10 loss versus the Jaguars. Regular starting kicker Tyler Loop (groin) is not eligible to return from injured reserve until after the Ravens' bye in Week 13, so the team is expected to either sign Moody to its active roster or elevate him again ahead of its Week 10 matchup versus the Chargers.

headline: Moody made his only field-goal attempt and his only extra-point try Thursday in a loss to Jacksonville.
story: Baltimore's offense struggled for most of the game, limiting Moody's opportunities. He did hit a 53-yard field goal in the first quarter and was good on the point-after attempt following Justice Hill's 65-yard rushing touchdown midway through the fourth. It was Moody's first appearance of 2026, as he was elevated to the active roster from the practice squad after Tyler Loop (groin) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday. Given his performance Thursday, Moody seems likely to retain his role as Baltimore's kicker for the team's Week 10 matchup against the Chargers.

headline: The Ravens elevated Moody from the practice squad for Thursday night's game against the Jaguars.
story: With Tyler Loop (groin) sent to injured reserve this week, Moody will handle kicking duties for Baltimore for the foreseeable future. With Joe Fagnano at the controls of the offense against Jacksonville, Moody is not an exciting fantasy bet.

headline: Head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Moody is on track to be elevated from the practice squad to handle kicking duties for the Ravens in Thursday's game against the Jaguars,  Sam Cohn of The Baltimore Sun reports.
story: According to Minter, Tyler Loop is a candidate to go on injured reserve after tending to a groin injury coming out of Sunday's loss to the Bills, so Moody is in line to fill in Thursday and quite possibly beyond. Moody most recently appeared in nine games in 2025 across stops with the 49ers, Bears and Commanders, converting 19 of 23 field-goal attempts and 15 of 16 extra-point attempts.

headline: Baltimore signed Moody to its practice squad Monday, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports.
story: Moody began the regular season on the Ravens' practice squad, but he was cut after Week 2, solidifying 2025 sixth-rounder Tyler Loop's position as the team's uncontested starting kicker. Loop missed his third field-goal try of the season during Sunday's game at Cleveland, and now Baltimore is bringing Moody back as competition, signaling Loop might be on the hot seat in the coming weeks.

headline: Hooper recorded an eight-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Hooper was on the field for just 11 of the Falcons' 72 offensive snaps, with his 15 percent share placing him comfortably behind Kyle Pitts (76 percent) and Charlie Woerner (44 percent) among Atlanta tight ends. The 32-year-old Hooper hasn't played more than half of the snaps in any of Atlanta's first 10 games and has turned in a 10-84-1 receiving line on 12 targets, a level of production that keeps him well off the fantasy radar.

headline: Hooper caught both of his targets for 21 yards in the Falcons' 29-20 win over the 49ers on Sunday.
story: Hooper played 29 offensive snaps and four special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The No. 3 tight end was utilized as a blocker and pass catcher but was outshined by No. 4 option Nick Muse, who caught a key touchdown as the team took down the undefeated 49ers.

headline: Hooper caught his only target for nine yards during Monday's 45-24 win at New Orleans.
story: The Falcons found little resistance on the ground in Week 4, rushing for 205 yards and five touchdowns as a team. This encouraged them to use their most capable blockers at tight end, and blocking specialist Nick Muse actually played more offensive snaps (17) than Hooper (12) for the first time this season. Hooper will hope to get more usage in a Week 5 matchup versus the Ravens.

headline: Head coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday that London was cleared of a concussion near the end of Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Chiefs, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: London was checked for a possible concussion in the fourth quarter of Week 10 action, but the result of the evaluation wasn't reported before the game concluded. Prior to his exit Sunday, he posted his third 100-yard game (109, to be exact) of the campaign on six catches and a season-high 12 targets. London will continue to operate as the Falcons' No. 1 WR after a Week 11 bye in the team's next game Sunday, Nov. 29, at Minnesota.

headline: London is being evaluated for a possible concussion during Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Before his departure late in the fourth quarter, London recorded six catches (on 12 targets) for 109 yards. If he's diagnosed with a concussion, he'll be subject to league protocol in order to gain clearance to play again, but the Falcons are on bye in Week 11, so he'll have plenty of time to recover for a Week 12 road matchup with the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: London caught all five of his targets for 68 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.
story: Cincinnati's secondary did a good job of limiting London's looks from Michael Penix, but the fifth-year wideout still led Atlanta in receiving yards, although Bijan Robinson caught one more pass and Charlie Woerner hauled in the QB's only touchdown. London has gotten only 11 targets over the last two games, turning them into a disappointing 6-76-0 line, and he could have a hard time breaking out in Week 10 against a stingy Kansas City secondary.

headline: London brought in one of six targets for eight yards in the Falcons' 16-0 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: Michael Penix was picked off four times by the Buccaneers' defense throughout the rainy afternoon while completing only 33.3 percent of his passes, so London's near career-worst numbers were a bit more understandable in that context. The talented wideout had come into the day with at least 62 receiving yards in five straight contests, and he should have a chance to bounce back when the Falcons face off with the Bengals in Madrid next Sunday.

headline: London (head) returned to Sunday's contest at Tampa Bay, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: London hit the sideline to be tested for a possible concussion but has since been cleared to return to the contest. He had no catches (on two targets) at the time of his exit in the middle of the first quarter.

headline: London is being evaluated for a possible concussion and is questionable to return to Sunday's game at Tampa Bay, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: QB Michael Penix was intercepted on a pass intended for London in the middle of the first quarter, after which the wide receiver hit the sidelines for the concussion check. London was sitting on no catches (on two targets) at the time of his departure.

headline: London secured seven of 10 targets for 66 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons' 29-20 win over the 49ers on Sunday.
story: London, who briefly exited Sunday's game for a concussion check, contributed team-high totals in receptions, receiving yardage and targets on the afternoon, and he added his first touchdown of the season on a 21-yard grab on the first play of the fourth quarter. While the 9.4 yards per reception he averaged Sunday represented a season low, London is still averaging a career-best 16.2 yards per grab and has three straight double-digit target tallies heading into a Week 8 road divisional clash against the Buccaneers next Sunday.

headline: London (head) was cleared to return to Sunday's game against the 49ers, Josh Kendall of The Athletic reports.
story: London was being evaluated for a concussion in the blue medical tent. However, it was a short time on the sidelines for the star wide receiver, who was quickly cleared to return in the third quarter.

headline: London brought in four of 10 targets for 62 yards in the Falcons' 31-23 loss to the Bears on Sunday. He also recorded a two-point conversion catch.
story: London finished second in both receptions and receiving yards on the afternoon for the Falcons, while also setting the pace in targets. The star wideout couldn't quite capitalize on a Bears defense that had proven beatable at times over the first five games of the season, and London ultimately equaled his second-lowest catch total of the campaign despite also tying his second-highest target tally. Irrespective of the inefficient performance, London will take a formidable 31-550-0 line on 47 targets into a Week 7 home showdown with the 49ers on Sunday.

headline: London caught seven of 11 targets for 118 yards in Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens.
story: London has recorded at least 96 receiving yards in three consecutive games since Michael Penix (ribs) made his season debut after missing the first two games of the season due to a knee injury, but Atlanta's top wideout is still searching for his first touchdown of the season. Penix sustained a rib injury late in the fourth quarter, and London had a 20-yard catch in overtime on a pass from Tua Tagovailoa, but Tagovailoa's next pass intended for London resulted in a game-losing interception. London should continue to lead Atlanta's passing game regardless of whom the Falcons start under center in Week 6 against the Bears.

headline: London brought in five of six targets for 96 yards in the Falcons' 45-24 win over the Saints on Monday night.
story: London set the pace for the Falcons' pass catchers for the second straight contest in all of receptions, receiving yards and targets, although his totals were appreciably more modest than the 9-194-0 line he'd produced on 10 targets in Week 3 against the Packers. Nevertheless, London and Michael Penix have quickly clicked during the latter's first two games of the season following his recovery from last year's ACL tear, and the talented receiver's prospects will therefore remain bright for a Week 5 home interconference showdown against the Ravens on Sunday night.

headline: The Falcons activated Williams (ankle) from injured reserve Wednesday, Tori McElhaney of the team's official site reports.
story: Williams was placed on IR before Atlanta's regular-season opener with an ankle injury, but he's now finally back to full strength following Week 9. Starting in Week 10, he projects to fill a depth role at tackle behind veteran Jake Matthews and offseason free-agent acquisition Jawaan Taylor.

headline: Williams (ankle), who remains on IR, has been ruled out for Sunday's clash against Cincinnati, Will McFadden of Atlanta's official site reports.
story: Williams was designated to return to practice Oct. 22 and logged a trio of full practices this week. However, the Falcons have elected against activating him ahead of Sunday's game. If Atlanta doesn't activate Williams by next Thursday, he'll be required to miss the remainder of the campaign.

headline: Williams (ankle) will remain on injured reserve and has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Tori McElhany of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Williams has been sidelined the entire regular season due to an ankle injury that he picked up in early September. He logged a trio of full practices during Week 8 prep, but he's not quite ready to return from IR, so his next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: The Falcons designated Williams (ankle) for return to practice from injured reserve Thursday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: Per Tori McElhaney of the team's official site, Williams was a limited participant at practice Thursday. The transaction opens a 21-day window during which Atlanta can take Williams off IR, after which he'd be required to stay there for the remainder of the campaign.

headline: Terrell (back/illness) is active for Sunday's game against Tampa Bay.
story: Terrell didn't play in Week 8 versus the 49ers, his first absence of the 2026 campaign. He practiced in a limited capacity during the week but still couldn't avoid a questionable designation for the divisional meeting with the Buccaneers. However, Terrell now has the green light to return from the one-game layoff, which will likely result in less work for C.J. Henderson (groin) and Mike Ford.

headline: Terrell (back/illness) is inactive against the 49ers on Sunday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Terrell was already listed as questionable due to a back injury, but he also picked up an illness Saturday, and the combination of ailments are enough for him to miss his first game of the season. A.J. Terrell was activated from injured reserve and figures to start at outside cornerback opposite Mike Hughes, with C.J. Henderson, Mike Ford and Robert Longerbeam all providing depth in the secondary.

headline: Terrell (back) is now recovering from an illness ahead of Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Terrell is still listed as questionable, but he now has to overcome an illness as well as a back injury in order to be available for Sunday's home contest. His potential absence would mean less depth in the secondary for the Falcons, although the team got reinforcements thanks to the activation of A.J. Terrell (groin) from injured reserve.

headline: Terrell (head) returned to Sunday's game against the Bears, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Terrell exited the contest to be evaluated for a right-side stinger and concussion. However, the rookie was cleared by team medical staff and returned to the game.

headline: Terrell (head) is questionable to return to Sunday's game versus Chicago, William McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Terrell not only suffered a right-side stinger but is also being evaluated for a concussion. With A.J. Terrell (groin) on injured reserve and C.J. Henderson (groin) ruled out, Mike Ford should see more snaps alongside Mike Hughes.

headline: Strand (coach's decision) is inactive as the emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Strand is the emergency third option behind Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa, while Andy Dalton (coach's decision) is a healthy scratch as he continues to learn the Falcons' offense. Strand will only enter Sunday's game against the 49ers if both Penix and Tagovailoa cannot continue due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Dalton is inactive for Sunday's game against the Chiefs but was designated as his team's emergency third quarterback.
story: Dalton remains the third option behind Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa. The "Red Rifle" will only enter Sunday's game if both Penix and Tagovailoa must exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Dalton is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bengals but was designated as his team's emergency third quarterback.
story: As was the case in Week 8, Dalton will not occupy a roster spot Sunday, but he will be permitted to play should both Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa be forced from the game and unable to return.

headline: Dalton is inactive for Sunday's game versus the Buccaneers, though he will be available as the team's emergency backup if necessary.
story: Dalton agreed to a deal with the Falcons in October. While the veteran signal-caller will be inactive for the Week 8 meeting against Tampa Bay, he will be eligible to play if Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Dalton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Dalton is a healthy scratch for Sunday's contest as he continues to ramp up his participation in the Falcons' offense. The quarterback joined the team after being cut by the Eagles on Oct. 9. Jack Strand (coach's decision) will be the inactive QB behind Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa for Week 7 against the 49ers.

headline: Head coach Kevin Stefanski said Wednesday that Dalton is in a "ramp-up period" and will be inactive for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Dalton was cut by the Eagles on Oct. 9, but it didn't take long for the veteran quarterback to find work with another team, as he signed with the Falcons on Monday. He's tracking toward being available for Week 8 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Nov. 1, and Dalton could supplant Tua Tagovailoa for Atlanta's backup role behind Michael Penix.

headline: Dalton agreed to a one-year contract with the Falcons on Monday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Per Schefter, Atlanta plans to release Cooper Rush to make room on the 53-man roster for Dalton, who will likely slot ahead of undrafted rookie Jack Strand but behind Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa on the depth chart at quarterback. While he was with the Eagles earlier this season, Dalton beat out Tanner McKee for the No. 2 job coming out of the preseason. However, he had dropped to third on the depth chart and was ultimately cut after throwing a red-zone interception in his lone pass attempt with the Eagles while briefly filing in for starter Jalen Hurts in a Week 3 loss to the Bears.

headline: The Eagles released Dalton on Friday, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: The move comes after Dalton was demoted to QB3 duties last Sunday against the Rams. The veteran opened the season as Jalen Hurts' backup but entered Week 3 against the Bears for four offensive snaps and tossed a back-breaking interception in the end zone on his lone pass attempt. Tanner McKee will serve as Philadelphia's QB2 moving forward.

headline: Dalton is expected to serve as the Eagles' No. 3 quarterback for Sunday's game against the Rams, while Tanner McKee moves up to second on the depth chart as the top backup to Jalen Hurts, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Dalton had been active ahead of McKee as the No. 2 quarterback for each of the Eagles' first three games of the season, but he didn't see any action until midway through the second quarter of Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears, when Hurts exited to get checked for a concussion. After three consecutive handoffs to Saquon Barkley got the Eagles to two-yard line to set up a third-and-goal, Dalton proceeded to throw a back-breaking interception in the end zone on his lone pass attempt before Hurts returned for the ensuing possession. The costly pick looks to have been enough to cost Dalton the No. 2 job, at least for one week.

headline: Penix completed 23 of 43 passes for 286 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and rushed four times for 29 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.
story: Penix struggled while the game was still in question, but he did manage to pad his stats some down the stretch as the Falcons unsuccessfully tried to overcome their deficit. Penix connected with eight different targets overall on the afternoon, and he ultimately finished with a season high in passing yards. Penix has now tossed six interceptions in the last three games, however, and he'll look to regroup during the Week 11 bye before tackling a difficult matchup against the Vikings on the road on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Penix completed 20 of 31 passes for 162 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 34-17 loss to Cincinnati. He added 50 rushing yards on three carries.
story: It looked like it would be a big day for the Falcons offense when Penix led his team to points on its first two drives. including a one-yard TD to Charlie Woerner, but Atlanta managed just seven more points over the final three quarters. The touchdown pass was Penix's 10th of the season, setting a new career high, but he's also been picked off five times in the last two games after throwing only one INT in his first five contests of 2026. He'll face a tough test in Week 10 against Kansas City.

headline: Penix completed eight of 24 passes for 125 yards with no touchdowns and four interceptions while rushing five times for 11 yards in the Falcons' 16-0 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.
story: Penix endured a career-worst all-around game in rainy conditions after coming into the afternoon with just one interception in his first five games. Only two of Penix's four picks led to Buccaneers points -- and just a pair of field goals at that -- but the Falcons defense was helpless against Tampa Bay's ground attack in the shutout. Sunday's conditions were a clear outlier, so Penix should be expected to bounce back across the pond in a Week 9 matchup against a vulnerable Bengals secondary next Sunday in Madrid.

headline: Penix completed 25 of 34 passes for 213 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions and added five carries for minus-1 yard in the Falcons' 29-20 win over the 49ers on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
story: Penix put together a solid, mistake-free effort that saw him toss a trio of touchdown passes for the second straight game. The 2024 first-round pick connected with Nick Muse (one yard), Kyle Pitts (five yards) and Drake London (21 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes, the latter two coming in the second half. Penix also completed over 71.0 percent of his passes for the third time in five games this season, and he'll take an excellent 9:1 TD:INT and 1,157 passing yards into a Week 8 road matchup against the Buccaneers next Sunday.

headline: Penix completed 19 of 33 passes for 225 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions while rushing once for one yard in the Falcons' 31-23 loss to the Bears on Sunday. He also threw two two-point conversion passes.
story: Penix and the Falcons faced a 28-7 deficit going into the fourth quarter, but he helped bring Atlanta back with 10- and five-yard scoring tosses to Kyle Pitts and subsequent two-point conversion passes to Zachariah Branch and Drake London, respectively. Penix also connected with Jahan Dotson for a 13-yard scoring strike in the later portion of the second quarter, and Sunday's game served as Penix's first multi-TD-pass effort of the season. The third-year signal-caller also visited the medical tent in the first quarter for an undisclosed issue, but Penix appears to be healthy heading into a Week 7 home showdown against the 49ers on Sunday.

headline: Penix (undisclosed) reentered Sunday's game versus the Bears, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Penix paid a visit to the sideline tent in the first quarter of Week 6 action, but after a spell on the bench he was able to check back into the contest. If Penix eventually does miss any snaps, Tua Tagovailoa is on hand to direct the Falcons offense.

headline: Penix (undisclosed) went to the medical tent during Sunday's game against the Bears, Will McFadden of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Penix was cleared to play in Week 6 after injuring his ribs near the end of a Week 5 overtime loss to the Ravens. The current health concern isn't known, but Tua Tagovailoa started warming up to replace Penix.

headline: Penix (ribs) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game against the Bears, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Thus, the rib injury that Penix suffered late in the fourth quarter of last Sunday's overtime loss to the Ravens is behind him. Through his three appearances this season, he's completed 52 of 77 passes (67.5 percent) for 719 yards, three touchdowns and one interception.

headline: Penix (ribs) practiced without limitations again Thursday, Daniel Flick of the Atlanta Journal-Constitution reports.
story: Penix has faced no limitations in Atlanta's first two practices ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears, suggesting that he's good to go after subbing out late in this past Sunday's overtime loss to the Ravens, in which Tua Tagovailoa threw the game-losing interception in OT. The Falcons have scored 34.3 points per game in Penix's three starts after averaging 8.0 PPG in the first two games of the season while Penix was wrapping up the rehab on his torn ACL.

headline: Penix (ribs) was a full practice participant Wednesday, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Penix suffered a rib injury late in the fourth quarter of this past Sunday's loss to the Ravens, which didn't allow him to take the field for the Falcons' only possession of overtime. Head coach Kevin Stefanski told Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com that Penix was slated to be limited at Wednesday's practice, but afterward the quarterback himself relayed to Josh Kendall of The Athletic that he "made every throw out there" and is "good to go this week." Penix's subsequent full listing indicates as much, and he'll remain Atlanta's starting quarterback for Sunday's contest against the Bears.

headline: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said that Penix (ribs) will practice Wednesday but will be limited in some fashion, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Penix was sidelined for the extra period of Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens due to the rib injury, which he sustained when he was sacked late in the fourth quarter. While Stefanski didn't go into any specifics regarding the extent of Penix's injury, the coach said that the 26-year-old quarterback should be on track to start this coming Sunday against the Bears "as long as everything goes accordingly" in practice this week, per Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site. Penix looks as though he'll be listed as limited on the Falcons' initial Week 6 injury report, but he'll likely be locked in for the start if he's able to practice fully Thursday and/or Friday.

headline: The Falcons have optimism that Penix's rib injury isn't overly serious and that he'll be available to play Sunday against the Bears, Jonathan Jones and Josh Kendall of The Athletic report.
story: Penix took a hard hit to his rib area late in the fourth quarter of this past Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Ravens and was unable to play in overtime. He relayed after the game that he didn't think his rib injury was a long-term concern, and the Falcons are keeping the door open for him to start in Week 6. Per Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com, head coach Kevin Stefanski said Monday that he didn't have any new information regarding the status of Penix and wouldn't get into any further specifics regarding X-rays or imaging performed on the quarterback's ribs. Stefanski added that he expects to have a better understanding of Penix's availability Wednesday, when the Falcons will hold their first practice of the week.

headline: Penix is scheduled to undergo an MRI on Monday after exiting Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens due to a rib injury, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Penix sustained the injury with 27 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter, when he took a hard sack from linebacker Tavius Robinson. After giving way to backup Tua Tagovailoa for one snap, Penix checked back into the contest for the next play and threw an incomplete pass on a third-and-six before the Falcons punted the ball away. Atlanta then listed Penix as questionable to return to the game, but Tagovailoa ended up directing the offense for the team's lone possession of overtime. Per Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com, Penix said that he likely would have been able to stay in the game if the Falcons had been on offense to begin overtime, but the pain in his ribs worsened during the Ravens' long touchdown drive to kick off the extra period. Penix is confident that his latest setback on the health front isn't a long-term concern, though the upcoming MRI will ultimately determine whether he has a realistic shot at playing in Week 6 against the Bears.

headline: Penix didn't return to Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens after sustaining a rib injury late in the fourth quarter, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.  He completed 19 of 32 passes for 240 yards and one touchdown while rushing twice for eight yards.
story: Penix was injured after taking a big hit on Atlanta's final possession of the fourth quarter. He came back into the game after missing one play and threw an incomplete pass to close out regulation before being listed as questionable to return for the extra period. He ultimately remained on the bench for overtime, with backup Tua Tagovailoa stepping in for Penix and throwing a game-ending interception on Atlanta's second offensive play of the extra session. The oft-injured Penix will try to overcome this latest setback before the Falcons host the Bears next Sunday.

headline: Penix completed 15 of 20 passes for 223 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions and rushed twice for minus-2 yards in the Falcons' 45-24 win over the Saints on Monday night.
story: Bijan Robinson helped stake the Falcons to a 14-0 lead after one quarter, so Penix immediately had some pressure off his shoulders in only his second start since returning from last year's ACL tear. However, the third-year signal-caller still looked very sharp when called upon, and he essentially left no doubt as to the outcome of the contest when he connected with Jahan Dotson for a 31-yard scoring strike with just under 10 minutes remaining in the contest. Penix spread the ball around to seven different targets overall, and he's now completed 73.3 percent of his passes heading into a Week 5 home showdown against the Ravens on Sunday night.

headline: Kyle Pitts Sr.'s Week 12 fantasy preview
story: Kyle Pitts Sr.'s Week 12 fantasy preview

headline: Pitts brought in four of five targets for 50 yards in the Falcons' 35-13 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: The veteran tight end had a slow start to the day before coming on when the Falcons went especially pass-heavy in the second half. Pitts' fumble, his first of the season, came with just over four minutes remaining in the game after the contest was out of reach, and his catch total was his highest since Week 7. Pitts remains a key complementary option in an Atlanta passing attack that's scuffled of late, and he'll look to bounce back after the Falcons emerge from a Week 11 bye with a Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Pitts caught three of five targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.
story: It was another quiet performance from Pitts, who hasn't reached 25 receiving yards in any of the last three games, and he had to watch backup tight end Charlie Woerner catch Michael Penix's only TD pass of the afternoon in the first quarter. Pitts will take a 25-220-4 line on 37 targets through nine contests into a Week 10 clash with Kansas City.

headline: Pitts caught two of five targets for six yards during Sunday's 16-0 loss to the Buccaneers.
story: Pitts was unable to make it four straight weeks with a touchdown, and he was held to two or fewer catches for the first time since Week 3 versus Green Bay. The tight end has exceeded 50 receiving yards just one time over eight contests to open the 2026 campaign, so fantasy managers are pretty reliant on him reaching the end zone. Pitts and the rest of the Falcons' offense will have a good chance to get back on track in Week 9 against the Bengals' inconsistent defense.

headline: Pitts brought in all five targets for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons' 29-20 win over the 49ers on Sunday.
story: Pitts tied for second in receptions and targets for the Falcons on the afternoon, but he averaged just 4.4 yards per catch. However, the veteran tight end did score for the third consecutive game, recording a five-yard touchdown catch with just under nine minutes remaining in the third quarter. Pitts' production will inevitably fluctuate week to week, but he's clearly established himself as a reliable red-zone target for Michael Penix heading into a Week 8 road matchup against the Buccaneers next Sunday.

headline: Pitts brought in five of seven targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons' 31-23 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
story: Pitts led the Falcons in receptions and was second and third in targets and receiving yards, respectively. The veteran tight end helped fuel an Atlanta comeback in the fourth quarter with touchdown grabs of 10 and five yards, his second and third scoring catches in the last two games. Pitts has also now posted back-to-back five-catch tallies as a Week 7 home matchup against the 49ers approaches Sunday.

headline: Pitts caught five of six targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens.
story: Pitts scored his first touchdown of the season on a five-yard reception in the second quarter. He has stirred to life after a painfully slow start, recording eight catches for 89 yards and a TD over the last two games after having just two catches for 20 yards through Week 3. Michael Penix sustained a rib injury late in the game, and while Tua Tagovailoa proceeded to throw the game-losing interception in overtime, it's worth noting that Pitts was Tagovailoa's primary target in the preseason. Atlanta's QB situation will bear monitoring ahead of a Week 6 home game against the Bears.

headline: Pitts secured all three targets for 47 yards in the Falcons' 45-24 win over the Saints on Monday night.
story: Pitts finished second in receptions and tied for runner-up status in targets on a night when Michael Penix didn't have to do an inordinate amount through the air thanks to the ground attack's exploits. Despite the relatively modest numbers, Pitts' final line was a vast improvement over his first three games of the season, when he'd mustered just a 2-20-0 line on six targets. Pitts' uptick in involvement could have some sticking power given his rapport with Penix, and the duo will look to continue clicking into a Week 5 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday night.

headline: Has Bijan Robinson had a disappointing fantasy season so far?
story: Has Bijan Robinson had a disappointing fantasy season so far?

headline: Robinson rushed 16 times for 71 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
story: The Falcons were down 14-3 by halftime and 21-3 doing into the final period, so Robinson's opportunities progressively dwindled due to game script. However, the star running back still averaged a solid 4.4 yards per carry and recorded his sixth rushing touchdown of the season on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter. Robinson has at least four receptions in three of the last four games, and he'll now have a Week 11 bye to rest up before a tough Week 12 road matchup against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Robinson carried the ball 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and caught six of seven targets for 47 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals.
story: Backup Khalil Herbert handled just three touches, as Robinson dominated the workload in the Atlanta backfield with his usual No. 2, Brian Robinson (hamstring), on the shelf. It was the first time since Week 4 that Bijan had reached the century mark in rushing yards, and also the first time since that game against the Saints he got into the end zone. Robinson will look to build upon this effort in Week 10 against Kansas City.

headline: Robinson rushed 19 times for 76 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Falcons' 16-0 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: It was a bizarre afternoon overall in very rainy conditions in Tampa Bay, and Robinson managed to salvage his day with a solid rushing yardage total. Robinson's tally on the ground was actually his best since Week 5, although his streak of games without a rushing touchdown extended to four. Robinson is still averaging 5.2 yards per carry on the season and now is up to 983 yards from scrimmage and five total touchdowns heading into next Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Bengals in Madrid.

headline: Robinson rushed 20 times for 63 yards and brought in all five targets for 59 yards in the Falcons' 29-20 win over the 49ers on Sunday.
story: As his rushing line suggests, Robinson was mostly held in check by a stout 49ers front. The All-Pro running back's longest run of the day went for only 12 yards, but Robinson did find a way to make up some of the fantasy production as a receiver. Robinson finished tied for second in receptions and targets while checking in as the runner-up in receiving yards for the Falcons on the afternoon, and his numbers in the first two categories were his second highest of the campaign. Robinson has seen a downturn in opportunity and production since rushing for 339 combined yards in Weeks 3 and 4, and he'll look to reverse that trend in a Week 8 road matchup against a tough Buccaneers run defense next Sunday.

headline: Robinson rushed nine times for 61 yards and brought in both targets for minus-8 yards in the Falcons' 31-23 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
story: While the final score wouldn't suggest it, the Falcons had to abandon the run fairly early Sunday, as the Bears already had a 21-7 lead at halftime before Atlanta made things somewhat interesting with a 16-point fourth quarter. Robinson therefore finished with his lowest rush attempt and rushing yardage totals of the season, although he did manage to average an impressive 6.8 yards per carry. Robinson may have an uphill battle to get back to a truly normal workload in Week 7 as well, as a high-powered 49ers offense that also has the ability to jump out to commanding leads comes to town next Sunday.

headline: Robinson rushed 17 times for 86 yards while catching four of seven targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 30-23 overtime loss to the Ravens.
story: Robinson was held without a touchdown after scoring four times over the previous two games, but he managed to top 100 scrimmage yards for the fourth time in five games. The star running back was far more effective than backup Brian Robinson, who also had four touchdowns over the previous two games but turned seven carries and one target into just 16 yards against the Ravens. Bijan has racked up 732 scrimmage yards and five total TDs heading into a Week 6 home game against the Bears. Michael Penix (ribs) was hurt late in Sunday night's loss to Baltimore, so it remains to be seen whether Penix or Tua Tagovailoa will start under center for Atlanta against Chicago.

headline: Robinson rushed 19 times for 145 yards and two touchdowns and brought in one of two targets for two yards in the Falcons' 45-24 win over the Saints on Monday night.
story: Fresh off a 194-yard, two-touchdown effort against the Packers that kicked off the Week 3 slate back on Sept. 24, a well-rested Robinson put together a very similar performance, albeit with a slight reduction in workload. Robinson set the tone just three plays into the contest, capping off the opening possession with a 59-yard touchdown run down the left side of the field. He came back just before the opening period ending with a four-yard scoring rush, and he then ceded three other red-zone opportunities in the second half to backfield mate Brian Robinson. Bijan already has 494 rushing yards and four touchdowns on the ground through his first four contests, and the switch to Michael Penix at quarterback has led to the star running back's top two efforts to date this season. Robinson next takes aim at a tough Ravens defense in a Week 5 home matchup Sunday night.

headline: Dexter (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the 49ers,  Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
story: Dexter sustained a hamstring injury during Friday's practice and was only able to log limited participation in the session. The defensive tackle appears capable of playing through the minor issue in Sunday's contest against the 49ers. The nose tackle may see a reduced share of defensive snaps as he manages the fresh injury, leaving Zach Harrison or LaCale London to pick up some additional opportunities on the Falcons' defensive line.

headline: Dexter (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers but is expected to be cleared to play, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Dexter popped up on Friday's injury report as a limited participant due to a hamstring injury. A mid-week injury typically isn't a good sign, but it looks like the fourth-year pro will suit up for Sunday's home tilt. He has 17 tackles (eight solo), including 1.5 sacks, and one pass defense through six regular-season games.

headline: The Falcons signed Dexter to a four-year, $78 million contract extension Wednesday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Atlanta acquired Dexter via a trade with the Bears back in August, and now the team will have him under contract through the 2030 season. Through three games in 2026, he has recorded seven tackles (two solo) including 0.5 sacks, and a pass defensed.

headline: Ioane (hand) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans.
story: Ioane popped up on Thursday's report as a limited practice participant due to a hand injury. He did not practice Friday, so the rookie first-rounder will observe Sunday's game from the sidelines, which leaves Ryan Neuzil and Emery Jones as the top options to start at right guard. Baltimore is on a bye for Week 13, so Ioane's next chance to suit up is Week 14 against Tampa Bay on Sunday, Dec. 13.

headline: Ioane (shoulder/knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Cordell Woodland of 105.7 The Fan Baltimore reports.
story: The offensive guard was limited during Wednesday's session. Ioane left Monday's loss to the Chargers with a shoulder injury and didn't return. The first-round pick out of Penn State has started all nine games he's played in this season.

headline: Ioane (shoulder/knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Ioane exited Monday's loss to the Chargers due to a shoulder injury and was unable to return to the contest. The rookie first-round pick showed enough improvement two days later to get back on the field in a limited capacity, which bodes well for his chances of playing Sunday against the Panthers.

headline: Ioane (shoulder) is questionable to return to Monday night's contest against the Chargers.
story: Ioane suffered a shoulder injury in the second half, and his status for the rest of the game is now up in the air. In his absence, Chuma Edoga has taken over as the Ravens' right guard versus Los Angeles.

headline: Ioane (knee) was a full participant at the Ravens' practice Tuesday.
story: Ioane is set to return to action Thursday night against the Jaguars after missing Week 8 with a sprained MCL in his right knee that he suffered in Week 7 against the Bengals. The 22-year-old will likely be back in his starting role at right guard versus Jacksonville.

headline: Ioane (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's battle against Buffalo.
story: Ioane suffered a sprained MCL in his right knee this past Sunday against Cincinnati. He did manage a pair of limited practices to end Week 8 prep, but that's not enough for him to suit up Sunday. The Ravens have a short week ahead -- they play Jacksonville next Thursday -- which makes it more challenging for Ioane to avoid missing multiple games.

headline: Ioane (knee) was a limited participant at the Ravens' practice Thursday.
story: Ioane suffered a sprained MCL in his right knee in Week 7 versus the Bengals, and he was initially expected to miss time. It now looks possible that he could be available as soon as this Sunday versus the Bills, but he will receive an official injury designation after Friday's final practice of the week.

headline: Ioane (knee) is expected to miss time after suffering an MCL sprain during Sunday's game versus the Bengals, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
story: Per Hensley, on the bright side, Ioane's injury is not believed to be a long-term issue. As of Tuesday, he has not been placed on the Ravens' injured reserve list. It's still not clear exactly how many games he'll have to sit out, but in the meantime, 2025 third-rounder Emory Jones figures to take over as Baltimore's starting right guard.

headline: Ioane (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Bengals.
story: Ioane exited the first quarter of Sunday's game with a knee injury. The rookie right guard's injury has been deemed too severe for him to return to the divisional contest against the Bengals, meaning Emery Jones will likely finish out the game with the Ravens' offensive line.

headline: Ioane (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bengals, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.
story: Ioane exited in the first quarter of Sunday's Week 7 game against the Bengals. The 22-year-old will be further evaluated to determine if he can return.

headline: Head coach Jesse Minter told reporters Friday that Humphrey (personal) will be available for Sunday's game against the Texans, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
story: Humphrey was benched for Week 11 against the Panthers following derogatory comments about the city of Baltimore on his podcast. The veteran cornerback will be available Sunday, but his role in the secondary is unclear and may not be known until the Ravens' defense takes the field for the first time. Humphrey has 40 tackles (23 solo), nine pass defenses, two forced fumbles and one fumble recovery across 10 games.

headline: Humphrey (personal) was back at practice Wednesday and was a full participant, Quentin Corpuel of the Ravens' official site reports.
story: Humphrey was a healthy inactive for Week 11 against the Panthers after making negative comments about the city of Baltimore on his podcast. It's unclear whether he'll play against the Texans on Sunday, with head coach Jesse Minter telling reporters Monday that the Ravens will make a decision about Humphrey's availability by the end of the week.

headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Humphrey has returned to the team's facility, but a decision hasn't been made regarding the defensive back's status for Sunday's game against the Texans, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
story: The Ravens sent Humphrey home Thursday and made him a healthy inactive for this past Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers after he made a negative comment about the city of Baltimore on his podcast. Though Humphrey is expected to be a full participant in practice throughout Week 12, Minter suggested that he'll determine at the end of the week whether he wants to make the 30-year-old cornerback available Sunday.

headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Humphrey won't play Sunday against the Panthers after the defensive back made a derogatory comment about the city of Baltimore in an episode of his podcast released Wednesday, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
story: Minter noted that after holding "internal conversations," he and the Ravens' brain trust decided to deactivate Humphrey for Week 11. Per Hensley, Humphrey acknowledged after Wednesday's practice that he regretted the comments he made in the podcast and issued an apology, so he's not expected to face any discipline beyond being held out of the matchup with the Panthers. Through the Ravens' first 10 games, Humphrey has tallied 40 tackles, nine pass breakups, two forced fumbles and one fumble recovery.

headline: Humphrey (calf/hamstring) is active for Sunday night's matchup with Atlanta.
story: Humphrey will ultimately be good to go for Week 5 after being limited at practice throughout the week with a pair of calf and hamstring injuries. The 30-year-old will operate as one of the team's starting cornerbacks against the Falcons' red-hot offense.

headline: Humphrey (calf/hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Humphrey was a limited participant in Friday's practice after logging DNPs in consecutive sessions to start Week 5 prep. The outside cornerback continues to deal with multiple injuries he sustained in the Ravens' Week 4 win over the Titans, and it is unclear if he will be able to overcome the issues in time for Sunday's contest.

headline: Humphrey (calf/hamstring) did not participate at the Ravens' practice Thursday.
story: Humphrey has missed back-to-back practices to open the week as he nurses a calf injury that he suffered in Week 4 against the Titans, as well as a hamstring injury. The cornerback will have one more chance to return to practice before Sunday night's matchup with Atlanta. If he is unavailable for the contest, Chidobe Awuzie would likely draw a start in his stead.

headline: Humphrey (calf) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Humphrey injured his calf in the first half, and the injury is severe enough for the veteran corner to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's game. Chidobe Awuzie will continue to operate in an elevated role defensively in Humphrey's absence.

headline: Humphrey (calf) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Humphrey exited in the first half of Sunday's game and is questionable to return. He had one solo tackle before exiting. Chidobe Awuzie will see more reps in his place.

headline: Madubuike (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Houston, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.
story: Madubuike is set to miss a second consecutive game due to a hamstring injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Chargers. With the Ravens on a bye for Week 13, the seventh-year defensive lineman's next opportunity to play is Week 14 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 13. Broderick Washington and Aeneas Peebles are both in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in Madubuike's absence.

headline: Madubuike (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
story: Madubuike was unable to play against the Panthers in Week 11 due to a hamstring injury that he sustained against the Chargers in Week 10. He would need to practice in at least a limited capacity over the next two days to have a realistic shot at playing against the Texans on Sunday.

headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter announced Friday that Madubuike (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's matchup against the Panthers.
story: Madubuike popped up on the injury report as a non-participant in back-to-back practices due to a hamstring injury. With the 29-year-old out, John Jenkins will likely see a higher snap count on defense. Madubuike has 22 tackles (12 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two pass deflections in eight regular-season games.

headline: Madubuike (hamstring) remained sidelined for Thursday's practice, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com reports.
story: Madubuike was injured in Monday night's loss to the Chargers and has logged back-to-back DNPs to open Week 11 prep work. Veteran John Jenkins would likely see a spike in defensive snaps if Madubuike is unable to play Sunday against the Panthers.

headline: Madubuike (hamstring) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
story: Madubuike sustained a hamstring injury during Monday's game versus the Chargers, and now his status for Week 11 is up in the air. He'll probably have to practice in some capacity Thursday or Friday to have a realistic chance of playing Sunday at Carolina.

headline: Madubuike (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of Monday night's contest against the Chargers.
story: Madubuike suffered a hamstring injury in the second half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end. In his absence, Broderick Washington is a top candidate to see an increase in workload on Baltimore's defensive line versus Los Angeles.

headline: Hawkins (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.
story: Hawkins' absence will extend to six games due to a knee injury that he sustained in a practice session during Week 7 prep. The Ravens are on a bye for Week 13, so perhaps the extra rest will be enough for Hawkins to be cleared to return for Week 14 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 13.

headline: Hawkins (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com reports.
story: Hawkins was held out of Wednesday's practice due to a lingering knee injury, which has prevented him from playing in each of the Ravens' last five games. However, a full session Friday could be enough for Hawkins to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

headline: Hawkins (knee) didn't participate in Wednesday's practice, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
story: Hawkins has missed the Ravens' last five games while recovering from a knee injury, and he was not cleared to return to practice Wednesday. He would have to log at least a limited session over the next two days to have a realistic chance of playing against the Texans on Sunday.

headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter announced Friday that Hawkins (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's matchup against the Panthers.
story: Hawkins was a limited participant throughout the practice week, but it isn't enough for him to return in Week 11. The 29-year-old will miss his fifth straight game due to a knee injury. K'Von Wallace will continue to take reps in Hawkins' place.

headline: Hawkins (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com reports.
story: Hawkins has missed the Ravens' last four games while working through a knee injury. He was able to log some limited practices during Week 10 prep, and if he can increase his practice participation over the next couple of days, then he would be on track to return for Week 11 against the Panthers on Sunday.

headline: Hawkins (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Chargers.
story: Head coach Jesse Minter ruled out the veteran safety for Monday Night Football following Saturday's practice. It will be the fourth consecutive absence for Hawkins, who is recovering from a knee injury, and that means K'Von Wallace will continue to see more snaps in the secondary. Hawkins' next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the Panthers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

headline: Hawkins (knee) was limited during Thursday's practice.
story: Hawkins missed the last three games due to a knee injury. While he practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, he likely has some hurdles to clear before getting the green light to suit up Monday night against the Chargers. If Hawkins can't play, K'Von Wallace should continue to see more snaps.

headline: Head coach Jesse Minter is "optimistic" Hawkins (knee) will return to practice this week, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com reports.
story: Hawkins has missed the last three games due to a knee injury. While he didn't practice last week, it appears there's a chance he will be back on the practice field ahead of the Week 10 meeting with the Chargers. However, that doesn't mean Hawkins will be ready to play, so K'Von Wallace might remain more involved.

headline: Hawkins (knee) is officially listed as out for Thursday's game versus the Jaguars, Ryan Mink of the Ravens' official site reports.
story: Hawkins was again unable to practice during the week, and he will be sidelined for his third consecutive game in Week 9 as he deals with a nagging knee injury. K'Von Wallace figures to continue to see increased reps in the secondary in Hawkins' stead.

headline: Hawkins (knee) was estimated as a non-participant on Monday's practice reports.
story: Hawkins has already missed the last two games, and now the Ravens are on a short week ahead of Thursday night's date with the Jaguars. K'Von Wallace will continue to see extra defensive snaps if Hamilton is unable to return for Week 9.

headline: Hawkins (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Buffalo.
story: Hawkins has missed six-straight practices due to a knee injury, which will result in him being sidelined for a second consecutive game. K'Von Wallace was the listed starter at safety alongside Malaki Starks in Week 7 against the Bengals, although Keyon Martin and Keondre Jackson are also in line for more defensive snaps in Hawkins' absence. Hawkins' next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Jaguars on Thursday.

headline: Hawkins (knee) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Hawkins has now been held out of four consecutive practices due to the knee issue and could be trending toward missing a second straight game Sunday in Buffalo. If Hawkins ends up being sidelined against the Bills, Keondre Jackson and K'Von Wallace would be in line for extra snaps alongside starting safety Malaki Starks.

headline: Hawkins (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Cordell Woodland of 105.7 The Fan Baltimore reports.
story: Hawkins popped up on Wednesday's practice report as a limited participant due to a knee injury, which prevented him from practicing each of the next two days. He won't play Sunday, and head coach Jesse Minter suggested Friday that Hawkins could be sidelined beyond Week 7. In Hawkins' absence, K'Von Wallace and Keondre Jackson figure to be the top candidates to start alongside Malaki Starks at safety.

headline: Hawkins (knee) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Hawkins popped up on the Ravens' injury report with a knee issue Wednesday, and he's now trending in the wrong direction ahead of a Week 7 matchup versus the Bengals. He'll likely have to return to practice in some capacity Friday to have a realistic chance of playing Sunday.

headline: Henry (concussion) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Texans, per Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio.
story: Henry has cleared concussion protocol after practicing without limitations Thursday and Friday. He'll try to help the Ravens snap a six-game losing streak Sunday against the Texans. Running room could be hard to come by against a stout Houston front that's allowing fewer than 100 rushing yards per game, though Henry has overcome more than his fair share of daunting matchups over the years.

headline: Henry (concussion) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice.
story: After logging a limited listing Wednesday, Henry's upgrade to 'full' Thursday has him trending in the right direction as Sunday's game against the Texans approaches. Either way, Friday's final injury report will dictate whether or not the Ravens' lead back carries an injury designation heading into the weekend.

headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said that Henry was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice after being placed back in concussion protocol, but the running back is expected to be available for Sunday's game against the Texans, Cordell Woodland of 105.7 The Fan Baltimore reports.
story: The Ravens had previously announced that Henry cleared the five-step protocol after being checked for a concussion late in Sunday's 35-33 loss to Carolina. However, Minter noted that the running back later had "a couple of small symptoms" crop up, resulting in him being subject to the protocol as the Ravens kicked off Week 12 prep, per Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic. The fact that Henry was able to practice in some fashion Wednesday indicates that he's already cleared a couple steps of the protocol, but he'll still need to upgrade to full activity and pass neurological tests before he's officially given the green light to play Sunday.

headline: Why this might be a good time for fantasy managers to trade Derrick Henry
story: Why this might be a good time for fantasy managers to trade Derrick Henry

headline: Henry cleared concussion protocol and was made available to the media following Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers, Giana Han of the Baltimore Banner reports.
story: Henry was checked for a concussion in the fourth quarter of the contest, but evidently passed all tests. Prior to his exit, Henry carried 13 times for 94 yards and a touchdown and hauled in four of his five targets for 17 yards. He also lost his second fumble of the season. Henry looks like he'll be ready to handle his normal role as the lead option out of the Baltimore backfield next Sunday against the Texans.

headline: Henry is being evaluated for a concussion during Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: Prior to his fourth-quarter exit and visit to the medical tent, Henry carried 13 times for 94 yards with a TD and caught four of his five targets for 17 yards. In his absence, Justice Hill and Rasheen Ali are next up for the Ravens' backfield touches versus Carolina.

headline: Henry rushed 10 times for 10 yards and two touchdowns and brought in all five targets for 10 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
story: Henry was surprisingly stymied by a Chargers defense that had surrendered 4.9 yards per carry on the road coming in. The Ravens also threw an atypically high 49 times in Jacoby Brissett's team debut, leaving Henry with season lows in carries and rushing yards. However, the bruising back salvaged his night with his ninth and 10th rushing touchdowns of the season, which came from two and one yard out, respectively. Henry now has failed to eclipse 58 rushing yards in five consecutive games, but with Brissett significantly reviving Baltimore's air attack in his first start, better days should be ahead for the former in short order, beginning with Sunday's Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

headline: The Ravens aren't expected to deal Henry before Tuesday's trade deadline, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: With Baltimore sitting at 4-5 and having lost its top two QBs in Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) for the foreseeable future and rest of the season, respectively, there has been speculation Henry may be available via trade, but the team has informed the running back that it doesn't intend to consider such a transaction. Instead, the Ravens have dealt for quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals to help stabilize the offense, which may help Henry end his streak being held under 100 yards rushing at four contests. Overall, Henry has racked up 689 yards and eight touchdowns on 175 carries for a career-low 3.9 YPC in his nine appearances in 2026.

headline: Henry rushed 17 times for 57 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night. He also completed one pass attempt for minus-3 yards.
story: With Joe Fagnano under center, the Jaguars unsurprisingly had the luxury of loading up to slow down Henry, and Jacksonville already came into the contest boasting an elite run defense to begin with. Henry therefore ran into a proverbial brick wall for most of the night, and he finished under 60 rushing yards for the fourth consecutive game. However, help is on the way, as impending trade acquisition Jacoby Brissett could be ready to make his first start for the Ravens as soon as a Week 10 home matchup against the Chargers on Monday night, Nov. 16.

headline: Henry rushed 11 times for 53 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for seven yards in the Ravens' 36-10 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
story: It was a nightmare of an afternoon for the Ravens offense, which lost both Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) during the first half and struggled to move the ball with emergency quarterback Joe Fagnano at the helm. Henry's rushing opportunities ultimately suffered as Baltimore's deficit grew, but he managed to punch in a two-yard touchdown run late in the first quarter before matters got out of hand. It's been a relatively rough three-game stretch for Henry following a 102-yard effort on the ground against the Falcons in Week 5, and with reports emerging Jackson will be placed on injured reserve, the talented back's best hope for reasonable game scripts for the foreseeable future lies in Huntley's ability to regain health.

headline: Henry rushed 17 times for 45 yards and brought in one of two target for four yards in the Ravens' 35-13 loss to the Bengals on Sunday.
story: Henry averaged below 3.5 yards per carry for the second consecutive game against a divisional opponent, and Sunday's inefficiency also dropped his season per-carry average under 4.0 (3.9). The bruising back does have seven rushing touchdowns on the season, but none have come within the last three games. Henry will look to bounce back to his usual level of production in a Week 8 road showdown against an improved Bills run defense next Sunday.

headline: Henry rushed 17 times for 58 yards and brought in his only target for two yards in the Ravens' 13-10 loss to the Browns on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Henry looked like he was on his way to one of his signature performances when he rattled off 11- and 17-yard gains on Baltimore's opening possession, but the veteran back found running room at a premium for most of the rest of the contest. Henry finished without a touchdown for the second straight game and tallied his lowest rushing yardage total of the campaign, while his early fourth-quarter fumble led to a Browns game-tying touchdown. Henry will aim to bounce back in a Week 7 home divisional matchup against the Bengals next Sunday.

headline: Henry rushed 24 times for 102 yards while catching one of two targets for an 18-yard touchdown in Sunday's 30-23 overtime win over the Falcons. He also ran in a two-point conversion.
story: Henry unsurprisingly worked as the focal point of Baltimore's offense in the absence of Lamar Jackson (ankle). The star running back pulled the Ravens within two points with his 18-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter. Baltimore's two-point conversion attempt after that touchdown failed, but Henry took matters into his own hands to convert a game-tying two-point conversion out of the wildcat formation with 40 seconds left in the fourth quarter. He then tacked on 32 rushing yards on Baltimore's touchdown drive in OT to top the century mark on the ground for the first time since Week 1. Henry has opened his 11th NFL season with a five-game touchdown streak, producing seven rushing touchdowns and one receiving score ahead of a Week 6 trip to Cleveland.

headline: Henry carried the ball 23 times for 73 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-18 win over the Titans. He also caught both his targets for six yards.
story: The star RB found the end zone for a fourth straight game to begin the season, rumbling in for a five-yard score on the Ravens' first possession. Henry already has seven rushing TDs, putting him firmly on pace for his ninth straight season in double digits, to go along with 374 rushing yards on 4.2 yards per carry. He'll look to extend his TD streak in in a Week 5 road trip to Atlanta.

headline: Green (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Green's practice reps were limited Wednesday due to a knee injury, but his full session Thursday puts him on track to play against the Texans on Sunday. The second-year edge rusher has accumulated 32 tackles (20 solo), including 7.5 sacks, across 11 regular-season games.

headline: Green (knee) was a limited participant during Wednesday's practice.
story: Green may have tweaked his knee during the Ravens' 35-33 loss to the Panthers in Week 11, when he recorded five tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks. He'll have two more opportunities to upgrade his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans. Green's 7.5 sacks through 11 regular-season games leads the Ravens and are 12th-most in the NFL.

headline: Green recorded five tackles (four solo) including 2.0 sacks during Sunday's 35-33 loss at Carolina.
story: Green continues to be a bright spot for a struggling Ravens team, and he logged two sacks for the second straight contest in Week 11. He might be worth IDP consideration in leagues that award a premium for sacks going into a Week 12 matchup at Houston.

headline: Green racked up six tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, in Monday's Week 10 loss to the Chargers.
story: Green's first sack came late in the second quarter, and he brought down Chargers QB Justin Herbert again early in the fourth. After registering 3.5 sacks in 17 regular-season games as a rookie last year, Green has already exceeded that mark with 5.5 sacks through 10 contests this season. His six total tackles in Week 10 also tied his career-high mark.

headline: Bateman (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com reports.
story: Bateman was limited in Wednesday's session due to a groin injury, but his full practice Thursday puts the sixth-year wide receiver on track to play against the Texans on Sunday. He hauled in his second touchdown of the year in a Week 11 loss to the Panthers and is up to a 25-403-2 receiving line on 42 targets through 11 regular-season games.

headline: Bateman (groin) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: The wideout was listed with a calf injury in practice last week, so this is a new issue for Bateman. He's mostly been running wind sprints for the Ravens this season, clearing out the underneath routes for Zay Flowers and the tight ends. Bateman is averaging 2.3 catches per game for 36.6 yards with two total touchdowns across 11 contests.

headline: Bateman recorded two catches for 67 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-33 loss to the Panthers.
story: The wideout's big play was a 52-yard touchdown strike from Jacoby Brissett in the first quarter. It was Bateman's first score since Week 2, and his 67 yards were his second-most in a game this season. Bateman has three or fewer catches in six straight contests and isn't someone to chase in fantasy ahead of next Sunday's date with the Texans.

headline: Bateman brought in three of five targets for 42 yards in the Ravens' 23-20 loss to the Chargers on Monday night.
story: Bateman put together a solid performance during his first opportunity to work with Jacoby Brissett, posting his best receiving yardage total since Week 5. The veteran wideout also recorded multiple receptions for the first time in three games, and two of his three catches went for first downs. Bateman seemed to lay a solid foundation with his new signal-caller, and he'll look to continue building on it in a Week 11 road matchup against the Panthers.

headline: Bateman (calf) was listed as a full participant on Friday's practice estimation.
story: After being limited at practice Thursday, the starting wideout is in line to face the Chargers on Monday night after being deemed 'FP' on Friday. While Bateman has turned in two consecutive one-catch efforts, there's a chance that working with the team's new QB Jacoby Brissett could spark some added production for the 2021 first-rounder while working alongside top WR Zay Flowers.

headline: Bateman (calf) was limited in practice Thursday.
story: Bateman now has two more opportunities to practice fully and thus avoid an injury designation prior to Monday night's game against the Chargers. The starting wideout is coming off back-to-back one-catch efforts, but he'll perhaps have an opportunity to bounce back against 0-8 Los Angeles, while working with a new QB in Jacoby Brissett.

headline: Bateman caught one of two targets for six yards in Thursday night's 33-10 loss to the Jaguars.
story: That's back-to-back one-catch games for Bateman with Joe Fagnano at quarterback for the Ravens. With Zay Flowers also healthy, Bateman has little fantasy appeal in season-long formats, though things could change when Jacoby Brissett takes over as Baltimore's starting quarterback in Week 10.

headline: Bateman caught one of three targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 36-10 loss to the Bills.
story: Bateman actually led the Ravens in receiving yards on a day in which three quarterbacks attempted passes for Baltimore. Since posting a 7-88-1 receiving line in Week 2 against the Saints, Bateman has totaled 12 grabs for 200 yards and no scores over his last six games. He has minimal fantasy appeal while Zay Flowers is healthy.

headline: Bateman caught two of four targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 35-13 loss to the Bengals.
story: Bateman was able to handle a full workload for the first time since Week 5 after dealing with a shoulder injury, and the wide receiver was on the field for 74 percent of the team's offensive snaps. He finished tied for third on the team in targets with running back Justice Hill and tight end Mark Andrews, and Bateman's 33 receiving yards ranked third. The wide receiver and the rest of the team's pass catchers would stand to see an increase in production if Lamar Jackson (ankle) is able to return to action in Week 8 versus Buffalo.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
story: A limited practice participant to begin the week after he exited this past Sunday's loss to the Browns due to the shoulder issue, Bateman cleared up any concern about his health by taking every rep during Thursday's session. While he'll be ready to play Sunday versus the Bengals, Bateman's standing as the No. 2 wideout on the depth chart behind Zay Flowers could be threatened after rookie Ja'Kobi Lane produced well in his return from injured reserve last week, logging four catches for 40 yards on five targets.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) was a limited practice participant Wednesday.
story: Per Jonas Shaffer of TheBaltimoreBanner.com, Bateman was sporting a no-contact jersey during the session, but his presence on the field in any capacity was a promising sign after he was unable to return to Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Browns. If he's able to take contact in practice at some point over the next two days, Bateman should be in good shape to play this weekend against the Bengals.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) is taking part in Wednesday's practice, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
story: Bateman sustained a shoulder injury during this past Sunday's loss at Cleveland and wasn't able to return. Head coach Jesse Minter told Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic on Monday that Bateman "should be OK," and the wide receiver's ability to mix into drills only days after the incident indicates he's trending in the right direction. Wednesday's practice report will reveal Bateman's activity level to begin Week 7 prep.

headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Monday that Bateman (shoulder) "should be OK" after exiting late in the second quarter of Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Browns, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports.
story: Listed on Ravens injury reports the past two weeks due to a shoulder issue, Bateman appeared to aggravate the injury late in the first half of Sunday's contest. He failed to haul in his lone target while running 11 routes in the game before the injury kept him out for the entire second half. Fortunately for Bateman, he seems to have avoided a major setback, but his practice activity over the next few days will likely determine whether he suits up next Sunday versus the Bengals. It's also worth noting that rookie Ja'Kobi Lane returned to action Sunday and saw five targets from Tyler Huntley.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) has been ruled out of Sunday's game in Cleveland.
story: Bateman appears to have aggravated the shoulder injury that bothered him during Week 6 prep. Now that it's confirmed Bateman won't return Sunday, he'll finish the contest with no catches (on one target). Ja'Kobi Lane, Devontez Walker and LaJohntay Wester are the Ravens' available wide receivers behind top option Zay Flowers.

headline: Bateman sustained a shoulder injury during Sunday's game at Cleveland, Brian Wacker of The Baltimore Sun reports.
story: Bateman tended to a shoulder injury during Week 6 prep, as he logged an LP/DNP/FP practice regimen. His listing Sunday indicates he aggravated the issue, which has left him questionable to return. Bateman didn't haul in his only target before exiting late in the first half.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Cleveland.
story: A full practice Friday erases the concern about Bateman's shoulder injury, whereas QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) still isn't practicing and won't play this week.

headline: Bateman (shoulder) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Head coach Jesse Minter told Jamison Hensley of ESPN.com on Wednesday that Bateman "should be fine" for Sunday's game against the Browns, but it's unclear if the Ravens remain as confident in the wideout's health a day later.
