story: Bills capitalize on blocked punt with winning FG as time expires

headline: Bass went 4-for-5 on field-goal tries and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
story: Bass was able to make at least three field goals for the fifth time in the team's last six contests. The kicker made field goals from 43 and 54 yards in the first half before adding makes from 40 and 28 yards in the fourth quarter. His lone miss of the day came in the third quarter, when he pulled a 54-yard try wide left, registering his first missed field-goal try of the year. Bass has now gone 24-for-25 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-5 from 50-plus yards, over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Bass made his sole field-goal attempt and all four PATs in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
story: Bass made a 37-yard field goal in the second quarter of Sunday's contest. The kicker continues his perfect streak, having made all 20 of his field-goal attempts so far in 2026, with three such conversions coming from beyond 50 yards.

headline: Bass connected on all three of his field-goal attempts and made both of his extra-point tries during the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday.
story: Bass opened Monday's scoring with a 39-yard field goal in the first quarter before converting on kicks from 25 and 52 yards in the second half. All three of his 50-plus yard field goals this season have come over his last two outings, and he's made all 19 of his field-goal attempts and 23 of 25 PAT's through eight regular-season games. Bass's scoring floor is one of the highest in the NFL given the Bills' juggernaut offense led by MVP candidate Josh Allen. They'll hit the road for Week 10 in an AFC East tilt against the Jets on Nov. 15.

headline: Bass made all three of his field-goal attempts as well as three PATs in the Bills' 36-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
story: Bass converted multiple long-range field goals for the Bills after the offense stalled several times due to drops. The kicker succeeded from 56 yards, 22 yards and 51 yards in the contest. Bass has converted all 16 of his field-goal attempts and is 21-for-23 on PATs through seven games this season.

headline: Bass converted all four of his field-goal attempts and all three of his extra-point tries during Buffalo's win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Bass was dominant during the victory, as he was perfect on all of his kicks. The 29-year-old continues to have a strong season, as he has missed just two kicks (both PATs) across his first six appearances.

headline: Bass went 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 29-26 loss to the Patriots.
story: Bass made multiple field goals in a contest for the first time since Week 1, converting a 27-yard attempt in the second quarter before adding a 38-yarder in the fourth quarter. The kicker has yet to attempt a kick from 50-plus yards this season, but he has has gone a perfect 6-for-6 on field-goal tries over the first four contests of the year.

headline: Davis turned four carries into six yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned three kickoffs for 71 yards during Buffalo's 13-10 win over Kansas City on Thursday.
story: The rain and wind limited the Bills' passing attack Thursday, and three of Davis' carries came in the first half. However, James Cook dominated the backfield touches with 32 carries for 117 yards (3.7 YPC) and a touchdown. Cook is clearly the RB1 in Buffalo, but if he were to ever miss time, then more opportunities would be available for both Davis and Ty Johnson. Davis has 21 carries for 61 yards (2.9 YPC) and four catches (on seven targets) for 46 yards through 11 regular-season games.

headline: Davis rushed one time for three yards and caught a six-yard pass on two targets in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
story: Even with the Bills having a quick Week 12 turnaround ahead of Thursday night's game against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving, Buffalo rode James Cook and handed him 22 carries rather than spelling him a little more ahead of a short week. Davis has handled 17 carries across 10 games this season, turning them into a measly 55 yards and no touchdowns. His only fantasy value is being Cook's backup.

headline: Davis (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: The backup running back was managed during the practice week but is good to go for his normal role behind lead back James Cook. With the Bills listed as 16.5-point favorites, Davis could see some extra reps in garbage time if Buffalo does indeed blow out Miami.

headline: Davis (hamstring) remained limited in Thursday's practice.
story: It's a new injury for the running back, which clouds his status for Week 11 against the Dolphins. If Davis is unable to handle his normal handful of snaps, Frank Gore could be elevated from the practice squad.

headline: Davis was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a hamstring injury.
story: Davis is making his first appearance on the injury report since Week 8, when he missed a practice due to an illness. Unless the hamstring issue was something that resulted in him exiting Wednesday's session early, Davis should still have decent odds of being ready to play Sunday against the Dolphins. The third-year back has seen limited playing time behind James Cook and Ty Johnson this season, earning no more than six touches in any of his nine appearances to date.

headline: Davis rushed three times for eight yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
story: Davis has been held to single-digit rushing yards in eight of nine games this season and has now managed to rush for just 52 empty yards on 16 carries for the season. He's nothing more than a bench stash in fantasy should something happen to James Cook.

headline: Davis logged two carries for two yards and didn't catch his only target Monday in a 23-6 victory against the Vikings.
story: Davis continues to be sparsely utilized on offense -- he has two or fewer touches in six of eight contests so far this season. He's pretty solidly stuck in Buffalo's No. 3 RB role, behind James Cook (who logged a Herculean 31 totes Monday) and Ty Johnson (who notched just three touches). That will make Davis a poor fantasy play in Week 10 despite going up against a Jets defense that has struggled against the run this season.

headline: Davis rushed six times for 30 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.
story: With the Bills throttling the Ravens and James Cook suffering a neck injury late in the game, Davis got some added run in the fourth quarter. If Cook misses any time, Davis would be the likely early-down replacement, with Ty Johnson sticking to his role on passing downs and four- and two-minute situations.

headline: Davis (illness) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: After sitting out practice Thursday, Davis practiced fully Friday and will assume his normal role as the Bills' RB3 behind James Cook and passing-down back Ty Johnson. Davis has rushed five times for 12 yards this season and holds only contingent value in fantasy in the case something happens to Cook.

headline: Davis didn't participate in Thursday's practice due to an illness, Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard reports.
story: Davis received the day off while he was feeling under the weather, but so long as he's able to get back on the practice field Friday, he should avoid taking a designation into Sunday's game against the Ravens. While handling a backup role behind lead back James Cook this season, Davis has carried just five times for 12 yards to go with three receptions for 40 yards through Buffalo's first six contests.

headline: Davis logged a four-yard carry and a five-yard catch on his lone target while returning three kickoffs for 85 yards during the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Davis made his impact felt early with a 40-yard return on the game's opening kickoff, which set the Bills offense up at midfield and led to a 44-yard field goal by Tyler Bass nine plays later. Both of Davis' touches on offense came on back-to-back plays in the second quarter, and his nine offensive snaps were behind both Ty Johnson (12) and James Cook (45). Davis isn't much of a factor offensively, but he would be in line for a larger role if one or both of Cook and Johnson miss time. The Bills will enjoy their bye week before hosting the Ravens in Week 8 on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Davis caught his lone target for 31 yards while adding two carries for two yards and three kickoff returns for 114 yards during the Bills' 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday.
story: Davis opened Monday's contest in style with a 70-yard return on the opening kickoff that set the Bills up deep in Rams territory, though the Rams defense forced a three-and-out and Buffalo had to settle for a 49-yard field goal. Davis made another big contribution early in the fourth quarter, when he turned a screen pass into a 31-yard gain before being tackled just short of the goal line, which led to a one-yard touchdown run by Josh Allen on the next play. Davis has been limited mostly to work on special teams while mixing in occasionally in the back field. That said, Davis and Ty Johnson could both be in the mix for more offensive touches, given that head coach Joe Brady said Tuesday that "...at some point there has to be consequences" in reference to James Cook's fumble issues this season, per Nick Suss of ESPN.com. The Bills will stay on the road for Week 6 against the Raiders on Oct. 18.

headline: Davis logged a four-yard carry, a three-yard reception and returned one kickoff for 29 yards during the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots in Week 4.
story: Both of Davis' offensive outputs came on back-to-back plays early in the second quarter, and his four snaps on offense were well behind starter James Cook (35) and backup Ty Johnson (19). Even as a returner, Davis took a back seat to Greg Dortch, the latter of whom returned four kickoffs for 91 yards and two punts for 16 yards. Davis' production on offense and special teams will continue to be limited unless one of Cook, Johnson or Dortch were to miss time.

headline: Davis (hamstring) is expected to play against the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Davis was questionable heading into Sunday's game after participating as a limited participant in Friday's practice. The 26-year-old has one rushing attempt through three regular-season games for three yards.

headline: Davis (hamstring) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Davis popped up on the injury report Thursday as a full participant, which would suggest he was possibly injured at the end of that practice. If Davis is unable to play in Week 4, Ty Johnson and Frank Gore will likely handle the backup duties behind James Cook.

headline: Johnson grabbed both of his targets for 12 yards during the Bills' 13-10 win over the Chiefs on Thursday.
story: Despite the rain and wind, Johnson was limited to a pass-catching role Thursday, with James Cook and Ray Davis combining for 36 of the Bills' 43 carries. Through nine regular-season games, Johnson has caught 27 passes (on 28 targets) for 281 yards and turned eight carries into 13 yards (1.6 YPC). The 2019 sixth-rounder is unlikely to log many rushes this season unless one of Cook or Davis were to miss time.

headline: Johnson rushed once for two yards and caught seven of his eight targets for 55 yards in the Bills' 26-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Johnson did not carry the rock much at all in the contest. The running back did, however, rank third in receiving yards for Buffalo behind Khalil Shakir (101) and DJ Moore (91). Johnson should continue to see receiving opportunities in Week 12 against the Chiefs as the Bills' preferred third-down back.

headline: Johnson caught his only target for four yards in a 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
story: For the third time in seven appearances this season, Johnson didn't log a single carry. The veteran running back also didn't have much of a role in the passing game with just one target. In fact, Johnson tallied just 10 offensive snaps, finishing behind both starter James Cook (35) and fellow backup Ray Davis (12). Johnson has had a few productive performances as a pass catcher this season, but his role is too unpredictable to warrant weekly fantasy consideration.

headline: Johnson rushed once for one yard and caught both of his targets for 36 yards against the Vikings in a 23-6 victory Monday.
story: Johnson got just one carry while workhorse No. 1 RB James Cook logged a hearty 31 totes. However, Johnson made one big play as a receiver, hauling in a 36-yard reception on a third-down play early in the third quarter to bring Buffalo into Vikings territory. While Johnson has been nearly invisible as a ball carrier this season, he's been effective in a pass-catching role, racking up 210 yards on 17 catches through six games.

headline: Johnson (illness) was a full practice participant Friday.
story: A quick return after Thursday's absence confirms Johnson isn't dealing with a serious illness. He should be fine for his usual role on passing downs Monday night at Minnesota.

headline: Johnson (illness) did not practice Thursday.
story: Johnson will have an extra day to rest up this week, as the Bills host the Vikings on Monday night. Buffalo's preferred pass-catching back, Johnson has rushed six times for just 10 yards through six games this season, but he has caught all 15 of his targets for 174 yards.

headline: Johnson took four carries for four yards and caught all three of his targets for 19 yards during Sunday's 36-10 win versus the Ravens.
story: In a game that Buffalo ran away with in the second half, Johnson's four carries were a season high, but he couldn't produce much on those rush attempts. Ray Davis actually saw more carries (six) in Week 8 and was more effective as a rusher (30 yards). As long as lead back James Cook is available, Johnson won't have much utility in most fantasy formats.

headline: Johnson logged a three-yard carry and caught both of his targets for 24 yards during the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Johnson and Ray Davis each saw only one carry during Sunday's win, with lead back James Cook turning 22 carries into 95 yards and a touchdown. Johnson was still involved somewhat in the passing game, and through four games he has 12 catches on as many targets for 155 yards. The veteran running back will continue to operate in a rotational role on offense, but his workload would expand significantly if Cook ever misses time. The Bills are on a bye for Week 7, and their next game will take place in Week 8 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Johnson (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Las Vegas, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Johnson was a new addition to the injury report this week, listed as limited Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full participation Friday. He made a big impact in the Week 5 win at Los Angeles, catching each of his four targets for 72 yards across just 14 snaps (21.9 percent snap share).

headline: Johnson (hamstring) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: Johnson popped up on the Bills' injury report with a hamstring issue Wednesday, and it was still bothering him at practice Thursday. Whether he ends up carrying an injury designation into the weekend might depend on his activity Friday, which will be his last chance to practice ahead of Sunday's game at Las Vegas. If he can go in Week 6, he'll be looking to build off the four-catch, 72-yard performance he managed in Week 5 against the Rams.

headline: Johnson (hamstring) was considered limited at the Bills' walkthrough practice Wednesday.
story: Johnson reeled in all four of his targets for 72 yards during Monday night's 37-34 overtime win against the Rams, but he may have picked up a hamstring injury in the process. The running back's ability to be limited Wednesday is a positive sign, and he'll have two more chances to log a full practice and erase any concern about his availability for Sunday's contest versus Las Vegas.

headline: Johnson caught all four of his targets for 72 yards during the Bills' 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday.
story: Johnson played only 14 of the Bills' 64 offensive snaps (21.9 percent) and didn't log a single carry. However, the veteran running back made his snaps count as a receiver, rumbling for 40 yards on his first catch midway through the second quarter to set up a 17-yard touchdown run by James Cook on the very next play. Johnson added three more catches, including a 26-yard grab, and finished second on the Bills in receiving yards behind Khalil Shakir's 80. Johnson will continue to operate as the Bills' change-of-pace back heading into Week 7 against the Raiders.

headline: Johnson rushed once for three yards and caught both of his targets for nine yards Sunday in a loss to New England.
story: Johnson logged 19 offensive snaps, well ahead of the four snaps played by Ray Davis and well behind the 35 snaps logged by starter James Cook. Johnson logged 50 receiving yards in his season debut in Week 3, and six of his seven touches this season have been receptions, so he clearly has a role as a pass catcher in Buffalo's offense. With that said, Johnson doesn't have a reliable weekly fantasy floor and isn't a trustworthy fantasy asset as long as Cook is healthy.

headline: Coleman didn't catch his only target in Thursday's 13-10 win over the Chiefs.
story: Coleman's involvement was minimal with DJ Moore healthy, as has been the case throughout the season. Josh Allen threw for just 81 yards Thursday, so none of Buffalo's receivers were particularly effective, but it would likely take another injury to Moore for Coleman -- who logged a 49 percent snap share in the contest -- to return to relevance in fantasy. Coleman hasn't exceeded 17 yards in a game or scored since Week 6. Up next for Coleman and the Bills is a Week 13 trip to New England.

headline: Coleman caught two of four targets for 17 yards during Sunday's 26-9 win over Miami.
story: Coleman finished with fewer than 20 receiving yards for the fourth straight week, and he hasn't reached the end zone since Week 6. The wide receiver has operated in a limited role on offense since DJ Moore returned to action in Week 8 following a shoulder injury, and Coleman will remain an unattractive fantasy asset ahead of the team's matchup with the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.

headline: Coleman caught one of three targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
story: Coleman failed to reel in multiple passes for the third time in the team's last five contests, and he played just 52 percent of the team's offensive snaps in the contest, his lowest percentage since Week 1. The wide receiver was briefly sidelined while being evaluated for a head injury before returning to the contest, which likely contributed to his lower workload. Coleman will continue to be an unpredictable fantasy option in Week 11 versus the Dolphins.

headline: Coleman, who was evaluated for a head injury, was later cleared to return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Coleman previously headed to the blue medical tent after taking a big hit during the contest, per Matt Parrino of News 4 Buffalo. However, after getting checked out, Coleman returned to the field to rejoin a WR corps that also includes DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir.

headline: Coleman finished Monday's 23-6 win over the Vikings with three catches for 17 yards on six targets.
story: Going up against a tough Minnesota defense, Bills QB Josh Allen posted a modest 234 passing yards with one touchdown and one interception. He spread the ball around to eight different pass catchers, with none of them hauling in more than four receptions. Coleman actually led Buffalo with six targets, but he finished seventh with just 17 receiving yards. The third-year wideout has been very up-and-down this season, registering 59 or more receiving yards three times but logging 17 or fewer receiving yards on four occasions. That makes his output quite difficult to predict for fantasy purposes.

headline: Coleman (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's contest in Minnesota.
story: Per Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News, Coleman again was spotted in a red non-contact jersey Saturday and eventually went down as a limited participant for a third consecutive practice. Despite the restrictions this week, though, Coleman is ready to suit up for an eighth straight game to begin the season, having put up a 20-287-3 line on 27 targets to date.

headline: Coleman (shoulder) was a limited practice participant Friday.
story: Coleman is on the injury report for the first time since Week 4, listed as a limited participant Thursday and Friday due to a shoulder injury. There's been no indication it's serious, so Coleman seems on track to play Monday night at Minnesota. Fellow Bills wideout DJ Moore (shoulder) also is gearing up to play.

headline: Coleman (shoulder) was limited in practice Thursday.
story: It's a new injury for Coleman, who is on the injury report for the first time since Week 4. With both DJ Moore (knee) and Dalton Kincaid (chest) healthy last Sunday against the Ravens, Coleman caught just one pass for four yards on three targets.

headline: Coleman hauled in one catch for four yards on three targets in Sunday's 36-10 win against Baltimore.
story: Coleman entered the weekend having recorded a touchdown in three straight contests, but he couldn't continue that streak Sunday. In fact, the third-year wideout was almost entirely uninvolved, as his only reception was a four-yarder at the end of the first quarter. Coleman did lead Buffalo wideouts with 63 offensive snaps, so his lack of production wasn't due to a downturn in playing time. He'll look to bounce back in Week 9, though he and the Bills will be on the road facing a tough Minnesota defense.

headline: Coleman brought in four of six targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Coleman led the Bills in receiving yards on the afternoon with the help of a 21-yard grab and a 12-yard touchdown reception with just over six minutes remaining in the third quarter. The score was Coleman's third of the season, with the previous two having come in each of the prior pair of contests against the Patriots and Rams. The oft-maligned 2024 second-round pick appears to be picking up some momentum in his third season, as Coleman already has a 19-283-3 line on 24 targets while helping make up for the multiple absences of DJ Moore (shoulder).

headline: Coleman caught a seven-yard touchdown pass on two targets during the Bills' 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday.
story: It was a statistically quiet night for Coleman despite the fact that DJ Moore (shoulder) was inactive, but Josh Allen completed only 12 of 19 passes and the Bills got most of their yardage on the ground. Coleman did have catches of 17 and seven yards in the third quarter negated by penalties, but the third-year pro was wide open for his touchdown after two Rams defensive backs collided. Coleman's 45 offensive snaps led all Bills wide receivers, and he has a 15-224-2 receiving line on 18 targets through five regular-season games. The Bills will stay on the road for Week 7 against the Raiders on Sunday, and Coleman's role on offense would shrink if Moore is cleared to return.

headline: Coleman secured six of seven targets for 116 yards and a touchdown in the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
story: DJ Moore went down in the first half with a shoulder injury, opening up plenty of opportunity in the Bills' air attack. Coleman almost fully maximized his additional targets, recording a team-high yardage figure while finishing second in both receptions and targets. Coleman's first two pro seasons were marked by inconsistency, but the third-year wideout has secured 14 of 16 targets for 217 yards and a touchdown over the first four games of 2026, and 10 of his catches have resulted in first downs. Coleman's 34-yard touchdown grab Sunday also would have delivered the game-winning points had Drake Maye not mounted a successful drive on the ensuing possession, and Coleman could remain in an elevated role during a Week 5 road matchup against the Rams on Monday night, Oct. 12, if Moore is sidelined for that contest.

headline: Coleman (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Coleman was DNP on Wednesday but got in a pair of limited practices Thursday and Friday and is ready to go for Sunday's divisional matchup. Coleman has made the most of his limited opportunities in a complementary role early on this season, securing eight of nine targets for 101 yards.

headline: Coleman (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: A spectator for the Bills' first Week 4 practice Wednesday, Coleman was able to take a step forward in activity a day later. The third-year wideout will likely need to upgrade to full activity to avoid carrying a designation into Sunday's game against the Patriots, but at this stage in the week, he appears to be trending toward playing.

headline: Coleman (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
story: Coleman dealt with the ankle injury in practice last week and was listed as questionable for Week 3 before suiting up and playing just 48.5 percent of the offensive snaps against the Chargers. He turned two targets into one catch for 37 yards. If Coleman is unable to play Sunday against the Patriots, Joshua Palmer would be in line for increased snaps.

headline: Coleman saw two targets and recorded a 37-yard catch during the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Coleman's practice reps during Week 3 prep were limited by an ankle injury, but he was cleared to play and ended up handling 32 of 66 offensive snaps (48.5 percent), third most among Bills wide receivers behind Khalil Shakir (48) and DJ Moore (42). Coleman was responsible for his team's longest play of the game late in the second quarter, setting up a one-yard TD for Josh Allen on the next play. Coleman is capable of making big plays, but it's hard to rely on him for consistent production when he's behind Moore, Shakir, tight end Dalton Kincaid and running back James Cook in the pecking order for targets. The Bills wrap up a three-game homestand this Sunday in an AFC East showdown against the Patriots, whose defense gave up 35 points (including three passing touchdowns) to the Jaguars in a Week 3 loss.

headline: Knox didn't catch his only target in Thursday's 13-10 win over the Chiefs.
story: Knox finished without a catch while Dalton Kincaid caught both of his targets in the latter's return from a one-game absence due to thumb and ankle injuries. Josh Allen threw for just 81 yards in difficult weather conditions, but Knox hasn't contributed much as a pass catcher even when Allen has been slinging the ball effectively. Heading into a Week 13 trip to New England, Knox has caught 16 of 24 targets for 117 yards and one TD through 11 appearances.

headline: Knox caught two of three targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
story: Knox was the top available TE for the Bills in the absence of Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle). The added opportunities helped Knox post his second-highest total of the season in receiving yards, but Knox remains off the radar in most fantasy formats heading into Thursday's game against the Chiefs. He hasn't scored since Week 2 while recording a meager 117 yards on 16 catches through 10 games.

headline: Knox will likely be the Bills' top tight end against the Dolphins on Sunday, given that Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is listed as doubtful for that contest, Maddy Glab of the Bills' official site reports.
story: Kincaid was held out of practice all week while tending to thumb and ankle injuries, and he's trending toward being inactive for Sunday's AFC East tilt. If Kincaid is indeed ruled out, then Knox will operate as the Bills' top tight end, with Jackson Hawes (shoulder) and Keleki Latu also in line for larger roles on offense. Knox has 14 catches (on 20 targets) for 86 yards and a touchdown through nine regular-season games, and the Bills face a Dolphins defense that ranks 25th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed per game to opposing tight ends.

headline: Knox caught one of his three targets for seven yards in the Bills' 31-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
story: Knox continues to receive targets as the No. 2 tight end in the Bills offense. The 30-year-old has consistently struggled to bring in catchable balls over the past few contests but remains a valuable part of Buffalo's 13-personnel packages as a blocker and receiving threat. Knox played 41 offensive snaps in Sunday's game and was on the field for 72 percent of the Bills' offensive plays.

headline: Knox caught four passes for 37 yards on five targets in Monday night's 23-6 win over the Vikings.
story: Knox's targets, catches and yards were all season highs. He also played 58 offensive snaps against Minnesota. With the blitz-happy Vikings defense opposite them, the Buffalo offense went with heavy tight end sets to try and get more blockers on the field. Knox won't be a recommended fantasy target for Sunday's game against the Jets. He has 13 grabs for 79 yards and a touchdown across eight games this season.

headline: Knox caught one of two targets for six yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.
story: It's a typical receiving line for Knox, whose main contributions come in the blocking department. Knox has nine grabs for 42 yards and one touchdown across seven appearances this season. He'd likely need multiple wideout and tight-end injuries to be a fantasy consideration.

headline: Knox caught his only target for no gain during Sunday's 33-30 win at Las Vegas.
story: He again played about as many snaps at tight end Sunday (47) as did starter Dalton Kincaid (49), but Knox continued to function mostly as a blocker. He has yet to draw more than three targets in a game this season, and he'll probably remain on the periphery of the passing offense as long as Kincaid is still available.

headline: Knox caught both of his targets for 13 yards in the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Knox was on the field frequently in 12-personnel packages during Sunday's contest but saw only two targets. The tight end likely will see the field more as the Bills lean back into 13-personnel packages to utilize Dalton Kincaid more in Week 5.

headline: Knox hauled in his lone target for five yards in a 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Knox and fellow tight end Dalton Kincaid combined for only four targets from Josh Allen, with wide receiver DJ Moore leading all pass catchers with 10 targets. Knox is up to a 4-17-1 line on four targets through three games, and his production will be limited to occasional red zone opportunities as long as Kincaid is healthy. The Bills will stay home for an AFC East clash against the Patriots in Week 4.

headline: Shakir brought in three of six targets for 33 yards in the Bills' 13-10 in over the Chiefs on Thursday.
story: Shakir's reception and yardage totals led the Bills on a night when Josh Allen threw for just 81 yards with a pair of picks. The veteran slot receiver was coming off a Week 11 showing against the Dolphins in which he accrued a season-high 101 receiving yards, and Thursday's downturn was largely explainable by Allen's struggles and less-than-ideal weather conditions. Shakir should remain a key target for Allen during a Week 13 road matchup Sunday, Dec. 6 with a Patriots squad that the wideout posted a 7-82-0 line against back in Week 4.

headline: Josh Allen's pass ricochets off Khalil Shakir for his second INT
story: Josh Allen's pass ricochets off Khalil Shakir for his second INT

headline: Shakir caught five of nine targets for 101 yards while rushing twice for two yards in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
story: Shakir led the Bills in receiving yards in the absence of TE Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle), posting 10 more than DJ Moore, who had one more target than Shakir. Sunday marked Shakir's first time reaching the 100-yard threshold since a 110-yard showing in Week 12 of last season. Shakir will look to build on this outing as he searches for his second TD of the season Thursday against the Chiefs.

headline: Shakir caught two of three targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
story: With Buffalo controlling this one most of the afternoon, Josh Allen attempted just 21 passes and completed only 11 on a day wind gusts played a factor. Shakir's 26 receiving yards were his fewest since Week 3. He's scored just one touchdown this season and has yet to hit 100 yards in a game all year, so the ceiling isn't that high for fantasy while the floor is what he produced Sunday. Shakir is more of fantasy WR4 in PPR-based formats.

headline: Shakir secured all four targets for 58 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night.
story: Shakir tied for the team lead in receptions while setting the pace in receiving yards on a night when Josh Allen spread the ball around to eight different targets. The veteran receiver continues to maintain his trademark steady presence in Buffalo's air attack, now having recorded at least Monday night's catch and yardage tallies in four of the last five games. Shakir carries a bright outlook into a Week 10 road matchup against a vulnerable Jets defense on Sunday.

headline: Shakir caught five of six targets for 64 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.
story: Shakir initially appeared to get in the end zone for a six-yard touchdown early in the first quarter, but he was ruled out at the one-yard line after review. Josh Allen then punched in the one-yard touchdown two plays later. On the day, Shakir paced the Bills with his five grabs and tied for second on the team in targets, one behind DJ Moore. Shakir has yet to hit 100 yards in a game this season and has just one touchdown, settling in as a low-ceiling WR4 in fantasy, especially when both Moore and Dalton Kincaid are healthy.

headline: Shakir brought in four of six targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Shakir posted his second-lowest yardage figure of the season, but the talented veteran recorded his first touchdown of the campaign on a nine-yard grab just past the midway point of the second quarter. His target total also tied for his second highest of the campaign, a figure he'd reached on two other occasions. The fifth-year pro should continue to garner his fair share of Josh Allen's attention moving forward, although Shakir's targets could take a slight hit if DJ Moore (shoulder) returns for a Week 8 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 1, following a Week 7 bye.

headline: Shakir brought in all three targets for 80 yards in the Bills' 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday night.
story: On a night when Josh Allen completed just 12 passes, Shakir led the Bills in receiving yards with a figure that marked his second straight 80-yard-plus effort. However, Shakir needed overtime to get there, as he recorded a game-long 57-yard catch and run during Buffalo's first drive of the extra period. Shakir otherwise didn't see much benefit from the absences of DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer due to shoulder injuries, but he is now averaging an impressive 14.2 yards per catch heading into a Week 6 road matchup against the Raiders.

headline: Shakir turned seven catches (on eight targets) into 82 yards during the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Shakir's final stat line Sunday nearly matched his 8-94-0 line on 15 targets across the first three games of the regular season. Most of the veteran slot receiver's yards came on a 51-yard connection with Josh Allen late in the second quarter, with the latter finishing the drive with a two-yard rushing touchdown. Unfortunately for Shakir, he also had the ball ripped out of his hands by Robert Spillane within the final seconds of the first half, though the Bills avoided any damage after the defense intercepted Patriots quarterback Drake Maye on the very next play. DJ Moore aggravated a previous shoulder injury during Sunday's loss, and while it's not considered a long-term issue, Bills pass catchers like Shakir, Keon Coleman and tight end Dalton Kincaid are all candidates to see more targets from Allen if Moore cannot play in Week 5 against the Rams on Monday, Oct. 12.

headline: Shakir caught one of his three targets for six yards in the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Shakir played 71 percent of the Bills' offensive snaps in the contest but caught just one pass. The wide receiver was bullied in coverage while Josh Allen struggled on a day when the team's offense combined for five total turnovers.

headline: Moore hauled in two of six targets for 15 yards in the Bills' 13-10 win over the Chiefs on Thursday.
story: Moore's production, like that of the rest of his fellow skill-position players, was very modest on a night when Josh Allen threw for only 81 yards and a pair of interceptions. The talented wideout's catch and yardage totals were both his third-lowest tallies of the season, but Moore is still averaging a formidable 14.6 yards per reception heading into a Week 13 road matchup against the Patriots on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Moore caught eight of 10 targets for 91 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
story: Moore's four-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter gave him his first multi-game regular-season touchdown streak since Weeks 15 and 16 of the 2025 campaign with the Bears. He briefly left the game later in the first half to have his knee looked at but promptly returned and ultimately reached the 90-yard threshold for a second consecutive game while leading the team in targets. Barring a setback with his knee on a short week, Moore should continue to work as Buffalo's top wide receiver Thanksgiving night against the Chiefs.

headline: Moore (knee) has returned to Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
story: Moore had headed to the locker room after sustaining what the Bills called a knee injury. However, his exit was a brief one, and the wideout will have an opportunity to build on the 5/41/1 receiving line he put up before sustaining what turned out to be a minor knee issue.

headline: Moore (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Dolphins due to a knee injury.
story: Per Matt Parrino of Syracuse.com, Moore headed to the locker room after he was helped off the field during the contest following a play where came down awkwardly on a catch attempt. Prior to his exit, Moore caught five passes for 41 yards and a TD.

headline: Moore caught four of six targets for 90 yards and a touchdown while rushing once for four yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
story: Moore's 45-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter accounted for half of his team-high total in receiving yards. This was his most productive outing since Moore went for 100 yards and a TD in his Bills debut, and the veteran wide receiver has chipped in 216 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in three games since returning from a shoulder injury. Josh Allen and James Cook continue to lead Buffalo's offense with their legs, but Moore has re-established himself as Allen's top target in the passing game heading into a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins.

headline: Moore secured three of five targets for 25 yards and rushed once for 11 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night.
story: The veteran receiver came into the game without an injury designation related to the shoulder issue he's managing, but Moore still put together a modest performance against a tough Vikings defense that kept pressure on Josh Allen throughout the night. Moore has a combined 7-107-1 line on on 12 targets in the two contests he's suited up for since returning from a two-game absence, and he should have a much better chance of downfield success in a Week 10 road matchup against the Jets' vulnerable defense Sunday.

headline: Moore (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's contest at Minnesota.
story: While logging three straight limited practices during Week 9 prep, Moore continued to wear a red non-contact jersey due to the AC joint sprain that he's been dealing with since Week 2. Now that he's in the clear for Monday's matchup, he'll look to build upon the 16-260-2 line on 27 targets that he's racked up through five eppearances on the campaign.

headline: Moore (shoulder) remained in a red non-contact jersey at Saturday's practice, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
story: Moore has been wearing such a jersey from time to time this season since suffering an AC joint sprain in Week 2 against the Lions. He's appeared in three of the Bills' five contests since then, accruing an 11-160-1 line on 19 targets. Saturday's practice report will determine if Moore has a designation for Monday's game at Minnesota.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was a limited practice participant Friday.
story: Moore has managed an AC joint sprain for most of the season, typically practicing in a non-contact jersey. He'll likely be ready for Monday's game at Minnesota, coming off a 4-82-1 receiving line (seven targets) in last week's 36-10 win over Baltimore.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was still wearing a non-contact jersey at Friday's practice, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.
story: Moore will likely be managing his shoulder injury for much of the remainder of the season, as he's dealing with an AC sprain that can pop out of place with contact. Moore should be fine for Monday night's game against the Vikings after returning to the lineup last Sunday against Baltimore.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Moore mustered some level of activity in Buffalo's first practice of Week 9 after downplaying the knee injury that forced him out late in the Week 8 win over Baltimore. He has an extra day to recover before the Bills face the Vikings on Monday Night Football. Moore has two more chances to practice without limitations and put himself in the clear to suit up.

headline: Moore (knee) is line to practice in some capacity Thursday, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.
story: Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network previously reported that Moore downplayed his late-game exit from this past Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens, which aligns with his looming practice presence. The Bills' Thursday injury report will reveal the wideout's official participation level, either way.

headline: Moore indicated following Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens that he's okay in the wake of his late-game exit due to a knee issue, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
story: That's encouraging, but Moore's status will nonetheless be worth monitoring ahead of the Bills' Nov. 9 contest against the Vikings. Before his departure from Sunday's contest, Moore caught four of his seven targets for 82 yards and a TD.

headline: Moore (undisclosed) headed to the medical tent during Sunday's game against the Ravens, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
story: It remains to be seen what prompted Moore's visit to the tent, but we'll keep an eye out for added context. Prior to his exit, the wideout caught four of his seven targets for 82 yards and a TD.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
story: Moore will suit up for the first time since Week 4, after an SC joint sprain in his shoulder kept him from playing in the Bills' last two contests prior to their Week 7 bye. The wideout was limited in practice throughout Week 8 prep before taking a designation into Sunday, but he's displayed enough progress for the Bills to clear him to return to action. In his two appearances with Buffalo in which he didn't exit early due to injury, Moore compiled 11 receptions for 167 yards and a touchdown on 18 targets.

headline: Moore (shoulder) remains listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens but is expected to play, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Moore had missed the Bills' last two games due to an SC joint sprain in his shoulder, but he appears to be in a better spot on the health front coming out of a Week 7 bye. He was still a limited participant in practice throughout the week, but despite carrying a designation into Sunday, he appears to have demonstrated enough progress in his recovery from the shoulder issue to suit up against Baltimore. Moore will be officially cleared to play when Buffalo releases its inactive list 90 minutes prior to the 1 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
story: Moore has missed the past two games and remained limited in practice this week coming out of Buffalo's bye. He failed to play through questionable designations in Weeks 5 and 6, so it remains unclear if the veteran wideout will be able to give it a go Sunday against the Ravens. If he's unable to return, Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir would likely soak up the bulk of the snaps atop the depth chart.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Moore has been listed as limited both Wednesday and Thursday while practicing in a non-contact jersey. The 29-year-old wide receiver missed Buffalo's last two games prior to a Week 7 bye after having appeared in 92 consecutive regular-season games. Keon Coleman stepped up in Moore's absence and could maintain a larger role Sunday against the Ravens if Moore is ultimately sidelined or limited.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was in a red non-contact jersey for a second straight day Thursday, Jay Skurski of the Buffalo News reports.
story: Moore continues to practice but has not been taking contact this week. If he sheds the non-contact jersey Friday, it'll be a strong indicator for his status going into Sunday's game against the Ravens. Moore has missed the last two weeks due to an AC joint injury.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: An AC joint sprain in his shoulder kept Moore from playing in Buffalo's past two games, but the wideout may be in a better spot on the health front coming out of a Week 7 bye. Per Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard, Moore was sporting a no-contact jersey during the open portion of Wednesday's practice, so he may need to take contact at some point in the next day or two in order for the Bills to clear him to play Sunday against the Ravens.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was spotted on the field for the open portion of Wednesday's practice but was donning a no-contact jersey, Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard reports.
story: Moore has been sidelined for the Bills' last two games due to an AC Joint sprain, but coming out of a Week 7 bye, head coach Joe Brady seemed to express optimism Wednesday about the receiver's chances of playing this Sunday versus the Ravens, per Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo. While Moore's presence on the field to begin Week 8 prep is an encouraging sign, he'll likely need to resume taking contact at some point Thursday or Friday to put himself on track to suit up Sunday. The shoulder issue has led to early exits for Moore in two of his four appearances on the season, but he's been productive in both of his two full games with 11 receptions for 167 yards and a touchdown on 18 targets between those contests.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is listed as inactive Sunday in Las Vegas.
story: After sitting out a Week 5 overtime win at the Rams, Moore managed just one limited practice (Friday) this week, and he donned a red non-contact jersey while doing so. Per Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic, Moore again didn't log much activity during pregame warmups for a second straight week, forecasting another absence was likely. With Moore's status now clarified, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman and Joshua Palmer (shoulder) should earn most of the WR reps in the Bills offense in Week 6.

headline: Moore (shoulder) will be listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Las Vegas, Jay Skurski of The Buffalo News reports.
story: Moore returned to practice Friday in a non-contact jersey, potentially setting up a game-time decision ahead of Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. Fellow Bills wideout Joshua Palmer (shoulder) also is listed as questionable, after both Moore and Palmer missed an overtime win at Los Angeles in Week 5. Keon Coleman, Khalil Shakir and Skyler Bell handled nearly all of the WR routes last week.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is practicing Friday in a non-contact jersey, ESPN's Nick Suss reports.
story: Listed as a non-participant the previous two days, Moore may nonetheless make a bid to play Sunday at Las Vegas. He missed a Week 5 win over the Rams after aggravating a shoulder injury in Week 4.

headline: Moore (shoulder) officially didn't practice Thursday.
story: In the wake of missing his first game of the season Monday at the Rams, Moore hasn't been able to practice in any capacity this week and has only one more opportunity Friday to prove the health of his shoulder before the Bills potentially make a ruling on his status for Sunday's contest in Las Vegas. Meanwhile, fellow WR Joshua Palmer (shoulder) remained limited Thursday, which leaves Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman, Greg Dortch and Skyler Bell as the healthy options at the position on the active roster

headline: Moore (shoulder) didn't participate in the media-access portion of Thursday's practice, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.
story: While Moore was in attendance for practice, he was sporting a red no-contact jersey and didn't take part in stretching or drills with his healthy teammates before heading inside to presumably get in some individual work, per Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard. After sitting out Monday's overtime win over the Rams and having gone down as a non-participant on the Bills' first two Week 6 practice report, Moore looks to be trending toward missing another game Sunday in Las Vegas.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was listed as a non-participant on Wednesday's estimated injury report.
story: The Bills conducted a walkthrough Wednesday after playing Monday night, but Moore would not have gotten any work in had the Bills decided to practice. Moore will have a couple chances to practice before the week comes to a close, but with Buffalo on bye in Week 7, the team could decide to hold him out again Sunday in an effort to maximize the recovery time.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is listed as inactive Monday at the Rams.
story: After suffering a shoulder injury in Week 4, Moore wasn't expected to be tending to a long-term issue, and head coach Joe Brady told Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News on Thursday that the wide receiver was "going to be able to do everything he can to be able to rock this week." Moore then managed just one limited session (Saturday) during Week 5 prep, which wasn't enough for him to gain clearance to play Monday. With both Moore and Joshua Palmer (shoulder) unavailable, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman, Greg Dortch, Skyler Bell and Trent Sherfield will handle WR reps for the Bills.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Rams, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
story: Moore was able to participate in Saturday's practice in a limited capacity after being sidelined for the first two sessions of Week 5 prep, and that's enough for the veteran wide receiver to draw the questionable tag for Monday night's contest. Joshua Palmer (shoulder) has already been ruled out, so if Moore is also sidelined, then Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman would operate as the top wide receivers for Buffalo.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was on the field for the start of Saturday's practice, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: Moore was a non-participant in each of the Bills' first two practices of the week, so it's a positive sign for him to be on the field for Saturday's session. The Bills' injury report following practice will provide clarity on Moore's status for Monday night's road game against the Rams, and if the veteran wide receiver cannot play, then Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman would serve as Buffalo's top wide receivers, with tight end Dalton Kincaid also in the mix for more targets from quarterback Josh Allen.

headline: Moore (shoulder) remained a non-participant in Friday's practice for the Bills.
story: With back-to-back absences, Moore isn't looking great for Monday's game at the Rams, though he'll still have one more chance Saturday to practice. If Moore doesn't end up playing, Keon Coleman and Joshua Palmer (shoulder) will be the top candidates to replace Moore's snaps, with slot receiver Khalil Shakir and tight end Dalton Kincaid potentially helping to pick up the slack in terms of target volume.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was not on the field for the start of Friday's practice open to the media, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: Moore has logged back-to-back DNPs to start Week 5 prep, but he does have an extra day to get ready, with the Bills and Rams not kicking off until Monday night. However, fantasy managers are going to need to have a backup plan in place if Moore doesn't get the green light to play after he aggravated his shoulder injury in last Sunday's loss to the Patriots. Dalton Kincaid, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman and Joshua Palmer would all be in line for elevated roles in the passing game if Moore ends up inactive.

headline: Moore (shoulder) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Moore made an early departure this past Sunday against the Patriots in the second quarter with a shoulder injury and wasn't able to return. While the issue isn't considered to be long term and head coach Joe Brady didn't rule Moore out for Monday's game at the Rams as of Thursday, per Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News, the wide receiver kicked off the week with no on-field work. Moore will have two more chances to prove his health before the Bills potentially make a ruling on his status once they post Saturday's injury report.

headline: Moore (shoulder) was not participating during the media viewing period of Thursday's practice,  Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.
story: Moore has not been ruled out for the Week 5 matchup against the Rams, but it seems he's got an uphill battle ahead of him. He aggravated his shoulder injury in the Week 4 loss to the Patriots and did not return to action. He may get some work in later in Thursday's session, but the official injury report will tell the tale.

headline: Head coach Joe Brady said Thursday that Moore (shoulder) is "going to be able to do everything he can to be able to rock this week," Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
story: Moore aggravated a shoulder injury during Buffalo's Week 4 loss to the Patriots. Brady didn't have a specific update on Moore's status Thursday, but it sounds like the veteran wide receiver at least has a chance to avoid missing Monday's game against the Rams. Moore has a 92-game regular-season ironman streak on the line.

headline: Moore (shoulder) is dealing with an injury that isn't considered long-term, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Moore exited Sunday's loss to the Patriots after aggravating a previous shoulder injury. He isn't expected to miss significant time, though it remains to be seen if Moore will play against the Rams in Week 5. The 29-year-old wide receiver has suited up for 92 consecutive regular-season games dating back to the 2020 season.

headline: Kincaid brought in both targets for 13 yards in the Bills' 13-10 loss to the Chiefs on Thursday.
story: Making his return from a one-game absence due to thumb and ankle injuries, Kincaid's numbers weren't quite as poor within the context of a night where Josh Allen threw for only 81 yards and completed less than 50.0 percent of his passes. Kincaid tied for runner-up slotting on the Bills in receptions, and he was third in receiving yards as well. Kincaid now has multiple catches in five straight games heading into a Week 13 road divisional matchup against the Patriots on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is listed as active for Thursday night's game against the Chiefs.
story: Kincaid, who was unavailable for this past Sunday's 26-9 victory over Miami, drew limited listings on Buffalo's injury reports Monday through Wednesday before approaching Thursday's contest with an official questionable designation. With the tight end's Week 12 status confirmed, Kincaid represents a viable fantasy lineup option at his position, having averaged 3.6 catches on 4.6 targets for 54.1 receiving yards with two TDs through nine games played.

headline: Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is listed as questionable for Thursday night's contest against the Chiefs.
story: Kincaid, who was inactive for this past Sunday's win over the Dolphins, logged a limited listing on the Bills' Monday through Wednesday practice/injury reports before being deemed questionable to face Kansas City. Per Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard, following Tuesday's practice Kincaid said that he's "most likely playing" Thursday, with the tight end's Week 12 status set to be confirmed once Buffalo's inactives are posted ahead of the team's 8:20 pm kickoff.

headline: The Bills listed Kincaid (thumb/ankle) as a limited participant in Tuesday's practice.
story: After failing to practice in any fashion in Week 11 before sitting out Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins, Kincaid has been upgraded to a limited participant on both of the Bills' first two injury reports of Week 12. He looks to be in a good spot on the health front as Thursday's game against the Chiefs approaches, with Kincaid telling Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard after Tuesday's practice that he'll "most likely" be playing in that contest. The Bills will release their final injury report of the week Wednesday and decide whether Kincaid carries a designation into Thursday.

headline: Kincaid (thumb/ankle) was listed as a limited participant on Monday's practice estimate.
story: Kincaid didn't practice at all last week before being made inactive for Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins. Though the Bills didn't actually practice Monday, Kincaid's 'limited' listing does represent an upgrade and suggests that the tight end has a chance to be available for Thursday night's game against the Chiefs. Further context regarding his Week 12 status is set to arrive via Tuesday's practice report, in any case.

headline: Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
story: Listed as doubtful heading into the weekend after failing to practice in any capacity Wednesday through Friday, Kincaid will wind up missing his first game of the season. Kincaid's 4.5 targets per game will be filtered out among the Bills' other pass-catching options, including Dawson Knox, who will operate as the team's clear No. 1 tight end this week. The Bills will face a quick turnaround for Week 12 with a Thursday matchup versus the Chiefs, so Kincaid may need to practice in some fashion prior to that contest to put himself on a path to play.

headline: Kincaid (thumb/ankle) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Matt Parrino reports.
story: The Bills are massive 16.5-point favorites at home against a Dolphins team missing its starting quarterback, so it presents an opportunity to give Kincaid a rest after he's been playing through injuries the last several weeks. Dawson Knox will remain an every-down tight end, with Jackson Hawes and Keleki Latu stepping into elevated spots. The biggest beneficiaries likely will be DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir in terms of target opportunities, though Buffalo should run all over this Miami defense.

headline: Kincaid (thumb) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: With Kincaid now having missed the open portion of practice on consecutive days, his status will remain worth tracking heading into Sunday's game against the Dolphins. If the tight end is limited or unavailable, Buffalo could have to lean more on DJ Moore and Khalil Shakir in the middle of the field, while Dawson Knox, Jackson Hawes and Keleki Latu would handle tight-end duties.

headline: Kincaid (thumb/ankle) wasn't spotted on the field for Thursday's practice, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: Kincaid has now kicked off Week 11 prep with consecutive absences from practice, but he'll be able to erase some concern about his status for Sunday's game against the Dolphins if he's able to get back on the field Friday in some capacity.

headline: Kincaid didn't practice Wednesday due to thumb and ankle injuries.
story: Kincaid finished with two receptions for 58 yards on three targets while logging a 46 percent snap share in this past Sunday's win over the Jets. The tight end had been nursing the ankle injury leading up to that contest, but the thumb issue is a new concern. Kincaid will have two more chances to get in some practice reps before the Bills decide whether he'll take an injury tag into this Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

headline: Kincaid caught two of three targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
story: Kincaid contributed catches of four and 54 yards to finish second on the team in receiving yards behind DJ Moore (90). The 2023 first-round pick has seen his usage fluctuate throughout the campaign, as Kincaid has failed to exceed three targets on five occasions but has drawn at least six looks from Josh Allen in each of the other four games. Kincaid is making the most of his opportunities for a second consecutive regular season, averaging 11.9 yards per target in 2026 after leading all qualified TEs with 11.7 YPT in 2025. Next up for Kincaid is a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins.

headline: Kincaid (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Kincaid was a full practice participant Friday after logging limited sessions the previous two days. He should be fine for his usual role against a porous Jets defense.

headline: Kincaid (ankle) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
story: Kincaid has opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited sessions. He has faced plenty of practice limitations throughout the season, but Kincaid has yet to sit out a game. That pattern seems unlikely to change in Week 10 against the Jets.

headline: Kincaid (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's walk-through.
story: Kincaid began last week with a limited session due to a chest issue, but was able to suit up for Monday night's win over the Vikings while seeing the field on 50 percent of the Bills' snaps on offense. In the process, the tight end caught all three of his targets for 28 yards. It's unclear if Kincaid's ankle injury occurred versus Minnesota or is something that occurred Wednesday, but either way added context regarding his status for this weekend's game against the Jets will arrive via Thursday's injury report.

headline: Kincaid secured all three targets for 28 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night.
story: Kincaid, like the rest of the members of the Bills' air attack, put up modest numbers on a night when Josh Allen had to navigate four sacks from a highly aggressive Vikings defense. The talented tight end still finished tied for second in receptions on the Bills, but Kincaid finished with his second-lowest yardage total of the campaign. Kincaid should have a good opportunity to boost his numbers in a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

headline: Kincaid (chest) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
story: Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo previously noted that Kincaid had shed his red non-contact jersey at Friday's practice, and the tight end's full participation in the session paves the way for him to be in uniform Monday night against the Vikings. Over his last two games, Kincaid (who overall is tied for first among Bills in catches (27) and leads the team in receiving yards (401)) has logged an 11-124-1 receiving line, a pace that keeps him relevant from a fantasy perspective.

headline: Kincaid (chest) is no longer in a red non-contact jersey at Friday's practice, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.
story: With Kincaid having been listed as a limited participant Thursday while dealing with a chest injury, shedding the non-contact jersey Friday is a positive sign for his practice progression and should put the tight end in the clear for Monday night's date with a tough Vikings defense.

headline: Kincaid (chest) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice,.
story: Fellow pass catchers DJ Moore (shoulder) and Keon Coleman (shoulder) also were limited Thursday, so the trio's statuses will need to be monitored ahead of Monday night's game against the Vikings. Over his last two outings, Kincaid has managed to make his mark from a fantasy perspective by logging an 11-124-1 receiving line in that span.

headline: Kincaid (chest) caught four of six targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.
story: Kincaid was questionable coming into the game due to a chest injury, but he managed to suit up and finished as the team leader in receiving yards. He made a 40-yard catch early in the fourth quarter and capped the following drive with a 23-yard touchdown catch. The streaky TE has returned to form with 11 catches for 124 yards and a touchdown over the past two games. Kincaid had just four catches for 52 yards over his previous three outings after starting the season with 12 catches for 225 yards and a TD through two games. Next up for Kincaid and the Bills is a Week 9 MNF clash with Minnesota's elite defense.

headline: Kincaid (chest) is active for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
story: After sustaining a chest injury in the Bills' Week 6 win over the Raiders, Kincaid didn't fully move past the issue following the team's Week 7 bye. A limited participant in practices Wednesday through Friday, Kincaid took a questionable tag into the weekend but will nonetheless get the green light to play versus Baltimore. Though Kincaid drew eight targets -- his most since Week 2 -- in the win over Las Vegas, he could struggle to see that sort of volume Sunday while the Bills welcome top wideout DJ Moore (shoulder) back to the lineup for the first time since Week 4.

headline: The Bills are optimistic that Kincaid (chest), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens, will be able to play, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: Citing a source familiar with Kincaid's situation, Fowler relays that "it would be a surprise" if the tight end didn't play Sunday, after he was listed as a limited participant in all three practices this week. Like Kincaid, wideout DJ Moore (shoulder) is listed as questionable but expected to play, so Buffalo appears to be tracking toward having all of its key pass catchers available for the first time since Week 4. Official word on the statuses of Kincaid and Moore will arrive when the Bills post their inactive list 90 minutes prior to Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Kincaid (chest) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News reports.
story: Kincaid returned to a Week 6 win at Las Vegas after being evaluated for an upper-body injury. Then, coming out of a Week 7 bye, Kincaid was a limited practice participant Wednesday and Thursday, donning a no-contact jersey. He seems more likely than not to play, but fantasy managers will want to check in ahead of the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff Sunday.

headline: Kincaid (chest) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Kincaid has started Week 8 prep with consecutive limited practice sessions coming out of Buffalo's Week 7 bye. The 27-year-old TE has yet to miss a game this season, but Kincaid has cooled down significantly after a scorching start, mustering 90 receiving yards over the past four games after posting 225 yards and a TD through Week 2. Kincaid will look to get back on track Sunday against the Ravens, assuming he plays through the chest injury that's limiting his practice participation.

headline: Kincaid (chest) remained in a red non-contact jersey for a second straight day Thursday, Jay Skurski of the Buffalo News reports.
story: This marks Kincaid's second straight practice in a non-contact jersey as Buffalo returns from the team's bye and prepares to host the Ravens in Week 8. Friday's practice will give a more clear picture of Kincaid's status going into the weekend.

headline: Kincaid was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a chest injury.
story: Before the Bills went on bye Week 7, Kincaid briefly exited a 33-30 win over the Raiders on Oct. 18 due to what the team referred to as a rib issue. His listed chest injury is presumably related and resulted in Kincaid donning a no-contact jersey during the open portion of Wednesday's practice, per Matt Parrino of The Syracuse Post-Standard. As long as the tight end is able to practice fully by the end of the week, he should be ready to handle his normal snap share in Sunday's matchup with the Ravens.

headline: Kincaid (ribs) returned to Sunday's 33-30 win at Las Vegas and finished with seven catches (on eight targets) for 38 yards.
story: Kincaid missed some time from late in the third quarter and into the fourth to be evaluated in the sideline tent, but he got back on the field with 8:01 remaining and added one more reception to his final line. Overall, he paced the Bills in catches and targets, but he ended Week 6 with his lowest YPC (5.4) of the campaign. The Bills have a Week 7 bye, so he'll have plenty of time to heal up for Buffalo's next game Sunday, Nov. 1 against the Ravens.

headline: Kincaid (ribs) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Kincaid was evaluated by trainers in the blue medical tent late in the third quarter before heading to the locker room, where he will undergo further tests to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. Dawson Knox and Jackson Hawes should both see a bump in offensive snaps for as long as Kincaid is sidelined.

headline: Kincaid brought in one of two targets for seven yards and recorded a two-point conversion catch in the Bills' 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday night.
story: Kincaid's quiet stretch after a stellar first two games of the season continued Monday in a game where Josh Allen recorded only 12 completions. However, the fourth-year tight end made one of the two times he touched the ball count, as he recorded a two-point conversion catch following Josh Allen's one-yard touchdown run early in the fourth quarter to give the Bills a seven-point lead at the time. Kincaid has a modest 4-52-0 line over the last three games outside of the two-pointer, however, so he'll be looking for a boost in opportunity during a Week 6 road matchup against the Raiders on Sunday.

headline: Kincaid brought in one of two targets for seven yards in the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Kincaid saw a reduced role in the air attack for the second straight week, although Sunday's downturn resulted in season-low figures across the board. Kincaid opened the season with a 12-225-0 line over the first two games, but he's managed just three receptions for 45 yards on five targets in the subsequent pair of contests. Kincaid will look to bounce back in a Week 5 marquee matchup on the road against the Rams on Monday night, Oct. 12.

headline: Josh Allen picked off in the end zone
story: Josh Allen picked off in the end zone

headline: Allen completed 10 of 21 passes for 81 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions and added seven carries for 43 yards in the Bills' 13-10 win over the Chiefs on Thursday.
story: Allen's abysmal numbers tell the tale of how difficult a night it was for the star signal-caller under less-than-ideal weather conditions and while facing a talented veteran defense. Allen's passing yardage total was a season low, and the two-interception tally was his second straight. Allen also took a pair of sacks and completed a season-worst 47.6 percent of his passes, but he helped bring Buffalo back from a 10-7 fourth-quarter deficit. Allen's lackluster showing aside, he'll remain an elite option in all formats for a Week 13 road divisional clash against the Patriots on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Josh Allen's pass ricochets off Khalil Shakir for his second INT
story: Josh Allen's pass ricochets off Khalil Shakir for his second INT

headline: Allen completed 27 of 45 passes for 304 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
story: Allen threw a four-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore in the second quarter but got picked off twice later in the first half and had a would-be third interception nullified by a penalty on the penultimate play before halftime. Despite some sloppy play and zero rushing production from Allen, the 9-1 Bills cruised past the 1-9 Dolphins as the star QB raised his season total to 25 touchdowns (14 passing, 11 rushing). Buffalo's likely to encounter more resistance Thursday night against the 8-2 Chiefs. Allen is 5-1 against Patrick Mahomes in the regular season but 0-4 when they face off in the playoffs.

headline: Allen completed 11 of 21 passes for 196 yards, one touchdown and one interception while rushing five times for five yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
story: Allen scored one-yard rushing touchdowns in the first and third quarters, bringing his season total up to 11 rushing TDs. He added his 13th touchdown pass of the campaign on a 45-yard strike to DJ Moore later in the third quarter, and Allen's fourth-quarter interception on third-and-long was basically an arm punt. Heading into a Week 11 home game against the Dolphins, the star QB has accounted for multiple touchdowns in all but one outing this season.

headline: Allen completed 21 of 31 passes for 234 yards with one touchdown and one interception while adding six carries for 15 yards in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night.
story: Allen came into the night undoubtedly expecting to have to work for everything he got, and Brian Flores' aggressive defensive unit helped validate that prognosis by sacking the star signal-caller on four occasions. However, Allen was able to navigate the dangers pretty effectively, spreading the ball around to eight different targets overall. He connected with Keleki Latu from 25 yards out late in the first half for his one touchdown pass, and Allen's lone turnover, a first-quarter interception on a deep shot in the Vikings' end zone, didn't lead to any Minnesota points. Allen hasn't eclipsed the 300-yard threshold since Week 1, but he'll take 2,027 passing yards and a 12:6 TD:INT alongside 285 rushing yards into a Week 10 road divisional clash against the Jets on Sunday.

headline: Allen completed 21 of 34 passes for 289 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens. He added 30 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown on seven rushing attempts.
story: Allen capped the opening drive with a one-yard touchdown plunge on which he went airborne to stretch the ball over the goal line. He struggled as a passer in the first half, including a first-quarter interception, but Allen heated up after halftime to post his highest passing yards total since a 334-yard Week 1 performance. Allen's 11-yard touchdown pass to DJ Moore (knee) in the fourth quarter gave Allen sole possession of first place in Bills history with 259 passing touchdowns, including postseason play. He added a 23-yard touchdown pass to Dalton Kincaid on the next drive as the Bills pulled away from a Ravens team that lost top two QBs Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe). Allen has led the Bills to a 6-1 record heading into a Week 8 road matchup against the 6-1 Vikings.

headline: Cook rushed 32 times for 117 yards and a touchdown and brought in his only target for eight yards in the Bills' 13-10 win over the Chiefs on Thursday.
story: Cook logged a season high in rush attempts while eclipsing the century mark for the third time in the last four games. Cook's longest gain went for only 10 yards, so he worked hard for everything he got against a tough Chiefs front. Cook added his 11th rushing touchdown of the season on a five-yard run early in the second quarter, and he'll have some extra recovery time before he takes aim at the Patriots defense in a Week 13 road matchup on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: James Cook III finds an opening for a Bills TD
story: James Cook III finds an opening for a Bills TD

headline: Cook rushed 22 times for 89 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for three yards in Sunday's 26-9 win over the Dolphins.
story: Cook extended his touchdown streak to nine games with a one-yard touchdown run in the second quarter. He accounted for all but five of Buffalo's rushing attempts as Josh Allen finished without one, but Cook came up short of 100 scrimmage yards for the first time since Week 4. The reigning NFL rushing yards leader continues to put up stellar production heading into Thursday night's home game against the Chiefs.

headline: Cook rushed 18 times for 157 yards and a touchdown and didn't catch his only target in Sunday's 31-12 win over the Jets.
story: Buffalo relied primarily on its ground game in the lopsided victory, as Cook's 74-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter provided the cherry on top after a pair of one-yard Josh Allen rushing scores helped the Bills pull away. Cook extended his touchdown streak to eight games by scoring his ninth rushing TD over that span. He has topped 100 scrimmage yards in all but one game during the productive stretch, bouncing back effectively after being held to 69 scoreless yards by the Texans in the season opener. Cook has a nice opportunity to keep rolling in Week 11, when the 8-1 Bills host the 1-8 Dolphins.

headline: Cook rushed 31 times for 107 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Bills' 23-6 win over the Vikings on Monday night.
story: Cook was repeatedly stonewalled through three quarters by a Vikings run defense that had been fairly beatable, but the star running back continued to get opportunities to test Minnesota's defensive front. That approach finally began paying off on an early fourth-quarter marathon scoring drive, one where Cook recorded runs of nine, six and 11 yards before capping off the march with a five-yard scoring rush to extend Buffalo's 13-6 lead. Cook ultimately fell just a carry short of tying his career high, and he eclipsed the century mark on the ground for the fourth time this season.
