The fifth-year pro's trip to the end zone extended his touchdown streak to seven games as well, and Cook will head into a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Jets just 186 rushing yards short of his fourth straight 1,000-yard campaign.

headline: Cook rushed 21 times for 80 yards and a touchdown while catching two of three targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 36-10 win over the Ravens.
story: Cook gave the Bills some breathing room with a five-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to extend Buffalo's lead to 23-10. He was evaluated for a head injury later in the game but received clearance to return and notched one more carry after that point. After being held to 57 rushing yards without a touchdown by the Texans in Week 1, Cook has rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in six consecutive games. Extending that streak won't be easy in Week 9 against Minnesota's elite defense on MNF.

headline: After being evaluated for a head injury, Cook was cleared to return to Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Cook had headed to the medical tent to get checked out, but the Bills' top back has returned to the contest. Prior to his exit, Cook had logged 20 carries for 76 yards and a TD.

headline: Cook (undisclosed) headed to the blue medical tent during Sunday's game against the Ravens after absorbing a hard hit, Matt Parrino reports.
story: Prior to that, Cook -- who was able to walk off the field his own -- carried 20 times for 76 yards and a TD. While he's out of the game, Ray Davis and Ty Johnson are next up for Buffalo's backfield touches.

headline: Cook rushed 22 times for 95 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for 58 yards in the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Cook put together productive runs throughout the afternoon, and he added a 26-yard reception as part of an impressive day as a pass catcher. The standout running back extended his streak of games with at least one rushing touchdown to five as well, crossing the goal line from three yards out with 4:43 remaining in the contest. Cook has put up between 75 and 154 rushing yards in the last five games after opening the season with a modest 57-yard showing on the ground against the Texans, and he's already amassed 716 yards from scrimmage over six games going into a Week 8 home showdown on Sunday, Nov. 1, against the Ravens following a Week 7 bye.

headline: Cook rushed 10 times for 121 yards and a touchdown and brought in his only target for seven yards in the Bills' 37-34 overtime win over the Rams on Monday night. He also committed two fumbles, losing one.
story: Cook put together another highly efficient night that saw him gain significant chunks of yards on multiple carries, and which featured his fifth rushing touchdown of the season on a 17-yard run in the later portion of the second quarter. However, Cook dodged what would have been a major blemish on his night -- a lost fumble at the Rams' 20-yard line in overtime -- when Josh Allen subsequently mounted a successful game-winning drive following a blocked field goal by Buffalo's special teams. Cook will take 532 rushing yards and an average of 5.6 yards per carry into a Week 6 road matchup against the Raiders on Sunday.

headline: Cook rushed 12 times for 75 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for eight yards in the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Cook consistently ripped off productive gains on the ground against the Patriots' defense, with his longest run of the day going for a relatively modest 17 yards. Cook's overall rushing opportunities were still somewhat capped, and he finished with a new season low in carries. However, the talented back extended his streak of games with a rushing TD to three when he went in from eight yards out early in the second quarter. Cook has now averaged well over 6.0 yards per carry for three straight games and is up to 421 rushing yards and three scores on the ground heading into a Week 5 road showdown against the Rams on Monday night, Oct. 12.

headline: Sanders (shoulder) is active for Thursday's game against Kansas City.
story: Sanders has been officially cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a shoulder injury, and his presence means DeWayne Carter will revert to a rotational role at defensive end for Thanksgiving Day. Sanders has 11 tackles (five solo) through five regular-season games.

headline: Sanders (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Thursday night's game against the Chiefs.
story: Sanders logged three consecutive limited sessions during Week 12 prep. The defensive tackle missed the Bills' Week 11 win over the Dolphins due to his shoulder injury and appears to be a game-time decision for Thursday's primetime showdown with the Chiefs. If Sanders must miss consecutive games, DeWayne Carter will likely start at defensive end alongside Deone Walker and Ed Oliver in the Bills' 3-4 defensive front.

headline: Sanders (shoulder) is inactive for Sunday's game against Miami.
story: Sanders logged a full practice Wednesday, though he posted limited sessions on Thursday and Friday. After carrying a questionable designation ahead of Sunday's meeting with the Dolphins, he has been ruled out, meaning his next opportunity to get back on the field will come in Week 12 versus the Chiefs.

headline: Sanders (appendix) practiced in full Thursday.
story: Sanders missed Week 1 due to a knee injury and then had an appendectomy. He logged two limited practices last week but didn't play versus New England on Sunday. However, with a full practice under his belt to begin Week 5 prep, Sanders is a good bet to suit up Monday night against the Rams.

headline: Sanders (appendix) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Sanders is still healing from appendix surgery on Sep. 22, though he did return to practice Thursday. Landon Jackson may get more playing time alongside Ed Oliver and Deone Walker while Sanders is out.

headline: Sanders (appendix) was a limited practice participant Thursday.
story: Sanders underwent surgery to have his appendix removed on Tuesday, Sept. 22, and he didn't play in Week 3 against the Chargers. The second-year pro didn't practice Wednesday to begin Week 4 prep, but he was able to participate in a limited capacity Thursday. That's a good sign Sanders is healing well, though it remains to be seen if he'll be ready to suit up Sunday versus New England.

headline: Williams (calf) is active for Thursday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Williams didn't play against the Dolphins in Week 11 due to a calf injury, but the fourth-year pro has been cleared by medical staff to play Thursday. He has accumulated 61 tackles (27 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass defenses (including two interceptions) and one fumble recovery across nine regular-season games.

headline: Williams (calf) is questionable for Thursday night's game against the Chiefs.
story: The linebacker was injured in Week 10 against the Jets and missed last Sunday's victory over Miami. He was able to log a trio of limited practices this week, giving Williams a chance to return from a one-game absence. Williams has piled up 61 tackles (27 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass breakups, including a pair of interceptions, and one fumble recovery across nine games this season.

headline: Williams (calf) was listed as limited for Monday's estimated practice.
story: Williams did not play in Sunday's win over the Dolphins due to a calf injury that kept him out of all Week 11 prep. The inside linebacker's estimated presence Monday is promising, but he will likely need to suit up for on-field work Tuesday and Wednesday to get the green light ahead of Thursday night's Thanksgiving showdown with the Chiefs.

headline: Williams (calf) has been ruled out for Sunday's matchup against the Dolphins, Maddy Glab of the Bills' official site reports.
story: Williams missed the last three practices with a calf injury he sustained in Week 10 against the Jets. The 25-year-old is set to miss his first game since Week 5 of the 2025 regular season. Kaleb Elarms-Orr should be in line to start in place of Williams, alongside Terrel Bernard.

headline: Williams (calf) didn't participate in Buffalo's walkthrough Wednesday.
story: Williams is still dealing with the calf injury that forced him to exit the Week 10 win over the Jets early. If the 2023 third-round pick ends up being unable to play in Sunday's matchup versus the Dolphins, Kaleb Elarms-Orr would be in line to start at inside linebacker in his place alongside Terrel Bernard.

headline: Williams (calf) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Williams sustained a calf injury in the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest. The linebacker logged nine tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defensed before leaving the game. Rookie linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr will likely finish the remainder of the contest at inside linebacker next to Terrel Bernard.

headline: Williams logged five tackles (three solo) and one pass defensed for an interception in the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Despite a relatively poor showing from a struggling Bills defense, Williams picked off Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins in the third quarter of Sunday's contest. The linebacker's stolen possession, the first interception of his NFL career, led to the Bills extending the lead from 16-13 to 23-13 with 6:22 remaining in the third quarter.

headline: Benford (groin) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Benford will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a groin injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Jets. Maxwell Hairston should see a bump in defensive snaps at outside cornerback in the absence of Benford, whose next chance to play is Week 13 against the Patriots on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Benford (groin) is questionable for Thursday night's game against the Chiefs.
story: After being listed as DNP on Monday, Benford was estimated to be a limited participant at Tuesday and Wednesday's walkthroughs. He's looking to return from a one-game absence that forced him to miss last Sunday's win over the Dolphins.

headline: Benford (groin) was a limited participant in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.
story: Benford is working through a groin injury that caused him to be sidelined for Sunday's win against the Dolphins. His return to practice is encouraging, even if it was in a limited capacity, and a full session Wednesday would put the fifth-year pro on track to return for Thanksgiving Day against the Chiefs. If Benford cannot play Thursday, then the Bills would likely elevate Tre'Davious White from the practice squad and rotate him with Maxwell Hairston at outside cornerback opposite Davison Igbinosun.

headline: Benford (groin) was listed as a non-participant on Monday's practice estimate.
story: The cornerback sat out of Sunday's win over the Dolphins after exiting the previous week's victory over the Jets with the injury. Buffalo still has two more practices this week ahead of Thursday night's clash with Kansas City, but Benford is not on track to play at this point. If he can't go, Tre'Davious White, Jordan Hancock and Maxwell Hairston could be in line to see more snaps.

headline: Benford (groin) is out for Sunday's matchup against the Dolphins, Maddy Glab of the Bills' official site reports.
story: Benford missed a trio of practices ahead of Week 11 after exiting early against the Jets with a groin injury. Sunday's game against the Dolphins marks the 26-year-old's second miss of the season. He has 33 tackles (23 solo) and eight pass deflections through eight regular-season appearances.

headline: Benford (groin) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Benford suffered a groin injury during Sunday's game against the Jets that knocked him out of that contest early, and now his availability for Week 11 is in serious jeopardy. Unless he's able to practice in some capacity Friday, odds are low he'll be able to suit up for Sunday's game versus the Dolphins.

headline: Benford (groin) was estimated as a nonparticipant in Wednesday's walkthrough.
story: Benford exited the Bills' Week 10 win over the Jets early with a groin injury and did not return to the contest. The star cornerback remains sidelined as he manages the issue. Benford will need to upgrade to at least a limited participant by Friday's practice session for a shot at avoiding an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

headline: Benford (groin) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Benford was cleared to play Sunday after recovering from a wrist injury, but he is now dealing with a groin issue, which will prevent him from playing for the rest of Week 10. Dee Alford (concussion) was ruled out, so the Bills' secondary will lean more heavily on the likes of Jordan Hancock, Maxwell Hairston and Damar Hamlin.

headline: Benford (wrist) is active for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Benford injured his wrist during the Bills' Week 9 win over the Vikings. He drew the questionable tag for Week 10 after posting an LP-LP-FP practice log, and the fifth-year defensive back has been cleared by medical staff to play in Sunday's AFC East tilt. Benford has accumulated 31 tackles (21 solo) and seven pass defenses through seven regular-season games.

headline: Benford (wrist) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Benford injured his wrist during the Bills' Monday night win over the Vikings, though he returned to the contest after sustaining the injury. The cornerback started Week 10 prep with consecutive limited practices before upgrading to a full participant in Friday's session. Benford will likely suit up for Sunday's contest to start in a secondary that should be bolstered by the trade-deadline acquisition of Amani Hooker.

headline: Benford (wrist) was limited in Wednesday's walkthrough practice.
story: Benford injured his wrist in Monday night's win over the Vikings but was able to return to the contest. Across seven starts this season, he has 31 tackles (21 solo) and seven pass breakups on 89 percent of the defensive snaps.

headline: Benford (wrist) has returned to Monday night's matchup with Minnesota.
story: Benford was briefly sidelined with a wrist injury late in the first half, but he has now returned to the field following the break. He will continue to be tasked with attempting to slow down Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison throughout the rest of the contest.

headline: Benford (wrist) is questionable to return to Monday night's contest against the Vikings.
story: Benford suffered a wrist injury late in the second quarter, and he ultimately was spotted being carted off the field, per Jay Skurski of The Buffalo News. In Benford's absence, Maxwell Hairston and Davison Igbinosun will stand to operate as the team's top two cornerbacks versus Minnesota.

headline: Benford (toe) does not carry an injury designation into Monday night's game against the Rams, Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic reports.
story: Benford has been given the green light to return from a one-game absence due to a toe injury that he sustained during the Bills' Week 3 win over the Chargers. He'll resume his starting spot at outside cornerback, and while rookie first-rounder Maxwell Hairston will start opposite Benford, rookie second-rounder Davison Igbinosun will also be involved in the Bills' secondary, per Nick Suss of ESPN.com.

headline: Benford (toe) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
story: Benford suffered a toe injury against the Chargers in Week 3 and didn't practice at all last week. After missing Sunday's matchup against the Patriots, the veteran cornerback was able to return to practice, albeit in a limited capacity, Thursday. The Bills play Monday against the Rams, so Benford will have two more days to try to ramp up to full practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of that contest.

headline: Benford (toe) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: The fourth-year pro was absent from practice heading into Sunday's game after exiting in the third quarter of the Patriots' Week 3 loss to Jacksonville. Davison Igbinosun is expected to see more playing time with Benford out.

headline: Benford (toe) did not participate in practice Wednesday or Thursday.
story: Benford suffered a toe injury during the third quarter of Sunday's Week 3 win over the Chargers and didn't return to the contest. With consecutive DNPs to begin the week of prep, the veteran cornerback's status for Sunday's matchup against the Patriots is looking very iffy. Should Benford not be able to suit up for that game, Davison Igbinosun could draw the start.

headline: Danna re-signed with the Bills on Tuesday.
story: Danna was released by Buffalo on Monday but he will return to the team after one day as a free agent. The 28-year-old has appeared in one contest with the team this season, failing to record any stats while logging eight defensive snaps and a one snap with the special-teams unit in Week 2 versus Detroit.

headline: Buffalo released Danna on Monday.
story: In a corresponding transaction, the Bills signed cornerback Anthony Kendall from their practice squad to their 53-man roster Monday. Danna will become an unrestricted free agent and likely start to seek another opportunity with a different team.

headline: Gaines (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice.
story: Gaines missed the Bills' last two games while recovering from a calf injury, but his full session Wednesday indicates that he'll return for Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Jets. He's accumulated 11 tackles (three solo) and one fumble recovery through six regular-season games, and his return gives the Bills additional depth on the defensive line.

headline: Gaines (calf) is inactive for Monday's game versus Minnesota.
story: Gaines didn't suit up for the Week 8 win over the Ravens. While he did practice in a limited capacity Saturday, he still isn't ready to get back on the field. The 30-year-old has appeared in six games during the 2026 campaign, amassing 11 total tackles (three solo) and one fumble recovery.

headline: Gaines (calf) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Gaines was added to Friday's practice report as a limited participant due to a knee injury. He was unable to get clearance from medical staff to play Sunday and will be sidelined for the first time all season as a result. The veteran defensive tackle has tallied 11 tackles and a fumble recovery through the Bills' first six games.

headline: Bell (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Bell made his third appearance of the 2026 campaign in Week 10, though he went without a catch. With Tyrell Shavers (knee) cleared to play for Sunday's divisional clash with Miami after spending time on injured reserve, Bell's services won't be needed. His next opportunity to play will come in Week 12 against the Chiefs.

headline: Bell will make his NFL regular-season debut against the Rams on Monday due to the absence of Joshua Palmer (shoulder), Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network reports.
story: Bell has been a healthy scratch for each of the Bills' first four games of the regular season. However, he's expected to absorb Palmer's reps during Monday's game, and Bell could take on an even larger role if DJ Moore (shoulder) is also ruled out. Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman and tight end Dalton Kincaid figure to be Josh Allen's go-to pass catchers if Moore cannot play, but Bell will at least be in the mix for targets in his NFL debut.

headline: Rousseau (back) was a full participant in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.
story: Rousseau was limited in Monday's session while managing a back injury, but his full participation Tuesday indicates that the sixth-year edge rusher will be available against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving Day. Rousseau logged two sacks against the Dolphins on Sunday, and his 10.0 sacks through 10 regular-season games are second-most in the NFL behind Will Anderson (11.5).

headline: Rousseau (back) was listed as limited for Monday's estimated practice.
story: Rousseau is coming off having recorded two more sacks against the Dolphins on Sunday. The linebacker now has four such games this season, and his 10.0 sacks in 10 games have already surpassed his previous single-season total of 8.0. The 26-year-old picked up a back injury in the win and will likely need to practice both Tuesday and Wednesday to avoid any injury designation ahead of Thursday's Thanksgiving showdown with the Chiefs.

headline: Rousseau logged four tackles (two solo) and two passes defensed in the Bills' 29-26 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Rousseau notched 2.0 sacks in each of the first three games of the 2026 regular season. The outside linebacker's historic streak concluded in Week 4, when he was unable to log any sacks over 81 percent of the Bills' defensive snaps. The Bills' lack of defensive pressure against quarterback Drake Maye was a key component in the outcome of the early-season divisional matchup.

headline: Rousseau logged eight tackles (five solo), including 2.0 sacks, in the Bills' 24-16 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Rousseau leads the NFL with 6.0 sacks, having logged 2.0 sacks in each of the first three games of the 2026 regular season. The linebacker has had a stunning breakout since switching to defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's 3-4 defense. The 26-year-old is entering his sixth NFL season and has begun to make a compelling early case that should put him on Defensive Player of the Year ballots if he can keep producing throughout the season.

headline: Brown (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Brown is a somewhat surprising activation after he missed Week 8 with a back injury before injuring his ankle in Week 9. The right tackle is set to suit up Sunday despite missing both the Thursday and Friday practice sessions in Week 10 prep. With Dion Dawkins, Alec Anderson and Brown all returning, the Bills will field a full starting offensive line for the first time since before the Week 7 bye.

headline: Brown (ankle) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Brown overcame a back injury to suit up for the Bills' Week 9 win over the Vikings on Monday. The right tackle picked up an ankle injury during the contest and ended Week 10 prep with consecutive DNPs. If the right tackle does not suit up for Sunday's game, Tylan Grable would be set to return to a starting role against the Jets.

headline: Brown (back) does not have a designation for Monday's matchup in Minnesota.
story: Brown missed last Sunday's win over Baltimore, but he'll be back in action Monday after logging an LP/LP/FP practice progression this week. His return will be especially critical if fellow starting offensive tackle Dion Dawkins (ribs, questionable) isn't able to suit up.

headline: Brown (back) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Brown has been working through a back issue that he sustained in Week 5 against the Rams. The injury is severe enough that he won't suit up Sunday, so Tylan Grable figures to start at right tackle. Brown's next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 9.

headline: Brown (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Brown injured his back against the Rams in Week 5 but was able to play through the issue in Week 6. He was a DNP on Wednesday and Thursday before logging a limited session Friday, and if he cannot play Sunday, then Tylan Grable would be a top candidate to start at right tackle.

headline: Brown (back) has been ruled out for the remainder of Monday night's game versus the Rams.
story: Brown sustained a back injury early in the contest, and his night has now officially come to a premature end. Tylan Grable will continue to operate as the team's starting right tackle in Brown's place.

headline: Brown (back) is questionable to return to Monday night's contest against the Rams.
story: Brown suffered a back injury in the first half of the contest, and his status for the remainder of the game is now uncertain. In his absence, Tylan Grable has taken over at right tackle versus Los Angeles.

headline: Hamlin (toe) is active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Hamlin missed the first two practices of Week 11 prep due to a toe injury, but he earned the questionable tag following Friday's limited session. The sixth-year defensive back was cleared by medical staff to play Sunday following pregame warmups, and he'll provide depth in the secondary behind Amani Hooker and Cole Bishop.

headline: Hamlin (toe) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Miami.
story: Hamlin was held out of practice in each of the first two practices of Week 11 prep due to a toe injury. He put together a limited session Friday to draw the questionable tag, but if he cannot play against the Dolphins, then Jalon Kilgore and Sam Franklin would operate as the Bills' backup safeties behind Amani Hooker and Cole Bishop for Sunday's AFC East tilt.

headline: Hamlin (toe) was estimated to be a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough.
story: Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News spotted Hamlin in a walking boot during the limited session. The reserve free safety played 17 defensive snaps and 17 special-teams snaps in Sunday's win over the Jets, likely sustaining the toe injury in one of his 34 reps.

headline: Hamlin (leg) has returned to Buffalo's matchup versus the Vikings on Monday, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.
story: Hamlin is back in the game after having briefly exited while dealing with cramping. Geno Stone had replaced Hamlin at safety while he was sidelined.

headline: Hamlin (leg) is probable to return to Buffalo's matchup versus the Vikings on Monday,
story: Hamlin is dealing with cramping, leaving his status for the rest of the matchup up in the air. Geno Stone will fill in for Hamlin at safety if he ends up being unable to return.

headline: Hooker logged two solo tackles and one pass defensed in the Bills' 26-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Hooker has now played in two games for the Bills, logging 100 percent of the team's defensive reps in Week 11 and 98 percent in Week 12. The strong safety has made for a good pairing with Cole Bishop, and the duo has helped the Bills' defense extend its streak of not allowing a touchdown to 15 straight quarters of play.

headline: Hooker (knee) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Hooker was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday due to a knee injury, but the veteran safety was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's AFC East showdown. Hooker made his Bills debut against the Jets in Week 10, when he logged seven tackles (four solo) and one pass defense in a 31-12 win for Buffalo.

headline: Hooker (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough.
story: Hooker likely sustained his knee injury in the Bills' Week 10 win over the Jets. The strong safety played all 70 defensive snaps in his first game as a Bill, logging seven tackles (four solo) and one pass defensed in the contest. The trade deadline acquisition from the Titans will need to continue to log limited or full practice sessions through Friday for a chance to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

headline: Head coach Joe Brady confirmed Friday that Hooker will play Sunday against the Jets, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports.
story: Hooker was one of several players who changed teams before Tuesday's trade deadline, with the Titans sending the veteran safety and a 2027 fifth-round pick to the Bills in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick. Hooker's addition bolsters a Bills defense that ranks 29th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (238.8) this season. It's unclear whether he'll start alongside Cole Bishop immediately or operate in a rotational role in the secondary in his Bills debut.

headline: The Bills acquired Hooker and a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Titans on Tuesday in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
story: As he moves on to Buffalo following a seven-plus-season run in Tennessee, Hooker should immediately step into a starting role at safety alongside Cole Bishop. The Bills had previously been leaning on Damar Hamlin and the since-released C.J. Gardner-Johnson to fill snaps at that spot in the secondary, but Hooker is expected to provide a notable upgrade. Through seven appearances with Tennessee this season, Hooker had recorded a career-high-tying five interceptions to go with 52 tackles.

headline: Hooker posted five tackles (two solo) during Sunday's 27-24 loss to Cleveland.
story: Sunday was the fourth time this season that Hooker played every single defensive snap, although his five stops were his lowest of the 2026 campaign. The veteran safety is up to 46 tackles (29 solo) and three pass defenses (including two interceptions) through six regular-season games, and he's second on the Titans in total stops behind rookie linebacker Anthony Hill (68).

headline: Hooker logged 13 tackles (seven solo) and one interception during the Titans' 26-20 win over the Colts on Sunday.
story: The Titans captured their first win of the season Sunday thanks largely to their defense and special teams. Hooker did his part with a game-high 13 combined tackles, and he made a toe-tap sideline interception off Daniel Jones late in the first quarter that stopped the Colts' red zone drive in its tracks. Hooker is up to 41 tackles (27 solo) and three pass defenses (including two interceptions) across five regular-season games and is on track to crack the tackling century mark for the first time in his eight-year NFL career.

headline: Hooker (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Hooker has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is set to suit up in Sunday's game. The starting safety missed the Titans' Week 5 loss to the Texans due to the injury.

headline: Hooker (concussion) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
story: Hooker was sidelined in Week 5 versus the Texans because of a concussion he suffered back in Week 4 at Baltimore, but it looks like he's making good progress towards returning to game action. With that said, he'll still need to obtain clearance from an independent neurologist before exiting league concussion protocol and getting the okay to play again.

headline: Hooker (concussion) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Hooker did not participate in a single Week 5 prep session as he dealt with a concussion sustained against the Ravens in the Titans' Week 4 loss. The strong safety's upgrade to limited participation to start the week is a good sign that he should be able to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before the team's Week 6 showdown with the Colts.

headline: Hooker (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
story: Hooker entered the league's concussion protocol following the Titans' 24-18 loss to the Ravens in Week 4. He was held out of practice all week and will observe Sunday's game from the sidelines, so Tony Adams will likely start alongside Kevin Winston at safety. Hooker's next chance to play is Week 6 against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 18.

headline: Hooker reported concussion symptoms following Sunday's 24-18 loss to the Ravens and won't practice Wednesday, Jim Wyatt of the Titans' official site reports.
story: Hooker finished with six solo tackles in the Week 4 loss. He'll have two more chances to progress through the protocol and practice this week, but even if he upgrades to full participation, he'll still need to pass an evaluation from an independent neurologist before being cleared to play Sunday against the Texans. Tony Adams would likely start next to Kevin Winston (shoulder) if Hooker isn't cleared to play this weekend.

headline: Franks (wrist) was a limited participant at practice Friday.
story: Franks popped up on the Panthers' injury report with a wrist injury Thursday, and now there's a cloud over his status for Week 12. He may end up taking an injury designation into game day if he's not able to upgrade to full participation at practice Saturday.

headline: Franks played all 21 of his snaps on special teams and was credited with two tackles in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
story: Franks has been active for all 10 of the Panthers' games to date, but he's been utilized almost exclusively on special teams. He hasn't logged more than nine snaps on offense in any contest and has yet to draw a target.

headline: Okereke (foot) did not participate at practice Friday.
story: Okereke has been sidelined for the Panthers' last three games because of a foot injury, and his availability for Week 12 is now in doubt. Unless he's able to return to practice Saturday, it's not likely he'll be able to suit up Monday against the Buccaneers.

headline: Okereke (foot) was listed as a non-participant in Carolina's practice estimate Thursday, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: Okereke is in danger of missing a third consecutive game as he continues to deal with a knee injury suffered during Week 8. If he ends up being unable to play in Monday's matchup versus the Buccaneers, Tyrel Dodson will likely get another start at inside linebacker.

headline: Okereke (foot) is out for Sunday's matchup against the Ravens, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: Okereke hasn't practiced all week and will miss his third straight game due to a foot injury likely suffered in Week 8. Tyrel Dodson is slated to get another start.

headline: Okereke (foot) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Okereke has been sidelined for each of the Panthers' last two games while recovering from a foot injury, which has also prevented him from practicing. He has two more chances to return to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's home game against the Ravens. Tyrel Dodson has stepped into a starting role at inside linebacker in Okereke's absence.

headline: Okereke (foot) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Okereke was estimated as a non-participant at Wednesday's walkthrough, and he remained sidelined for Thursday's full-speed practice. Barring a return to practice Friday, Okereke could be in line for a second consecutive absence Sunday against the Saints after he racked up 49 tackles (31 solo) through his first seven games with the Panthers.

headline: Okereke (foot) was estimated as DNP on Wednesday's practice report.
story: The veteran linebacker missed last Sunday's loss to the Broncos, so Devin Lloyd and Tyrel Dodson handled the bulk of the snaps at linebacker for Carolina. Through seven games this season, Okereke has produced 49 tackles (31 solo), including 1.0 sacks, five pass breakups, including an interception, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.

headline: Okereke (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's matchup against the Broncos.
story: Okereke is dealing with a foot injury that caused him to sit out practice all week. As a result, he's going to miss his first game since the 2024 campaign. Tyrel Dodson figures to get a start at linebacker in Okereke's stead.

headline: Okereke (foot) did not practice Thursday, Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports.
story: It was a second consecutive DNP for Okereke, who has yet to miss a game this season. The 30-year-old has one more opportunity to practice ahead of Sunday's game versus Denver or he could carry an injury designation. Okereke has 49 total tackles (31 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one interception in his seven appearances during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Okereke (foot) didn't participate in Carolina's practice Wednesday.
story: Okereke popped up on the injury report due to a foot injury and is now in danger of missing his first game of the season. If the 2019 third-round pick ends up being unable to play in Sunday's matchup against the Broncos, Tyrel Dodson would likely get the start in his place.

headline: Okereke tallied 10 tackles (seven solo) and a defensed pass in Sunday's loss to Tampa Bay.
story: Okereke paced the Panthers in stops during a tough day for the team's defense, as Tampa Bay cruised to a 43-13 win. The veteran linebacker reached the double-digit tackle mark for the first time this season, and he's posted six or more stops in five of his six games. On the season, Okereke leads Carolina with 44 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, and has added five defensed passes (including one interception) and one forced fumble.

headline: Okereke recorded eight tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two pass defenses during the Panthers' 25-14 win over the Eagles in Week 6.
story: Okereke led the Panthers in both combined and solo tackles in Week 6, and he set the tone early for the defense by sacking Tanner McKee on the Eagles' first offensive play of the game. It was Okereke's first sack of the season and matches his total across 17 regular-season games with the Giants in 2025. The veteran linebacker is up to 34 tackles (21 solo), four pass defenses (including one interception) and one forced fumble through five regular-season games.

headline: Evans (Achilles) was a limited participant at practice Friday.
story: Evans took a step in the right direction by practicing to some extent Friday after being listed as non-participant on Thursday's estimate. He'll have one more chance to reach full participation Saturday ahead of Monday's game against the Buccaneers. Evans had his best game of 2026 in the Week 11 win over Baltimore, catching all five of his targets for 44 yards and his first touchdown of the season.

headline: Evans (Achilles) was listed as a DNP on Thursday's estimated practice report, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: Evans may have picked up the injury during the Panthers' 35-33 win over the Ravens this past Sunday, when he caught all five of his targets for 44 yards, which included a 23-yard grab in the first quarter. Given that the Panthers didn't practice Thanksgiving Day, Evans' practice participation over the next two days will be worth monitoring ahead of Monday's game against the Buccaneers.

headline: Evans caught all five of his targets for 44 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
story: Evans was able to reel in a season-high five passes while notching multiple receptions for the fourth time in five weeks. The tight end's biggest moment of the game came in the first quarter when he secured a 23-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Bryce Young, registering his first score of the year. Evans has now caught 17 of 20 targets for 191 yards and a touchdown over 10 contests during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Evans caught both of his two targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 26-21 loss versus the Broncos.
story: For the third game in a row, Evans drew exactly two targets and caught both of them Sunday. With that said, he also again trailed in snaps at tight end (31) behind teammates Tommy Tremble (46) and Darren Waller (35), both of whom also drew more targets in Week 9. Evans' role in the Panthers' passing offense isn't big enough to warrant fantasy consideration in most formats going into a Week 10 matchup at New Orleans.

headline: Evans gathered in both targets for 39 yards during Sunday's 43-13 loss versus Tampa Bay.
story: Evans logged more offensive snaps than Darren Waller for the third consecutive contest. However, despite the increased involvement, it was another unproductive effort from the 23-year-old, who now has just eight catches for 105 yards in six regular-season games in 2026.

headline: Tremble (knee) remained a limited participant at practice Friday.
story: Tremble was limited again Friday after being listed a limited participant on Thursday's practice estimate. He has one more opportunity to upgrade to full participation Saturday, which could help Tremble avoid an injury designation for Monday's game against the Buccaneers.

headline: Tremble (knee) was listed as a limited participant on Thursday's estimated practice report, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: Tremble was cleared to play through a knee injury against the Ravens in Week 11, when he hauled in his lone target for 18 yards while playing 59 of 71 offensive snaps (83.1 percent) in a 35-33 win for the Panthers. Carolina did not practice Thanksgiving Day, so Tremble's participation over the next two days will provide clarity on his status ahead of Monday's NFC South showdown against Tampa Bay.

headline: Tremble caught one pass for 18 yards in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
story: The tight end played on 82 percent of the offensive snaps but only saw one target. Tremble has 36 targets across 10 appearances this season, recording 26 catches for 245 yards and three scores.

headline: Tremble (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
story: Tremble opened Week 11 prep as a non-participant Wednesday due to a knee injury, which he followed up with limited sessions Thursday and Friday and a questionable tag for Sunday. The same can be said for fellow TE Darren Waller (knee), and both now are available to the Panthers offense. In nine outings this season, Tremble has compiled a 25-227-3 line on 35 targets.

headline: Tremble (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Tremble put together a DNP-LP-LP practice log during Week 11 prep while managing a knee injury that he picked up during the Panthers' 20-17 win over the Saints in Week 10. Darren Waller (knee) also is listed as questionable, which leaves Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders as the Panthers' healthy tight ends on the 53-man roster heading into the weekend. Tremble's status for Sunday's game may not officially be known until 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, when Carolina announces its list of inactive players.

headline: Tremble (knee) was limited in Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: Both Tremble and Darren Waller (knee) were upgraded to limited work after being DNP on Wednesday. Friday's participation levels and injury designations will tell a better story for their Week 11 availability versus Baltimore. Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders are next in line at tight end for Carolina.

headline: Tremble didn't practice Wednesday due to a knee issue, with head coach Dave Canales noting after the session that the tight end's injury is a "concern," Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports.
story: Canales said the same about Darren Waller (knee), who was also a non-participant to open Week 11 prep. The practice activity of the Panthers' top two tight ends will thus warrant monitoring over the next two days to get a sense if either player will be available to play Sunday versus the Ravens. Beyond Tremble and Waller, the Panthers have three other tight ends -- Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders -- on the 53-man roster.

headline: Tremble caught four of five targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints.
story: The tight end's five targets tied Chuba Hubbard for second on the team behind Tetairoa McMillan's seven. Tremble has yet to reach 50 receiving yards in a game this season, and his four catches matched his season high. More of a blocker and red-zone specialist, Tremble has very little fantasy appeal in a Carolina offense that likes to use three tight ends.

headline: Tremble caught four of six targets for 24 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.
story: The Panthers continue to use three tight ends heavily on offense, and Tremble has settled in as the do-it-all tight member of the trio, while Darren Waller is solely a pass catcher and Mitchell Evans focuses on blocking. Tremble doesn't have nearly the upside of Waller, but the former still draws Bryce Young's eye in the red zone. On the year, Tremble is up to 21 grabs for 179 yards and three touchdowns on 30 targets across eight games. He's not an exciting fantasy option.

headline: Tremble hauled in one of two targets for eight yards during Sunday's 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers.
story: Tremble had two touchdowns in the 25-14 win over the Eagles in Week 6. However, it was a different story in Week 7, with the 26-year-old catching just one pass for the second time this season. While Tremble could find the end zone again at some point moving forward, he likely won't be consistent enough to be considered anything other than a desperation fantasy option, especially while Darren Waller is on the field.

headline: Tremble caught all four targets for 46 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 25-14 win over the Eagles.
story: Tremble played 54 snaps to Mitchell Evans' 43 and Darren Waller's 36, and Tremble ran the most routes of the trio. His touchdowns were both of the red-zone variety, as he scored from 12 and 19 yards out. The tight end entered Sunday with 11 catches for 82 yards on 15 targets, so he's not worth chasing in fantasy ahead of next Sunday's date with the Bucs.

headline: Tremble (ribs) has no injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles.
story: Tremble upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice after opening Week 6 prep as a limited participant. The tight end is all set to suit up for the Panthers' showdown with the Eagles on Sunday.

headline: Tremble (ribs) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday.
story: Tremble played a reduced role at tight end in Week 4 versus Detroit before the Panthers' bye in Week 5, and it seems plausible that whatever rib injury he's dealing with now could also have been the reason for that. In any case, he'll probably have to practice in full Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Tremble caught all four targets for 12 yards in Sunday night's win over the Lions.
story: Involved in a three-man committee at tight end, Tremble's 38 snaps trailed both Mitchell Evans (46) and Darren Waller (40) at the position. He also ran fewer routes than both. Tremble's 11 grabs this season have produced 82 scoreless yards on 15 targets. He has no fantasy appeal.

headline: Brooks (groin) practiced without limitations Friday.
story: Brooks has shed any practice limitations, but he'll still need to be added back to the active roster to play Monday in Tampa Bay. Even if Brooks gets the green light to suit up and is activated by the Panthers, he'll likely have to settle for a change-of-pace role behind Chuba Hubbard against Tampa Bay's excellent run defense.

headline: Brooks (groin) was estimated as a full practice participant on Thursday's report, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: The Panthers didn't practice Thursday for Thanksgiving, so the report provided by the team was an estimation. Given that, Brooks' practice participation over the next two days will provide a better indication of his status heading into Monday's NFC South tilt against the Buccaneers. However, Brooks would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Week 12. The third-year running back landed on IR in late September after undergoing surgery to repair a core-muscle injury that he sustained against the Falcons in Week 2.

headline: Head coach Dave Canales suggested Wednesday that a decision on Brooks (core) being activated from injured reserve before his 21-day window expires next week will hinge on the Panthers having a role available to him, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: After having his window opened Nov. 11, Brooks was a limited practice participant throughout Week 10 before practicing fully for all three of the Panthers' Week 11 sessions. Brooks is poised to remain a full practice participant leading up to Monday's game at Tampa Bay, but he doesn't appear to be a lock to get activated from IR for that contest. Canales noted that Chuba Hubbard has thrived of late as the Panthers' lead back, while Trevor Etienne is coming off a positive showing as the top complement to Hubbard in this past Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens. Meanwhile, Anthony Tyus has carved out a role as Carolina's kickoff returner, and AJ Dillon looms as a fourth option at running back. Given the crowding in the Carolina backfield along with his lack of contributions on special teams, Brooks may need to look impressive in practice this week for the Panthers to justify adding him back to the 53-man roster.

headline: Brooks (groin) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Brooks was a full practice participant in all three sessions during Week 11 prep. However, the third-year running back is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve, and he's slated to miss his eighth consecutive game while recovering from a groin injury. Trevor Etienne, Anthony Tyus and AJ Dillon will continue to operate as the Panthers' backfield depth options behind Chuba Hubbard in the absence of Brooks, whose next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Buccaneers on Monday, Nov. 30.

headline: Brooks (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
story: Brooks remains on injured reserve, so the questionable tag suggests Carolina at least may activate him ahead of Sunday's contest. If he's cleared to play, the running back would be in line to make his first appearance since Week 2, though he's no real threat to Chuba Hubbard's standing as the Panthers' lead back.

headline: Brooks (groin) remained a full participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: Brooks is still on injured reserve but appears to be tracking toward a Week 11 return against Baltimore on Sunday. Chuba Hubbard should remain head-and-shoulders above Brooks on the depth chart as the clear RB1 for Carolina, but the Panthers likely also want to use the rest of the season to see if Brooks can stay healthy for a stretch and produce when given opportunities. Brooks is worth adding in fantasy, but his role will need to be defined before plugging him in lineups.

headline: Brooks (groin) was a full participant at Wednesday's walkthrough.
story: Brooks was listed similarly last Wednesday before capping the week with back-to-back limited practices and receiving a doubtful tag for Week 10 action. He then was downgraded to out before this past Sunday's game at New Orleans. Brooks is seeking a return from injured reserve, where he's resided since after Week 2 due to core muscle surgery.

headline: Brooks (groin) has been downgraded from doubtful to out for Sunday's game against the Saints, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
story: Brooks ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices, but he was tagged as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Panthers. The third-year running back is not quite fully recovered from a groin injury that landed him on IR in late September, so his next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 22. Trevor Etienne, AJ Dillon and Anthony Tyus will continue to operate in rotational backfield roles behind Chuba Hubbard while Brooks is sidelined.

headline: Brooks (groin) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game at New Orleans after being limited in practice throughout the week, Kassidy Hill of the Panthers' official site reports.
story: Brooks remains on injured reserve and isn't likely to be activated by the 4:00 p.m. ET deadline Saturday. He was listed as a full practice participant at the beginning of the week, but coach Dave Canales revealed Friday that there was a reporting error with Brooks and CB Mike Jackson (groin), both of whom should have been listed as limited. Both were then listed as limited Thursday and Friday, with 'doubtful' designations for Sunday's game. Brooks appears on track to return for Week 11 or 12, at which point he could take a few touches away from Chuba Hubbard.

headline: Brooks (groin) was a full practice participant Thursday.
story: The Panthers also listed Brooks as 'FP' on Wednesday's estimated practice report. Now that he's actually logged a full practice, Brooks may have a real shot to be activated from injured reserve for Sunday's game at New Orleans. The Panthers would need to make that move by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday to have Brooks on the active roster Sunday.

headline: Brooks (groin) was listed as a full participant on Wednesday's estimated injury report.
story: Brooks hasn't played since Week 2 due to a groin injury that required core-muscle surgery and a stint on injured reserve. The Panthers designated him for return from IR on Wednesday, and he kicked off Week 10 prep with an uncapped walkthrough. How Brooks is listed on the injury report when Carolina holds practice Thursday and/or Friday may be the determining factor in his chances to play Sunday at New Orleans.

headline: The Panthers designated Brooks (core) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: As a result of the transaction, Brooks will return to practice Wednesday, and the Panthers will have 21 days to evaluate him for a return to the 53-man roster. Unless he logs multiple full practices this week, Brooks could face an uphill battle to getting activated ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints, but he'll likely be back in action for Carolina before the end of November. Once he's reinstated, Brooks will likely handle a complementary role behind lead back Chuba Hubbard.

headline: Head coach Dave Canales said Monday that the Panthers will spend the next two days discussing the status of Brooks (core), Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: Brooks, who remains on IR, was seen working off to the side during the Panthers' unofficial practice last Tuesday, per Joe Person of The Athletic, perhaps signaling some progress for the oft-injured RB, who last saw game action in Week 2. In Brooks' absence, Chuba Hubbard has dominated Carolina's backfield touches.

headline: Brooks (core) was seen working off to the side during the Panthers' unofficial practice Tuesday, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
story: The Panthers haven't yet opened Brooks' 21-day practice window, but that might happen soon after head coach Dave Canales said Monday that the young running back would "potentially" be designated for return from injured reserve this week. Brooks hasn't played since Week 2 after undergoing core-muscle surgery, so he'll likely need to turn in multiple full practices before the Panthers are comfortable clearing him for game action. Once he's activated from IR, Brooks will likely handle a supporting role out of the backfield behind starter Chubba Hubbard.

headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Monday that Brooks (core) will "potentially" be designated for return from injured reserve this week, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
story: Canales noted that Brooks still has some checkpoints he needs to hit in his recovery process before getting the green light to practice, but the running back looks to have at least made progress on some level since undergoing core-muscle surgery Sept. 23. The running back has already spent more than four games on IR and will be eligible to be added back to the 53-man roster whenever the Panthers deem him healthy. Once activated, Brooks will likely have to settle for a change-of-pace role behind lead back Chubba Hubbard.

headline: Brooks (core) was seen jogging at practice Thursday, Sheena Quick of Fox Sports Radio 1340 reports.
story: Brooks appears to be making incremental progress in his recovery from core muscle surgery, though he wasn't in uniform Thursday and has yet to be cleared for participation in practice drills while he remains on injured reserve. The 2024 second-round pick has suited up for just five of a possible 38 regular-season games in his career and will miss a minimum of two additional games before he's eligible to return, though his absence could linger beyond then. Chuba Hubbard has worked as the clear lead back for the Panthers, with AJ Dillon (ankle) siphoning off less work than Brooks had been prior to getting hurt.

headline: Waller (knee) practiced in a limited fashion Friday.
story: Waller was among four Panthers tight ends to have a capped session Friday, the others being Tommy Tremble (knee), Mitchell Evans (Achilles) and Feleipe Franks (wrist). Waller was able to play through his knee injury this past Sunday against the Ravens, when he handled a 46 percent snap share en route to three catches (on three targets) for 42 yards.

headline: Waller (knee) was listed as limited on Thursday's estimated injury report, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: For s second week in a row, Waller is dealing with a knee injury, but his listing to begin this week implies he's a bit healthier after kicking off Week 11 prep with a DNP. He'll have two more opportunities to practice in full Friday and Saturday before the Panthers potentially make a call on his status for Monday's game at Tampa Bay.

headline: Waller caught all three of his targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
story: The veteran tight end was out-produced by second-year player Mitchell Evans, who posted a 5-44-1 line on five targets, but Waller made more of an impact than Tommy Tremble, who caught his only target for 18 yards. With all three members of the trio capable of making a splash in any given week, Waller will be tough to rely on heading into a Week 12 meeting with the Buccaneers.

headline: Waller (knee) is listed as active Sunday against the Ravens, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
story: The Panthers kicked off Week 11 prep with their top two tight ends (Waller and Tommy Tremble) not practicing due to knee injuries, after which head coach Dave Canales told Steve Reed of the Associated Press that those issues were a "concern." Both Waller and Tremble were limited Thursday and Friday and entered the weekend listed as questionable. Now that Waller is confirmed to be active -- along with Tremble -- the former will look to continue to build upon his 25-323-4 line on 39 targets that he's accrued in nine appearances this season.

headline: Waller (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
story: According to Person, Waller told coach Dave Canales he's ready to play Sunday against Baltimore, so fantasy players should proceed as if Waller will be active. Waller's production has been all over the place this season, making him difficult to pin down as a reliable weekly fantasy option. He's more of a best-ball type of fantasy asset.

headline: Waller (knee) is practicing again Friday, Joseph Person of The Athletic reports.
story: The same applies to fellow TE Tommy Tremble (knee), with both players having logged limited practices Thursday after being deemed 'DNPs' a day earlier. The Panthers' upcoming Friday injury report will clarify the duo's game statuses heading into the weekend. Waller is coming off a two-catch, 24-yard effort on four targets in Week 10 versus the Saints, but the week prior he put up an 8/90/1 receiving line on 10 targets versus the Broncos.

headline: Waller (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN reports.
story: One day removed from being a non-participant Wednesday due to a knee injury, Waller was able to mix into some drills, but he now has just one more chance to get back to full Friday, at which point his odds to suit up Sunday against the Ravens will become known.

headline: Waller (knee) is suited up for Thursday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: Head coach Dave Canales called knee injuries for Waller and fellow TE Tommy Tremble concerning when they didn't practice Wednesday, but both players returned to drills one day later. Ultimately, Thursday's injury report will reveal their respective activity levels.

headline: Waller didn't practice Wednesday due to a knee issue, and afterward head coach Dave Canales called the tight end's injury a "concern," Steve Reed of the Associated Press reports.
story: The Panthers' top two tight ends in Waller and Tommy Tremble (knee) showed up as DNPs to begin Week 11 prep, and Canales' "concern" comment also extended to Tremble. It's unclear if either or both are in danger of missing Sunday's game against the Ravens, but Mitchell Evans, Feleipe Franks and Ja'Tavion Sanders are the healthy TEs on Carolina's active roster.

headline: Waller caught two of four targets for 24 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints.
story: One week after his 8-90-1 receiving outburst, Waller came back to normalcy in the Panthers' three-man committee at tight end. Waller has big upside, but his ceiling games are difficult to predict. He's been held below 40 yards with no touchdowns in five of nine games this season. Waller will be a low-floor TE2 with upside for Week 11 against the Ravens.

headline: Waller caught eight of 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.
story: The veteran tight end was Bryce Young's favorite option on the afternoon, leading the Panthers in catches, targets and receiving yards, and Waller was on the other end of a 15-yard TD strike from the QB in the third quarter. It was Waller's most productive game since he returned from a brief retirement last season, and through eight games in 2026 he's put together a 23-299-4 line on 35 targets. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 against the Saints.

headline: Waller corralled one of two targets for 11 yards during last Thursday's 27-19 loss at Green Bay.
story: Waller has been hit or miss from a fantasy perspective this season, with two touchdown grabs in Week 2 in Atlanta and a 50-yard TD catch in Week 7 against the Buccaneers serving as the notable performances. Otherwise, he has one 50-yard effort in his five other appearances, sitting on a 15-209-3 line on 25 targets on the season. Waller next takes aim at the tough Broncos defense this coming Sunday.

headline: Waller brought in one of two targets for a 50-yard touchdown in the Panthers' 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: Waller's one catch not only netted Bryce Young his only passing touchdown of the day, but it also generated team-high receiving yardage. The veteran tight end's splash play naturally was a boon for his fantasy managers, but Waller has seen just four targets over the last two games after opening the season with multiple catches in each of the first four contests. Waller will take a 14-198-3 line into a Week 8 road matchup against the Packers on Thursday.

headline: Waller failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 25-14 win over the Eagles.
story: Waller dealt with a toe injury during the practice week and ended up playing behind both Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans in this one, as Tremble was the big producer in the box score, catching a pair of red-zone touchdowns. Waller is one of the many touchdown-or-bust fantasy options at the tight end position.

headline: Waller (toe) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Philadelphia.
story: Waller should be fine to handle his usual role after upgrading to full practice participation Friday. He was limited Wednesday and Thursday, coming out of a Week 5 bye.

headline: Waller (toe) remained limited at Thursday's practice.
story: Waller has registered back-to-back limited practice sessions coming out of Carolina's Week 5 bye. The veteran TE could avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Eagles but ramping up his participation level to full Friday. Tommy Tremble (ribs) has also opened Week 6 prep with consecutive limited practices, but both Waller and Tremble seem likely to suit up Sunday, as neither has missed a game this season.

headline: Waller was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's practice estimate due to a toe injury.
story: Waller has been a regular part of the Panthers' passing game this season, sitting on a 13-148-2 line on 19 targets through four contests. Coming out of the team's Week 5 bye, though, both Waller and fellow TE Tommy Tremble (ribs, LP) are tending to injuries, leaving some question marks in the position group. Practices Thursday and Friday likely will determine if either of them enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Philadelphia.

headline: Waller caught three of six targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
story: Waller finished second on the Panthers in targets and was one yard behind John Metchie for second on the team in receiving yards, but Tetairoa McMillan (14 catches for 192 yards and two TDs on 16 targets) was the clear No. 1 option in the passing game as the Panthers played without starting wide receiver Jalen Coker (quadriceps). The Lions had given up a league-high six touchdowns to tight ends entering play Sunday, but Waller was unable to add to that total. Waller and the Panthers will be on bye in Week 5 before facing the Eagles in Week 6.

headline: McMillan (foot) practiced in a limited capacity Friday, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: McMillan's return to the practice field generally is a positive sign as he works through a sore foot, but he now has just one more chance to get back to full Saturday, at which point the Panthers may tag him with a designation for Monday's game at Tampa Bay. No matter, head coach Dave Canales has expressed optimism this week that McMillan will be able to go in Week 12, per Kaye.

headline: McMillan (foot) was not in uniform for the team stretch portion of Friday's practice, but he did suit up afterward, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
story: Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reported earlier Friday that McMillan was in a helmet and pads, and although he ditched them while stretching he put them back on shortly afterward. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will include McMillan's activity level, if any, after he was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's practice estimate due to a sore foot.

headline: McMillan (foot) was wearing a helmet and pads ahead of Friday's practice, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: McMillan was listed as a DNP on Thursday's estimated injury report due to a sore foot, but his return one day later backs up head coach Dave Canales' expressed optimism to Kaye about the wide receiver's status for Week 12. Friday's practice report will reveal McMillan's activity level.

headline: McMillan (foot) was listed as a DNP on Thursday's practice estimate, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: After McMillan didn't participate in Wednesday's unofficial practice due to a sore foot, head coach Dave Canales told Kaye that the team is "optimistic" that the wide receiver will play Monday at Tampa Bay. McMillan will have two more chances to mix into drills this week before the Panthers potentially tag him with a designation for Week 12 action.

headline: Head coach Dave Canales said Wednesday that the Panthers are "optimistic" that McMillan (foot) will play Monday in Tampa Bay, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: McMillan didn't partake in Wednesday's unofficial practice, after which Canales revealed that the wide receiver dealt with soreness in his foot after Sunday's win against the Ravens in which he hauled in six of nine targets for 71 yards and one touchdown. Considering the Panthers likely are practicing Wednesday in lieu of a session on Thanksgiving, McMillan appears set to be listed as a DNP on the team's first Week 12 injury report Thursday.

headline: McMillan wasn't spotted at Wednesday's unofficial practice, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
story: Because the Panthers don't play until Monday at Tampa Bay, they won't be posting an injury report until Thursday, at which point a reason for practice restrictions, if any, for McMillan will become known. According to Person, McMillan limped off the field during this past Sunday's win against the Ravens but returned to action, so he may be dealing with a health concern as Carolina begins Week 12 prep.

headline: McMillan caught six of nine targets for 71 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-33 win over the Ravens.
story: The second-year wideout posted his best yardage total since Week 6 while leading the Panthers in receiving yards, catches and targets. McMillan capped his solid performance with a seven-yard TD from Bryce Young in the second quarter. McMillan has slowed down since a torrid start to the season, but he still sports a 55-731-4 line on 87 targets through 10 games heading into a Week 12 clash with the Buccaneers.

headline: McMillan caught three of seven targets for 35 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over New Orleans.
story: The seven targets led the Panthers on the afternoon, but the second-year wideout wasn't able to do much with them. The 35 yards were McMillan's lowest total since Week 3, and he'll take a 49-660-3 line on 78 targets through nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Ravens.

headline: McMillan caught four of six targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.
story: The second-year wideout caught Bryce Young's third TD of the afternoon, a four-yard toss late in the fourth quarter that gave the Panthers some late hope. It was McMillan's first trip to the end zone since Week 4, and through eight games he's collected a 46-625-3 line on 71 targets. He'll look to build on this performance in a Week 10 road trip to New Orleans.

headline: McMillan brought in six of 11 targets for 57 yards in the Panthers' 27-19 loss to the Packers on Thursday.
story: McMillan led the Panthers in receiving yards despite generating a modest total, and the second-year wideout has now fallen under 60 receiving yards in consecutive games for the first time this season. He does have at least six grabs in three of the past four games and a trio of double-digit target tallies on the season, so he continues to sport a formidable fantasy floor despite Bryce Young's current struggles. Carolina's air attack may have a tough time bouncing back in Week 9, however, as the stingy Broncos defense comes to town on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: McMillan secured four of six targets for 40 yards in the Panthers' 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: As the final score implies, it was a total washout for the Panthers in the divisional clash, making McMillan's modest numbers unsurprising. The 2025 first-round pick did tie for the team lead in receptions and set the pace in targets, but his receiving yardage total was his second lowest of the campaign. McMillan still sports an impressive 36-511-2 line on 54 targets heading into a Week 8 road matchup against the Packers on Thursday night.

headline: McMillan secured six of nine targets for 86 yards in the Panthers' 25-14 win over the Eagles on Sunday.
story: McMillan tied for the team lead in receptions with Jalen Coker while finishing second to his talented position mate in receiving yards and targets. The 2025 first-round pick was coming off a career-best 14-catch, 192-yard performance that also included two touchdowns against the Lions back in Week 4, and he's gone for at least 75 receiving yards in four of his first five games of the campaign as a Week 7 home divisional showdown against the Buccaneers approaches.

headline: McMillan caught 14 of 16 targets for 192 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
story: McMillan got open at will against Detroit's struggling secondary, setting career highs in catches, receiving yards and targets while posting his third multi-touchdown performance through 21 regular-season games. The 2025 first-round pick caught a 32-yard touchdown pass in the second quarter and a 10-yard touchdown pass in the third quarter. McMillan entered play Sunday with 23 targets through three games compared to 22 targets for fellow starting wide receiver Jalen Coker (quadriceps), who was inactive against the Lions. Coker will have an extra week to heal up during Carolina's Week 5 bye before possibly rejoining McMillan in Week 6 against the Eagles.

headline: Phillips (hamstring) is active against the Saints on Sunday, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
story: Phillips has been cleared by medical staff to return from a three-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Prior to the injury, he accumulated 10 tackles (three solo), including 2.5 sacks, across five regular-season games. His return will bolster the Panthers' pass rush alongside Patrick Jones, Trevis Gipson and Princely Umanmielen.

headline: Phillips (hamstring), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints, is in line to play, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Phillips looks poised to play for the first time since Week 6, after a hamstring injury sidelined him for the Panthers' previous three games. The edge rusher was able to practice throughout the week, sandwiching a pair of full sessions around a limited session Thursday.

headline: Phillips (hamstring) was estimated as a full participant on Wednesday's practice report.
story: Phillips has missed the last three games for Carolina, but he appears to be ready to return to the field Sunday versus New Orleans. Across five games this season, Phillips has produced 10 tackles (three solo), including 2.5 sacks.

headline: Phillips (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 9 battle against the Broncos.
story: Phillips continues to deal with a hamstring injury he suffered in Week 6 against the Eagles. He didn't practice at all this week, so it doesn't seem that he was particularly close to suiting up. With Phillips set to miss his third consecutive contest, Princely Umanmielen could again be asked to step up as a pass rusher.

headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Monday that Phillips (hamstring) is trending in the right direction and considered day-to-day heading into Sunday's game against the Broncos, Joe Person of The Athletic reports.
story: Phillips hasn't practiced since aggravating a hamstring injury in the Panthers' Week 6 win over the Eagles. With the benefit of a mini-bye coming off a Thursday night loss to the Packers in Week 8, Phillips may have a chance at putting an end to a two-game absence. The Panthers will see what, if anything, Phillips is able to do in practice this week before deciding on his status for the matchup with the Broncos.

headline: Phillips (hamstring) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday night's game against the Packers.
story: Phillips did not practice at all during the Panthers' Week 8 prep. The linebacker aggravated a hamstring injury in the team's Week 6 win over the Eagles and continues to pay the price. It is unclear whether Phillips is tracking to return to practice ahead of Week 9 or will need to miss even more time due to the injury.

headline: Phillips (hamstring) was listed as a non-participant on Monday's practice estimate.
story: Phillips aggravated a hamstring injury in the Week 6 victory over Philadelphia and was subsequently ruled out for Sunday's loss to Tampa Bay. If Phillips can't suit up for a second consecutive game Thursday against the Packers, Princely Umanmielen should continue to receive more snaps.

headline: Phillips (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
story: Phillips aggravated a hamstring injury during the Panthers' Week 6 win over the Eagles. The injury prevented him from practicing during Week 7 prep, and his absence means Princely Umanmielen will likely start opposite Patrick Jones at the edge rusher position. Phillips' next chance to play is Thursday against the Packers at Lambeau Field.

headline: Phillips (hamstring) did not participate in practice Thursday, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
story: Phillips was once again absent from Thursday's practice, putting his availability for Sunday's matchup against Tampa Bay in doubt. The 27-year-old is healing from a hamstring injury sustained in Week 6 versus Philly. Should Phillips miss Week 7, Princely Umanmielen could draw a start.

headline: Phillips (hamstring) was estimated as a non-participant on the Panthers' official injury report Wednesday, Darin Gantt of the team's official site reports.
story: Per Mike Kaye of ESPN.com, coach Dave Canales said Wednesday it's fair to expect that Phillips won't play in Week 7 as he recovers from a hamstring injury he picked up during Sunday's game at Philadelphia. In that case, 2025 third-rounder Princely Umanmielen could draw a start on the edge versus the Buccaneers.

headline: Phillips (hamstring) has returned to Sunday's game against the Eagles, Kassidy Hill of the Panthers' official site reports.
story: Phillips exited the first half of Sunday's game with a hamstring injury before returning in the third quarter. The weakside linebacker's replacement, Thomas Incoom (calf), exited the game shortly after Phillips and has been ruled out.

headline: Phillips (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Eagles, Kassidy Hill of the Panthers' official site reports.
story: Phillips exited the first half of Sunday's game with a hamstring injury. If the Panthers' starting edge rusher cannot return to face his former team, Thomas Incoom will likely absorb the reps at strongside linebacker.

headline: Phillips (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Darin Gantt of the Panthers' official site reports.
story: Phillips sustained a hamstring injury during the Panthers' Week 4 win against the Lions. He had extra time to recover courtesy of Carolina's Week 5 bye, and the sixth-year pro has been given the green light to play Sunday after going through pregame warmups. Phillips has eight tackles (three solo), including 2.0 sacks, through four regular-season games.

headline: Phillips (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
story: Phillips was aiming to suit up for Week 6 but may not be quite ready to go. The linebacker was limited in the Panthers' Wednesday and Thursday sessions before upgrading to a full participant in Friday's practice. Phillips will likely play in Sunday's game against the Eagles, but there is still a chance the team will be overly cautious with the star pass rusher.

headline: Phillips (hamstring) could return to the Panthers' lineup as early as the Week 6 game against the Eagles on Sunday, Oct. 18, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reported Monday.
story: Phillips sustained a hamstring injury in the Panthers' Week 4 win over the Lions. The linebacker is week-to-week with the injury and has the benefit of Carolina's Week 5 bye to aid in the recovery process. Princely Umanmielen or Trevis Gipson would likely start at strong-side linebacker opposite Patrick Jones if Phillips ultimately can't make it back in time for the Week 6 matchup against Philadelphia.

headline: Phillips (back) is questionable to return to Sunday night's contest against Detroit, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: Phillips is also being evaluated for a concussion, making it unlikely that he'll be able to return to the field before the game's conclusion. In his absence, Trevis Gipson and Princely Umanmielen are both candidates to see an increase in workload at outside linebacker.

headline: The Panthers designated Incoom (calf) to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
