A frontrunner in the MVP conversation, Burrow has been playing lights-out football for the past month-plus, as he and Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins are firing on all cylinders.

headline: Burrow completed 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards with four touchdowns and no interceptions and added one rush for eight yards in the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday night.
story: The latest installment in what is looking like an MVP-worthy campaign for Burrow included quite a milestone, as the 2020 first overall pick became the only other player in NFL history beside Peyton Manning in 2004 to score four-plus total touchdowns in five consecutive games. All of Burrow's scores Sunday night came through the air, as he connected with Drew Sample (three yards), Chase Brown (two, four yards) and Dohnte Meyers (15 yards) for his quartet of TD strikes. Burrow also found the bulk of his success when focusing on top wideout Ja'Marr Chase, who was responsible for 11 of Burrow's completions and 231 of his yards on 14 targets. Burrow has now exceeded 400 passing yards on three occasions this season, including twice in the last three games, heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Commanders on Monday night, Nov. 23.

headline: Cook (ankle) has returned to Monday night's matchup with the Commanders, Mike Petraglia of CLNSCincy.com reports.
story: The safety suffered a right ankle injury late in the first half and was questionable to return. Now that he's back, he should be able to resume his role in the lineup at free safety.

headline: Cook (ankle) is questionable to return to Monday night's contest against Washington.
story: Cook suffered a right ankle injury late in the first half, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. In his absence, PJ Jules is a top candidate to handle the lion's share of the workload at free safety versus the Commanders.

headline: Cook registered 10 tackles (five solo) during the Bengals' win over the Falcons on Sunday.
story: Cook had his most productive outing of the campaign, logging a season-high 10 tackles. The 2022 second-round pick will look to build on this performance and keep producing during the team's Week 10 matchup versus the Steelers.

headline: Cook recorded nine tackles (six solo), including 0.5 sacks, during the Bengals' 35-13 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
story: Cook and Boye Mafe combined for a split sack on Tyler Huntley midway through the fourth quarter, which was Cook's first sack since his rookie year in 2022. The fifth-year safety is up to 26 tackles (18 solo), including 0.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through five regular-season games.

headline: Cook (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against Miami.
story: Cook didn't play in Week 4 against Jacksonville but will return Sunday versus Miami, likely resulting in fewer defensive snaps for PJ Jules.

headline: Cook (ankle) is listed as questionable against the Dolphins on Sunday, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
story: Cook has a chance to return from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury, and he ended Week 5 prep on a positive note with a full practice Friday. If he's cleared to play against Miami, then PJ Jules would revert to a depth role at safety behind Cook and Jordan Battle.

headline: Cook (ankle) was a limited practice participant Thursday.
story: Cook hurt his ankle in Week 3 against Pittsburgh and was unable to suit up this past Sunday versus Jacksonville. He didn't practice Wednesday, but his ability to participate in a limited fashion Thursday gives Cook at least a chance of suiting up in Week 5 against Miami. He'll likely carry an injury designation into the weekend unless he's able to practice in full Friday.

headline: Cook (ankle) is inactive for Sunday's Week 4 tilt against Jacksonville.
story: Cook suffered an ankle injury last Sunday versus Pittsburgh. Though he was able to re-enter that contest, he was limited in all three practices this week and has ultimately been ruled out for Sunday's matchup. Kyle Dugger (quadriceps) is also out Week 4, so PJ Jules is likely to step into a starting role.

headline: Cook (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
story: Cook injured his ankle during the Bengals' Week 3 loss to the Steelers, though he was able to return to that contest. He was a limited participant in all three practices during Week 4 prep, and if he's unable to play against Jacksonville, then PJ Jules would likely start at safety alongside Jordan Battle, seeing as Kyle Dugger (quadriceps) has already been ruled out.

headline: The Bengals reinstated Parker from injured reserve and list him as active for Monday's game against the Commanders.
story: Parker had been on IR all season due to a knee injury but was added back to the 53-man roster after turning in five consecutive full practices upon having his 21-day evaluation window opened Nov. 12. He'll serve as a depth option at guard during Monday's contest.

headline: The Bengals opened Parker's (undisclosed) 21-day practice window Thursday.
story: Parker was placed on injured reserve on cutdown day with a designation to return. It appears the 22-year-old has progressed through his undisclosed injury and could be a candidate to return soon. Should he suit up this season, the sixth-round rookie will likely serve in a depth role on the offensive line.

headline: The Bengals reinstated Bozeman (forearm) from injured reserve and list him as active  for Monday's game against the Commanders.
story: Bozeman was designated for return from IR on Thursday and needed just three full practices before the Bengals were comfortable adding him back to the 53-man roster. While serving mainly as a special-teams contributor, Bozeman tallied four tackles through the first five weeks of the season before landing on IR due to a broken forearm.

headline: The Bengals designated Bozeman (forearm) for return from injured reserve Thursday.
story: The linebacker suffered a broken forearm in Week 5 against the Dolphins but now has a maximum of 21 days to get ready for a return to action. He played just one defensive snap across the first four games of the season but was a fixture on special teams.

headline: The Bengals placed Bozeman on injured reserve Monday due to a fractured forearm, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
story: The third-year linebacker out of Southern Miss sustained the injury during Sunday's 31-24 win over the Dolphins, and he'll now be sidelined for at least four weeks after landing on IR. Bozeman had suited up in four of the Bengals' first five contests of the season, seeing most of his action on special teams while tallying four tackles.

headline: Bozeman (arm) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Bozeman injured his arm in the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest and was promptly ruled out. Joe Giles-Harris is now the only reserve option at linebacker for the Bengals' defense.

headline: Bozeman (groin) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Bozeman logged limited participation in practice Thursday and upgraded to full participation by the end of the week, Friday. The 27-year-old will add depth behind Barrett Carter at linebacker.

headline: Bozeman (groin) is inactive for Sunday's matchup against Jacksonville.
story: Bozeman was a limited practice participant Thursday and didn't practice Friday, leading to a designation of questionable entering the weekend. He's now slated to miss at least Week 4. Bozeman has been a core special-teamer for the Bengals this season but has yet to log a defensive snap.

headline: Hill (illness) is active for Monday night's contest against the Commanders.
story: Hill was absent from practice for the entire week due to an illness, but he is now good to go for Monday Night Football. The 26-year-old will operate in his starting role at slot cornerback versus Washington.

headline: Hill (illness) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Commanders.
story: Hill was held out of practice all week while battling through an illness. He could still suit up Monday if he progresses enough in his recovery, but if he's not cleared to play, then Josh Newton, PJ Jules and DJ Ivey would all be in line for more snaps in the secondary.

headline: Hill (illness) did not participate in practice Thursday, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
story: The cornerback played on 82 percent of the defensive snaps last week against Pittsburgh and has yet to miss a game this season. Hill does have an extra day to get over this illness, as the Bengals don't play until Monday night against the Commanders.

headline: The Bengals placed Burks (groin) on injured reserve Saturday.
story: Burks has been working through a groin issue for the past couple of weeks, and he aggravated the injury during the Bengals' 38-18 win over the Steelers on Sunday. His placement on IR means he'll be required to miss at least the next four games, so his next opportunity to play is Week 15 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 20.

headline: Burks (groin) did not participate at practice Thursday, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
story: Burks was forced out of the Bengals' matchup versus the Steelers in Week 10 with a groin injury, and now his availability for Week 11 is in question. He'll probably have to return to practice Friday or Saturday to have a realistic chance of suiting up Monday at Washington.

headline: Burks (groin) will not return to Sunday night's game against the Steelers, Jay Morrison of SI.com reports.
story: Prior to leaving, Burks recorded a pair of solo tackles. He's primarily played on special teams this season. Jack Kiser will be in line for increased reps with Burks sidelined.

headline: Flacco took the field for the Bengals' final possession of Sunday's 38-18 win over the Steelers, attempting no passes while handing off to running back Tahj Brooks on all three of his snaps.
story: With the Bengals having built their lead to 20 by the midway point of the fourth quarter, head coach Zac Taylor pulled starter Joe Burrow from the contest and turned to Flacco to run down the clock in the win. The appearance was Flacco's third of the season, but the veteran signal-caller still has yet to attempt a pass.

headline: Barber (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: The rookie third-rounder didn't practice Wednesday due to a knee injury, but he drew the questionable tag after ending Week 12 prep with back-to-back limited sessions. Zak Zinter would likely start at right guard in the event that Barber is not cleared to play Sunday.

headline: Barnett (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday night's game against the Raiders, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: The veteran edge rusher was injured in Week 10 against the Texans but was able to return to the contest. The Week 11 bye wasn't enough time for Barnett to get right to play against Las Vegas. Sam Williams and Jamree Kromah will see elevated snaps along the defensive line.

headline: Barnett (hamstring) has returned to Sunday's game against Houston, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Barnett left in the first quarter due to a hamstring injury, but the veteran defensive lineman was cleared by medical staff to return to Sunday's contest.

headline: Barnett (hamstring) is questionable to return for Sunday's game against the Texans.
story: Barnett exited the first quarter of Sunday's contest with a hamstring injury. Sam Williams will see more rotational defensive reps behind Jared Verse and Isaiah McGuire while Barnett is absent.

headline: McGuire (calf) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday night's game against the Raiders, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: After back-to-back DNPs to begin the practice week, McGuire was limited Friday. It was apparently enough to avoid an injury designation altogether for Sunday night. McGuire has started all 10 games this season, producing 27 tackles (13 solo), including 4.0 sacks, on a career-high 63 percent of the defensive snaps.

headline: McGuire (calf) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: The Browns are coming out of a bye, so it's unclear whether McGuire picked up the injury during the Browns' Week 10 win over the Texans. Regardless, he'll have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.

headline: Hickman (concussion) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Raiders, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Hickman missed the Browns' last game before their Week 11 bye, but he's apparently cleared concussion protocol since and will be available in Week 12. He figures to start at safety next to Grant Delpit on Sunday.

headline: Hickman (concussion) logged a full practice Wednesday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Hickman was held out of the Browns' Week 10 win over the Texans while in the league's concussion protocol. Cleveland's Week 11 bye gave him extra time to recover, and while his full session Wednesday is encouraging, Hickman would need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to clear protocol and be available to play Sunday against Las Vegas.

headline: Hickman (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Texans, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Hickman entered the league's concussion protocol following the Browns' 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints in Week 9, when he recorded nine tackles (four solo) and two pass defenses. He was unable to practice in any capacity during Week 10 prep, and his absence means rookie second-rounder Emmanuel McNeil-Warren will likely start alongside Grant Delpit at safety, with Daniel Thomas and Donovan McMillon both providing depth at the position. The Browns are on a bye for Week 11, so Hickman will have additional time to progress through the five-step concussion protocol before Week 12 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Wednesday that Hickman is in concussion protocol, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Hickman suffered a concussion in Week 9 against the Saints. He will have multiple steps to work through, but has the full week to clear concussion protocol. The fourth-year pro has 57 tackles (26 solo), four pass deflections and one interception in nine regular-season games this season.

headline: Hickman registered 10 tackles (six solo) and a fumble recovery during Sundays' 27-24 win over Tennessee.
story: Hickman and Quincy Williams co-led the Browns in tackles Sunday, with the former playing every defensive snap for the sixth time this season. Hickman's 10 tackles were his most of the season, and the fourth-year safety is up to 41 tackles (19 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses (including one interception) and two fumble recoveries through seven regular-season contests.

headline: Hickman logged five tackles (one solo) and one pass defensed in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: Hickman played all 64 of the Browns' defensive snaps in the contest. The free safety's pass defensed marked his second of the season, with his first coming in Week 3 as a key interception against the Panthers. Hickman also played three special-teams snaps in the contest, helping the Browns on kick coverage.

headline: Hickman made eight tackles (three solo) and had one pass defensed for an interception in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
story: Hickman intercepted Bryce Young on a third down with 16 seconds left in the game while the Browns were up by three points. The turnover sealed the game, securing the Browns consecutive wins for the first time since December 2023. The free safety played all 74 defensive snaps in the contest.

headline: Williams (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday night's game against the Raiders, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: The linebacker was limited Wednesday and Thursday before logging a full practice Friday. Williams has started all 10 games this season, producing 71 tackles (42 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass breakups and four forced fumbles across 95 percent of the defensive snaps.

headline: Williams (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Williams may have picked up the injury during the Browns' Week 10 win over the Texans, when he logged nine tackles (five solo) and one pass defense. The injury designation follows the Browns' Week 11 bye, and he'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation ahead of Sunday's game against Las Vegas.

headline: Williams (hamstring) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against Houston.
story: Williams has had his practice reps over the last couple of weeks limited while tending to a hamstring injury, but he has yet to miss a regular-season game, and that trend will continue for Sunday's home tilt. The veteran linebacker has accumulated 62 tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, three pass defenses and four forced fumbles through nine regular-season games.

headline: Williams (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Williams has been working through a hamstring issue as of late, although he was cleared to play against the Saints in Week 9, when he logged seven tackles (five solo) in a 23-22 overtime loss for the Browns. He's opened Week 10 prep with a limited session, and he has two more chances to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

headline: Williams has no injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Williams finished the week with back-to-back limited practices heading into Week 9 against the Saints. Williams has recorded 55 total tackles (32 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and four forced fumbles in eight games this season.

headline: Williams (hamstring) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
story: Head coach Todd Monken stated he is "optimistic" Williams will be available for the Week 9 meeting with the Saints. Although the 30-year-old was limited Thursday, it seems he's at least moving in the right direction. Williams has appeared in all eight of Cleveland's games this season, amassing 55 total tackles (32 solo), 1.0 sacks and four forced fumbles.

headline: Williams (hamstring) did not participate in practice Wednesday, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: Williams missed Wednesday's practice with a hamstring injury, which likely occurred at some point during the Browns' Week 8 loss to the Steelers. However, head coach Todd Monken said he is "optimistic" that the 30-year-old will be ready for Week 9. Williams will need to upgrade his practice status by Friday for a chance to play.

headline: Williams finished Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans with 10 tackles (seven solo).
story: Williams was working through neck and back injuries during Week 7 prep, but he was cleared to play Sunday and ended up playing every single defensive snap while co-leading the Browns in tackles with Ronnie Hickman. It was the second time in three games that Williams recorded double-digit stops, and he is up to 50 tackles (30 solo), including 1.0 sacks, two pass defenses and three forced fumbles through seven regular-season contests.

headline: Williams (neck) is active for Sunday's game against Tennessee.
story: Williams was limited in Friday's practice, an upgrade from his inactivity both Wednesday and Thursday. That was enough for him to draw the questionable tag for Week 7, and the veteran linebacker has been cleared by medical staff after going through pregame warmups. Williams has tallied at least six total tackles in four of his last five games.

headline: Williams (neck) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans but expressed optimism Friday that he will play, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
story: Williams didn't practice Thursday due to a neck injury, but he was cleared to return for Friday's session, for which he was listed as a limited participant. The veteran linebacker told reporters that he was at full speed during Friday's practice, but his official status may not be known until 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, which is when the Browns will announce their list of inactive players. If Williams cannot play, then Justin Jefferson and Winston Reid would be the top candidates to start alongside Carson Schwesinger and Easton Mascarenas-Arnold at linebacker.

headline: Williams (neck) did not participate at the Browns' practice Thursday.
story: Williams was added to the injury report with an apparent neck injury Thursday, and he was forced to miss practice. The linebacker will have another chance to return to the field for the team's final practice Friday, but if he is unavailable in Week 7, Justin Jefferson would be a top candidate to draw a start at strongside linebacker versus the Titans.

headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Wednesday that Jenkins has cleared the league's concussion protocol, Tom Withers of The Associated Press reports.
story: Jenkins practiced fully Wednesday, putting him on track to play in Sunday's game against the Jets. He missed the Browns' Week 4 win over the Steelers while recovering from the concussion.

headline: Jenkins (concussion) is officially listed as out for Thursday's game versus the Steelers.
story: Jenkins was unable to practice during the week after entering concussion protocol, and he'll now spend at least one game on the sidelines as he recovers. In his stead, Luke Wypler projects to start at center in Week 4.

headline: Jenkins didn't participate at practice Tuesday due to a concussion, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Jenkins entered the concussion protocol in the wake of Sunday's 21-18 win over the Panthers. With no listed participation in the Browns' first two Week 4 sessions, Jenkins could have a tough time clearing the protocol ahead of Thursday's game against the Steelers. If Jenkins can't play Thursday, Luke Wypler would likely be in line to start at center.

headline: Sanders (hip) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Mary Kay Cabot of the Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Sanders was designated to return from injured reserve Tuesday, and he would need to be added to the active roster with an official transaction prior to Sunday's game to have a chance to play. Even if Sanders gets the green light, he's unlikely to see much action on offense, with Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson and Jaleel McLaughlin all healthy in Cleveland's backfield.

headline: Sanders (hip) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Sanders was designated to return from injured reserve Tuesday, and he was limited in his first practice session since suffering a hip injury against the Jets in Week 5. He'll have two more opportunities to log a full practice, but Sanders would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Raiders.

headline: The Browns designated Sanders (hip) for return from injured reserve Tuesday.
story: Cleveland elected to open Sanders' practice window following their Week 11 bye, giving the team up to 21 days to evaluate him for a return to the 53-man roster. Before landing on IR on Oct. 13 due to a hip issue, Sanders carried nine times for 43 yards and added 11 receptions for 74 yards on 12 targets over five contests. He'll likely slot in behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson on the depth chart at running back once he's activated.

headline: The Browns placed Sanders (hip) on injured reserve Tuesday.
story: Sanders opened the year as Cleveland's No. 3 running back but saw his role increase after Dylan Sampson (knee) landed on IR. During the season's first four games, Sanders gained 42 yards on eight carries and added eight catches for 49 yards on nine targets before going down with a hip injury in Week 5. Sanders will be sidelined for at least the next four games.

headline: Sanders (hip) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Sanders exited the game in the fourth quarter with a hip injury. The running back rushed three times for 12 yards and caught his sole target for one yard before exiting the contest.

headline: Sanders accrued two rushes for nine yards and gathered in both of his two targets for seven yards during Thursday's 27-24 win versus the Steelers.
story: Sanders logged 22 offensive snaps, his second-highest mark of the 2026 campaign. However, the 24-year-old was a non-factor offensively. Instead, it was Jaleel McLaughlin who took advantage of his limited workload by scoring a 28-yard rushing touchdown early in the second quarter. While Sanders should remain the No. 2 back on the depth chart behind Quinshon Judkins, assuming the latter stays healthy, he will be difficult to trust from a fantasy standpoint moving ahead.

headline: Boston (quadriceps) will be listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Coach Todd Monken noted Friday that the team pushed Boston (who was deemed a 'DNP' at practice over the last few days) pretty hard earlier in the week, then pulled back a little bit, while adding that the Browns should have a better idea regarding the wide receiver's Week 12 status Saturday. If Boston ends up out or limited this weekend, Malachi Corley, Tylan Wallace and Isaiah Bond would be in line to see added opportunities behind KC Concepcion and Jerry Jeudy.

headline: Boston (quadriceps) wasn't present for Friday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of the Cleveland Plain Dealerreports.
story: With Boston now on track to log a trio of 'DNP' listings this week, his status for Sunday night's game against the Raiders is cloudy. Friday's final injury report will reveal whether the Browns' starting WR has any chance to play versus Las Vegas or is ruled out ahead of Week 12 action.

headline: Boston (quadriceps) was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's practice estimate, Sam Warren of The Athleticreports.
story: The Browns didn't actually practice Thursday, but Boston's estimated 'DNP' on the heels of Wednesday's missed session puts the focus on what the starting wideout is able to Friday ahead of the team posting its final injury report for Sunday night's 8:20 p.m. ET game against the Raiders. If Boston isn't cleared for the contest prior to the weekend, his fantasy managers will be put in a tricky spot, considering Cleveland's late Week 12 kickoff.

headline: Boston didn't practice Wednesday due to a quadriceps injury, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Boston had been listed with a toe issue on Browns injury reports ahead of their previous two games, but he's nursing a new health concern coming out of a Week 11 bye. The rookie second-round pick will have two more opportunities to potentially practice this week before the Browns decide whether he carries a designation into Sunday's game against the Raiders.

headline: Boston wasn't spotted at Wednesday's practice, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN reports.
story: Prior to a Week 11 bye, Boston was managing a toe injury and missed Wednesday and Thursday practices Wednesday before being a limited participant Friday. Though he had been listed as questionable ahead of the Browns' Nov. 15 game against the Texans, Boston was ultimately active and recorded an 85 percent snap share in a 27-24 win. It's not clear if Boston is still nursing the same toe injury coming out of that game, or if a different health concern is keeping him off the field to begin Week 12 prep.

headline: Boston (toe) didn't take part in the Browns' unofficial practice Tuesday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Though Boston played 58 of 68 offensive snaps in the Browns' Week 10 win over the Texans, he was managing a toe injury leading up to that contest that may have hindered his effectiveness. He was limited to just a 16-yard reception on two targets in the win over Houston and appears to still be managing the injury coming off a Week 11 bye. The Browns will post their first Week 12 injury report Wednesday, when it will be known whether Boston is still tending to the toe issue or a different health concern.

headline: Boston caught just one pass for 16 yards on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.
story: The rookie wideout entered play Sunday dealing with a toe injury and appeared to aggravate it versus Houston. At less than 100 percent health, Boston was unproductive in the box score and saw a microscopic five percent target share. After popping back up for 6-98-0 receiving last Sunday in New Orleans with Shedeur Sanders at quarterback, Boston reverted to his sluggish ways with Deshaun Watson in Week 10. Over his last four games with Watson, Boston has compiled 11 catches for 95 empty yards. Boston can't be trusted in fantasy lineups until he shows more consistency.

headline: Boston (toe) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Texans, Kelsey Russo of The Athletic reports.
story: Boston missed practice both Wednesday and Thursday, but was able to log a limited session Friday, with coach Todd Monken being quoted as saying that the 2026 second-rounder was "trending in the right way" heading into the weekend. With his active status confirmed, in absence of any in-game limitations or setbacks, Boston is positioned to maintain his key role in a Cleveland WR corps that also features KC Concepcion and Jerry Jeudy. Through his first nine regular-season games as a pro, Boston leads him team with 507 receiving yards, while having hauled in 32 of his 60 targets in that span along with three TDs.

headline: Boston (toe), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Texans, is expected to play barring a surprise, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
story: After missing practice Wednesday and Thursday, Boston returned to a limited session Friday, with coach Todd Monken noting that the WR was "trending in the right way." Now, assuming no setbacks in warmups, it appears as though Boston will be available versus Houston, with his official game status set to be confirmed once Cleveland's inactives are posted about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1 pm ET kickoff.

headline: Boston (toe), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Texans, per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN,  is trending in the right direction ahead of the contest.
story: With that in mind, coach Todd Monken noted Friday that Boston "moved around pretty good...it's trending in the right way." It's worth noting, however, that Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer relays that Boston left the team's locker room in a walking boot, but it's possible that's simply a precautionary measure. Either way, the wideout's Week 10 status will be known prior to the first batch of games Sunday, with the Browns kicking off at 1:00 pm ET. Assuming he's available this weekend, Boston and fellow rookie KC Concepcion would be in line to lead Cleveland's WR corps versus Houston, with Jerry Jeudy also in the mix.

headline: Boston (toe) returned to practice Friday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN reports.
story: Boston has dealt with calf, foot and toe injuries in recent weeks, never missing a game or requiring any workload limitations. He missed back-to-back practices to open this week, but he sounded optimistic Thursday and is now back on the field Friday. It remains to be seen if Boston will get an injury designation on the final report Friday afternoon. The Browns host the Texans on Sunday, facing a talented defense that struggled in the first half of the season and still has injury concerns after a Week 9 bye.

headline: Boston (toe) wasn't present for Thursday's practice, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN reports.
story: Zac Jackson of The Athletic previously reported that Boston indicated that his toe was feeling better and said he was hoping to return to practice Thursday after missing Wednesday's session. With Boston now set to log another 'DNP,' what the wideout is able to do (if anything) Friday will be telling with regard to his chances of being available Sunday against the Texans.

headline: Boston (toe) said Thursday that he's hoping to return to practice and "definitely feel(s) better" after sitting out Wednesday's practice, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
story: If Boston indeed practices in at least some capacity Thursday, that would be a substantive step in the right direction for the rookie wide receiver as he tries to avoid what would be the first game absence of his young career Sunday against the Texans. After notching a career-high 98 receiving yards in Cleveland's Week 9 overtime loss to the Saints, Boston is up to 32 catches for 507 yards and three touchdowns through nine games.

headline: Boston isn't slated to practice Wednesday due to a toe injury, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN reports.
story: Boston logged a 93 percent offensive snap share in this past Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints en route to hauling in six of his seven targets for 98 yards. However the rookie WR emerged from the contest with a toe issue that will make his status worth watching ahead of this weekend's game against the Texans. If Boston -- who's expected to return to practice Thursday, per Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer -- ends up being available, he'll be catching passes once again from Deshaun Watson, while Week 9 starter Shedeur Sanders will revert to serving as the Browns' QB2.

headline: Boston caught six of seven targets for 98 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints.
story: The 98 yards led the Browns on the afternoon, and Boston showed some immediate chemistry with Shedeur Sanders, connecting with the QB on a 60-yard strike in the third quarter that nearly resulted in a touchdown. The rookie receiver was also the target on a two-point conversion attempt that would have won the game in OT, but the pass got broken up. Boston also set a new career high in receiving yards with the performance, and if Sanders takes over for Deshaun Watson (concussion) under center on a permanent basis, it could lead to plenty more big plays. Through his first nine NFL games. Boston has delivered a 32-507-3 line on 61 targets.

headline: Boston (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at New Orleans, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: With Boston upgrading from limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday to full participation Friday, he should be fine for his usual role as a near-every-down player in a young Cleveland offense. It'll be his first chance to work with Shedeur Sanders extensively outside of a practice environment, as the Browns reportedly won't start Deshaun Watson (head) even if he clears concussion protocol before the game.

headline: Boston (calf) remained limited in Thursday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Boston dealt with a foot issue a couple weeks ago, but the calf injury is new this week. The rookie wideout has been scuffling after a hot start to the season. Perhaps the likely insertion of Shedeur Sanders this Sunday against the Saints can help Boston regain his big-play ability. Boston is a low-floor, upside WR4 for fantasy.

headline: Boston was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a calf injury, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Boston made appearances on the injury report in Weeks 6 and 7 due to a foot issue, but he's tending to a new health concern coming out of this past Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers. The rookie wideout will have two more chances this week to upgrade to full practice, and if he does, he should head into Sunday's game in New Orleans without an injury designation.

headline: Boston caught six of 11 targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.
story: Boston entered Week 8 having caught just four of 13 targets for 42 yards over the previous two games, so Sunday's output was a step in the right direction. The wide receiver's 11 targets were a new career high, and he ranked second behind tight end Harold Fannin (12) in the category versus Pittsburgh. Boston has now reeled in 26 of 53 targets for 409 yards and three touchdowns over the first eight games of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Boston caught three of eight targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans.
story: The wide receiver was the favorite for the Offensive Rookie of the Year after the first five weeks of the season, but he's now posted back-to-back subpar games against the Ravens and Titans. During those two contests, Boston has four catches for 42 yards on 13 targets. He's been extremely inefficient with his looks and isn't getting loose for big plays over the top of the defense. He'll try to get back on track next Sunday in Pittsburgh.

headline: Boston (foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
story: Boston played through the same injury last week and took 92 percent of Cleveland's snaps on offense in a 13-10 win over the Ravens. He caught just one of five targets for 15 yards, showing the downside of being a deep threat in an offense with poor QB play.

headline: Boston (foot) remained limited at Thursday's practice.
story: Boston has been bothered by a foot injury since the start of Cleveland's Week 6 preparations against the Ravens. He suited up for that game after three limited practices but was held to one catch, and the rookie second-round pick has opened Week 7 prep with a pair of limited sessions. Boston will look to increase his practice participation Friday and avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans.

headline: Boston (foot) was a limited participant at Wednesday's practice, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: Though he didn't end up practicing fully at any point in Week 6 while managing the same foot injury, Boston still avoided a designation for this past Sunday's 13-10 win over the Ravens and ended up logging more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps. As long as he maintains or increases his current level of practice activity throughout the week, Boston should be ready to handle his usual playing time this coming Sunday versus the Titans.

headline: Boston caught one of five targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 13-10 win over the Ravens.
story: It was easily the rookie wideout's least productive game of the season, but the Browns struggled as a whole to get anything going against Baltimore's pass defense. Deshaun Watson amassed just 164 passing yards. Boston was still second on the team in targets, seeing just one fewer than KC Concepcion. Boston will try to rebound in a softer matchup with the Titans next Sunday.

headline: Boston (foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: A limited practice participant throughout the week, Boston should be fine for his usual workload unless there's an in-game setback Sunday. He's rarely left the field for Cleveland this season, and his big plays have been about the only bright spot on offense.

headline: Boston (foot) remained limited at Thursday's practice.
story: Boston has logged back-to-back limited practices to kick off Week 6 prep. The rookie wideout could still avoid taking an injury designation into Sunday's pivotal home game against the Ravens, especially if he can upgrade to full participation Thursday. Fellow rookie WR KC Concepcion (concussion) was also limited both Wednesday and Thursday. More opportunities could be available for Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond should one or both of Boston and Concepcion sit Sunday.

headline: Boston was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a foot injury, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: The rookie second-round pick is making his first career appearance on the injury report, but his ability to practice on at least a limited basis to begin Week 6 prep is a good sign for his chances of playing Sunday against the Ravens. The current betting favorite for the Offensive Rookie of the Year Award, Boston has opened his career with a 16-330-3 receiving line on 29 targets through five games.

headline: Boston caught three of seven targets for 46 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets.
story: Boston's 29-yard touchdown catch with 6:15 left in the fourth quarter gave the Browns a 12-10 lead, but Cleveland failed to hold that advantage. The rookie second-round pick has caught 16 of 29 targets for 330 yards and three touchdowns while exceeding 40 receiving yards in each of his first five NFL outings. KC Concepcion, who was drafted 15 picks ahead of Boston at 24th overall, exited Sunday's loss due to a concussion. Boston could get a larger share of targets from Deshaun Watson if Concepcion doesn't rejoin Cleveland's WR room in Week 6 against the Ravens.

headline: Boston brought in four of seven targets for 89 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: The impressive start to Boston's NFL career continued Thursday, with the rookie second-round pick leading the Browns in receiving yards and tying for runner-up status with Quinshon Judkins in targets. The bulk of Boston's production came on an impressive 60-yard reception to kick off an early second-quarter possession that culminated in a Judkins two-yard touchdown run. Boston has quickly amassed a 13-284-2 line on 22 targets through his first four career games, affording him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Whiteheart was listed as full participant in Cleveland's practice estimate Thursday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Whiteheart popped up on the injury report Wednesday due to a hip issue but should be good to go for Sunday's matchup versus the Raiders. The 26-year-old tight end has caught four of his seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown across 10 games this season.

headline: Whiteheart (hip) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Whiteheart is dealing with a hip issue coming out of the Browns' Week 11 bye, but he'll have two more opportunities to practice in full and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders. The 26-year-old tight end has four catches on seven targets for 48 yards and a touchdown through 10 regular-season games.

headline: Fannin (groin) was listed as a full practice participant on Thursday's injury report, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: The Browns didn't hold a practice on Thanksgiving Day, but the fact that Fannin was estimated as a full participant Thursday indicates that the second-year tight end is on track to play against the Raiders on Sunday. Fannin has caught at least six passes in three of his last four outings, and has compiled a 25-378-1 receiving line on 32 targets over that span.

headline: Fannin (groin) was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN reports.
story: The Browns were on bye last week, but it's worth noting that Fannin's reps were also limited Wednesday and Thursday (by the same listed groin issue) ahead of Week 10 action, before the TE logged a full session that Friday and was then cleared to face Houston. With no reported setbacks in his team's 27-24 win over the Texans on Nov. 15, a game in which the TE recorded an 87 percent offensive snap share, it seems likely that Fannin's Wednesday limitations were maintenance-related.

headline: Fannin brought in seven of nine targets for 91 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
story: Fannin led the Browns across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his 30-yard grab on Cleveland's penultimate possession set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning five-yard touchdown rush on the next play. Fannin's chemistry with Deshaun Watson has been outstanding, and the second-year tight end now has at least 91 receiving yards in three of the past four games. Fannin will remain a central figure in Cleveland's impressive air attack when the team returns to action in a home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a Week 11 bye.

headline: Fannin (groin) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Texans, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: After logging limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday, Fannin's full practice to close the week paves the way for him to continue to lead the Browns' TE corps this weekend. Through nine games thus far, Fannin has yielded fantasy lineup utility by compiling a 37/453/4 receiving line on 53 targets in that span.

headline: Fannin (groin) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: The same applies to Fannin's Wednesday practice participation, but it's worth noting that the tight end also was limited by his groin issue last Thursday and Friday before approaching the Browns' Week 9 overtime loss to the Saints without an injury designation. Friday's injury report will reveal whether that pattern is repeated ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

headline: Fannin (groin) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Fannin dealt with the groin issue in practice last week but ultimately avoided an injury designation ahead of last Sunday's overtime loss to the Saints. In that contest, Fannin caught both of his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown. He had been silent for much of the game before producing a 39-yard touchdown in the extra frame. The overall TE7 in half-PPR points per game this season, Fannin has 37 catches for 453 yards and four touchdowns on 53 targets through nine appearances.

headline: Fannin caught both his targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints.
story: With Shedeur Sanders under center for the first time in place of Deshaun Watson (concussion), Fannin did little in regulation as the second-year QB instead looked for rookie wideouts Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion. Sanders went back to a more familiar target in OT, however, connecting with Fannin on a 39-yard TD in the extra frame that saw the tight end flatten a couple defenders with stiff arms on his way to the end zone. Fannin had a slow start to the season, but over the last three weeks he's amassed an 18-287-1 line on 23 targets, giving him plenty of momentum heading into a Week 10 clash with the Texans no matter who is throwing him passes.

headline: Fannin (groin) will play Sunday against the Saints, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Coach Todd Monken said Fannin is "a little sore" but will be out there against New Orleans. On paper, it's a great spot for Fannin, but playing at less than 100 percent knocks him down a peg as a backend TE1 for fantasy.

headline: Fannin (groin) is practicing Friday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: After being listed as a limited participant Thursday, Fannin appears to be back on the field ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints. His Friday activity is a positive sign for his availability, but it doesn't confirm whether he'll carry an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Fannin (groin) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Fannin wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, so his appearance on it a day later is notable. It remains to be seen if Thursday's listed limitations were maintenance related or indicative of a setback, but the tight end may need to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Saints without an injury designation.

headline: Fannin brought in 10 of 12 targets for 154 yards in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Fannin was one of the few bright spots for the Browns on either side of the ball in the ugly loss despite an early fumble, setting new career highs in receptions, receiving yards and targets. Cleveland's gradual shift to a pass-centric approach as its deficit grew was a boon for Fannin's production, and the second-year tight end now has a combined 16-245-0 line on 21 targets over the last two games alone. Fannin will aim to carry over the elite caliber of play into a Week 9 road matchup against the Saints next Sunday.

headline: Fannin caught six of nine targets for 91 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans.
story: The second-year tight end delivered a season high in receiving yards, and Fannin's last catch was his biggest. With the game tied at 24-24 in the final minute of the fourth quarter, Fannin took a short pass over the middle from Deshaun Watson and tacked on about 30 yards after the catch to set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning field goal. Fannin will take a 25-257-3 line on 39 targets through seven games into a Week 8 clash with the Steelers.

headline: Fannin brought in one of three targets for nine yards in the Browns' 13-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
story: Fannin was quiet for a second straight game while Jerry Jeudy surprisingly paced the Browns' air attack with a season-high 69 receiving yards. Fannin's production has been hard to trust during the first few weeks of the season, as he's recorded five or more catches just twice and three receptions and 27 receiving yards or less in his other four games. Fannin will look for a boost in his numbers during a Week 7 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday.

headline: Fannin caught one of four targets for four yards in Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets.
story: Fannin was neutralized by New York's defense in rainy conditions at MetLife Stadium. The 2025 third-round pick's sophomore season is off to an inconsistent start, as Fannin has failed to exceed 27 yards on three occasions while recording at least 51 yards on two occasions. He had scored three times during a brief two-game touchdown streak that was snapped in Sunday's dud. Fannin will try to get back on track in Week 6 against the Ravens.

headline: Fannin secured three of five targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: After surging over the last pair of contests, Fannin had a quiet night somewhat reminiscent of his Week 1 performance against the Jaguars. However, the second-year tight end still rewarded fantasy managers by crossing the goal line for the third time in the last two games on a two-yard catch late in the first half. Fannin does have at least five targets in three straight games, and he should have a good chance of continuing to serve as a key target for a resurgent Deshaun Watson in a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Campbell logged five tackles (one solo) and three passes defensed, including one interception, in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
story: Campbell's three defended passes matched his season total heading into the contest. The cornerback's biggest moment of the day was intercepting C.J. Stroud at the Cleveland 24-yard line with 48 seconds left in the first half. Campbell's turnover likely stole at least three points from the Texans in a game that was decided by the same swing.

headline: Campbell accumulated seven tackles (six solo) and one pass defensed in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: Campbell's six solo tackles led the Browns in the contest. The cornerback played 98 percent of the team's snaps, appearing fully healthy after missing the team's Week 3 win over the Panthers with a knee injury.

headline: Campbell (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Campbell opened the week with back-to-back DNPs before fully practicing Wednesday, putting him on track to play in Thursday's AFC North showdown against the Steelers. With Campbell back in the fold, Mekhi Blackmon will revert to a depth role in the secondary for Week 4. Campbell has 12 tackles (seven solo) through two regular-season games.

headline: Schwesinger logged 13 tackles (eight solo) in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
story: Schwesinger continues to be a model of consistency, having played all 658 defensive snaps for the Browns in 2026. The middle linebacker has logged double-digit tackles in six of the team's 10 contests so far, adding 3.0 sacks and three forced fumbles over that span.

headline: Schwesinger (wrist) does not have an injury designation against the Texans on Sunday.
story: Schwesinger opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices while tending to a wrist injury, but his full session Friday was enough for the second-year linebacker to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. Schwesinger's 89 total tackles through nine regular-season games are third-most in the NFL behind Alex Singleton (107) and Nakobe Dean (99).

headline: Schwesinger (wrist) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Schwesinger may have tweaked his wrist during the Browns' 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints in Week 9, when he logged a season-high 15 tackles (10 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and one forced fumble. He has two more chances to log a full practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans.

headline: Schwesinger notched 10 tackles (four solo) in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.
story: Schwesinger led the Browns in tackles during the lopsided Week 8 loss. The 2025 second-round pick has 74 tackles (30 solo) this season, having cracked double digits in four of eight games.

headline: Schwesinger finished Sundays' 27-24 win over the Titans with eight tackles (four solo).
story: Schwesinger finished third on the Browns in tackles Sunday behind both Quincy Williams and Ronnie Hickman (10 each). Schwesinger has played every single defensive snap through seven regular-season games and has logged at least eight stops in six of those contests. He's up to 64 total tackles on the year, which leads the Browns and is sixth-most in the NFL.

headline: Schwesinger (ankle) was a limited participant at the Browns' practice Thursday.
story: Schwesinger was able to return to the field after missing the team's first practice of the week while tending to his lingering ankle injury. The linebacker has been able to play through the injury the last few weeks, and he seems likely to be good to go Sunday versus the Titans.

headline: Schwesinger (ankle) did not participate at practice Wednesday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Schwesinger was able to play through his lingering ankle injury in Week 6 versus the Ravens, recording a season-high 13 total tackles in that game. The Browns may simply be exercising an abundance of caution, but Schwesinger's activity at practice as the week continues will still be worth keeping an eye on ahead of Sunday's contest at Tennessee.

headline: Schwesinger logged 13 tackles (five solo) and one forced fumble during the Browns' 13-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
story: Schwesinger was nursing an ankle injury during Week 6 prep, but he was given the green light to play after going through pregame warmups. He ended up leading the Browns in stops while playing every single defensive snap, and he made arguably the most important play of the game when he punched the ball out of Derrick Henry's hands early in the fourth quarter, and the Browns' offense capitalized with a two-yard rushing touchdown by Audric Estime seven plays later. Schwesinger has logged double-digit stops in three of six regular-season games and is up to 56 combined tackles, which is tied with Nakobe Dean and Anthony Hill for fifth-most in the NFL.

headline: Schwesinger (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Despite sustaining a Grade 1 right ankle sprain in last week's loss to the Jets and managing just one limited practice during Week 6 prep, Schwesinger has been cleared to suit up Sunday after making it through a pregame workout no worse for the wear. After taking home NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year honors in 2025, Schwesinger is off to another strong start to the current campaign, having compiled 43 tackles, including 1.0 sacks, a forced fumble and a pass breakup through five games.

headline: Schwesinger (ankle), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest against the Ravens, will go through a pregame workout before the Browns make a call on his status, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: The reigning NFL Defensive Rookie of the Year is nursing a Grade 1 right ankle sprain coming out of this past Sunday's loss to the Jets and was contained to one limited practice during Week 6 prep. Schwesinger showed enough during Friday's session for the Browns to keep the door open for him to play Sunday, but he'll need to check out well in his pregame work in order to get the green light to suit up. Official word on the linebacker's status will arrive when the Browns post their inactive list 90 minutes prior to the game's 1 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Schwesinger (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Schwesinger was held out of the first two practices of Week 6 prep due to a Grade 1 ankle sprain that he picked up during the Browns' Week 5 loss to the Jets. He was able to practice in a limited fashion Friday to draw the questionable tag, but if he cannot play Sunday, then Winston Reid and rookie fifth-rounder Justin Jefferson would be the top candidates to start at linebacker.

headline: Schwesinger (ankle) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Schwesinger suffered a Grade 1 right ankle sprain in the Browns' contest against the Jets in Week 5, and his status for Week 6 is now in serious doubt. Unless he's able to get back on the practice field Friday, it's unlikely he'll be able to suit up Sunday versus the Ravens.

headline: Schwesinger sustained a Grade 1 right ankle sprain during the Browns' 17-12 loss to the Jets on Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Schwesinger was spotted wearing a walking boot on his right foot following Sunday's loss, when he played every single defensive snap and logged eight tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble. The Grade 1 sprain is a best-case scenario for the second-year linebacker, and he has not been ruled out for Week 6 against the Ravens, though his practice participation will provide clarity on whether he'll be cleared to play this coming Sunday. Winston Reid and rookie fifth-rounder Justin Jefferson figure to be the top candidates to start at linebacker if Schwesinger were to miss time.

headline: Schwesinger (lower leg) was seen in a walking boot after the Browns' 17-12 loss to the Jets on Sunday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Schwesinger sustained a lower-leg injury during Sunday's loss but did not receive an official injury designation. It is unclear how significant the injury to the defensive captain and signal caller is.

headline: Schwesinger made nine tackles (three solo) in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: Schwesinger played all 64 of the Browns' defensive snaps in the contest. The middle linebacker and defensive signal caller has played all 262 defensive snaps for the team through four regular-season games in 2026. Schwesinger's nine total tackles led the Browns and tied Steelers inside linebacker Payton Wilson for the most in the game.

headline: Schwesinger logged six tackles (one solo) in the Browns' 21-18 win over the Panthers on Sunday.
story: Schwesinger played all 74 defensive snaps in Sunday's contest. He has played all 196 defensive snaps for the Browns through three regular-season games. The middle linebacker and signal caller for the defense did not have any incredible box-score feats in the Week 3 win but practiced stellar communication that helped enable Mason Graham's 2.0 sacks and Ronnie Hickman's game-winning interception.

headline: Corley caught all three of his targets for 37 yards in addition to returning two kicks for 51 yards during Cleveland's win over the Texans on Sunday.
story: Corley had not caught a pass across the first nine games of the campaign before hauling in three passes during Sunday's victory. He ended up finishing the contest third on the team in receiving yards behind Harold Fannin and Jerry Jeudy.

headline: Corley went untargeted while playing 13 of 70 snaps on offense Sunday in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers. He returned one kickoff for 26 yards.
story: For the fourth time in eight appearances, Corley logged double-digit snaps on offense, but the third-year receiver has yet to draw a target this season. He'll continue to provide most of his value to the Browns as a kickoff returner.

headline: Wallace caught both of his two targets for nine yards during Sunday's 27-24 win versus the Texans. He also recorded one tackle in kick coverage.
story: Wallace again played a rotational role in Week 10, logging 13 snaps at wide receiver. He was able to draw a season-high two targets and come down with both of them, making him one of eight Browns to catch a pass from quarterback Deshaun Watson Sunday. Barring an injury to one of the wideouts ahead of him on the depth chart, he doesn't have a clear path to more consistent playing time following Cleveland's bye in Week 11.

headline: Wallace recorded a three-yard reception on his lone target in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.
story: The reception was Wallace's second of the season, after he previously notched a 12-yard grab in a Week 6 win over the Ravens. A key part of the Browns' special-teams coverage units, Wallace continues to handle a limited role on offense while the the team relies primarily on rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston and veteran Jerry Jeudy to fill out snaps at receiver.

headline: Wallace (knee) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against Baltimore.
story: Wallace has been given the green light to return from a two-game absence after logging a full practice Friday. He's unlikely to see much work offensively, given that he's behind KC Concepcion, Denzel Boston, Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond on the depth chart.

headline: Wallace (knee) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: Wallace has sat out the Browns' last two games because of a nagging knee injury, and while he was at least able to return to practice Wednesday, it's evidently still bothering him. If he can't manage a full practice Friday, it wouldn't be surprising to see him carry an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Wallace (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Wallace has not practiced since sustaining a knee injury in the Browns' Week 3 win over the Panthers. The wide receiver will now miss consecutive games due to the issue, again leaving Malachi Corley as the No. 5 wideout option for the Browns' offense.

headline: Wallace (knee) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Wallace hurt his knee in Week 3 against Carolina and didn't play last Thursday in a win over the Steelers. He hasn't practiced since getting injured, so his chances of suiting up Sunday aren't promising. Wallace has yet to log a target this season, but another absence will likely mean that Malachi Corley gets more opportunities on offense.

headline: Wallace (knee) did not participate at practice Wednesday.
story: Wallace sat out Cleveland's contest versus the Steelers in Week 4 due to a knee injury, and now his availability for Week 5 is up in the air, too. He'll probably need to return to practice in some capacity Thursday or Friday to have a realistic chance of playing Sunday against the Jets.

headline: Wallace (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Steelers.
story: A knee injury prevented Wallace from practicing all week, so the sixth-year pro will observe Thursday's game from the sidelines, which means Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley are both in line to see a slight uptick in offensive snaps. Wallace's next opportunity to play is Week 5 against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Wallace (knee) didn't participate in Cleveland's practice Tuesday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Wallace is in danger of missing Thursday's matchup versus the Steelers, as he was also listed as a non-participant in Monday's practice estimate after suffering a knee injury during the Week 3 win over Carolina. Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley could be in line for increased playing time if Wallace is unable to suit up for Thursday's game.

headline: Szmyt made two of his three field-goal attempts and all three of his PATs in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday.
story: Szmyt knocked through field goals from 49 and 26 yards in Sunday's contest. The kicker stumbled in the fourth quarter, missing a 54-yard attempt with 11:02 remaining that would've brought the game within a point. Szmyt is now 21-for-24 on field-goal attempts and 15-for-16 on PATs over 10 regular-season contests in 2026.

headline: Szmyt went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to New Orleans.
story: Szmyt was able to convert multiple field-goal tries for the eighth straight game, and his three makes matched a season high for the 28-year-old. The kicker made a 41-yarder in the second quarter and a 30-yard attempt in the third quarter before tying the game up at 16-16 with a 51-yard make with eight seconds left in regulation. Szmyt has now gone 19-for-21 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-3 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Szmyt made both of his field-goal attempts in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
story: Szmyt converted his 31-yard and 32-yard field-goal attempts in the second quarter of Sunday's contest. The kicker accounted for all six of the Browns' points in the divisional loss. Szmyt is now 16-for-18 on field-goal attempts and 11-for-12 on PATs through eight regular-season games in 2026.

headline: Szmyt went 2-for-3 on field-goal tries while making all three of his extra-point attempts during Sunday's 27-24 win over Tennessee.
story: Szmyt converted exactly two field goals for the fifth straight week, while Sunday's performance marked his sixth in a row with multiple field-goal makes. The kicker made a 28-yarder as time expired in the first half before hitting the right upright on a 43-yard miss with 14:09 left in the fourth quarter. Szmyt got his redemption later, though, nailing a game-winning 32-yard try in the final seconds of the game. The 28-year-old has now gone 14-for-16 on field-goal tries while making 11 of 12 PATs over the first seven contests during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Szmyt went 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 13-10 win over the Ravens.
story: Szmyt made multiple field goals for the fifth week in a row. The kicker made his first try from 48 yards in the third quarter before missing another 48-yard try wide left with 3:44 left in regulation. Szmyt was able to get the last laugh though, nailing a game-winning 37-yard field goal as time expired in the fourth quarter. On the year, Szmyt has gone 12-for-13 on field-goal tries while making eight of nine extra-point attempts over six games.

headline: Szmyt made both of his field-goal attempts but missed his lone extra-point try during Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets on Sunday.
story: Szmyt paced the Browns' scoring in the first half with made field goals from 25 and 41 yards in the first and second quarter, respectively. He missed his first PAT of the season in the fourth quarter in what would have extended Cleveland's lead to 13-10, but both teams battled the elements during Sunday's contest at MetLife Stadium. Szmyt has made all 10 of his field-goal attempts and has gone 7-for-8 on extra-point tries through the first five games of the regular season, with two of his made field goals coming from 50-plus yards. The Browns will head back home for a Week 6 AFC North tilt against the Ravens on Oct. 18.

headline: Szmyt made both of his field-goal attempts and all three of his extra-point tries Thursday in a 27-24 win over Pittsburgh.
story: Szmyt's first field goal was pretty clutch, as he nailed a 44-yarder to give Cleveland an eight-point lead midway through the fourth quarter. However, the second-year kicker's next FG was much more dramatic -- he sailed a 56-yarder through the uprights with 10 seconds remaining to give his team a three-point victory. Szmyt has quietly emerged as one of the most consistent kickers in the NFL, as he's made 22 consecutive field-goal tries dating back to last season. His 56-yard game-winner Thursday was the longest of his career so far.

headline: Gabriel (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Texans but will serve as the Browns' emergency third quarterback.
story: Gabriel was the backup to Shedeur Sanders for Week 9 against the Saints. With Deshaun Watson clearing concussion protocol, Sanders will revert to QB2 duties while Gabriel operates as the emergency third quarterback. That means Gabriel is not allowed to play unless Watson and Sanders both leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Gabriel "will serve as the backup quarterback" Sunday against the Saints, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: It was announced earlier in the week that Shedeur Sanders would start Sunday's contest due to Deshaun Watson being in concussion protocol, and although Watson has not officially been ruled out for Week 9 as of yet, he reportedly will be. That will leave the backup spot to Gabriel, but presumably for only one contest, as the report notes Watson is expected back for Week 10.

headline: Gabriel (coach's decision) is inactive but will be the emergency third quarterback against the Steelers on Sunday, Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports.
story: Gabriel opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a back injury, but he was cleared to be activated from IR on Monday. He'll be the Browns' emergency QB3 in his return, which means he's not allowed to play Sunday unless both Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: The Browns activated Gabriel (back) from injured reserve Monday.
story: Cleveland needed to make a decision on the quarterback after opening his 21-day practice window 20 days ago, so he'll now join the 53-man roster as one of the team's four quarterbacks. The Browns figure to make a move at the position in the near future, and perhaps they'll try to gauge trade interest in Gabriel.

headline: Gabriel (back) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
story: The Browns opened Gabriel's 21-day return window on Oct. 6. If the second-year quarterback is not activated by Tuesday's deadline, he will be forced to spend the remainder of the 2026 season on IR. The Browns have been struggling to make decisions at quarterback, so it remains unclear if the team will activate him, keep him stashed on IR, or waive him once a judgment call is forced.

headline: Gabriel (back) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Gabriel logged full participation in every practice session during the Browns' Week 5 prep. The quarterback remains on injured reserve due to a back injury, and it appears the team will milk the 21-day practice window until it expires. By keeping the backup quarterback on IR, the Browns temporarily save a roster spot for another player.

headline: Gabriel (back) was a full participant at practice Wednesday.
story: Per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com, coach Todd Monken did not say Wednesday that there was any imminent activation planned for Gabriel, so it seems like the Browns may use most of the 21-day practice window they opened Tuesday to ultimately determine whether he'll be activated. Cleveland already has three healthy quarterbacks on its active 53-man roster, and Gabriel projects to land behind starter Deshaun Watson and 2025 fifth-rounder Shedeur Sanders on the depth chart if he is eventually activated.

headline: The Browns opened the 21-day practice window for Gabriel (back) on Tuesday.
story: After Gabriel sustained a back injury in the final preseason game, the Browns used one of their eight IR return designations on the QB. Now that he's missed the requisite four games, Gabriel is eligible to be activated at any point, but the team will likely wait until closer to the end of the 21-day window to reinstate him. Once he's added back to the 53-man roster, Gabriel will slot in third on the depth chart behind Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders.

headline: Jefferson (hip) was a full participant at practice Wednesday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Jefferson left the Browns' contest versus the Ravens in Week 6 early with a hip injury, but it looks like he'll be good to go for Week 7. Through two games in 2026, all 34 of his snaps have come on special teams.

headline: Jefferson (hip) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Jefferson exited Sunday's contest in the third quarter with a hip injury. The linebacker's absence means Winston Reid is now the sole depth option behind Quincy Williams and Easton Mascarenas-Arnold for the Browns' defense.

headline: Green (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback Sunday against the Saints, Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports.
story: With Deshaun Watson (concussion) inactive, Green will stay the emergency third option for a different starter-backup duo. Shedeur Sanders is set to start at quarterback, with Dillon Gabriel ready to back him up. Green will only enter the contest if both Sanders and Gabriel exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Green (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback Sunday against the Titans, Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports.
story: Dillon Gabriel (back) is staying on IR, so Green will once again serve as the emergency QB3 behind Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders. As such, Green is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Watson and Sanders leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Green (coach's decision) is listed as inactive but will serve as the Browns' emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports.
story: Green will once again act as the emergency third quarterback behind Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders. Green will only enter the game if neither Watson nor Sanders can play.

headline: Green (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets, though he will serve as the Browns' emergency quarterback.
story: Green will be inactive for the fifth consecutive contest but is listed as the Browns' QB3, meaning he will take over if Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Green (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Steelers, though he will serve as the Browns' emergency quarterback.
story: Green will be inactive for the fourth consecutive game but is listed as Cleveland's QB3. That means Green won't be on the field unless Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: McLaughlin was limited to one snap on offense and none on special teams in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.
story: Since Week 7, McLaughlin has logged just three snaps on offense in the Browns' ensuing three games, but prior to Sunday, he still appeared to be in the mix for work on kickoff returns. However, Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley have since taken over as the team's preferred kickoff returners, leaving McLaughlin without a role on special teams. McLaughlin will likely continue to see little use as Cleveland's No. 3 back behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson.

headline: McLaughlin turned five kickoff returns into 117 yards during the Browns' 27-24 win over the Titans on Sunday.
story: McLaughlin played a key role in the Browns' Week 6 win over the Ravens, when he had nine carries for 41 yards and a touchdown while catching all four of his targets for 13 yards. However, his role on offense evaporated Sunday due to the returns of both Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson. McLaughlin figures to be limited to return duties moving forward unless one or both of Judkins or Sampson misses time.

headline: McLaughlin's role in the offense could sharply decrease against the Titans on Sunday, as Quinshon Judkins (ankle) has been cleared to play and Dylan Sampson (knee) is expected to be activated off injured reserve, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: McLaughlin turned 13 touches (nine carries, four catches) into 55 yards in a Week 6 win against the Browns, but Cleveland was without Judkins, Sampson and Raheim Sanders (hip) for that contest. With Judkins and Sampson both on track to play Sunday, McLaughlin and Audric Estime will revert to depth roles on offense and will likely be limited to work on special teams.

headline: McLaughlin rushed nine times for 41 yards and brought in all four targets for 14 yards in the Browns' 13-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
story: McLaughlin served as the lead back with Quinshon Judkins (ankle) declared inactive and both Raheim Sanders (hip) and Dylan Sampson (knee) on injured reserve. While his rushing opportunities were capped, McLaughlin was reasonably efficient with them while also recording a pristine catch rate on his four targets. The former Bronco is ideally suited for a change-of-pace role, but his speed has always afforded him some fantasy upside. McLaughlin could find himself in a similar role in a Week 7 road matchup against the Titans if Judkins remains sidelined and Sampson isn't activated from IR.

headline: McLaughlin was the first running back to take reps during pregame warmups and appears likely to draw the start Sunday against the Ravens, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: With Quinshon Judkins (ankle) inactive and both Raheim Sanders (hip) and Dylan Sampson (knee) on injured reserve, McLaughlin is the next man up out of the backfield for Cleveland. Cleveland signed Audric Estime off the Minnesota practice squad earlier in the week to provide another option at running back, but McLaughlin projects to serve as the lead ballcarrier as well as the team's top option on passing downs. In four games with the Browns since being signed to the roster, McLaughlin has played just 27 total snaps on offense, carrying twice for 31 yards and a touchdown while going without a catch on two targets.

headline: McLaughlin turned his lone carry into a 28-yard touchdown during the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
