story: McLaughlin was on the field for only one offensive snap Thursday. He made that play count, with the fourth-year pro taking advantage of strong run blocking to reach the end zone for the fourth touchdown of his NFL career. That score may have earned McLaughlin some more reps moving forward, though he's still firmly behind both Quinshon Judkins and Raheim Sanders in the pecking order for backfield snaps. The Browns will hit the road for a Week 5 tilt against the Jets.

headline: Sampson rushed four times for six yards and caught four of six targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Texans.
story: Sampson hardly carries the ball for Cleveland and is merely the pass-catching complement to Quinshon Judkins out of the backfield. Across five games this season, Sampson has rushed 19 times for 79 yards while adding 16 catches for 152 yards on 22 targets. He's playable in PPR fantasy leagues as a desperation RB2 option, particularly in games for which the Browns are projected to play from behind.

headline: Sampson rushed eight times for 21 yards while catching three of six targets for 27 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss against the Saints.
story: Sampson toted the rock a season-high eight times, but he averaged a minimal 2.6 yards per carry. The running back remained heavily involved in the passing game, tying wide receiver KC Concepcion for second on the team in targets behind wideout Denzel Boston (seven). Sampson has now reeled in three or more passes in three straight games, and he figures to remain most valuable as a pass catcher for fantasy managers ahead of the team's Week 10 matchup with Houston.

headline: Sampson rushed one time for seven yards and caught six of eight targets for 62 yards in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.
story: Sampson was out-carried 11 to one by Quinshon Judkins, but the former has carved out a role as the preferred pass-catching back for Cleveland since returning from injured reserve in Week 7. Over the last two games, Sampson has turned 11 targets into nine catches for 94 yards while adding seven carries for 52 yards. Sampson will have some PPR fantasy appeal during weeks when the Browns are projected to trail on the scoreboard.

headline: Sampson (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Sampson was limited in the Browns' first practice of the week, but he was likely just having his reps managed after he had missed five straight games due to the knee injury before returning to action during this past Sunday's win over the Titans. With a full practice now under his belt, Sampson is in the clear to serve as the top change-of-pace option behind lead back Quinshon Judkins in this weekend's game against the Steelers.

headline: Sampson (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Sampson's limitations were presumably maintenance-related after he suited up in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans following a five-game stint on injured reserve due to the knee injury. In his return to action, Sampson served as the No. 2 option out of the backfield behind Quinshon Judkins and carried six times for 45 yards while adding three receptions for 32 yards on three targets.

headline: Sampson carried the ball six times for 45 yards and caught all three of his targets for 32 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans.
story: Seeing his first action since Week 1, and his first offensive snaps of the season, after recovering from a knee injury, Sampson logged nine touches to Quinshon Judkins' 18 in impressive performances from both. Sampson is the clear No. 2 RB when the Browns' backfield is at 100 percent, but there could be enough volume for Sampson to have fantasy value in that role given the team's fairly underpowered aerial attack. Sampson will look to stay productive in Week 8 against the Steelers.

headline: Sampson (knee) was activated from injured reserve Saturday.
story: Sampson also had his questionable injury designation removed and has been cleared to play against the Titans on Sunday. He's missed the Browns' last five games due to a knee injury, but his return means Cleveland's backfield will have its top backfield options in Sampson and Quinshon Judkins (ankle) for Week 7.

headline: Sampson (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: With Sampson still on injured reserve, the Browns will need to activate him by Saturday afternoon to have him available for Sunday's game against the Titans. Starting running back Quinshon Judkins (ankle) has been cleared to return from a one-game absence, in any case, which potentially limits Sampson to a passing-down role if he plays.

headline: Sampson (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Since being designated for return from injured reserve last week, Sampson has turned in four consecutive limited practices. While the Browns haven't indicated that Sampson has experienced any setbacks with his knee since making his return to practice, he may need to upgrade to full participation Friday to put himself on a path to come off IR prior to Sunday's game against the Titans.

headline: Sampson (knee) was deemed a limited  participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com previously noted that coach Todd Monken indicated that he was optimistic Sampson -- who last saw action in Week 1 -- will be able to come off IR ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans. The Browns may also welcome lead RB Quinshon Judkins (ankle) back to the lineup this weekend, and if both Judkins and Sampson are available versus Tennessee, Sampson figures to work as a pass-catching complement behind Judkins (ankle).

headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said that he's optimistic that Sampson (knee) will be activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Sampson landed on IR after tweaking his knee in the Browns' Week 1 loss to the Jaguars, but he had his 21-day evaluation window opened last week when he first became eligible to resume practicing with the team. The second-year back turned in a pair of limited practices in Week 6 before ultimately sitting out Cleveland's 13-10 win over Baltimore, but if he can upgrade to full participation at some point before Friday, he'll likely get the green light to play this weekend. Once he's reinstated, Sampson will likely settle back in as a pass-catching complement behind lead back Quinshon Judkins (ankle), whom Monken is also optimistic will be able to play against the Titans after being inactive for the Week 6 win.

headline: Sampson (knee) won't be activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's contest against the Ravens, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
story: Sampson has been sidelined since injuring his left knee during a Week 1 loss to the Jaguars, and while he was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, he didn't do enough in practice since then to warrant activation. With Sampson still sidelined and Quinshon Judkins' (foot) status up in the air for Week 6, the Browns may be looking at a situation in which Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime are powering the ground game this weekend.

headline: Sampson (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Though the Browns officially designated Sampson for return from injured reserve Wednesday, he didn't end up taking any reps in the team's first Week 6 practice session. Sampson was back on the field a day later as a limited participant, but in order to have a shot at being reinstated from IR ahead of Sunday's game against the Ravens, he may need to upgrade to a full practice Friday. Lead back Quinshon Judkins (foot) hasn't been able to practice in any fashion this week and looks to be trending toward sitting out versus Baltimore, so Sampson could be in line for a prominent role if he ends up getting activated this weekend.

headline: Sampson (knee) was a non-participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Despite being designated for return from injured reserve earlier Wednesday, Sampson didn't end up logging any reps after having his 21-day practice window opened. Prior to the Browns' first Week 6 practice, head coach Todd Monken told Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram that Sampson has a chance at being activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Ravens, but the second-year back would likely need to put in a full workout Thursday or Friday to make that a reality.

headline: The Browns designated Sampson (knee) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: The transaction clears the way for Sampson to practice Wednesday and opens a 21-day window for the Browns to evaluate him for a return to the 53-man roster. The second-year back has been sidelined since sustaining the left knee injury during the Browns' Week 1 loss to the Jaguars, but head coach Todd Monken suggested that Sampson could have a shot at playing Sunday versus the Ravens, per Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram. Sampson will likely need to turn in at least one full practice over the next three days for the Browns to feel comfortable activating him from injured reserve ahead of their Week 6 matchup.

headline: Head coach Todd Monken said Monday that there is a "possibility" that the Browns open the 21-day practice window for Sampson (knee) this week, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Sampson was placed on injured reserve in mid-September due to a left knee injury he sustained in Week 1 against the Jaguars. Monken opened the door for Sampson to be designated to return from IR during Week 6 prep, though his practice participation over the coming days ultimately will determine whether he's ready to play against the Ravens on Sunday. Sampson's potential return could be an important one for the Browns, given that Quinshon Judkins (foot) and Raheim Sanders (hip) both left this past Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets due to their respective injuries.

headline: Jeudy recorded two catches on four targets for 74 yards in a 27-24 victory over the Texans on Sunday.
story: Jeudy boosted his final line considerably on a 65-yard connection with Deshaun Watson in the second period. Watson carried the ball into the end zone on the following snap to bring the Browns to within seven points. Jeudy's 74 receiving yards were a season-high mark, though he finished with two or fewer receptions for the third straight week. The veteran wideout is behind both WRs Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, not to mention tight end Harold Fannin, in the pass-catcher pecking order, so he may need to rely on big plays to have a chance to make an impact for fantasy managers.

headline: Jeudy caught two of four targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints.
story: The veteran wideout had zero grabs headed into the Browns' finals drive of regulation, but a 30-yard grab down the left sideline followed up a by a seven-yard gain two plays later set Cleveland up for the game-tying field goal to send it to overtime. The fourth option in the passing attack for the Browns, Jeudy has 18 catches for 208 yards and no touchdowns through nine games this season. He's well off the fantasy radar.

headline: Jeudy did not catch his lone target Sunday in Cleveland's 27-6 loss to Pittsburgh.
story: Quarterback Deshaun Watson had a relatively productive day with 324 passing yards (albeit without a score), but Jeudy was on the receiving end of only one of his passes. The veteran wideout logged his usual amount of playing time, notching a 60 percent offensive snap share to finish third among Cleveland wide receivers. It was the third time this season Jeudy has finished without a catch, but the other two instances were in Weeks 3 and 4, and he had been more involved of late, averaging 3.5 catches and 36.3 receiving yards over his previous four games. With that in mind, he could get back on track in Week 9 against a New Orleans defense that has been middle-of-the-pack against wideouts this year.

headline: NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports that the Browns are currently "less likely" to trade Jeudy before the Nov. 10 deadline.
story: The rookie wide receiver duo of Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, along with second-year tight end Harold Fannin, have dominated most of the targets from quarterback Deshaun Watson. Jeudy has been less involved offensively, although he's had a slight uptick in work of late, accumulating 14 catches (on 18 targets) for 145 yards over his last four games. The 2020 first-rounder brings a veteran presence to the Browns' pass-catching group, but given his lower workload compared to his younger teammates in Cleveland, Jeudy could garner interest from a team who is in more need of depth at wide receiver.

headline: Jeudy caught all four of his targets for 21 yards during Sunday's 27-24 win at Tennessee.
story: Jeudy now has four catches in each of his last two games, an encouraging sign after he had no more than three in any of the first five games of the season. He's still trailing rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in terms of playing time, however. Jeudy is not on the radar in most formats going into a Week 8 matchup at Pittsburgh.

headline: Jeudy caught all four targets for 69 yards in Sunday's 13-10 win over the Ravens.
story: Jeudy's four targets were third on the team, but he made the most of them and ended up leading the Browns in receiving on a day Deshaun Watson threw for just 164 yards and no touchdowns. The veteran wideout entered Week 6 with just eight catches for 81 yards and can largely be ignored in fantasy as Cleveland's fourth or fifth option on offense most weeks.

headline: Jeudy hauled in three of seven targets for 19 yards during Sunday's 17-12 loss against the Jets.
story: Quarterback Deshaun Watson struggled mightily against a tough Jets defense in Week 5, completing just 15 of his 33 pass attempts for 155 yards and getting sacked eight times. Jeudy's production still managed to lag behind even that baseline, as he averaged fewer than three yards per target Sunday. He'll be hoping to at least keep up the target volume in a Week 6 matchup versus the Ravens.

headline: Jeudy caught all three of his targets for 36 yards in Thursday's 27-24 win over Pittsburgh.
story: It looked like Jeudy could be shut out for the third straight game after finishing the first half with no targets. However, the veteran wideout gave Cleveland a first down with a nine-yard reception late in the third quarter, then came up with two big catches -- a 17-yarder and a 10-yarder -- after the two-minute warning in the fourth to help set up Andre Szmyt's game-winning field goal. The two fourth-quarter catches alone accounted for more yardage than Jeudy had recorded across his first three games of the campaign, so perhaps he and QB Deshaun Watson have found some chemistry that they can carry over into a Week 5 matchup versus the Jets.

headline: Jeudy finished Sunday's 21-18 victory against Carolina with no targets or touches.
story: It was the second straight week that Jeudy didn't log a reception, and this time he didn't even get a target (he logged just one in Week 2 versus Tampa Bay). The veteran wideout continues to be on the field fairly often -- he's recorded an offensive snap share of over 50 percent in each of the Browns' three contests, including Sunday when he played 51 percent. However, he doesn't seem to be clicking well with QB Deshaun Watson, and at this point fantasy managers have little reason to include him in their lineups.

headline: Concepcion caught three of eight targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 27-24 win over Houston. He also gained six yards on one carry.
story: Concepcion finished second on the Browns in targets behind tight end Harold Fannin, who had nine. However, whereas Fannin was able to turn his looks into seven receptions and 91 yards, Concepcion posted a much more modest 3-21-0 line. The rookie wideout departed to the medical tent during the first half of the game due to an undisclosed issue, but he was able to quickly return. Concepcion hasn't put up prolific numbers this season, but he does have at least three receptions in eight of his 10 appearances. Cleveland is on bye in Week 11, so Concepcion will next suit up Sunday, Nov. 29, against Las Vegas.

headline: Concepcion (undisclosed) returned to Sunday's game against the Texans, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Concepcion visited the medical tent in the first half of this Week 10 matchup, but his absence didn't last long. He'll continue to operate as one of the Browns' top two wide receivers along with Denzel Boston.

headline: Concepcion (undisclosed) headed to the medical tent during Sunday's game against the Texans, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN, prior to that Concepcion was slow to get up after dropping a deep pass from QB Deshaun Watson. The rookie WR has one catch for six yards (on four targets) to his credit thus far in Sunday's contest.

headline: Concepcion caught four of six targets for 85 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. He added three yards on his only carry.
story: Most of Concepcion's production came on a 64-yard TD in the fourth quarter as Shedeur Sanders found him just inside New Orleans' 30-yard line and the speedy rookie -- who briefly exited the contest after sustained what appeared to be a right leg issue -- to did the rest by eluding a couple defenders. It was Concepcion's first career NFL touchdown, and he sports a 37-437-1 line on 55 targets through his first nine games for the Browns. If Sanders takes over from Deshaun Watson (concussion) on a permanent basis, it could lead to plenty more big plays for Concepcion.

headline: Concepcion returned to Sunday's game against the Saints after previously appearing to injure his right leg, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Cabot initially reported that Concepcion couldn't put weight on his right leg after an sustaining an apparent non-contact injury. However, following the injury scare, the rookie WR is back on the field to reclaim his key role in the Browns' passing offense.

headline: Concepcion, who was helped off the field Sunday, appeared to be having trouble putting pressure on his right leg, Ross Jackson of Louisianasports.net reports.
story: Per Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer, it was a non-contact injury for Concepcion, who had caught both of his targets in the game for 11 yards. For now, Denzel Boston, Jerry Jeudy, Tylan Wallace, Malachi Corley and Isaiah Bond are Cleveland's available WRs.

headline: Concepcion caught three of four targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers.
story: After a breakout game last Sunday against the Titans, which saw Concepcion record eight grabs for 129 yards on 10 targets, the rookie wideout came crashing back down against a divisional foe. Concepcion's four targets were a distant fourth on the team behind Harold Fannin (12), Denzel Boston (11) and Dylan Sampson (eight), and his four looks were good for just a 10.3 percent target share. Concepcion will try to rebound next Sunday against the Saints, but he's shown little upside, with zero touchdowns and just two games with more than 50 receiving yards.

headline: Concepcion caught eight of 10 targets for 129 yards and added 23 yards on three carries in Sunday's 27-24 win over Tennessee.
story: The rookie wideout put together a breakout performance, with his 10 targets, eight catches and 129 receiving yards all being season highs. If fact, the yardage total was more than Concepcion had produced in any two of his first six NFL games combined. Concepcion's chemistry with Deshaun Watson is growing, and he'll be hunting for his first career touchdown in Week 8 against the Steelers.

headline: Concepcion (calf/quadriceps) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Zac Jackson of The Athletic reports.
story: Neither does fellow Browns wideout Denzel Boston, who has been limited in practice with a foot injury. There's been no indication that either WR was ever in serious danger of missing Sunday's game, so normal workloads can be expected unless there's an in-game setback.

headline: Concepcion (calf/quadriceps) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Concepcion and Denzel Boston (foot) have now been limited in both of the Browns' first two Week 7 practices, so the two rookie wideouts may need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid taking injury designations into Sunday's game against the Titans. After sustaining a concussion in the Browns' Week 5 loss to the Jets, Concepcion was able to clear the five-step protocol prior to last week's game against the Ravens and went on to finish with four catches for 37 yards on six targets while adding two yards on two carries in a 13-10 win.

headline: Concepcion (calf, quad) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: The rookie is starting the week with a limited practice due to calf and quad issues. That he was able to participate is a good sign, however, even if Concepcion wasn't a full-go. Concepcion's status for Sunday's game against the Titans will become more clear with Friday's injury report.

headline: Concepcion brought in four of six targets for 37 yards, rushed twice for two yards and returned one punt for 13 yards in the Browns' 13-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
story: The rookie made a quick recovery from the concussion he'd suffered in Week 5 against the Jets, and Concepcion tied for the team lead in receptions and boasted Cleveland's top target tally while finishing as the runner-up in receiving yards. The first-round pick usually works in a short-area role that limits his fantasy utility outside of PPR formats, but Concepcion's 22 receptions heading into a Week 7 road matchup against the Titans do suggest he has plenty of Deshaun Watson's trust.

headline: Concepcion has cleared concussion protocol and will play Sunday against the Ravens, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Concepcion sustained a concussion last Sunday when he took a big hit from Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, with his helmet slamming into the turf afterward. However, Concepcion was able to make quick work of the protocol for head injuries this week and will be available to the Browns offense Sunday. Prior to his abbreviated outing in Week 5, the rookie first-rounder had a 17-144-0 line on 28 targets through the first four games of his career.

headline: Concepcion (concussion) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: While Concepcion's ability to practice in some capacity for a second straight day is an encouraging sign, he still has a couple of hurdles to clear in order to play Sunday versus the Ravens. In addition to upgrading to full practice participation Friday, Concepcion will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist no later than Saturday before he's removed from concussion protocol. If the rookie wideout can't play against Baltimore, Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond would be in store for more reps behind Denzel Boston (foot), who was also limited in practice Thursday.

headline: Concepcion (concussion) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Just three days after sustaining a concussion when he was on the receiving end of a helmet-to-helmet hit from the Jets' Minkah Fitzpatrick, Concepcion was able to make enough progress through the five-step protocol to open Week 6 prep on the field, albeit in a limited fashion. He'll have two more chances to upgrade to full participation and will then need to receive clearance from an independent neurologist before being removed from the protocol. If Concepcion can't play Sunday against the Ravens, Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond would be in line for added reps alongside Denzel Boston (foot) in two- and three-receiver sets.

headline: Concepcion is progressing well in his recovery from a concussion and is set to practice Wednesday, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Though he remains in the five-step concussion protocol after being knocked out of this past Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets following a helmet-to-helmet hit from safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, Concepcion's ability to practice in any fashion to begin Week 6 prep is an encouraging sign. The rookie wideout will likely need to upgrade to full practice participation by the end of the week in order to have a shot at playing Sunday against the Ravens, and he'll also need to gain clearance from an independent neurologist.

headline: Concepcion has entered the NFL's concussion protocol, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reported Sunday.
story: Concepcion sustained a concussion in the Browns' 17-12 loss to the Jets on Sunday after taking a hard hit from Minkah Fitzpatrick. The rookie wideout will now have to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol before he can return to game action. Concepcion's status for a Week 6 home divisional matchup against the Ravens will bear monitoring over the upcoming practice week.

headline: Concepcion (head) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game at the Jets.
story: Concepcion took a hit from Jets safety Minkah Fitzpatrick early during Week 5 action and hit his head on the turf, after which the rookie wide receiver went directly to the locker room before the Browns made a ruling on his status. In Concepcion's absence, Denzel Boston will handle WR1 duties, with Jerry Jeudy, Isaiah Bond and Malachi Corley filling in behind him.

headline: Concepcion secured five of eight targets for 64 yards and returned two punts for 10 yards in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday.
story: Concepcion and fellow rookie Denzel Boston continued to spark the Browns' air attack Thursday, and the former finished second in receptions and receiving yards while setting the pace in targets. Concepcion's catch and yardage totals also qualified as new career highs, and the productive night served as a welcome bounce-back effort after the rookie first-round pick had been held to 2-9-0 receiving line in the Week 3 win over the Panthers. He should continue to garner plenty of Deshaun Watson's attention in a Week 5 road matchup against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Concepcion finished Sunday's 21-18 victory versus Carolina with two catches (on nine targets) for nine yards. He also returned one punt for one yard.
story: Concepcion actually tied tight end Harold Fannin for the team lead with nine targets, but the rookie wideout managed to haul in just two of those looks. His receptions went for five and four yards, continuing what has become a trend, as he's averaging a meager 6.7 yards per reception so far this season. The target share indicates that the Browns want Concepcion to be an integral part of the passing game, but so far he doesn't seem to be clicking with QB Deshaun Watson.

headline: Why Mike Clay is high on Deshaun Watson as a streaming option in Week 12
story: Why Mike Clay is high on Deshaun Watson as a streaming option in Week 12

headline: Watson completed 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards with no touchdowns and one interception while adding eight rushes for 49 yards and a score in the Browns' 27-24 win over the Texans on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that remained with Cleveland.
story: Watson helped the Browns overcome a 17-point first-half deficit, even though he didn't throw any touchdown passes for the fourth straight game. The veteran signal-caller did pile up the passing yardage against his old team, however, eclipsing 300 yards for the third straight game in the process. Watson also hit Harold Fannin with a critical 30-yard pass on his last pass attempt of the afternoon to set up Quinshon Judkins' game-winning rushing touchdown, and he'll next draw a highly favorable matchup against the Raiders in a Week 12 home matchup on Sunday, Nov. 29, following a Week 11 bye.

headline: The Browns announced Wednesday that Watson (concussion) will start Sunday's game against the Texans, Kelsey Russo of the team's official site reports.
story: Watson cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol this past Saturday, but because he managed just one limited practice during Week 9 prep, the Browns opted to make him inactive for their matchup with the Saints. Shedeur Sanders drew his first start of the season and threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns in the team's 23-22 overtime loss in New Orleans, but he'll return to the No. 2 role this week while a healthy Watson reclaims the starting job. Though the Browns have gone 5-3 with Watson under center this season, he hasn't been without his flaws (six turnovers, 33 sacks taken). As such, Watson may need a strong showing against the Texans to hold off Sanders for the starting job in the weeks to come.

headline: Watson (concussion) will serve as the Browns' starting quarterback in Sunday's game against the Texans, a source tells Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com first reported Monday that Watson was in line for the Week 10 start, after his placement in concussion protocol during Week 9 kept him from playing in this past Sunday's 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints. Head coach Todd Monken then said later Monday that he wasn't ready to name a Week 10 starter between Watson and Shedeur Sanders, the latter of whom performed respectably in the loss to New Orleans. Ultimately, the Browns look like they'll go back to Watson, who cleared protocol Saturday and will be able to get in a full week of practice leading up to the matchup with the Texans. Watson guided the Browns to a 5-3 record through the first eight games while completing 65.5 percent of his passes and accounting for eight touchdowns (seven throwing, one rushing).

headline: The Browns are planning for Watson (concussion) to start Sunday's game against the Texans, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: After entering concussion protocol following the Browns' Week 8 loss to the Steelers, Watson was able to resume practicing in a limited fashion Friday and then passed neurological tests Saturday. However, because of the lack of prep time leading up to Sunday, Watson ended up being inactive for the Browns' 23-22 overtime loss to the Saints while Shedeur Sanders made his first start of the season. Though Sanders performed capably in the losing effort, Watson -- who helped lead Cleveland to a 5-3 record through its first eight games -- will retain the starting gig and will return to the lineup against Houston following a normal week of practice, barring any setbacks.

headline: Watson (concussion) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Saints, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Watson, who reported concussion symptoms Tuesday, didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday before being deemed limited Friday and subsequently heading into the weekend with a 'questionable' tag. Though Watson has cleared the NFL's concussion protocol, the Browns have elected to err on the side of caution with the QB who has compiled a 5-3 record as the team's starter to date. With Watson listed as inactive versus New Orleans, Shedeur Sanders will draw the start, while Dillon Gabriel will serve as Cleveland's No. 2 signal-caller. Taylen Green is the team's emergency No. 3 QB.

headline: Watson (concussion) is expected to be inactive for Sunday's game at New Orleans, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: After reporting concussion symptoms Tuesday, Watson didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday before returning to a limited session Friday and earning a questionable tag ahead of Week 9 action. He then cleared the concussion protocol Saturday, per the Browns. Despite Watson getting the thumbs-up from an independent neurologist, head coach Todd Monken already has announced Shedeur Sanders as Sunday's starter, and Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports that Dillon Gabriel will serve as the No. 2 QB this weekend. In the end, Watson is slated to be back in action next Sunday against the Texans.

headline: Watson cleared the concussion protocol Saturday but remains questionable for Sunday's game at New Orleans.
story: Since Watson reported concussion symptoms Tuesday, he didn't practice Wednesday and Thursday before being limited Friday and earning a questionable tag for Week 9 action. Head coach Todd Monken relayed to Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site Friday that Shedeur Sanders will be the team's starting quarterback Sunday, so some possibilities for Watson this weekend are active as the backup or inactive as the emergency third QB.

headline: Watson (concussion) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints, but Shedeur Sanders will start even if Watson is active Kelsey Russo of the Browns' official site reports.
story: Per Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com, coach Todd Monken said Friday that he hasn't decided if Watson will be the team's Week 9 backup, as the QB -- who is in the NFL's concussion protocol -- has yet to be cleared. In any case, if Watson is active come Sunday, he'll merely be the backup. He was a limited practice participant Friday, after missing the previous two days.

headline: Watson (concussion) was present for practice Friday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Ian Rapoport of NFL Network previously suggested that Watson "is unlikely to start" Sunday's game against the Saints, but either way, the QB's return to the field, in any capacity, is a positive step toward him advancing through the NFL's concussion protocol. Friday's final injury report will add further clarity to Watson's Week 9 status, but if he isn't cleared to play this weekend, Shedeur Sanders would be in line to start in his place.

headline: Watson (concussion) "is unlikely to start" Sunday's game against the Saints, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Watson has not practiced since being placed in the NFL's concussion protocol Tuesday, and it appears he will not be cleared to suit up for Week 9. The Browns will provide an official update on Watson's status later Friday, and if he is unable to go, Shedeur Sanders would presumably get the start in his place.

headline: Watson (concussion) remained sidelined from practice Thursday, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: With Watson, who is in the NFL's concussion protocol, in line to log back-to-back DNPs, the QB's status for Sunday's game against the Saints remains cloudy. In the event that Watson doesn't gain clearance to play this weekend, Shedeur Sanders will draw the start in his place.

headline: The Browns listed Watson (concussion) as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Early in this past Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers, Watson exited the game to get checked for a concussion following a helmet-to-helmet hit, but he was cleared to re-enter the contest after missing just four offensive snaps. However, after he had some late-surfacing symptoms, Watson entered concussion protocol Tuesday and was a spectator for the Browns' first Week 9 session. According to Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com, Watson "felt a lot better" Wednesday and was involved in meetings, but Shedeur Sanders took all the reps with the first-team offense. Sanders appears to be trending toward starting Sunday against the Saints, as Monken acknowledged that it will be difficult for Watson to play even if he ends up clearing the protocol late in the week, per Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram.

headline: Watson is expected to face an uphill battle to clear concussion protocol prior to Sunday's game against the Saints, leaving Shedeur Sanders as the Browns' likely Week 9 starting quarterback, Mary Kay Cabot of the Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: After reporting concussion symptoms Tuesday following Sunday's loss to the Steelers, Watson entered the protocol and isn't expected to practice Wednesday. Sanders will take all of the first-team reps Wednesday, and unless Watson can pass through the protocol quickly, the Browns will prepare for the second-year signal-caller to direct the offense in Week 9.

headline: The Browns announced Wednesday that Watson has been placed in concussion protocol.
story: Watson took a helmet-to-helmet hit in the first quarter of Sunday's 27-6 loss to the Steelers, and after being examined by an independent consultant he was cleared to return to the game. Though subsequent tests after the game and Monday morning showed no symptoms of a concussion, Watson informed the Browns on Tuesday morning that he was experiencing symptoms and was "immediately placed in the concussion protocol," per the team. Watson will need to clear the five-step protocol in order to play in Cleveland's Week 9 matchup with New Orleans, but if he's unable to go, Shedeur Sanders would be in line to start at quarterback for the first time this season.

headline: Watson completed 27 of 39 passes for 324 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions while rushing three times for two yards in the Browns' 27-6 loss to the Steelers on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Watson couldn't lead the Browns to a single touchdown, but he exceeded 300 passing yards for the second straight game since Cleveland was forced into a pass-centric approach. Watson displayed the most chemistry with Harold Fannin (10-154-0 on 12 targets), and he recorded completions to seven different targets overall. Watson also lost the handle on a combined sack by Patrick Queen and Cameron Heyward in the first quarter, which led to a Steelers touchdown. Watson will look to rebound in a favorable road matchup against the Saints in Week 9 next Sunday.

headline: Watson (undisclosed) returned to Sunday's game in Pittsburgh, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Watson endured a big hit on the Browns' first offensive possession and was required to visit the medical tent for what likely was to check on a possible concussion. He's since been cleared to return to action.

headline: Watson went to the sideline tent in the first quarter of Sunday's game at Pittsburgh, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Watson took a big hit on the Browns' first offensive possession, and it appears he may be undergoing a check for a possible concussion. Shedeur Sanders will take over for Watson for as long as the latter is sidelined.

headline: Watson completed 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards with an interception in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans. He added 19 yards and a touchdown on three carries.
story: While he didn't throw a TD pass for a second straight game, Watson produced a season high in passing yards and scored his first rushing TD since Week 2 of the 2024 season on a nine-yard scamper in the fourth quarter. Watson also led his fifth game-winning, fourth-quarter drive of the year, completing another comeback after the Browns fell behind 14-0 early. The veteran QB will take a 7:3 TD:INT through seven games into a Week 8 meeting with the Steelers.

headline: Watson completed 16 of 26 passes for 164 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and added eight carries for 29 yards in the Browns' 13-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
story: As Watson's numbers suggest, he didn't do anything of particular note as either a passer or runner, but the veteran signal-caller did avoid turnovers despite taking five sacks. That alone helped keep Cleveland in a game in which the Browns faced a 10-0 halftime deficit, and he was then able to lead fourth-quarter touchdown and field-goal drives that completed the comeback. Watson has surprisingly helped the Browns to a 4-2 record, and he's provided a solid 7:2 TD:INT and 196 rushing yards along the way. He'll look to carry over the momentum into a Week 7 road clash with the Titans on Sunday.

headline: Watson completed 15 of 33 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown while rushing six times for 40 yards in Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets. He also lost a fumble.
story: Watson orchestrated a go-ahead touchdown drive in the fourth quarter for the fourth consecutive game, giving the Browns a 12-10 lead with a 29-yard touchdown pass to Denzel Boston with 6:15 remaining. Cleveland's defense held up to win the previous three games, but that streak was snapped here, as the Jets scored a go-ahead touchdown with 3:01 remaining while the Browns failed to score on their final three drives, the last of which ended with a Watson fumble on fourth down. Watson and the Browns will take a 3-2 record into a key Week 6 home game against the Ravens.

headline: Schoonmaker wasn't targeted in Thursday's loss to the Eagles.
story: With Jake Ferguson (knee) still sidelined, Schoonmaker played 16 of 77 offensive snaps behind Brevyn Spann-Ford (57). The Cowboys used more of a jumbo tight end look against Philly, giving offensive tackle Broderick Jones a role as a sixth lineman, lining up for 16 offensive snaps at tight end. Schoonmaker has five grabs for 48 yards on six targets across 10 games this season.

headline: Schoonmaker caught his lone target for six yards in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.
story: With Jake Ferguson (knee) remaining out for Dallas, Schoonmaker played 25 of 65 offensive snaps behind Brevyn Spann-Ford. Schoonmaker ran 12 routes, five fewer than Spann-Ford, and the duo combined to see three targets on a day Dak Prescott attempted 33 passes. Schoonmaker has five catches for 48 yards on six targets across nine games this season and has no fantasy appeal.

headline: Schoonmaker (illness) is active for Sunday's Week 11 matchup against Tennessee.
story: Schoonmaker was unable to practice Thursday or Friday because he was under the weather, but the tight end appears to be feeling well enough to suit up Sunday. Meanwhile, Jake Ferguson (knee/ankle) will miss his second straight game, opening the door for Schoonmaker to potentially log a larger workload than usual on offense. With Ferguson out last Sunday versus San Francisco, Schoonmaker posted a season-high 35 percent offensive snap share and caught one of two targets for 12 yards.

headline: Schoonmaker (illness) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: Schoonmaker was held out of practice Thursday and Friday due to an illness, and he's drawn the questionable tag heading into the weekend. Jake Ferguson (knee) has already been ruled out, and with Schoonmaker under the weather, that leaves Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell as the Cowboys' two healthy tight ends on the 53-man roster ahead of Sunday's contest. Michael Trigg could be elevated from the practice squad to the active roster depending on Schoonmaker's recovery.

headline: Schoonmaker caught one of two targets for 12 yards during Sunday's 46-40 loss to the 49ers.
story: Schoonmaker garnered a season-high two targets, but he failed to produce his first multicatch performance of the year. The tight end played 28 offensive snaps in contest, ranking second at his position behind Brevyn Spann-Ford (55) and ahead of James Mitchell (five). With Jake Ferguson (knee) expected to remain sidelined in Week 11, Schoonmaker will have another chance to operate as the team's top reserve option at tight end versus the Titans on Sunday.

headline: Schoonmaker (groin) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: The tight end has missed the past two games for Dallas, but appears to be ready to return and could see significant snaps behind Brevyn Spann-Ford while Jake Ferguson (knee) is sidelined.

headline: Schoonmaker (groin) is inactive for Sunday's clash against the Colts.
story: Schoonmaker continues to tend to a groin issue and will miss his second straight game. He did manage a trio of limited practices during the week, so the tight end may be able to play next Sunday, Nov. 15, against San Francisco. Dallas' tight-end corps will consist of Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell in Week 9.

headline: Schoomaker (groin) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Schoonmaker was unable to practice Thursday nor Friday due to a groin injury that he sustained during Week 8 prep. He'll miss his first game of the regular season Sunday, and he'll aim to recover enough to return for Week 9 against the Colts on Nov. 8. Jake Ferguson, Brevyn Spann-Ford and James Mitchell will be the Cowboys' three active tight ends against Arizona.

headline: Schoonmaker went without a target while playing 11 of the Cowboys' 68 offensive snaps in Monday's 38-21 win over the Eagles.
story: After drawing even with Brevyn Spann-Ford in snaps during the Cowboys' Week 1 loss to the Giants, Schoonmaker has settled in as the clear No. 3 option on the depth chart at tight end behind Jake Ferguson and Spann-Ford in the subsequent six games. He's played less than 20 percent of the offensive snaps in four consecutive contests, drawing just one target during that span while functioning mainly as a blocker during his time on the field.

headline: Brown caught his lone target for 19 yards in Thursday's loss to the Eagles.
story: The wide receiver played four offensive snaps, and his catch was the first of his career. Brown is no higher than the fifth receiver in Dallas and has no fantasy appeal in redraft leagues.

headline: Brown (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Texans, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.
story: The undrafted rookie has yet to make his regular-season debut despite making the Cowboys' 53-man roster after a strong training camp, and his next opportunity to do so is Thursday against the Buccaneers. The Cowboys will have five active wide receivers for Sunday's game, with the position group led by CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.

headline: Turpin caught a 31-yard touchdown on three targets in Thursday's loss to the Eagles.
story: Turpin's three targets were a distant third on the team, trailing both CeeDee Lamb (10) and George Pickens (nine) on a day when Dak Prescott attempted 28 passes. In three games since returning from a ribs injury, Turpin has two catches for 41 yards and a touchdown on seven targets.

headline: Live on FOX: KaVontae Turpin takes it to the house for Cowboys TD
story: Live on FOX: KaVontae Turpin takes it to the house for Cowboys TD

headline: Turpin failed to reel in his only target while rushing twice for 41 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans. He added 121 yards as a kick returner and logged a 13-yard punt return.
story: Turpin went without a catch for the fourth time this season, but he was able to make his mark as a rusher in Week 11. The wideout was able to break loose for a 22-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, notching his second score on the ground this season. Turpin has now caught five of 11 targets for 49 yards, rushed five times for 60 yards and two touchdowns, and added 695 kick-return yards and 121 yards as a punt returner over eight contests so far during the 2026 season.

headline: Turpin is expected to resume return duties on both kickoffs and punts Sunday against the Titans, Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News reports.
story: The wide receiver had to sit for three games with a rib injury before coming back for last Sunday's loss to the 49ers, in which he fielded punts but not kickoffs. Turpin has 574 kickoff-return yards and 108 punt-return yards on the year.

headline: Turpin caught one of three targets for 10 yards Sunday in a Week 10 loss to San Francisco. He also rushed once for nine yards.
story: Dak Prescott took to the air 51 times in the offensive slugfest, but Turpin got only three of his targets. Meanwhile, George Pickens drew a whopping 18 looks, CeeDee Lamb got 13 and Ryan Flournoy got seven, and all three of those wideouts scored at least one touchdown. Turpin logged a 17 percent offensive snap share in his return from a three-game absence caused by an injury to his ribs. He's fallen below a 20 percent offensive snap share in all but one of his seven appearances this season, so Turpin seems to be steadfastly locked into no higher than Dallas' No. 4 wideout role.

headline: Turpin (ribs) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: Turpin has missed the Cowboys' last three games while recovering from a rib injury that he suffered in Week 6 against the Packers. His return will bolster Dallas' special teams, as he is the top returner on kickoffs and punts, and he'll also give the offense a boost as an explosive playmaker.

headline: Turpin (ribs) was limited in Thursday's practice, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports.
story: Turpin was limited for a second consecutive practice. He has missed the last three games, and if that trend continues Sunday versus San Francisco, Jonathan Mingo (ankle) and Camden Brown could remain more involved than usual.

headline: Turpin (ribs) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: Turpin has missed three straight games, but a limited practice to start the week gives him a chance to return for Sunday's game against the 49ers. Jonathan Mingo (ankle) and Camden Brown have been seeing wideout snaps in recent weeks.

headline: Turpin (ribs) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: Turpin has not practiced since sustaining a rib injury in Week 6 and will now miss a third consecutive contest due to the issue. The main kick and punt returner for the Cowboys has been replaced by a combination of Tyler Goodson and Jonathan Mingo, who will continue to fulfill the role in his absence.

headline: Turpin (ribs) did not practice Wednesday, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: Turpin has missed the past two contests with the injury, and his Week 9 prep isn't off on the right foot. Jonathan Mingo and Camden Brown handled reserve wideout duties behind CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens (hamstring) and Ryan Flournoy last Sunday against the Cardinals.

headline: Turpin (ribs) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: Turpin continues to work through a rib injury that he sustained in Week 6 against the Packers. The injury will sideline him for a second consecutive week, and his next chance to play is Week 9 against the Colts on Sunday, Nov. 8. Tyler Goodson and Jonathan Mingo will continue to serve as the Cowboys' returners on kickoffs and special teams in Turpin's absence.

headline: Turpin (ribs) was a non-participant in practice Thursday, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: Turpin was also a DNP on Wednesday, though that was a walkthrough. The Cowboys held a standard practice Thursday, and Turpin was unable to participate, casting doubt on his availability for Sunday's game against Arizona. Still, Turpin will have a chance to log at least a limited session Friday ahead of the weekend.

headline: Turpin (ribs) was estimated to be a nonparticipant in Wednesday's walkthrough, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports.
story: Turpin continues to miss practice with a rib injury he picked up in the Cowboys' Week 6 loss to the Packers. If the team's main returner continues to miss sessions, Tyler Goodson and Jonathan Mingo should continue to return kicks in Week 8 against the Cardinals.

headline: Turpin (ribs) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Eagles, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Turpin was held out of practice all week due to a rib injury that he picked up against the Packers this past Sunday. He'll miss his first game of the regular season, and his absence means Tyler Goodson and Jonathan Mingo will likely serve as the Cowboys' returners on kickoffs and punts. Turpin's next opportunity to play is Week 8 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Turpin (ribs) did not participate at practice Thursday, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: Turpin is not expected to be available for Monday's game at Philadelphia, so it doesn't come as a big surprise that he's unable to practice as the Cowboys begin preparing for the Week 7 tilt. Unless he returns to practice Friday or Saturday, he should be expected to be out come Monday.

headline: Turpin (ribs) is expected to miss the team's Week 7 matchup with the Eagles, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.
story: Turpin suffered an injury to his ribs on the opening kickoff during the team's loss to the Packers on Sunday night. The wide receiver now appears to be on track to miss at least one game while recovering from the injury. His absence would primarily impact the team on special teams versus Philadelphia.

headline: Turpin (ribs) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday night's contest versus the Packers, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: Turpin has been sidelined since the first play of the game and he will now be forced to miss the remainder of Week 6. In his absence, running back Tyler Goodson has taken over as the team's kick returner while wide receiver Jonathan Mingo has been handling the team's punt returns.

headline: Turpin (ribs) is questionable to return to Sunday night's matchup against Green Bay, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: Turpin suffered an injury to his ribs during the game's opening kickoff, and his status for the rest of the contest is now unclear. In Turpin's absence, Dallas will have to find replacements at both kick returning and punt returning vs. the Packers.

headline: Turpin caught two of four passes for 22 yards during the Cowboys' 24-16 loss to the Buccaneers on Thursday. He also returned one punt for 10 yards and added 127 yards on five kickoff returns, fumbling on one of them.
story: Right after the Buccaneers took a 21-10 lead midway through the third quarter, Turpin gave the ball right back to Tampa Bay on the ensuing kickoff after the ball was stripped from his hands, which led to a 41-yard field goal by Chase McLaughlin eight plays later. Turpin's receiving numbers were all season highs, though that was largely due to top wideout CeeDee Lamb leaving the game due to a quad bruise. Given the extra rest, Lamb is expected to play against the Packers on Sunday, Oct. 18, so most of Turpin's on-field impact will continue to come on special teams as a returner.

headline: Flournoy wasn't targeted in Thursday's 39-38 loss to the Eagles.
story: The wideout played 55 off 77 offensive snaps and ran 29 routes on Dak Prescott's 33 dropbacks, but Flournoy was just out there doing cardio against Philadelphia. He has just one catch for 11 yards on one target over the last two games, as CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are dominating the pass-game looks in Dallas' offense.

headline: Flournoy caught just one pass for 11 yards on one target in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.
story: The Cowboys' slot receiver drew just one look on Dak Prescott's 33 pass attempts. He'd caught multiple passes in all 10 games leading up to Sunday's contest. A favorite target of Prescott in the red zone, Flournoy will try to rebound at home against the Eagles on Thanksgiving, when he'll be playable on three-game fantasy slates for Thursday.

headline: Flournoy tallied six catches for 71 yards and one touchdown on seven targets during Sunday's loss to San Francisco. He also recovered a fumble.
story: Dallas played catch-up for much of the second half in the offensive slugfest, so quarterback Dak Prescott took to the air 51 times. Flournoy got seven of those targets, finishing third on the team behind George Pickens (18) and CeeDee Lamb (13). Flournoy's six receptions and 71 yards were both his second-highest figures so far this season, and the TD was his third in the past five weeks. That last stat in particular gives him relevance in most fantasy leagues, especially in matchups during which Prescott is expected to air it out often. The Cowboys will seek a much-needed win next Sunday at home against Tennessee.

headline: Flournoy caught two of three targets for 53 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts.
story: Flournoy had a chance to operate in a more prominent role on offense with George Pickens (hamstring) inactive, but Flournoy ultimately finished with his fewest catches since Week 3, despite playing 77 of 79 offensive snaps. The wide receiver helped set up Dallas for the game-winning score late in the fourth quarter, reeling in a deep ball from quarterback Dak Prescott for a 46-yard gain. Flournoy now has reeled in 32 of 47 targets for 395 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: With George Pickens (hamstring) inactive, Flournoy is slated to move into the No. 2 WR role opposite CeeDee Lamb in Sunday's game against the Colts, while Jonathan Mingo will be the team's No. 3 receiver, Todd Archer of ESPN reports.
story: With Lamb already seeing high volume on a regular basis, Flournoy -- who has been targeted four times in each of his last two games -- could see added opportunities in Week 9, along with Mingo to some degree. To date, Flournoy has compiled a 30/342/2 receiving line on 42 targets in eight games, but he could be worth a lineup look Sunday for those scrambling to find a Pickens pivot.

headline: Flournoy caught three of four targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss to the Cardinals.
story: Flournoy ran 26 routes on Dak Prescott's 38 dropbacks against Arizona, and with Dallas moving more toward three-wide sets and away from multiple tight-end sets while decreasing Jake Ferguson's (ankle) playing time, Flournoy has been a big beneficiary in recent weeks. Over the last four weeks, Flournoy has recorded 238 yards and two touchdowns on 18 grabs across 21 targets. He's achieved WR4 valuation in fantasy and would receive a major boost if CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens ever went down with an injury.

headline: Flournoy secured all four targets for 70 yards in the Cowboys' 38-21 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
story: Flournoy tied with George Pickens for second in receptions and outgained his teammate by 13 receiving yards to finish as the runner-up in that category as well. The second-year wideout has popped for 90- and 70-yard tallies in two of his last three games, and although his week-to-week production remains somewhat erratic, Flournoy does have some upside thanks to his growing chemistry with Dak Prescott.

headline: Flournoy caught seven of nine targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 23-13 loss to the Packers.
story: Flournoy has emerged as the clear third option in the passing game for Dallas, knocking an underperforming Jake Ferguson down the target totem pole. Flournoy's nine targets trailed CeeDee Lamb's 18 and George Pickens' 11 on a night where Dak Prescott attempted 54 passes. Flournoy found the end zone late with a six-yard score, and he's now posted 23 catches for 234 yards and one score on 36 targets through six games. He's an elite bench stash in the event something happens to Lamb or Pickens.

headline: Flournoy brought in three of four targets for 90 yards in the Cowboys' 24-16 loss to the Buccaneers on Thursday night.
story: Flournoy finished tied for distant runner-up slotting in receptions, but he also was a comfortable second in receiving yards thanks in large part to a team-high 48-yard catch. His yardage tally was his highest since Week 14 of last season, and it was his first above 37 receiving yards in the current campaign. Despite the breakout Thursday, Flournoy remains a volatile week-to-week option unless CeeDee Lamb (quadriceps) or George Pickens are unavailable.

headline: Flournoy caught four of five targets for 37 yards in Dallas' 34-30 win over the Texans on Sunday.
story: His five targets were actually tied for second on the team, but it was a distant second behind CeeDee Lamb's 21 on Dak Prescott's 45 attempts. Flournoy continues to run plenty of routes as Dallas' top slot receiver between Lamb and George Pickens, but with that duo accounting for most of the receiving production in any given week, Flournoy likely will need an absence from one of them to become usable in fantasy.

headline: Flournoy caught just two of eight targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Ravens.
story: Flournoy logged 66 percent of the offensive snaps against Baltimore, and his eight targets were good for second on the team and a respectable 20 percent share. He obviously was unable to do much with them against a stingy Ravens secondary. Flournoy has a valuable role as the third receiver in a Dallas offense that likes to use plenty of 11 personnel, but he'd likely need an injury to CeeDee Lamb or George Pickens to become anything more than a bench stash in fantasy.

headline: Corbin reverted to the Cowboys' practice squad Friday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: Corbin operated as the Cowboys' RB2 behind Javonte Williams during Thursday's 39-38 loss to the Eagles, with the former turning five carries into 21 yards. Corbin has been elevated to the active roster for two consecutive weeks, and he could be brought up for Week 13 against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7.

headline: Corbin turned five carries into 21 yards during the Cowboys' 39-38 loss to the Eagles on Thursday.
story: As he's done for most of the season, Javonte Williams had a stranglehold on the Cowboys' backfield touches and finished with 29 carries for 101 yards (3.5 YPC) and two touchdowns while adding three catches on as many targets for 22 yards and another score. Corbin's five carries were second most on the Cowboys on Thursday, and he's eligible to be elevated from the practice squad one more time this season. That could come in Week 13 against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7, although Israel Abanikanda is another candidate for elevation to the active roster.

headline: The Cowboys elevated Corbin from the practice squad Wednesday.
story: The running back will again be active as Javonte Williams' backup after rushing five times for 32 yards, adding one catch for five yards on one target, across 18 offensive snaps last Sunday against the Titans.

headline: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer confirmed Tuesday that Corbin will be elevated from the practice squad for Thursday's game against the Eagles, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reports.
story: Corbin will be back up with the Cowboys for the second time in as many weeks after making a positive impression in his team debut during this past Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans. He served as the top backup to starting running back Javonte Williams in that contest, finishing with five carries for 32 yards and one catch for five yards while logging 18 of the Cowboys' 65 offensive snaps. Another strong showing in Week 12 could give Corbin a shot at earning a permanent spot on the 53-man roster.

headline: Corbin reverted to the Cowboys' practice squad Monday.
story: Corbin was elevated to the active roster ahead of the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday. He finished the contest with five carries for 32 yards and one catch for five yards, with all of those touches being spread across four quarters while he operated lead back Javonte Williams' top backup. With Tyler Goodson (knee) and Malik Davis (hip) both on injured reserve, Corbin is a top candidate to be elevated again Week 12 against the Eagles.

headline: Corbin was elevated from the Cowboys' practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.
story: Corbin signed with the Cowboys' practice squad Nov. 4, and Saturday was his first elevation to the 53-man roster. With Tyler Goodson (knee) and Malik Davis (hip) both on injured reserve, Corbin will operate as Dallas' RB2 behind workhorse Javonte Williams. Corbin last saw regular-season action in 2023, when he appeared in six games as a member of the Giants.

headline: The Cowboys signed Corbin to their practice squad Wednesday, Joe Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News reports.
story: Corbin was released from Dallas' active roster on Tuesday but is now set to join the team's practice squad. The 26-year-old didn't see any action across the first seven weeks of the campaign and hasn't appeared in a regular-season game since 2023 with the Giants.

headline: Head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday that Williams has been diagnosed with a back strain and back spasms following Thursday's 39-38 loss to the Eagles, Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News reports.
story: Williams tweaked his back late in the fourth quarter of Thursday's game and did not return, finishing with four tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks. The veteran defensive lineman's practice reps during Week 13 prep will ultimately determine what his status will be against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7.

headline: Williams injured his back during the fourth quarter of Thursday's 39-38 loss to the Eagles, but the veteran defensive lineman will have extra time to rest before the Cowboys' Week 13 tilt against the Seahawks on Monday, Dec. 7, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reports.
story: Williams recorded four tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, before leaving late in the fourth quarter due to back spasms. He was not cleared to return to Thursday's game, but there doesn't appear to be much concern over his status for Week 13 given the extended time between games.

headline: Williams (back) is questionable to return to Dallas' matchup versus the Eagles on Thursday, Tommy Yarrish of the team's official site reports.
story: Williams exited the game in the fourth quarter, leaving his status for the rest of the game up in the air. Elijah Garcia should see an uptick in playing time if Williams is unable to return.

headline: Williams recorded five tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, one forced fumble and a pass breakup in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.
story: The star defensive tackle has been one the select few bright spots on the Dallas defense this season. He leads the league with 18 tackles for loss through 11 games and has racked up 51 total tackles (30 solo), including 8.0 sacks, four forced fumbles and two pass breakups on 65 percent of the defensive snaps. Williams could be looking at another All-Pro selection in 2026.

headline: Williams (hamstring) is set to play Sunday against Arizona, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: Williams was limited in practice during the first two days of Week 8 prep, but he upgraded to full participation Friday. Consequently, he wasn't given a designation for Sunday's matchup. Williams will be looking to sack the quarterback for a third straight game, and Arizona is tied for 16th in the league with 15 sacks allowed so far.

headline: Williams (hamstring) practiced in a limited fashion Thursday, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: Williams was also labeled as limited for Wednesday's walkthrough, so the hamstring issue isn't entirely preventing him from practicing. Still, the veteran defender will likely get tagged with a designation for Sunday's matchup against Arizona if he's not able to upgrade to full participation Friday. Williams has been an important part of the Cowboys' pass rush of late, logging a sack in three of his past four games.

headline: Williams (hamstring) was estimated to be a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports.
story: Williams is dealing with a hamstring injury he likely sustained in the Cowboys' Week 7 win over the Eagles on Monday. The defensive lineman will probably need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.

headline: Spann-Ford caught his lone target for 15 yards during Dallas' loss to the Eagles on Thursday.
story: Spann-Ford served as the team's starting tight end for the third consecutive game as Jake Ferguson remains sidelined with a knee injury. However, Spann-Ford had a quiet outing but will look to play a larger role next week versus the Seahawks if Ferguson is out again.

headline: Spann-Ford caught both of his targets for five yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.
story: With Jake Ferguson (knee) still sidelined, Spann-Ford played 44 of 65 offensive snaps against Tennessee and ran 17 routes on Dak Prescott's 36 dropbacks. The Cowboys don't throw to their tight ends often and funnel most targets through CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, but Spann-Ford did catch a two-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter. He has 18 catches for 161 yards and the one score on 26 targets across 11 games this season.

headline: Spann-Ford caught one of three targets for 26 yards during the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
story: Spann-Ford operated as the Cowboys' No. 1 tight end in Week 10 due to the absence of Jake Ferguson (knee). However, George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy were the top targets for Dak Prescott. Ferguson is expected to be sidelined for multiple weeks while recovering from his injury, so Spann-Ford should once again top the depth chart in Week 11 against a Titans team that has given up 40-plus points in each of its last two games.

headline: Spann-Ford caught two of three targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win versus the Colts.
story: Spann-Ford opened Week 9 in his typical reserve role behind Jake Ferguson at tight end, but Ferguson suffered a knee injury in the third quarter. With Ferguson set to miss multiple weeks of action, Spann-Ford will have a chance to operate as the team's primary option at tight end beginning in Week 10 versus the 49ers. On the season thus far, Spann-Ford has reeled in 19 of 27 targets for 136 yards and four touchdowns over nine contests.

headline: Spann-Ford caught four of five targets for 31 yards during Sunday's 33-30 overtime loss versus the Cardinals.
story: Starting tight end Jake Ferguson logged only four offensive snaps before leaving Sunday's contest with an ankle injury, and Spann-Ford ended up playing a career-high 65 offensive snaps as a result. He ended up second on the team in targets behind CeeDee Lamb (11), and he could be worth a look as a streaming option in deeper formats if Ferguson is unable to suit up in Week 9 at Indianapolis.

headline: Spann-Ford finished with two catches for 11 yards on two targets in Monday's 38-21 win over the Eagles.
story: With the Cowboys opening the game in 12 personnel, Spann-Ford was credited with a start and was on the field for 36 of the team's 68 offensive snaps on the night (52.9 percent). Though Jake Ferguson is locked in as Dallas' top tight end, Spann-Ford has consistently repped ahead of Luke Schoonmaker as the No. 2 option at the position since Week 2. While he's mainly functioned as a blocker, Spann-Ford has been a solid complementary option in the passing game with a 9-79-0 line on 13 targets.

headline: Aubrey converted one of his two field-goal attempts and all five of his extra-point tries during Dallas' 39-38 loss to the Eagles on Thursday.
story: Aubrey missed a kick from 40 yards out in the fourth quarter, which ended up being the difference in the game. The 31-year-old has now converted 21 of his 26 field-goal attempts and 36 of his 38 extra-point tries across 12 games this season and will look to bounce back during next week's matchup against the Seahawks.

headline: Aubrey made his lone field-goal attempt and all six PATs in Sunday's 51-30 win over the Titans.
story: The Cowboys scored touchdowns on each of their first six possessions against Tennessee, so Aubrey was busy kicking extra points. His field goal was good from 49 yards in the second half. It's been a struggle at times for Aubrey this season, as he's made just 20 of 25 field-goal tries through 11 games, but he's 31-for-33 on extra points in Dallas' high-octane offense.

headline: Aubrey made both of his field-goal attempts and went 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
story: Aubrey connected on 52-yard field goals in both the first and third quarters, although his PAT in the second missed wide left. It was the second missed extra-point try of the season for Aubrey and his seventh miss overall, although five of those failed kicks have come on field-goal attempts from 50-plus yards. The Cowboys will stay home for Week 11 against the Titans, who give up 26.6 points per game (27th in the NFL) and have yielded 40-plus points in each of their last two contests.

headline: Aubrey went 2-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his PATs during Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts.
story: Aubrey was able to convert multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game, but he did miss a kick for the second straight week. The kicker had makes from 45 and 28 yards in the contest, but he continued his long-range struggles Sunday, pulling a 50-yard attempt wide left late in the fourth quarter. Aubrey has now gone 17-for-22 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-8 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests to open the 2026 campaign.

headline: Aubrey made three of his four field-goal attempts and all three PATs in the Cowboys' 33-30 overtime loss to the Cardinals.
story: Aubrey missed a 61-yard field goal before halftime in a game that ended with a three-point difference. The kicker converted from 31 yards, 35 yards and 41 yards in the contest as the Cowboys offense ended up stalling after long drives multiple times. Aubrey moves to 15-for-19 on field-goal attempts and 20-for-21 on PATs through eight regular-season games in 2026.

headline: Aubrey made all three of his field-goal attempts and all three PAT tries in Monday's 38-21 win over the Eagles.
story: Aubrey benefited from a bounce-back performance out of Dallas' offense, as he had been limited to one field-goal attempt and two PATs over the previous two games combined. Monday marked the third time Aubrey made three field goals in a game this season, as he connected from 55, 27 and 24 yards. Aubrey's likely to remain busy in Week 8 against the Cardinals, who are giving up a league-high 29.7 points per game.

headline: Aubrey did not attempt any field goals but converted his only extra-point try during Sunday's 23-13 loss at Green Bay.
story: In a game where the Cowboys fell into a hole early and turned the ball over three times in opposing territory, Aubrey was mostly a spectator, failing to make at least one field goal in a game for the first time since Week 1 against the Giants. Dallas' offense will have better days than it did Sunday, and one of those could come in Week 7 against a Philadelphia defense that has looked poor at times this season.

headline: Aubrey made his only field-goal attempt and his lone extra-point try in a Week 5 loss to Tampa Bay on Thursday.
story: Aubrey didn't get many opportunities to kick, but he did nail a 41-yard FG just before halftime. The All-Pro kicker is now 9-for-12 on field-goal tries this season, with all of his misses (including two that were blocked) coming from at least 59 yards out. Aubrey is still one of the league's elite kickers, and he figures to continue getting opportunities from very deep considering the strength of his leg.

headline: Aubrey went 2-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made all four PATs in Sunday's 34-30 win over the Texans.
story: Both of Aubrey's misses were from long distance, as he had a 62-yard attempt blocked and a 65-yard try go wide left, both of which came in the second quarter. He did convert 39- and 50-yard tries. On the season, Aubrey is now 7-for-10 on field-goal tries and 12-for-13 on extra-point attempts. He'll remain a top fantasy kicker for Thursday's game against the Bucs.

headline: Pickens caught five of nine targets for 67 yards in Thursday's 39-38 loss to the Eagles.
story: It was a step back for Pickens after he hauled in 18 of 28 targets for 247 yards and four TDs over the prior two games. The 25-year-old wideout is the clear No. 2 option in the Dallas passing attack behind CeeDee Lamb, but the team's woeful defense and limited depth behind the duo ensures that Pickens will see big volume from Dak Prescott more often than not. Pickens will take a 62-847-6 line on 99 targets into a Week 13 clash with the Seahawks.

headline: Pickens secured seven of 10 targets for 102 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.
story: Pickens played second fiddle to CeeDee Lamb (11-132-1) in Sunday's blowout win, but that still equated to a rewarding effort for the franchise-tagged receiver. The game marked Pickens' third 100-yard tally of the season and second straight, and he now has seen double-digit targets in four of the last six games overall. Pickens rounded out his day Sunday with his sixth touchdown reception of the campaign on a 10-yard catch in the latter portion of the second quarter, and he should be teed up for another busy day when the Cowboys host the Eagles for a Week 12 matchup on Thanksgiving Day.

headline: Pickens brought in 11 of 18 targets for 145 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys' 46-40 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
story: After watching fellow wideout CeeDee Lamb have several monster performances through the first half of the season, Pickens stepped up and took his turn in his return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Pickens was peppered with targets from Dak Prescott all afternoon, and the star receiver finished with career-high reception and target totals and a season high in receiving yards. Pickens struck from 35, 39 and five yards out on his trio of scoring grabs, which constituted Dak Prescott's first three TD passes on the day. A now clearly healthy Pickens is up to a 50-678-5 line on 80 targets for the season heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

headline: Pickens (hamstring) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the 49ers, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: After being listed as limited on five consecutive injury reports going back to last week due to a hamstring issue, Pickens practiced fully Friday and thus is set to miss just one game as a result. In eight appearances so far this season, he's talled a 39-533-2 line on 62 targets.

headline: Pickens (hamstring) moved well in Thursday's practice, which coach Brian Schottenheimer said is a positive sign for the wide receiver's availability for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports.
story: Pickens didn't play last week but has a chance to avoid further absences. He's been a limited practice participant so far this week, and a 'questionable' designation seems likely heading into the weekend. We'll find out more when the Cowboys release their final injury report Friday afternoon/evening.

headline: Pickens (hamstring) practiced in a limited fashion Thursday, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports.
story: As he was a week ago, Pickens continues to operate with practice restrictions, giving him just one more chance this week to get back to full Friday, at which point the Cowboys may tag him with a designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers. He's looking to limit his absence to only one contest due to a hamstring injury.

headline: Pickens (hamstring) was in uniform and taking part in individual drills during Thursday's practice, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reports.
