Cobie Durant will likely fill in for Bland should the standout cornerback miss any time.

headline: Bland (ankle) will undergo X-rays and an MRI, Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News reports.
story: Bland hurt his ankle during Sunday's loss to San Francisco and couldn't finish the game. The issue may be an aggravation of the injury that limited the cornerback in practice Friday. The results of Bland's imaging should provide clarity about whether he's at risk of missing additional time. Cobie Durant would likely slide back into a starting role if Bland does have to sit out any games.

headline: Bland (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's matchup versus San Francisco, Calvin Watkins of The Dallas Morning News reports.
story: Bland dealt with an ankle issue throughout Week 10 prep, so he may have aggravated the injury Sunday. The veteran cornerback has logged every defensive snap in six of Dallas' nine games so far, so it will be a significant blow to the Cowboys' secondary if he's unable to return. Cobie Durant has entered the game in Bland's stead.

headline: Bland (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports.
story: Bland was added to Friday's injury report with an ankle injury. The starting outside cornerback seems to have recovered from the recent injury in time for Sunday's contest. Bland will suit up across from Joey Porter, who missed Week 9 due to an ankle injury of his own.

headline: Bland (ankle), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, is expected to play, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Bland was added to the Cowboys' injury report Friday after the ankle issue limited his participation in the team's final practice of Week 10, but the injury doesn't look as though it will prevent him from suiting up Sunday. Additionally, Joey Porter (ankle) is listed as questionable but trending toward playing after a one-game absence, so Dallas looks as though it will have both of its top two cornerbacks available versus San Francisco.

headline: Bland (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports.
story: Bland first appeared on Friday's practice report as a limited participant, which indicates that he injured his ankle during that session. That's not a good sign for Bland heading into the weekend, and the Cowboys could be without both of their starting outside cornerbacks depending on the status of Joey Porter (ankle), who is also listed as questionable. Cobie Durant, Ameer Speed and Shavon Revel are the top candidates to start at outside cornerback if one or both of Bland or Porter were to miss time.

headline: Bryant caught four of seven targets for 42 yards in Friday's 27-5 loss to the Steelers.
story: Bryant finished third on the team in receiving yards behind Jaylen Waddle (53) and Jonah Coleman (46). Heading into a Week 13 home game against the Dolphins, Bryant continues to be Denver's most efficient wide receiver. The 2025 third-round pick is averaging 9.4 yards per target compared to Waddle's 6.8 YPT and Courtland Sutton's abhorrent 4.8 YPT following the latter's four-yard, eight-target performance Friday.

headline: Bryant caught three passes for 32 yards on four targets in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders.
story: The wideout briefly exited the game in the third quarter after he appeared to tweak his previously injured ankle, but Bryant quickly returned and was able to finish out the contest. His four targets were fourth on the team on a day Bo Nix targeted nine different players on 35 pass attempts. The Denver offense spreads the ball around to five different receivers, three tight ends and its running backs most weeks, making it difficult for any of the pass catchers to post big numbers in the box score.

headline: Bryant returned to Sunday's game against the Raiders after making a brief visit to the sideline tent, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
story: Bryant's time away from the field occurred in the middle of the third quarter. He'll look to build upon the 3-32-0 line on three targets that he accrued to that point in the contest.

headline: Bryant caught four of five targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina.
story: Bryant was activated from IR on Saturday after recovering from an ankle injury, and he came up big late in Sunday's contest, hauling in a 26-yard TD strike from Bo Nix with less than six minutes left in the fourth quarter for what proved to be the game-winning score. The second-year wideout's clutch play came after Jaylen Waddle (concussion) had left the game, and if a Week 10 bye doesn't give him enough time to recover, Bryant could see an elevated role in Week 11 against the Raiders.

headline: Bryant (ankle) is active for Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Panthers.
story: The second-year wideout foreshadowed a return to game action this past week by putting in three full practices, which led to his activation from injured reserve Saturday. Bryant still carried a questionable tag heading into Sunday, but with his availability now confirmed, he should be ready to reprise the No. 3 role he filled behind Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle prior to his Week 4 injury. Bryant saw generally modest volume during his three-plus games to date, posting a 9-133-1 line on 12 targets and adding a 16-yard rush on his one carry.

headline: Bryant (ankle) was activated from injured reserve Saturday, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game in Carolina, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
story: Bryant was carted off the field due to a sprained right ankle during a Week 4 loss at San Francisco that forced him to injured reserve before Week 5 action. Since the Broncos designated him for return from IR on Wednesday, he logged full practices during the entirety of Week 9 prep, and while he was listed as questionable for Sunday, head coach Sean Payton told Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette on Friday that the second-year pro is in line to play this weekend. Ultimately, Bryant's status will be confirmed about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Coach Sean Payton said Friday that Bryant (ankle) is in line to play in Sunday's game against the Panthers, Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette reports.
story: Though Bryant, who was designated to return from IR on Wednesday, is officially listed as questionable ahead of Week 9 action, he practiced fully all week and is thus slated to be activated no later than Saturday, at which point his injury designation could be removed. If he is indeed in uniform this weekend, he'll have an opportunity to reclaim a key role in a Denver WR corps that has thus far been led by Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton.

headline: Bryant (ankle) was a full participant at the Broncos' practice Wednesday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
story: After being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Bryant was back on the practice field with no restrictions. With a bye looming for the Broncos in Week 10, it's unclear if the team will decide to activate the wide receiver before Sunday's matchup with the Panthers. Regardless of whatever decision the team makes, Bryant appears to be fully recovered from the ankle injury that has sidelined him since Week 4.

headline: The Broncos designated Bryant (ankle) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
story: Help is on the way for the Broncos' passing game, as Bryant is making progress toward a return now that his 21-day practice window has been opened. Though the wideout will be back on the field to begin Week 9 prep, it's unclear if the Broncos intend to activate him from IR ahead of Sunday's game at Carolina.

headline: Bryant (ankle) was placed on the Broncos' injured reserve Friday.
story: Because of his placement on IR due to an ankle injury, Bryant will be required to miss at least the next four games. The earliest he can return is Week 9 against the Panthers on Sunday, Nov. 11, but with the Broncos on bye for Week 10, the second-year wide receiver could be held out until Week 11 against the Raiders in late November. Troy Franklin figures to step into the WR3 role behind Courtland Sutton and Jaylen Waddle for as long as Bryant is sidelined.

headline: The Broncos plan to place Bryant (ankle) on injured reserve, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: The official transaction should happen at some point Friday or Saturday. With Bryant ruled out for the next four games, Troy Franklin is the favorite to step in as Denver's No. 3 wide receiver. Marvin Mims and Lil'Jordan Humphrey also could take on roles.

headline: Bryant (ankle) isn't participating in Thursday's practice, Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette reports.
story: Though Bryant looks poised to avoid a stint on injured reserve after an MRI on the right ankle he injured in Sunday's loss to the 49ers ruled out a long-term injury, the second-year wideout still appears likely to miss some time. He's been a spectator for the Broncos' first two practices of Week 5 and likely will be officially ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers following Friday's session.

headline: Bryant (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
story: Bryant sprained his right ankle during the Broncos' Week 4 loss to the 49ers. An MRI did not reveal a high-ankle sprain, which is good news for the second-year wide receiver. Bryant is still expected to miss time, so he can be considered on the doubtful side for Sunday's AFC West showdown against the Chargers. He has a 9-133-1 receiving line (on 12 targets) through four games, and assuming Bryant is sidelined for Week 5, that workload will be absorbed by Jaylen Waddle, Courtland Sutton, Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin.

headline: The Broncos are confident that Bryant avoided a long-term right ankle injury after an MRI on Monday yielded good news, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: The report doesn't offer any specifics regarding what the MRI revealed, but Bryant may have avoided a dreaded high-ankle sprain after exiting Sunday's 24-14 loss to the 49ers. Bryant still appears likely to miss time due to the injury, with Adam Schefter of ESPN relaying Monday that the second-year wideout is expected to be sidelined for "a few weeks." Assuming Bryant is out for at least this Sunday's game against the Chargers, the Broncos would have more reps available for Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin behind starting receivers Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton.

headline: Bryant is expected to miss "a few weeks" after spraining his right ankle in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the 49ers, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Bryant finished with three receptions for 47 yards on three targets before he checked out of the game after he appeared to injure the ankle when he was tackled at the end of his final catch of the day with just under three minutes left in the third quarter. The second-year wideout's expected absence should open up more playing time for Marvin Mims and/or Troy Franklin as the Broncos' No. 3 receiver behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton.

headline: Bryant (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the 49ers, Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette reports.
story: Bryant was injured at the tail end of a catch in the second half and had to be carted to the locker room. That he's being considered questionable to return may suggest it's not a serious injury for Bryant. Prior to leaving, he caught all three of his targets for 47 yards. Marvin Mims and Troy Franklin are next in line for snaps behind Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton.

headline: Bryant (leg) was carted off the field in the third quarter of Sunday's contest against the 49ers, Jennifer Lee Chan of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Bryant suffered a right leg injury after a catch and run of 30 yards with 2:47 left in the third quarter. The wide receiver's day is almost certainly done, and it's possible that he will be forced to miss action moving forward. More information on his status will likely be provided in the near future, and in the meantime, Jaylen Waddle and Courtland Sutton will continue to operate as the top two wideouts for Denver.

headline: Bryant recorded two receptions for 44 yards and a touchdown on two targets in Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams. He also scored on a two-point conversion.
story: Bryant reached the end zone for the first time this season with 7:44 left in the third quarter, connecting with quarterback Bo Nix on a five-yard catch. The second-year wideout has seen his snap share gradually climb through the first three weeks, topping out at 70 percent in Week 3. The Broncos have been without Marvin Mims (foot) for the past two games, however, so Bryant could see a slight downturn in playing time once the Denver receiving corps is at full strength.

headline: Sutton caught one of eight targets for four yards in Friday's 27-5 loss to the Steelers.
story: Denver's entire offense struggled mightily, generating just three points while allowing Pittsburgh's defense to score two touchdowns off turnovers by Bo Nix. Sutton was right down there with Nix among Friday's worst performers in an outing reminiscent of Week 4 at San Francisco, when Sutton caught one of six targets for four yards. The 31-year-old WR has caught just one of 10 targets over the past two games, and Sutton has secured less than half of his targets (26 of 56) heading into a Week 13 home game against the Dolphins.

headline: Sutton didn't corral either of his two targets during Sunday's 38-24 victory versus the Raiders.
story: Sutton thus was blanked in the box score for the first time Week 7 of the 2024 campaign, a span of 39 games (including playoffs). Considering he's surpassed 50 receiving yards just one time in 10 appearances in 2026, he doesn't hold much sway for fantasy purposes, especially in a Broncos offense that often has sputtered this season. Sutton's next chance to turn the tide arrives Friday at Pittsburgh.

headline: Sutton caught five of nine targets for 45 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
story: The five grabs and nine targets led the Broncos on the day, but Pat Bryant just edged him out for the receiving yards lead. The highlight of Sutton's solid performance was a three-yard TD from Bo Nix in the first quarter, as none of his receptions went for longer than 12 yards. Denver gets a well-timed bye in Week 10, but if Jaylen Waddle (concussion) isn't cleared to play on the other side of it, Sutton could see bigger volume in Week 11 against the Raiders. On the season, the long-time Bronco sports a 25-266-2 line on 46 targets through nine games.

headline: Sutton caught all four of his targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City.
story: For the fourth straight game, Sutton failed to see more than five targets, but his four grabs and 53 yards were both season highs. It's been a rough campaign so far for the 31-year-old receiver in an inconsistent Broncos aerial attack, and Sutton will take a 20-221-1 line on 37 targets through eight games intro a Week 9 clash with the Panthers.

headline: Sutton (undisclosed) briefly left Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
story: Sutton went to the medical tent after taking a hard hit, but the wideout was able to return to action not long after he did so. In the process he'll bolster a Denver Week 9 WR corps that also includes Jaylen Waddle, Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims and Lil'Jordan Humphrey.

headline: Sutton caught three of five targets for 45 yards during Sunday's 30-16 win over Arizona.
story: Sutton was able to reel in three passes for the first time since Week 3, and his 45 receiving yards were his second highest total in a contest this year. The wide receiver has had an overall disappointing campaign so far, but Jaylen Waddle (chest) exited the contest in the fourth quarter, so Sutton could be thrust into a more prominent role in Week 8 against the Chiefs.

headline: Sutton brought in two of three targets for 19 yards in the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks on Thursday.
story: Sutton tied for third in receptions and targets while holding the same slotting in receiving yards for the Broncos on a night when Bo Nix could manage only 107 passing yards. The veteran wideout also took a hard hit on the one target he couldn't corral, and Sam Jane of The Denver Post reported Sutton was seen bent over and slightly limping on the sideline but never required a trip to the medical tent. Like fellow wideout Jaylen Waddle, the long-time Bronco's production has suffered as a result of Nix's tendency to stick to a very short-area passing attack this season, as Sutton is averaging a career-low 9.5 yards per reception heading into a Week 7 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday, Oct. 25.

headline: Sutton posted two catches (on three targets) for 18 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 23-17 victory at the Chargers.
story: Sutton has found the going tough through five games this season, sitting on 11 catches for 104 yards on 25 targets, but his five-yard TD connection Sunday with QB Bo Nix marked the wide receiver's first of the campaign, salvaging his day somewhat from a fantasy perspective. Considering his volume has fallen from 7.6 targets per game in his first two seasons working with Nix to 5.0 in 2026, Sutton doesn't hold much appeal at the moment in the Broncos offense.

headline: Sutton caught just one of six targets for four yards in Sunday's 24-14 loss to the 49ers.
story: Sutton has been wholly unproductive to begin the season, producing just nine catches for 86 scoreless yards on 21 targets through four games. His 0.69 yards per route run is easily a low point for his career. Sutton has not been productive as a fantasy player so far, and it doesn't help that he plays in a low-scoring offense that likes to spread the ball around to multiple different players.

headline: Nix completed 22 of 40 passes for 169 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions in Friday's 27-5 loss to the Steelers. He also rushed once for seven yards and lost a fumble.
story: Nix was directly responsible for two first-half Pittsburgh touchdowns, as T.J. Watt recovered a Nix fumble in the end zone to open the scoring and Jalen Ramsey scored on a pick-six to extend Pittsburgh's lead to 24-5. Neither offense did much after halftime as Nix continued to struggle. Friday's dud drops Nix's season average to just 193 passing yards per game to go with a 12:7 TD:INT through 11 starts, but the Broncos still boast an excellent 8-3 record heading into a Week 13 home game against the Dolphins.

headline: T.J. Watt recovers Bo Nix's fumble for a Steelers TD
story: T.J. Watt recovers Bo Nix's fumble for a Steelers TD

headline: Nix completed 19 of 35 passes for 225 yards, one touchdown and one interception and notched six carries for five yards during Sunday's 38-24 victory against the Raiders.
story: After a hit-or-miss first six appearances of the season, Nix has settled into a four-game stretch in which his passing yards have ranged from 222 to 237 weekly, a span in which he boasts a 6:2 TD:INT and 84 rushing yards and another score. He also displayed some promise with offseason acquisition Jaylen Waddle (3-61-0 on six targets) while connecting with TE Adam Trautman for his 12th touchdown pass in 10 contests. Nix will look to keep things rolling Friday at Pittsburgh.

headline: Nix completed 25 of 37 passes for 237 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers. He added two rushing yards on five carries.
story: The Broncos had the home team right where they wanted them heading into the fourth quarter -- holding a lead -- and Nix worked his usual magic over the final 15 minutes, leading back-to-back touchdown drives capped by a nine-yard TD run from Jonah Coleman and a 26-yard strike to Pat Bryant for what proved to be the winning score. Nix did throw his first INT since Week 3 in the win, but he heads into a Week 10 bye with Denver riding a five-game win streak that has taken it to the top of the AFC West.

headline: Nix completed 20 of 32 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City. He added four rushing yards on three carries and threw a two-point conversion to Jaylen Waddle.
story: The Broncos were staring at a 24-13 deficit heading into the fourth quarter, but late comebacks are nothing new for Nix. The QB hit Nate Adkins for a two-yard score with about nine minutes left before connecting with Jonah Coleman on a 51-yard catch-and-run to set up the game-winning TD plunge by the rookie RB just after the two-minute warning. It's the 15th time that Nix has led Denver on a game-winning drive in the fourth quarter or overtime, the most by any quarterback in the first three seasons of his career since the AFL-NFL merger in 1970. While he's thrown multiple TDs just twice in the first eight games of the season, Nix has gone five straight contests without tossing an INT. He'll take a 9:3 TD:INT into a Week 9 road tilt against the Panthers.

headline: Nix completed 15 of 29 passes for 222 yards and a touchdown while rushing seven times for 73 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals.
story: Nix led the Broncos in rushing yards thanks to a 62-yard rushing touchdown in the second quarter, which was the longest regular-season rushing score by a QB since Justin Fields ran in a 67-yard TD in 2022. Nix added a 52-yard touchdown pass to RJ Harvey in the third quarter, but it was another quiet outing as a passer for the third-year QB, as Nix has only one multi-touchdown performance through seven starts and is averaging just 182 passing yards per game. Those poor numbers include a 131-yard, one-TD Week 1 performance against the Chiefs, whom the Broncos will host for a Week 8 rematch.

headline: Nix completed 17 of 27 passes for 107 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed four times for two yards in the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks on Thursday. He also recovered a fumble.
story: Nix continued his season-long trend of sticking to mostly short-area passes, leading to a season-low passing yardage figure and average of 4.0 yards per attempt. The third-year signal-caller did reverse a trend of three straight games with sub-60.0 percent completion rates, but Nix also failed to throw a touchdown for the first time all season. Denver's defense did most of the heavy lifting, and both of the Broncos' touchdowns came on the ground, while Nix now has three sub-200-yard passing efforts in the last four contests. The Oregon product should have a good chance of boosting his numbers in Week 7, however, as the Broncos visit the defensively challenged Cardinals on Sunday, Oct. 25.

headline: Nix was 16-for-27 passing for 123 yards, one touchdown and no interceptions, took four carries for 10 yards and fumbled twice (one lost) during Sunday's 23-17 victory at the Chargers.
story: With head coach Sean Payton taking over play-calling duties from offensive coordinator Davis Webb in Week 5, the decision didn't exactly light a fire under Nix and the Broncos offense. Nix settled for his fewest passing yards of the season, but he at least tossed a TD pass (to WR Courtland Sutton) for a fifth game in a row to kick off the campaign, giving him a 6:3 TD:INT so far. Nix may have a tough time producing better results on a short week when Denver hosts the defending champion Seahawks on Thursday night.

headline: Waddle caught five of eight targets for 53 yards in Friday's 27-5 loss to the Steelers.
story: Waddle has exceeded 50 yards in consecutive games for the first time in his Broncos tenure, but his eight catches for 114 yards over the past two games still aren't anything to write home about. With QB Bo Nix struggling, Waddle has substantially underperformed the lofty expectations that accompanied the speedy wideout from Miami to Denver when the Broncos sent a first-round pick the other way in an offseason trade. Waddle will face his former team in Week 13, having caught 38 of 66 targets for 451 yards and two touchdowns through 11 games with his new club.

headline: Dopp out on Jaylen Waddle in Week 12 vs. Steelers
story: Dopp out on Jaylen Waddle in Week 12 vs. Steelers

headline: Waddle secured three of six targets for 61 yards during Sunday's 38-24 win versus the Raiders.
story: Waddle sustained a concussion in the Broncos' last game in Week 9 at Carolina, but with the benefit of a Week 10 bye, he had enough time to gain clearance from the protocol for head injuries and miss no additional time as a result. With a 24-yard connection with QB Bo Nix on Sunday, Waddle now has recorded exactly one catch of at least that distance in four straight games. Unfortunately for Waddle's fantasy managers, his 61 receiving yards marked his second most of the campaign after a 138-yard outburst in Week 2 against the Jaguars, so he remains an underwhelming asset in most formats.

headline: Waddle (concussion) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Raiders after practicing fully this week.
story: Waddle was limited to just 14 snaps and one catch for 22 yards before exiting the Broncos' Week 9 win over the Panthers with a concussion. Following a well-time Week 10 bye, Waddle has progressed through the NFL's concussion protocol, ensuring that Denver's top pass catcher -- who has recorded a 30/337/2 receiving line on 52 targets through nine contests -- will be available this weekend.

headline: Waddle (concussion) was a full practice participant Thursday.
story: A full practice participant for the second day in a row, Waddle looks to be close to clearing the NFL's concussion protocol after he sustained the head injury in a Nov. 8 win over the Panthers. Assuming he can receive clearance from an independent neurologist by the weekend, Waddle will be removed from the protocol and suit up Sunday versus the Raiders.

headline: Waddle (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Waddle sustained a concussion during a Nov. 8 win over the Panthers, and it looks like the Broncos' Week 10 bye has afforded their most productive wideout enough recovery time to be available Sunday against the Raiders. However, since it has yet to be officially confirmed that Waddle has cleared the NFL's concussion protocol, his status will still need to be monitored until that happens.

headline: Waddle (concussion) was present for Wednesday's practice, Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette reports.
story: Denver is back from the bye, and Waddle is back on the practice field after suffering a concussion in Week 9 against the Panthers. It hasn't been reported whether Waddle has cleared the protocol at this stage, but his presence at Wednesday's practice is a positive marker going into Sunday's game against the Raiders.

headline: Waddle (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
story: After being evaluated for a potential concussion, Waddle is done for the day and will thus target a potential return to action Nov. 22 against the Raiders, following Denver's Week 10 bye. In his absence Sunday, Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims will handle the team's WR duties versus Carolina.

headline: Waddle is being evaluated for a potential concussion during Sunday's game against the Panthers, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
story: Per Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette, Waddle headed to the locker room Sunday after having absorbed a hard hit, leaving Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims as the Broncos' available WRs. Prior to his exit, Waddle caught his only target for 22 yards.

headline: Waddle caught three of six targets for 39 yards and a touchdown and added a two-point conversion in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City.
story: Despite the fact that the wideout was playing through a chest injury, Waddle came up big when it counted, connecting with Bo Nix on a one-yard TD in the second quarter before snagging a two-point conversion in the fourth as Denver mounted a comeback from a 24-13 deficit. Waddle's 29-315-2 line on 51 targets through his first eight games as a Bronco is disappointing, but he still has time to pick up the pace beginning with a Week 9 tilt against the Panthers.

headline: Waddle (chest) is active for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
story: Waddle attempted to play through a chest injury in Week 7, but he exited in the fourth quarter and didn't return. He then didn't practice to open Week 8 prep before back-to-back limited sessions Thursday and Friday left him listed as questionable. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Sunday morning that Waddle is trending well to play, which now has been confirmed. Since joining the Broncos via trade in the offseason, Waddle has had one vintage performance (8-138-0 on 10 targets versus Jacksonville in Week 2), but he otherwise has combined for an 18-138-1 line on 35 targets in his six other appearances in 2026.

headline: Waddle (chest) is trending in a positive direction for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Waddle made a late exit from the Broncos' Week 7 win at Arizona due to a chest injury, which held him out of practice Wednesday before limited sessions Thursday and Friday left him questionable for Week 8 action. He may need to go through a pregame warmup unscathed to be available Sunday, something that'll be confirmed about 90 minutes before a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Waddle (chest) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Chiefs after he was a limited participant in Friday's practice.
story: After opening the week with a missed practice and then logging limited sessions Thursday and Friday, Waddle's status remains unsettled heading into the weekend. The Broncos and Chiefs are scheduled for a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, which could mean limited alternatives for fantasy managers if Waddle comes down to a game-time decision and then doesn't play. If that were to happen, Denver would likely look to Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims and Lil'Jordan Humphrey to take more WR snaps alongside Courtland Sutton.

headline: Waddle (chest) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
story: Waddle departed in the fourth quarter of this past Sunday's win at Arizona due to a chest injury, which limited him in practice last Wednesday and Thursday before he returned to a full session Friday and didn't enter the weekend with a designation. This week has been a different story, though, as he kicked it off with a DNP on Wednesday before Thursday's capped session. Friday's injury report will reveal Waddle's chances to suit up Sunday against the Chiefs.

headline: Waddle (chest) is present for the medica-access portion of Thursday's practice, Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette reports.
story: Waddle was listed as a non-participant despite being seen at the media-access portion of Wednesday's practice, so his fantasy managers shouldn't rejoice just yet. That being said, it's likely that the veteran wide receiver will put forth at least some level of participation Thursday, which will be clarified on Thursday's practice report. Waddle faced limitations in practice during Week 7 prep due to a chest injury that he ultimately aggravated in a win over the Cardinals.

headline: Waddle (chest) was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: According to Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com, Waddle was present for the media-access portion of practice, but he didn't end up doing enough on the field to go down as a limited participant on the Broncos' first report of Week 8. The wideout thus has two more opportunities to log practice reps ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Per Mike Klis of 9News Denver, the Broncos remain hopeful that Waddle will be able to suit up Sunday, after he aggravated the chest injury when he was tackled for a 12-yard loss after bobbling a pitch from quarterback Bo Nix on a reverse play in last week's win over the Cardinals.

headline: Waddle (chest) was present for Wednesday's practice, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
story: The extent of Waddle's participation has yet to be revealed, but it's encouraging that he was with the team for Wednesday's session. Waddle is dealing with a chest injury that had him reported as uncertain to play this week as of early Wednesday. Things seem to be trending in the right direction, but Friday's injury report will give the firm answer on Waddle's status going into the big game against the Chiefs.

headline: Waddle aggravated a previous chest injury during last week's 30-16 win over the Cardinals, and his status for Sunday's game against the Chiefs will be determined based on how he fares in practice this week, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Waddle recorded four receptions for 48 yards on seven targets against Arizona before checking out of the game in the fourth quarter due to the lingering chest issue, which had limited his participation in two practices during Week 7 prep. The wideout's practice activity appears likely to be affected in Week 8, but the Broncos aren't yet counting him out from suiting up against the Chiefs.

headline: Waddle didn't return to Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals due to a chest injury, Parker Gabriel of the Denver Post reports.
story: Waddle went to the locker room in the fourth quarter, and the Broncos confirmed shortly before the end of the game that he was dealing with a chest injury. Sunday's injury could be an aggravation of the chest injury that bothered Waddle in practice leading up to the game. Waddle is likely to pop up on the injury report as the Broncos prepare for a Week 8 rematch with the Chiefs, who defeated Denver in Week 1. He finished with four catches for 48 yards on seven targets against the Cardinals.

headline: Waddle (undisclosed) headed to the locker room in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
story: Waddle had his practice reps limited leading up to the game due to a chest injury. He was grabbing at his chest/shoulder area prior to exiting, per Gabriel, suggesting Waddle may have aggravated the injury as he went to the ground to avoid a fumble on a botched reverse. Prior to getting hurt, Waddle caught four of seven targets for 48 yards.

headline: Waddle (chest) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Arizona.
story: Waddle already confirmed that he'll play. He upgraded to full practice participation Friday after being limited earlier in the week. Waddle has a target share of 22 percent and an air-yardage share of 35 percent, but he's averaging just 38.0 receiving yards per game in a struggling Denver offense.

headline: Waddle (chest) said he is good to go for Sunday's game at Arizona after being listed as a limited practice participant the previous two days, Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette reports.
story: It remains to be seen if Waddle will duck an injury designation, but he left no doubt that he expects to play.

headline: Waddle (chest) remained a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: With back-to-back limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, Waddle appears to at least have a good chance to play through the issue Sunday against Arizona. Waddle has been one of the more disappointing early-round fantasy picks through six weeks, collecting just 22 catches for 228 yards and one touchdown on 38 targets across six games.

headline: Waddle (chest) was at practice Thursday after being limited Wednesday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
story: Waddle at least hasn't taken a step back, though it remains to be seen if he can upgrade to full participation Thursday and assuage any concerns about missing Sunday's game against the Cardinals. The offseason trade acquisition has lived up to the hype only once through six games with the Broncos, notching 138 receiving yards in Week 2 against the Jaguars and just 90 receiving yards across five other games combined.

headline: Waddle was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a chest injury, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
story: Waddle missed a brief spell in last Thursday's win against the Seahawks due to a shoulder injury, finishing Week 6 with four catches (on seven targets) for 24 yards. Almost one week later, he's tending to a chest issue, meaning his status will be watched closely as the weekend draws closer.

headline: Waddle secured four of seven targets for 24 yards in the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks on Thursday.
story: Waddle exited the game briefly due to a shoulder injury, but he was still able to finish as the Broncos' reception and targets leader on the night. His yardage total, modest as it was, also qualified him for runner-up status in that category on a night when Bo Nix threw for only 107 yards and averaged 4.0 yards per attempt. Waddle's production has suffered collateral damage from Nix's constant short-area throwing thus far this season, as the veteran receiver is averaging a career-low 10.4 yards per reception and just 38.0 receiving yards per game heading into a Week 7 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday, Oct. 25.

headline: Waddle suffered a shoulder injury in the third quarter of Thursday's game against the Seahawks but was able to return, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post and Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com report.
story: Now that he's back after missing a handful of minutes of game action, Waddle will look to add to his two catches (on five targets) for 15 yards.

headline: Waddle corralled two of five targets for 19 yards and also had a nine-yard carry during Sunday's 23-17 road win against the Chargers.
story: Waddle has hit once (8-138-0 on 10 targets in Week 2 against the Jaguars) and otherwise hasn't done much (10-66-1 on 21 targets) in his other four appearances in his first campaign with the Broncos. It didn't help any of Denver's skill-position players that QB Bo Nix's 27 passes went for only 123 yards, and a quick turnaround to face the Seahawks defense Thursday isn't a recipe for Waddle or any of his teammates to turn around their fortunes to begin the 2026 season.

headline: Waddle secured five of six targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos' 24-14 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
story: Waddle recorded his first touchdown as a member of the Broncos at a critical juncture, as his 13-yard scoring grab with just over four minutes remaining helped Denver get to within three points at the time. Waddle finished second in receptions and tied for runner-up status in targets as well, and he's now seen a total of 23 passes from Bo Nix come his way in the last three contests. The Broncos' air attack and Waddle's chemistry with Nix remains a work in progress, but the veteran receiver takes a solid 16-185-1 line on 26 targets into a Week 5 divisional road matchup against the Chargers next Sunday.

headline: Waddle (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the 49ers.
story: Following the Broncos' Week 3 win over the Rams, Waddle was spotted with his walking boot on his right foot, but he wasn't inhibited by the injury during Week 4 prep. He was a full participant in practices Wednesday through Friday, clearing the way for him to head into the weekend without a designation. Waddle isn't expected to face any restrictions with his snaps Sunday.

headline: Waddle (leg) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
story: Though he was seen donning a walking boot following Sunday's win over the Rams, Waddle may have just been wearing the boot as a precaution. He was back on the field three days later and took every rep in practice, with head coach Sean Payton relaying afterward that Waddle is "doing fine." Waddle thus looks like he'll be ready to handle his usual allotment of snaps in Sunday's game at San Francisco.

headline: Waddle (leg) was on the field Wednesday for the start of the Broncos' practice session, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
story: Following Sunday's 30-26 win over the Rams, Waddle was spotted wearing a walking boot on his right foot. His presence on the field to begin Week 4 prep suggests he might have been wearing the boot as a precaution, but fantasy managers nonetheless will want to track Waddle's practice activity leading up to this weekend's game in San Francisco. Through his first three contests with the Broncos, Waddle has recorded 11 catches for 150 yards on 20 targets while carrying once for a 14-yard gain.

headline: Waddle is believed to be "fine" despite being seen wearing a walking boot on his right foot following Sunday's victory over the Rams, Sam Jane of The Denver Post reports.
story: The Broncos haven't indicated the specific nature of the issue, but it appears Waddle is not dealing with any sort of serious setback. The wideout's practice reps are likely to be limited early in the week, but so long as he sheds the boot quickly, he should be good to go for a Week 4 tilt against the 49ers.

headline: Coleman rushed 15 times for 26 yards and caught eight of 10 targets for 46 yards in Friday's 27-5 loss to the Steelers.
story: Coleman easily led Denver's backfield with 23 touches while Cody Shrader had seven carries and Tyler Badie had one in the latter's return from an IR stint due to a thumb injury. J.K. Dobbins will be eligible to return from a team-imposed one-game suspension in Week 13 against the Dolphins, while RJ Harvey (knee) could come off IR by then as well, but Coleman has established himself as the top option in Denver's crowded backfield. Over the past four games, Coleman has turned 67 carries and 20 catches into 393 yards from scrimmage and five touchdowns.

headline: Coleman reeled off 111 yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries and hauled in four of five targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 38-24 win against the Raiders.
story: Since returning from an IR stint due to a sprained ankle in Week 7, Coleman has increased his touch count in four consecutive contests, taking a stranglehold on the Broncos backfield in the process. As evidence, his 25 touches easily outpaced fellow RB J.K. Dobbins' one, which went for no yards. Coleman, a rookie fourth-round pick, also cracked the 100-yard mark on the ground for the first time in his career. With RJ Harvey (ankle) on injured reserve for at least one more game, Coleman again is set to act as a workhorse in Friday's road matchup with the Steelers.

headline: Coleman carried the ball 17 times for 57 yards and a touchdown and caught all four of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 26-21 win over the Panthers.
story: The rookie has seized control of the lead-back role for the Broncos, with his 21 touches dwarfing J.K. Dobbins' five, and Coleman's nine-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter put his team in the lead for good. Coleman has piled up 261 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns over the last three games, and there's no reason to think his role will shrink on the other side of a Week 10 bye.

headline: Coleman received the first rep with the starters during warmups before Sunday's game against the Panthers, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
story: Coleman has not started in any of the four appearances he has made in his rookie season, but he led Broncos running backs in both snaps and touches each of the last two weeks, and it appears he could get the start over J.K. Dobbins on Sunday. Both players should be involved one way or another, and with RJ Harvey (knee) on injured reserve, Cody Schrader will be the only other Broncos running back available for Week 9.

headline: Coleman carried the ball 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown and caught four of five targets for 63 yards in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City.
story: With RJ Harvey (knee) on the shelf, Coleman saw a season-high 15 touches compared to J.K. Dobbins' seven, and the rookie was instrumental in the Broncos' fourth-quarter comeback. After a Harrison Butker missed field goal gave Denver great field position, Coleman was a one-man show on a two-play drive, taking a short pass from Bo Nix and turning it into a 51-yard gain before punching in a five-yard TD on the other side of the two-minute warning. Dobbins will still mix in on early downs, but Coleman may have just seized control of the backfield for the Broncos. He'll look to solidify his spot in Week 9 against a Panthers defense that's among the worst in the league against the run.

headline: Coleman said Friday that he'll be ready for a larger role if that's what the team needs in the absence of RJ Harvey, who has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Kansas City due to a knee injury, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
story: Coleman already appeared to make his move last week during a 30-16 win over Arizona, playing 50 percent of snaps on offense while leading the Broncos in carries (nine) and rushing yards (54). Meanwhile, Harvey (25 percent snap share, five touches) and J.K. Dobbins (21 percent snap share, six touches) both scored touchdowns despite losing a lot of playing time to Coleman in the rookie's first game back from injured reserve. There's no assurance Coleman's role will continue to grow, but Harvey's upcoming absence -- be it for one game or longer -- does give Coleman a better chance to consolidate rushing and receiving work in Denver's backfield.

headline: Coleman (ankle) rushed nine times for 54 yards and caught both of his targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals.
story: Coleman led the team in carries in his return from injured reserve and finished second behind Bo Nix (73) in rushing yards. J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey combined for just 29 rushing yards on nine rushing attempts, though Dobbins had a rushing touchdown and Harvey had a receiving touchdown. Coleman was notably the team's running back of choice as the Broncos ran out the clock in the fourth quarter, and head coach Sean Payton said after the game that the team has "got to get (Coleman) more touches," per Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site. Denver will likely continue to utilize all three running backs in Week 8 against the Chiefs, but this was an encouraging performance for Coleman in the rookie fourth-round pick's first action since Week 2.

headline: Coleman (ankle) is listed as active Sunday at Arizona, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
story: The Broncos placed Coleman on injured reserve just before Week 3 due to a sprained ankle, and with four absences under his belt after Week 6, the team designated him for return Wednesday. He then logged three consecutive full practices this week before being tagged as questionable Friday and being activated from IR on Saturday. Now that Coleman is in the clear to play in Week 7, his role may be muted with both J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey healthy at the moment.

headline: The Broncos activated Coleman (ankle) from injured reserve Saturday but continue to list him as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
story: Though he'll still carry a designation into Sunday, Coleman's reinstatement from IR indicates that he's on track to play for the first time since Week 2. With Tyler Badie (thumb) on injured reserve, Coleman will likely in as the No. 3 back behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. Though Harvey remains the Broncos' clear favored option on passing downs, if Dobbins goes down with an injury at any point, Coleman might be the favorite to lead Denver in carries.

headline: Coleman (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Arizona.
story: A full practice participant all week, Coleman appears ready to return just as Tyler Badie (thumb) is set to miss at least one game. If Coleman is activated from injured reserve before Sunday, his role could include some of the snaps in clear passing situations. J.K. Dobbins remains the favorite to start and lead the team in carries, but his status as the lead runner may be on thin ice, as he's averaging just 3.3 yards per carry.

headline: Coleman (ankle) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Coleman has been full each of the first two days of the practice week but remains on injured reserve. He's eligible to be activated ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals. In an offense looking for a jolt, Coleman could immediately have a significant role out of the backfield when he returns. The rookie running back should be rostered in all fantasy formats.

headline: Coleman (ankle) was at practice for a second straight day Thursday, Zac Stevens of DNVR Sports reports.
story: Coleman avoided any setbacks at Wednesday's practice, during which he was a full participant. The rookie fourth-round pick has a good chance of being activated from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals, though his standing in a Broncos backfield that also includes J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie (thumb) is murky.

headline: Coleman (ankle) was a full participant at Wednesday's practice.
story: Coleman's full participation Wednesday after he was designated to return from injured reserve is an encouraging sign regarding his health ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals, though the rookie running back will still need to be added back to the active roster with a subsequent transaction in order to suit up Sunday. Barring any setbacks, Coleman appears poised to rejoin a crowded Broncos backfield that also includes J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey and Tyler Badie (thumb).

headline: Coleman (ankle) was on the field for practice Wednesday after being designated for return from injured reserve, Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette reports.
story: The transaction opens up a 21-day window wherein the Broncos can evaluate Coleman for a return from the 53-man roster. Though Coleman is eligible to play as soon as Sunday against the Cardinals, the rookie running back may need more than a week of practice time before the Broncos are ready to bring him back from IR. Prior to being deactivated due to an ankle sprain, Coleman logged 10 carries for 39 yards and a touchdown to go with three catches for 19 yards on three targets through Denver's first two games.

headline: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive for Friday's game against the Steelers but will work as Denver's emergency third QB.
story: Ehlinger won't get into any Black Friday action unless both Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham have to exit due to injury, illness or ejection in Denver's Week 12 tilt against the Steelers.

headline: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Broncos' emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday.
story: As the emergency QB3, Ehlinger is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Carolina but is listed as the team's emergency quarterback, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
story: Ehlinger is officially inactive Sunday, though he will be available if Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive but will be the third emergency quarterback against the Chiefs on Sunday, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
story: As the emergency QB3, Ehlinger is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
story: Ehlinger will only be available if quarterbacks Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham must exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against Seattle, though he is listed as the emergency quarterback, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
story: While Ehlinger is inactive for this contest, he will be available if Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Ehlinger (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback in Sunday's game against the Chargers, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
story: Ehlinger continues to fulfill the role of an additional depth option behind Bo Nix and Jarrett Stidham. Ehlinger will only enter the game if both Nix and Stidham are forced out of the contest.

headline: Badie (thumb) is active Friday against the Steelers.
story: Badie was activated from injured reserve Thursday and will make his return Friday, likely working in a change-of-pace role behind Jonah Coleman while J.K. Dobbins is suspended. Cody Schrader also is on the roster at running back, while RJ Harvey (knee) could be activated from IR himself as soon as Week 13 against the Dolphins.

headline: The Broncos activated Badie (thumb) from injured reserve Thursday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
story: Badie is still listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Steelers, but his activation from IR indicates that the Broncos are confident that the fifth-year running back will be available to play against Denver. In the event that he's cleared to play, Badie would be in line to operate as the Broncos' RB2 behind rookie Jonah Coleman because of the absence of J.K. Dobbins, who was suspended by Denver on Tuesday for one game due to conduct detrimental to the team.

headline: Badie (thumb) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against the Steelers.
story: Since being designated for return from injured reserve Tuesday, Badie has been listed as a 'full' participant on each of his team's three practice reports ahead of Week 12. With RJ Harvey (knee) not yet ready to return from IR and J.K. Dobbins set to serve a team-imposed suspension this week, Badie is in a position to serve in a backup role behind ascending rookie Jonah Coleman, provided he's activated from IR by Friday afternoon. Also potentially in the mix on that front is practice-squad member Cody Schrader.

headline: The Broncos designated Badie (thumb) for return from injured reserve Tuesday, Susanna Weir of the team's official site reports.
story: Badie was back on the field for Tuesday's walkthrough practice, with Denver estimating him as a full participant, per Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site. Before fracturing his thumb in Week 6, Badie had handled a light role out of the backfield over five appearances, carrying the ball just six times for 22 yards to go with six catches for 67 yards. However, with RJ Harvey (knee) not yet ready to return from IR and with J.K. Dobbins (personal) serving a team-imposed suspension in Week 12, Badie could find himself as the top backup to rookie Jonah Coleman if he gets activated from IR ahead of Friday's game at Pittsburgh.

headline: The Broncos placed Badie (thumb) on injured reserve Saturday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
story: Per Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette, Badie broke his thumb during the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks in Week 6. Badie is required to miss at least four games, and the earliest he can return is Week 12 against the Steelers on Friday, Nov. 27. Jonah Coleman (ankle) was activated from injured reserve in a corresponding move, and if he's cleared to play Sunday, then he would slot in as the RB3 behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.

headline: Badie (thumb) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Badie injured his thumb during the Broncos' Week 6 win over the Seahawks, and the injury prevented him from practicing during Week 7 prep. The Broncos could promote Cody Schrader from the practice squad to the active roster to give the team extra backfield depth due to the absence of Badie, whose next chance to play is Week 8 against the Chiefs on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Badie (thumb) did not participate at practice Thursday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
story: Badie was knocked out of the Broncos' contest versus the Seahawks in Week 6 early by a thumb injury, and now his status for Week 7 is in jeopardy. Unless he's able to return to practice Friday, odds are not great he'll be able to play Sunday at Arizona.

headline: Badie (thumb) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette reports.
story: Badie sustained a thumb injury during the first half of the Broncos' Week 6 win over the Seahawks this past Thursday and did not return to the contest. He's opened the week with a DNP, and he'll have two more chances to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's road game against the Cardinals.

headline: Badie (thumb) won't return to Thursday's game against Seattle, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports. He finished with one carry for six yards.
story: Badie suffered a thumb injury in the first half and was considered questionable to return. Now that he has been ruled out for the remainder of Thursday's contest, RJ Harvey and J.K. Dobbins should each get a few more touches.

headline: Badie (thumb) is questionable to return to Thursday's game against Seattle, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
story: Badie suffered a thumb injury in the first half. He has just one carry for six yards in this contest, so his absence could mean a few additional snaps for J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey.

headline: Badie carried twice for seven yards, caught both of his targets for 32 yards, ran in a two-point conversion and returned one kickoff for 21 yards in a loss to San Francisco in Week 4.
story: Badie chipped in for the Broncos in multiple facets. The highlights of his performance were a 25-yard catch-and-run play in the first quarter and a two-point conversion on a run up the middle in the fourth quarter. Badie doesn't have much fantasy value given the low volume of touches he gets on a weekly basis, so it would likely take injuries ahead of him on the RB depth chart for Badie to become an intriguing waiver-wire addition.

headline: Rapp (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Steelers, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
story: Rapp was limited in each of the first two practices of Week 12 prep due to a quad injury that he may have picked up during the Broncos' 38-24 win over the Raiders on Sunday, when he logged two tackles (one solo). He will not travel with the team to Pittsburgh, so his next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. JL Skinner, Devon Key and Jahdae Barron are all candidates to see a bump in defensive snaps in Rapp's absence.

headline: The Broncos signed Rapp from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
story: Rapp was cut from the Broncos' active roster in early November before opting to stick around as a member of the team's practice squad. His elevation gives Denver more depth in the secondary in the event that Brandon Jones (hamstring) cannot play against the Raiders on Sunday.

headline: The Broncos signed Rapp off the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
story: The addition of Rapp gives the Broncos more depth in the secondary, and he could see some work on defense against the Chiefs on Sunday due to the absence of Talanoa Hufanga (ankle). Rapp played in both Weeks 6 and 7 and logged eight tackles (two solo) over those two appearances.

headline: Humphrey (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Las Vegas.
story: Humphrey will be a healthy scratch for a second consecutive game. His next chance to play is Week 12 against the Steelers on Black Friday, although Humphrey is unlikely to see the field unless a wide receiver ahead of him on the depth chart is not available.

headline: Humphrey (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game versus the Panthers, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
story: Humphrey has appeared in Denver's last four regular-season contests. However, he will be a healthy scratch for the meeting with Carolina, meaning his next opportunity to play will come in Week 11 against the Raiders, following the Broncos' bye.

headline: The Broncos signed Humphrey off the practice squad to the active roster Friday.
story: It'll be Humphrey's third stint on the Broncos' 53-man roster this season, and it comes after the team placed Pat Bryant (ankle) on injured reserve. Humphrey's lone appearance in the regular season was in Week 2 against the Jaguars, when he failed to haul in his lone target while playing only three offensive snaps. He'll operate in a depth role at wide receiver behind Jaylen Waddle, Courtland Sutton, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims.

headline: Humphrey signed a practice-squad contract with the Broncos on Saturday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
story: Humphrey was released by Denver on Friday but quickly inked a deal to remain in the organization. However, Gabriel notes that the Broncos aren't elevating anyone for Sunday's matchup against San Francisco, so Humphrey won't be active while he resides on the practice squad. The veteran wideout has logged just three offensive snaps so far this season and didn't catch his only target.

headline: Humphrey was released by the Broncos on Friday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
story: Fullback Adam Prentice was signed to the 53-man roster from the practice squad, so Humphrey was released in a corresponding move. However, assuming Humphrey wants to remain with the Broncos, there's a good chance the team will bring him back, even if it means he'll work as a member of the practice squad.

headline: Bentley (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the 49ers.
story: The rookie seventh-rounder has yet to suit up for a regular-season game. His next chance to do so is Week 5 against the Chargers on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: The Broncos placed Jones (hamstring) on injured reserve Thursday.
story: Jones had previously been ruled out for Friday's matchup versus the Steelers but will now be forced to miss at least four games before he's eligible to return. In his absence, Tyler Onyedim should be in line for increased playing time.

headline: Jones (hamstring) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Steelers, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
story: Jones was held out of the first two practices of Week 12 prep due to a hamstring injury that he may have picked up in Denver's 38-24 win over Las Vegas on Sunday. Tyler Onyedim and Jordan Jackson are in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in the absence of Jones, whose next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Jones (hamstring) didn't participate in Denver's walkthrough Tuesday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
story: Jones is dealing with a hamstring injury, putting his status for Friday's matchup versus the Steelers up in the air. The rookie third-round pick has compiled eight tackles (two solo), including 1.0 sacks, across nine games, and Tyler Onyedim would be in line for increased playing time if Jones ends up being unable to play.

headline: The Broncos signed Schrader off the practice squad to the active roster Thursday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
story: Schrader reached the maximum three games of elevation from the practice squad, but now that he's on the active roster, the Missouri product is eligible to suit up for the Broncos moving forward. He's expected to contribute as a kickoff returner, and Schrader could also settle in as the No. 2 or 3 running back behind starter Jonah Coleman in Friday's game against the Steelers with J.K. Dobbins serving a one-game suspension.

headline: Schrader reverted to the Broncos' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
story: Schrader was elevated to the active roster prior to Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders. The running back registered a three-yard rush while playing two snaps on offense and also added three kick returns for 71 yards over five snaps with the special-teams unit in the contest. Schrader has now been elevated three times, and as a result, Denver will have to officially sign him to the active roster in order for him to appear in another contest with the team this year.

headline: The Broncos elevated Schrader from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday, Susanna Weir of the team's official site reports.
story: Schrader's elevation is his third of the season, so he'll need to be signed to Denver's active roster in order to see game action for the team beyond Sunday. In his previous two appearances, the third-year pro played a total of two offensive snaps and nine snaps on special teams without recording any carries or targets. Schrader isn't likely to be much of a factor on offense Sunday against Las Vegas, as Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins should continue to lead the Broncos' backfield. However, Schrader could contribute as a kick returner -- he's tallied 68 yards on three kickoff returns this season.

headline: Schrader reverted to Denver's practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction reports.
story: Schrader didn't see any playing time on offense during Denver's win over the Panthers but did play four snaps on special teams and returned one kickoff for 18 yards. This was the second consecutive week the 27-year-old was elevated, and the team will be able to do so one more time this season before having to sign him to the active roster.

headline: The Broncos elevated Schrader from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's matchup in Carolina, Aric DiLalla of the team's official site reports.
story: Schrader has been elevated for the second straight week after making his Broncos debut last Sunday against Kansas City. He logged just two offensive snaps and didn't get a touch or target in that game, but he he did rack up 50 yards on two kick returns. Schrader figures to fill a similar role against the Panthers as the No. 3 RB behind Jonah Coleman and J.K. Dobbins.

headline: The Broncos elevated Schrader from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
story: The Broncos needed more depth in the backfield after placing RJ Harvey (knee) on injured reserve Saturday. It's the first time Schrader has been promoted to the active roster this season, and he'll operate as the Broncos' RB3 behind J.K. Dobbins and rookie Jonah Coleman for Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Schrader has appeared in two regular-season games -- both with the Rams -- since entering the league as an undrafted free agent in May of 2024.

headline: Lohner (foot) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Steelers.
story: Lohner was a full participant in all three practice sessions during Week 12 prep. However, the second-year pro is not quite ready to be activated from injured reserve, so his next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Dec. 6. Lohner is in the final stages of his recovery from a procedure on his foot in June.

headline: Lohner (foot) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
story: The Broncos opened Lohner's 21-day practice window Wednesday. The tight end is not quite ready to make his season debut, as he is still tending to his recovery from a foot injury he sustained in the offseason. Lohner was a full participant in all three Week 11 prep sessions, meaning his odds of returning in Week 12 are quite good if he can continue to log full sessions.

headline: The Broncos opened Lohner's (lower body) 21-day practice window Wednesday, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
story: Lohner opened the season on injured reserve after undergoing a procedure on his lower body in June. It appears the 25-year-old could make his return soon, as the Broncos have 21 days to officially activate him from IR before he becomes ineligible to return in 2026.

headline: The Broncos placed Dobbins on the reserve/suspended list Wednesday, Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com reports.
story: Head coach Sean Payton had previously announced Tuesday that Dobbins would be suspended for Friday's game against the Steelers due to conduct detrimental to the team, but it wasn't immediately clear whether or not the running back would count toward the 53-man roster. As a result of Wednesday's transaction, the Broncos will now have an open roster spot to use for Week 12, and Tyler Badie (thumb) could be activated from injured reserve to help fill the void in the backfield. Dobbins' suspension came after he played just one snap in the Broncos' 38-24 win over the Raiders on Sunday, when rookie Jonah Coleman took on a bell-cow role and handled 28 touches.

headline: Broncos head coach Sean Payton announced Tuesday that Dobbins has been suspended one game for conduct detrimental to the team, Chris Tomasson of The Denver Gazette reports.
story: Payton didn't go into details regarding what contributed to the Broncos' decision to suspend Dobbins, but the ban comes after the veteran running back played a season-low one snap in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders. Dobbins wasn't present for Wednesday's practice, and Payton confirmed that the 27-year-old will remain away from the team throughout Week 12 prep, per Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com. With Dobbins out of the picture for Friday's matchup with the Steelers, rookie Jonah Coleman should be in store for another hefty workload out of the backfield after breaking out for 129 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns on 28 touches in Week 11. Tyler Badie (thumb) was designated for return from injured reserve Tuesday and could be activated to serve as Coleman's top backup.

headline: Dobbins logged just one snap in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Raiders, though head coach Sean Payton said Monday that Dobbins "is going to be super important" moving forward, Will Petersen of 104.3 The Fan reports.
story: Dobbins' opportunities have been dwindling since Week 7 against Arizona, when he dropped to 14 offensive snaps after tallying 31 the week prior. That contest against the Cardinals was when rookie Jonah Coleman returned from a four-game absence, and Coleman has since forced his way into Denver's lead-RB role with blossoming production that has included five rushing TDs over his past three games. Coleman got nearly every running-back snap for Denver on Sunday, with practice-squad elevation Cody Schrader logging just two snaps and Dobbins one. Despite Payton's proclamation that Dobbins still has a "super important" role with the team, there's little reason to expect him to be a reliable fantasy asset as long as Coleman is healthy.

headline: Dobbins rushed once for no gain during Sunday's 38-24 win over Las Vegas.
story: Dobbins finished with fewer than 10 carries for the fourth straight game, and his lone rush came in the first quarter of the team's Week 11 victory. Rookie Jonah Coleman (24-111-3) has officially taken full command of Denver's backfield, and Dobbins figures to have to compete with RJ Harvey (knee) for the No. 2 spot behind Coleman with Harvey returning from injured reserve as soon as Week 12 against the Steelers.

headline: Dobbins rushed four times for 18 yards and caught his only target for four yards during Sunday's 26-21 win over Carolina.
story: Dobbins saw 13 fewer carries than rookie running back Jonah Coleman (17-57-1) in the game. The four rushes were a season low for Dobbins, and he figures to continue to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield moving forward.

headline: Dobbins carried the ball seven times for 13 yards in Sunday's 28-24 win over Kansas City.
story: While the veteran RB got the start, by the end of the game Dobbins had fully given way to rookie Jonah Coleman, who wound up delivering 104 scrimmage yards on 15 touches and scored the game-winning touchdown. With RJ Harvey (knee) on IR, Dobbins will still have a role in the Denver backfield, but Coleman made a compelling case Sunday to become the team's new No. 1 back. Dobbins should at least be more productive in Week 9, even on limited volume, against a Panthers defense that's among the worst in the league against the run.

headline: Dobbins and Jonah Coleman will lead the Broncos' backfield against the Chiefs on Sunday due to the absence of RJ Harvey (knee), Eric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
story: Harvey popped up on Thursday's injury report due to a knee injury and was unable to practice Friday, which resulted in him being ruled out for Sunday's AFC West tilt. Dobbins found the end zone in Week 7 against the Cardinals but was less efficient with his carries than Coleman, although the duo could have a fairly even split in backfield duties in Harvey's absence. Through seven regular-season games. Dobbins has turned 87 carries into 293 yards (3.4 YPC) and three touchdowns while adding eight catches on nine targets for 27 yards.

headline: Dobbins rushed six times for 23 yards and a touchdown and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals.
story: Dobbins extended his touchdown streak to three games with a one-yard rushing score to end the third quarter, but he was far less efficient on the ground than Jonah Coleman, who rushed nine times for 54 yards in his return from an ankle injury, averaging 6.0 YPC to Dobbins' 3.8. Coleman and RJ Harvey each had two catches, with Harvey breaking free for a 52-yard touchdown on one of those receptions, while Dobbins hasn't exceeded 12 receiving yards in a game this season. With Coleman likely to claim a chunk of the rushing opportunities moving forward, Dobbins profiles as a touchdown-dependent Week 8 fantasy option against the Chiefs.

headline: Dobbins rushed 17 times for 41 yards and a touchdown and brought in all three targets for five yards during the Broncos' 17-14 overtime win over the Seahawks on Thursday.
story: Dobbins was in the customary position of leading the Broncos' ground attack in rush attempts and rushing yards, but he averaged only 2.4 yards per carry against a stingy Seahawks front. Nevertheless, the veteran back made a trip to the end zone for the second consecutive game, going in from four yards out early in the second quarter. After averaging 4.5 yards per carry in a Week 1 loss to the Chiefs, Dobbins has hit a wall in terms of efficiency, but he'll remain the top option in the ground attack for a favorable Week 7 road matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday, Oct. 25.

headline: Dobbins recorded 18 carries for 68 yards and one touchdown and gathered in both targets for six yards during Sunday's 23-17 win at the Chargers.
story: Dobbins easily led both teams in touches with 20, which marked a season high, and he also reached the end zone for the first time in the current campaign. Meanwhile, fellow RB RJ Harvey was contained to three rushes for seven yards, marking his lowest touch count of 2026. Dobbins has received a more consistent workload among the two players with 13.8 touches per game (as opposed to 8.8 per contest for Harvey), making him the more appealing of the two backfield options in Denver.

headline: Dobbins rushed 11 times for 40 yards and brought in both targets for 12 yards in the Broncos' 24-14 loss to the 49ers on Sunday.
story: Dobbins functioned in his usual lead-back role, but the Broncos eventually had to focus more on the pass in the fourth quarter after falling behind by a 17-6 margin. The veteran back has logged double-digit carries in three straight games, yet he's topped out at 49 rushing yards in terms of a single-game high thus far this season. Dobbins is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry and has a scant three receptions for 16 yards over the first four games, which doesn't give him much momentum as he heads into a Week 5 road divisional matchup against the Chargers.

headline: Jones (hamstring) was listed as a full participant at the Broncos' walkthrough practice Tuesday, Aric DiLalla of the team's official practice reports.
story: Jones has missed the team's last two games while nursing a hamstring injury, but he now appears to be all set to return to action Friday against the Steelers. The 28-year-old will have a couple more chances to officially practice before potentially returning to his starting role at free safety in Week 12.

headline: Jones (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Jones will miss a second consecutive game due to a hamstring injury, which limited his practice participation during Week 11 prep. JL Skinner and Taylor Rapp are the top candidates to start alongside Talanoa Hufanga at safety in the absence of Jones, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Steelers on Black Friday.

headline: Jones (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
story: Jones strung together three limited practices Week 11 prep, and he has a chance to return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury that he picked up in Week 8 against the Chiefs. JL Skinner figures to be the top candidate to start alongside Talanoa Hufanga at safety if Jones is not cleared to play against Las Vegas.

headline: Jones (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Jones was unable to play in Week 9 against the Panthers due to a hamstring injury that he picked up against the Cowboys in Week 8. He's had extra time to recover thanks to the Week 10 bye, and he'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation ahead of Sunday's game against Las Vegas.

headline: Jones (hamstring) is officially listed as out for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: Jones was forced out of the Broncos' contest versus the Chiefs in Week 8 early by a hamstring injury, and he'll now have to sit out his first game of the season as he recovers. In his absence, Devon Key could get a start at safety in Week 9.

headline: Jones (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's contest against the Chiefs, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.
story: Jones entered Sunday's matchup with a questionable tag after suffering a hamstring injury at practice during the week. Although the safety was ultimately able to play, it's possible that he tweaked the injury during the game, and he will now have to shift his sights to Week 9. In his absence, Taylor Rapp and Devon Key will operate as Denver's two primary safeties against Kansas City.

headline: Jones (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site reports.
story: Jones popped up on Thursday's injury report due to a hamstring issue, but he's been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday. He has 52 tackles (31 solo), five pass defenses (including two interceptions) and one fumble recovery across seven regular-season games.

headline: Jones (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Jones may have tweaked his hamstring during Week 8 prep, seeing as he popped up on Thursday's injury report as a limited practice participant.
