headline: Gibbs rushed 15 times for 46 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of seven targets for 31 yards in the Lions' 32-26 loss to the Panthers on Sunday night.
story: Gibbs' season-low rushing yardage total was particularly surprising considering no team had allowed more rushing yards to running backs than Carolina coming into Week 4. Gibbs also wasn't able to make up for the lack of rushing production with his work as a pass catcher, but he at least added his fifth rushing touchdown of the season on a one-yard run late in the first half. Gibbs and the Lions will look to bounce back in a Week 5 road matchup against the Cardinals next Sunday.

headline: Ratledge (ankle/knee) returned to Thursday's contest against the Bears, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
story: Ratledge had his lower leg rolled up on in the first quarter but was able to rejoin the lineup as the Lions' right guard one possession later.

headline: Ratledge is questionable to return to Thursday's Thanksgiving Day matchup against Chicago due to ankle and knee injuries.
story: Ratledge was hurt in the first half and isn't certain to return. Miles Frazier has taken over at right guard for the Lions.

headline: Rodriguez (ankle) returned to Thursday's game versus the Bears, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
story: Rodriguez's left ankle was rolled up on in the third quarter, but after a spell on the sideline, he got back on the field in the fourth. He'll look to build upon the four tackles and fumble recovery that he recorded before his departure.

headline: Rodriguez suffered an ankle injury during Thursday's game against the Bears.
story: Rodriguez has his ankle rolled up on in the third quarter and immediately made his way to the sideline tent before the Lions deemed him questionable to return. He had four tackles and a fumble recovery before his exit.

headline: Wonnum (back) is inactive for Thursday's Week 12 battle against the Bears.
story: Wonnum was able to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday, but that didn't end up being enough for him to suit up Thursday. He leads the Lions with 7.0 sacks this season, so the veteran defensive end's absence is a big deal for Detroit. Tyler Lacy, Ahmed Hassanein, Eric O'Neill and Anthony Lucas could all be involved in trying to fill the void left by Wonnum's absence Thursday.

headline: Wonnum (back) is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against the Bears.
story: Wonnum missed two Week 12 prep sessions before participating in the Lions' practice session Wednesday as a limited participant. The defensive end likely picked up his back injury in the team's Week 11 win over the Buccaneers. If Wonnum cannot suit up for Thursday's game, Eric O'Neill and Tyler Lacy will likely see more snaps at defensive end opposite Derrick Moore in the game.

headline: Wonnum (back) did not participate at the Lions' walkthrough practice Monday.
story: Wonnum registered five solo tackles, including 1.0 sacks, while also adding a pass defensed and a forced fumble during Sunday's 31-21 win over the Buccaneers. The defensive lineman may have picked up a back injury during the contest, and he will have two more chances to return to practice prior to Thursday's matchup with the Bears.

headline: Wonnum (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Patriots in Munich, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
story: Wonnum entered the league's concussion protocol during the Lions' Week 8 win over the Vikings. He was held out of Detroit's Week 9 win over Miami, but Wonnum has cleared protocol after passing an evaluation by an independent neurologist. His return bolsters the Lions' rotational depth on the defensive line alongside Aidan Hutchinson, Tyler Lacy and Derrick Moore.

headline: Wonnum (concussion) was a full participant in practice Thursday.
story: Wonnum posted back-to-back full practices Wednesday and Thursday while working through a concussion. It's unclear whether he can play in Sunday's matchup against New England, but he appears to be moving in the right direction. The 29-year-old has 14 tackles (eight solo), including 5.0 sacks, and one pass deflection across seven regular-season games.

headline: Wonnum (concussion) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Wonnum was unable to clear the NFL's five-step concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's contest. The defensive end did not practice at all during Week 9 prep and remains sidelined with the head injury.

headline: Wonnum (concussion) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Vikings.
story: Wonnum and Brian Branch collided with each other in the second quarter, and both players are now in the league's concussion protocol. Derrick Moore, Trevor Nowaske and Eric O'Neill are in line for more defensive snaps in Wonnum's absence.

headline: Clark (hamstring) is inactive for Thursday's clash against Chicago.
story: Clark dealt with a hamstring issue during Week 12 prep and is going to miss his first game of the campaign as a result. He's been a starter at safety for the Lions all season and played every defensive snap in three of Detroit's past four games. Kerby Joseph and Brian Branch will start at safety Thursday, with Andre Cisco working in reserve.

headline: Clark (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against the Bears.
story: Clark ended Week 12 prep with a limited practice after starting the week's walkthrough as a DNP. The free safety played 100 percent of the Lions' defensive snaps in Week 11 despite Kerby Joseph's return to the field, meaning an inactive status for Thursday's contest against the Bears would harm the Lions' starting secondary in a significant way.

headline: Clark (hamstring) was a limited participant in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.
story: Clark was held out of Monday's walkthrough session while tending to a hamstring injury, but he was back on the field Tuesday in a limited fashion. His participation in Wednesday's practice will shed light on his chances of playing against the Bears on Thanksgiving Day. Rookie fifth-rounder Keith Abney, as well as Kerby Joseph and Christian Izien, would all be in line for more defensive snaps if Clark cannot play Thursday.

headline: Clark (hamstring) was considered to be a non-participant at the Lions' walkthrough practice Monday.
story: Clark was able to play every defensive snap during Sunday's 31-21 win over the Buccaneers, notching eight total tackles (two solo), including 1.0 sacks, and a pass defensed. The safety may have picked up a hamstring injury during the game, and he will have two more chances to return to practice before Thursday's matchup with the Bears.

headline: Clark registered five tackles (three solo) and one interception during the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins in Week 9.
story: Clark jumped in front of a Malik Willis (abdomen) deep pass intended for Caleb Douglas early in the third quarter, which the Lions offense converted into a 33-yard field goal by Jake Bates eight plays later. It was Clark's second interception of the season and first since Week 1 against the Saints. The veteran safety is up to 49 tackles (28 solo), including 1.0 sacks, three pass defenses and one forced fumble through eight regular-season games.

headline: Clark finished Sunday's 31-24 win over the Jets with seven tackles, including 1.0 sacks, and a forced fumble.
story: Clark continues to start at safety for Detroit with with Brian Branch (Achilles) and Kerby Joseph (knee) both on the PUP list. Clark logged just a 45 percent defensive snap share in Week 1, but he upped that to 86 percent in Week 2 before playing every one of the Lions' 61 defensive snaps in Week 3. The veteran defender came up with a huge play late in the contest, sacking Jets QB Geno Smith and causing him to fumble with less than a minute remaining and New York nearing the red zone while trailing by seven points. The sack was Clark's first since he played for the Jets in 2024.

headline: Rakestraw (shoulder) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday's game against the Bears.
story: Rakestraw did not participate in any Week 12 prep sessions due to the shoulder injury that kept him out of Sunday's game against the Buccaneers. The cornerback will now miss consecutive games, leaving Khalil Dorsey as the backup behind D.J. Reed and Rock Ya-Sin.

headline: Rakestraw (shoulder) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
story: A shoulder injury limited Rakestraw's practice reps during Week 11 prep. He was initially tagged as questionable, but after he went through pregame warmups, medical staff has determined that Rakestraw is not in good enough shape to suit up for Sunday's contest. With D.J. Reed (hip) also sidelined, Khalil Dorsey figures to start opposite Rock Ya-Sin at outside cornerback. Rakestraw's next opportunity to play is Thanksgiving Day against the Bears.

headline: Rakestraw (ankle) does not have a game designation for Sunday's Week 8 tilt versus the Vikings.
story: Rakestraw suffered an ankle injury late in this past Sunday's win over Green Bay. He was held to limited practice sessions Wednesday and Thursday but was able to upgrade to full participation Friday. As such, Rakestraw is good to go for Sunday's big battle against Minnesota.

headline: Rakestraw (ankle) is not believed to be dealing with a major injury after he was forced to exit Sunday's win over the Packers, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
story: Coach Dan Campbell said Rakestraw could practice this week, and he has a chance to a play Sunday against the undefeated Vikings. Rock Ya-Sin filled in at cornerback following Rakestraw's injury and would be in line for increased snaps on defense if the latter is unable to face Minnesota.

headline: Rakestraw exited Sunday's game against the Packers with an ankle injury and is questionable to return.
story: Prior to leaving in the second half, the cornerback recorded two tackles. Rock Ya-Sin and Khalil Dorsey would be in line for increased snaps at cornerback the rest of the way against Green Bay.

headline: The Lions placed Gill-Howard (knee) on injured reserve Wednesday.
story: Gill-Howard suffered a season-ending knee injury during the Lions' Week 11 win over the Buccaneers. The rookie sixth-rounder will finish his first NFL campaign with 11 tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, across 10 regular-season games.

headline: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said Tuesday that Gill-Howard needs season-ending knee surgery, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
story: Gill-Howard suffered a season-ending knee injury and will miss the rest of the year. The 24-year-old rookie recorded 11 tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks in 10 games.

headline: Branch logged six tackles (one solo) and two passes defensed in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: Branch played 98 percent of the Lions' defensive snaps in the contest. The strong safety has now had two passes defensed in consecutive weeks, totaling five in his five regular-season games in 2026. Sunday's game marked the first of 2026 that Branch and free safety Kirby Joseph played alongside each other, and they could certainly help shore up the back end of the defense down the stretch.

headline: Branch (hip) was a full participant in practice Thursday.
story: Branch upgraded his practice status to full participation after beginning the week limited. The 25-year-old has 14 tackles (seven solo) and one interception in three regular-season games.

headline: Branch (hip) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday.
story: Branch played all 57 of the Lions' defensive snaps in Week 9, and the fact that he was present for Wednesday's practice session suggests his injury is likely not overly severe. If he can upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday, there's a good chance he'll avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Branch (concussion) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: With consecutive full practices to close out Week 9 prep, Branch has officially cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol. The starting strong safety is all set to suit up for Sunday's game alongside free safety Chuck Clark.

headline: Branch (concussion) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
story: It's unclear if Branch remains in the concussion protocol, but his full participation puts him on track to play Sunday against the Dolphins after he was injured in the Week 8 win over Minnesota.

headline: Branch (concussion) was estimated as a limited participant on the Lions' official injury report Wednesday, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
story: Branch suffered a concussion during Sunday's game versus the Vikings, and now his status for Week 9 is in doubt. He'll need to clear the league's five-step concussion protocol before he'll be allowed to suit back up for game action, and his activity at practice Thursday and Friday could give some indication of any progress he makes ahead of Sunday's game at Miami.

headline: Branch (concussion) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Vikings.
story: Branch and D.J. Wonnum collided with each other in the second quarter, and both players have been diagnosed with concussions. Keith Abney should see more defensive snaps in Branch's absence.

headline: Branch recorded four tackles (one solo) and an interception during Sunday's 20-17 win over Green Bay.
story: Branch was given the green light to play Sunday in what was his first game since he tore his Achilles in Week 14 of the 2025 season. He was on the field for 45 of the Lions' 67 defensive snaps (67.2 percent), and his return was highlighted by his interception off of Jordan Love early in the fourth quarter. Having Branch back in the fold significantly boosts the Lions' secondary, especially since the defense ranks dead last in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (291.8). Detroit will stay home for Week 8 to host Minnesota in another NFC North tilt.

headline: The Lions activated Branch (Achilles) from injured reserve Saturday.
story: Branch no longer holds any injury designation and appears all set to suit up for the Lions' game against the Packers on Sunday. The strong safety has finished recovering from the Achilles tear he sustained in early December of 2025, just in time for a divisional showdown that could be key in determining the final standings of the AFC North.

headline: Branch (Achilles) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Packers.
story: Branch was listed as a full practice participant on each of the Lions' three injury reports during Week 7 prep, and there's a chance that he's activated from the reserve/PUP list ahead of Sunday's NFC North tilt. He's nearing clearance to return after spending the last 10 months rehabbing from a torn Achilles, and his presence would boost a Lions' defense that allows a league-worst 297.4 passing yards per game.

headline: The Lions listed Branch as a full participant on Wednesday's estimated practice report.
story: The Lions did not practice for their first session following the Week 6 bye, but it's a promising sign to see Branch listed as a full participant. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a torn Achilles that he suffered in December of 2025, and he could be activated from the Lions' reserve/PUP list ahead of Sunday's NFC North tilt against the Packers.

headline: Branch (Achilles) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Branch returned to practice Wednesday after the Lions opened up his 21-day practice window. The strong safety managed to log limited practice in all three Week 5 prep sessions but is not quite ready to return to the field. Christian Izien will continue to start at strong safety while Branch puts the finishing touches on his recovery.

headline: Branch (Achilles) had his 21-day practice window opened by the Lions on Sunday, Richard Silva of The Detroit News reports.
story: Branch was limited in Wednesday's practice, but it was an encouraging sign to see the fourth-year pro back on the field following a lengthy recovery from a torn Achilles that he sustained in early December of 2025. The Lions' secondary has been one of the worst in the league this season, and while Branch's return would be a significant upgrade to the unit, he'll likely need to log multiple full practices before being activated from the reserve/PUP list. While it's unlikely he'd play, Branch's first opportunity to make his 2026 debut is Sunday against the Cardinals.

headline: Head coach Dan Campbell said Friday that Branch (Achilles) is close to returning, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
story: "Close" is a relative term, so it's unclear how close Branch actually is, considering he remains on the reserve/PUP list and has yet to begin practicing. It sounds like that could change next week. The Lions have been relying on Roger McCreary at slot cornerback in Branch's absence.

headline: Ya-Sin logged 10 tackles (nine solo) in the Lions' 31-21 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: Ya-Sin played 59 defensive snaps in the contest and one snap on special teams. The cornerback played 91 percent of the team's defensive snaps, drawing the start due to the absence of Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder). Ya-Sin could see an elevated role again in Week 12 on Thursday against the Bears if Rakestraw remains sidelined.

headline: Ya-Sin (hamstring) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Packers.
story: The veteran defensive back has been cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury, with Ya-Sin having the benefit of extra rest courtesy of the Week 6 bye. His return gives the Lions depth in the secondary and another contributor on special teams.

headline: Ya-Sin (hamstring) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Ya-Sin has not practiced since he sustained a hamstring injury during the Lions' Week 4 loss to the Panthers. In the cornerback's absence, Khalil Dorsey or Keith Abney is set to be the primary backup at outside cornerback behind starters D.J. Reed and Ennis Rakestraw.

headline: Ya-Sin (hamstring) is expected to be sidelined in Week 5 at Arizona, Richard Silva of The Detroit News reports.
story: Ya-Sin hurt his hamstring during Sunday night's contest at Carolina, and it looks like he is likely going to have to miss at least one game as he recovers. If Ya-Sin does log at least one absence, Roger McCreary figures to see an uptick in snaps in the secondary.

headline: Ya-Sin (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday night's contest against the Panthers.
story: Ya-Sin suffered a hamstring injury in the second half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end. The Lions are having a fair amount of trouble stopping the Panthers' passing attack, and Detroit will now be even thinner in the secondary for the stretch run of the contest.

headline: Ya-Sin (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday night's contest against the Panthers.
story: Ya-Sin is dealing with a hamstring injury, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. In his absence, D.J. Reed and Ennis Rakestraw will operate as the primary options at cornerback for Detroit.

headline: Reed (hip) was considered to be a full participant at the Lions' walkthrough practice Monday.
story: Reed appears to be on track to return to action Thursday against the Bears after missing three straight games with a hip injury. The cornerback will have two more chances to officially practice ahead of Week 12.

headline: Reed (hip) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
story: Reed expressed pessimism Wednesday that he would be cleared to return for Week 11 due to a hip injury, and the veteran defensive back will, in fact, be sidelined for a third consecutive game. Khalil Dorsey will likely start opposite Rock Ya-Sin at outside cornerback in the absence of Reed, whose next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bears on Thanksgiving Day.

headline: Reed (hip) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
story: Reed was a limited participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep while tending to a hip injury, which has prevented him from playing in each of the Lions' last two games. Per Jeremy Reisman of PrideofDetroit.com on Wednesday, Reed did not express optimism that he would face Tampa Bay. Khalil Dorsey (ankle) and Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder) are both also listed as questionable, which leaves Rock Ya-Sin, Roger McCreary and Christian Izien as the only healthy cornerbacks on the Lions' 53-man roster heading into the weekend.

headline: Reed (hip) was a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice.
story: A hip injury has prevented Reed from playing in each of the Lions' last two games, and the veteran defensive back expressed pessimism Wednesday about his ability to suit up for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, per Jeremy Reisman of PrideofDetroit.com. If Reed doesn't play in Week 11, then Khalil Dorsey (ankle) would likely start opposite Rock Ya-Sin at outside cornerback.

headline: Reed (hip) did not travel to Munich with the Lions and is ruled out for Sunday's matchup against the Patriots.
story: Reed did not participate in practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a hip injury suffered late in Week 8. Rock Ya-Sin and Ennis Rakestraw could see extended playing time for the second straight week in Reed's stead. Reed has 42 tackles (29 solo) and seven pass deflections, including one interception, in seven regular-season games.

headline: Reed (hip) did not participate at practice Wednesday.
story: Reed was sidelined for Sunday's game at Miami because of a hip issue, and now his availability for Week 10 is in jeopardy. He'll likely have to get back on the practice field Thursday or Friday to have a realistic chance of playing Sunday versus the Patriots.

headline: Reed (hip) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Reed suffered a hip injury in the fourth quarter of the Lions' Week 8 win over the Vikings. The cornerback was unable to practice during Week 9 prep and will not suit up for Sunday's contest. Rock Ya-Sin is set to start opposite rookie Ennis Rakestraw against the Dolphins.

headline: Reed (hip) is not expected to practice Wednesday, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
story: Reed suffered a hip injury late in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Vikings and did not return to the contest. The cornerback's injury appears to be significant enough for Reed to be ruled out of practice a day ahead of time. It remains unclear whether or not the starting cornerback will participate in any practice sessions ahead of the team's Week 9 game against the Dolphins.

headline: Reed (hip) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Reed suffered a hip injury in the fourth quarter and is being checked by training staff to determine whether he can return. Khalil Dorsey and Rock Ya-Sin are candidates for more defensive snaps while Reed is out of the game.

headline: Reed (ribs) is active for Sunday night's matchup with the Panthers.
story: Reed will ultimately be able to give it a go after operating as a limited participant a practice throughout the week with a rib injury that he suffered in Week 3. The cornerback will likely be tasked with trying to hold Tetairoa McMillan in check during Sunday Night Football.

headline: Reed (ribs) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: Reed logged limited practice sessions throughout the Lions' Week 4 preparations. The cornerback's status for Sunday's contest remains uncertain as he works through the rib issue he suffered in the Week 3 win over the Jets. If Reed cannot suit up, Rock Ya-Sin will likely start at outside cornerback across from Ennis Rakestraw.

headline: Reed (ribs) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Reed presumably picked up the injury during the Lions' 31-24 win over the Jets in Week 3, when he played 62 of 66 defensive snaps (93.9 percent) and finished with eight tackles (five solo) and one pass defense. He'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation to full and avoid an injury designation for Sunday's road game against the Panthers.

headline: Dorsey (wrist) has re-entered Sunday's matchup against Tampa Bay, Justin Rogers of DetroitFootball.net reports.
story: Dorsey hurt his wrist early in Sunday's game and was initially deemed questionable to return. The veteran cornerback has since been able to re-enter the game, albeit with a club over the hand that he injured. Dorsey has been working in a rotational role at cornerback, logging a defensive snap share between 32 and 38 percent three straight weeks.

headline: Dorsey (wrist) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Tampa Bay.
story: Dorsey exited in the first half of Sunday's game. It's unclear if the injury is related to a wrist injury that landed him on injured reserve earlier in the season.

headline: Smack made both of his field-goal tries and his lone extra-point attempt Wednesday in a loss to the Rams.
story: Neither of Smack's field goals were chip shots; he nailed a 54-yarder late in the first quarter and a 48-yarder late in the second. The rookie entered Wednesday having gone just 15-for-21 on FG tries over his first 10 NFL games, so his accuracy Wednesday may have given him some needed job security. The most impressive aspect of Smack's rookie campaign has been his big leg. Despite his overall struggles, he's gone 4-for-5 on FG tries from 50-plus yards away.

headline: Smack went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made his only extra-point try during Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: Smack pushed a 53-yard field-goal try wide right in the first quarter before later converting a 40-yard attempt in the final seconds of the third quarter. The rookie has now gone 15-for-21 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-4 from 50-plus yards, while making 21 of 24 extra-point attempts over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Smack (calf) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Smack was limited in Wednesday's practice due to a calf injury. Head coach Matt LaFleur anticipated the kicker would practice without limitations Thursday, and that's exactly what happened, clearing the way for his availability in Week 10 against Minnesota. Smack is coming off a solid performance, making all three field-goal attempts while converting each of his four extra-point tries in the Packers' Week 9 victory over the Patriots.

headline: Head coach Matt LaFleur said he expects Smack (calf) to practice without limitations Thursday, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Per Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com, LaFleur added that he isn't concerned with Smack's mechanics being affected by the kicker's right calf injury based on Smack's performance at Wednesday's practice. If Smack returns to full participation Thursday after being limited Wednesday, that would put him in the clear to face the Vikings on Sunday.

headline: Smack (calf) was estimated as limited in Wednesday's jog-through practice.
story: It's a new injury for the Packers' rookie kicker, who went a perfect 7-for-7 on kicks in last Sunday's demolition of the Patriots. The team doesn't currently employ another kicker on the active roster or practice squad.

headline: Smack went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made all four of his PATs during Sunday's 45-27 win against the Patriots.
story: Smack put together one of the more impressive performances of his rookie campaign. The kicker converted a 41-yard field goal in the second quarter before later adding makes from 51 and 38 yards in the second half. Smack entered Week 9 having made just five of his last nine field-goal tries, so Sunday's performance was a much-needed one for the 23-year-old.

headline: Smack converted three of four extra-point tries and didn't attempt a field goal Thursday in a 27-19 win over Carolina.
story: Smack's evening began poorly, as he clanged the extra-point attempt off the left upright following Green Bay's first touchdown of the game midway through the first quarter. However, the rookie kicker recovered to make his other three PATs. Still, the missed kick may have put Smack on even thinner ice, and his struggles likely contributed to Green Bay's decision to punt on a fourth-down play from the Panthers' 37-yard line while up eight points late in the fourth period rather than letting him attempt a 54-yard field goal that would have essentially iced the game. On the season, Smack has made 11 of 16 FGAs and 16 of 19 extra points.

headline: Smack went 1-for-3 on field-goal tries and converted both of his PATs during Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Lions.
story: Smack continued his up-and-down rookie campaign in Week 7, and he started Sunday's contest by pushing a 26-yard field-goal attempt wide right on the Packers' first possession of the game. The kicker was able to convert a 43-yard try in the fourth quarter, but he then had 35-yard try partially blocked by D.J. Wonnum with 3:25 left in regulation. Smack has now gone 6-for-11 on field-goal attempts over the last five games, and it's unclear how long the Packers will stick with him moving forward if he can't get back on track.

headline: Smack made all three of his field-goal attempts and both of his extra-point tries during Green Bay's win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
story: Smack had a solid bounce-back performance after missing two field goals and an extra point during the Week 5 win over the Bears. The 23-year-old now has made 10 of his 13 field-goal attempts and 11 of his 13 extra-point tries across the first six games of his rookie campaign.

headline: Smack went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during the Packers' 31-7 win over the Bears on Sunday.
story: Smack missed field goals from 43 and 47 yards in the fourth quarter, which came after his extra-point try early in the third missed wide left. It was by far the worst performance of the rookie's young NFL career, but luckily for him, the Packers dominated enough offensively and defensively that his kicking miscues were a wash. Smack will have a prime opportunity to bounce back in Week 6 on Oct. 18 against the Cowboys, who give up the seventh-most points in the NFL this season (27.2).

headline: Smack made his only field-goal attempt and both of his PATs during Sunday's 17-14 win over Tampa Bay.
story: Smack had only one opportunity to kick a field goal in Week 4, but he made the most of it. The rookie nailed a 58-yard attempt as time expired in the first half, delivering the Packers a 10-7 lead at the break. Smack's field goal would prove to be the difference in a low-scoring battle. On the year, the kicker has gone 6-for-7 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-3 from 50-plus yards, over four contests so far.

headline: Moore returned three kickoffs for 48 yards and one punt for 11 yards Wednesday in a loss to the Rams.
story: Moore continued to serve as Green Bay's primary kick and punt returner, but he logged just one snap on offense. That limited usage as a receiver was even more concerning for his fantasy outlook given that star wideout Christian Watson couldn't play at all in the second half due to a concussion. Moore did notch 14 targets over his first five games, but since returning in Week 10 from a stint on IR, he's played just one offensive snap over two contests.

headline: Moore (ankle) is active for Wednesday's game against the Rams, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Moore aggravated an ankle injury against the Vikings in Week 10, but the fifth-year pro has been cleared to play Wednesday after going through pregame warmups. Moore has mostly operated on special teams as a returner this season and has not caught a catch since Week 5 against the Bears.

headline: Moore (ankle) is listed as questionable for Wednesday night's game against the Rams, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Moore was limited in all three practices ahead of Week 12 after re-injuring his ankle in Week 10 against the Vikings. The 26-year-old has had a smaller role on offense since Savion Williams returned from injury, but Moore still plays a key role in the kick return unit on special teams.

headline: Moore (ankle) remained limited in Monday's practice.
story: Moore re-injured his ankle after just three snaps on special teams in the Packers' Week 10 loss to the Vikings. He's been practicing ahead of Wednesday's game against the Rams, but it remains to be seen if Moore will be able to play. His role on offense has mostly evaporated with the return of Savion Williams behind Matthew Golden and Christian Watson.

headline: Moore (ankle) was a limited participant in Sunday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Moore tweaked his ankle during the Packers' 30-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 10. He's mostly operated as a returner on kickoffs and punts this season, so those return duties would fall to Savion Williams, Matthew Golden and Bo Melton (thigh) if Moore is unable to play against the Rams on Wednesday.

headline: Moore (ankle) participated in practice Saturday, Bill Huber of SI.com reports.
story: Moore made his return from injured reserve last Sunday against the Vikings but played just three special-teams snaps before aggravating his existing ankle injury. It's not believed to be a serious issue, and Moore has a chance to play Wednesday versus the Rams.

headline: Moore's ankle injury is not considered serious, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: The Packers' decision to rule Moore out with an ankle injury in the Week 10 loss to the Vikings was a precautionary move after the 26-year-old made his first appearance since returning from injured reserve. It's unclear if the fifth-year pro will be sidelined for any coming games, but Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will likely act as primary return options if Moore misses any time.

headline: Moore (ankle) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Vikings, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Moore suffered an ankle injury in the first quarter, and after being evaluated by medical staff, it's been determined that the fifth-year pro will not return to Sunday's contest. With Bo Melton (thigh) also done for the day, the Packers will turn to Savion Williams and Matthew Golden as return options on kickoffs and special teams. Moore is in jeopardy of missing the Packers' next contest, which takes place in Week 12 against the Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

headline: Moore (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Vikings.
story: Moore appeared to injure his ankle in the first quarter. He missed the Packers' four prior games due to an ankle issue, but it's unclear whether the injury occurred on the same leg. Bo Melton, Matthew Golden and Savion Williams are candidates to fill in as returners on kickoffs and special teams for as long as Moore is out of the game.

headline: Moore (ankle) is listed as active Sunday versus the Vikings, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Moore has spent the requisite four contests on injured reserve due to an ankle injury, and his activation from the list Saturday set him up for his first game action since Week 5. Prior to the stint on the sidelines, he had a bit role on offense (7-35-0 on 14 targets) while handling most of the return responsibilities. Expect Moore to serve behind fellow WRs Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Savion Williams in Week 10.

headline: The Packers activated Moore (ankle) from injured reserve Saturday, and he remains questionable for Sunday's matchup against Minnesota.
story: Moore was placed on injured reserve Oct. 17 and has missed the required four games. He was designated to return Wednesday and participated in a limited fashion in all three of Green Bay's practices this week. Moore has a chance to suit up Sunday now that he's been activated, and if he plays he'll likely feature in the return game while adding contributions as a depth wideout.

headline: Moore (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Moore has remained on IR since suffering an ankle injury in Week 5. The wide receiver logged limited practice sessions throughout Week 10 prep but likely will not be elevated for Sunday's contest, as the Packers are set to allocate any additional roster space to the running back position in Josh Jacobs' (finger) absence.

headline: Moore (IR, ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Moore has been working his way back from an ankle injury after last playing in the Week 5 meeting with the Bears. The wideout remains on injured reserve. While it's unclear if Moore will be ready to suit up Sunday versus the Vikings, it appears his return is imminent.

headline: The Packers designated Moore (ankle) to return from injured reserve Wednesday.
story: Moore was a limited participant in Wednesday's jog-through practice, which was his first on-field action since being placed on injured reserve in mid-October due to an ankle injury. He's mostly operated as a returner on kickoffs and punts this season, but his return would also give the Packers some extra depth at wide receiver.

headline: The Packers placed Moore (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday.
story: Moore wasn't able to return after injuring his ankle last Sunday against the Bears, and in the midst of not practicing during Week 6 prep, he was seen wearing a boot on his left boot and using a scooter to move about the locker room, per Matt Schneidman of The Athletic. Moore thus will miss at least the next four games, meaning his next chance to suit up will be Sunday, Nov. 15 against the Vikings. In Moore's absence, some combination of Bo Melton, Savion Williams (ankle) and Matthew Golden likely will handle return duties.

headline: Moore (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday night's game against the Cowboys, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Moore was held out of practice all week due to an ankle injury that he picked up during the Packers' Week 5 win against the Bears. The injury is severe enough for him to be sidelined for Sunday's game, so Bo Melton, Kaleb Johnson and Matthew Golden figure to be the top candidates to take over return duties on kickoffs and punts. Moore's next opportunity to play is Week 7 against the Lions on Sunday, Oct. 25.

headline: Moore (ankle) remained a non-participant at Thursday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Moore injured his ankle in the Week 5 win over the Bears and seems to be trending toward a Week 6 absence Sunday against the Cowboys, which would open the door for Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant to take on larger roles behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. The Packers would also need to find an alternative option to return kickoffs and punts if Moore sits, with Sturdivant, Melton, Golden and Pierre Strong among the top candidates to contribute in those situations.

headline: Moore (ankle) did not participate at the Packers' practice Wednesday.
story: Moore was sidelined at practice to open the week, as expected. The wide receiver suffered an ankle injury during the team's 31-7 victory over Chicago in Week 5, and he was using a scooter to get around the locker room while his left foot was in a boot Wednesday, per Matt Schneidman of The Athletic. Moore seems unlikely to be available for Week 6, and if he is unable to play, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant would both be candidates to see an increase in opportunities on offense versus Dallas.

headline: Moore (ankle) wasn't spotted at Wednesday's practice, Bill Huber of SI.com reports.
story: Moore will open Week 6 prep as a non-participant after he made an early exit from this past Sunday's 31-7 win over the Bears due to the ankle injury. He'll have two more chances to potentially get back on the practice field before the Packers decide on his status for this Sunday's game against the Cowboys. If Moore isn't available to play, Bo Melton would likely step in as the Packers' No. 3 wideout behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.

headline: The Packers ruled out Moore (ankle) for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Bears.
story: Moore hauled in his lone target for no gain before exiting the contest early in the second quarter. With Moore done for the rest of the afternoon, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant are expected to serve as the Packers' primary kickoff returners, while Matthew Golden will likely take over on punt returns. The Packers will also rely on Melton and Sturdivant to fill in for Moore at the No. 3 receiver spot.

headline: Moore is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bears due to an ankle injury.
story: Moore headed to the locker room in the second quarter to receive further evaluation on his ankle injury. Before departing, Moore reeled in his lone target for no gain. If Moore is unable to check back into the game, the Packers will rely on Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant to handle the No. 3 receiver role, while Matthew Golden will likely fill in for Moore on punt returns.

headline: Moore caught one of two targets for minus-2 yards while also adding 52 kickoff-return yards and 19 yards as a punt returner during Sunday's 17-14 win over the Buccaneers.
story: Moore was unable to build off his seven targets from Week 3, garnering his fewest looks since Week 1 in the team's marginal victory versus Tampa Bay. The 26-year-old doesn't carry much upside as a fantasy asset, and he figures to operate as a distant No. 3 option at wide receiver behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden moving forward.

headline: Coach Matt LaFleur said Wednesday that Moore will be the next man up at wide receiver after it was announced Jayden Reed (neck) will undergo season-ending surgery, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports.
story: With Reed out last Thursday night against the Falcons, Moore played 34 of 66 offensive snaps and ran 27 routes on Jordan Love's 55 dropbacks. Moore caught three of seven targets for 31 yards. He's expected to fight for scraps behind all three of Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft in the pecking order for targets.

headline: Melton finished Wednesday's Thanksgiving Eve loss to the Rams with one rush for three yards and two catches (on three targets) for 20 yards. He also returned two kickoffs for 31 yards.
story: Melton's carry was his first of the season, so he hasn't been a weapon in that regard. However, he did step up a bit as a receiver, notching multiple receptions for the first time since he logged a season-high three catches in Week 5. Melton's main role this season has been as a kick returner, so he's well off the fantasy radar.

headline: Melton (thigh) is active for Wednesday's game against the Rams, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Melton's practice reps were limited due to a thigh injury he picked up against the Vikings in Week 10, but the 2022 seventh-rounder has been cleared by medical staff to suit up Wednesday. He has five catches on 10 targets for 34 yards through 10 regular-season games but has not recorded a reception since Week 7 against the Lions.

headline: Melton (thigh) is listed as questionable for Wednesday night's game against the Rams, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Melton had a trio of limited practices leading up to the Packers' Week 12 matchup against the Rams. The 27-year-old injured his thigh in the team's Week 10 loss to the Vikings. The fifth-year pro has appeared in all 10 games for Green Bay this season, catching five of 10 targets for 34 yards.

headline: Melton (thigh) was limited in Monday's practice.
story: Melton was injured in the Packers' Week 10 loss to the Vikings and has been limited in practice each of the last two days leading up to Wednesday's game against the Rams. The wide receiver has appeared in all 10 games this season, recording five catches for 34 yards on 10 targets across 150 offensive snaps.

headline: Melton (thigh) was a limited participant in Sunday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Melton's practice reps Sunday were limited due to a thigh injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Vikings. His practice participation over the coming days will shed light on his chances of playing Wednesday against the Rams.

headline: Melton (thigh) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Vikings, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Melton exited Sunday's game because of a thigh injury, and he will not be cleared to return to the contest. Skyy Moore (ankle) will also not return, so Savion Williams and Matthew Golden will operate as the top return options on kickoffs and punts.

headline: Melton (thigh) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Vikings.
story: Melton exited the second quarter of Sunday's game with a thigh injury. With Skyy Moore (ankle) questionable to return as well, Savion Williams and Matthew Golden are set to be the main kick- and punt-return duo for the remainder of the contest.

headline: Melton (head) was removed from the injury report ahead of Sunday's game against Minnesota, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Melton exited the Week 9 win over the Patriots due to a possible concussion. However, with his omission from Thursday's edition of the injury report, he's good to go for Sunday's divisional showdown with the Vikings. The 27-year-old hasn't had a productive 2026 campaign, catching just five passes (10 targets) for 34 yards.

headline: Melton (head) was a full participant in Wednesday's jog-through practice.
story: Melton was removed from this past Sunday's game against the Patriots to be evaluated for a possible concussion. His ability to practice in full Wednesday is an encouraging sign for his availability for Week 10 against the Vikings on Nov. 15. Melton has five catches (on 10 targets) for 34 yards and 372 yards on 14 kickoffs through nine regular-season games, although he has not recorded a reception since Week 7 against the Lions.

headline: Melton exited Sunday's game against the Patriots and is being evaluated for a concussion.
story: Melton wasn't targeted prior to departing, but he did return four kicks for 110 yards. J. Michael Sturdivant will be next up for wideout snaps behind Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Savion Williams.

headline: Melton caught one of his two targets for four yards and logged a 24-yard kickoff return in the Packers' 20-17 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
story: Melton played 13 offensive snaps and 14 special-teams snaps in the contest. The No. 4 wide receiver remains a versatile depth option for the Packers, filling in wherever he is needed without garnering much attention.

headline: Melton (back) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions.
story: Melton logged just one limited session during Week 7 prep. The wide receiver's Friday upgrade to limited after consecutive DNPs appears to have been enough to green-light the No. 4 option for Sunday's divisional bout with the Lions.

headline: Melton (back) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Lions, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Melton opened Week 7 prep with back-to-back DNP's, but his limited session Friday was enough for him to draw the questionable tag for Sunday's NFC North tilt. Savion Williams would see an uptick on both offense and special teams as a returner on kickoffs and punts if Melton cannot play against Detroit.

headline: Melton (back) did not participate in practice Thursday, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Melton did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday due to a back injury that likely occurred in the Packers' win over the Cowboys in Week 6. The 27-year-old will likely need to practice in some capacity to have a chance at playing Sunday against the Lions.

headline: Melton (back) was a non-participant participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Melton may have tweaked his back during the Packers' win over the Cowboys on Sunday, when he played 34 snaps (18 on offense, 16 on special teams) and drew a 37-yard pass interference penalty late in the second quarter before adding a tackle on kickoff coverage. He'll have two more practices to increase his participation to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Lions.

headline: Williams carried twice for 18 yards and caught one of three targets for three yards against the Rams in a Thanksgiving Eve loss Wednesday.
story: It was another rough performance for Green Bay's ground game, which gained just 55 yards on 14 carries. Williams got two totes, and the wide receiver ended up atop the team's rushing leaderboard with 18 yards, ahead of RBs Kaleb Johnson (13 yards on eight carries) and MarShawn Lloyd (10 yards on one carry). Williams has consistently seen minor work out of the backfield this season, logging at least one carry (but no more than three) in all but one of his six appearances. That gives a small boost to his fantasy outlook, but he's yet to reach 50 receiving yards in a game this season, so Williams is a very risky fantasy play. However, he'd probably get a boost in that regard if Christian Watson (concussion), who exited late in the first half Wednesday and didn't return, isn't able to suit up in Week 13 against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Williams caught two passes for 27 yards on two targets in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: As he's been doing since making his season debut in Week 6, Williams operated as the Packers' third receiver against Minnesota. He logged 20 offensive snaps and ran 16 routes on 37 dropbacks. Williams has yet to hit 50 receiving yards in any of his five games this season and has no real fantasy appeal in 12-team fantasy leagues. He's well behind Matthew Golden, Christian Watson and Tucker Kraft in the order for touches and targets.

headline: Williams (groin) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Despite being listed as limited on all three of the Packers' Week 10 practice reports due to a groin injury, Williams has been cleared for Sunday's matchup. In his four appearances this season, he's turned his 19 touches (11 catches, eight rushes) into 153 yards from scrimmage and one receiving touchdown.

headline: Williams (groin) was a limited practice participant Thursday.
story: Since Williams made his season debut in Week 6 against the Cowboys, his snap share has ranged from 48 to 60 percent over the last four games, and he's made his mark on offense in each one, gathering in 11 of 13 targets for 109 yards and one touchdown and taking eight carries for 44 yards. A groin issue has capped his reps so far this week, and Friday's injury report will determine if he has a designation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Vikings.

headline: Williams (groin) was limited in Wednesday's jog-through practice.
story: It's a new injury for Williams, who previously missed a chunk of the season with an ankle injury. He's been running as the Packers' clear third receiver behind Matthew Golden and Christian Watson over the last few weeks. If Williams is unable to play against Minnesota on Sunday, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant could see an uptick in snaps, though Skyy Moore (ankle) had his 21-day practice window opened and could also be an option.

headline: Williams caught three of four targets for 25 yards and a touchdown while adding three rushes for 13 yards during Sunday's 45-27 win over the Patriots.
story: Williams was able to reel in multiple passes for the third time in four games since returning from injured reserve following an ankle injury. The wide receiver's biggest moment of the game came in the third quarter when he secured a 10-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Jordan Love by making an acrobatic catch. Williams has now reeled in 11 of 13 targets for 109 yards and a touchdown while turning eight carries into 44 yards over four contests this season.

headline: Williams caught three passes on as many targets for 47 yards and turned two carries into four yards during the Packers' 20-17 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
story: Quarterback Jordan Love spread the ball around Sunday to eight different receivers, and Williams was one of five pass catchers to record at least three receptions. Williams finished fourth on the team in receiving yards, with two of his catches going for 27 and 20 yards in the first and second quarters, respectively. The second-year pro is cemented as the Packers' WR3 behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, and tight end Tucker Kraft also is in the mix for looks from Love. The Packers will head back to Lambeau Field and practice on a short week for Thursday night's game against the Panthers, whose defense ranks sixth in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (195.7) and fifth in passing touchdowns allowed (seven).

headline: Williams (ankle) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Lions, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: A knee injury limited Williams' practice participation all week, but he's done enough to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's NFC North showdown. The second-year pro made his 2026 debut against the Cowboys in Week 8, when he caught all four of his targets for 32 yards and added two carries for nine yards in a 23-13 win for the Packers. Williams figures to operate as Green Bay's WR3 behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.

headline: Williams (ankle) was listed as limited at Thursday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Williams was also listed as limited on Wednesday's estimated injury report. The same applies to Christian Watson (ankle) and Matthew Golden (shoulder), while Bo Melton (back) has drawn consecutive 'DNP' listings. Friday's final injury report thus is slated to add further context with regard to the health of the Packers' WR corps for Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff against the Lions.

headline: Williams (ankle) was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's estimated injury report, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Also estimated as limited participants Wednesday were Christian Watson (ankle) and Matthew Golden (shoulder), while Bo Melton was a deemed a non-participant. Thursday's on-field session should provide a better idea of the health of Green Bay's wideout corps ahead of Sunday's game against the Lions. In his regular-season debut in a Week 6 win over the Cowboys, Williams logged a 53 percent snap share while working behind Watson and Golden en route to catching all four of his targets for 32 yards and rushing twice for nine yards.

headline: Williams caught all four of his targets for 32 yards and rushed twice for nine yards during Sunday night's 23-13 win over Dallas.
story: Williams made his regular-season debut after missing the team's first five contests while on injured reserve with an ankle injury. The wide receiver finished fifth on the team in targets, but he ranked third at his position behind Matthew Golden (13) and Christian Watson (eight). With Jayden Reed (neck) done for the season and Skyy Moore (ankle) on injured reserve, Williams will have a chance to carve out a solid role for himself as the team's No. 3 WR moving forward in 2026.

headline: Williams (ankle) is active for Sunday night's game against the Cowboys.
story: Williams was activated from injured reserve Saturday and will make his 2026 season debut against Dallas. With Skyy Moore (ankle) placed on IR over the weekend, Williams has a chance to immediately claim WR3 duties behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.

headline: The Packers activated Williams (ankle) from injured reserve Saturday.
story: Williams remains questionable for Sunday night against the Cowboys, but the transaction Saturday paves the way for him to play versus Dallas. With Skyy Moore (ankle) joining Jayden Reed (neck) on injured reserve Saturday, Williams could see offensive snaps behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, and there's a real chance Williams takes over WR3 duties in Green Bay moving forward. Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant are his main competitors for snaps on offense.

headline: Williams (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Williams opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a high-ankle sprain and had his 21-day practice window opened during Week 5 prep. He's drawn the questionable tag for Week 6 after stringing together three limited practices, but he will not be eligible to play unless activated from IR on Saturday.

headline: Williams (ankle) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: Williams still hasn't been able to manage a full practice since Green Bay opened his 21-day practice window ahead of its Week 5 contest versus the Bears, and now his status for Week 6 is up in the air. He'll likely have to upgrade to full participation at practice before the Packers officially activate him from their injured reserve list.

headline: Williams (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bears, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Williams opened the regular season on IR due to a high-ankle sprain that he suffered late in training camp. He was designated to return from IR on Wednesday and was a limited participant in practice all week, and while the second-year wideout is not yet quite ready to make his 2026 regular-season debut, his next chance to do so is Week 6 against the Cowboys on Sunday, Oct. 18. Williams could be in line for WR3 duties behind Matthew Golden and Christian Watson in his return, given the fact that Jayden Reed (neck, IR) is out for the rest of 2026.

headline: Williams (ankle) was a limited participant Wednesday after the Packers opened his 21-day practice window.
story: Williams sustained a high-ankle sprain late in training camp, prompting the Packers to place the second-year wide receiver on injured reserve. After sitting out the team's first four games, Williams is ready to mix back into drills, but he'll likely need to practice fully Thursday and Friday in order to have a shot at returning from IR and suiting up this Sunday against the Bears. Once activated, Williams will likely be a factor in the return game and could push Skyy Moore for the No. 3 receiver role behind Christian Watson and Matthew Golden.

headline: Brooks rushed once for four yards and caught four of five targets for 22 yards in Wednesday's Thanksgiving Eve loss to the Rams.
story: Brooks and Kaleb Johnson split the workload pretty evenly at running back for Green Bay, with the former logging 19 offensive snaps and the latter 24. Meanwhile, MarShawn Lloyd tallied just three snaps on offense. Whereas Johnson led the group with eight carries, Brooks was by far the most active in the passing game, tying for the overall team lead with both his five targets and four receptions. He had just four catches over five games coming into Wednesday, so it remains to be seen if the bump in work as a pass catcher continues for Brooks moving forward. The entire breakdown of the Packers backfield could shift in Week 13 against the Saints if Josh Jacobs (finger) is ready to return to action.

headline: Brooks rushed two times for one yard and caught his only target for two yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: It was Brooks' first action since Week 4 after spending five games on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. With Josh Jacobs (finger) inactive against Minnesota, Brooks led the backfield with 26 offensive snaps in Week 10, but it didn't translate to touches or opportunities to handle the football. With Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd also involved, it's difficult to pinpoint any of these three as reliable fantasy options despite Jacobs' absence.

headline: Brooks (ankle) is active for Sunday's game versus the Vikings, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Brooks is back after a five-game stint on injured reserve due to an ankle issue that he suffered in Week 4. With top RB Josh Jacobs (finger) out of the lineup and Pierre Strong a healthy scratch Sunday, Brooks rejoins a backfield composed of MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson. Brooks got some modest run with the Packers offense before he was sidelined, turning 15 rushes into 70 yards (4.7 YPC) and three catches (on five targets) for 24 yards, but he's most valuable in pass protection for QB Jordan Love.

headline: Green Bay activated Brooks (ankle) from injured reserve Saturday, though he is still questionable for Sunday's Week 10 clash against the Vikings.
story: Brooks has missed the required four contests after being placed on injured reserve Oct. 10. He was limited in all three practices this week, and it remains to be seen if he'll suit up Sunday. If Brooks does play, he'll help make up for the backfield absence of Josh Jacobs, who has been ruled out due to a finger injury. MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong are the Packers' current healthy RBs.

headline: Brooks (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Brooks logged three consecutive limited practices during Week 10 prep as he works his way back from an ankle injury he suffered in Week 4 that landed the running back on IR. With Josh Jacobs (finger) ruled out for Sunday's divisional contest, Brooks could be activated ahead of Sunday's game to play alongside MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson.

headline: Brooks (IR, ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Brooks suffered an ankle injury in the Week 4 meeting with the Buccaneers and eventually landed on injured reserve. While he's been working his way back since then, it's unknown if he will be ready for Sunday's divisional clash with the Vikings.

headline: Brooks (ankle) was listed as a limited practice participant for Wednesday's jog-through session.
story: Brooks continues to work his way back from an ankle injury that caused him to land on injured reserve in early October. He would likely need to log consecutive full practices before being activated from IR. The Packers face the Vikings on Sunday, and Green Bay is expected to be without Josh Jacobs for two to three weeks due to a broken right ring finger, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network.

headline: As Week 10 approaches, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com indicates that Brooks (ankle) may be ready to return from IR.
story: Brooks -- who last played in Week 4 -- was designated to return from injured reserve this past Wednesday and listed as questionable ahead of Week 9. Though the Packers held off on activating Brooks for Sunday's win over the Patriots, he could be needed more than expected going forward, with Josh Jacobs in line to miss time with a finger injury that may result in an IR stint.

headline: The Packers didn't activate Brooks (ankle) from injured reserve Saturday, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Brooks landed on IR in early October and has missed the required four games. He was designated to return Wednesday and was limited in practice all week before drawing a tag of questionable for Sunday's game against New England. The running back didn't end up being activated Saturday, so Brooks isn't eligible to suit up again until at least Sunday, Nov. 15, against Minnesota.

headline: Brooks (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Brooks was a limited participant throughout Week 9 prep as he looks to make his return from injured reserve. The running back will likely not be rushed back due to the recent return of Josh Jacobs. The Packers have until Nov. 25 to return Brooks to the active roster, or he will spend the remainder of the 2026 season on IR.

headline: Brooks (ankle) was designated to return from injured reserve by the Packers on Wednesday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
story: Brooks was a limited participant at the team's first practice of the week as Green Bay opened his 21-day practice window Wednesday. The running back has been on IR since suffering an ankle injury in Week 4 against the Buccaneers, but he could be nearing a return to action.

headline: The Packers placed Brooks (ankle) on injured reserve Saturday.
story: Brooks thus will miss at least the next four games, including Sunday against the Bears, due to the ankle injury that he sustained during a Week 4 win at Tampa Bay. With Josh Jacobs (personal) still on the commissioner's exempt list, MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong are the current healthy running backs on Green Bay's active roster.

headline: Brooks (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game versus the Bears, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Brooks limped off the field in the first quarter of this past Sunday's win at Tampa Bay and wasn't able to return due to an ankle injury, which kept him out of all Week 5 practices. With Brooks unavailable this weekend, MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong will be Green Bay's backfield options. Brooks' next chance to suit up is Sunday, Oct. 18 against the Cowboys.

headline: Brooks (ankle) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Brooks was held out of practice for a second straight day, and his consecutive absences could put his availability in jeopardy for Sunday's game against the Bears. Perhaps out of concern for Brooks' status heading into the weekend, the Packers signed Pierre Strong off their practice squad Thursday to give the team another healthy option in the backfield behind MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson. If Brooks ends up sitting out Sunday, Strong could end up handling some of Brooks' responsibilities on passing downs.

headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said that Brooks (ankle) won't practice Wednesday, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Brooks was forced out of this past Sunday's win over the Buccaneers due to an ankle injury, but the severity of the injury isn't fully known. If Brooks is unable to play in Week 5 against the Bears, MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson would absorb his share of the snaps in what has been a three-man backfield up to this point in the season.

headline: Brooks underwent further tests on his ankle Monday, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Brooks underwent further tests on his ankle after leaving Sunday's Week 4 game with an ankle injury. The 26-year-old has seen more reps through four weeks with starter Josh Jacobs (personal) remaining out.

headline: Brooks is questionable to return to Sunday's Week 4 matchup against Tampa Bay due to an ankle injury, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Brooks began the game in solid form, rushing four times for 30 yards and catching his lone target for five yards before limping to the sideline near the end of the first quarter. He'll be evaluated by team trainers before a determination is made about whether Brooks will be able to return. In the meantime, MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson are Green Bay's two healthy running backs.

headline: Lloyd rushed once for 10 yards and caught his only target for six yards in Wednesday's Week 12 loss to the Rams.
story: After logging double-digit snaps in each of his first nine games of the season, Lloyd totaled just three offensive snaps Wednesday. In that context, his production was relatively efficient -- in fact, his 10-yard run on his lone carry put him just behind starting running back Kaleb Johnson, who tallied just 13 rushing yards on eight totes. With that said, it's hard to see a path to meaningful fantasy production for Lloyd if he doesn't get more opportunities, and he could be phased out of the game plan altogether if Josh Jacobs (finger) is able to return for the Packers' Week 13 matchup in New Orleans on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Lloyd finished Sunday's loss to Minnesota with 13 yards on four carries while catching all three of his targets for 26 yards.
story: With Josh Jacobs (finger) sidelined, Green Bay turned to the trio of Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Chris Brooks in the backfield. Johnson led the team with 10 carries and 42 total yards despite not getting any targets. Meanwhile, Lloyd turned his seven touches into 39 yards, and Brooks tallied just three yards on his three touches. Green Bay is on bye during the coming week, but Jacobs may still miss the team's next game, which will take place Wednesday, Nov. 25, against the Rams. If that's the case, Lloyd will likely work as part of a shared backfield again, which isn't great for his fantasy outlook.

headline: Lloyd (knee) is not listed on the Packers' injury report Wednesday.
story: The running back appears ready to return to the lineup for Sunday's game against the Vikings after missing Week 9 against New England. With Josh Jacobs (finger) set to miss some time, Lloyd figures to be part of the backfield mix, joining Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong.

headline: Lloyd (knee) is listed as inactive Sunday at New England, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: The Packers added Lloyd to the Week 9 injury report Thursday as limited due to a knee injury, and he maintained that activity level Friday before the team tagged him as questionable ahead of the weekend. Now that Lloyd is confirmed to be unavailable, Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson will be the team's complementary backfield options behind No. 1 option Josh Jacobs.

headline: Lloyd (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Lloyd was added to the injury report Thursday, which is rarely a good sign for a player's availability Sunday. If Lloyd can't play, Pierre Strong figures to draw in as the pass-catching complement to Josh Jacobs out of the Packers' backfield.

headline: Lloyd was limited at practice Thursday due to a knee injury.
story: Lloyd's addition to the Packers' practice report midweek is something to monitor, especially because it may indicate a health concern that occurred during Thursday's session. Ultimately, Friday's injury report may provide some clarity into the situation.

headline: Lloyd rushed three times for seven yards and brought in his only target for nine yards in the Packers' 27-19 win over the Panthers on Thursday.
story: In his second game of the season, Josh Jacobs logged a total of 27 touches, leaving precious little work for any other back. Lloyd slightly outpaced Pierre Strong by two carries, but he still logged a season low in rush attempts. With Jacobs looking fully capable of handling a workhorse role moving forward, Lloyd may be destined for similar volume to Thursday's on most weeks as long as his star teammate is available.

headline: Lloyd tallied six carries for 20 yards and two catches (on two targets) for 15 yards during Sunday's 20-17 loss in Detroit.
story: The Packers got top RB Josh Jacobs back in the lineup for the first time this season after he spent the first six contests on the commissioner's exempt list. However, he wasn't able to provide a jolt to a moribund ground game, as the team averaged just 3.2 YPC on its 19 rushes. On a positive note for Lloyd, though, he was the only Green Bay running back other than Jacobs to earn a touch, as an active Pierre Strong did not, and Kaleb Johnson (coach's decision) was a healthy scratch. Lloyd appears set to serve as the team's No. 2 backfield option moving forward, which should provide him regular reps with which to work behind Jacobs.

headline: Lloyd rushed eight times for 10 yards while failing to catch his only target during Sunday night's 23-13 win over Dallas.
story: Lloyd was rather inefficient in Week 6, averaging 1.3 yards per carry while logging three fewer carries than fellow running back Pierre Strong (11). Lloyd was briefly sidelined by an undisclosed injury during the contest, but his ability to finish the game would suggest that whatever he was dealing with is minor. With Josh Jacobs expected to be removed from the Commissioner's Exempt List on Monday, Lloyd will likely transition into a complementary role behind Jacobs in the backfield moving forward.

headline: Lloyd rushed 10 times for 31 yards and two touchdowns while catching one of two targets for six yards during Sunday's 31-7 win over the Bears.
story: Lloyd was able to open the second quarter with a 10-yard touchdown run before later adding a four-yard score in the fourth quarter. The running back's 10 carries were his most since logging 13 rushes for 37 yards in Week 1 versus Minnesota. Lloyd has now compiled 112 rushing yards on 40 carries and two touchdowns while reeling in 10 of 13 targets for 55 yards and a score over five games to open the 2026 season while operating as Green Bay's primary option in the backfield with Josh Jacobs (personal) on the Commissioner's Exempt List.

headline: Lloyd rushed seven times for 13 yards and brought in all five targets for 36 yards in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: It was more of the same on the ground for Lloyd, who barely eclipsed the season-low 11 rushing yards he produced in Week 3 against the Falcons. However, the third-year back set new career highs in receptions, receiving yards and targets, offering some modest fantasy value on the afternoon. Lloyd's backfield mate Kaleb Johnson led the ground attack with eight carries for 42 yards Sunday, and although Lloyd remains largely ineffective as a runner, he'll likely remain in a relevant role in Week 5 at home against the Bears if the ankle injury that forced Chris Brooks' exit from the contest keeps him sidelined for that divisional contest.

headline: Johnson rushed eight times for 13 yards and brought in one of two targets for 19 yards in the Packers' 26-13 loss to the Rams on Wednesday night.
story: As his final numbers indicate, Johnson couldn't find any running room but was very productive with his one catch. The 2025 third-round pick of the Steelers was in the lead role once again with Josh Jacobs (finger) inactive, but Johnson couldn't come close to matching the encouraging rushing production he'd managed over the previous two games (24 carries, 110 yards, one TD). Jacobs is expected back for the Packers' Week 13 road matchup against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6, a development that would relegate Johnson to his more customary reserve role.

headline: Johnson handled the first RB reps during the open portion of Sunday's practice, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Josh Jacobs logged his first official practice Sunday since undergoing finger surgery on Nov. 13, going down as a limited participant. Head coach Matt LaFleur relayed to Wes Hodkiewicz of the team's official site earlier in the day that Jacobs is "gonna have to show a lot of progress" the next few days to be available in Week 12. If Jacobs isn't active Wednesday at the Rams, Johnson may be the favorite to lead Green Bay's backfield in carries and rushing yards, as he did in a Week 10 loss to the Vikings, when he took 10 rushes for 42 yards. Meanwhile, fellow RB MarShawn Lloyd had seven touches for 39 yards from scrimmage in that contest, and Chris Brooks logged three touches for three total yards.

headline: Johnson carried the ball 10 times for 42 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: The former Steeler led the Packers' backfield in totes and rushing yards, with MarShawn Lloyd chipping in 39 scrimmage yards on seven touches. Johnson has produced modest but decent numbers over the last two games, averaging a 4.6 YPC on 24 carries as the top early-down option for Green Bay. Josh Jacobs (finger) could return after the team's Week 11 bye, but if he isn't cleared, Johnson could find himself atop the depth chart again in Week 12 against the Rams.

headline: Johnson could serve as the Packers' lead option on the ground in Sunday's game against the Vikings with Josh Jacobs (finger) expected to miss multiple weeks and with the status of MarShawn Lloyd (knee) uncertain, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: After being a healthy inactive for the Packers' previous two games, Johnson suited up for Sunday's tilt with the Patriots while Lloyd was inactive. With Jacobs leaving the contest late in the first quarter after fracturing his right ring finger, Johnson was thrust into action and delivered the Packers' best rushing performance of the season, finishing with 14 carries for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 45-27 win. Head coach Matt LaFleur relayed Monday that Jacobs will need surgery and could land on injured reserve, and while Lloyd could have a chance at returning to action Week 10, the Packers likely came away encouraged enough by Johnson's showing in Foxborough to give him another turn as their lead option on the ground. Johnson isn't likely to earn much passing-down work, however, as Lloyd, Pierre Strong and Chris Brooks (ankle) -- who could return from IR this week -- are all more capable options in that phase.

headline: Johnson rushed 14 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Josh Jacobs exited the game in the first quarter due to a hand injury, leaving Johnson in a lead role that the Steelers' 2025 third-round pick filled effectively. Johnson's carry and yardage totals were both new career highs by a fairly wide margin, and he also punched in his first career touchdown on a two-yard run with under five minutes remaining in the first half. The impressive showing combined with Jacobs' injury and that of MarShawn Lloyd (knee), who was inactive Sunday, could leave Johnson in possession of the top role again in a Week 10 home divisional showdown against the Vikings next Sunday.

headline: Johnson (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against the Panthers, Mike Spofford of the team's official site reports.
story: Johnson didn't suit up in the Week 7 loss to Detroit. The 23-year-old will be held out for a second consecutive contest, and he likely won't get back on the field moving forward if Josh Jacobs, MarShawn Lloyd and Pierre Strong are active.

headline: Johnson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Lions.
story: Johnson is inactive one week after logging eight carries for 42 yards in the Packers' Week 6 win over the Buccaneers. The running back has likely been sidelined due to a crucial fourth-quarter fumble, combined with the return of Josh Jacobs from the Commissioner's Exemption List.

headline: Johnson logged eight carries for 42 yards and lost one fumble in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: Johnson had a strong 5.3 yards per carry in the win but coughed up the football in a close game. The running back relinquished the ball to Tykee Smith with 9:13 remaining in the fourth quarter on the Tampa Bay 4-yard line while the Packers were up by only three points. The defense held off the Buccaneers offense, but it appears the Packers chose to ride MarShawn Lloyd to finish out the game.
