headline: Love completed 17 of 29 passes for 198 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions and rushed once for seven yards in the Packers' 26-13 loss to the Rams on Wednesday night.
story: Love already had a daunting challenge coming in against a talented Rams secondary. It was made exponentially more difficult due to Christian Watson, to whom he threw his only touchdown pass of the night in the second quarter from six yards out, exiting the game for good late in the first half due to a possible concussion. The veteran signal-caller unsurprisingly scuffled throughout, and his two interceptions came in the second half while the game was still within reach for Green Bay. The game marked Love's first with multiple interceptions this season, as well as his third below 200 passing yards. Love will look to bounce back when the Packers return to action on the road against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Love completed 17 of 27 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: The 28-year-old QB came into the game having been sacked just 17 times in his first nine games of the season, but Minnesota brought Love down eight times Sunday. Despite that onslaught, he was able to find J. Michael Sturdivant for a 32-yard TD in the third quarter to salvage his line slightly. It was the first time since Week 6 that Love had failed to throw multiple touchdowns, and just the second time all season. He'll get a Week 11 bye to heal up from Sunday's pummeling before facing Myles Garrett and the Rams in Week 12.

headline: Love completed 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions and rushed once for a 13-yard score in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday. He also ran in a two-point conversion.
story: Love continued to attack downfield with great efficacy in the significant road upset for the Packers. Love averaged 12.8 yards per attempt while amassing his second-highest passing yardage total of the season, a figure bested only by the 387-yard tally he managed in Week 1. Love generated his second straight three-touchdown day through the air as well, connecting with Matthew Golden (five yards), Savion Williams (10 yards) and Christian Watson (39 yards) for his trio of scoring strikes and kicking off the scoring on the day with a 13-yard rush just 1:41 into the contest. Love is up to 2,618 passing yards with a 19:6 TD:INT and a pair of rushing scores heading into a Week 10 home divisional clash against the Vikings next Sunday.

headline: Love completed 30 of 41 passes for 288 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and recovered a fumble in the Packers' 27-19 win over the Panthers on Thursday.
story: Love continued his season-long trend of prolific passing yardage totals in the Packers' fifth win of the season, and Thursday's total was accomplished with Christian Watson missing almost a full quarter because of chest and rib injuries. Love connected with Tucker Kraft (12 yards), Matthew Golden (24 yards) and Josh Jacobs (four yards) for his trio of TD passes, a figure that marked a new season high. Love did throw an interception for a third straight game, but it didn't lead to any Panthers points. Love is already up to what is currently a league-high 2,246 passing yards and 16 touchdown passes on the season heading into a Week 9 road showdown against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Golden secured one of five targets for 39 yards in the Packers' 26-13 loss to the Rams on Wednesday night.
story: Golden saw Christian Watson exit for good late in the first half due to a possible concussion, but the former still couldn't capitalize on a night when Jordan Love threw for a modest 198 yards and tossed two interceptions. Golden's yardage total tied for his second-lowest figure of the season, while Wednesday marked his first game without multiple receptions. Golden will look to bounce back in a Week 13 road matchup against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Golden caught five of nine targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: The second-year wideout was the only Packer to have much success on offense, leading the team in catches, targets and receiving yards. Golden has reached 70 yards in three straight games and five of the last six, and he heads into a Week 11 bye with a 58-853-5 line on 101 targets through 10 contests. His next chance to add to those numbers will come in Week 12 against the Rams.

headline: Golden brought in all 10 targets for 164 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Golden led the Packers in receptions and targets while finishing second in receiving yards, and the latter total was also a new career high. The second-year wideout also laid claim to the game's longest catch (49 yards), and he reeled in the first of Jordan Love's three TD passes on the day with a five-yard grab at just under the eight-minute mark of the first quarter. Golden now has four 100-yard efforts in what is already a breakout campaign that's seen him amass a 53-783-5 line on 92 targets heading into a Week 10 home showdown against the Vikings next Sunday.

headline: Golden brought in seven of 13 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 27-19 win over the Panthers on Thursday.
story: The second-year speedster finished second in receptions and receiving yards for the Packers on the night, while also leading the way in targets with a season-high-tying figure. Golden struck for his fourth touchdown of the season as well on a 24-yard scoring grab just after the two-minute warning in the first half, and the 2025 first-round pick now has at least six catches in four consecutive contests. He should remain busy in a Week 9 road showdown against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 8, one where New England shutdown cornerback Christian Gonzalez could spend the majority of his time on Christian Watson.

headline: Golden (shoulder/foot) is listed as active Thursday against the Panthers, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Golden was contained to just one limited walkthrough (Wednesday) during Week 8 prep due to shoulder and foot injuries, but James Palmer of NFL on Prime Video reported earlier Thursday that the Packers were optimistic about the second-year wide receiver's availability. Indeed, Golden is suiting up, looking to build upon the 36-540-3 line on 69 targets that he's racked up through the first seven contests of the season.

headline: The Packers expect Golden (shoulder/foot), who is listed as questionable for Thursday night's game against the Panthers, to suit up, James Palmer of NFL on Prime Video reports.
story: Golden was given a questionable tag after being listed as a limited participant at Wednesday's walkthrough following practice absences Monday and Tuesday. If the 2025 first-round pick gets the green light when game statuses are confirmed approximately 90 minutes prior to Thursday night's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, Golden would likely occupy his customary starting role across from Christian Watson.

headline: Golden (shoulder/foot) is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against the Panthers, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Golden opened Week 8 prep as a listed non-participant both Monday and Tuesday due to shoulder and foot injuries, but he was able to upgrade to limited at Wednesday's walkthrough and thus put himself in a position to play Thursday. His status will be confirmed, one way or another, about 90 minutes before an 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff

headline: Golden (shoulder/foot) didn't participate in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.
story: Coming out of Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Lions, Golden is nursing a pair of injuries that have resulted in him going down as a non-participant on the Packers' Week 8 injury report. The Packers will see if Golden can upgrade to limited or full participation in Wednesday's session before deciding whether he'll carry a designation into Thursday's game against the Panthers. Despite leading the NFL with six drops through the first seven weeks, Golden has emerged as a useful fantasy asset in his second NFL season with 36 receptions for 540 yards and three touchdowns on 69 targets to go with six rushing yards.

headline: Golden (shoulder/foot) was listed as a non-participant on Monday's practice estimate, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports
story: After being limited last week due to a shoulder injury, Golden was able to suit up Sunday at Detroit, logging an 85 percent snap share and corralling six of 12 targets for 39 yards. As Week 8 prep kicks off, he's also tending to a foot issue. Golden will have two more chances to be listed as something other than DNP this week before the Packers potentially tag him with a designation for Thursday's game against the Panthers.

headline: Golden gathered in six of 12 targets for 39 yards during Sunday's 20-17 defeat in Detroit.
story: Golden has been targeted at least 12 times by QB Jordan Love in four of seven appearances this season, resulting in three 100-yard efforts to date. Drops and near misses between the two continue to be a feature in the Packers offense, though, as Golden has recorded a catch rate of 50 percent or better four times, with his mark in 2026 sitting at only 52.2 percent. Golden and Green Bay next have a Thursday night matchup with the Panthers on the docket in Week 8.

headline: Golden (shoulder) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Lions.
story: After being limited in practice this week, Golden is good to go for Sunday's divisional matchup in what projects to be a shootout at Ford Field. In just six games this season, Golden has already surpassed last year's marks in catches, yards and touchdowns, producing a 30-501-3 receiving line on 51 targets. He's developed into an every-week WR2 for fantasy.

headline: Golden (shoulder) was limited at Thursday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Both Golden and fellow WR Christian Watson (ankle) have opened Week 7 prep as limited on both of the Packers' first two injury reports. Head coach Matt LaFleur told Demovsky on Thursday that he has no concern about the availability of either player for Sunday's contest at Detroit. Friday's report will reveal if Golden or Watson enter the weekend with a designation.

headline: Head coach Matt LaFleur said Thursday that the Packers have no concern regarding Golden's (shoulder) availability for Sunday's game against the Lions, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Golden and Christian Watson (ankle) were both listed as limited participants at Wednesday's practice, but Green Bay's coach is confident that both starting wideouts will be available Sunday. Watson (538) and Golden (501) have combined for the most yards by any pair of teammates at wide receiver in the league this season.

headline: Golden (shoulder) was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's estimated injury report, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Golden's inclusion coincides with QB Jordan Love (back) and WR Christian Watson (ankle), among others, also being listed as limited to kick off Week 7 prep. The situation thus bears monitoring as the week continues to see if any of the trio is in danger of missing Sunday's contest at Detroit.

headline: Golden caught six of 13 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-13 win over the Cowboys.
story: Golden reached 100 receiving yards for the second consecutive game and third time overall this season. He capped the opening drive with a nine-yard touchdown catch, which gives the 2025 first-round pick three receiving touchdowns in his last four games after Golden began his career with a 16-game regular-season touchdown drought. Golden would have had an even bigger game if not for a pair of near-misses in the second quarter on a deep ball and an end-zone pass that were both in his hands before falling incomplete. Heading into a Week 7 matchup with Detroit's weak secondary, Golden has drawn a team-high 57 targets from Jordan Love, which is nine more than Christian Watson.

headline: Golden secured six of seven targets for 123 yards in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Bears on Sunday. He also returned two punts for 27 yards.
story: As good as Golden's afternoon was, he was actually slightly outshined by fellow wideout Christian Watson, who had 20 more receiving yards on the same number of catches and one additional target. Nevertheless, Golden's afternoon included a new career high in receiving yards, as well as a career-high-tying reception total. The second-year speedster is already well on his way to a breakout campaign, and he now has had at least seven targets in four of his first five games. The 2025 first-round pick will take a 24-397-2 line on 44 targets into a favorable Week 6 home matchup against the Cowboys next Sunday night.

headline: Golden brought in three of seven targets for 21 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday. He also rushed once for six yards.
story: Jordan Love threw for a modest 197 yards overall on the afternoon, so Golden's subdued production can be viewed within that context. The second-year speedster tied with Tucker Kraft for the team lead in targets on the afternoon, and although Golden brought in less than half of them. he recorded his second touchdown grab of the campaign on a two-yard reception early in the second quarter. Golden's reception and yardage totals were season lows, but he's still on pace for a breakout second campaign with an 18-274-2 line going into a Week 5 home divisional matchup against the Bears next Sunday.

headline: Kraft brought in three of five targets for 24 yards in the Packers' 26-13 loss to the Rams on Wednesday night. He also lost a fumble.
story: Kraft finished second in receptions and tied for the team lead in targets for the Packers on a night when Jordan Love threw for under 200 yards. The veteran tight end saw Christian Watson exit the game twice with thigh and head injuries in the first half, the latter issue forcing his exit for the rest of the game. Kraft recorded multiple receptions for the first time in three contests in the process, but his first-quarter fumble led to a Rams field goal. Kraft carries an unremarkable 40-394-3 line heading into a Week 13 road matchup against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Kraft caught one of four targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: The tight end's numbers reflected how much time his quarterback had to look downfield, as Jordan Love got sacked eight times in the rout. Kraft has been held to just one catch in back-to-back games, and he heads into a Week 11 bye with a 37-370-3 line on 56 targets through 10 games, with the Rams as the next opponent on the horizon in Week 12.

headline: Kraft brought in one of three targets for one yard and rushed twice for eight yards in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
story: The athletic tight end didn't get in on any of the fun on a day when Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns. Kraft's stat line set (receptions, receiving yards) or tied (targets) season lows, while his work on the ground included a pair of season-high figures. Nevertheless, it was an utterly forgettable showing for Kraft, who'll look to atone in a Week 10 home divisional clash against the Vikings next Sunday.

headline: Kraft secured all six targets for 53 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 27-19 win over the Panthers on Thursday.
story: Kraft kicked off the scoring on the night for the Packers with his 12-yard TD grab in the first quarter, marking his third of the season and second in as many games. The athletic tight end also recorded the third-most catches and receiving yards on the night for Green Bay, and Kraft now has at least five receptions in four of the last five games. Kraft will take a 35-350-3 line on 49 targets into a Week 9 road matchup against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Kraft compiled four catches (on six targets) for 48 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 20-17 loss at Detroit.
story: Kraft's 14-yard TD connection with QB Jordan Love late in the first quarter marked the tight end's second end-zone visit in seven games on the season. Having said that, Kraft has surpassed 50 receiving yards in just two contests, leaving him on a 29-297-2 line on 43 targets to date. WRs Matthew Golden (12 targets Sunday) and Christian Watson (eight) continue to dominate the attention of Love so far, meaning Kraft is the third option at best in the Packers' passing attack at the moment.

headline: Kraft caught five of eight targets for 37 yards in Sunday night's 23-13 win over the Cowboys.
story: Kraft briefly exited the game in the second half but quickly returned after a visit to the medical tent. His eight targets tied Christian Watson for second on the team behind Matthew Golden's 13, and the Green Bay offense has settled on funneling its targets mostly through the two wideouts and tight end. Kraft has just one touchdown on the season and has failed to top 65 receiving yards in a game, while being held below 45 yards four times. The upside hasn't been there, but Kraft's position as an every-down tight end in an elite offense keeps him squarely in the TE1 conversation.

headline: Kraft brought in all five targets for 64 yards and rushed once for two yards in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Bears on Sunday.
story: Kraft was an ideal complementary piece alongside top receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, who combined for 12 receptions for 266 yards and two touchdowns (Watson) on the afternoon. Kraft still managed to finish with his second-highest reception and receiving yardage totals of the season, and he should remain busy in what is likely to be a high-scoring Week 6 home showdown against the Cowboys next Sunday night.

headline: Kraft brought in six of seven targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday. He also rushed once for three yards.
story: Kraft set the pace for the Packers in receptions and tied with Matthew Golden for the team lead in targets on the afternoon while also finishing as the runner-up in receiving yards for Green Bay. The talented tight end also notched his first touchdown of the season with a two-yard catch early in the second half that was originally ruled out of bounds before being overturned on replay. Kraft has made a remarkable recovery from last year's season-ending knee injury, producing a 15-148-1 line over his first four games heading into a Week 5 home matchup against the Bears next Sunday.

headline: Sorrell (thumb) is questionable to return to Wednesday night's game against the Rams.
story: Prior to leaving, the linebacker recorded four tackles (two solo). Dani Dennis-Sutton and Brenton Cox will see an uptick in snaps off the edge for Green Bay.

headline: Watson (concussion) has been ruled out for the rest of Wednesday's game against the Rams.
story: The wideout hasn't cleared concussion checks and will miss the remainder of the Week 12 contest after he was injured at the end of the second quarter when Watson took a hit to the head from Kamren Kinchens. Look for J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton to see increased snaps alongside Matthew Golden and Savion Williams with Watson sidelined.

headline: Watson is being evaluated for a concussion and is questionable to return to Wednesday's game against the Rams.
story: This is Watson's second in-game injury scare Wednesday after he previously returned from a thigh issue. If he can't get back on the field, Green Bay would be down one of its top playmakers for the second half. Prior to the injury, Watson caught all four of his targets for 65 yards and a touchdown. J. Michael Sturdivant and Bo Melton would be in line for elevated snaps on offense if Watson is unable to return.

headline: Watson (undisclosed) appeared to sustain an injury after taking a hard hit in the second quarter of Wednesday's game against the Rams, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: The wide receiver suffered a thigh injury in the first quarter but returned to the contest, but Watson then took a big shot to the helmet at the end of the second quarter. Kamren Kinchens was actually ejected for the illegal hit. Prior to the injury, Watson caught four passes for 65 yards and a touchdown on four targets.

headline: Watson (thigh) returned to Wednesday's game against the Rams, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: The star wideout was injured on the Packers' first offensive play after making a six-yard catch. He missed the remainder of the drive but returned for the start of Green Bay's second possession. A crisis has therefore been averted for the Packers and fantasy managers alike.

headline: Watson (thigh) is questionable to return to Wednesday's game against the Rams.
story: The wideout was injured on the Packers' opening offensive play after securing a six-yard grab. He was lying down on the sideline before being shown working with trainers. If Watson is unable to return, J. Michael Sturdivant would stand to see the biggest increase in snaps opposite Matthew Golden.

headline: Watson caught three of five targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 30-10 loss to Minnesota.
story: The Packers' passing game was stifled as the Vikings sacked Jordan Love eight times, giving him little time to find receivers like Watson. The 37 yards were a season low for the fifth-year wideout, while the three grabs tied for his lowest volume of 2026. Watson will take a 52-916-7 line on 79 targets through 10 contests into a Week 11 bye before facing the Rams in Week 12.

headline: Watson secured seven of eight targets for 171 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Watson repeatedly got the best of Christian Gonzalez and the rest of a talented Patriots secondary, recording team- and career-high receiving yardage totals along the way. Watson burned New England for four catches of 20-plus yards, including a game-long 49-yard grab, as well as a 39-yard touchdown reception in the latter portion of the third quarter. Watson's career-best line is up to a tally of 49-879-7 on 74 targets heading into a Week 10 home matchup against the Vikings next Sunday.

headline: Watson (ribs) will be "full go" in Sunday's game at New England, per Jay Glazer on Fox NFL Sunday.
story: Watson suffered a broken rib during a Week 8 win against the Panthers in which he visited a Green Bay-area hospital during the game before returning to action in the second half. He finished that contest with his third 100-yard performance of the season -- an 8-113-0 line on 10 targets -- but he was limited during Week 9 prep before avoiding a designation for this Sunday's matchup. Glazer's report indicates Watson should be good for his typical 80-plus percent snap share and 8.3 targets per game on the campaign.

headline: Watson (ribs) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest at New England.
story: Despite being limited on all three of the Packers' Week 9 injury reports due to the broken rib he sustained during last Thursday's win against the Panthers, Watson will be available to Green Bay's offense. It stands to reason he'll wear some sort of protection around his midsection Sunday, but he nonetheless is a plug-and-play option due to his 42-708-6 line on 66 targets through the first eight games of the campaign.

headline: Watson (ribs) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Watson now has back-to-back capped sessions under his belt to begin Week 9 prep, which stems from the broken rib that he suffered during last Thursday's win against the Panthers. He'll have one more chance Friday to get back to full participation, at which point the Packers may tag him with a designation for Sunday's contest at New England.

headline: Watson (ribs) is wearing pads for Thursday's practice, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Watson was listed as a limited participant at Wednesday's practice after sustaining a rib injury in Green Bay's Week 8 win over the Panthers. His participation level Thursday has yet to be revealed, but it's a good sign that Watson is able to practice in pads and take contact as the Packers prepare to face the Patriots on Sunday.

headline: Watson (ribs) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: After making a visit to the hospital during last Thursday's win against the Panthers, Watson was able to return and finished with eight catches (on 10 targets) for 113 yards. Afterward, he was revealed to have a broken rib, which likely will be an injury he plays through while managing pain tolerance. In any case, Friday's injury report will unveil whether or not he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at New England.

headline: Packers passing game coordinator Jason Vrable said Monday that Watson (ribs) is sore but "doing great," Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Watson suffered a broken rib during this past Thursday's win over the Panthers, and while Vrable notes with regard to Watson's status for this Sunday's game against the Patriots, "We'll see as the week goes," he added that the wideout will do everything possible to get his body ready in advance of Week 9 action. In the event that Watson is unavailable, added reps behind Matthew Golden will be available for Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant.

headline: Watson said he suffered a broken rib in Thursday night's 27-19 win over the Panthers, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Watson took a hard fall in the second quarter after hauling in a 53-yard deep shot from Jordan Love. He landed on the football and was coughing up blood afterward, necessitating a trip to the hospital just before halftime. Scans showed a broken rib, but Watson was deemed fit to return to the game in the third quarter. He'll now have 10 days to rest up before the Packers' next game in Week 9 against the Patriots.

headline: Watson, who was hospitalized for a portion of Thursday's 27-19 win over the Panthers on Thursday to be evaluated for chest and rib injuries, finished the contest having brought in eight of 10 targets for 113 yards. He also lost a fumble.
story: Watson managed to lead the Packers in receptions and receiving yards despite missing almost a full quarter, making his numbers all the more admirable. The veteran speedster, who's on pace for a career-best season, set a new season high in catches, and he now has three 100-yard efforts on the campaign. Watson's second-quarter fumble didn't lead to any Panthers points, so he ultimately enjoyed a successful night in every sense. Watson now boasts a 42-708-6 line heading into a Week 9 road showdown against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Watson (chest) returned to Thursday night's game against the Panthers, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Watson was injured in the second quarter and missed roughly one full quarter to go to the hospital for testing on his chest and ribs area. Evidently, the results of the scans and tests came back clean, and Watson was cleared to reenter the game. He caught six passes for 100 yards on seven targets in the first half.

headline: Watson (chest) is questionable to return to Thursday night's game against the Panthers, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports.
story: Watson was injured hauling in a 53-yard pass from Jordan Love midway through the second quarter and is headed to the hospital to undergo further testing, according to Kaylee Hartung on the Amazon Prime broadcast. Matthew Golden, Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant will handle wideout duties while Watson is sidelined for Green Bay.

headline: Watson (undisclosed) headed to the locker room during the second quarter of Thursday night's game against the Panthers, Dominique Yates of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reports.
story: Watson was injured when he hauled in a 53-yard deep shot from Jordan Love. Prior to exiting, he caught six of seven targets for 100 yards. Savion Williams, Bo Melton and J. Michael Sturdivant will be in line for more snaps while Watson is in the locker room.

headline: Watson notched five catches (on eight targets) for 57 yards and no touchdowns during Sunday's 20-17 defeat at Detroit.
story: Watson's team-high 28-yard catch in the second quarter got the Packers into the red zone for the third time in Week 7, but after a Jordan Love to Tucker Kraft TD connection on the team's second possession, Green Bay otherwise failed to score on three of four trips to premium territory. Watson himself paced the team in receiving yards Sunday, but he also wasn't able to score a TD for the third time in the last four games, leaving him sitting on six scores in seven appearances. He and his teammates have a quick turnaround with a Thursday night matchup with the Panthers on tap in Week 8.

headline: Watson (ankle) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Detroit, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Watson was listed as limited on all three of Green Bay's Week 7 injury reports due to an ankle issue, but it won't stop him from being available Sunday. Both he and Matthew Golden (shoulder) are in the clear ahead of the weekend, meaning QB Jordan Love will have his top pass catchers at his disposal for the divisional matchup.

headline: Watson (ankle) practiced in a limited fashion Thursday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Watson now has logged a limited walkthrough and a capped practice to kick off Week 7 prep as he tends to an ankle issue. Head coach Matt LaFleur downplayed Watson's injury Thursday, telling Demovsky that he has no concerns about Watson and fellow WR Matthew Golden (shoulder) for Sunday's game in Detroit. Having said that, Watson may still be tagged with a designation when the Packers post their final practice report of the week Friday.

headline: Head coach Matt LaFleur said Thursday that the team has no concern regarding Watson's (ankle) availability for Sunday's game against the Lions, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: LaFleur said the same thing about Matthew Golden (shoulder) after Green Bay's top two wide receivers were both limited participants at Wednesday's practice. Watson may continue to have his practice reps monitored, but he isn't in any danger of sitting out Sunday's matchup against Detroit's struggling secondary.

headline: Watson was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's practice estimate due to an ankle injury, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Not only was Watson listed as limited, but so were QB Jordan Love (back) and WR Matthew Golden (back), among others. The situation thus leaves the Packers offense in a bit of flux as the team begins Week 7 prep, but two practices remain before Green Bay potentially tags players with designations for Sunday's game in Detroit.

headline: Watson caught three of eight targets for 64 yards in Sunday's 23-13 win over the Cowboys.
story: Watson was held without a touchdown for only the second time this season while tying tight end Tucker Kraft for second on the team in targets, five behind Matthew Golden. The wide receiver duo of Golden and Watson has accounted for the majority of Green Bay's offensive production this season. Watson needs just 82 receiving yards to match his career high of 620, which the oft-injured wideout set during the 2024 regular season. He'll have a nice opportunity to reach that mark in Week 7 against a Lions defense that has struggled in coverage.

headline: Watson brought in six of eight targets for 143 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers' 31-7 win over the Bears on Sunday.
story: Watson tied for the team lead in receptions with Matthew Golden while setting the pace in both receiving yards and targets. Watson struck for the first of his two touchdowns with a 42-yard grab that capped off Green Bay's 10-play opening drive. The veteran field-stretcher then added a spectacular contested 53-yard touchdown reception to put a stamp on the Packers' first drive of the second half, and Watson ultimately finished just five yards short of eclipsing the season-high 147 he put up in Week 1 against the Vikings. Watson will take a 26-474-6 line into a Week 6 home showdown against the Cowboys next Sunday night.

headline: Watson secured all three targets for 47 yards in the Packers' 17-14 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: Watson led the Packers in receiving yards on an afternoon when Jordan Love threw for only 197 yards. The speedy wideout's reception, receiving yardage and target totals were all season lows, but Watson has still enjoyed a productive start to the campaign with a 20-331-4 line on 32 targets and good health throughout. Watson and the Packers' air attack as a whole will look for a boost in production at the expense of the division-rival Bears in a Week 5 home matchup next Sunday.

headline: Zeitler (triceps/ankle) is active for Wednesday's game against the Rams, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Zeitler was unable to play against the Vikings in Week 10 due to triceps and ankle injuries, but the veteran offensive lineman has been cleared to play Wednesday. He should start at right guard while Travis Glover provides depth at the position.

headline: Zeitler (triceps) is officially questionable for Wednesday's game against the Rams, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Zeitler missed Green Bay's last game before the team's Week 11 bye due to ankle and triceps injuries, and it looks like his availability for Week 12 is truly up in the air. If he can't go Wednesday, the Packers could end up being perilously thin on the interior of their offensive line, as starter Sean Rhyan (ankle) and key backup Travis Glover (shoulder) are also questionable.

headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said that Zeitler had been in line to start at right guard in Sunday's loss to the Vikings before sustaining a triceps injury in practice Thursday, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Since Zeitler signed a one-year deal Sept. 30, the Packers had been easing him back into game action after he didn't have a proper training camp. He got the chance to play his first extended snaps of the season in the Packers' Week 9 win over the Patriots, and after performing well, Zeitler was primed to draw his first start of the season in Week 10. However, the triceps injury as well as an ankle issue resulted in him sitting out Sunday, prompting the Packers to go with Lucas Glover at right guard. With Glover and the Green Bay offensive line struggling as a whole while the Vikings sacked quarterback Jordan Love eight times in Week 10, Zeitler should get the opportunity to start if he's healthy coming out of the team's Week 11 bye.

headline: Zeitler (ankle/triceps) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Zeitler was initially deemed as questionable due to ankle and triceps injuries, which will ultimately prevent him from playing in Sunday's NFC North tilt. His next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

headline: Zeitler (ankle/triceps) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Zeitler was held out of Friday's practice while tending to ankle and triceps injuries. He signed with the Packers in late September but has not started in any of his four appearances with Green Bay. His absence would weaken the Packers' depth on the offensive line.

headline: Zeitler (ankle/triceps) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
story: Zeitler logged a second consecutive limited practice session Thursday. If he can't suit up in Week 10 against the Vikings, Laken Tomlinson would likely fill the void.

headline: Zeitler is inactive for Week 4's matchup against Tampa Bay.
story: Zeitler was signed this week and is expected to provide some relief for Green Bay's offensive line woes, but he won't make his Packers debut just yet. His next chance to suit up will be a home game Week 5 against Chicago.

headline: The Packers signed Zeitler to a one-year contract Wednesday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: The contract is worth $4.05 million, with a maximum value of $5 million. It's another move the Packers are making to revamp their offensive line, as the team ranks last in the league in rushing yards per game (48.7). It's possible that Zeitler supplants Jacob Monk (quadriceps) for the starting job at right guard for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.

headline: Green Bay conducted a tryout with Zeitler (quadriceps) on Tuesday, Tom Silverstein of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reports.
story: Zeitler finished the 2025 season with the Titans after picking up a quad injury late in the year, but it appears he's now healthy again and back on the free-agent market. The Packers' offensive line has been arguably the worst in the league through the first three weeks of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Glover (shoulder) is active for Wednesday's game against the Rams, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Glover's practice reps were limited due to a shoulder injury, but the third-year pro was given the green light by medical staff to play Wednesday. He's started in five regular-season games, most recently in Week 10 against the Vikings, but he'll likely operate in a depth role at right guard behind starter Kevin Zeitler.

headline: Glover (shoulder) is officially questionable for Wednesday's game against the Rams, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Glover appeared on Green Bay's injury report Monday with a shoulder issue, and it seems like he's truly questionable for Week 12. With starters Sean Rhyan (ankle) and Kevin Zeitler (triceps) also questionable, the Packers might be playing with a makeshift offensive line against a stout Rams defense Wednesday, though if Zeitler is able to go, Glover could shift to a backup role.

headline: Glover (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Glover's practice reps were limited during Week 10 prep due to a knee injury that prevented him from playing against the Patriots in Week 9. The third-year pro was cleared by medical staff to play Sunday, and he should reclaim his starting role at right guard from Laken Tomlinson.

headline: Glover (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Glover didn't play against the Patriots in Week 9 due to a knee injury. He was limited in practice in all three Week 10 sessions, but if he cannot play Sunday, then Laken Tomlinson will likely start at right guard.

headline: Glover (knee) was limited in Thursday's practice.
story: Glover wasn't available for the Week 9 win over the Patriots. Since he has practiced, albeit in a limited capacity, the door is open for a potential return in Sunday's divisional game against Minnesota. If Glover can't get back on the field against the Vikings, Laken Tomlinson could fill the void once again.

headline: Glover (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Patriots, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Glover will miss his fifth game of the season due to a persistent knee injury. The starting right guard will be replaced by Laken Tomlinson for Sunday's contest as the Packers' starting offensive line continues to shift amidst multiple injuries.

headline: Glover (knee) did not practice Thursday.
story: It was a second consecutive DNP for Glover, who didn't play in Week 8 against the Panthers. If he misses another game Sunday versus the Patriots, Laken Tomlinson may be needed to fill in.

headline: Glover (knee) won't play in Green Bay's game versus Carolina on Thursday.
story: Glover is set to miss his fourth game of the season due to a knee injury, leaving the Packers shorthanded along the interior of the offensive line, as Sean Rhyan (ankle) and Jacob Monk (quadriceps) are out as well. In Glover's absence, Kevin Zeitler will likely start at right guard during Thursday's matchup.

headline: Rhyan (ankle) is active for Wednesday's game against the Rams, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Rhyan suffered a high ankle sprain against the Lions in Week 7, which sidelined him for the Packers' following three games. He's been cleared by medical staff to play Wednesday, and Rhyan will reclaim his starting spot at center while John Williams reverts to a depth role.

headline: Rhyan (ankle) is officially questionable for Wednesday's game against the Rams, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Rhyan sat out Green Bay's last three games before the team's Week 11 bye after suffering a high ankle sprain back in Week 7 at Detroit, and now his availability for Week 12 looks like a coin-flip proposition. If he can't suit up Wednesday, 2025 seventh-rounder John Williams may need to make another start at center against the Rams.

headline: Rhyan (ankle) was a limited practice participant Sunday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Rhyan suffered an ankle injury against Detroit in Week 7 and hasn't played since. In fact, he hadn't practiced in any capacity until his limited session Sunday. Rhyan's ability to get in some reps suggests that he's progressing in his recovery, though it remains to be seen if he'll be able to return to action Wednesday versus the Rams.

headline: Rhyan (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Rhyan will miss a third consecutive game due to an ankle injury, and his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Josh Williams is expected to start at center in Rhyan's absence.

headline: Rhyan (ankle) did not practice Thursday.
story: Rhyan has missed the last two games because of an ankle injury. He didn't practice on Wednesday and Thursday, so unless he practices in at least a limited capacity Friday, he likely won't suit up for the Week 10 divisional showdown with the Vikings. If that's the case, John Williams would be in line for another start.

headline: Rhyan (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Patriots, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: John Williams is set to once again suit up at center due to Rhyan's absence. The 26-year-old remains sidelined with an ankle injury, with no return date in sight after yet another week of three consecutive DNPs in practice.

headline: Rhyan (ankle) was absent from practice Thursday.
story: It was a second consecutive absence for Rhyan, who was injured in Week 7 against the Lions and subsequently missed the Week 8 meeting with the Panthers. If he's not on the field Sunday versus the Patriots, John Williams would likely take his spot in the starting lineup once again.

headline: Rhyan (ankle) has been ruled out for Green Bay's matchup versus the Panthers on Thursday.
story: Rhyan's absence doesn't come as a surprise, as it was previously announced that he's expected to be sidelined for a month due to a high ankle sprain suffered during the Week 7 loss to the Lions. In his absence, John Williams is expected to start at center against Carolina.

headline: Rhyan was diagnosed with a high ankle sprain and is expected to miss at least one month, Matt Zenitz of CBSSports.com reports.
story: Rhyan was injured in Sunday's loss to the Lions. To make matters worse, Jacob Monk (quadriceps) landed on injured reserve Monday, meaning the Packers may continue to rely on John Williams, the 2025 No. 250 overall pick, to fill the void at the center position for the foreseeable future.

headline: Rhyan (ankle) is expected to miss multiple weeks after being injured in Sunday's loss to the Lions, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Green Bay is in deep trouble at center. After Rhyan went down against Detroit, replacement Jacob Monk (quadriceps) was unable to finish the game, forcing John Williams into action for his first career offensive snaps after being taken in the seventh round of the 2025 Draft.

headline: Rhyan (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's matchup with the Lions.
story: Rhyan will be forced to miss the rest of Week 7 after sustaining an ankle injury early in the first quarter. With Jacob Monk (quad) also banged up, John Williams has taken over as Green Bay's center versus Detroit.

headline: Rhyan (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Lions.
story: Rhyan suffered an ankle injury on the Packers' first offensive drive of Sunday's game. The center limped off the field and is being further evaluated. John Williams replaced Rhyan at center.

headline: Franklin (shin) is inactive for Wednesday's game against the Rams, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Franklin drew the questionable tag for Wednesday's game following three consecutive limited practices. However, the veteran linebacker will end up missing a fifth consecutive game due to a hairline fracture in his shin that he suffered during a practice session in late October, so Ty'Ron Hopper will continue to operate in an elevated role on defense. Franklin's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Saints on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Franklin (shin) is listed as questionable for Wednesday night's game against the Rams, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Franklin was limited in all three practices leading up to Wednesday night's showdown against the Rams. The questionable tag is positive news for the 30-year-old linebacker, as he's missed the past four games due to a shin injury.

headline: Head coach Matt LaFleur said Monday that Franklin (shin) is progressing well, but the Packers haven't yet determined if he'll play Wednesday versus the Rams, Weston Hodkiewicz of the team's official site reports.
story: Franklin has missed the Packers' last four games due to the shin injury and isn't yet 100 percent healthy coming out of a Week 11 bye. He was listed as a limited participant Monday for a second straight practice and may need to upgrade to full activity Tuesday to avoid taking a designation into Wednesday.

headline: Franklin (shin) was listed as a limited practice participant for Sunday's session, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: A shin injury has prevented Franklin from playing in each of the Packers' last four games. A full practice over the next two days would probably be enough for him to return for Week 12 against the Rams on Wednesday.

headline: Franklin (shin) participated in practice Saturday, Bill Huber of SI.com reports.
story: Franklin has missed four straight games with a fractured shin, but his participation in practice Saturday gives him a chance to play in Wednesday's Thanksgiving Eve game against the Rams. Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper have been manning linebacker for Green Bay.

headline: Franklin (shin) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
story: Franklin did not participate in Week 10 prep due to a shin injury he suffered in Week 6. The inside linebacker will now miss a fourth consecutive game, leaving Isaiah McDuffie to continue as the starter alongside Ty'Ron Hopper.

headline: Franklin (shin) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Franklin was a non-participant throughout the Packers' Week 10 prep, but the linebacker has not yet been officially ruled out ahead of Sunday's divisional contest. If Franklin is inactive come game time, Isaiah McDuffie is in line to take over as the starting inside linebacker opposite Ty'Ron Hopper.

headline: Franklin (shin) did not practice Thursday.
story: Franklin has missed the last three games for the Packers. It appears the 30-year-old won't be back on the field in Week 10 versus the Vikings. If that's the case, Isaiah McDuffie remains in line for more snaps.

headline: Franklin (shin) remained sidelined at practice Thursday, Dominique Yates of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reports.
story: Franklin has yet to resume practicing since sustaining a hairline fracture during Green Bay's Week 6 win over Dallas. He's trending toward a fourth consecutive absence Sunday against the Vikings, with confirmation on that front to come Friday when the Packers release injury designations.

headline: Franklin (shin) did not participate in Wednesday's jog-through practice.
story: Franklin has missed the Packers' last three games while recovering from a hairline fracture in his shin that he suffered in Week 6 against the Cowboys. He hasn't been cleared to practice since sustaining the injury, so unless he can return to on-field action over the next couple of days, Franklin is unlikely to be available for this Sunday's NFC North showdown against the Vikings. Isaiah McDuffie has stepped into a starting role at inside linebacker in Franklin's absence.

headline: Franklin (shin) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Patriots, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Franklin has not practiced since he sustained a hairline fracture to his shin in Week 6. The linebacker will miss yet another game due to the injury, leaving Isaiah McDuffie to start alongside Ty'Ron Hopper at inside linebacker again for Sunday's contest.

headline: Franklin (shin) did not participate in practice Wednesday, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Franklin started the week as a nonparticipant in practice Wednesday and hasn't played since Week 6 after suffering a hairline fracture in his shin. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur added Wednesday that the 30-year-old is making progress in his recovery and he hopes Franklin can return soon. The ninth-year pro has 41 tackles (18 solo), one pass deflection and one forced fumble in six games this season.

headline: Franklin (shin) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Panthers, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Franklin is considered week-to-week due to a hairline fracture in his leg, and the injury will cause him to miss a second consecutive game. Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper will continue to serve as the Packers' starters at inside linebacker in the absence of Franklin, whose next chance to play is Week 9 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Franklin suffered a hairline fracture in his shin during last Thursday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: The veteran linebacker missed Sunday's loss to the Lions and is expected to miss additional time, but coach Matt LaFleur indicated Franklin will not be placed on injured reserve. Isaiah McDuffie and Ty'Ron Hopper will continue to hold down the fort at linebacker for the Packers while Franklin is sidelined.

headline: Franklin (shin) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Lions, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Friday that Franklin injured his shin on a collision during Thursday's practice, and the injury is severe enough for the veteran linebacker to miss his first game of the 2026 season. He's played every defensive snap in five of six games, and that workload will likely fall on Isaiah McDuffie or Nick Niemann for Sunday's NFC North tilt. Franklin's next chance to play is Week 8 against the Panthers on Thursday.

headline: Franklin practiced in a limited capacity Thursday due to a shin injury.
story: Franklin wasn't on the injury report Wednesday, so he may have suffered the injury at some point during practice. Regardless, the 30-year-old linebacker's practice status Friday should shed light on whether he's at risk of missing Sunday's tilt against Detroit. Franklin has played every defensive snap in five of Green Bay's six games so far this season.

headline: Burton (back) is active Week 5 against Chicago.
story: It's a similar story to last week for Burton, who was limited in practice by a back injury but will ultimately be cleared to suit up in what's likely a depth role.

headline: Burton (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bears, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Burton ended Week 5 prep with back-to-back limited practices while working through a back issue. His absence would reduce the Packers' depth at offensive line for Sunday's NFC North tilt.

headline: Burton (back) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: Burton did not practice Wednesday, so his activity Thursday was actually a step in the right direction ahead of Sunday's game versus the Bears. If he can upgrade to full participation at practice Friday, he may still be able to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Burton (groin) is active Week 4 against Tampa Bay.
story: Burton will suit up despite a week of limited practices and will likely be relegated to a depth role in Green Bay's new-look offensive line.

headline: Burton (groin) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Burton appeared on the Packers' injury report Thursday with a groin issue. The reserve center was able to practice through the injury in a limited capacity Thursday and Friday, but his status for Sunday's game is still uncertain.

headline: Jacobs (finger) is listed as inactive Wednesday at the Rams, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
story: Coming out of the Packers' Week 11 bye, head coach Matt LaFleur told Matt Schneidman of The Athletic on Saturday that he didn't expect Jacobs to play in Week 12, but he also gave the running back a "chance to prove" he can. Jacobs then was listed as limited on practice reports Sunday through Tuesday and tagged as questionable ahead of Wednesday's game. Such activity wasn't enough for Jacobs to get the all clear to suit up, meaning Green Bay's backfield will be manned by Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks for a second consecutive contest.

headline: The Packers list Jacobs (finger) as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Rams, Wes Hodkiewicz of the team's official site reports.
story: Coming off a bye week, Jacobs went down as a limited participant in all three of the team's Week 12 practice sessions. While the Packers aren't closing the door on Jacobs suiting up Wednesday, head coach Matt LaFleur previously noted Sunday and Monday that the running back was still viewed as unlikely to play against the Rams. Before making a decision on Jacobs' status prior to Wednesday's 8 p.m. ET kickoff, the Packers could put him through a pregame workout to gauge if his surgically repaired right ring finger presents any issues with gripping or securing the football. If Jacobs is forced to miss a second consecutive game, Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd would be in line to lead the Green Bay rushing attack for another week.

headline: Jacobs (finger) was a limited participant in Monday's practice, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Though Jacobs went down as a limited participant on the second injury report in a row after going through individual drills, head coach Matt LaFleur reiterated prior to Monday's session that the running back is unlikely to play Wednesday versus the Rams. Unless Jacobs takes a notable step forward in his activity during Tuesday's practice that leaves the Packers more optimistic that he'll be ready to play in Los Angeles, Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd appear poised to lead the Green Bay ground game in Week 12.

headline: Jacobs (finger) participated in Monday's practice to some degree but still isn't expected to play Wednesday against the Rams, Bill Huber of SI.com reports.
story: Coach Matt LaFleur previously noted that Jacobs has been doing individual drills just to stay sharp, but after having broken the ring finger on his right hand, the running back's ability to grip/take care of the football is presumably still an issue. In the event that Jacobs is indeed out versus Los Angeles, Kaleb Johnson could end up logging the most carries in Green Bay's Week 12 backfield, with MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks also in the mix for touches.

headline: Coach Matt LaFleur noted Monday that Jacobs (finger) remains unlikely to play in Wednesday's game against the Rams, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Per the report, LaFleur indicated that Jacobs has been doing individual drills just to stay sharp. Barring a change in tone over the next couple of days, it looks like a Dec. 6 return at New Orleans seems like a more realistic possibility for the running back. In the event that Jacobs is ruled out versus Los Angeles, Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks will be called upon to handle Green Bay's backfield duties in Week 12.

headline: Jacobs (finger) was listed as limited at Sunday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN reports.
story: With the Packers playing Wednesday against the Rams, the team posted an official practice report Sunday, and Jacobs was one of nine players deemed limited in the session. While it's encouraging that the running back was able to get some work in Sunday, Wes Hodkiewicz of the team's official site noted earlier Sunday that coach Matt LaFleur indicated Jacobs will "have to show a lot of progress" over the next couple days to be available versus Los Angeles. If Jacobs remains out Wednesday, Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks would be in line to handle Green Bay's backfield duties in his absence.

headline: Jacobs (finger) is practicing Sunday, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Jacobs underwent surgery on a broken right ring finger on Nov. 13, which sidelined him during a Week 10 loss to the Vikings. He now has mixed into drills on back-to-back days, but head coach Matt LaFleur relayed to Wes Hodkiewicz of the team's official site Sunday that Jacobs will "have to show a lot of progress" over the next couple days to be available Wednesday at the Rams. If Jacobs doesn't return in Week 12, Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks will man Green Bay's backfield.

headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said that Jacobs (finger) did some individual work Saturday, but the running back will "have to show a lot of progress" over the next two days to be available Week 12 versus the Rams, Weston Hodkiewicz of the team's official site reports.
story: Based on LaFleur's comments, Jacobs seems like he could be listed as a limited participant when the Packers post their first Week 12 injury report Sunday. However, unless Jacobs mixes into team drills over the next couple of days, he appears to be facing an uphill battle to play in the Packers' next game Wednesday versus the Rams. Jacobs underwent surgery Nov. 13 after fracturing his right ring finger in a Week 9 win over the Patriots and proceeded to sit out last week's loss to the Vikings while recovering from the procedure.

headline: Jacobs (finger) is participating in Saturday's practice session, Bill Huber of SI.com reports.
story: Head coach Matt LaFleur didn't sound optimistic about Jacobs' chances of playing against the Rams on Wednesday, but the veteran running back will "have a chance to prove" that he can suit up for that contest over the next few days at practice, per Matt Schneidman of The Athletic. Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site relayed that Jacobs was spotted at Saturday's practice with a "claw-like cast" on his fingers. In the event that Jacobs doesn't play Wednesday, the Packers would enter the game with a backfield of Kaleb Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks.

headline: Jacobs (finger) isn't expected to play Wednesday against the Rams, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Head coach Matt LaFleur did tell reporters Saturday that Jacobs will "have a chance to prove" that he can suit up Wednesday depending on his practice participation over the coming days. However, it appears Jacobs will be sidelined for a second consecutive game while recovering from a procedure to repair a broken right ring finger, which was an injury that he sustained in Week 9 against the Patriots. If he's ruled out for Week 12, then Kaleb Johnson would be in line to lead a Packers backfield that also includes MarShawn Lloyd and Chris Brooks.

headline: Jacobs (finger) has a "realistic chance" of returning to action Nov. 25 against the Rams following the Packers' Week 11 bye, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Jacobs sustained a fractured right ring finger in the Packers' Nov. 8 win over the Patriots and underwent surgery this past Friday, with the procedure carrying a projected recovery timeline of 2-to-3 weeks. The veteran running back sat out Sunday's 30-10 win over the Vikings, but that could end up being the extent of his absence, as a well-timed Week 11 bye gives him a shot at returning at the short end of his estimated recovery timetable. Kaleb Johnson stepped up as Green Bay's top option out of the backfield while Jacobs has been sidelined for most of the past two games, carrying 24 times for 110 yards and a touchdown between those contests.

headline: Jacobs underwent surgery on his fractured right ring finger Friday and "should be back in the next few weeks," Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
story: Jacobs fractured his finger in last week's victory over the Patriots, and he underwent a procedure Friday to repair it. It's unclear exactly how much time he will miss, but he has been ruled out for Week 10 and has avoided injured reserve for the time being, so reports of him missing 2-to-3 weeks appear accurate. It's unclear exactly how things will shake out in Green Bay's backfield while Jacobs works his way back, but all of MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson, Chris Brooks (ankle) and Pierre Strong are candidates to fill roles.

headline: Jacobs will undergo finger surgery Friday, and the Packers will have a better sense of his recovery timetable afterward, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Jacobs exited Green Bay's Week 9 win over the Patriots after fracturing his ring finger and is in line to be sidelined for Sunday's game against the Vikings. A more precise recovery timeline is expected to be established after Jacobs undergoes surgery on the injured finger Friday, though initial estimates put his likely absence at 2-to-3 weeks on the optimistic side. MarShawn Lloyd, Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong are currently available to handle Green Bay's backfield duties while Jacobs is sidelined, plus Chris Brooks (ankle) is a candidate to return from IR as soon as this weekend.

headline: Jacobs will undergo surgery on his broken right ring finger later this week and could be cleared to play in as soon as 2-to-3 weeks, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Jacobs will be sidelined for Sunday's game against the Vikings, but with the Packers on bye in Week 11, the running back has a shot at returning to action as soon as Week 12 versus the Rams on Nov. 25. The Packers will wait for Jacobs' surgery to be completed before deciding Saturday whether he'll require a stint on injured reserve -- and the automatic four-game absence that comes with it -- or if he'll remain on the 53-man roster. For however long Jacobs ends up being sidelined, the Packers are likely to lean on Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd (knee) as their top options on the ground.

headline: When asked if IR is a possibility for Jacobs (finger), coach Matt LaFleur said Monday, "I think everything is a possibility," Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, LaFleur confirmed Monday that Jacobs will undergo surgery on his fractured ring finger. As a result of the looming procedure, Pelissero adds that that the running back is out indefinitely, which supports the notion that an IR stint for Jacobs could be on the table. Given that MarShawn Lloyd is dealing with a knee injury that sidelined him Sunday, Kaleb Johnson is Green Bay's top healthy back at the moment, with Pierre Strong also on hand. However, it's possible help is on the way, and outside reinforcements may not be needed, according to Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com, as Chris Brooks (ankle) could be nearing a return from IR.

headline: Jacobs is in line to undergo surgery on his injured finger this week and is expected to miss a maximum of three weeks, according to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports.
story: The Packers may provide further clarification, but it looks like the team will be without its top running back this weekend against the Vikings, at a minimum. With MarShawn Lloyd dealing with a knee injury that sidelined him in Week 9, Kaleb Johnson profiles as Green Bay's top healthy back, with Pierre Strong also in the mix.

headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged after Sunday's 45-27 win over the Patriots that Jacobs' (finger) availability for the team's Week 10 matchup with the Vikings is uncertain, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports. "Hopefully we can do something to allow him to go out there," LaFleur said of Jacobs. "But he was just having a hard time gripping the ball."
story: Jacobs was limited to just 10 snaps before leaving Sunday's game in the first quarter after fracturing his right ring finger while attempting to stiff-arm a defender at the end of his fourth and final carry of the day. He made two trips to the locker room with the hope of adding enough protection to his hand to enable him to return to the game, but the Packers ultimately determined that Jacobs wouldn't have been able to securely grip the football if he had checked back in. With MarShawn Lloyd (knee) inactive against the Patriots and Jacobs leaving early, Kaleb Johnson (14 carries for 68 yards) ended up finishing as the Packers' rushing leader on the day.

headline: Jacobs fractured his finger during Sunday's 45-27 win over the Patriots, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Head coach Matt LaFleur revealed the nature of Jacobs' injury after the game. Jacobs exited the win with what was initially deemed a hand injury. He was unable to return against the Patriots, but the Packers are hoping Jacobs will be available for Week 10 against the Vikings. If Jacobs can't go, Pierre Strong, Kaleb Johnson and possibly MarShawn Lloyd (knee) would be Green Bay's backfield options.

headline: Jacobs (hand) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Prior to hurting his hand, Jacobs had carried four times for five yards in the contest. Given that MarShawn Lloyd (knee) is inactive Sunday, Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson are currently Green Bay's RB options against New England.

headline: Jacobs doesn't anticipate missing any additional game action due to the release of additional allegations of physical and verbal abuse against him, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: "With all the evidence that we have and that they have at this point, it's not one of those things where I'm sitting back on my hands like, 'OK, am I going to play this week?'" Jacobs said. "I'm not worried about feeling like I'm going to miss any more time than I already have." Jacobs spent the first six weeks of the season on the Commissioner's Exempt List. Those six absences would count toward any suspension the NFL hands down to Jacobs in connection with the league's investigation into his possible violations of the league's personal conduct policy.

headline: Head coach Matt LaFleur said Monday that the Packers are aware of the prior physical abuse allegations involving Jacobs that recently surfaced and "anticipate him being a member" of the team moving forward, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports.
story: Before making his season debut Week 7, Jacobs missed the Packers' first six games after he was placed on the commissioner's exempt list after he was officially charged Aug. 27 with two misdemeanors stemming from his May arrest for a domestic incident. The legal process related to that incident has since played out, but Jacobs' status with the team had been called into question after the NFL announced Saturday that it was reviewing additional allegations of physical and verbal abuse from three different women in incidents dating back to April 2021 that were released following a public records request. Unless the NFL elects to place him back on the exempt list while it reviews the incidents in question, Jacobs looks like he'll be available for Green Bay's next game Sunday at New England. Despite the missed time to begin the season, Jacobs has immediately settled back into a lead role in the backfield and has scored three touchdowns in two games, but he's mustered just 75 yards on 32 carries (2.3 average) to go with 11 receptions for 68 yards on 13 targets.

headline: "Newly released records," according to NBC 26, "show additional women contacted the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department to report alleged physical incidents involving Jacobs."
story: Per the initial report, "The accounts surfaced during the department's investigation into a May 23 incident at Jacobs' home," and according to the Associated Press "were included in evidence regarding Jacobs' battery case," which he ultimately pleaded no contest to. The follow-up report notes that the NFL will "review these allegations as part of its investigation, which has remained open."

headline: Jacobs rushed 21 times for 39 yards and a touchdown and brought in all six targets for 13 yards and another score in the Packers' 27-19 win over the Panthers on Thursday.
story: Jacobs saw a sizable increase in workload after making his Week 7 season debut just four days earlier, and although he couldn't crack the code of what had been a vulnerable Panthers run defense, he still put together a useful fantasy performance thanks to the pair of scores. The veteran back first went into the end zone on a one-yard run that capped off a nine-play, 90-yard march in the second quarter, and he added his four-yard touchdown grab midway through the third. Jacobs looks fully prepared to remain in a workhorse role moving forward, and he'll next take aim at the Patriots' talented front seven in a Week 9 road showdown on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Jacobs rushed 11 times for 36 yards and hauled in five of seven targets for 55 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 20-17 loss at Detroit.
story: After missing the first six games of the season while on the commissioner's exempt list, Jacobs claimed the lion's share of the Packers' backfield touches, with MarShawn Lloyd handling the other eight (for 35 total yards). Meanwhile, an active Pierre Strong didn't get a touch, and Kaleb Johnson was inactive as a healthy scratch. Running room continued to be difficult to find for Green Bay's RBs, with the team overall averaging just 3.2 YPC on Sunday. Jacobs likely will hold on to a majority share of the reps among the group moving forward, with the team next set to host the Panthers on Thursday night.

headline: Jacobs is active for Sunday's game against the Lions.
story: After being removed from the Commissioner's Exempt list Monday, Jacobs rejoined the Packers for practice Wednesday. Jacobs proceeded to practice without any restrictions throughout the week, prompting Green Bay to clear him for his season debut Sunday. Though Jacobs will draw the start out of the backfield in Detroit, the Packers may not hand him his normal workload right away and could decide on the extent of his role as the game unfolds, per Jay Glazer of Fox Sports. Even if he doesn't end up serving as a three-down workhorse in Week 7, Jacobs should eventually settle back into that role in the weeks to come, after Green Bay struggled mightily to generate production from its other running backs in the first six games of the season.

headline: Jacobs is active for Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Lions.
story: Jacobs was removed from the Commissioner's Exempt List on Monday after sitting out the first six games of the season, and the veteran running back proceeded to participate in all Week 7 prep without limitations. Reports earlier Sunday indicated Jacobs' workload will likely be watched closely as the game unfolds; however, the fact he was able to continue participating in individualized conditioning work at the team facility throughout the time he was on the CEL should leave Jacobs prepared to handle some solid volume in his first game action since the wild-card loss to the Bears in January.

headline: Jacobs is expected to start in his season debut Sunday against the Lions, but the extent of his role is likely to be decided upon as the game unfolds, according to Jay Glazer of Fox Sports.
story: While he spent the first six weeks of the season on the commissioner's exempt list, Jacobs was still allowed at the Green Bay facility and was able to stay on top of his conditioning, but he wasn't cleared to resume practicing with the team until Wednesday. After a full week of drills, the Packers were comfortable enough with activating Jacobs for Sunday, but the team plans to "keep an eye on him" and may not be ready to hand him his normal workload right off the bat. In the weeks to come, Jacobs shouldn't have much trouble reclaiming a three-down workhorse role, given the struggles of Green Bay's other running backs in generating production over the first six games of the season.

headline: Jacobs had his roster exemption removed by the Packers and is expected to play Sunday at Detroit, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: After missing the first six games of the season while on the commissioner's exempt list, Jacobs is now in line for his 2026 debut following a full week of drills. It remains to be seen what kind of workload he'll be able to handle off the bat, but he at least appears as if he'll be in the mix for RB reps along with MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson on Sunday.

headline: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Jacobs is on track to play Sunday against the Lions, Rob Demovsky of ESPN reports.
story: Jacobs was removed from the exempt list Monday, and all signs point to the veteran running back making his 2026 season debut against Detroit. Green Bay's backfield production has been abysmal through six weeks, so Jacobs' return can only help the situation. Jordan Love's incredible pass volume could also take a hit with Jacobs returning to the lineup.

headline: Jacobs took part in practice Thursday, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Jacobs was removed from the commissioner's exempt list Monday, and while the Packers held a walkthrough Wednesday, it wasn't open to the media, so his activity Thursday marks his first visible on-field work since training camp. It remains unclear if Green Bay will clear him to play Sunday at Detroit, but the team has a roster exemption at its disposal that lasts until Monday, Oct. 26, which allows it flexibility if Jacobs isn't deemed ready to make his season debut this weekend.

headline: Jacobs remains uncertain to play Sunday at Detroit, with head coach Matt LaFleur saying, "We'll see. We'll work through it," Rob Demovsky of ESPN reports.
story: Despite Jacobs being removed from the commissioner's exempt list Monday, the Packers have a one-game roster exemption for the running back that expires Monday, Oct. 26. As such, Jacobs currently doesn't count against Green Bay's active roster, and the team won't have to officially include him among its Week 7 inactives if the exemption still stands as of Sunday. In the event Jacobs doesn't play this weekend, MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson will be the options out of the Packers backfield.

headline: Jacobs (personal) has officially been removed from the Commissioner's Exempt List, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: As expected, Jacobs is off the list and eligible to practice. Head coach Matt LaFleur told Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site Monday that Jacobs is expected to take on a full week of drills, but the team hasn't determined if the running back will make his season debut this coming Sunday at Detroit. It should be noted that Green Bay has been granted a one-game exemption for Jacobs that expires next Monday, Oct. 26, per the NFL's transaction log, meaning he currently doesn't count against the active roster. If Jacobs doesn't play in Week 7, MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson will continue to handle the Packers backfield.

headline: Head coach Matt LaFleur said that Jacobs (personal) will get in a full week of practice, but the Packers have yet to determine whether he'll be able to make his season debut Sunday in Detroit, Weston Hodkiewicz of the team's official site reports. "We feel he's in a pretty good spot," LaFleur said. "He's been training but he's missed the exposure to football."
story: Jacobs will practice with the Packers for the first time since the preseason Wednesday, after he was scheduled to be removed from the commissioner's exempt list Monday. Though he was able to work out at the Packers' team facility over the past two months while his playing status was in limbo due to the ongoing legal saga related to his May arrest in a domestic incident, Jacobs may need more than a full week of practice for the team to feel comfortable having him play in games. Whenever Jacobs is deemed ready to suit up, his addition will provide a boost to a Green Bay running game that ranks last in the NFL by a wide margin with an average of 59.8 yards per contest through six weeks.

headline: Jacobs (personal) will be removed from the Commissioner's Exempt List on Monday and be eligible to play as soon as the Packers' Week 7 game at Detroit, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
story: Jacobs' playing status has been in limbo since his May arrest following a domestic incident that led to the running back pleading no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property in early September. He since has missed the first five games of the season and will miss a sixth contest Sunday, and while he'll be able to practice next week and make his 2026 debut on Sunday, Oct. 25, the NFL will keep its investigation of Jacobs open, reserving the right to add further discipline if new information comes to light, per Adam Schefter of ESPN.

headline: Jacobs filed a civil suit Wednesday seeking a permanent injunction restricting access to records pertaining to his May 23 altercation with a woman at his home, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: After being arrested following the domestic incident, Jacobs appeared in court Sept. 10 and pleaded no contest to charges of battery and criminal destruction of property. He was ultimately convicted of battery and fined $1,000, while agreeing to a deferred judgment agreement on a charge of damage to property. Later that month, a judge lifted a temporary seal of the records pertaining to the case and turned the decision whether to release part or all of the records over to the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department. Jacobs has appealed the release of those records, which could further delay the NFL's efforts to wrap up its investigation into the running back and levy a potential suspension. So long as the NFL's investigation is ongoing, Jacobs will remain on the commissioner's exempt list.

headline: Parsons (knee) is active for Wednesday's game at the Rams, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports.
