story: Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Monday that Parsons gained clearance to return to action, but first the Packers needed to activate him from the reserve/PUP list, which came to pass Tuesday. Parsons was listed as questionable ahead of Wednesday's matchup, and he's now ready for his first game since Dec. 14, 2025, when he tore the ACL and meniscus in his left knee. Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported Wednesday that Parsons will play approximately 50 percent of the defensive snaps in his season debut.

headline: The Packers reinstated Parsons (knee) from the PUP list on Tuesday.
story: Parsons remains listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Rams, but he's fully expected to play in Week 12 in what will mark his 2026 debut. The five-time Pro Bowler will be making his first appearance since tearing the ACL and meniscus in his left knee Dec. 14, 2025 and requiring season-ending surgery. Parsons has worked exclusively as a limited participant in practice since being designated for return from the PUP list Nov. 4, so the Packers could monitor his snaps closely in his first game action in more than 11 months.

headline: Parsons (knee) is officially listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Rams, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Though he remains on the PUP list, Parsons looks on track to be activated by the 4 p.m. ET deadline Wednesday for the Packers to make Week 12 roster moves. Per Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com and Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Parsons received final clearance Monday from his surgeon, Dr. Neal ElAttrache, to make his 2026 debut in what will mark the star edge rusher's first NFL action since he tore the ACL in his left knee Dec. 14, 2025. Given that he hasn't been listed as anything more than a limited participant in practice since being designated for return from the PUP list back on Nov. 4, Parsons could be operating with some playing-time restrictions in his first game in just over 11 months.

headline: Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Monday that Parsons (knee) has received clearance to return to action Wednesday at the Rams.
story: Parsons remains on the reserve/PUP list and continued to be listed as a limited participant on injury reports as of Monday, but per Rapoport the pass rusher is closing in on his first game action since Dec. 14, 2025, when he tore the ACL and meniscus in his left knee. Assuming he's activated by Wednesday afternoon and gains active status that evening, he at least will be a part of the Packers' pass-rush rotation, but the team may ease him back in considering the severity of last year's injury.

headline: Parsons (knee) remained a limited practice participant Monday, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Parsons has yet to turn in a full practice since being designated for return from the reserve/PUP list Nov. 4, but the Packers seemingly haven't closed the door on him making his season debut Wednesday versus the Rams. According to Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com, Parsons said that he's still awaiting final clearance for game action from his surgeon, Dr. Neal ElAttrache, whom he's scheduled to meet with in the next day or two. If Parsons gets the green light to play in Week 12, he could have his snap count managed to some extent.

headline: Parsons (knee) practiced in a limited capacity Sunday, Rob Demovsky of ESPN reports.
story: For a third week in a row, Parsons has maintained limited listings on Packers injury reports as he strives for his first game action since Dec. 14, 2025, when he tore the ACL in his left knee. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported earlier Sunday that Parsons is "on track" to return to action Wednesday versus the Rams, but first Green Bay will need to activate him from the reserve/PUP list for him to have a chance to do so.

headline: Parsons (knee) is "on track" to return from the PUP list to make his season debut Wednesday against the Rams, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Since Green Bay opened his 21-day practice window Nov. 4, the Week 12 matchup with the Rams always looked to be the target date for Parsons' debut. The star pass rusher has gradually increased the intensity of his practice activity over the past two and a half weeks, and he appears to have thus far avoided any setbacks with his surgically repaired knee. Assuming all goes swimmingly for Parsons during the Packers' three Week 12 practices, he should be formally activated in the hours leading up to Wednesday's contest.

headline: Parsons (knee) participated in the Packers' unofficial practice session Saturday, Bill Huber of SI.com reports.
story: Green Bay is on bye in Week 11, but Parsons was able to get in another on-field workout as he gears up for a likely return from the PUP list ahead of Wednesday's game against the Rams. He's expected to be listed as a full participant for each of Green Bay's three Week 12 practices before being formally activated Wednesday.

headline: Parsons (knee) is expected to participate in all three practice sessions during Week 12 prep ahead of Wednesday's game against the Rams, Tom Silverstein of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel reports.
story: Parsons is in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL in his left knee that he sustained in December of 2025. He's been limited in practice since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 4, and a full session over the coming days should be enough for Parsons to make his 2026 debut. He will likely operate under a snap count once he's cleared to return, but his availability would also impact the workload of both Lukas Van Ness and Barryn Sorrell.

headline: Head coach Matt LaFleur acknowledged that Parsons (knee/illness) could be ready to make his season debut following the Packers' Week 11 bye, but he still has "a couple more hurdles" to clear before being deemed ready to play, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports.
story: Since opening Parsons' 21-day practice window Nov. 4, the Packers have seemingly targeted their Nov. 25 matchup with the Rams in Week 12 for the star pass rusher's 2026 debut. That plan doesn't appear to have changed while Parsons has been a limited participant in practice for the past two weeks, but he'll likely need to start practicing in full during Week 12 prep before the Packers give him the green light to play. If Parsons does in fact gain clearance to play against the Rams, he could be operating with a restricted snap count in what would mark his first game action since tearing his left ACL on Dec. 14, 2025.

headline: Parsons (knee/illness) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Parsons now has put together back-to-back weeks of limited sessions as he inches closer to his first game action since Dec. 14, 2025, when he tore the ACL in his left knee. With a Week 11 bye on tap, he'll have a bit more time to get healthy before the Packers' Week 12 road matchup with the Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25, which coincides with his 21-day practice window coming to a close.

headline: Parsons (knee/illness) practiced on a limited basis Thursday.
story: Despite dealing with an illness Wednesday, Parsons was able to go down as a limited participant in the ensuing jog-through, and he maintained that activity level one day later. He's seeking his first game action since Dec. 14, 2025, when he suffered a torn ACL in his left knee, and he so far has completed nearly two weeks of capped sessions since he was designated for return from the reserve/PUP list last Wednesday. Friday's injury report will reveal if Parsons has a chance to play Sunday against the Vikings, but more realistically the Packers likely are eyeing a road matchup with the Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25 for his season debut.

headline: Parsons (knee/illness) officially was limited at Wednesday's jog-through.
story: Prior to Wednesday's session, head coach Matt LaFleur told Ryan Wood of USA Today that Parsons wasn't slated to participate Wednesday due to an illness, but he instead did enough to avoid a DNP listing. On top of that, Parsons is expected to return to team drills later this week, so it'll be interesting to see if he goes down as a full participant Thursday and/or Friday. The Packers are exactly one week into a 21-day window in which to evaluate Parsons and activate him from IR, so the team likely will continue to exercise caution with his return to action.

headline: Parsons (knee) won't practice Wednesday due to an illness, but head coach Matt LaFleur said the pass rusher is expected to mix into team drills this week, Ryan Wood of USA Today reports.
story: This marks Parsons' second week of work since the Packers designated him for return from the reserve/PUP list last Wednesday. While an illness will delay his initial practice reps of this week, his potential return to team drills Thursday and/or Friday may mean a full listing is possible this time around. In any case, Friday's injury report will reveal if Parsons has a chance to play Sunday against the Vikings.

headline: Parsons (knee) officially was ruled out for Sunday's contest in New England.
story: After the Packers designated Parsons for return from injured reserve Wednesday, he logged three straight limited sessions as he ramps up for his first game action since Dec. 14, 2025 in Denver, when he tore the ACL in his left knee. Parsons himself told Ryan Wood of USA Today that he won't "pinpoint a day" for his return, but his 21-day window conveniently ends on Wednesday, Nov. 25, when the Packers take on the Rams in Los Angeles.

headline: Parsons (knee) practiced in a limited fashion Wednesday.
story: Head coach Matt LaFleur told Matt Schneidman of The Athletic earlier Wednesday that Parsons will participate in individual drills in his return to practice. Before that could go down, though, the Packers designated him for return from the reserve/PUP list, per the NFL's transaction log. According to Ryan Wood of USA Today, Parson declined to "pinpoint a day" for his first game action since Dec. 14, 2025 at Denver, but Green Bay now has a 21-day window in which to evaluate him and determine when that'll occur.

headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said that Parsons (knee) will be designated for return from the reserve/PUP list and will take part in individual work during Wednesday's practice, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Parsons will take part in practice for the first time in nearly 11 months, after a lengthy recovery from surgery to repair the ACL in his left knee, which he tore in a Dec. 14, 2025 game against the Broncos. Though LaFleur confirmed that Parsons has been cleared for full activity, the Packers are expected to limit the star edge rusher to individual work throughout Week 9. Parsons is then expected to advance to team work in Week 10, and if his knee continues to respond well to practice coming out of a Week 11 bye, he'll likely be activated from the PUP list to make his 2026 debut Nov. 25 versus the Rams.

headline: Head coach Matt LaFleur said Monday that the Packers' "intention" is for Parsons (knee) to resume practicing in Week 9, Weston Hodkiewicz of the team's official site reports. "It's gonna be a process trying to get him back," LaFleur said. "We're hopeful he'll be able to get out there sometime this week."
story: Once the Packers officially designate Parsons for return from the PUP list, the team will have 21 days to evaluate him in practice before reinstating him to the 53-man roster. Parsons, who is working his way back from the torn ACL he sustained last December, doesn't appear to be in consideration to play this Sunday against the Patriots if he resumes practicing this week. Instead, the Packers are targeting their Nov. 25 game against the Rams in Week 12 for Parsons' debut, per Ian Rapoport of ESPN. The star edge rusher is initially expected to be limited to individual work once the Packers open his 21-day window before potentially advancing to team drills in Week 10.

headline: Parsons (knee) and the Packers are targeting a return for Week 12 against the Rams on Wednesday, Nov. 25, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN reports.
story: Parsons remains on the reserve/PUP list while recovering from a torn ACL that he sustained in December of 2025. Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reported Wednesday that Parsons has a chance to participate during Week 9 prep, but he would likely have to string together consecutive full practices in order to be removed from the Packers' PUP list. Lukas Van Ness and Barryn Sorrell will continue to operate as Green Bay's primary edge rushers while Parsons is on the mend.

headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Tuesday that Parsons (knee) has "a chance" to resume practicing next week, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Parsons has spent all season on the PUP list while he continues to recover from the torn ACL he sustained Dec. 14, 2025. Though the Packers haven't relayed that Parsons has experienced any setbacks in his rehab, the team has taken a deliberate approach with easing him back on to the field. After a Thursday game against the Panthers, the Packers will benefit from an extended break leading up to their Week 9 matchup with the Patriots on Nov. 8, which could represent a good opportunity for the team to open Parsons' 21-day evaluation window. Even if Parsons begins practicing next week, he'll still likely face an uphill battle to suit up against New England.

headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said that Parsons (knee) won't practice in Week 7, Weston Hodkiewicz of the team's official site reports. "He has to clear some hurdles yet before we get to that point," LaFleur said.
story: With Green Bay not yet ready to open Parsons' 21-day practice window this week, the star edge rusher can safely be ruled out from making his 2026 debut Sunday in Detroit. LaFleur isn't dismissing the possibility of Parsons playing Week 8 versus the Panthers, though because that game will be a Thursday night matchup, the five-time Pro Bowler may face an uphill battle to gain clearance. At this point, the Packers' Week 9 matchup with the Patriots on Nov. 8 looks to be a more realistic target for Parsons to make his return to action, after his 2025 season came to an end when he tore his ACL on Dec. 14.

headline: The Packers aren't planning on opening Parsons' (knee) 21-day practice window this week ahead of Sunday's game against the Cowboys, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Parsons had previously noted in the early stages of training camp that the Week 6 matchup with his former team was a realistic target for his season debut. The 27-year-old ultimately won't be ready to play against Dallas, and while the Packers remain hopeful he'll be able to return to action at some point in October, his absence looks increasingly likely to stretch into November since he has yet to resume practicing with the team. Green Bay hasn't indicated that Parsons has experienced any setbacks from the torn ACL in his left knee that he sustained Dec. 14, as the team may simply be taking a deliberate approach with the star pass rusher's recovery.

headline: Parsons (knee), per head coach Matt LaFleur, will not practice this week, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: With four weeks in the books, Parsons now is eligible to be activated from the reserve/PUP list, but with him not yet ready to practice he will not return to action in Week 5 against the Bears, and it may be tough for him to make it back for Green Bay's Week 6 matchup against his former Dallas team.

headline: McDuffie registered 10 tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery during the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots in Week 9.
story: McDuffie's first tackle of the game was a nine-yard sack on Drake Maye early in the first quarter, which led to the Patriots punting the ball away on the next play. McDuffie also recovered the fumble he forced late in the third quarter, which the Packers offense turned into a 37-yard touchdown pass from Jordan Love to Christian Watson one play later. McDuffie has racked up double-digit stops in three consecutive games, and he's been the starting inside linebacker in each of those contests due to the absence of Zaire Franklin (shin). McDuffie should hang onto his starting role against the Vikings on Sunday assuming Franklin is ruled out for that game.

headline: McDuffie finished last Thursday's 27-19 win over Carolina with 10 tackles (three solo).
story: McDuffie tied with Evan Williams for the team lead in tackles. He played every one of the Packers' defensive snaps for the second straight game in the absence of Zaire Franklin (shin). McDuffie has tallied 21 tackles in the pair of contests, so he's looking like a strong IDP option, at least for as long as Franklin remains sidelined.

headline: McDuffie logged 11 tackles (six solo), one fumble and one fumble recovery during the Packers' 20-17 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
story: McDuffie was operating in an elevated role defensively due to the absence of veteran linebacker Zaire Franklin (shin). McDuffie answered the call by playing every single defensive snap while leading the Packers in tackles. He was credited with forcing the ball out of Jahmyr Gibbs' hands late in the second quarter, although it appeared as though it was the hand of Lions center Cade Mays that caused the fumble. However, McDuffie did land on the loose ball caused by a botched snap from Mays to Jared Goff early in the third, which the Packers' offense capitalized on with a five-play drive that ended with a 25-yard touchdown pass from Jordan Love to Josh Jacobs. Franklin was diagnosed with a hairline fracture in his shin, so McDuffie figures to be remain a starter on defense in the short term, with the Packers hosting the Panthers on Thursday.

headline: Cisse (ribs) practiced fully Monday.
story: The Packers' rookie cornerback is ready to go for Wednesday's game against the Rams after he exited Week 10 early against the Vikings. Cisse has started all 10 games this season, recording 38 tackles (26 solo), including 1.5 sacks, and nine pass breakups, including an interception, on 83 percent of the defensive snaps.

headline: Cisse (ribs) was a limited participant in Sunday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Cisse is working through a rib injury that he picked up during the Packers' Week 10 loss to the Vikings. If he can log a full session over the next two days, then he would be on track to play against the Rams on Wednesday.

headline: Cisse (ribs) practiced Saturday, Bill Huber of SI.com reports.
story: Cisse was forced out of last Sunday's loss to the Vikings, but his injury isn't considered serious, and it sounds like the cornerback will be ready to go for Wednesday's game against the Rams.

headline: Cisse (ribs) is "fine" after exiting the Packers' Week 10 loss to the Vikings early, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Cisse did not return to Sunday's contest after exiting the game during the first quarter with a rib injury. Coach Matt LaFleur says the cornerback is "fine," and it appears Cisse will return to practice after the Packers' Week 11 bye.

headline: Cisse (ribs) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Vikings.
story: Cisse picked up the injury during the first quarter, and he's being checked on by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. Carrington Valentine, Kamal Hadden and Benjamin St-Juste are candidates for more defensive snaps while Cisse is being evaluated in the locker room.

headline: Cisse (shoulder) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Lions, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Cisse logged three consecutive limited practice sessions during Week 7 prep. Despite not logging a full session, Cisse managed to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's contest. The cornerback is all set to suit up at outside cornerback opposite Keisean Nixon for the divisional showdown with the Lions.

headline: Cisse (shoulder) was a limited participant in Wednesday's walkthrough session, Matt Schneidman of The Athletic reports.
story: Cisse suffered a stinger during the Packers' Week 6 win over the Cowboys, but he expressed optimism Tuesday that he'll be available for this Sunday's road tilt against the Lions, per Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site. Cisse has now been tagged with a shoulder injury, and he'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation to avoid an injury designation ahead of Week 7.

headline: Cisse, who suffered a stinger during Sunday night's win over the Cowboys, indicated Tuesday that he's fine as this weekend's contest against the Lions approaches, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Prior to his exit from the contest, Cisse played 54 of a possible 78 snaps on defense, en route to recording four tackles and a pick. Assuming no setbacks, the 2026 second-rounder is in line to occupy a starting cornerback slot this weekend opposite Keisean Nixon.

headline: Cisse (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday night's contest against Dallas.
story: Cisse suffered a stinger late in the second half and his availability for the final stretch of the contest is now unclear. In his absence, Carrington Valentine will operate in a more prominent role at cornerback during Sunday Night Football.

headline: Cisse (hip) is active for Sunday night's game against the Cowboys.
story: Cisse had been listed as questionable after popping up on the injury report Friday. The second-round rookie cornerback has started all five games this season, registering 21 tackles (16 solo), including 1.5 sacks, and a pair of pass breakups.

headline: Cisse (hip) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys, Wes Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Cisse popped up on Friday's injury report as a limited participant due to a hip injury. His status could change over the weekend, but whether he'll play Sunday may not be officially known until the Packers announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff. Carrington Valentine would likely start opposite Keisean Nixon at outside cornerback if Cisse is not cleared to play.

headline: Cisse (neck) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Cisse suffered a neck injury during the Packers' Week 4 win over the Buccaneers. The cornerback cleared an independent concussion check and was believed to have suffered a short-term issue. Cisse is now back to full participation and appears set to continue preparing for Sunday's divisional showdown with the Bears.

headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said that Cisse isn't in the concussion protocol but is tending to what is believed to be a short-term neck injury coming out of Sunday's 17-14 win over the Buccaneers, Weston Hodkiewicz of the team's official site reports.
story: The rookie cornerback tallied six tackles before making a late departure from Sunday's game due to the neck injury and to get checked for a concussion. Fortunately for Cisse, he doesn't appear to be dealing with a significant issue, though he's not yet in the clear for the Packers' Week 5 game against the Bears. He may need to practice fully by Friday to avoid carrying a designation into the weekend.

headline: Cisse suffered a neck injury and was also evaluated for a concussion in Sunday's 17-14 win over the Buccaneers, Zach Jacobson of the team's official site reports. He finished with six total tackles (five solo).
story: The Packers defense took a beating Sunday, with Cisse exiting the contest due to multiple injuries. The 2026 No. 52 overall pick could carry an injury designation ahead of the NFC North clash with the Bears in Week 5, assuming he's not ruled out altogether before then. If Cisse can't suit up for that one, Carrington Valentine could continue to see more snaps.

headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Saturday that he doesn't anticipate Musgrove (neck) returning from the PUP list this season, according to NFL reporter Jason B. Hirschhorn.
story: LaFleur acknowledged that Musgrove is still in the process of rehabbing the neck injury he sustained during OTAs in June, and the Packers haven't yet prepared for the tight end to resume practicing. Barring dramatic progress in his recovery over the next month, Musgrave looks like he'll be sidelined for the final season of his rookie deal before hitting free agency in the spring.

headline: Packers head coach Matt Lafleur said Thursday it's "tough to say" whether Musgrave (neck) plays this season, Weston Hodkiewicz of the Packers' official site reports.
story: Musgrave has yet to return to the Packers since being placed on the PUP list prior to Week 1 of the regular season, and until the 26-year-old proves otherwise, he will likely continue to sit out. Tucker Kraft and Jonnu Smith will continue leading the charge at the tight end position.

headline: Williams logged eight tackles (two solo) and a pass defense during the Packers' 30-10 loss to the Vikings in Week 10.
story: Williams played every single defensive snap in Week 10 and finished tied for the second-most tackles on the Packers behind Isaiah McDuffie (10). Williams has recorded at least eight stops in three of his last four outings and is up to 84 tackles (50 solo), including 1.0 sacks, eight pass defenses (including three interceptions) and a fumble recovery through 10 regular-season games. He is well on track to surpass 100 tackles for a second consecutive year.

headline: Williams logged five tackles (four solo) and one interception during the Packers' 45-27 win over the Patriots in Week 9.
story: Brandon Cisse broke up a deep pass from Drake Maye to Kyle Williams early in the second quarter, and Williams was able to make a toe-tapping grab for the takeaway. Williams is up to three interceptions on the year, which ties his career high that he set across 16 regular-season games in 2025. The third-year defensive back is up to 76 tackles (48 solo), including 1.0 sacks, seven pass defenses and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

headline: Williams recorded 10 total tackles (seven solo) during Thursday night's 27-19 win over the Panthers.
story: Williams finished tied for the team lead in takedowns with linebacker Isaiah McDuffie, notching double-digit stops for the fourth time this season. The safety has now compiled 71 total tackles (44 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding six passes defensed, two of which are interceptions, and a fumble recovery over the first eight games of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Williams finished Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Lions with nine tackles (five solo) and one pass defense.
story: As he's done in each of the first six games of the regular season, Williams was on the field for every single defensive snap Sunday, and he finished third on the Packers in tackles behind Isaiah McDuffie (11) and Xavier McKinney (10). Williams has posted at least nine tackles four times this season, and his 61 total tackles lead the Packers and is tied with Jacob Rodriguez and Payton Wilson for eighth-most in the NFL .

headline: Williams recorded six total tackles (five solo) and an interception during Sunday night's 23-13 win over the Cowboys.
story: Williams has yet to miss a defensive snap this season, and his biggest moment in Week 6 came in the second quarter when he jumped in front of a pass from Dak Prescott for his second interception of the year. The safety has now compiled 52 total tackles (32 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding five passes defensed, two of which are interceptions, and a fumble recovery over six games so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Williams (illness) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
story: Williams popped up on Green Bay's injury report with an illness Wednesday, but it looks like he's now over it as Sunday's game versus the Cowboys approaches. He's likely in line for a busy night at safety in Week 6 against a pass-happy Dallas offense.

headline: Williams (illness) was a limited participant at the Packers' practice Wednesday.
story: Williams is dealing with an illness to open the week, and he was unable to be a full participant at practice as a result. The safety will have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday night's matchup with the Cowboys.

headline: Williams finished Sunday's 17-14 win over the Buccaneers with seven tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two pass defenses (including one interception).
story: Williams picked off undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels midway through the first quarter, and the Packers offense made the most of the takeaway with a 16-play, 68-yard drive that ended with a two-yard touchdown pass from Jordan Love to Matthew Golden. Williams has played every single defensive snap for the Packers, accumulating 34 tackles (20 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and four pass defenses (one interception) through four regular-season games.

headline: Teller (back) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Teller didn't play against the Colts in Week 11 due to a back injury, but he's been cleared by medical staff to play in Sunday's contest. He could start at left guard for the Texans in the absence of Keylan Rutledge (neck).

headline: Teller (back) is inactive for Thursday's game versus the Colts.
story: Teller was unavailable in Week 10 against the Browns due to an illness, and he'll be sidelined in Week 11 by a back injury. In his absence, rookie fourth-rounder Febechi Nwaiwu projects as the Texans' top option off the bench at guard.

headline: Teller (illness) was a full participant in Monday's walkthrough practice.
story: Teller was unable to suit up for Sunday's loss to the Browns due to an illness. The reserve right guard's estimated participation in Monday's walkthrough suggests the 31-year-old is likely over the issue. As long as Teller can return to practice by Wednesday, he should be ready to suit up for Thursday night's AFC South contest against the Colts.

headline: Teller (illness) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Browns.
story: Teller must miss Sunday's contest due to an illness. The reserve right guard's absence means third-string option Evan Brown will be next up behind Ed Ingram and Febechi Nwaiwu if any members of the Texans' interior offensive line must exit the game.

headline: Rutledge (neck) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Rutledge was not cleared to practice due to a neck injury that he sustained in the Texans' Week 11 win over the Colts. He won't be available Sunday, so Febechi Nwaiwu will likely draw the start at left guard. Rutledge's next chance to suit up is Week 13 against the Steelers on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Rutledge (stinger) was deemed questionable to return near the end of Thursday's 26-3 win against Indianapolis and didn't end up re-entering the game.
story: The Texans announced Rutledge's injury in the waning moments of the contest, but he had been in the medical tent well before that time. Febechi Nwaiwu took over at left guard following Rutledge's departure. With Houston not set to play again until Sunday, Nov. 29, against Baltimore, Rutledge will look to recover from the stinger in time to suit up.

headline: Rutledge (neck) was a full participant in Monday's walkthrough practice.
story: Rutledge was unable to participate in any Week 10 prep sessions due to a neck injury and then sat out Sunday's loss to the Browns. Rutledge's estimated return to practice is a good sign for the first-round rookie's chances of playing in Thursday night's divisional showdown against the Colts.

headline: Rutledge (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns.
story: Rutledge did not participate in any Week 10 prep for the Texans. The rookie offensive guard will not suit up for Sunday's contest, leaving Wyatt Teller (illness) or Evan Brown to start at left guard in a game with massive potential playoff implications for both the Texans and the Browns.

headline: Hunter (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Hunter is set to miss a third consecutive game due to a hamstring injury. In his absence, Jadeveon Clowney and Dominique Robinson will continue to operate in elevated roles on the Texans' defensive front opposite NFL sack leader Will Anderson. Hunter's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Steelers on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Hunter (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Hunter did not play in Thursday's win over the Colts due to his hamstring injury. The defensive end has still not returned to practice since sustaining the injury during Week 10 prep. If Hunter continues to miss practice, he will be in line to miss his third consecutive game due to the injury.

headline: Hunter (hamstring) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday night's game against the Colts.
story: Hunter will now miss consecutive contests due to a hamstring injury he sustained during Week 10 prep. The pass rusher was unable to practice during Week 11 prep as he continues to deal with the issue. Jadeveon Clowney is set to start at defensive end opposite Will Anderson for Thursday's AFC South showdown.

headline: Hunter (hamstring) did not participate at practice Tuesday.
story: Hunter sat out Sunday's game at Cleveland due to a hamstring injury that popped up during practice, and he's now in danger of missing a second straight contest. Unless he returns to practice Wednesday, he'll likely end up on the sidelines during Thursday's game versus the Colts.

headline: Hunter (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns.
story: Hunter popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a hamstring injury. He was unable to practice Friday, and the injury is severe enough for him to miss his first game of the 2026 regular season. The Texans could also be without fellow star edge rusher Will Anderson (ankle), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game despite also sitting out of Friday's practice. Jadeveon Clowney, Dominique Robinson and Sabastian Harsh will all see more defensive snaps in the absence of Hunter, whose next chance to play is Week 11 against Indianapolis on Thursday.

headline: Hunter (hamstring) was limited in Thursday's practice, Mary Kay Cabot of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
story: This is the first mention of Hunter's hamstring injury. His availability for Friday's practice should provide more clarity regarding his status for Sunday's game against the Browns, though he should be considered questionable for now. The 32-year-old has appeared in all eight of the Texans' regular-season games, accumulating 10 total tackles (nine solo), including 4.0 sacks.

headline: Jordan (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: The tight end logged a trio of DNPs this week and will miss a third straight contest. With Jordan remaining sidelined, Dalton Schultz, Foster Moreau, Marlin Klein and Cade Stover will be the healthy options at the position for Houston. Jordan has two catches for 12 yards on two targets across five contests this season.

headline: Jordan (foot/illness) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday night's game against the Colts.
story: Jordan missed all three Week 11 practice sessions due to an injury and an illness. The tight end will miss a second straight game, this time with two separate issues as opposed to the finger injury that plagued him ahead of Week 10. Marlin Klein or Cade Stover is set to be the No. 3 tight end behind Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau for Thursday night's contest.

headline: Jordan (foot/illness) did not participate at practice Tuesday.
story: Jordan missed Sunday's game at Cleveland because of a finger injury, but it's now a foot issue and an illness that's keeping him off the practice field. If he doesn't practice in some capacity Wednesday, he'll probably end up listed as out for Thursday's game versus the Colts.

headline: Jordan (finger) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns.
story: Jordan was unable to practice all week while tending to a finger injury, and his absence Sunday means Foster Moreau, Marlin Klein and Cade Stover are all in line for more snaps on offense behind starting tight end Dalton Schultz. Jordan's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Colts on Thursday.

headline: Jordan (finger) did not practice Wednesday, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
story: Jordan has dealt with knee and foot injuries this season and has played pretty sparingly behind Dalton Schultz, Foster Moreau and Cade Stover for much of the campaign. Jordan has logged just 29 offensive snaps across nine appearances.

headline: Jordan (foot) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Jordan likely sustained his foot injury during Thursday's practice, but the tight end was quickly able to upgrade to a full participant in Friday's practice. Jordan is all set to suit up as a depth option at tight end in Sunday's contest.

headline: Jordan was limited in practice Thursday due to a foot issue.
story: Jordan may have hurt his foot during practice, as he was a full participant Wednesday. Whatever the case may be, the veteran tight end will likely need to practice in full Friday to avoid being tagged with a game designation heading into the weekend. Starting tight end Dalton Schultz is managing a quadriceps issue and was also limited in practice Thursday, so it's currently uncertain what the Texans' tight-end corps will look like for Sunday's game against the Giants.

headline: Rankins (ankle) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Rankins missed Wednesday's practice due to an ankle injury he sustained in Week 11 against the Colts. He logged a limited session Thursday, and Friday's full practice was enough for him to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's contest. The veteran defensive tackle has accumulated 25 tackles (17 solo), including 4.0 sacks, and one pass defense across 10 games this season.

headline: Rankins (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Rankins sustained an ankle injury during Thursday's win over the Colts and did not return to the contest. The defensive tackle's absence from Wednesday's session suggests the injury was significant. Rankins will have Thursday and Friday's sessions to return to practice in time to avoid an injury designation, or to at least have a chance to suit up for Sunday's game against the Ravens.

headline: Rankins (ankle) is questionable to return to Thursday's game versus the Colts.
story: Rankins sustained an apparent ankle injury during the second quarter of Thursday's contest, and he was able to walk gingerly to the sideline under his own power. In his absence, rookie second-rounder Kayden McDonald figures to see an increase in snaps on the defensive line.

headline: Montgomery operated as the Texans' RB1 against the Colts in Week 11, but he could see a dip in touches due to the impending return of Woody Marks (concussion) for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Marks was in the league's concussion protocol for Week 11, when Montgomery led the Texans backfield with 26 carries for 107 yards and three catches (on four targets) for 17 yards in a 26-3 win over the Colts. Marks' return means the second-year pro and Montgomery will share the field Sunday for the first time since Week 5 against the Titans, when the latter suffered a groin injury that caused him to miss the Texans' next four games. The duo should split work Sunday against a Baltimore defense that has given up at least 146 rushing yards in three of the team's last four games (all losses).

headline: Montgomery rushed 26 times for 107 yards and brought in three of four targets for 17 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
story: Making his return from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, Montgomery functioned as the clear lead back with Woody Marks (concussion) unavailable. The former put together the best rushing yardage total of his brief Texans tenure, handling his highest number of carries since Week 4 of his 2023 debut campaign with the Lions. Montgomery also was encouragingly involved in a complementary role in the passing game, and he'll now have some extra time to recover from Thursday's workload ahead of a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29. However, if Marks is able to clear concussion protocol ahead of that contest, Montgomery will see his touch count take a hit.

headline: Montgomery (groin) doesn't have an injury designation and is expected to play in Thursday's game against the Colts, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Montgomery was sidelined for the Texans' past four games due to the groin injury, but he's good to go for the Week 11 matchup after he was listed as a full practice participant from Monday through Wednesday. Before going down with the injury, Montgomery had been part of a timeshare with Woody Marks, but Montgomery will have a fairly clear path to a lead role Thursday with Marks sidelined due to a concussion. Montgomery made a splash in his Texans debut with three touchdowns in a Week 1 loss to the Bills, but he accrued just 126 scoreless yards on 36 touches (32 carries, four receptions) across his subsequent four contests prior to the four-game absence.

headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed that Montgomery (groin) is trending toward playing in Thursday's game against the Colts, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
story: Montgomery has been sidelined for the Texans' past four games, but he concluded Week 10 prep as a full practice participant and appears to have shown continued improvement in his recovery from the groin injury in Week 11. After being listed as a full participant for Monday's walkthrough, Montgomery was on the practice field again Tuesday, with Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston noting that the 29-year-old was "feeling and moving a lot better" compared to previous weeks. With Woody Marks (concussion) expected to be sidelined Thursday, Montgomery should have a clear path to a lead role out of the backfield in his return to action.

headline: Montgomery (groin) is slated to practice Tuesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Listed as a full participant Monday for a walk-through session, Montgomery will take part in a proper practice Tuesday. According to Wilson, Montgomery is "feeling and moving a lot better" compared to previous weeks, so assuming he emerges from Tuesday's session no worse for the wear, the 29-year-old will likely lead the Houston backfield Thursday against the Colts in his first appearance since Week 5. Before missing time with the groin injury, Montgomery had fallen into a timeshare with Woody Marks after averaging just 2.7 yards per carry through the Texans' first five contests. Montgomery may not face much competition for reps in Week 11 with Marks tracking toward sitting out after sustaining a concussion in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.

headline: Montgomery (groin) was a full participant at Monday's walkthrough.
story: Montgomery was held out of Sunday's loss at Cleveland, which marked his fourth absence in a row due to a groin injury. Head coach DeMeco Ryans said afterward that he's "not certain" if Montgomery will be able to play Thursday against the Colts, per DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN.com. Montgomery's full session was his second straight going back to last week, and assuming he's trending toward a return to action this week, he's poised to take on a large workload considering fellow RB Woody Marks is in the concussion protocol and was a DNP on Monday.

headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Sunday that he's "not certain" if Montgomery (groin) will be able to play Thursday against Indianapolis, DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN reports.
story: Montgomery hasn't suited up since he suffered a groin injury Week 5 in Tennessee. However, he practiced in full this past Friday for the first time since getting hurt, and the Texans described his work during Week 10 prep as a "ramp-up" ahead of potentially returning Week 11. Ryans didn't sound certain after Sunday's loss to Cleveland that Montgomery will be able to play versus the Colts, but if the veteran running back does suit up, it could be a huge boost to a Houston offense that may be without the RB who has been filling in as the starter for Montgomery. Woody Marks suffered a concussion Sunday and isn't likely to be cleared in time to play Thursday.

headline: Montgomery (groin) has been downgraded from questionable to out for Sunday's game against the Browns.
story: Montgomery drew the questionable tag for Week 10 after logging a full practice Friday. However, the veteran running back has not progressed enough in his recovery from a groin injury to return for Sunday's contest, which will mark his fourth consecutive absence. With Montgomery sidelined, Woody Marks will once again serve as the Texans' RB1 while Emari Demercado provides backfield depth. Montgomery's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Colts on Thursday.

headline: Montgomery (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns, while Woody Marks (knee) doesn't have an injury designation.
story: Montgomery returned to practice Thursday after missing a month, and he upgraded from limited participation to full for Friday's practice. It's still not clear he'll be active ahead of the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff Sunday, so Marks could be tasked with a heavy workload for a fifth straight game. If Montgomery does return, he'll likely share work with Marks, making it difficult to trust either Houston RB in fantasy lineups.

headline: Montgomery (groin) practiced for a second straight day Friday after missing the past month, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Woody Marks (knee) is also practicing Friday, after sitting out Thursday. At this point, it isn't clear if either or both will be available Sunday at Cleveland. Montgomery is coming back from an injury that's kept him out for more than a month, while Marks is dealing with something that seems to be more recent but less severe.

headline: Montgomery (groin) was limited at practice Thursday, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: Montgomery last saw game action in Week 5, and after he was listed as a 'DNP' on Wednesday, his upgrade to limited participation a day later is especially notable given that fellow RB Woody Marks (knee) didn't practice. Friday's injury report will reveal both the practice participation, as well as the duo's official game statuses for Sunday's road contest against the Browns.

headline: Montgomery (groin) was present for practice Thursday, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
story: The report adds that coach DeMeco Ryans said that the Texans are pleased with the progress of the running back, who last played in Week 5. The team's upcoming injury report is slated to reveal if Montgomery, who logged a 'DNP' on Wednesday, is officially credited with some level of participation a day later. Per Wilson, at this stage whether Montgomery will play this weekend against the Browns is still up in the air

headline: Montgomery (groin) remained sidelined at practice Wednesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Coach DeMeco Ryans noted Monday that he was hopeful Montgomery could resume practicing this week or next. With a DNP on Wednesday, the running back now has two more chances to make an on-field appearance prior to Sunday's game against the Browns. In the event that his absence continues, Woody Marks would continue to lead Houston's backfield, with Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale in reserve.

headline: Coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday he's hopeful that Montgomery (groin) resumes practicing this week, or next week, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Montgomery last saw game action in Week 5, but at this stage he appears to be inching closer to a return, with Ryans adding Monday that he's pleased with the veteran back's progress. In Montgomery's absence, Woody Marks has served as the Texans' clear-cut RB1, but once Montgomery is back, Houston's backfield timeshare figures to be restored.

headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday that Montgomery (groin) has made some progress but is still viewed as week-to-week and will remain out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
story: Montgomery missed Houston's last two games before a Week 8 bye, and he doesn't look like he'll be ready to return to action any sooner than Nov. 15, when the Texans face the Browns on the road. With Montgomery set to miss another game, Woody Marks is poised to maintain a lead role out of the backfield. While Montgomery was sidelined the previous two contests, Marks averaged 81.0 scrimmage yards on 18.5 touches per game.

headline: Montgomery (groin) wasn't present for the portion of Wednesday's practice open to the media, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
story: Montgomery missed the Texans' two games before a Week 8 bye due to a groin issue, and his status remains up in the air as the team prepares for Sunday's contest at the Chargers. He hasn't practiced since sustaining the injury Oct. 11 at Tennessee, meaning he likely will need to mix into drills Thursday and/or Friday to have a chance to suit up this weekend.

headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that he has "no significant update" on the status of Montgomery (groin) heading into a Week 9 matchup with the Chargers, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
story: Prior to the Texans' Week 8 bye, Montgomery missed two straight games due to a groin injury and wasn't able to practice in advance of either of those contests. Ryans didn't offer much of an indication that Montgomery's condition has dramatically improved following the bye, with the coach noting that the running back will be evaluated throughout the week before a decision is made on his status for Sunday's contest. If Montgomery ends up being sidelined for a third consecutive game, Woody Marks would be in store for another turn as Houston's lead back.

headline: Montgomery (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Montgomery still hasn't returned to practice and will miss a second straight game, leaving Woody Marks to handle a large workload against the Giants. Jawhar Jordan (quad) was effective off the bench last week, but he's now on the practice-squad injured list, which leaves Dare Ogunbowale as the No. 2 RB. Ogunbowale's history as a special teamer and passing-down specialist suggest Marks should dominate carries.

headline: Montgomery (groin) isn't expected to play Sunday against the Giants, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Montgomery is poised to miss a second straight game, and with Jawhar Jordan (quadriceps) injured on the practice squad after he was elevated for Week 6, the Texans will ride Woody Marks and special-teamer Dare Ogunbowale out of the backfield, with Marks likely to see virtually every meaningful carry versus New York.

headline: Montgomery (groin) isn't practicing Thursday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Wilson adds that Montgomery is expected to miss Sunday's game against the Giants, though head coach DeMeco Ryans has yet to confirm as much. In any event, Montgomery's chances of playing look slim at best, as he has yet to practice since exiting during Houston's Week 5 win over the Titans. Woody Marks started in Montgomery's absence against the Jaguars in Week 6, and Marks is poised to lead the backfield again Sunday, with Dare Ogunbowale likely to fill a change-of-pace role and Jawhar Jordan (quadriceps) no longer a candidate to be elevated after being placed on the practice squad injured list.

headline: Montgomery (groin) isn't practicing Wednesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Still seemingly being viewed as week-to-week after he failed to practice in any fashion last week before sitting out the Texans' win over the Jaguars in London, Montgomery appears to be trending toward another absence this weekend against the Giants. If Montgomery ends up missing another contest, Woody Marks would be in line for another turn as Houston's lead back, with Dare Ogunbowale and practice-squad member Deuce Vaughn operating as depth options.

headline: The Texans ruled Montgomery (groin) out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London.
story: After making an early exit from the Texans' Week 5 win over the Titans due to the groin injury, Montgomery was unable to practice in any capacity Wednesday or Thursday. He'll stay behind in Houston while the Texans make the trip overseas and will set his sights on a return to action Week 7 against the Giants. With Montgomery set to miss his first game of the season, Woody Marks should be in store for a sizable workload once again after handling 19 touches and playing 56 of 66 offensive snaps in Week 5.

headline: Montgomery (groin) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Since being labeled week-to-week by head coach DeMeco Ryans on Monday, Montgomery has sat out the Texans' ensuing two practices. Unless he's able to take part in Friday's practice in some fashion, Montgomery will likely be officially ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London. Woody Marks looks poised to handle a workhorse role out of the backfield Week 6 with Montgomery expected to be inactive for the first time this season.

headline: Montgomery (groin) isn't practicing Wednesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Montgomery made an early exit from the Texans' Week 5 win at Tennessee due to a groin injury, which head coach DeMeco Ryans since has called a "week-to-week" concern for the running back, per Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle. As a result, Montgomery's lack of activity Wednesday isn't a surprise, and Houston ultimately could make a ruling on his availability for Sunday's game in Jacksonville when it posts its final practice report of the week Friday. Woody Marks is lined up to lead the backfield for as long as Montgomery is sidelined.

headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that Montgomery (groin) is considered week-to-week, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle reports.
story: Montgomery exited Sunday's 26-3 win over the Titans midway through the second quarter due to the groin injury and was unable to return. Based on Ryans' comments a day later, Montgomery looks to be trending toward missing his first game of the season in Week 6, when the Texans travel to London to face the Jaguars on Sunday. Montgomery's expected absence this coming weekend should clear the way for Woody Marks to take on a lead role out of the Houston backfield, with Dare Ogunbowale and practice-squad members Jawhar Jordan and Deuce Vaughn representing candidates to handle depth roles. Since scoring three touchdowns on 23 touches in a Week 1 loss to the Bills, Montgomery has failed to find the end zone while being limited to 78 yards on 32 carries (2.4 average) and four catches for 48 yards over the Texans' subsequent four contests.

headline: The Texans ruled out Montgomery (groin) for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Houston will be left with Woody Marks and Dare Ogunbowale as its available options out of the backfield for the rest of the afternoon after Montgomery was unable to return following his departure from the game midway through the second quarter. Prior to exiting, Montgomery gained 11 yards on five carries and went without a target.

headline: Montgomery suffered a groin injury during Sunday's game at Tennessee.
story: Prior to his exit in the middle of the second quarter, Montgomery had five carries for 11 yards. While Montgomery is considered questionable to return after walking slowly to the locker room, Woody Marks will take on lead-back duties for the Texans.

headline: Montgomery carried the ball 10 times for 24 yards and added 19 receiving yards on a hook-and-ladder play in Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
story: The veteran RB's longest gain on the ground went for only six yards, and Woody Marks scampered for the Texans' only rushing TD of the afternoon on a six-yard run just before the two-minute warning in the fourth quarter -- a score set up by Montgomery's 19-yard dash following a lateral from Dalton Schultz just one play before. Montgomery hasn't found the end zone himself or reached 50 scrimmage yards since Week 1, a streak he'll look to end in a Week 5 road trip to Tennessee.

headline: Schultz (illness) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Schultz practiced without limitations Friday, shedding any doubts about his availability after an illness limited his participation Thursday. The Ravens have allowed seven TDs to TEs this season, which is seventh most in the NFL, but Schultz has scored only once all season and is coming off consecutive one-catch performances.

headline: Schultz (illness) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Schultz wasn't listed on Wednesday's injury report, which indicates that the illness is a new concern for the veteran tight end. A full session Friday would likely be enough for him to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Ravens. Brevin Jordan (finger/foot), Foster Moreau and Marlin Klein would all be in line for larger roles on offense in the event that Schultz is not cleared to play in Week 12.

headline: Schultz brought in his only target for 11 yards in the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts on Thursday.
story: Schultz had a minimal role on a night when C.J. Stroud threw for a modest 194 yards and recorded completions to nine different targets. The veteran tight end now has consecutive one-catch, 11-yard tallies after recording multiple receptions in each of his first eight games of the season, and Schultz's production will remain hard to trust heading into a Week 12 home matchup against the Ravens on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Schultz caught one pass for an 11-yard touchdown on two targets in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
story: While Schultz got into the end zone for the first time this campaign, his catches and targets were new single-game lows for 2026. Schultz has yet to produce more than 45 yards in a game when Nico Collins is healthy this season. The veteran tight end is a low-floor, TD-or-bust fantasy bet.

headline: Schultz caught two of four targets for 42 yards in Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers.
story: Not counting his 12-140-0 receiving explosion in Week 2 when Nico Collins was out with a hamstring injury, Schultz has mustered 23 grabs for 244 yards and no touchdowns across his seven other appearances. He's failed to reach 50 receiving yards in any of those contests and is merely a TE2 in fantasy.

headline: Schultz caught five of six targets for 45 yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
story: The veteran tight end paced the Texans with his six targets, matching Xavier Hutchinson, as the duo saw one more than Nico Collins on a day when C.J. Stroud targeted nine different pass catchers. Schultz is still looking for his first touchdown of the season and has settled in as a low-ceiling fantasy tight end.

headline: Schultz (quadriceps) was a full participant in Friday's practice and doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants, Adam Caplan or SiriusXM reports.
story: Schultz has lot some playing time to Foster Moreau in recent weeks, but it's still Schultz who gets the nod in most of the clear passing situations. A full practice Friday suggests the tight end won't have any limitations come Sunday.

headline: Schultz (quadriceps) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
story: Schultz took a step forward Thursday after sitting out Wednesday's practice. He'll have one more opportunity Friday to log a full practice, which could help him avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants. Schultz is still searching for his first touchdown of the season.

headline: Schultz (quadriceps) returned to practice Thursday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Schultz sat out practice Wednesday due to a quadriceps injury. His participation level Thursday will be revealed later in the day, but it's a good sign that Schultz is set to practice in at least some capacity. He remains locked in atop Houston's depth chart at tight end when healthy. The Texans have made their way back from London and will host the Giants on Sunday.

headline: Schultz didn't practice Wednesday due to a quadriceps injury.
story: Schultz is making his first appearance of the season on the injury report after he apparently got banged up during this past Sunday's 34-31 win over the Jaguars in London. The Texans haven't yet indicated that Schultz's availability for this weekend's game versus the Giants is in any peril, but he'll need to resume practicing in some fashion over the next two days to assuage fantasy managers' concerns about his health.

headline: Schultz caught four of six targets for 33 yards in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Jaguars.
story: Schultz actually led the team with his six targets, but C.J. Stroud spread the ball around to 10 different pass catchers on a day he attempted 34 passes. Schultz has been held to 35 yards or fewer in five of six games this season and has yet to visit the end zone. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy bet ahead of next Sunday's date with the Giants.

headline: Schultz caught three of four targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 26-3 win over the Titans.
story: Schultz has now caught three or fewer passes while failing to exceed 30 receiving yards in three straight contests. The tight end has garnered just nine targets since Week 2 after he caught 16 of 22 targets for 175 yards over the first two weeks of the season. Schultz may have a tough time getting back on track against the Jaguars' impressive defense in Week 6.

headline: Schultz caught both of his targets for nine yards in Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
story: With Nico Collins back from his hamstring injury after missing two weeks, Schultz's voluminous pass-catching role evaporated against Dallas. For as long as Collins is healthy, Schultz is little more than a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option ahead of next Sunday's date with the Titans.

headline: Boutte (hip) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Boutte's absence will coincide with the return of Marvin Harrison (hamstring) from a two-game absence. Harrison will join Nico Collins, Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson while Boutte sits out due to an hip injury the latter sustained in last Thursday's win over the Colts, which subsequently prevented Boutte from practicing in any capacity during Week 12 prep. Boutte's next chance to take the field will be Sunday, Dec. 6, at Pittsburgh.

headline: Boutte (hip) isn't practicing Friday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Wilson adds that Boutte isn't expected to play Sunday against the Ravens, and while things are certainly trending that way based on his inability to practice all week, that notion has yet to be confirmed by an official team source. Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Marvin Harrison will compete for playing time and targets alongside Nico Collins if Boutte is ruled out.

headline: Boutte (hip) did not participate in Thursday's practice session.
story: Boutte has missed the first two practices of Week 12 prep while managing a hip injury that he sustained during the Texans' 26-3 win over the Colts in Week 11. If he doesn't practice Friday, then Boutte should be considered on the doubtful side of playing Sunday against the Ravens. Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison and Nikko Remigio would all be in line for larger roles in the Texans' offense in the event that Boutte doesn't play against Baltimore.

headline: Boutte (hip) didn't participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: This past Friday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston indicated that the hip injury Boutte suffered in last Thursday's win over the Colts didn't appear to be serious. However, with a DNP to start the practice week, the wideout's status will need to be monitored as Sunday's game against the Ravens approaches. Apart from a 4-125-2 receiving line in a 44-22 win over the Chargers in Week 9, Boutte has produced modest fantasy outputs more often than not, maxing out at five targets (three times) in 10 contests.

headline: Boutte's hip injury he suffered in Thursday night's win over the Colts doesn't appear to be serious, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: The wideout had one of his more productive games of the season before being injured, as he caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown. His 40 yards were the second-most he's produced in a game this season. Boutte is up to 21 grabs for 359 yards and three touchdowns on 31 targets across 10 games in 2026.

headline: Boutte (hip) was deemed questionable to return to Thursday's Week 11 win over Indianapolis and didn't return to the game.
story: The Texans didn't announce Boutte's injury until near the end of the contest when the team's offense was running out the clock. As such, it's difficult to ascertain how serious his hip injury is. The veteran wideout finished the Texans' victory with two catches for 40 yards and a touchdown on two targets, with his score coming on a 24-yard grab in the second quarter. Houston doesn't play again until Sunday, Nov. 29, against Baltimore, giving Boutte extra time to recover and attempt to avoid missing a contest for the first time this season.

headline: Boutte failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
story: Even with Marvin Harrison (hamstring) out and Jaylin Noel (toe) done for the season, Boutte was targeted on just one of C.J. Stroud's 38 pass attempts versus Cleveland. Boutte's 47 snaps on offense were fewer than both Nico Collins (57) and Xavier Hutchinson (51) but 14 more than Tank Dell, though Dell out-targeted Boutte four to one. Boutte popped off for 4-125-2 in Week 9 against the Chargers but otherwise has failed to reach 40 receiving yards in any of his eight other appearances this season.

headline: Boutte erupted for four catches (on five targets) for 125 yards and two touchdowns during Sunday's 44-22 road win against the Chargers.
story: Boutte entered Week 9 action with a cumulative 15-194-0 line on 23 targets through seven appearances this season, so Sunday's performance was a true outburst. It didn't hurt that Boutte and his teammates were facing the only winless team in the NFL, but QB C.J. Stroud took full advantage of the opportunity, including Boutte (twice) among his five TD tosses. Ultimately, the Texans' receiving corps has a clear No. 1 in WR Nico Collins, who is the best bet among the group to produce most weeks.

headline: Boutte caught one of two targets for 25 yards during Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss versus the Giants.
story: Boutte played a season-low 18 offensive snaps in Week 7, trailing behind Nico Collins (34) and Xavier Hutchinson (31) and tying with Jaylin Noel (toe). Predictably, Boutte wasn't very involved in an inefficient passing game. As recent trade acquisition Marvin Harrison gets acclimated, Boutte's role probably will continue to shrink as the campaign continues.

headline: Boutte finished with two receptions for 16 yards on three targets in Sunday's 34-31 win over the Jaguars in London.
story: Though the newly acquired Marvin Harrison was limited to just 12 snaps in his Texans debut, his presence may have been enough for Boutte to see a notable role reduction in Week 6. Boutte took the field for 26 of the Texans' 63 snaps, with his 41.3 percent share representing a season-low rate and placing him fourth among Houston receivers. Harrison is likely to see his snaps pick up once he gains a full grasp of his new playbook, and Boutte could end up being a casualty from a playing-time standpoint.

headline: Boutte caught three of five targets for 38 yards during Sunday's 26-3 win over the Titans.
story: Boutte finished tied with fellow wide receivers Xavier Hutchinson and Jaylin Noel for second on the team in targets, and his 38 receiving yards set a new season high for him. With Houston acquiring Marvin Harrison from the Cardinals on Sunday, it's unclear how the wide receiver room will be organized moving forward. On the season, Boutte has caught 12 of 18 targets for 153 yards over five contests.

headline: Boutte caught three of four targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 34-30 loss to the Cowboys.
story: With Nico Collins back from a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury, he dominated targets and left the remainder of the Houston pass catchers fighting for leftovers. Boutte ran 24 routes on C.J. Stroud's 35 dropbacks, but the summer trade pickup has yet to really make an impact with the Texans, recording nine catches for 115 yards on 13 targets after four games.

headline: Boutte hauled in both of his targets for 21 yards during the Texans' 19-17 loss to the Colts on Sunday.
story: For a second consecutive week, Boutte operated in an elevated role on offense due to the absence of Nico Collins (hamstring). Boutte's 37 offensive snaps actually led all Texans wide receivers, but he didn't see a target from C.J. Stroud until late in the fourth quarter, setting up a Woody Marks one-yard rushing touchdown. Per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston, head coach DeMeco Ryans expressed optimism Monday that Collins would be back for Week 4 against the Cowboys, which would return Boutte to a secondary role.

headline: Marks (concussion) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
story: Marks, who was inactive Nov. 19 against the Colts, logged 'full' listings at practice Wednesday through Friday and now has gained clearance to rejoin the lineup after being sidelined for one game. His Week 11 absence coincided with the return to action of fellow RB David Montgomery, and now that both backs are available for the first time since Week 5, look for Marks to see a noticeable dip in volume while sharing touches with Montgomery, who logged 26 carries versus Indianapolis.

headline: Marks (concussion) was listed as a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Marks didn't practice last week before being ruled out for this past Thursday's 26-3 win over the Colts, but with some extra recovery time since then, the running back is trending toward a return to the lineup Sunday against the Ravens. To get there, however, he'll need to fully progress through the NFL's concussion protocol in the days leading up to the Texans' Week 12 contest.

headline: Marks (concussion) was on the practice field Wednesday, Jonathan M. Alexander of the Houston Chronicle  reports.
story: Marks, who was inactive for last Thursday's game against the Colts, was, as of Monday, "trending in the right direction," according to coach DeMeco Ryans, per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston. The running back's presence for Wednesday's session supports that notion, with Marks' official participation level in line to provide key context ahead of this Sunday's matchup against the Ravens.

headline: Head coach DeMeco Ryans said Monday that Marks (concussion) is "trending in the right direction," and the Texans "are hopeful to have him" for Sunday's game against the Ravens, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: After sustaining a concussion in a Nov. 15 loss to the Browns, Marks was unable to clear the five-step protocol on a short week and ended up sitting out this past Thursday's 26-3 win over the Colts. Since then, Marks appears to have progressed on some level through the protocol, though it's not yet clear if he'll be available to practice when the Texans kick off Week 12 prep Wednesday. If Marks ends up getting the green light to play versus the Ravens, he may be part of a timeshare in the backfield or be forced to settle for No. 2 duties behind David Montgomery (groin), who returned from a four-game absence in Week 11 to run for a season-high 107 yards.

headline: Marks (concussion) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Colts.
story: After sustaining a concussion in this past Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns, Marks will be sidelined for the first time this season after he was unable to practice in any capacity on a short week. The second-year player had been operating as the Texans' clear lead back over the past four contests, but for at least one week, those duties are expected to fall to David Montgomery (groin), who has been cleared to return to action following a four-game absence. Once Marks clears the protocol, he could be form a timeshare with Montgomery.

headline: Marks (concussion) didn't practice Tuesday.
story: Marks' continued absence at practice comes as little surprise after he entered concussion protocol upon sustaining a head injury in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns. Head coach DeMeco Ryans has already indicated that Marks is unlikely to clear the five-step protocol ahead of Thursday's game against the Colts, so expect the second-year back to get formally ruled out for the Week 11 contest following Wednesday's practice.

headline: Marks (concussion) missed Monday's walkthrough.
story: Marks sustained a concussion during Sunday's loss in Cleveland, and head coach DeMeco Ryans said afterward that the running back isn't likely to gain clearance to play Thursday versus the Colts, according to DJ Bien-Aime of ESPN.com. The Texans may make a ruling on Marks' status as soon as they post Wednesday's injury report, and conversely position mate David Montgomery (groin) appears to be closing in on a return to action after logging a second full listing in a row going back to last week.

headline: Coach DeMeco Ryans acknowledged after Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Browns that Marks (concussion) is unlikely to play in Thursday night's game against the Colts, ESPN.com's DJ Bien-Aime reports.
story: With the Texans on a short week ahead of the contest, Ryans noted of Marks, "Just not enough time for him to turn it around that quickly." As for the Week 11 status of fellow RB David Montgomery (groin) -- who was inactive again Sunday -- Ryans said, "I'm not certain if David can play or not," adding "We'll take it one day at a time to see how he feels and how he can get back." Prior to his exit Sunday, Marks had 12 carries for 50 yards and one catch for 15 yards. Meanwhile, Emari Demercado finished with seven carries for 16 yards and one catch for minus-one yard, while Dare Ogunbowale logged one carry for two yards and one catch for 13 yards.

headline: Marks (concussion) has been downgraded to out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Browns.
story: Prior to his exit from the contest, Marks carried 12 times for 50 yards and caught his only target for 15 yards. With David Montgomery (groin) inactive, Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale will handle Houston's backfield duties versus Cleveland going forward versus Cleveland. The Texans' next game is Thursday, so Marks has a limited amount of time to progress through the NFL's concussion protocol ahead of Week 11 action.

headline: Marks is being evaluated for a possible concussion during Sunday's game at Cleveland.
story: Marks remained on the turf for some time in the third quarter before making his way to the sideline and the medical tent. If Marks is diagnosed with a concussion, Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale will be the Texans' remaining running backs with David Montgomery (groin) still sidelined.

headline: Marks will be the Texans' lead back against the Browns on Sunday after David Montgomery (groin) was ruled out for that contest.
story: Montgomery was initially tagged as questionable for Week 10 after logging a full practice Friday, but the veteran running back will end up missing a fourth straight game due to a groin injury. That means Marks will once again operate as Houston's RB1 while Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale -- the latter of whom was signed to the practice squad and elevated to the active roster Saturday -- provide backfield depth. Marks has logged at least 15 carries in each of his last four outings, and over that span, he has turned 67 carries into 254 yards (3.8 YPC) and added eight catches on 12 targets for 67 yards. He has not found the end zone since Week 4 against the Cowboys.

headline: Following a full practice Friday, Marks (knee) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Browns.
story: After experiencing knee discomfort Wednesday and not practicing Thursday due to lingering soreness from hits, per Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston, Marks worked fully to close the practice week and heads into the weekend without any availability concerns. Marks has seen the bulk of Houston's backfield work of late, but he may have some competition for carries Sunday, as David Montgomery (groin) -- who hasn't played since Week 5 -- practiced fully Friday and is listed as questionable to face Cleveland.

headline: Marks (knee) was back at practice Friday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: After sitting out Thursday's practice, Marks' return to the field Friday is a positive sign for his chances of being available Sunday against the Browns. David Montgomery (groin) is also practicing Friday, following a limited session Thursday, but it isn't yet clear if he'll be ready in time for Sunday's matchup with the Browns.

headline: Marks (knee) didn't practice Thursday, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: Marks was limited Wednesday, so his 'DNP' on Thursday is concerning, though it could be more of a workload management situation, as opposed to a setback-related downgrade, a notion supported by Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston's report that the running back dealt with mild knee discomfort in Wednesday's practice and didn't finish the session for precautionary reasons. Meanwhile, fellow backfield member David Montgomery (groin) -- who hasn't played since Week 5 -- returned to a limited session Thursday. Valuable context regarding the duo's statuses will arrive Friday, when the Texans have their final practice before Sunday's road game against the Browns.

headline: Marks (knee) wasn't spotted during the portion of Thursday's practice session open to reporters, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: After being deemed a limited participant Wednesday, Marks' apparent absence a day later is noteworthy, though it's possible it's maintenance-related. Thursday's upcoming injury report will provide added context on that front, as well as the participation level of fellow RB David Montgomery (groin), who was on the field Thursday.

headline: Marks (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Chris Easterling of the Akron Beacon Journal reports.
story: In this past Sunday's 44-22 win over the Chargers, Marks played on 66 percent of the Texans' snaps on offense and logged 18 carries for 70 yards while catching one of his four targets for four yards.
