story: Ogletree was held out of Wednesday's practice due to a knee injury, but his full session Thursday puts the fifth-year tight end on track to play against the Giants on Sunday. Ogletree has a 4-21-0 receiving line on seven targets through 11 regular-season games and has not been targeted in three of his last four outings.

headline: Ogletree (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
story: The tight end has been dealing with a knee issue for the better part of the past month, but Ogletree has continued to play through the injury. Across 11 games this season, Ogletree has four catches for 21 yards on seven targets.

headline: Ogletree went without a target while playing 24 of the Colts' 50 snaps on offense in Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Texans.
story: For the third time in four weeks, Ogletree failed to draw a look in the passing game, but he wasn't held off the stat sheet entirely, as he collected a pair of tackles on special teams. Though the fifth-year tight end has been active for all 11 of the Colts' games, he's cobbled together a lowly 4-21-0 receiving line on seven targets.

headline: Ogletree (knee) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Cowboys.
story: Ogletree was able to play through his nagging knee issue in Week 8 at Jacksonville, and he'll be active again in Week 9 despite missing practice Wednesday and logging a limited practice session Thursday. He figures to continue to compete with Mo Alie-Cox and Will Mallory for snaps at tight end behind clear frontrunner Tyler Warren.

headline: Ogletree (knee) upgraded to a limited practice Thursday.
story: After being a DNP on Wednesday, Ogletree's return to practice puts him on track for Sunday's game against Dallas. The Colts are using four tight ends most weeks, featuring Tyler Warren in the passing game, while Mo Alie-Cox, Ogletree and Will Mallory play part-time roles.

headline: Ogletree (knee) did not participate at the Colts' practice Wednesday.
story: Ogletree opened the week on the sideline at practice as he continues to nurse a knee issue. The tight end was able to play through the injury during the team's 42-7 loss to the Jaguars in Week 8, and he will have two more chances to return to practice before potentially giving it a go again Sunday versus the Cowboys.

headline: Ogletree (knee) is active Week 8 against the Jaguars.
story: Ogletree will get the go-ahead to suit up despite failing to log a full practice all week and even missing Friday's session entirely. The ceiling is likely capped, however, as he'll be competing against the likes of Will Mallory and Mo Alie-Cox for tight end snaps following the return of starter Tyler Warren (groin).

headline: Ogletree (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
story: Ogletree's practice reps Wednesday and Thursday were limited by a knee injury that he likely picked up against the Vikings in Week 7. He was a DNP for Friday's session, but the Colts have left the door open for Ogletree to suit up Sunday, depending on how his knee feels over the weekend and during pregame warmups. Tyler Warren (groin) has been cleared to return from a two-game absence, but Ogletree's absence would mean more offensive snaps would be available for Will Mallory, Mo Alie-Cox and Pharaoh Brown.

headline: Ogletree (knee) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Ogletree hasn't had a productive 2026 campaign, totaling three catches (five targets) for 16 yards. Still, if the knee issue prevents him from suiting up Sunday against Jacksonville, it could at least mean more snaps for Will Mallory and Mo Alie-Cox behind Tyler Warren (groin).

headline: Ogletree (knee) was estimated as a limited participant on the Colts' official injury report Wednesday.
story: Ogletree presumably picked up the knee injury during Sunday's game at Minnesota, but his status indicates it's probably not too severe. If he can practice in full Thursday or Friday, he could still avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Ogletree caught both of his passes for 12 yards during the Colts' 16-10 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Ogletree and the other Colts tight ends stepped into larger roles offensively for a second consecutive week due to the absence of Tyler Warren (groin). Ogletree's 35 offensive snaps were second most among Indianapolis' tight ends, and he set season highs in catches, targets and receiving yards. He's mostly worked as a blocker on offense, and his snap count would be lower in Week 8 against the Jaguars if Warren is cleared to return for that contest.

headline: Ogletree (ankle) practiced in full Thursday.
story: Ogletree didn't practice Wednesday due to an ankle issue, but he has apparently avoided a serious injury given his return to full participation Thursday. The veteran tight end has just one catch on three targets for four yards through six games this season, as he's been primarily used as a blocker. Ogletree should be good to go for Sunday's battle against the Vikings.

headline: Ogletree (ankle) did not participate at the Colts' practice Wednesday.
story: Ogletree appears to have picked up an ankle injury during the team's 26-20 loss to the Titans in Week 6. The tight end will have two more opportunities to return to practice before Sunday's matchup with the Vikings.

headline: Mallory (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
story: Mallory is set to miss a fourth consecutive game due to a hamstring injury. The Colts are on bye for Week 13, so his next opportunity to play is Week 14 against the Eagles on Sunday, Dec. 13. Drew Ogletree (knee) is listed as questionable after stringing together a DNP-FP-DNP practice log, and if he cannot play Sunday, then Pharaoh Brown would serve as the Colts' TE2 behind Tyler Warren.

headline: The Colts ruled out Mallory (hamstring) for Thursday night's games against the Texans.
story: Mallory was absent from practice all week heading into Thursday night's divisional showdown versus Houston. This marks the 27-year-old's third straight missed game. He has caught two of nine targets for 20 yards in three games during the 2026 season.

headline: Mallory (hamstring) was estimated as a non-participant for Tuesday's practice walkthrough.
story: Tuesday was the second straight day that the Colts held a walkthrough instead of a traditional practice, and Mallory was deemed a DNP in both cases. It's looking increasingly unlikely that the tight end will be able to play Thursday versus Houston, though he could give himself a chance to suit up if he's able to show improvement over the next day. Should Mallory be out Thursday, Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown would be the healthy tight ends behind starter Tyler Warren.

headline: Mallory (hamstring) did not participate in Monday's walkthrough practice.
story: Mallory suffered a hamstring injury during Week 10 prep, and he was not cleared to play in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Indianapolis is operating on a short week, so Mallory faces an uphill battle to play against the Texans on Thursday.

headline: Mallory (hamstring) has been downgraded from questionable to out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Mallory was a late addition to the Colts' injury report due to a hamstring issue that cropped up Friday. The fourth-year pro will not be available for Sunday's contest, and with Mo Alie-Cox (groin) placed on injured reserve, Tyler Warren will be backed up by Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown. Mallory's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday.

headline: Mallory (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Miami.
story: Mallory was added to Friday's practice report as a limited participant due to a hamstring injury. His late addition isn't a great sign heading into the weekend, and with Mo Alie-Cox (groin) already ruled out, the Colts would turn to both Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown to step into larger roles behind Tyler Warren if Mallory is also sidelined.

headline: Mallory did not catch any of his three targets during Sunday's 16-10 loss to Minnesota.
story: Mallory and the other Colts tight ends worked in larger roles offensively Sunday due to the absence of Tyler Warren (groin). However, the former's 21 offensive snaps ranked third behind Mo Alie-Cox (39) and Drew Ogletree (35), and Mallory could not connect with Daniel Jones, with the third and final pass that came his way resulting in an interception by Harrison Smith. Mallory has seen nine targets over his last two games since coming off injured reserve, but his role would shrink against the Jaguars in Week 8 if Warren is given the green light to play in that contest.

headline: Mallory will once again operate in an expanded role after Tyler Warren (groin) was ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings, Abby Halpin of the Colts' official site reports.
story: Warren will end up missing a second consecutive game while battling a groin injury, so Mallory and Mo Alie-Cox will serve as the Colts' top tight ends for Sunday's contest. Mallory turned six targets into two catches for 20 yards in a Week 6 loss to the Titans, and he finished that contest third in targets behind Keenan Allen (11) and Josh Downs (eight).

headline: Mallory caught two of six passes for 20 yards during Sunday's 26-20 loss to the Titans.
story: Mallory was cleared to make his 2026 debut Sunday after missing the Colts first five games of the regular season due to a thumb injury that was severe enough for him to go on injured reserve. Although he didn't put up eye-popping stats, he led all Colts tight ends with 43 offensive snaps and finished third on the team in targets behind Keenan Allen (11) and Josh Downs (eight). Mallory's playing time would likely decrease if Tyler Warren (groin) was cleared to return for Week 7 against the Vikings on Oct. 25.

headline: The Colts activated Mallory (thumb) from injured reserve Saturday.
story: Mallory doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Titans and is slated to make his 2026 debut. He should slot into the tight-end mix alongside Mo Alie-Cox and Drew Ogletree behind Tyler Warren (groin). Mallory has 23 career catches for 252 yards across 24 regular-season appearances.

headline: Mallory (thumb) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Mallory strung together a trio of full practices during Week 6 prep while in the final stages of his recovery from a thumb injury that landed him on injured reserve at the start of the regular season. He would need to be activated from IR by the Colts on Saturday in order to be available for Sunday's AFC South tilt.

headline: Mallory (thumb) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
story: Mallory was designated to return to practice Wednesday. The tight end remains on injured reserve with a thumb injury but was able to log full practice sessions throughout Week 5 prep. The 27-year-old likely has not yet built up his conditioning enough for the Colts to allow him to suit up for Sunday's contest.

headline: Mallory (thumb) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
story: Mallory's 21-day practice window to be activated from IR was opened by the Colts Wednesday, and it seems like he could be trending towards being available in Week 5. Indianapolis' final injury report of the week Friday will shed more light on his status ahead of Sunday's game at Pittsburgh.

headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said that Mallory (thumb) will have his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
story: After sustaining a thumb injury in August, Mallory was sent to injured reserve at the conclusion of the preseason. The 27-year-old has made good progress in his recovery and after he missed the minimum four games, the Colts have decided to clear him to practice at the first opportunity in which he's eligible to do so. Mallory could make his 2026 debut as soon as this Sunday in Pittsburgh, though he'll likely struggle to earn playing time behind fellow tight ends Tyler Warren, Mo Alie-Cox and Drew Ogletree.

headline: Ward (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
story: Ward failed to practice in any capacity during Week 12 prep, and the veteran defensive back will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a knee injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Dolphins. He'll have additional time to rest thanks to the Week 13 bye, and Ward will aim to return for Week 14 against the Eagles on Sunday, Dec. 13. Johnathan Edwards, Kapena Gushiken and Kenneth Harris are all candidates to start opposite Sauce Gardner at outside cornerback for Sunday's game.

headline: Ward (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Ward missed the Colts' Week 11 game against the Texans due to a knee injury he sustained in Week 10. The cornerback's upgrade to limited participation to start Week 12 prep is a good sign, but he will need to continue logging active sessions for a chance to suit up for Sunday's game against the Giants.

headline: The Colts have ruled out Ward (knee) for Thursday night's game against the Texans.
story: Ward's availability for Thursday night's duel against the Texans was in doubt after the veteran corner left Week 10 early with a knee injury. On a short week, the Colts are without the starting cornerback. With Sauce Gardner (calf) also questionable, the secondary could be short come Thursday. Kenneth Harris could see more reps with Ward out.

headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said that Ward (shin) is uncertain to be available for Thursday's game against the Texans after exiting Sunday's 24-22 win over the Dolphins, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
story: The Colts finished the Week 10 win without both of their top two cornerbacks, as Sauce Gardner (calf) also made an early exit. Both Ward and Gardner are in danger of missing Thursday's game against the Texans, which could open up more snaps in the secondary for Justin Walley, Kenneth Harris and Kapena Gushiken.

headline: Ward (shin) is questionable to return against the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Ward sustained the injury in the third quarter and was carted to the locker room, where he's undergoing tests to determine whether he can return. Kenneth Harris and Kapena Gushiken are both in line for more defensive snaps in the secondary for as long as Ward is out of the game.

headline: Ward (groin) is active for Sunday's game against Pittsburgh.
story: Ward ended the practice week Friday by logging a full session, though his participation wasn't enough to avoid a questionable tag. The veteran has since been cleared to play in Week 5, meaning he will start opposite Sauce Gardner.

headline: Ward (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
story: Ward registered an LP-LP-FP practice log, and while he's been tagged as questionable, he's probably closer to probable for Sunday's game given his full practice participation Friday. If he's not cleared to play, then Cam Taylor-Britt would be the top candidate to start opposite Sauce Gardner at outside cornerback.

headline: McGowan (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
story: DJ Giddens is set to inherit change-of-pace duties behind Jonathan Taylor in McGowan's absence. McGowan, who injured his hamstring in the Week 11 loss to the Texans, will have a bye to heal before possibly returning against the Eagles in Week 14.

headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said that McGowan will miss some time after injuring his hamstring in Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Texans, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports.
story: McGowan went down with the injury while returning a kickoff in the first half of the Week 11 loss. The rookie seventh-round pick had been solidified as the top backup to starting running back Jonathan Taylor, but DJ Giddens now is positioned to serve as Taylor's main understudy for however long McGowan is sidelined. McGowan can be safely ruled out for the Week 12 game against the Giants, though a Week 13 bye could help the 25-year-old back avoid additional absences beyond that.

headline: McGowan (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Thursday's game against the Texans, Jane Slater of NFL Network reports.
story: McGowan was injured just before halftime while returning a kickoff. He was deemed questionable to return at the beginning of the third quarter and subsequently was ruled out shortly thereafter. The rookie running back gained seven yards on three carries and caught his only target for one yard before exiting while adding 117 yards on three kickoff returns. Jonathan Taylor should continue to get most of the work at running back for the Colts for the rest of the game, and DJ Giddens should handle whatever backfield snaps that Taylor doesn't get.

headline: McGowan is dealing with a hamstring injury and is questionable to return to Thursday's Week 11 game against Houston.
story: McGowan appeared to get injured while returning a kickoff just before halftime. The rookie running back had three carries for seven yards and one catch for one yard before getting hurt. Should McGowan not be able to return to action Thursday, Jonathan Taylor would likely get an even bigger share of carries for the Colts, and DJ Giddens should get more opportunities as well.

headline: McGowan rushed 12 times for 77 yards and a touchdown and returned two kickoffs for 61 yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: The rookie had shown well in recent weeks while trade speculation swirled around Jonathan Taylor, and even though the latter ultimately stayed put at the deadline, McGowan still compiled a new career high in rush attempts and rushing yards. The Kentucky product also followed up his first career rushing touchdown in Week 9 against the Cowboys with a four-yard scoring run early in the second quarter Sunday, and McGowan was also productive in his returner role. While Taylor should remain the de facto top backfield option for the Colts, McGowan should remain in an elevated role for what remains of Indianapolis' non-contending season.

headline: McGowan rushed six times for 45 yards and a touchdown and brought in his only target for minus-3 yards in the Colts' 27-23 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday.
story: McGowan recorded his first NFL touchdown on a two-yard run in the first quarter, perhaps a harbinger of a larger role as early as next Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Dolphins. McGowan came just a rush yard short of equaling his career-best tally in that category, and if Jonathan Taylor is indeed moved off the roster by Tuesday's trade deadline, the former would be in line to serve as the lead back moving forward.

headline: McGowan rushed five times for 29 yards and returned four kickoffs for 103 yards Sunday in a loss to the Jaguars.
story: McGowan's best run was a 16-yarder up the middle midway through the third quarter to take the ball to Jacksonville's three-yard line. That set up Indianapolis' only touchdown in the blowout loss. McGowan logged a modest 15 offensive snaps to starter Jonathan Taylor's 38, but the former outgained Taylor on the ground, 29-23. Meanwhile, DJ Giddens paced the Colts with 43 rushing yards on six totes. The big story, of course, is that the Colts are entertaining trade offers on Taylor, and if the star RB is ultimately dealt, McGowan and Giddens both figure to take on significantly larger roles, though it's unclear which of the two would become the starter. With that in mind, it's worth noting that Giddens didn't enter until the fourth quarter and racked up all of his yardage in garbage time.

headline: McGowan turned 11 carries into 46 yards, caught his only target for two yards and added 140 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: McGowan played a season-high 31 percent of the team's offensive snaps, and as a result, he was able to set new highs in both carries and rushing yards. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded in the coming weeks, the rookie would stand to operate as the team's lead back following Taylor's departure. On the season, McGowan has rushed 34 times for 134 yards and reeled in four of five targets for 12 yards while compiling 566 kickoff-return yards over seven contests so far.

headline: McGowan took four carries for 27 yards during Sunday's 26-20 loss versus the Titans.
story: McGowan played exactly 19 offensive snaps for the third straight week Sunday, and, although he was slightly less involved than he has been of late in terms of touches, he managed a career-best 6.8 yards per carry in Week 6. He's merely a change-of-pace back as long as three-time Pro Bowler Jonathan Taylor is healthy, but he has the physical traits to become a workhorse should that not be the case at any point this season.

headline: McGowan turned six carries into 31 yards and caught one of two targets for seven yards during Sunday's 30-13 win over the Commanders in London. He also returned four kickoffs for 102 yards.
story: McGowan actually saw most of his offensive output in the second quarter with four carries for 18 yards and his seven-yard catch. Most of his on-field production figures to come on special teams as a returner, but the rookie seventh-rounder would be poised for RB1 duties if Jonathan Taylor misses time. The Colts will hit the road for Week 5 against the Steelers this Sunday.

headline: Curry underwent surgery to repair a ligament tear in his wrist earlier this week and will be sidelined for the rest of the 2026 season, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.
story: Curry was placed on the Colts' injured reserve Tuesday, and head coach Shane Steichen informed reporters Wednesday that the rookie sixth-rounder's wrist injury was severe enough for him to require season-ending surgery. Curry will end his first NFL campaign with 26 tackles (14 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and two fumble recoveries across 11 regular-season games. His absence means Carl Lawson, Jaylahn Tuimoloau and George Gumbs are all in line for more rotational snaps at defensive end.

headline: The Colts placed Curry (undisclosed) on injured reserve Tuesday.
story: In a corresponding move, Indianapolis signed veteran defensive end Carl Lawson from its practice squad to its 53-man roster. Over the first 11 weeks of the regular season, Curry recorded 26 tackles (14 solo) including 1.0 sacks and two fumble recoveries on defense, but most of his snaps came on special teams. He'll have to miss at least the next four games as he recovers.

headline: Gardner (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Gardner did not play in the Colts' Week 11 loss to the Texans due to a calf injury. The cornerback has recovered since Thursday's contest and is all set to practice in full throughout Week 12 prep. Gardner's fellow starting cornerback Charvarius Ward (knee) also missed Week 11 and was a limited participant Wednesday, meaning the Colts could get both corners back for Sunday against the Giants.

headline: Gardner (calf) is inactive for Thursday night's game against the Texans.
story: The cornerback has a history of calf issues, and the Colts, in the middle of a lost season, have no reason to push Gardner to play on a short week. With Charvarius Ward (knee) also out, Indy is down its top two cornerbacks against a pass-heavy Houston offense.

headline: According to Jane Slater of NFL Network, Gardner (calf) is not in line to play Thursday night against the Texans.
story: Gardner is officially listed as questionable for the contest after being listed as a 'DNP' from Monday through Wednesday. His reported looming absence represents a hit to the Colts' Week 11 secondary that will be contending with the WR trio of Nico Collins, Xavier Hutchinson and Tank Dell on Thursday. Official confirmation of the cornerback's availability will, in any case, arrive once Indy's inactives are posted ahead of the team's 8:15 pm ET kickoff.

headline: Gardner (calf) is listed as questionable for Thursday's game against the Texans.
story: Gardner was held out of all three practice sessions during Week 11 prep while recovering from a calf injury that he sustained against the Dolphins on Sunday. He hasn't been ruled out for Thursday's AFC South game despite the lack of practice reps, but if he joins Charvarius Ward (knee) on the inactive list, then the Colts would turn to a combination of Johnathan Edwards, Kapena Gushiken and Kenneth Harris to serve as the starting outside cornerbacks.

headline: Gardner (calf) was listed as a DNP for Monday's walkthrough practice.
story: Gardner suffered a left calf injury during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Per James Boyd of The Athletic, head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that Gardner's injury puts the fifth-year cornerback in jeopardy of missing Thursday's game against the Texans. If Gardner joins Charvarius Ward (knee) on the sidelines, then Johnathan Edwards, Kapena Gushiken and Kenneth Harris would be the top candidates to start at outside corner for Thursday's AFC South tilt.

headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen reported Gardner suffered a left calf injury during Sunday's 24-22 win over the Dolphins and may not play Thursday versus Houston, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
story: Gardner did not return to Sunday's meeting with Miami and is now in danger of missing Thursday's game against the Texans. With Charvarius Ward (shin) also not a lock to suit up against Houston, there could be more snaps for Kenneth Harris and Kapena Gushiken alongside Justin Walley.

headline: Gardner (calf) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.
story: Gardner has been working through a calf issue all season, and it appears the injury has cropped up again in Week 10. Charvarius Ward (shin) is also questionable to return, so the Colts will need to rely more heavily on Justin Walley, Kapena Gushiken and Kenneth Harris at corner.

headline: Gardner (calf) practiced in full Thursday.
story: Gardner departed Indianapolis' Week 6 loss to Tennessee due to a calf issue and didn't play Week 7 versus Minnesota. However, he practiced in a limited capacity this Wednesday, and with a full practice under his belt one day later, Gardner appears good to go for Sunday's clash in Jacksonville. That should be a big boost to the Colts' secondary after Cam Taylor-Britt (groin) landed on IR on Tuesday.

headline: Gardner (calf) was estimated as a limited participant on the Colts' official injury report Wednesday.
story: Indianapolis held only a walkthrough practice Wednesday, but the team gave indication Gardner may have made progress in his recovery from the calf issue that sidelined him in Week 7. He'll still likely have to log a full practice Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Gardner (calf) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
story: The decision doesn't come as much of a surprise, given that Gardner is considered week-to-week due to a calf injury that he picked up during the Colts' Week 6 loss to the Titans. Cam Taylor-Britt will likely start opposite Charvarius Ward at outside cornerback in the absence of Gardner, whose next chance to play is Week 8 against the Jaguars on Nov. 1.

headline: Gardner was diagnosed with a mild left calf strain following an MRI on Monday and is considered week-to-week, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Gardner was unable to return to Sunday's 26-20 loss to Tennessee after going down with the calf injury in the third quarter. While the Colts are confident that the calf strain won't result in an extended absence, the two-time Pro Bowl cornerback appears likely be sidelined for the team's Week 7 game versus the Vikings. Gardner has gotten off to a lackluster start to his first full season in Indianapolis, logging 17 tackles, four pass breakups and no interceptions through the team's first six games.

headline: Gardner (calf) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Titans, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.
story: Gardner exited the third quarter of Sunday's game with a calf injury. The cornerback returned to the locker room with what appears to be a significant issue. Cam Taylor-Britt is in at outside cornerback opposite Charvarius Ward.

headline: When addressing the press Wednesday, Pierce (heel) noted that the offseason procedure he underwent this past March was done because he was dealing with heel pain that impacted his Achilles, Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports.
story: Additionally, Pierce acknowledged that playing in Week 1 was a bit lofty, per Bowen, with the WR saying Wednesday that he was still managing some pain at that stage. In any case, Pierce indicated that he's confident that his current recovery plan will lead to a full return to health. When that will be remains to be seen, but the 2022 second-rounder is still on IR ahead of Week 12, with the Colts presumably not planning to rush him back given the team's 3-8 record in a campaign that's been marked by the team moving several key players ahead of the trade deadline.

headline: Head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that Pierce continues to rehab his left heel injury, and the wideout hasn't been ruled out for a return from injured reserve before the end of the season, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
story: Steichen rebuffed a report Sunday from Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, who relayed that the Colts were planning to "exercise great caution" by holding Pierce out for the season as he works his way back from an aggravation of his surgically repaired heel. However, given the 3-8 Colts' place in the standings in addition to their $114 million investment in Pierce, Steichen acknowledged that the 26-year-old wideout still faces an uphill battle to make it back from IR before season's end if he's anything less than 100 percent. According to James Boyd of The Athletic, Steichen said that Pierce currently is "doing plyometrics" and "running" after landing on IR on Sept. 26, but it's unclear how close Pierce may be to practicing.

headline: Pierce's season "is almost certainly over" due to the heel injury that landed the wideout on IR on Sept. 26, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network.
story: The 3-8 Colts traded both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen ahead of the NFL trade deadline, and now it appears they'll err on the side of caution with Pierce for the remainder of what has turned into a lost season for the team. With that in mind, Pierce will be able to turn his focus toward returning to full health in advance of the 2027 NFL campaign. Heading into next Sunday's game against the Giants, the Colts will proceed with a WR corps comprised of Laquon Treadwell, Deion Burks, Anthony Gould, Ashton Dulin, Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and Quez Watkins.

headline: When asked Wednesday whether Pierce (heel) has a chance to return from IR this season, Colts head coach Shane Steichen was noncommittal, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
story: "We'll see. Like I said last week, he's still in that rehab process, and I'm not going to put a timetable on return," Steichen noted of the wideout, who's been on IR since Sept. 26. At 2-7, the Colts were sellers ahead of the NFL's trade deadline, so the team presumably has no reason rush Pierce back. With Keenan Allen and Josh Downs no longer in the mix, Indy's healthy WRs for now are Ashton Dulin, Laquon Treadwell, Anthony Gould, Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.

headline: When asked Wednesday when Pierce (heel) might be able to return to practice, Colts head coach Shane Steichen noted that he "can't put a timetable on it right now," Kevin Bowen of 107.5 The Fan Indianapolis reports.
story: Steichen said that Pierce, who has been on IR since Sept. 26, is currently rehabbing his injury, but the wideout's return is clearly not imminent. At 2-6, the Colts, who are already sellers ahead of the NFL trade deadline, have little incentive to rush Pierce back. Meanwhile, fellow WR Josh Downs has asked to be dealt, a situation that further clouds the team's pass-catching corps ahead of Week 9.

headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that Pierce (heel) will "most likely not" have his 21-day practice window opened in Week 8, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.
story: A couple weeks ago, Pierce shed the cast that he had been wearing to protect his surgically repaired left heel, but the wideout looks like he'll remain limited to rehab work for at least another week before potentially making his return to practice. In Pierce's continued absence, the Colts will lean on Josh Downs, Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell to serve as their primary receiver trio, though none of the three have been consistent fantasy producers while quarterback Daniel Jones (4:7 TD:INT, 5.8 yards per attempt) has struggled mightily through the first seven weeks of the season.

headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that Pierce (heel) won't have his 21-day practice window opened in Week 7, Nathan Brown of The Indianapolis Star reports.
story: Pierce now has spent the requisite four games on injured reserve after re-injuring his surgically repaired left heel in the Colts' Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, but he'll need some more time to complete a rehab program before getting back on the practice field. Given the recurring nature of Pierce's injury in addition to the significant financial investment in him, the Colts are likely to take a deliberate approach in bringing the wideout back from IR.

headline: Pierce was spotted without a cast on his left ankle/heel Wednesday, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
story: It's a sign that Pierce is progressing in his recovery from a left heel injury that he aggravated during the Colts' Week 2 overtime loss to the Chiefs. The earliest he is eligible to return from injured reserve is Week 7 against the Vikings, and while Pierce opted for rehab and avoided surgery, Boyd believes that the fifth-year wide receiver is not close to a return. Josh Downs popped up on Wednesday's injury report with a hamstring injury, so Keenan Allen could be the Colts' top wide receiver for Sunday's AFC South showdown against the Titans.

headline: Taylor will be joined in the backfield in Sunday's game against the Giants by Anthony Richardson, who was named the Colts' new starting quarterback after Daniel Jones was cut Friday, Mike Chappell of Fox 59 News Indianapolis reports.
story: Taylor is slated to take his first extended snaps alongside Richardson since the 2024 season, when the two started together 10 times. The threat that Richardson presented to defenses as a runner seemed to aid Taylor's own effectiveness, as the running back averaged 4.8 yards per carry and scored eight touchdowns over that 10-game stretch. Now two years later, the Colts have a much less formidable offensive line in place and few established pass-catching weapons that defenses need to hone in on, so Taylor will likely be hard-pressed to match the lofty production he previously achieved with Richardson under center. Additionally, the 3-8 Colts may be cognizant of not overworking Taylor amid a losing season, though the loss of top backup Seth McGowan (hamstring) for at least Week 12 may result in Taylor seeing a slight uptick in opportunities after he played fewer than 70 percent of snaps in each of the last five games and averaged 16.6 touches in those contests.

headline: Taylor rushed 11 times for 21 yards and brought in four of five targets for six yards in the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
story: Taylor put some distance between himself and promising rookie backfield mate Seth McGowan in terms of workload, as the former outpaced his teammate in carries by an 11-3 margin, even with the latter exiting before halftime with a hamstring injury. However, the extra opportunity was a moot point, as Taylor couldn't find any space to operate as either a runner or receiver. Daniel Jones' mediocre play under center certainly isn't helping the ground attack's cause, and Taylor now has recorded less than 50 rushing yards in three of the last four contests. The star running back will have some additional time to prepare for a relatively favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Taylor rushed 16 times for 83 yards and brought in two of four targets for 20 yards in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Indianapolis.
story: Taylor made it through the trade deadline unscathed after rumors swirled around a possible change of scenery, but the talented back still split plenty of work with rookie backfield mate Seth McGowan, who logged 12 carries. Taylor still remained the No. 1 option and was the only one of the two to see any targets, and the rushing yardage total was his best since Week 7, just before serious trade speculation began. Taylor is staying put for the rest of the campaign, but it seems likely that he'll continue ceding a fair share of touches to McGowan moving forward.

headline: The Colts informed Taylor that he won't be traded before Tuesday's deadline, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
story: In order to move Taylor, Indianapolis was reportedly seeking a blockbuster trade package on par with what Carolina received in exchange for Christian McCaffrey back in 2022, but Pelissero relays that inquiring teams weren't willing to meet that price tag. As a result, Taylor -- who is under contract through 2028 -- will stick around in Indianapolis through the remainder of the campaign, though it's possible that the Colts entertain trade offers for the 27-year-old running back again during the offseason.

headline: Taylor rushed 13 times for 46 yards and brought in all five targets for 18 yards in the Colts' 27-23 loss to the Cowboys on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Taylor suited up for what might have been his final game in a Colts uniform with Tuesday's trade deadline looming, and the star running back had a positively ordinary day. Taylor couldn't fully exploit a vulnerable Cowboys defense, and the fumble they forced from him early in the fourth quarter at Dallas' 20-yard line cost Indianapolis what seemed like a sure scoring opportunity. Taylor has seen reduced usage in the last two games as rumors have swirled about a potential trade, and James Boyd of The Athletic reports that Taylor answered "I don't know. I know as much as you" when asked about whether Sunday had marked his last game as a Colt. Taylor declined to confirm whether he'd requested a trade, and the next 48 hours will bring clarity on whether he'll still be helming the team's ground attack in Week 10 against the Dolphins.

headline: The Colts have an offer of "at least a second-round pick and more" on the table for Taylor but are "holding out for more," Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Despite the Colts' 2-6 start to the season, Taylor has remained the engine that drives the offense, racking up 169 touches for 812 yards from scrimmage and eight rushing TDs. The seventh-year pro thus sits 188 total yards shy of reaching 1,000 such yards for the sixth time in his career, so if the right offer crosses Indianapolis' desk, he'd be a vast upgrade for most backfields in the NFL.

headline: Taylor was a full participant at Thursday's practice, and Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports that both Taylor and head coach Shane Steichen have maintained that Taylor will play Sunday against the Cowboys despite ongoing trade rumors surrounding the star running back.
story: "You can't avoid it," Taylor said of the trade rumors. "But it's more about trying to block that out." Taylor's preparing for what could well be his last game as a member of the Colts. Per NFL reporter Jordan Schultz, the 2-6 Colts have received trade calls on numerous players including Taylor, but Indianapolis doesn't intend to complete any additional trades prior to the conclusion of Sunday's game.

headline: Taylor rushed eight times for 23 yards and brought in four of five targets for 24 yards in the Colts' 42-7 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Taylor opened the game in his usual starting role with trade rumors swirling around him, and the star running back finished with a wholly unremarkable performance. Taylor ultimately ceded plenty of snaps to backfield mates Seth McGowan and DJ Giddens, the likeliest heir-apparent candidates if Taylor is indeed moved to another team in the coming days. Taylor had exceeded 90 rushing yards in back-to-back games and on five occasions overall heading into Week 8, so even if his Colts tenure finishes with Sunday's whimper, he'll have plenty to offer in a new destination.

headline: The Colts are fielding trade offers for Taylor, and while the asking price currently appears to be "too high," a deal seems likely to happen, per NFL reporter Jordan Schultz.
story: Adam Schefter of ESPN and Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Saturday morning that the Colts are willing to trade Taylor, but Schultz's report includes a new wrinkle, namely that a trade is more likely than not to occur. The Vikings, Giants, Broncos, Bengals and Packers are among the teams mentioned by Schultz that have checked in with Indianapolis regarding the seventh-year pro, who has looked like his usual dynamic self this season with 765 yards from scrimmage and eight rushing TDs on 157 touches in seven contests.

headline: Taylor is being made available via trade by the Colts, Adam Schefter of ESPN  reports.
story: Taylor himself was not requesting a trade earlier in the week, but Indianapolis' recent flurry of moves opened the possibility that the star running back would also be moved in the team's teardown before a rebuild. The Colts moved on from Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner and got significant draft capital from the Seahawks and 49ers in return. Now a market is forming for Taylor, 27, who could help put a contender over the top. Per Schefter, the Colts are seeking a deal similar to what the Panthers got in 2022 when they traded Christian McCaffrey.

headline: Taylor told reporters Thursday that he hasn't requested a trade out of Indianapolis, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports. "I haven't heard anything, and I can't control that," Taylor said regarding the possibility of being traded. "Obviously, you guys know that I'm always proud to wear the horseshoe, proud to be here."
story: The 2-5 Colts have gone into sell mode after firing GM Chris Ballard. Indianapolis traded away guard Quenton Nelson and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to Seattle and San Francisco, respectively, but both of those players are on expiring contracts. Taylor signed a two-year, $44 million extension with the Colts in August, so the team may not feel as much urgency to trade him, and the star running back confirmed he hasn't requested a trade. Several teams have reportedly inquired about Taylor's availability.

headline: Taylor carried the ball 18 times for 95 yards and a touchdown and caught two of three targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: The Colts managed only 218 yards of offense in total, and Taylor had nearly as many rushing yards as Daniel Jones had passing yards. Taylor also scored his team's only TD on a 38-year-old dash in the first quarter. The star RB is still looking for his first 100-yard rushing performance of the season, but he's topped 90 yards in five of seven games and has produced 100-plus scrimmage yards four times while racking up eight scores on the ground. Taylor will face another tough run defense in Week 8 versus the Jaguars.

headline: Indianapolis signed Lawson from its practice squad to its 53-man roster Tuesday.
story: In a corresponding transaction, the Colts placed rookie sixth-round defensive end Caden Curry on injured reserve. In his one appearance so far this season back in Week 8 at Jacksonville, Lawson played just eight defensive snaps.

headline: The Colts signed Lawson to their practice squad Wednesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Lawson spent most of last season on the Ravens' practice squad, suiting up for just one regular-season game, but he'll now get a fresh start with a new club. With veteran defensive end Arden Key expected to miss multiple games with a hamstring injury, it makes some sense that Indianapolis would try to add some organizational depth on the edge.

headline: The Colts signed Buechele off the Bills' practice squad Tuesday.
story: Buechele takes the QB No. 3 spot in Indy behind Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard. The 28-year-old spent the previous 11 weeks of the NFL season with Buffalo, splitting time on the active roster and practice squad.

headline: Buechele reverted to the Bills' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: Buechele was inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets. The journeyman could see another elevated for Sunday's Week 11 game against the Jets to serve as an emergency option behind Josh Allen and Kyle Allen.

headline: The Bills elevated Buechele from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
story: It's the first time this season that Buechele has been elevated from the practice squad. He'll likely operate as the Bills' emergency third quarterback behind Josh Allen and Kyle Allen for Sunday's game against the Jets.

headline: Giddens will likely move up to the No. 2 RB role for the Colts in the short term, as Seth McGowan is expected to miss time due to a hamstring injury, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
story: Head coach Shane Steichen said Monday that McGowan "will miss some time" but didn't specify how long the absence may be. For however long McGowan is sidelined, Giddens figures to serve as Jonathan Taylor's backup at running back. Giddens has shown some flashes this season in limited playing time, amassing 48 yards on seven carries (6.9 YPC) and catching his only target for 11 yards over three games.

headline: Giddens rushed one time for five yards and caught his lone target for 11 yards in Thursday night's 26-3 loss to the Texans.
story: With Seth McGowan (hamstring) exiting early with an injury, Giddens spelled Jonathan Taylor and played seven offensive snaps. Through three games this season, Giddens has rushed seven times for 48 yards and registered one catch for 11 yards. If McGowan's injury costs him time, Giddens figures to handle RB2 duties in his absence.

headline: Giddens played two offensive snaps and didn't show up on the box score otherwise during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Giddens barely saw the field during Sunday's win, and his two offensive snaps were well behind fellow running backs Jonathan Taylor (40) and Seth McGowan (17). Giddens -- a fifth-round pick of the Colts in the 2025 NFL Draft -- has seen little playing time since making his 2026 regular-season debut in Week 8 against the Jaguars. His role will likely stay minimal for Week 11 against the Texans on Thursday.

headline: Giddens was active but didn't play in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
story: Giddens didn't see any action after turning six carries into 43 yards in Week 8 against the Jaguars. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, Giddens would stand to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind rookie Seth McGowan if Taylor departs.

headline: Giddens racked up 43 yards on six carries in Indianapolis' Week 8 loss to Jacksonville on Sunday.
story: Giddens entered Sunday having not logged a snap this season, but he got an opportunity in the blowout loss and made the most of it, ripping off a pair of 12-yard runs on the way to a team-leading 43 rushing yards. However, it must be noted that he didn't enter until the game was far out of reach in the fourth quarter, so all of his production came in garbage time. Still, it was a meaningful performance by Giddens in the context of Indianapolis fielding trade offers for star RB Jonathan Taylor amidst a lost season. Should Taylor indeed be dealt, Giddens would immediately take on a more prominent role in the Colts backfield along with seventh-round rookie Seth McGowan.

headline: Giddens did not play a single snap during Sunday's 13-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: Giddens dressed for Sunday's game, but he observed the entire contest from the sidelines while Seth McGowan served as the Colts' lone backup to Jonathan Taylor. Giddens has yet to play a snap this regular season, but that could change if the Colts -- who have a 2-5 record -- are sellers at the trade deadline and opt to send Taylor to another team.

headline: Brown went without a target while playing eight of the Colts' 50 offensive snaps in Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Texans.
story: For the second week in a row, Brown ended up seeing more snaps on special teams (11) than offense. Through four games with Indianapolis, Brown has drawn just one target, which he turned into a seven-yard reception during a Week 6 loss to the Titans.

headline: Brown was signed to the 53-man roster Tuesday.
story: Brown is currently listed on the depth chart behind Tyler Warren, Mo Alie-Cox and Drew Ogletree, so it doesn't appear he will have a prominent role anytime soon. The 32-year-old has played for the Browns, Texans, Patriots, Seahawks and Cardinals since entering the NFL in 2017, totaling 74 catches (102 targets) for 752 yards and three touchdowns in 92 regular-season appearances.

headline: The Colts announced Friday that Leonard will act as Anthony Richardson's backup at quarterback, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports.
story: The Colts released starting quarterback Daniel Jones after a disastrous 26-3 Thursday night loss to the Texans in Week 11. With Richardson in line to start moving forward, Leonard is the next QB up on the depth chart. The second-year pro has been with the Colts since 2025, when he played in five games, completing 39 of 67 attempts for 415 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions. He also rushed six times for 27 yards and two touchdowns.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Colts' emergency third quarterback for Thursday's game at Houston.
story: Leonard will retain the same role he's played for Indianapolis all season in Week 11, being ready on the sidelines in case both Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson are knocked out of action. There have been some holes in the Texans' pass defense through their first nine games of the campaign, but it's unclear whether the Colts have pass-catching personnel capable of taking advantage.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Colts' emergency third quarterback against the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: As he's done all season, Leonard will be Indianapolis' emergency QB3, which means he is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cowboys but is listed as the team's emergency quarterback, Abby Halpin of the team's official site reports.
story: As has been the case throughout the season, Leonard is a healthy scratch. However, he will be available if Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Jaguars on Sunday, JJ Stankevitz of the Colts' official site reports.
story: As the emergency QB3, Leonard is now allowed to see the field Sunday unless both Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson are taken out of the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Colts' emergency third quarterback against the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Leonard will continue to serve as the team's emergency QB3, and as such, he is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson are removed from the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Colts' emergency third quarterback against the Titans on Sunday.
story: Leonard will once again serve as the emergency QB3, meaning that he is restricted from playing Sunday unless both Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Leonard (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Steelers, though he is listed as the team's emergency quarterback.
story: Leonard is inactive once again. However, as has been the case in previous weeks, Leonard will be available if Daniel Jones and Anthony Richardson exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Leonard is inactive for Sunday's game against the Commanders in London as the Colts' emergency No. 3 quarterback.
story: Leonard hasn't been active for any of the Colts' first four games after Anthony Richardson beat him out for the No. 2 job coming out of the preseason. The second-year player out of Notre Dame will only be available in the event both starter Daniel Jones and Richardson are unable to finish the game.

headline: Boettcher recorded six tackles (three solo) during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
story: Boettcher finished Thursday's game tied for the fourth-most tackles on the Colts. The rookie fourth-rounder has started in each of Indianapolis' last three games, which has lined up with the absence of Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee, IR). Boettcher is up to 50 tackles (16 solo) through 11 regular-season games.

headline: Boettcher recorded 12 tackles (four solo) in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
story: With Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) inactive against Dallas, Boettcher saw a spike in playing time alongside CJ Allen at linebacker for the Colts. The fourth-round rookie Boettcher played a season-high 73 percent of the defensive snaps and recorded his first career game with double-digit tackles.

headline: Boettcher (groin) was a full participant at the Colts' practice Wednesday.
story: Boettcher appears to be on track to return to action Sunday versus the Cowboys after missing the team's last two contests with a groin issue. The 24-year-old will likely be back in his starting role at strongside linebacker against Dallas.

headline: Boettcher (groin) is inactive Week 8 against the Jaguars.
story: Boettcher seemed like a long shot to play despite entering the week with a "questionable" status, as he failed to take the practice field in any capacity all week. While the rookie misses his second consecutive games, Austin Ajiake and Jaylon Carlies are candidates to see extra reps at linebacker.

headline: Boettcher (groin) is questionable for Sunday's matchup against the Jaguars.
story: Boettcher missed Week 7 due to a groin issue and didn't practice at all this week. Despite his trio of DNPs, the Colts think he at least has a chance of being ready to play Sunday. Boettcher has logged 25 tackles (eight solo) through his first six NFL contests.

headline: Boettcher (groin) is inactive against the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Boettcher strung together a DNP-FP-DNP practice log during Week 7 prep due to a groin injury, but he has not been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday. Germaine Pratt, Austin Ajiake and Tahj Chambers are all in line for more defensive snaps in the absence of Boettcher, whose next chance to play is Week 8 against the Jaguars on Nov. 1.

headline: Adebawore finished Thursday's 26-3 loss to the Texans with seven tackles (four solo), including 1.0 sacks.
story: Adebawore recorded his fifth sack of the season early in the third quarter, when he took down C.J. Stroud for a seven-yard loss. Adebawore has already set a career-high in sacks through 11 regular-season games and has accumulated 31 tackles (15 solo), one defense and a scoop-and-score in 2026.

headline: Adebawore agreed Tuesday with the Colts on a two-year, $35 million contract extension, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
story: Per Pelissero, the deal includes a $13 million signing bonus and $22.5 million in new money through next season. A 2023 fourth-round draft pick, Adebawore had been in the final year of his rookie deal and was considered a potential trade chip leading up to the Nov. 10 deadline, but the Colts have instead elected to keep him around on a longer-term basis. Through the Colts' first eight games of the season, 25-year-old defensive tackle has matched the career-best total of four sacks he posted over a 17-game slate in 2025. Adebawore has also added 19 tackles and two pass breakups.

headline: Adebawore finished Sunday's loss to Minnesota with five tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a defensed pass.
story: The Vikings have stood out this season for their ability to get to the passer, but Adebawore gave them some of their own medicine Sunday. He brought down Kyler Murray twice in the fourth quarter as Indianapolis tried to stage a comeback. Adebawore is up to 4.0 sacks through seven games, so he's already tied the career-best regular-season mark he established last year.

headline: Haulcy logged nine tackles (four solo) and an interception during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
story: The rookie third-rounder recorded the first interception of his career in the first quarter, when a pass from C.J. Stroud intended for Nico Collins bounced off Haulcy's helmet, off the hands of Cam Bynum and into Haulcy's arms. The LSU product is up to 53 tackles (30 solo) and three pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

headline: Haulcy (ankle) was a full participant at Thursday's practice.
story: Haulcy missed the Colts' Week 9 loss to Dallas due to an ankle injury and sat out practice Wednesday, but his return without limitations Thursday suggests the rookie third-round pick is ready to return to action. He's poised to reclaim the starting strong safety role Sunday against the Dolphins.

headline: Haulcy (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
story: Haulcy was added to the injury report last Friday and ended up missing Sunday's loss to the Cowboys. With the third-round rookie safety inactive against Dallas, Hunter Wohler played 77 of 79 defensive snaps alongside Cam Bynum.

headline: Haulcy (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Cowboys, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
story: Haulcy appeared on Friday's injury report with an ankle injury. The strong safety initially entered the weekend listed as questionable but has now been downgraded to out ahead of Sunday's contest. Second-year safety Hunter Wohler is set to start at safety alongside Cam Bynum against the Cowboys.

headline: Haulcy (ankle) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus the Cowboys.
story: Haulcy was a surprise addition to the Colts' injury report Friday with an ankle injury, and his status for Week 9 is now in doubt. If he can't play Sunday, 2025 seventh-rounder Hunter Wohler could be called on to start at safety next to Cam Bynum.

headline: Haulcy produced nine tackles (five solo) in a loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
story: The game was mostly centered on defense, and Haulcy helped Indianapolis hang close with a team-leading nine stops. That was a season-best mark for the rookie safety, who has taken on a starting role in his debut NFL campaign. Haulcy has logged 36 tackles and two defensed passes through seven contests.

headline: Allen posted 16 tackles (seven solo) during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
story: It was a busy night for the rookie second-rounder, who finished with a career-high in stops while logging double-digit tackles for the third time this season. Allen has 45 total tackles over his last four outings, and most of that extra playing time has come in the absence of Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee, IR).

headline: Allen posted nine tackles (three solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Allen led the Colts in tackles Sunday, and he got to Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord for an eight-yard loss late in the fourth quarter. Allen also picked off McCord earlier in the fourth, although the play was nullified by an illegal contact penalty by Colts defensive back Kenneth Harris. Allen has logged at least 10 tackles in each of his last three outings, and he has accumulated 34 tackles (12 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass defenses across seven regular-season games.

headline: Allen recorded 10 tackles (three solo) and a pass breakup in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
story: With Akeem Davis-Gaither (knee) out versus Dallas, Allen played all 79 defensive snaps for Indy, marking the first time the second-round rookie has played 100 percent of the defensive snaps in a game. He's started back-to-back contests and is up to 25 tackles (nine solo), including 1.0 sacks, and the one pass breakup across six appearances this season.

headline: Allen (ankle) was listed as a full participant in Wednesday's walkthrough.
story: Allen was unable to play against the Vikings in Week 7 due to an ankle injury, but his full practice designation Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. The rookie second-rounder has served in a rotational role so far this season, but James Boyd of The Athletic relays that Allen is expected to step into a starting role moving forward, which could mean less defensive snaps for Bryce Boettcher (groin) and Jaylon Carlies.

headline: Allen (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings.
story: Allen was downgraded to out Saturday after being listed as questionable Friday. The rookie second-rounder will not be able to overcome his ankle injury in time for Sunday's contest, leaving the Colts' defensive depth thinner against the Vikings.

headline: Watkins caught one of his three targets for 26 yards during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.
story: Watkins played just five offensive snaps for the Colts in Thursday night's game. Despite playing only 10 percent of the offensive snaps, Watkins totaled the third-highest yardage by Colts pass catchers on the night with his 26-yard grab. The reserve wide receiver could see an expanded role down the stretch as the Colts experiment with starting quarterback Anthony Richardson in what is all but a lost season.

headline: The Colts signed Watkins from their practice squad to their 53-man roster Tuesday.
story: A spot on the 53-man roster opened up when Indianapolis placed linebacker Jaylon Carlies (neck) on IR, and the team elected to give Watkins the opening. The veteran wideout was elevated for Sunday's Week 10 win over Miami, but he didn't end up playing. With that said, there could be an opportunity for Watkins to garner some work in the passing game after Indianapolis traded Josh Downs to the Chiefs and Keenan Allen to the 49ers last week. Watkins last logged regular-season NFL action in 2023, when he caught 15 of 21 targets for 142 yards and a touchdown over nine games with the Eagles.

headline: Watkins reverted to the Colts' practice squad Monday.
story: Watkins was active for Sunday's win over the Dolphins but didn't play any snaps. The wide receiver has two more practice-squad elevations remaining this season before he would need to be signed to the Colts' 53-man roster in order to suit up on game days.

headline: The Colts elevated Watkins from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
story: The move gives the Colts more depth at wide receiver after the team traded Josh Downs and Keenan Allen to the Chiefs and 49ers, respectively, on Thursday. If Watkins sees the field against the Dolphins on Sunday, then it would mark his first regular-season appearance since 2023 as a member of the Eagles, when he appeared in nine regular-season games and accumulated 15 catches (on 21 targets) for 142 yards and a touchdown.

headline: The Colts signed Watkins to the practice squad Tuesday.
story: Watkins last appeared in a regular-season game for Philadelphia in 2023, where he caught 15 of 21 targets for 142 yards and one touchdown in nine games. The 28-year-old has since struggled to remain healthy. Should he see the field with the Colts, he will likely act as a depth piece at wide receiver.

headline: Dulin caught two of his four targets for 30 yards and assisted on two tackles on kick coverage during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.
story: Dulin played 22 offensive snaps and 10 special-teams snaps in the contest. The No. 4 wide receiver saw plenty of attention, catching 50 percent of his targets to accumulate the second-highest receiving yardage for the Colts, behind Anthony Gould's 48 yards.

headline: Dulin caught one of two targets for 30 yards and returned three kickoffs for 77 yards during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also recorded two tackles on special teams.
story: Even with Josh Downs and Keenan Allen being sent out at the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Dulin's 13 offensive snaps were fourth-most among Colts wide receivers behind Laquon Treadwell (52), Deion Burks (34) and Anthony Gould (32). Dulin did connect on a 30-yard pass from Daniel Jones late in the second quarter, which was a pivotal part of a nine-play, 92-yard drive that ended with a seven-yard touchdown catch by Treadwell. Dulin has logged catches of 55 and 30 yards in each of his last two outings, and he could be the Colts' WR3 for Thursday's AFC South tilt against the Texans if Gould is not cleared to play due to a toe injury.

headline: Head coach Shane Steichen said that Dulin will be one of the Colts receivers tasked with absorbing the snaps vacated by Keenan Allen, who was traded to the 49ers on Tuesday, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.
story: Steichen also mentioned Deion Burks and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine as other candidates to fill in at the outside receiver spot opposite Laquon Treadwell, while noting that Anthony Gould will serve as the Colts' starting slot receiver after the team also traded Josh Downs to the Chiefs on Tuesday. With Alec Pierce's (heel) return from injured reserve seemingly not imminent, Dulin could have a prime opportunity to see extended snaps over the next few weeks, provided he can hold off the likes of Burks and Westbrook-Ikhine for playing time. Dulin already made a bit of a splash in the Colts' Week 9 loss to the Cowboys, connecting with Daniel Jones on a 55-yard touchdown reception while also carrying once for a three-yard gain.

headline: Dulin caught one of two targets for a 55-yard touchdown in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. He added three rushing yards on one attempt.
story: Dulin caught a screen pass at the line of scrimmage and raced all the way down the left sideline for the touchdown on his big play to pull the Colts within three points at the end of the third quarter. He still ran just six routes on Daniel Jones' 38 dropbacks against Dallas, leaving Dulin out of the fantasy picture unless the Colts make some trades at the position before Tuesday's deadline.

headline: Dulin (hamstring) was a limited participant in practice Thursday.
story: That's two straight limited sessions to begin the week for Dulin after he missed the Colts' past two games due to a hamstring issue. The veteran wideout appears to be making progress in his recovery, as he didn't practice at all during Week 5 and Week 6 prep. Dulin's likelihood of returning for Sunday's matchup in Minnesota should gain clarity with the release of Friday's injury report and game designations.

headline: Dulin (hamstring) was a limited participant at the Colts' practice Wednesday.
story: Dulin was able to return to practice for the first time since suffering a hamstring injury in Week 4. The wide receiver will have two more chances to log a full practice before potentially returning to action Sunday versus the Vikings.

headline: Dulin (hamstring) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Joel A. Erickson of The Indianapolis Star reports.
story: Dulin was unable to participate in any Week 6 prep sessions. The wide receiver will miss a second consecutive game as he focuses on recovering from his hamstring issue. Deion Burks is set to be the No. 4 wide receiver for the Colts again.

headline: Dulin (hamstring) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Dulin sat out Sunday's game at Pittsburgh due to a hamstring injury, and he now appears to be trending towards missing a second game because of it. Unless he's able to return to practice in some capacity Friday, it's unlikely he'll be available in Week 6 versus the Titans.

headline: Dulin (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday's practice session.
story: Dulin has not been cleared to practice or play since sustaining a hamstring injury during the Colts' Week 4 win over the Commanders in London. He'll have two more chances to log at least a limited practice ahead of the Colts' AFC South showdown against the Titans on Sunday.

headline: Dulin (hamstring) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
story: Dulin likely sustained his hamstring injury in the Colts' Week 4 win over the Commanders. The wide receiver has not practiced since appearing on Wednesday's injury report with the issue and will likely need to miss some time. Deion Burks is set to be the No. 4 option at wide receiver in Dulin's absence.

headline: Dulin (hamstring) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Dulin popped up on the Colts' injury report Wednesday with a hamstring issue, and his availability for Week 5 is now in serious doubt. He'll probably have to return to practice in some capacity Friday to have a realistic chance of suiting up Sunday at Pittsburgh.

headline: Dulin didn't participate in Wednesday's practice due to a hamstring injury.
story: Dulin missed two consecutive games due to an ankle injury before being cleared to play against the Commanders in Week 4, when he caught three of six targets for 29 yards. He's now working through a different lower-body injury, but he'll have two more opportunities to return to practice ahead of Sunday's road game against the Steelers.

headline: Dulin (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Commanders in London.
story: Though he had been listed as questionable heading into the weekend, Dulin had always appeared likely to put an end to his two-game absence after practicing fully Thursday and Friday. Dulin projects to make his biggest impact on special teams when the Colts are at full strength at receiver, but he'll be needed to handle a depth role on offense Week 4 while fellow wideouts Keenan Allen (groin) and Darius Slayton (coach's decision) are inactive.

headline: Dulin (ankle) was a full participant in practice Thursday.
story: Dulin practiced for the first time since suffering an ankle injury that kept him out the past two games. While the 29-year-old split time on offense and special teams in Week 1, he could see more reps in the former capacity Sunday as a depth piece with Alec Pierce (heel, IR) unavailable. However, Keenan Allen (groin), Josh Downs, and Laquon Treadwell should still see reps before the eighth-year pro, although a downgrade on the part of Allen would bump Dulin up another notch on the depth chart.

headline: Dulin (ankle) is not practicing Wednesday, James Boyd of The Athletic reports.
story: Dulin has missed the past two games, and his practice week ahead of Week 4 is off on the wrong foot. With Alec Pierce (heel/IR) also out last Sunday against the Texans, the Colts used a three-wide set of Laquon Treadwell, Josh Downs and Keenan Allen.

headline: Burks was targeted three times for zero catches, had one kick return for 10 yards and made one tackle on kick coverage during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday night.
story: Burks was the No. 2 wide receiver for the Colts in the contest. Despite being targeted three times, the wide receiver could not haul in any passes from since-cut quarterback Daniel Jones. Burks played 32 offensive snaps and two special-teams snaps in the contest.

headline: Burks failed to haul in either of his two targets during the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. He also recorded one tackle on special teams.
story: With Josh Downs and Keenan Allen being shipped off at the Nov. 10 deadline, the Colts turned to Burks, Laquon Treadwell and Anthony Gould to serve as the top wideouts for Week 10. Burks' 34 offensive snaps were a season high and second among the team's wide receivers, but the rookie seventh-rounder failed to record a catch for the fifth time in 10 games, with one of his intended passes from Daniel Jones being intercepted midway through the second quarter. Gould is working through a toe injury, so Burks could step into a bigger role on offense against the Texans on Thursday.

headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Wednesday that Burks and Anthony Gould will step into larger roles after the team traded Keenan Allen and Josh Downs, Stephen Holder of ESPN.com reports.
story: A rookie seventh-round pick with 4.30 speed, Burks has caught six of nine targets for 60 yards across 49 routes (18.3 percent target rate, 1.22 yards per route). He won't necessarily see a lot of targets in an offense that runs through the RBs and TEs, but Burks should at least get far more playing time in the second half of the season, if only because the Colts' other wideouts are veterans with minimal history of production. Laquon Treadwell and Ashton Dulin are the other favorites for regular playing time, and Nick Westbrook-Ikhine is also on the roster.

headline: Burks played 17 of the Colts' 64 offensive snaps in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys, finishing with a zero-yard reception on his lone target.
story: A rookie seventh-round pick out of Oklahoma, Burks has seen sparse playing time through the Colts' first nine games. He's logged less than one-third of the snaps in each of those contests and has posted a 6-60-0 receiving line on nine targets go with 21 yards on three carries. Despite his modest output to date, Burks could nonetheless be primed for more opportunities in the Indianapolis passing game over the second half of the season. Tight end Tyler Warren will likely rank as the team's top pass-catching option, but the Colts should have plenty of targets left over after trading away Keenan Allen to the 49ers and Josh Downs to Kansas City on Tuesday, and with Alec Pierce (heel) lacking a clear timeline for his return.

headline: Shrader went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts during the Colts' 26-3 loss to the Texans on Thursday.
story: Shrader opened Thursday's scoring with a 34-yard field goal early in the first quarter. Those ended up being the only three points scored by the Colts, as Shrader missed a 56-yarder later in the quarter, and his 62-yarder in the second quarter was blocked by Logan Hall. It was the second time this season that Shrader has missed two kicks, and the third-year kicker now is 24-for-28 on field-goal attempts (including 9-for-12 on kicks from 50-plus yards) and 19-for-20 on extra-point tries through 11 regular-season games. His scoring potential figures to be lower for the rest of the season after the Colts waived Daniel Jones on Friday, which paves the way for Anthony Richardson to start under center in Week 12 against the Giants on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Shrader made his sole field-goal attempt and converted all three PATs in the Colts' 24-22 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Shrader sole field-goal attempt was a 51-yard make in the third quarter of Sunday's contest. The kicker moves to 23-for-25 on field-goal attempts and 19-for-20 on PATs through 10 games of the 2026 regular season.

headline: Shrader went 3-for-3 on field-goal tries and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys.
story: Shrader entered Week 9 having made just three field goals over the team's last three games, but he got back on track Sunday. The kicker made a 47-yard attempt in the third quarter before adding makes from 59 and 50 yards in the final quarter. Shrader has now converted multiple field-goal attempts in six contests this year, and he's gone 22-for-24 on field-goal tries, including 8-for-9 from 50-plus yards, over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Shrader made his sole PAT in the Colts' 42-7 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
story: Shrader did not have a very active night, making the sole kick he was called upon for. He's now 14-for-15 on PATs while remaining 19-for-21 on field-goal attempts through eight regular-season games in 2026.

headline: Shrader went 1-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only extra-point try during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings.
story: Shrader entered Week 7 without having missed a field-goal try over the team's first six contests, but he was unable to remain perfect. The kicker was able to make a 43-yard field goal as time expired in the first half, giving Indianapolis a 10-6 lead at the break. Shrader then missed a 56-yard try wide left in the third quarter before pushing a 48-yard attempt wide right in the fourth quarter. He has now gone 19-for-21 on field-goal tries while making 13 of 14 extra-point attempts over seven contests this season.

headline: Shrader made both of his field-goal attempts and both of his PATs in the Colts' 26-20 loss to the Titans on Sunday.
story: While the Colts' story of the day was a special teams failure due to a blocked punt returned for a Titans touchdown, Shrader had no part in the error. The kicker made field goals from 23 and 43 yards in the contest that kept the game close. Shrader is a perfect 18-for-18 on field-goal attempts and 12-for-13 on PATs through six regular-season contests in 2026.

headline: Shrader made all five of his field-goal attempts and converted on his lone point-after try during Sunday's 34-22 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
story: Quarterback Daniel Jones led the Colts on six offensive drives during Sunday's loss, though only one of those drives ended with a touchdown. That meant a busy day for Shrader, who made field goals from 57 and 56 yards in the first half before connecting on three more kicks from 22, 40 and 28 yards in the second. His five made field goals were his most in a game since Week 2 of the 2025 season, and he's attempted at least three field goals in each of the Colts' last four games. His 16 made field goals through five regular-season games leads the NFL, and he also leads all kickers with six made field goals from 50-plus yards. The Colts have a juicy Week 6 matchup against the 0-5 Titans on Oct. 18.

headline: Shrader went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his PATs in Sunday's 30-13 win over Washington.
story: Shrader was able to stay red-hot across the pond in London. The kicker nailed field goals from 48, 52 and 44 yards in the contest, remaining perfect on the season. Through four games, Shrader has gone 11-for-11 on field-goal tries, including 5-for-5 from 50-plus yards, and he's becoming one of the more reliable fantasy options in the league.

headline: Little (knee) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Little injured his knee in Week 11 against the Giants. However, he's been cleared to play Sunday after stringing together three consecutive limited practices and will start at left tackle against Tennessee.

headline: Little is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Giants due to a knee injury.
