story: Little started the game at left tackle. Wyatt Milum has entered the game on the Jaguars' offensive line.

headline: Hainsey (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: The Jaguars' center logged three limited practices this week but could miss a second straight contest after he was initially injured in the Week 10 win over Tennessee. Jonah Monheim started at center last Sunday.

headline: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen announced Wednesday that Hainsey (knee) is out for Sunday's game against the Giants, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Jonah Monheim will draw the start at center in place of Hainsey, who exited this past Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans due to a knee sprain, per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com. According to Fowler, Hainsey's knee injury isn't considered season-ending, but the veteran lineman is viewed as week-to-week and could be a candidate for injured reserve.

headline: Hainsey (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Hainsey appeared to injure his knee while blocking on a run play in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's contest. Jonah Monheim has taken over at center in Hainsey's absence.

headline: Hainsey has cleared the league's concussion protocol and will play against the Titans on Sunday.
story: Hainsey's practice reps were limited all week while he was in the league's concussion protocol. However, he has been given the green light to play in Sunday's AFC South tilt after passing an evaluation from an independent neurologist. Hainsey has started in each of the Jaguars' first eight games of the regular season.

headline: Dickerson (neck) does not have an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Dickerson did not play against the Giants in Week 11 due to a neck injury, but the UCLA product has been cleared by medical staff to play in Sunday's AFC South game. The UCLA product has 11 tackles (five solo) and one pass defense across nine games while operating in a rotational role on the Jaguars' interior defensive line.

headline: Dickerson (neck) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Giants.
story: A neck injury limited Dickerson's practice reps during Week 11 prep, and he has not been cleared by medical staff to play in Sunday's contest. Ruke Orhorhoro and Davon Godchaux will both see a bump in rotational snaps on the defensive interior line in the absence of Dickerson, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Titans on Nov. 29.

headline: Mekari (back) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Mekari got in three limited practices this week but will sit out after having his 21-day practice window opened earlier in the week. He's yet to play this season but appears to be knocking on the door of his season debut. Ezra Cleveland has been manning right guard for Jacksonville.

headline: The Jaguars designated Mekari (back) to return from injured reserve Wednesday.
story: Mekari now has a 21-day window for the Jaguars to return him to the active roster. The right guard returned to practice as a limited participant. If Mekari can upgrade to a full participant by Friday's session, there is a chance he could be activated for Sunday's game against the Titans. The Jaguars could just as easily take it slow with the veteran offensive lineman to ensure he is healthy and ready for his return to the field, so Ezra Cleveland may be in line for another start at right guard.

headline: Green (forearm) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Green has been a full practice participant since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 11. He's not quite ready to return, but with his 21-day window set to close, he would need to be activated from IR during Week 13 prep, otherwise he would be sidelined for the rest of the season. His next opportunity to play is Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Bears.

headline: Green (forearm) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
story: Green has strung together six consecutive full practices since being designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 11. He's not quite ready to be activated from IR, so his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 29. Green is in the final stages of his recovery from an elbow injury that he suffered in Week 1 against the Browns.

headline: Green (forearm) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
story: Green's 21-day practice window opened Nov. 11. The Jaguars' defensive end logged three consecutive full sessions in his return to practice but was ultimately deemed not ready to suit up for Week 10.

headline: The Jaguars designated Green (elbow) to return from injured reserve Wednesday.
story: Green landed on injured reserve in mid-September after suffering an elbow injury in Week 1 against the Browns. The Jaguars now have 21 days to activate Green from injured reserve, otherwise the Colorado product would be sidelined for the rest of the 2026 season.

headline: With Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) ruled out, Rodriguez is slated to operate as the Jaguars' top backfield option for Sunday's AFC South tilt against the Titans, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
story: Tuten was held out of practice all week due to a left ankle/foot injury that he aggravated during the Jaguars' Week 11 loss to the Giants. That means Rodriguez will take on the RB1 role for Sunday's game against a Titans defense that has given up at least 40 points in three consecutive games and ranks 25th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (127.1). Rodriguez has logged 63 carries for 261 yards (4.1 YPC) and four touchdowns and caught five of six targets for 49 yards across 10 regular-season games in 2026.

headline: Rodriguez rushed four times for 28 yards in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants. He added one catch for 13 yards on one target.
story: With the Jaguars chasing points and playing from behind most of the afternoon, Bhayshul Tuten and Rodrgiuez combined for just 14 carries, while Trevor Lawrence dropped back to pass 50 times. Rodriguez's catch was just his fifth of the season, and he's handled single-digit carries in eight of 10 contests. He's merely an insurance policy behind Tuten in fantasy.

headline: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.
story: The backup running back has been dealing with the hand issue for weeks but continues to play through it. Rodriguez has averaged an underwhelming 3.9 yards per carry on 59 attempts this season, allowing Bhayshul Tuten to run away with lead-back duties in Jacksonville.

headline: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Though Rodriguez has been limited in both of the team's first two Week 11 practices, the Jaguars haven't indicated that the running back's availability for Sunday's game against the Giants is in any real peril. In fact, Rodriguez could be headed for his most substantial workload of the season Sunday, as Bhayshul Tuten's (ankle/foot) may be at risk of sitting out that contest after downgrading from limited participation Wednesday to no activity during Thursday's practice.

headline: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Rodriguez was listed on injury reports both of the past two weeks due to the hand issue, but he proceeded to suit up for wins against the Ravens and Titans and handled his usual backup duties behind lead back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot). Assuming his limitations Wednesday were maintenance-related and not the result of any setback, Rodriguez should be ready to play Sunday against the Giants.

headline: Rodriguez rushed for five yards on four carries in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
story: Rodriguez was out-carried 26 to four by Bhayshul Tuten, who has very much proven himself as the Jaguars' clear RB1 in one of the league's best offenses. Tuten also out-snapped Rodriguez 52 to 10, while LeQuint Allen (12 snaps) saw more playing time. Rodriguez is little more than a deep-league bench stash should something happen to Tuten.

headline: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
story: Rodriguez was listed as a limited practice participant all week, but his hand issue is something he'll play through, while working alongside Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot), who returned to a limited session Friday and was also cleared for Week 10 action. Rodriguez has 55 carries in eight games to date, while Tuten has logged 122 rushes in that span, but Rodriguez has at least helped out his fantasy managers of late by scoring in each of his last two contests.

headline: Rodriguez (hand) was a limited practice participant Thursday, while Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) didn't participate.
story: The catch is that Tuten didn't practice last week and ended up playing in a 33-10 win at Baltimore on Thursday night. Rodriguez played through his hand injury, so he should be able to take on an expanded workload this week if Tuten doesn't play.

headline: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as limited in Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: While Rodriguez fit some work in on Wednesday, fellow RB Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a DNP by the Jaguars. The duo's status is thus worth monitoring closely in the coming days, but if Tuten ends up limited or out this weekend, Rodriguez -- if available -- and Ameer Abdullah would be next up for the team's backfield touches Sunday against the Titans.

headline: Rodriguez rushed 10 times for 19 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 13 yards in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.
story: Rodriguez finished with just two fewer carries than Bhayshul Tuten, who came into the game managing ankle and foot injuries and was able to log a relatively abbreviated workload thanks to game script. Both backs had plenty of trouble against Baltimore's stout run defense, but Rodriguez salvaged his fantasy night with a two-yard TD run just past the midway point of the fourth quarter. Rodriguez now has scored in back-to-back games heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

headline: Rodriguez (hand) doesn't carry an injury designation for Thursday night's game against the Ravens.
story: Meanwhile, Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) has been deemed questionable for the contest after being listed as a DNP on each of the Jaguars' injury reports, Monday through Wednesday. Given that Tuten has been the team's lead back this season, his playing status (and potential workload, if he's active Thursday) will provide valuable context related to the Week 9 fantasy prospects of Rodriguez, who could assume a larger backfield role versus Baltimore if Tuten ends up out or limited.

headline: Rodriguez (hand) was listed as a limited participant in Tuesday's practice.
story: Though he's been deemed a limited participant on both of the Jaguars' first two Week 9 practice reports, Rodriguez still looks to be in a better spot on the health front than Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot), who has yet to log any practice activity. If Tuten winds up being sidelined for Thursday's game in Baltimore, Rodriguez would be the favorite to lead the Jacksonville ground attack, provided he's not inhibited by his own hand injury.

headline: Rodriguez was listed as limited on Monday's practice estimate due to a hand injury.
story: The Jaguars listed two running backs on their first Week 9 injury report, with No. 1 option Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) going down as a non-participant. There's no telling if Tuten is in danger of missing Thursday's contest at Baltimore, but Rodriguez could be in line for more early down work if he's active and the former is inhibited or sidelined. On the season, Rodriguez is averaging 6.7 touches per game.

headline: Rodriguez registered 41 yards and a touchdown on six carries while reeling in his only target for 17 yards during Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts.
story: Rodriguez was able to exceed 40 rushing yards for the second straight game after failing to do so in any of the team's first five contests of the year. Additionally, the running back slashed through the Colts' defense for a 26-yard touchdown in the third quarter, reaching the end zone for the third time this season. Rodriguez has now rushed 45 times for 209 yards and three scores while reeling in one of two targets for six yards over seven contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Rodriguez rushed 11 times for 55 yards while failing to reel in his only target during Sunday's 34-31 loss to Houston.
story: Rodriguez led the team in rushing yards, out-producing fellow running back Bhayshul Tuten's 39 yards on 12 carries. Although the two split the carries almost evenly, Tuten caught all four of his targets for 48 yards and two scores in the contest. Rodriguez has now compiled 168 yards on 39 carries while catching one pass for six yards over six contests to open the 2026 campaign.

headline: Rodriguez rushed twice for five yards and caught his only target for six yards during Sunday's 19-17 win over Philadelphia.
story: Rodriguez was scarcely used in Week 5, logging his fewest carries in a game this season. Starting running back Bhayshul Tuten turned 22 carries into 72 yards, and he's clearly the preferred option over Rodriguez in the backfield, regardless of circumstance. Over five games this season, Rodriguez has rushed 28 times for 113 yards and two touchdowns while catching one pass for six yards.

headline: Rodriguez rushed six times for 35 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Bengals.
story: After a slow start to the season, Rodriguez has found the end zone in back-to-back games, this time scoring from 25 yards out for his longest run of the season. Rodriguez has handled exactly six carries in three of the four games and remains a total zero in the passing game with zero targets. He's the definition of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet playing behind Bhayshul Tuten.

headline: Thomas could handle a larger role Sunday against the Titans, as Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports that Parker Washington (shoulder) won't suit up.
story: Thomas has had a disappointing third season in Jacksonville, mustering a meager 84 receiving yards over his last eight appearances while seemingly having fallen out of favor in coach Liam Coen's offense. Washington's absence against Tennessee's struggling secondary could provide Thomas with an opportunity to turn back the clock and put up a performance reminiscent of the 2024 first-round pick's elite rookie season. Jakobi Meyers and Josh Cameron also are in line for expanded roles in Jacksonville's wide-receiver room.

headline: Thomas caught one pass for an 18-yard touchdown on three targets in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants.
story: Thomas' three targets were a distant fourth on the team, as Parker Washington (17), Jakobi Meyers (10) and Josh Cameron (seven) combined to see a combined 34 looks on Trevor Lawrence's 47 pass attempts. Thomas ran 32 routes, 14 more than Cameron as the Jaguars' nominal WR3, but the former hasn't been seeing meaningful target volume for months. After drawing nine targets in Week 2, Thomas has averaged 2.1 targets per game over his last eight contests. He's well off the fantasy radar while Washington and Meyers are healthy.

headline: Thomas caught three of four targets for 29 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
story: The three catches tied his season high, while the four targets represented his biggest volume since Week 2. The Jaguars' decision not to deal Thomas at the trade deadline remains a curious one, as the third-year wideout simply doesn't have a significant role in Liam Coen's offense and might not step into one even if someone like Parker Washington got injured -- Josh Cameron was more productive Sunday on three targets and caught one of Trevor Lawrence's three TDs. Thomas will take a 13-146-2 line on 26 targets over nine games into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

headline: The Jaguars have relayed to inquiring teams that they intend to keep Thomas through Tuesday's trade deadline, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: After sending out a first-round pick, two second-round picks, a fifth-round pick and a sixth-round pick Monday in separate deals to bring in defenders Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates and Davon Godchaux, the Jaguars likely could have recouped some of that draft capital if they had opted to move Thomas. Instead, Fowler indicates that the Jaguars plan to keep the rest of their roster intact ahead of the deadline, which will result in Thomas sticking around. Rather than operating as the high-volume target earner he was during his banner 2024 rookie campaign, Thomas looks like he'll continue to serve mainly as a vertical threat who frees up opportunities in the short and intermediate areas for other pass catchers. Thomas has drawn three or fewer targets in six straight games, producing a weak 4-37-2 receiving line during that stretch.

headline: Thomas wasn't targeted in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.
story: Thomas played just 19 of 56 offensive snaps and ran only 11 routes on Trevor Lawrence's 26 dropbacks. It's become clear that Thomas is no longer a big part of the offense and needs an injury ahead of him or a trade out of Jacksonville to become relevant in season-long fantasy. He has just one catch for a 12-yard touchdown over his last four games.

headline: Thomas has drawn interest from other teams leading up to the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Ian Rapoport of ESPN reports.
story: Since delivering an 87-1,282-10 receiving line over 17 games as a rookie in 2024, Thomas' production has cratered in the ensuing two seasons. He's been firmly behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers (hamstring/ankle) in terms of snap share through the Jaguars' first seven games and has drawn more than three targets in just one of those contests. Though the vertical threat Thomas presents might make him an appealing target for teams seeking a big-play receiver, it's unclear if the Jaguars have much motivation to move him. Despite his declining role within the Jacksonville offense, Thomas remains under contract through next season at relatively modest cap hits of $4.01 million in 2026 and $4.66 million in 2027.

headline: Thomas caught one of two targets for a 12-yard touchdown in Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts.
story: Thomas got the scoring started against Indianapolis, securing a red-zone touchdown with 5:30 left in the opening quarter. With the Jaguars throttling the Colts, Trevor Lawrence dropped back just 17 times all afternoon. On 17 pass attempts between Lawrence (14) and Quinn Ewers (three), 11 different Jaguars drew at least one target. Through seven games this season, Thomas has 10 catches for 117 yards and two touchdowns on 22 targets. A low catch rate and diminished snaps have led to Thomas' name being circulated in trade rumors 10 days ahead of the trade deadline.

headline: Thomas didn't haul in either of his two targets during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans in London.
story: Per Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com, Thomas logged 15 offensive snaps in the first half but none after halftime, while all of fellow wideouts Parker Washington (11 targets), Jakobi Meyers (10) and Travis Hunter (four) had major roles in the Jaguars offense. Thomas maintained a regular workload in the first five games of the season, with his snap shares ranging from 35 to 62 percent en route to a 9-105-1 line on 18 targets. Sunday's development could be a sign of things to come for Thomas without the team mentioning any sort of injury during or after Sunday's contest.

headline: Thomas failed to catch any of his three targets in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
story: Getting the ball to Parker Washington was once again was the primary focus for Trevor Lawrence, as the fourth-year wideout popped for a 6-124-2 line on nine targets, and Thomas didn't do anything with the little volume he got to prove he should be a bigger part of the game plan. Thomas has gotten three targets ore fewer in four of five games to begin the season, leading to a meager 9-105-1 line on 18 targets, and there's little reason to expect a breakout in Week 6 against the Texans.

headline: Thomas secured both targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
story: Thomas was a minimal part of the air attack once again, but that description also applied to fellow wideouts Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington as the Bengals did an effective job taking away Trevor Lawrence's primary targets. However, Thomas was able to break through with what turned out to be a key score, as he recorded a seven-yard scoring grab late in the first half in a game that was ultimately decided by five points. Thomas still has a modest nine receptions for 105 yards and Sunday's touchdown on 15 targets as the Jaguars head across the pond to face the Eagles in London in Week 5.

headline: Cameron is in line to handle a larger role Sunday against the Titans, as Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports that Parker Washington (shoulder) won't suit up.
story: Cameron and Brian Thomas are the top candidates to absorb extra targets alongside Jakobi Meyers in Washington's absence. Washington is considered week-to-week, so his absence could extend beyond Week 12. Cameron has 111 receiving yards and a touchdown over the past two games, so the rookie sixth-round pick was trending up even prior to Washington's injury. An increased role against a Titans defense that's giving up the most catches and yards per game to wide receivers could set Cameron up for a breakout performance.

headline: Cameron caught three of seven targets for 44 yards during Sunday's 23-18 loss against the Giants. He also returned two kickoffs for a total of 40 yards.
story: Despite being on the field for only 25 of the Jaguars' 68 offensive snaps in Week 11, Cameron drew a career-high seven targets. He wasn't terribly efficient on those targets, but neither was Jacksonville's offense as a whole Sunday. He'll be lining up against a much softer pass defense in a Week 12 tilt versus the Titans.

headline: Cameron caught all three of his targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23, Week 10 win over Tennessee. He also returned five kickoffs for 142 yards.
story: Cameron gave the Jaguars a 14-point lead early in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 25-yard touchdown pass from Trevor Lawrence. It was the rookie wideout's third touchdown of the campaign but his first since Week 3. Cameron's 67 receiving yards marked a career high, while his three receptions tied the most he's had as a pro. Cameron's propensity for finding the end zone (his three TDs have come on just 12 total catches) is appealing, but at this point he isn't getting enough volume to be a reliable week-to-week fantasy asset.

headline: Cameron caught his only target for six yards in Thursday night's 33-10 victory over the Ravens.
story: Cameron didn't see the ball until the fourth quarter despite playing the third most snaps at wide receiver (25) for the Jaguars on Thursday, behind only Parker Washington (38) and Jakobi Meyers (38). This marks the third game in a row during which the 23-year-old played as the Jaguars' No. 3 option at receiver, but his limited usage keeps him as a low-priority waiver-wire add.

headline: Cameron did not catch his lone target in a 42-7 rout of the Colts on Sunday. He returned one punt for six yards and one kickoff for 18 yards.
story: Jacksonville didn't need to go to its air-game much given the easy win, and QB Trevor Lawrence threw just 14 passes. None of those went to Cameron -- his only target (which he didn't catch) came from backup signal-caller Quinn Ewers in garbage time. Cameron did log a season-high 52 percent offensive snap share, but game script didn't do him any favors in terms of production. With no catches in three of his seven games this season, Cameron doesn't make for an appealing fantasy asset.

headline: Cameron didn't garner a target and recorded 46 kickoff-return yards during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
story: Cameron went without a target for the first time since Week 2, but he did play a season-high 50 percent of the team's offensive snaps. The wide receiver played 19 more snaps on offense than Brian Thomas, and he appears to have officially taken over as the team's No. 3 option behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers at his position. On the year, Cameron has caught eight of 12 targets for 117 yards and two touchdowns while also adding 245 yards as a kick returner over six games.

headline: Cameron caught three of six targets for 43 yards during the Jaguars' 19-17 win over the Eagles on Sunday in London. He also returned one kickoff for 18 yards and added a tackle on special teams.
story: Cameron opened Sunday's game in style, when he took the first kickoff of the contest 90 yards to the house for a touchdown, but that score ended up being nullified by a holding penalty on the Jaguars. The rookie sixth-rounder still managed to contribute offensively and finished third on the Jaguars in catches, targets and receiving yards, including a 32-yard catch early in the third quarter. Cameron's 22 offensive snaps were fourth-most among Jacksonville wide receivers, but his 6-97-1 receiving line (10 targets) over the last three weeks is noticeably better than Brian Thomas (3-25-1 on six targets) in that same span. The Jaguars will stay in London for a Week 6 AFC South showdown against the Texans on Oct. 18.

headline: Cameron hauled in both of his targets for 42 yards during the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday. He also returned two kickoffs for 45 yards.
story: Cameron got on the board in the second quarter with a 29-yard catch before connecting with Trevor Lawrence on a 13-yard pass in the third. The rookie sixth-rounder played 22 of the Jaguars' 61 offensive snaps (36.1 percent), which was fourth most among Jacksonville's wide receivers. Cameron has a 5-74-2 line on six targets through four games, and his scoring floor figures to remain limited unless the Jaguars are without one or more of Parker Washington, Brian Thomas or Jakobi Meyers. Up next for the Jaguars is a Week 5 home game against the Eagles.

headline: Cameron secured one of two targets for a 12-yard touchdown in Sunday's 35-6 win over the Patriots.
story: Cameron got the scoring started early in the second quarter, catching the first of Trevor Lawrence's three touchdown passes. The rookie ended up finishing with 23 offensive snaps against New England, the same amount as Brian Thomas but behind Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers, who both played 50 snaps on offense. Cameron could be pushing Thomas for the No. 3 receiver role in Jacksonville.

headline: Meyers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Titans, Ryan O'Halloran of the Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Meyers has managed to shake off an ankle injury that limited his practice participation earlier in the week. He racked up a season-high 85 yards on 10 targets in Jacksonville's Week 11 loss to the Giants, and Meyers is likely to get plenty of attention from Trevor Lawrence against Tennessee's league-worst secondary Sunday in the absence of top Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington (shoulder), giving Meyers appealing upside in nearly all fantasy formats.

headline: Meyers was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to an ankle injury.
story: Dating back to Week 8, Meyers has been listed on Jaguars injury reports with the ankle issue, but it hasn't stopped him from being available on game days. His limitations Wednesday were most likely maintenance-related after he turned in one his best performances of 2026 in this past Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants. Meyers played 83 percent of the offensive snaps in the loss, finishing with four catches for a season-high 85 yards on 10 targets.

headline: Meyers was spotted working off to the side during Wednesday's practice, Demetrius Harvey of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: The Jaguars will release their first Week 12 injury report later Wednesday, when it will be known why Meyers was held out of drills. The veteran wideout has frequently had his practice reps managed throughout the season while he's nursed a few different injuries, so he could just be getting some rest as the Jaguars begin prepping for a Week 12 matchup with the Titans. Meyers was most recently listed on the Jaguars' injury report in Week 11 due to an ankle issue, but he didn't take a designation into this past Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants and finished with four receptions for 85 yards on 10 targets while playing 83 percent of the offensive snaps.

headline: Meyers brought in four of 10 targets for 85 yards in the Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
story: Meyers finished second across the board to Parker Washington in receptions, receiving yards and targets for the Jaguars on the afternoon, and the latter pair of totals also established and tied a season high, respectively. Meyers' yardage and reception tallies have fluctuated this season, but Sunday's performance underscores the fact he remains a key complementary piece of the Jaguars' typically efficient air attack. Meyers will look to exploit a favorable Week 12 matchup against the Titans defense at home next Sunday.

headline: Meyers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.
story: Meyers has been playing through the ankle injury for weeks, so his status was never in real doubt despite limited practices all week. The veteran wideout doesn't have a touchdown catch since Week 3 and has topped 65 receiving yards in a game just once all season. He's a low-floor, low-ceiling fantasy option.

headline: Meyers (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Meyers had his reps capped for a second straight practice, but if he can maintain limited activity or upgrade to full participation Friday, he should be on track to play Sunday against the Giants. The veteran slot receiver has yet to miss a game this season, recording 29 receptions for 408 yards and two touchdowns on 43 targets through nine appearances.

headline: Meyers (ankle) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: The Jaguars have often kept Meyers limited early in the week since the veteran suffered an ankle injury, but he has yet to miss a game this year. There have even been weeks when Meyers did not practice Wednesday but still ended up playing. As it stands, Meyers' status will be worth monitoring for the rest of the week, but limited midweek work has been the norm for him.

headline: Meyers caught three of six targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
story: The six targets were second on the Jaguars behind Parker Washington's nine, but Meyers' longest gain of the day went for only 15 yards. The veteran wideout has also failed to find the end zone in six straight games, a stretch in which he's managed just a 19-256-0 line on 32 targets. Meyers will try to end that drought in a Week 11 clash against the Giants.

headline: Myers (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's matchup with Tennessee, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
story: Meyers has fought through one injury or another for most of the season. This week, he managed limited practices Thursday and Friday, setting him up to play against the last-place Titans.

headline: Meyers (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Meyers has managed one injury or another throughout the season without missing any games. His return to practice Thursday after a Wednesday absence suggests this may just be another cause of maintenance/caution. If Meyers plays, he'll face a Tennessee defense that's allowing a league 40.7 PPR points per game to wide receivers.

headline: Meyers (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Meyers was listed with hamstring and ankle injuries last week before playing 68 percent of Jacksonville's offensive snaps and catching four passes for 65 yards in a Thursday blowout at Baltimore. It's unclear if the ankle has worsened or if Wednesday's absence is just a matter of caution/maintenance. Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter would all be candidates for additional WR snaps if Meyers were to miss time.

headline: Meyers brought in four of six targets for 65 yards in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.
story: Meyers set the pace for the Jaguars in both receptions and receiving yards on the night, bouncing back nicely from a quiet 2-24-0 line just four days earlier in a blowout win over the Colts. The veteran wideout has multiple catches in all but one game, although Meyers hasn't topped 83 receiving yards in any contest to date in 2026. Meyers remains a key target for Trevor Lawrence, but he could see at least a slight boost in his outlook heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15, if Brian Thomas is moved at the trade deadline.

headline: Meyers (hamstring/ankle) does not carry an injury designation going into Thursday's game at the Ravens.
story: Though Meyers was limited in practice, the Jaguars are not listing him on the injury report going into Thursday's game. The veteran has battled through bumps and bruises throughout the season but has yet to miss a game. He'll be good to go for Week 9 in Charm City.

headline: Meyers (hamstring/ankle) was listed as a limited participant in Tuesday's practice.
story: Though he's managing a pair of lower-body concerns coming out of Sunday's win over the Colts, Meyers' ability to practice in any fashion Tuesday bodes well for his chances of playing Thursday against the Ravens. However, Meyers may need to upgrade to full practice participation Wednesday to avoid taking an injury designation into the Week 9 contest.

headline: Meyers was listed as limited on Monday's estimated injury report due to hamstring and ankle issues.
story: Meyers was capped at Monday's walkthrough as a result of the health concerns that impacted him in practice last week, but he still suited up Sunday versus the Colts, handling a 54 percent snap share and gathering in two of three targets for 24 yards. Considering he was able to play through them in Week 8, he's likely trending toward being available Thursday in Baltimore, but his status nonetheless will be watched to ensure as much.

headline: Meyers logged two catches for 24 yards on three targets in Sunday's 42-7 win against Indianapolis.
story: He put up a subpar fantasy line, but Meyers actually led Jacksonville in targets and tied for the team lead in receptions on a day when quarterback Trevor Lawrence threw only 14 passes, 10 of which he completed. Meyers also logged a 54 percent offensive snap share -- second among Jaguars wideouts behind Parker Washington -- after dealing with a hamstring injury during the week. He's still looking to build some momentum, as Meyers has three or fewer catches in five of his seven contests and topped 40 receiving yards just twice.

headline: Meyers (hamstring) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Meyers logged a pair of limited practices this week before sitting out Friday's session entirely, but as reports Sunday morning indicated, he'll ultimately be available to take the field. Following Jacksonville's Week 7 bye, Meyers will look to find the end zone for the first time since Week 3 against a middle-of-the-pack Colts defense allowing 215.9 passing yards per game.

headline: Meyers (hamstring/ankle) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Colts, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Meyers dealt with a hamstring injury during Week 8 prep, logging limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday before sitting out Friday's practice entirely. Assuming he's deemed active approximately 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, he'll be looking to build upon the season-high 83 receiving yards he put up in the Jaguars' last game in Week 6 against the Texans in London.

headline: Meyers (hamstring/ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Meyers didn't practice Friday, but the Jaguars are leaving the light on for the veteran wideout to face Indianapolis. He's coming off a productive Week 6 game against the Texans in which Meyers caught five of 10 targets for 83 yards. The Jaguars are fresh off their bye. If Meyers can't go, Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and Travis Hunter would have expanded roles behind Parker Washington.

headline: Meyers (hamstring) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Coming out of a bye week, Meyers has had his reps capped in the Jaguars' first two practice sessions of Week 8. The Jaguars haven't indicated that Meyers is at any real risk of sitting out Sunday's game against the Colts, but if he's able to upgrade to full participation Friday, he'll likely head into the weekend without an injury designation.

headline: Meyers (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a hamstring injury.
story: Meyers had previously made appearances on Jaguars injury reports earlier in the season due to a thumb issue, but he's nursing a different health concern coming out of the team's Week 7 bye. Unless the hamstring injury was something that cropped up during Wednesday's practice, Meyers' ability to begin Week 8 prep on the field in some capacity is generally a good sign for his chances of suiting up Sunday versus the Colts.

headline: Meyers caught five of 10 targets for 83 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
story: While Parker Washington led the Jaguars with 11 looks from Trevor Lawrence, Meyers paced the club in catches and receiving yards on his largest target volume of the season. The 83 yards were also a season best for Meyers, and the veteran wideout will take a 20-285-2 line on 28 targets into a bye before clashing with the Colts in Week 8.

headline: Meyers caught two of three targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 19-17 win against the Eagles.
story: Meyers was limited to 40 or fewer receiving yards for the fourth time this season, and he finished tied with running back Bhayshul Tuten for fourth on the team in targets Sunday. Meyers has solidified himself as the team's No. 2 wide receiver behind Parker Washington early in the season, but his production hasn't been that notable. Through five games, Meyers has caught 15 of 18 targets for 202 yards and two touchdowns.

headline: Meyers caught three of four targets for 33 yards during Sunday's 22-17 win against the Bengals.
story: Meyers finished second on the team in targets behind tight end Brenton Strange (eight), but his performance was far from noteworthy. The wide receiver has operated as a distant No. 2 option behind Parker Washington at his position this season, and Sunday's performance was his third game with 40 or fewer receiving yards over four contests.

headline: Meyers (thumb) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
story: With limited listings earlier in the week, Meyers practiced fully Friday and is fine for his normal workload against Cincinnati. Meyers was targeted a season-high eight times last Sunday against the Patriots but has just 11 targets on the season over three games. He's a low-floor WR4 for fantasy, but this game does have some shootout appeal.

headline: Meyers (thumb) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: The Jaguars have been restricting Meyers' practice activity through the four weeks of the regular season after he jammed his right thumb during a joint practice with Carolina in training camp, but the issue hasn't kept him from suiting up on game days. He's expected to be cleared to play Sunday in Cincinnati following Friday's practice.

headline: Meyers (thumb) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: Meyers dealt with the thumb issue last week but ultimately didn't carry an injury designation into last Sunday's blowout win over the Patriots, where the veteran wideout hung a 7-64-1 receiving line on eight targets. Playing as a clear starter ahead of Brian Thomas, Meyers has 10 catches for 132 yards and two touchdowns on 11 targets through three games this season.

headline: Tuten (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Titans, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Tuten was unable to practice this week and now will target a potential return to action Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Bears. In his absence this weekend, Chris Rodriguez will be in line for an increased workload in the Jacksonville backfield, a context that gives him Week 12 fantasy relevance, with LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah also in the mix versus 1-9 Tennessee.

headline: Tuten (ankle) wasn't spotted at Friday's practice, Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports.
story: If Tuten's absence Friday is confirmed by the team's injury report, that would mark a third consecutive 'DNP' for Jacksonville's starting running back. Coach Liam Coen intimated earlier Friday that Tuten's participation level Friday will factor into his potential availability for Sunday's game against the Titans, so he appears more likely than not to sit out Sunday based on this latest development. If Tuten is ruled out, Chris Rodriguez would be in line to lead a backfield that also includes LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah.

headline: Head coach Liam Coen said Friday that the team is "not sure yet" whether Tuten (ankle/foot) will be available Sunday against the Titans, Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Tuten was unable to practice Wednesday or Thursday, but Coen said how Tuten looks Friday will affect the determination on the starting running back's status for Sunday's game, which suggests the team plans for Tuten to practice in at least some capacity Friday. If Tuten is ultimately deemed questionable on Friday's injury report, his status may not be clarified until around 90 minutes prior to Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff. Chris Rodriguez would be in line to lead Jacksonville's backfield against the Titans if Tuten joins Parker Washington (shoulder) on the sidelines Sunday.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) didn't practice Thursday, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Back-to-back 'DNPs' Wednesday and Thursday cloud Tuten's status for Sunday's game against the Titans, with the running back's Friday practice participation level looming large in terms of his Week 12 availability. If Tuten isn't active versus Tennessee, Chris Rodriguez will be in line for an increased workload in the Jacksonville backfield, with LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah also in the mix.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) didn't practice Wednesday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times Union previously noted that he didn't spot Tuten at Wednesday's session, and the Jaguars have officially confirmed the running back's absence. Added context regarding Tuten's Week 12 status will arrive via Thursday's injury report, but it's unclear if the team will hold a full-scale practice Thanksgiving Day.

headline: Tuten (ankle) wasn't spotted at Wednesday's practice,  Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times Union reports.
story: Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union previously reported that Jaguars head coach Liam Coen noted Monday that the re-check stemming from the aggravation of the ankle injury Tuten suffered in Week 11 suggested that the issue "wasn't too bad." That said, with the running back in line to log a Wednesday 'DNP," his status needs to be tracked leading up to Sunday's game against the Titans. If Tuten is limited or out this weekend, Chris Rodriguez would be next in line to see added touches, with LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah also on hand.

headline: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Tuten aggravated a right ankle injury in Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants, while noting that an examination Monday revealed nothing "too bad," Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Tuten carried 10 times for 33 yards and recorded three receptions for 20 yards before exiting the contest with 3:40 remaining, when his ankle got stepped on for the second time that day. Though the injury was to the same ankle/foot that has resulted in Tuten being listed on the Jacksonville injury report for three straight weeks, Coen seemed to imply that the aggravation isn't viewed as a major concern. Even so, Tuten's practice activity is likely to be affected in Week 12, putting his availability for next Sunday's game against the Titans in question.

headline: Tuten (undisclosed) exited Sunday's 23-18 loss to the Giants after an eight-yard gain with 3:40 left in the contest, Garry Smits of the Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Per the report, following the fourth-quarter play, Tuten limped off the field, seeming favoring his right leg. The running back then didn't return for the rest of the possession, with the Giants running out the clock after that. Though the exact nature of Tuten's latest injury is unclear, as John Oehser, Brian Sexton, Kainani Stevens and John Shipley of the Jaguars' official site note, the running back has been dealing with a foot/ankle injury for the last few weeks. In any case, Tuten's status will need to be monitored closely as the team's Nov. 29 contest against the Titans approaches. In the event that he's limited or out in Week 12, Chris Rodriguez would be in line to see added touches, with LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah also in the mix.

headline: Tuten rushed 10 times for 33 yards and brought in all three targets for 20 yards in the Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
story: Tuten saw his rushing opportunities capped by a surprising game script that saw the Jaguars trail for almost the entirety of the afternoon, and he found running room at a premium when he did touch the ball. The second-year back now has under 40 rushing yards in three of the past five games, and he's averaged under 3.4 yards per carry in five of the last six contests as well. Nevertheless, Tuten's locked-in dual role makes him an appealing asset heading into a favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.
story: Tuten was limited at practice Wednesday, listed as a 'DNP' on Thursday, and then returned to a limited session Friday as he continues to manage the ankle and toe issues he has played through over the last two weeks. Also cleared to play versus New York were fellow RBs Chris Rodriguez (hand) and LeQuint Allen (hamstring), but Tuten nonetheless remains the clear top option in Jacksonville's backfield on the heels of recording a 70 percent snap share en route to carrying 26 times for 88 yards and a TD, to go along with three catches on four targets for 25 yards, in last weekend's 40-23 win over the Titans.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) was present for the stretching portion of Friday's practice before moving to a side field, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Tuten was deemed limited at practice Wednesday and then was a non-participant Thursday. It remains to be seen how the Jaguars classify his participation (or lack thereof) in Friday's session, with added clarity on that front set to arrive via the team's upcoming injury report.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot), per head coach Liam Coen, "will maybe run around a little bit" at Friday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Tuten did not get any work in Thursday after being limited at Wednesday's practice, but Coen's comments suggest he could be back on the field Friday. Tuten was listed as either limited or as a non-participant the last eight times the Jaguars released an injury report but has not missed a game, so while his status is up in the air there is reason to believe he will be out there Sunday. Tuten's status for Week 11 will officially be revealed when the Jaguars release their next injury report later Friday.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a non-participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Tuten was deemed a limited participant Wednesday, so his downgrade in activity a day later is notable, though the listing could be maintenance-related rather than due to a setback. O'Halloran previously relayed that the running back was working off to the side during the media-access portion of Thursday's session. The extent of Tuten's participation in Friday's practice bears watching, as the Jaguars look to determine whether he'll take an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Giants.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) was working off to the side during the stretching portion of Thursday's practice, according to Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union.
story: Tuten has been listed as a limited participant in the Jaguars' last two practices (including this past Friday) as he continues to manage ankle and foot issues. It appears as though that approach is in play again Thursday, though the running back's official participation level won't be clarified until the team's upcoming injury report is posted.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: As were fellow RBs Chris Rodriguez (hand) and LeQuint Allen (hamstring), though there's a decent chance that the listed limitations of Tuten and Rodriguez were maintenance-related as opposed to being indicative of setbacks on their part. Both players were limited at practice this past Friday by the same injuries and headed into Week 10 action without injury designations. Though we'll continue to track both players in the coming days, there's no indication so far that either of their statuses for Sunday's game against the Giants is in any danger.

headline: Tuten carried the ball 26 times for 88 yards and a touchdown and caught three of four targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 40-23 win over Tennessee.
story: It's the second time this season that Tuten has reached triple-digit scrimmage yards in a game, with both those performances coming since the Jaguars' Week 7 bye. The second-year RB capped the rout with a six-yard TD run in the fourth quarter, extending his scoring streak to four games -- a stretch in which Tuten has racked up 260 rushing yards and three touchdowns on the ground while adding a 9-128-3 line on 10 targets through the air. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 11 against the Giants.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's matchup with Tennessee, Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com reports.
story: Tuten played through the injury last week without practicing, and he'll now suit up for Week 10 after just one limited practice Friday. Chris Rodriguez (hand) also is cleared to play and could help ease the burden if Jacksonville is wary of overworking Tuten while he's banged up.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) will practice Friday, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Tuten was unable to practice both Wednesday and Thursday, but head coach Liam Coen revealed that he will be back out there Friday. It won't be clear until after practice if Tuten practiced fully or on a limited basis, but his participation alone bodes well for his chances of suiting up Sunday against the Titans.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Tuten didn't practice Wednesday either, though as Mia O'Brien of 1010 XL 92.5 FM Jacksonville points out, Tuten logged 'DNPs' Monday through Wednesday last week yet still played in last Thursday's win over the Ravens. In any case, Friday's practice report will reveal whether Tuten is able to work at all this week, as well as his game status for Sunday's game against the Titans. Next up for carries if he ends up sidelined this weekend is Chris Rodriguez (hand), who was limited Thursday.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) was the Jaguars' only player without a helmet during the initial portion of Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Tuten was deemed a non-participant in practice Wednesday, but his presence on the field a day later suggests that he could advance to limited participation Thursday. In any case, the Jaguars' next practice report will clarify that, as well as how much work fellow RB Chris Rodriguez (hand) got in.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) was listed as a non-participant in practice Wednesday, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: It remains to be seen if Tuten is simply managing a couple of aches and pains in the wake of Week 9 action or is in danger of missing the Jaguars' next game, so his status is worth tracking ahead of Sunday's game against the Titans. Fellow RB Chris Rodriguez also appeared on Wednesday's injury report after being deemed limited by a hand injury.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) rushed 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night.
story: Tuten fought through the pair of lower-body injuries that made him a game-time decision, recording his fourth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a one-yard run to cap off the opening possession of the contest. The second-year back had to grind for every yard he got on the ground, but fortunately for Tuten, the Jaguars built a comfortable enough lead where he was able to benefit from an early end to his night. Tuten has now scored in back-to-back games, and he'll have some extra time to get healthier ahead of a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) officially is listed as active for Thursday night's game against the Ravens.
story: It was previously reported that Tuten, who was viewed as a game-time decision for the contest, would be good to go, and now that has been confirmed. Assuming no in-game limitations or setbacks, Tuten is in line to continue to lead the Jaguars backfield in Week 9. If, however, his reps end up being managed at all, added touches could be available for Chris Rodriguez, Ameer Abdullah and LeQuint Allen. When healthy, Tuten has maintained steady volume through seven games, averaging 15.7 carries and 70.3 rushing yards with three rushing scores, while also having recorded a 15-181-3 receiving line in that span.

headline: Tuten (ankle) is on track to play in Thursday night's game against the Ravens, after going through what Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com describes as an extensive pregame workout.
story: Tuten, who was listed as a DNP on all three of the Jaguars' Week 9 injury reports, was viewed as a game-time decision for Thursday's contest, but it looks like the running back will give it a go after all. Official confirmation of his status will arrive, either way, once the Jaguars' inactives are posted ahead of the team's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) "should be" available for Thursday night's game against the Ravens barring any pregame setbacks, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
story: Tuten logged DNP listings on all three of the Jaguars' Week 9 injury reports ahead of the contest and had been considered a game-time decision. Fowler's report indicates that the running back is trending toward active status, but those considering Tuten in Week 9 fantasy lineups nonetheless will want to verify his playing status ahead of Thursday's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) is listed questionable for Thursday's game against the Ravens.
story: For the third day in a row, Tuten went down as a non-participant on the Jaguars' injury report, even though head coach Liam Coen suggested the running back would practice in a limited fashion Wednesday, per Cameron Wolfe of NFL Network. The coach added that the Jaguars will be viewing Tuten as a game-time decision for Thursday's tilt, with his availability perhaps hinging on how he fares during a gameday workout. If Tuten ends up missing his first game of the season or is active but available in only a limited capacity, Chris Rodriguez would be in store for a larger role out of the backfield.

headline: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said Wednesday that Tuten (ankle/foot) is feeling better, but the running back's status for Thursday's contest versus the Ravens is expected to come down to a game-time decision, John Shipley of SI.com reports.
story: Tuten was listed as a non-participant on the Jaguars' first two Week 9 practice reports, but he may be in line to take some reps during Wednesday's session. The 23-year-old looks poised to take a questionable tag into the team's matchup with Baltimore, but if he fares well in practice Wednesday and while working out early Thursday, he could get the green light to play on a short week. If Tuten suits up, it's conceivable that he handles a lighter workload than normal, after receiving no fewer than 15 touches in any of the Jaguars' first seven contests.

headline: The Jaguars listed Tuten (ankle/foot) as a non-participant in Tuesday's practice.
story: For the second day in a row, Tuten went down as a non-participant on Jacksonville's Week 9 injury report while he nurses a pair of lower-body injuries coming out of this past Sunday's win over the Colts. If Tuten can get back on the field in some capacity Wednesday, it would put him in a good spot to play Thursday against the Ravens. However, if Tuten fails to practice and is ultimately ruled out for Thursday, Chris Rodriguez (hand) -- who has been a limited practice participant so far this week -- would be the top candidate to lead Jacksonville's ground attack in Baltimore.

headline: Tuten (ankle/foot) was not spotted during the portion of Tuesday's practice open to the media, according to Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com.
story: Tuten was listed as a non-participant on Monday's estimated injury report on a day the Jaguars did not practice, and although the Jaguars will return to the field Tuesday, it appears Tuten will not due to the lower-leg injuries. Tuten will not have much time to get any work in this week with the Jaguars facing the Ravens on Thursday, and if he is unable to go the door will be opened for Chris Rodriguez (hand), LeQuint Allen and Ameer Abdullah.

headline: Tuten was a non-participant at Monday's walkthrough due to ankle and foot injuries.
story: Tuten is coming off a sterling performance Sunday against the Colts in which he reeled off 159 yards from scrimmage and two total TDs on 18 touches, but he now has a pair of health concerns in tow. The Jaguars may be exercising caution with their No. 1 RB, but his status -- along with backup Chris Rodriguez (hand), who was listed as limited -- will be watched to get a sense of who may be available to the backfield Thursday at Baltimore.

headline: Tuten rushed 16 times for 104 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 55 yards and another score in the Jaguars' 42-7 win over the Colts on Sunday.
story: Tuten looked refreshed coming out of the Week 7 bye, breaking out for a new single-game career-high rushing total. Tuten also recorded his third rushing touchdown of the season on a rumbling 39-yard run during the second quarter where he broke several tackles, and he added his third receiving score over the last two games with a 25-yard grab as time expired in the third quarter. Tuten is up to 4.5 yards per carry after averaging a season-best 6.5 yards per tote Sunday, and he's added six total touchdowns heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Ravens on Thursday night.

headline: Tuten carried the ball 12 times for 39 yards and caught all four of his targets for 48 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
story: While the Houston front seven kept him bottled up on the ground -- Tuten's longest run went for just five yards -- the second-year RB made an impact through the air, turning a dump pass from Trevor Lawrence into a 27-yard score in the second quarter before catching another two-yard TD before halftime. The receiving touchdowns were his first of the season and tied his total from all of 2025, and Tuten topped 80 scrimmage yards for the fourth straight game. The Jaguars will get a bye before facing the Colts in Week 8.

headline: Tuten carried the ball 22 times for 72 yards and caught two of three targets for 24 yards in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
story: The second-year back set new season highs in touches and scrimmage yards as he reached 90 in the latter category for a third straight game. Tuten has yet to have a truly huge performance this season, but he's been very steady so far as the Jaguars' No. 1 RB, collecting 349 rushing yards and two TDs on 4.3 yards per carry while adding a 9-78-0 line on 10 targets through five games. Tuten hasn't gotten into the end zone in two straight games, a streak he'll look to snap in Week 6 against the Texans.

headline: Tuten rushed 17 times for 73 yards and brought in both targets for 18 yards in the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
story: Tuten filled his usual role as the clear lead option in Jacksonville's ground attack with aplomb, grinding out tough yards on many of his carries and also contributing a 20-yard run. He also recorded multiple receptions for the third consecutive game, and although he saw backfield mate Chris Rodriguez score the Jaguars' only rushing touchdown of the day that came on a breakaway run from 25 yards out as opposed to in close. Tuten has at least 15 carries in three of his first four games heading into a Week 5 showdown against the Eagles in London next Sunday.

headline: Head coach Liam Coen said Friday that it will be tough to pivot to an increased role for Hunter at wide receiver on short notice after Parker Washington (shoulder) was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Titans, Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Washington's shoulder injury seems to have taken a sudden turn for the worse, but the Jaguars had been preparing for their top receiver to be available, so they hadn't been utilizing Hunter much on offense in practice. Hunter should hold down his usual outside cornerback role on defense, but it's likely that most of the targets vacated by Washington will go to some combination of Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and CJ Williams rather than Hunter among Jacksonville's wide receivers.

headline: Hunter caught his lone target for three yards, added a nine-yard carry and logged six tackles (four solo) during the Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
story: As has been the case for most of the 2026 season, Hunter spent the majority of his time on the field playing defense, and his six tackles were fourth most on the Jaguars. He had a quiet day offensively, and the second-year pro is up to a 10-94-1 line on 11 targets through 10 regular-season games. On the defensive side of the ball, Hunter is up to 42 tackles (28 solo) and seven pass defenses (including three interceptions).

headline: Hunter caught both of his targets for 16 yards, recorded a three-yard carry and contributed five tackles (three solo) and an interception during the Jaguars' 40-23 win over the Titans on Sunday.
story: Fifty-six of Hunter's 62 snaps Sunday came on defense, and that's where he made his biggest impact with a diving interception on a Cam Ward pass intended for Elic Ayomanor, and the Jaguars offense converted that takeaway into a field goal 10 plays later. Hunter's impact on both sides of the ball has been undeniable: he has 28 catches (on 45 targets) for 298 yards and a touchdown, along with 36 tackles (24 solo) and seven pass defenses (including three interceptions) through nine regular-season games. The Jaguars will hit the road for Week 11 against the Giants on Nov. 22.

headline: Hunter caught his only target for minus-1 yard and lost a fumble in Thursday night's 33-10 win over the Ravens.
story: Hunter played six offensive snaps against Baltimore but turned the ball over on his only touch. After posting a 4-59-1 receiving line against the Texans in London back in Week 6, Hunter has done very little on offense. He needs the Jaguars' opponents to make games closer so the coaching staff feels obligated to utilize Hunter's big-play ability.

headline: Hunter failed to catch his lone target in Sunday's 42-7 win over the Colts. He added five rushing yards on one attempt.
story: With the Jaguars destroying their division rivals, Trevor Lawrence dropped back to pass just 17 times. Hunter's playmaking ability wasn't needed, as he logged just six offensive snaps. He'd likely benefit from a Brian Thomas trade ahead of next week's deadline.

headline: Hunter caught all four of his targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans in London. He also recorded three tackles and an interception.
story: The two-way player is beginning to flash the talent that made him the second overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. Hunter's receiving numbers were by far a season high -- he had only two catches coming into Sunday -- and his day on offense was capped by a seven-yard touchdown reception from Trevor Lawrence in the fourth quarter that brought the Jaguars to within a field goal at 31-28. Hunter then made an impact on the very next possession, picking off a C.J. Stroud pass in the end zone with just under four minutes left on the clock to keep his team in the game. The touchdown and interception were each the second of his career in his 13th NFL game, and Hunter became the first player since 2002 to have one of each in the same game. Jacksonville's receiver room is crowded with Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Brian Thomas at the top of the depth chart, but head coach Liam Coen hinted after the game that Hunter's role on offense could continue to grow following the team's Week 7 bye, per CBS 47 Jacksonville.

headline: Hunter recorded a nine-yard reception and tallied six tackles and a pass breakup in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles in London.
story: After not getting any run on offense in the Jaguars' Week 4 win over the Bengals, Hunter ended up taking the field for six of 72 snaps in Week 5 and was able to come away with his second reception of the season. The two-way player continues to see the overwhelming amount of his playing time on defense, where he was on the field for all 62 snaps. Expect the Jaguars continue to use Hunter almost exclusively at cornerback while sprinkling him into the offensive game plan only occasionally.

headline: Hunter logged four tackles (three solo) and two pass defenses during the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
story: After snagging his first NFL interception against the Patriots in Week 3, Hunter demonstrated his defensive prowess in Week 4 with two pass defenses. Notably, for the first time this season, the 2025 second-overall pick did not play a single snap on offense. It appears the Jaguars are comfortable with rookie Josh Cameron serving as the depth wideout behind Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Brian Thomas, so Hunter's playing time figures to be limited to defense. Hunter has 13 tackles (nine solo) and four pass defenses (including one interception) through the first four games of the regular season.

headline: Hunter played five offensive snaps in Sunday's 35-6 win over the Patriots.
story: He failed to see a target in the passing game for the second straight week and is clearly not in the team's plans on that side of the ball with everyone healthy at wideout. Hunter would likely need one or even two injuries ahead of him on the depth chart to see significant snaps on offense. On defense against New England, Hunter logged four tackles (three solo) and one pass breakup, including his first career regular-season interception.

headline: Washington (shoulder) will be out for Sunday's game against the Titans and is considered week-to-week moving forward, Demetrius Harvey of the Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Washington was added to Jacksonville's injury report Thursday due to a shoulder injury, and the impact of the injury has escalated from limiting his practice participation Thursday to sidelining Jacksonville's top receiver Sunday and possibly beyond then. In Washington's absence, Jakobi Meyers (ankle), Brian Thomas, Josh Cameron and possibly Travis Hunter or CJ Williams -- to a lesser degree -- could garner more attention from Trevor Lawrence against a Titans secondary that has allowed the most catches and yards per game in the league to wide receivers. Additional details regarding Washington's injury should emerge before the Jaguars travel to Chicago in Week 13.

headline: Washington (shoulder) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Washington wasn't on Wednesday's injury report, so his addition to it a day later is certainly of note. It remains to be seen if the WR, who is coming off consecutive big games for the Jaguars, is managing a shoulder issue stemming from Week 11 action or was hurt in Thursday's practice. Friday's report will reveal both Washington's participation level to close the week, as well as his game status for a 1:00 p.m. ET matchup versus the Titans on Sunday.

headline: Washington secured eight of 17 targets for 103 yards in the Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants on Sunday.
story: Washington led the Jaguars across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his day could have been even better had what appeared to be an acrobatic touchdown catch in the back of the end zone early in the fourth quarter not been ruled incomplete. Washington still made several tough grabs throughout the afternoon against a stingy Giants secondary, and he now has consecutive 100-yard efforts for the first time in 2026. Washington needs just 100 receiving yards to eclipse his career high of 847 heading into a very favorable Week 12 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

headline: Washington caught seven of nine targets for 152 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans.
story: The 152 receiving yards were a new career high for Washington, and the fourth-year WR highlighted his big day with a two-yard TD toss from Trevor Lawrence in the first quarter to open the scoring. It's Washington's second game this season with 100-plus yards, and he'll take a 36-645-6 line on 64 targets through nine contests into a Week 11 tilt against the Giants.

headline: Washington secured two of seven targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday night. He also returned one punt for 11 yards.
story: Washington led the Jaguars in targets while tying for second in receptions and receiving yards on the night. The fourth-year receiver snapped a two-game touchdown drought, crossing the goal line from 50 yards out on a catch and run over the middle with under a minute remaining in the first half. Washington has eclipsed 60 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Titans on Sunday, Nov. 15.

headline: Washington brought in one of two targets for 16 yards and rushed once for 10 yards in the Jaguars' 42-7 win over the Colts on Sunday.
story: The Jaguars had little need to be aggressive through the air with the Colts non-competitive throughout the afternoon. Trevor Lawrence ultimately put up only 14 pass attempts and Quinn Ewers added another three in mop-up duty, leaving little for Washington and the rest of the air attack to produce with. Washington has a 27-432-4 receiving line on 48 targets through seven games heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the reeling Ravens on Thursday night.

headline: Washington caught four of 11 targets for 64 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
story: Despite leading the Jaguars in targets, Washington finished second to Jakobi Meyers in both catches and receiving yards, and he wasn't on the other end of any of Trevor Lawrence's four TDs. It's the third time in the last four games that Washington has failed to reach five grabs or 70 yards, but the fourth contest featured a 6-124-2 line from the fourth-year wideout. Washington will take a 26-416-4 line on 46 targets into a bye before facing the Colts in Week 8.

headline: Washington caught six of nine targets for 124 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
story: The fourth-year wideout accounted for both of the Jaguars' TDs on the day, breaking free for a 51-yard score in the first quarter and then beating blanket coverage from Riq Woolen for a spectacular one-handed grab in the fourth quarter from 27 yards out. Washington was apparently just scratching the surface of his potential in 2025, and through five games this season he's posted a 22-352-4 line on 35 targets as Trevor Lawrence's top downfield option. Washington will look to keep rolling in Week 6 against a Texans defense that has unexpectedly struggled so far in 2026.

headline: Washington secured one of three targets for seven yards, rushed once for three yards and returned one punt for three yards in the Jaguars' 22-17 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
story: Washington had been Trevor Lawrence's top target by a comfortable margin over the first three games of the season, but the Bengals effectively shut down the bulk of Jacksonville's wide-receiver production Sunday. Washington saw the biggest downturn, making it a forgettable fantasy afternoon overall despite the team-level success the Jaguars enjoyed. Washington figures to have an uphill battle in terms of a potential Week 5 resurgence as well, considering the Jaguars will face off with a talented Eagles defense in a Week 5 matchup in London next Sunday.

headline: Striggow (concussion) was listed as a full participant during Jacksonville's practice estimate Thursday, Ryan O'Halloran of The Florida Times-Union reports.
story: Striggow will be good to go for Sunday's matchup against the Titans after clearing the league's concussion protocol. The 24-year-old has compiled 13 tackles (nine solo), including 1.0 sacks, across nine games this season while playing on both defense and special teams.

headline: Striggow (concussion) has been downgraded to out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
story: Striggow wasn't able to clear concussion protocol. He's appeared in nine games this season, logging 25 percent of the defensive snaps as a rotational defensive lineman.

headline: Striggow (concussion) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Giants.
story: Striggow entered the league's concussion protocol following the Jaguars' Week 10 win over the Titans. He was limited in all three practice sessions during Week 11 prep, and he would need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to clear protocol and be available for Sunday's contest. Bryan Thomas and Wesley Williams would both see a bump in rotational snaps at defensive end if Striggow is inactive.

headline: Striggow (concussion) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday.
story: Striggow was forced to check out of Sunday's game at Tennessee after suffering a blow to the head, and he's now dealing with a concussion as the Jaguars begin their Week 11 preparations. If he's able to upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday, it could signal he's close to clearing concussion protocol ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants.

headline: Striggow is being evaluated for a possible concussion and is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Striggow has operated in a rotational role on the defensive line, so Bryan Thomas should see a bump in defensive snaps for as long as the former is out of the game.

headline: Jones (chest) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Jones suffered a chest injury during the first half of the Jaguars' 23-18 loss to the Giants in Week 12 and did not return. However, his full session Wednesday indicates that Jones' injury isn't a severe one and puts him on track to play in Sunday's AFC South tilt against the Titans. Jones has 26 tackles (19 solo) and eight pass defenses (including an interception) across 10 regular-season games.

headline: Jones (chest) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's contest against the Giants.
story: Jones suffered a chest injury early in the first half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end. The Jaguars will now have to operate without their top slot cornerback for the stretch run versus New York.

headline: Jones (chest) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Giants.
story: Jones picked up a chest injury in the first quarter, and his availability for the rest of the game is now uncertain. In his absence, Jourdan Lewis and Jaylon Jones are both candidates to see an increase in workload at cornerback versus New York.

headline: Oluokun compiled nine tackles (seven solo) during Jacksonville's loss to the Giants on Sunday.
story: Oluokun had a solid outing despite the loss, logging a team-high nine tackles while playing every defensive snap. The 2018 sixth-round pick has now totaled 77 tackles (48 solo), including 2.0 sacks, two interceptions and a forced fumble across 10 games this season.

headline: Oluokun finished Sunday's 40-23 win over the Titans with 10 tackles (nine solo).
story: Sunday was the third time in nine regular-season games that Oluokun played every single defensive snap and the second time that he reached double-digit tackles. His nine solo stops were a season high and most in a game since Week 1 of the 2024 season. Oluokun has accumulated 44 tackles (30 solo), including 2.0 sacks, over his last five outings.

headline: Oluokun recorded seven tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Thursday's 33-10 victory over Baltimore.
story: Oluokun tied for his team's lead in stops and notched his second sack of the season when he brought down Joe Fagnano early in the second quarter. Oluokun has been a reliable fantasy IDP asset in 2026 with at least seven tackles in six of his eight games so far. He's tallied 58 total stops, including the 2.0 sacks, along with two interceptions and a forced fumble.

headline: Oluokun recorded nine total tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Sunday's 42-7 win against the Colts.
story: Oluokun led the team in takedowns, notching at least eight tackles for the third straight game. The linebacker was also able to get to quarterback Daniel Jones for his first sack of the year in the second quarter, matching his season total from both the 2024 and 2025 campaigns. Oluokun is as steady as it gets from a fantasy perspective, and he has now registered 51 total tackles (31 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding two interceptions and a forced fumble over seven contests to open the regular season.

headline: Oluokun logged eight tackles (four solo) in the Jaguars' 34-31 loss to the Texans in London on Sunday.
story: Oluokun did not have an outstanding game by any metrics but did put up a solid stat line in a close divisional loss. The linebacker played 94 percent of the Jaguars' defensive snaps in the contest while logging an additional 24 percent of the team's snaps on special teams.
