While the team's backfield is banged up this week, Kelce ability to return to action Sunday at least assures the Chiefs that their top pass catchers are available for QB Patrick Mahomes to target.

headline: Kelce (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Falcons, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.
story: Kelce injured his right ankle at the tail end of his 23-yard catch early in the first quarter, and he's been taken to the locker room to undergo further tests to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. Noah Gray, Jake Briningstool and Jared Wiley are all in line for more snaps at tight end for as long as Kelce is sidelined.

headline: Kelce went to the locker room during Sunday's game in Atlanta due to an apparent ankle injury, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Per Nate Taylor of ESPN.com, Kelce had his right ankle twisted up during a 23-yard catch on the Chiefs' first possession and then walked off the field slowly. For as long as Kelce is sidelined, Noah Gray, Jake Briningstool and Jared Wiley will man tight end for Kansas City.

headline: Kelce brought in four of six targets for 72 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. He also rushed once for one yard.
story: Kelce led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in targets on the afternoon, and his tally in the former category also served as the legendary tight end's second highest of the season. Kelce got there with a big boost from a game-high 38-yard catch, and he'll take a formidable 33-482-2 line into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

headline: Kelce (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Kelce was deemed a limited participant Wednesday, but the tight end's full participation Thursday paves the way for him to be in uniform Sunday against the Jets. Over his last two games, the Chiefs' leader in catches and receiving yards has amassed nine catches (on 15 targets) for 111 yards with a TD, and as long as he stays healthy he'll merit weekly fantasy lineup consideration.

headline: Kelce (ankle) was listed as limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: Kelce logged a limited session this past Thursday before practicing fully a day later. He then approached Week 8 action without an injury designation, en route to recording a 78 percent offensive snap share and catching five of his seven targets for 67 yards in the Chiefs' 28-24 loss to the Broncos. Chances are, the tight end's listed limitations Wednesday were maintenance-related, and he will now have two more chances to work fully ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

headline: Kelce caught five of seven targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.
story: The 37-year-old tight end caught more than four passes and topped 60 yards for the first time since Week 2, but his TD drought stands at four games. Kelce moved up another rung on the NFL's all-time leaderboards with this performance, as he passed Torry Holt to take over 18th place in career receiving yards (13,412). Kelce will take a 29-410-2 line on 42 targets through seven games in the current campaign into a Week 9 clash with the Jets.

headline: Kelce (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: Kelce logged a limited practice Thursday and has been dealing with an ankle issue for a couple weeks. He played through it last Sunday night against the Seahawks and posted four catches for 44 yards on eight targets. The veteran tight end hasn't visited the end zone since Week 3.

headline: Kelce (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Kelce logged a full practice Wednesday, so the tight end's listed limitations a day later make his status for Sunday's game against the Broncos worth monitoring. He also was limited in practice last week but ended up approaching his team's 20-3 loss to Seattle (in which he caught four of his eight targets for 44 yards) without an injury designation.

headline: Kelce caught four of eight targets for 44 yards in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks.
story: Kelce increased his career total to 1,104 regular-season catches, passing Hall of Famers Marvin Harrison (1,102) and Cris Carter (1,101) to move up to fifth on the all-time list. Jason Witten holds the fourth spot with 1,228 receptions, so Kelce is more likely to be caught by Keenan Allen (1,084) than Kelce is to catch Witten. Kelce led the Chiefs with eight targets in the absence of WR Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) and tied fellow TE Noah Gray for the team lead in receiving yards as Kansas City mustered just three Harrison Butker field-goal attempts on offense, two of which missed. This was only the second time Kelce failed to reach the 50-yard threshold in six appearances this season. He had 71 yards in Week 1 against the Broncos, whom the Chiefs will face in a Week 8 road rematch.

headline: Kelce (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: Despite logging limited practices all week, Kelce is good to go for Sunday's trip to hostile Seattle. Particularly with Rashee Rice (hamstring) still sidelined for the Chiefs, Kelce projects as Patrick Mahomes' safety valve over the middle of the field. Kelce has 20 grabs for 299 yards and two touchdowns on 29 targets through five games this season.

headline: Kelce (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Kelce has operated with a cap on his reps for the Chiefs' first two practices of Week 7, but as long as he's able to maintain limited activity or upgrade to full participation Friday, he should be in good position to play Sunday in Seattle. With top wideout Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) remaining sidelined for Thursday's practice and perhaps trending toward another missed game in Week 7, Kelce could be a candidate to take on more volume than usual in the Kansas City passing attack if he's not too hindered by the ankle issue.

headline: Kelce (ankle) was a limited practice participant Wednesday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
story: After a quick start to the season with a 14-231-2 line on 18 targets through the first three games, Kelce has taken a step back over the last two appearances (6-68-0 on nine targets). With an ankle injury now in tow, his status will be watched as the week goes on to get a sense of his availability for Sunday's contest at Seattle.

headline: Kelce caught four of five targets for 53 yards during Sunday's 22-6 win over the Chargers.
story: Kelce was able to exceed two receptions for the first time since Week 2, finishing second on the team in targets and catches behind wide receiver Xavier Worthy, who caught all seven of his targets for 73 yards. Kelce has now reeled in 20 of 27 targets for 299 yards and two touchdowns over five contests to open the 2026 campaign.

headline: Kelce caught two of four targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders.
story: Kelce was surprisingly quiet in this battle between AFC West rivals that both entered the game with 3-0 records. This was the second consecutive game in which Kelce was held to two catches, but he was averaging 77 receiving yards per game prior to Sunday's 15-yard performance. He will celebrate his 37th birthday Monday and will have a chance to rest up during a Week 5 bye before the Chiefs return to action in Week 6 against the Chargers.

headline: Johnson rushed 17 times for 72 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 24 yards in the Chiefs' 13-10 loss to the Bills on Thursday.
story: Making a third straight start in place of Kenneth Walker (groin), Johnson put together another useful all-around performance that included his third rushing touchdown of the season on a one-yard run early in the third quarter. Johnson also recorded at least four catches for the third consecutive game, and he's now accumulated 410 scrimmage yards and four total TDs over his three starts. Walker is likely to be back for next Thursday's Week 13 road showdown against the Rams, but Johnson is likely to retain a solid complementary role even when his star teammate is back on the field.

headline: Chiefs take the lead with Emmett Johnson TD
story: Chiefs take the lead with Emmett Johnson TD

headline: With Kenneth Walker (groin) ruled out for Thursday night's game against the Bills,  Johnson is once again set to lead the Chiefs' backfield.
story: The Chiefs are on a short week, so the team elected to err on the side of caution with Walker, setting the stage for Johnson to log his third straight start at RB for the team. The 2026 fifth-rounder thus remains an extremely viable Week 12 fantasy lineup option. In both of his previous turns in a starting capacity, Johnson has exceeded 100 rushing yards while adding 10 catches and three total TDs in that span.

headline: Emmett Johnson could be a flex option even when Kenneth Walker III returns
story: Emmett Johnson could be a flex option even when Kenneth Walker III returns

headline: Johnson rushed 23 times for 105 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 38 yards in the Chiefs' 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Making a second consecutive start in place of Kenneth Walker (groin), Johnson once again provided starter-quality production as both a runner and receiver. The rookie also added his second career rushing TD on a three-yard run late in the first quarter, making it an all-around rewarding fantasy day. The Chiefs expect Walker to be ready to return for a Thanksgiving night showdown against the Bills in four days, but even if that comes to pass, Johnson has likely earned himself a larger role for the stretch run with his performance the last two contests.

headline: With Kenneth Walker (groin) ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Johnson is in line to handle workhorse duties for the second straight week, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: There was no sense in pushing Walker to play against a Cardinals team that is injury-ruined and likely to be blown out at Arrowhead. Johnson will get another crack at RB1 duties after he dismantled Atlanta's defense for 171 total yards and two touchdowns on 28 touches last Sunday. He's a top fantasy RB play.

headline: Johnson rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
story: Drawing his first career start due to Kenneth Walker (groin) being sidelined, Johnson put on a pretty convincing impression of his star teammate. Not only did Johnson just get himself over the century mark in rushing yards, but he finished as the team leader in receptions and targets while checking in as the runner-up in receiving yards. Johnson struck from 12 and six yards out for his two receiving TDs, underscoring his considerable versatility. If Walker is unable to garner active status for next Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Cardinals, the Chiefs' ground attack will remain in good hands with Johnson.

headline: Johnson will be the Chiefs' top running back for Week 10 after Kenneth Walker (groin) was ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Walker popped up on Friday's practice report as a DNP due to groin tightness, and the injury is severe enough for the fifth-year running back to miss his first game of the season. That leaves Johnson -- the Chiefs' fifth-round pick of the 2026 NFL Draft -- as the lead back for Sunday's game, and with Jaydn Ott (hamstring) listed as questionable, the team could elevate Nate Carter from the practice squad to provide additional backfield depth. Through eight regular-season games, Johnson has turned 26 carries into 111 yards (4.3 YPC) and a touchdown and caught 14 passes on 16 targets for 237 yards and a score.

headline: Coach Andy Reid noted that Johnson would take the bulk of the Chiefs' carries in the event that Kenneth Walker -- who didn't practice Friday due to groin tightness -- is forced to miss Sunday's game against the Falcons, Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star reports.
story: Added context regarding Walker's status will arrive via Friday's final injury report when the Chiefs assign their Week 10 injury designations. Chances are, Walker will be deemed questionable, but if he ends up sidelined this weekend, Johnson would provide those who roster Walker, or otherwise need RB help, with a viable pivot option.

headline: Johnson rushed six times for 34 yards and a touchdown and returned one kickoff for 29 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
story: The Chiefs held a 28-12 lead by the end of three quarters, which provided the opportunity for head coach Andy Reid to give Kenneth Walker, who scored three total touchdowns, some down time in the latter portion of the contest. Johnson took advantage of his opportunities, recording a six-yard touchdown run with 3:35 remaining. The rookie fifth-round pick's yardage total was a new career high, while his carry tally was his highest since Week 3. Johnson will remain in a modest No. 2 role for a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

headline: Johnson carried the ball once for 15 yards and caught all five of his targets for 128 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos. He added 44 yards on his only kickoff return.
story: The rookie running back flashed his explosiveness on a 73-yard catch-and-run in the second quarter that produced Johnson's first career NFL touchdown. He came into Sunday with a 9-109-0 line on 11 targets through six games, and his six touches were firmly behind Kenneth Walker's 25, but Johnson's breakout performance can only encourage Andy Reid to find more ways to get the ball in his hands. Johnson will look to build on this effort in Week 9 against the Jets.

headline: Johnson caught two of three passes for 17 yards and returned three kickoffs for 81 yards during Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks. He also added two tackles on special teams.
story: Johnson was held without a carry for the second time in three games, with lead back Kenneth Walker bottled up for 36 yards on 14 carries (2.6 YPC). Johnson has seen three carries or fewer in four of the first six games of the regular season and figures to be limited to a third-down role as a pass catcher unless Walker misses time. The Chiefs will stay on the road for a Week 8 divisional matchup against the Broncos on Nov. 1.

headline: Johnson turned three carries into six yards and caught two of three targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 22-6 win over the Chargers. He also returned two kickoffs for 50 yards.
story: Johnson maintained his rotational role in the Chiefs offense, with his 18 offensive snaps well behind Kenneth Walker's 45. Given Walker's tremendous start to the season, Johnson is one of the premier handcuff running backs in fantasy, and his scoring floor would rise significantly if the former ever misses time. The Chiefs will take their 5-0 record on the road for Week 7 against the Seahawks on Oct. 25.

headline: Johnson caught his lone target for 10 yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders.
story: The rookie running back didn't handle a single rushing attempt behind Kenneth Walker's 22 carries for 177 yards and two touchdowns. Johnson still played 17 offensive snaps and remains the clear backup and bench stash to own in fantasy should something ever happen to Walker.

headline: Johnson carried the ball six times for 17 yards and returned one kickoff for 31 yards in Kansas City's 24-10 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Johnson played 13 offensive snaps and nine special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The rookie fifth-rounder continues to give Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker an occasional breather, but Johnson's role on offense doesn't figure to expand beyond that without an injury to the former Seahawk.

headline: Nussmeier (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Chiefs' emergency third quarterback against the Bills on Thursday.
story: Nussmeier has yet to appear in a game this season but will once again serve as the team's emergency quarterback. The rookie seventh-round pick will only be able to play against Buffalo if both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Nussmeier (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Chiefs' emergency third quarterback against the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: The rookie seventh-rounder has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026. As the emergency QB3, Nussmeier is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Nussmeier (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Chiefs' emergency third quarterback against the Falcons on Sunday.
story: Nussmeier will continue to be the Chiefs' emergency third quarterback, which means he is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Nussmeier is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets but will serve as the Chiefs' emergency third quarterback.
story: It's a familiar role for the rookie seventh-round pick, who has served as the emergency No. 3 QB regularly this year. Nussmeier won't be able to see the field unless both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Nussmeier (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Denver, though he will be available as the team's emergency quarterback.
story: Nussmeier is inactive for another contest. However, the signal-caller will be available if Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Nussmeier (coach's decision) is inactive as the emergency third quarterback for Sunday night's game against the Seahawks.
story: The rookie seventh-round pick continues to sit behind Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields to begin the season.

headline: Nussmeier (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Nussmeier will once again be the Chiefs' emergency QB3, meaning the rookie seventh-rounder is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Patrick Mahomes and Justin Fields leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Woods (neck) is active for Thursday's game against the Bills.
story: Woods drew the questionable tag for Thanksgiving Day, and the rookie first-rounder has been cleared by medical staff to return from a three-game absence due to a neck injury. In seven regular-season games prior to the injury, Woods accumulated 13 tackles (three solo), including 0.5 sacks, and one pass defense while operating in a rotational role on the Chiefs' interior defensive line.

headline: Woods (neck) is listed as questionable for Thursday night's game against the Bills.
story: Woods has missed three consecutive games with a neck injury. The rookie first-rounder was a full participant in Wednesday's practice session but remains questionable to suit up for Thursday's primetime contest.

headline: Woods (neck) was listed as a full participant for Monday's estimated practice.
story: Woods ended Week 11 prep as a limited participant and did not play in Sunday's win over the Cardinals. The defensive tackle has now been listed as limited or better in four straight sessions, making a compelling case for his return to the field for Thursday night's primetime showdown with the Bills.

headline: Woods (neck) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Woods opened Week 11 prep with back-to-back full practices before having his reps limited Friday, which prompted the Chiefs to tag him as questionable. The rookie first-rounder has not been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday, so he will miss his third consecutive game due to a neck injury. Bryson Eason and Marcus Harris will continue to operate in rotational roles on the interior defensive line behind Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga in the absence of Woods, whose next chance to play is Thanksgiving Day against the Bills.

headline: Woods (neck) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Woods has missed the Chiefs' last two contests with a neck injury he sustained in the team's Week 8 loss to the Broncos. The rookie first-rounder now starts Week 11 prep as a full participant, meaning he will likely suit up for Sunday's contest against the Cardinals as a rotational option for the Chiefs' defensive line.

headline: Woods (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons.
story: Woods will miss consecutive games due to a neck injury he sustained early in the Chiefs' Week 8 loss to the Broncos. The rookie first-rounder is progressing in his recovery, but it remains unclear when he will return to the field.

headline: Woods (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets, Nate Taylor of ESPN.com reports.
story: Woods will not play in Sunday's game as he continues to deal with a neck injury he sustained in the Chiefs' Week 8 loss to the Broncos. The rookie first-rounder is continuing to make progress in his recovery.

headline: Woods (neck) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's contest against the Broncos.
story: Woods went down with a neck injury early in the contest, and his night has now officially come to a premature end. Woods will now shift his focus toward being ready to go for the team's Week 9 matchup with the Jets.

headline: Woods (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Broncos.
story: Woods suffered a neck injury in the first quarter, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. In his absence, Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga will continue to operate as the Chiefs' top options at defensive tackle.

headline: The Chiefs ruled out Walker (groin) for Thursday's game against the Bills.
story: Though Walker was able to log a limited practice Tuesday, he was listed as a non-participant Wednesday and will wind up missing a third straight contest while he continues to nurse a sore groin. With Walker sidelined, rookie Emmett Johnson is set for another turn as the Chiefs' lead back, with Jaydn Ott serving as his top backup and Nate Carter a possible practice-squad elevation. Given that the Chiefs on are on a short week, Walker -- who last saw game action Nov. 8 -- will have added time to heal before the team's next contest Dec. 3 against the Rams.

headline: The Chiefs listed Walker (groin) as a limited participant in Tuesday's practice.
story: After he had been listed as a non-participant on five straight injury reports and missed two games along the way, Walker was able to take a step forward Tuesday as he works his way back from a sore groin. Per Nate Taylor of ESPN.com, head coach Andy Reid said prior to the session that Walker was "feeling pretty good," while noting that Tuesday's practice would be important in deciding whether the running back suits up Thursday versus the Bills. Though Walker will reclaim a starting role if he ultimately gets cleared to play Thanksgiving Day, he could wind up ceding more snaps and touches to rookie Emmett Johnson, who shined as the Chiefs' lead back over the past two weeks.

headline: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said that Walker (groin) will practice Tuesday, Nate Taylor of ESPN.com reports. "I'm not anticipating a ton of work," Reid said. "Let's see how does. He's feeling pretty good."
story: Walker has been sidelined for the Chiefs' last two games due to a sore groin and was listed as a non-participant in Monday's practice. Though the running back appears poised to take a step forward in terms of activity Tuesday, Reid's comments suggest that Walker will likely be a limited participant. The Chiefs will wait and see how Walker responds to practice Tuesday before having a better feel for his status for Thursday's game against the Bills.

headline: Walker (groin) was listed as a non-participant on Monday's practice estimate.
story: Since the Chiefs are coming off a 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday, the team held a walkthrough Monday in preparation for Thursday's game against the Bills. Nate Taylor of ESPN.com previously reported that the Chiefs are "optimistic" that Walker may be available for the team's Thanksgiving night contest, but with one 'DNP' now on the books, the running back has two more opportunities to log any listed level of practice participation before the team posts its Week 12 game statuses.

headline: Walker (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Walker, who wasn't able to practice this week, will thus target a potential return Thursday against the Bills. The Chiefs -- per ESPN.com -- are "optimistic" he will play Thanksgiving night, but they will err on the side of caution with a short week ahead, and as such Emmett Johnson -- who rushed 22 times for 101 yards and brought in six of seven targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in Week 10 -- is headed toward a second consecutive start this weekend.

headline: Head coach Andy Reid said Friday that Walker (groin) "most likely" won't be available Sunday against the Cardinals, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.
story: Walker showed up at the Chiefs' facilities last Friday with a tight groin and eventually was ruled out for this past Sunday's game in Atlanta. With no practice reps to speak of yet during Week 11 prep, he appears to be trending toward another absence this Sunday, which again will thrust rookie Emmett Johnson into a workhorse role out of Kansas City's backfield.

headline: Walker (groin) wasn't spotted during the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Pete Sweeney of The Kansas City Star reports.
story: Walker hasn't practiced at all this week and should be expected to be ruled out for Sunday's game against Arizona later Friday. With the Cardinals bringing their minor-league team to Kansas City this weekend, there's no reason to push Walker when the Chiefs have a quick Week 12 turnaround with a game against the Bills on Thanksgiving. Emmett Johnson will be a top fantasy RB for Week 11 once Walker is officially ruled out.

headline: Walker (groin) did not practice Thursday.
story: Walker is looking extremely unlikely to play Sunday against a Cardinals team that Kansas City should handle with ease at home. The Chiefs have a quick Week 12 turnaround against the Bills on Thanksgiving, and it may make sense to let Walker rest for another week in preparation for that contest, especially after rookie Emmett Johnson showed in Week 10 against Atlanta that he's more than capable of carrying the torch in the backfield. Fantasy players need to be prepared to be without Walker for at least one more week.

headline: Walker (groin) won't practice Wednesday, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.
story: Walker was sidelined for the Chiefs' Week 10 win over the Falcons, and in his absence, rookie Emmett Johnson erupted for 171 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns on 28 touches. Now sidelined to begin Week 11 prep, Walker will have two more chances to practice before the Chiefs make a call on his status for Sunday's game against the Cardinals. Walker's sore groin isn't believed to a major concern, and head coach Andy Reid told Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site on Wednesday that the tailback is "feeling a lot better." The Chiefs will see how Walker progresses as the week rolls along, but it wouldn't be surprising if the team erred on the side of caution and held him out for another game. Kansas City will be heavy favorites for its matchup with Arizona before facing a quick turnaround in Week 12 for what should be a more competitive matchup with the Bills next Thursday.

headline: Walker (groin), who won't play Sunday in Atlanta, is expected to "be able to go" next Sunday against the Cardinals, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Walker showed up at the Chiefs' facilities Friday with a tight groin, didn't take part in the ensuing practice and then was listed as questionable for Week 10 action. The team then ruled him out Saturday, which Rapoport called "more precautionary than anything else." In Walker's absence, rookie fifth-round pick Emmett Johnson is expected to be Kansas City's primary runner.

headline: Walker (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Jordan Schultz of Fox Sports reports.
story: Walker was a late addition to the Chiefs' practice report Friday as a DNP due to what was described as "groin tightness." He was initially tagged as questionable for Sunday's contest, but the injury is severe enough for the fifth-year running back to miss his first game of the regular season. Rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson is projected to lead Kansas City's backfield against Atlanta in Walker's absence, and with Jaydn Ott (hamstring) listed as questionable, the Chiefs could elevate Nate Carter from the practice squad to the active roster. Walker's next opportunity to play is Week 11 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 22.

headline: Walker (groin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
story: Walker was added to the Chiefs' Week 10 injury report due to groin tightness that kept him from practicing Friday. Now that he's carrying an official 'questionable' designation heading into the weekend, the running back's status will need to be tracked as Sunday's 1:00 pm ET kickoff approaches. In the event that Walker -- who is averaging a robust 109.0 rushing yards per game and has scored 11 total TDs through eight contests -- is made inactive for the contest, Emmett Johnson would be in line to handle the bulk of the team's carries versus Atlanta.

headline: Walker (groin) sat out Friday's practice due to groin tightness, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.
story: Per McDowell, coach Andy Reid noted of Walker on Friday, "we'll see how he feels through this afternoon, with rehab, and through tomorrow." Based on this report, there's a good chance Walker will be deemed questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons. If he ends up limited or out this weekend, the door would be open for rookie Emmett Johnson to step into an expanded role in Week 10.

headline: Walker rushed 18 times for 102 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 41 yards and two more scores in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday.
story: Walker put together another one of his signature high-efficiency performances on the ground, averaging 5.7 yards per carry in the process. He contributed a seven-yard touchdown reception on the first play of the second quarter, and he struck again as a receiver via a 25-yard scoring grab with just over five minutes remaining in the first half. Walker capped off the highly fantasy-friendly day with his seventh rushing touchdown of the season, a two-yard run in the waning moments of the third quarter. Walker is up to 872 rushing yards, 172 receiving yards and 11 total touchdowns heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

headline: Walker carried the ball 21 times for 69 yards and caught four of five targets for 15 yards in Sunday's 28-24 loss to the Broncos.
story: The star running back was held below 100 scrimmage yards for a second straight game, but Walker watched his rookie backup, Emmett Johnson, erupt for a 5-128-1 line on five targets and take his only carry for 15 yards. Walker is still the clear No. 1 in the Kansas City backfield, but Johnson may have earned more consistent work with Sunday's impressive effort -- touches which might come at Walker's expense. He'll head into a Week 9 meeting with the Jets second in the race for the NFL rushing crown with 770 yards, just behind Bijan Robinson's 780.

headline: Walker rushed 14 times for 36 yards while catching four of five targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks.
story: Walker was held in check by his former team after recording at least 70 rushing yards in each of his first five games with the Chiefs. The MVP of Super LX with Seattle entered play Sunday leading the league with 665 rushing yards on 6.3 yards per carry in the 2026 regular season, but he mustered just 2.6 YPC in by far his quietest performance of the season against a Seahawks defense that hasn't allowed a 100-yard rushing performance since Week 8 of the 2024 regular season. Walker has a nice bounce-back opportunity in a Week 8 road clash with the Broncos, against whom he generated 191 scrimmage yards and two total touchdowns in the season opener.

headline: Walker ripped off 128 yards and two touchdowns on 19 carries and added two catches (on three targets) for 11 yards during Sunday's 22-6 win against the Chargers.
story: Following the Chiefs' Week 5 bye, Walker continued his early-season momentum with his new team, surpassing 100 yards on the ground for the fourth time in five games in a different uniform than the Seahawks. He now boasts 133.0 rushing yards per game, which prorated over a 17-game slate (2,261) would easily go past Eric Dickerson's NFL record 2,105 from the 1984 campaign and also mark the 10th 2,000-yard season in the history of the league. Walker's next chance to strike occurs next Sunday when he visits his former teammates in Seattle.

headline: Walker rushed 22 times for 177 yards and two touchdowns while catching his only target for two yards in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Raiders.
story: Walker's two touchdowns came just 19 seconds apart in the fourth quarter, as he gave Kansas City the lead with a two-yard touchdown run and added a 22-yard touchdown run to create some breathing room after the Raiders fumbled the ensuing kickoff. The free-agent addition has paid immediate dividends for his new team, racking up 537 rushing yards and six total touchdowns through four games with the Chiefs. Walker has handled heavy workloads early in the season and will have a chance to rest up during a Week 5 bye before the 4-0 Chiefs host the Chargers in Week 6.

headline: Norman-Lott (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday night's game against the Bills.
story: Despite logging full participation sessions in Week 12 prep, Norman-Lott will not suit up for Thursday night's contest. The Chiefs activated the defensive tackle from the reserve/PUP list Nov. 18, but he is not quite ready to return to the field.

headline: Norman-Lott (knee) was listed as a full participant for Monday's estimated practice.
story: Norman-Lott missed Sunday's win over the Cardinals due to a knee injury. The defensive tackle was activated from the Chiefs' reserve/PUP list Wednesday and logged three limited practices during Week 11 prep. The upgrade to full participation, even for an estimated practice, is a strong sign Norman-Lott will be set to suit up for Thursday night's showdown with the Bills.

headline: Norman-Lott (knee) is inactive against Arizona on Sunday.
story: Norman-Lott was activated from the Chiefs' reserve/PUP list Wednesday, but he was limited in all three practices during Week 11 prep and drew the questionable tag for Sunday's game. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025, but he's not quite ready to make his return. Norman-Lott's next opportunity to make his 2026 regular-season debut is Thanksgiving Day against the Bills.

headline: Norman-Lott (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against Arizona.
story: Norman-Lott was removed from the reserve/PUP list Wednesday, but he may not be ready to make his 2026 regular-season debut as he continues to work his way back from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025. His return would give the Chiefs more depth on the interior defensive line behind starters Chris Jones and Khyiris Tonga.

headline: The Chiefs activated Norman-Lott (knee) from the reserve/PUP list Wednesday, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
story: Norman-Lott was removed from the PUP list prior to the expiration of his 21-day practice window. He was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and his participation over the next two days will determine whether he'll make his 2026 regular-season debut against the Cardinals on Sunday. Norman-Lott is in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025.

headline: The Chiefs designated Norman-Lott (knee) to return from injured reserve Wednesday.
story: Norman-Lott was limited in his return to practice Wednesday. He's in the final stages of his recovery from a torn ACL that he sustained in October of 2025. The Chiefs now have 21 days to activate Norman-Lott from the PUP list, otherwise he would be forced to miss the entire 2026 season.

headline: Moore (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday night's game against the Bills.
story: Moore will miss his third consecutive game with an ankle injury. Joshua Ezeudu will once again be called upon to start at right tackle for the Chiefs' offense.

headline: Moore (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Moore will miss a second consecutive game due to an ankle injury, which means Joshua Ezeudu will likely start at right tackle against Arizona. Moore's next chance to play is Week 12 against Buffalo on Thanksgiving Day.

headline: Moore (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site reports.
story: Moore did not play against the Falcons in Week 10 due to an ankle injury he sustained against the Jets in Week 9. He'll have two more chances to practice in at least a limited capacity, but if he cannot play against the Cardinals on Sunday, then Joshua Ezeudu would likely start at right tackle for a second consecutive game.

headline: Moore (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Falcons.
story: Moore suffered an ankle injury in the Chiefs' Week 9 win over the Jets. The right tackle will not suit up for Sunday's game due to the injury, leaving Joshua Ezeudu to start against the Falcons.

headline: Head coach Andy Reid stated Moore (ankle) is considered "day-to-day," Charles Goldman of AtoZSports.com reports.
story: Moore suffered an ankle injury in Sunday's win over the Jets. While he hasn't been ruled out for Week 10 versus the Falcons, there's certainly the possibility of an absence. If that's the case, Joshua Ezeudu may fill the void at right tackle.

headline: Moore (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Moore exited the second half of Sunday's game with an ankle injury. While the 28-year-old undergoes further evaluation, Joshua Ezeudu will return to play left tackle for the Chiefs' offense.

headline: Moore (concussion) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: The lack of an injury designation indicates that Moore has cleared the league's concussion protocol. He should reclaim his starting spot at right tackle while Joshua Ezeudu reverts to a depth role.

headline: Moore (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Moore has progressed enough through the league's concussion protocol to practice without restrictions Wednesday. However, he needs to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to clear protocol and be available for Sunday's game against the Broncos.

headline: Moore (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: Moore entered the league's concussion protocol during the Chiefs' Week 6 against the Chargers. He was not cleared to practice during Week 7 prep and will be sidelined for Sunday's contest, so Joshua Ezeudu will likely draw the start at right tackle. Moore's next opportunity to play is Week 8 against the Broncos on Nov. 1.

headline: Moore (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Chargers.
story: Moore has entered the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not return to Sunday's game. Joshua Ezeudu will likely finish out the contest at right tackle.

headline: Moore (head) is questionable to return to Sunday's game with a potential concussion, Matt Derrick of ChiefsDigest.com reports.
story: Moore is being evaluated by one of the NFL's independent neurologists. If the right tackle is deemed to have suffered a concussion, he will be ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game. Joshua Ezeudu is in at right tackle.

headline: The Chiefs placed VanSumeren (knee) on the reserve/injured list Tuesday.
story: VanSumeren didn't practice Tuesday due to a sprained knee that will now keep him out for at least the next four weeks, according to Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site. In six regular-season games in 2026, the fourth-year pro played a majority of his reps on special teams, with just six of 104 total snaps coming on offense.

headline: VanSumeren (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: VanSumeran injured his knee in the second half, and with no other fullback on the 53-man roster, the Chiefs could turn to tight end Jake Briningstool to provide additional blocking out of the backfield. VanSumeran's status over the coming days will be worth monitoring, given that the Chiefs are operating on a short week and play against the Bills on Thanksgiving Day.

headline: Tranquill recorded eight total tackles (three solo) during Sunday's 34-7 win against the Cardinals.
story: Tranquill led the team in stops in Week 11, notching at least eight tackles for the third straight week. He was able to put together an impressive performance while playing a season-low 39 defensive snaps as a result of the team's blowout victory. Tranquill has now compiled 83 total tackles (42 solo), two passes defensed and a fumble recovery over the team's first 10 games of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Tranquill recorded nine total tackles (six solo) during Sunday's 35-13 victory over the Falcons.
story: Tranquill finished tied for the team lead in tackles with fellow linebacker Nick Bolton in Week 10, notching at least nine takedowns for the third time in four weeks after not having reached that mark in any of the team's first five games of the year. On the season, Tranquill has now produced 75 total tackles (39 solo), two passes defensed and a fumble recovery over nine contests so far.

headline: Tranquill collected 13 tackles (seven solo) in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
story: It was Tranquill's second double-digit tackles game of the season, and both have come over the last three weeks. The veteran linebacker has piled up 66 tackles (33 solo), two pass breakups and one fumble recovery on 88 percent of the defensive snaps across eight games this season.

headline: Tranquill finished Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks with 12 tackles (four solo).
story: Tranquil led the Chiefs in combined tackles Sunday, and he was one of three Kansas City defenders to reach double-digit stops. He's logged at least seven tackles in each of the first six games of the regular season and is up to 48 tackles (22 solo), two pass defenses and one fumble recovery in 2026.

headline: Bolton recorded five total tackles (two solo) and a pass defensed during Sunday's 34-7 win over Arizona.
story: Bolton was on the field for a season-low 38 defensive snaps as Kansas City dominated the Cardinals in Week 11, and as a result, he notched his fewest takedowns since Week 1. The linebacker has now registered 94 total tackles (46 solo), three passes defensed and two forced fumbles over 10 contests to open the 2026 season.

headline: Bolton (shin) was a full participant at practice Thursday.
story: Bolton popped up on the Chiefs' injury report with a shin issue Wednesday, but it doesn't look like it was anything serious. He's fifth in the league in total tackles (89) going into a Week 11 matchup versus a pass-happy Cardinals offense.

headline: Bolton (shin) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Bolton likely picked up the injury during the Chiefs' 35-13 win over the Falcons in Week 10, when he posted nine tackles (five solo) and a forced fumble. The sixth-year linebacker will have two more opportunities to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.

headline: Bolton recorded nine total tackles (five solo) and a forced fumble during Sunday's 35-13 win over Atlanta.
story: Bolton was able to notch at least nine takedowns for the eighth straight game, and he forced a fumble for the second straight week. The linebacker stripped the ball from Kyle Pitts with 4:10 left in the fourth quarter, and the fumble was recovered by teammate Chamarri Conner. On the year, Bolton has now registered 89 total tackles (44 solo), two passes defensed and two forced fumbles over nine contests so far.

headline: Bolton recorded 12 tackles (five solo) and a forced fumble in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
story: Bolton doesn't do much in the box scores other than rack up tackles, but he's good at that and now has five double-digit tackles games through eight contests to begin the 2026 campaign. For the season, Bolton is up to 80 tackles (39 solo), two pass breakups and a forced fumble on 99 percent of the Chiefs' defensive snaps.

headline: Bolton registered 11 tackles (six solo) during the Chiefs' 20-3 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
story: Bolton played all but one of the Chiefs' 69 defensive snaps during Sunday's loss, and he finished second on the team in tackles behind Drue Tranquill (12). Bolton has recorded double-digit stops in four of six regular-season games and is up to 59 tackles (29 solo) and two pass defenses on the year.

headline: Bolton recorded 11 total tackles (three solo) during Sunday's 22-6 win over the Chargers.
story: Bolton led the team in takedowns, notching double-digit tackles in a game for the third time this season. The linebacker has now registered 48 total tackles (23 solo) and two passes defensed over five contests to open the 2026 campaign.

headline: Bolton posted nine tackles (four solo) during the Chiefs' 30-27 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Bolton played every single defensive snap during Sunday's win and finished as the Chiefs' second-leading tackler behind rookie corner Mansoor Delane (10). Through four regular-season games and heading into the Chiefs' Week 5 bye, Bolton leads the team with 37 combined tackles, which is tied with Akeem Davis-Gaither and Jihaad Campbell for sixth-most in the NFL.

headline: Bolton recorded 11 tackles (eight solo) and a pass breakup in Sunday's 24-10 win over the Dolphins.
story: Bolton has now posted double-digit tackles in back-to-back games. He has 100-plus tackles in four of the last five seasons and appears to be well on his way to another triple-digit campaign. Bolton has 28 tackles (16 solo) and a pair of pass breakups through three games to begin the 2026 season.

headline: Josh Allen picked off in the end zone
story: Josh Allen picked off in the end zone

headline: Karlaftis recorded four total tackles (three solo), including 2.5 sacks, and a forced fumble during Sunday's 34-7 win over the Cardinals.
story: Karlaftis was a man on a mission in Week 11, getting to Cardinals quarterback Josh Johnson on three separate occasions. The defensive lineman combined with teammate Chris Jones to sack Johnson in the second quarter before securing full sacks of the quarterback on back-to-back plays in the third quarter. Karlaftis is now up to 38 total tackles (20 solo), including 8.0 sacks, while also adding a career-high 10 passes defensed, one of which is an interception, and two forced fumbles over 10 contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Karlaftis recorded six tackles (four solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a pass breakup in Sunday's 35-12 win over the Jets.
story: After starting the season without a sack in his first four games, Karlaftis has 4.0 sacks over his last four contests. For the season, the 25-year-old edge rusher is up to 32 tackles (16 solo), including the 4.0 sacks, a career-high nine pass breakups, including his first career interception, and a forced fumble across eight games. He's on pace to shatter his previous career high of 48 tackles, which was set last season.

headline: Karlaftis registered six total tackles, a sack and two pass breakups in Sunday's 22-6 win over the Chargers.
story: Though Sunday's contest marked the first time all season that he notched a sack, Karlaftis has been making life difficult on quarterbacks throughout the campaign. Per Pro Football Focus, Karlaftis ranks seventh in the NFL with 27 total quarterback pressures, including 19 over the Chiefs' past two games. Karlaftis has also tallied 21 tackles, four pass breakups and an interception through five appearances.

headline: Ott logged five rushing attempts for 12 yards and logged one tackle on kick coverage in the Chiefs' 34-7 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Ott logged 12 offensive snaps and eight special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The running back saw a few carries behind Emmett Johnson due to the absence of Kenneth Walker (groin). With Walker likely returning for Thursday night's game against the Bills, Ott may not see the field on offense in that contest.

headline: Ott (hamstring) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Ott was unable to play against the Falcons in Week 10 due to a hamstring injury. However, the undrafted rookie out of Oklahoma was cleared to practice in full Wednesday, so he should be available for Sunday's home game against the Cardinals. If Kenneth Walker (groin) cannot play in Week 11, then Ott would have the opportunity to serve as the Chiefs' RB2 behind rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson.

headline: Ott (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Matt McMullen of the Chiefs' official site reports.
story: Ott drew the questionable tag for Week 10 after popping up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a hamstring injury. The injury is severe enough for him to miss Sunday's game, and his next chance to suit up is Week 11 against the Cardinals on Nov. 22. With both Ott and Kenneth Walker (groin) sidelined, the Chiefs' backfield will be led by rookie fifth-rounder Emmett Johnson, while Nate Carter -- who was elevated from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday -- operates in a rotational role.

headline: Ott (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
story: Ott popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a hamstring injury. He was also limited in Friday's session, and with Kenneth Walker (groin) also questionable, the Chiefs enter the weekend with Emmett Johnson as the only healthy running back on the 53-man roster. Nate Carter is the only running back on Kansas City's practice squad and would be a top candidate for elevation to the active roster depending on the statuses of both Ott and Walker.

headline: The Chiefs signed Ott from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.
story: The Chiefs placed Brashard Smith (hamstring) on injured reserve Saturday in a corresponding move. Smith's injury leaves an opportunity for Ott. The undrafted free agent out of Oklahoma could make his NFL debut during Sunday Night Football as the Chiefs take on the Seahawks in Week 7.

headline: Keenan (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Keenan was unable to practice during Week 12 prep due to a knee injury he sustained against the Broncos in Week 11, and his next chance to play is Week 14 against the Chargers on Sunday, Dec. 13. The Raiders will enter the weekend with only two healthy defensive lineman on the 53-man roster in Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi.

headline: Keenan (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's contest against Denver.
story: Keenan went down with a knee injury in the first half, and he will now officially be sidelined for the rest of Week 11. With Adam Butler (concussion) also done for the day, JJ Pegues will handle the bulk of the workload at defensive tackle versus the Broncos.

headline: Keenan (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Broncos.
story: Keenan picked up a knee injury late in the first half, and his availability for the rest of the game is now up in the air. In his absence, Adam Butler and JJ Pegues are the team's two remaining defensive tackles versus Denver.

headline: Powers-Johnson (Achiles) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Powers-Johnson was injured in Friday's practice, and coach Klint Kubiak suggested it could be a serious injury, according to Sam Warren of The Athletic. He hasn't logged an offensive snap since Week 5 after opening the season as the Raiders' starting right guard. Trey Zuhn has been manning the position.

headline: Powers-Johnson (groin) was a full participant in practice Thursday.
story: Powers-Johnson suffered a groin injury against New Orleans in Week 3 and didn't practice at all last week. The third-year offensive lineman didn't play against Kansas City this past Sunday, but now that he's returned to full practice participation, it seems likely Powers-Johnson will be able to suit up Sunday in New England.

headline: Powers-Johnson (groin) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Powers-Johnson was unable to practice all week due to a groin injury. Bryce Cabeldue will be the lone reserve guard behind starters Caleb Rogers and Spencer Burford in the absence of Powers-Johnson.

headline: Butler (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday night's game against the Browns, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: The defensive lineman sustained a concussion last Sunday against the Broncos and will miss at least one contest while he works through the protocol. With Tim Keenan (knee) also out against Cleveland and JJ Pegues (elbow) questionable, the Raiders may be especially thin up front Sunday night.

headline: Butler (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Butler enterted the NFL's concussion protocol after being ruled out for the remainder of the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos. The defensive tackle will need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to return to full-contact practice.

headline: Butler (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's contest against the Broncos.
story: Butler took a blow to the head late in the first half, and his night has now officially come to a premature end due to a concussion. With Tim Keenan (knee) also done for the night, JJ Pegues is the last man standing at defensive tackle for Las Vegas.

headline: Butler (head) is questionable to return to Sunday's matchup with the Broncos.
story: Butler is dealing with a potential head injury that he suffered late in the first half, and as a result, his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. With Tim Keenan (knee) also questionable to return, Las Vegas has become rather thin at defensive tackle.

headline: Hemingway (stinger) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns, Scott Petrak of the Elyria Chronicle-Telegram reports.
story: Hemingway missed the final two practices of Week 12 prep due to what was classified as a stinger, and the second-year defensive tackle will end up missing his second consecutive game. He'll join Adam Butler (concussion) and Tim Keenan (knee) on the sidelines Sunday, and that leaves Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi as the only healthy defensive lineman on the Raiders' active roster heading into the weekend. With the Raiders on a bye for Week 13, Hemingway's next opportunity to play is Week 14 against the Chargers on Sunday, Dec. 13.

headline: Hemingway (upper body) was listed as a non-participant in Las Vegas' practice estimate Thursday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Hemingway is still battling the shoulder injury that sidelined him for the Week 11 loss to Denver. The 25-year-old will likely need to be upgraded to a full participant in Friday's practice in order to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's matchup against the Browns.

headline: Hemingway (upper body) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Hemingway did not play in the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos due to a stinger injury. The defensive lineman has continued to suffer the stinger's effects in Week 12 prep but has upgraded to a limited participant. Hemingway will likely need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice for a chance to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns.

headline: Hemingway (upper body) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Broncos, Paul Gutierrez of the Raiders' official site reports.
story: Hemingway did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions as he continues to deal with a stinger injury he likely suffered in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. With Hemingway ruled out and Folorunso Fatukasi (toe) listed as questionable, Thomas Booker is currently the only healthy defensive end for the Raiders as they head into a divisional bout.

headline: Hemingway (upper body) didn't participate in Las Vegas' practice Wednesday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Hemingway is currently dealing with a stinger, making his status for Sunday's matchup versus Denver uncertain. With Folorunso Fatukasi (toe) also dealing with an injury, the Raiders could find themselves shorthanded along the defensive line against the Broncos, as Thomas Booker is the only healthy defensive end currently on the active roster.

headline: Hemingway (concussion) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Rams.
story: Hemingway was unable to play against the Bills in Week 6 while in the league's concussion protocol. He strung together a DNP-LP-FP practice log during Week 7 prep, and he's cleared protocol after passing tests administered by an independent neurologist. Hemingway's return will bolster the Raiders' defensive line, with Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi reverting to rotational roles.

headline: Hemingway (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bills, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Hemingway was unable to practice all week while in the league's concussion protocol. His next chance to play is Week 7 on Oct. 25 against the Rams, but Hemingway would have to return to practice in at least a limited capacity to indicate that he's progressing through protocol. Thomas Booker and Folorunso Fatukasi are both in line for more defensive snaps in Hemingway's absence.

headline: Hemingway is in concussion protocol ahead of Week 6 versus Buffalo, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Hemingway exited Sunday's 45-17 loss to the Patriots in the first half with what was initial described as a neck injury. The defensive lineman is dealing with a concussion in addition to the potential neck injury, and his status for Week 6 is now uncertain. Hemingway will have three chances to return to practice and clear concussion protocol prior to the team's upcoming matchup with the Bills.

headline: Hemingway (neck) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Hemingway's neck injury is significant enough that the Raiders will not allow the defensive tackle to return to the field during Sunday's contest. Folorunso Fatukasi and Thomas Booker will need to continue to fill in at defensive tackle against the Patriots.

headline: Hemingway (neck) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Hemingway exited the first half of Sunday's game with a neck injury. Folorunso Fatukasi and Thomas Booker will likely share reps at defensive tackle in Hemingway's absence.

headline: Pegues (forearm) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Pegues exited the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Broncos late in the fourth quarter and did not return to the contest. The defensive tackle's full participation and injury clearance in the first prep session of Week 12 imply Pegues did not return to the Week 11 loss because he exited late, when the game was out of reach.

headline: Pegues is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Broncos due to a forearm injury.
story: Pegues managed to log one tackle across 30 defensive snaps before exiting late in the fourth quarter. He's the third defensive lineman for the Raiders to be injured against Denver.

headline: Bowers (ankle) will be listed as questionable for Sunday night's game against the Browns, Adam Hill of the Las Vegas Review-Journal reports.
story: Per Sam Warren of The Athletic, Bowers didn't practice Friday after being limited the previous two days. It's unclear if the star TE's 'DNP' to close the week was maintenance or setback related, but the Raiders' late kickoff presents an issue for those considering Bowers in Week 12 fantasy lineups. As one of the marquee names carrying a 'questionable' tag into the weekend, look for added context regarding his status to arrive no later than Saturday night or Sunday morning via the usual notable NFL insiders.

headline: Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) wasn't on the field for the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Bowers kicked off Week 12 prep with limited listings on the Raiders' first two injury reports, and while he may join his teammates on the practice field at some point Friday, there's now a chance he's a non-participant. He's fighting through ankle and quadriceps injuries that sidelined him this past Sunday at Denver, and Friday's practice report will reveal his activity level and also his odds to suit up Sunday in Cleveland.

headline: Bowers (ankle) remained a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: The star tight end, who was inactive this past Sunday against the Broncos, now has strung together four straight limited practices, which bodes well for his chances of being back for this weekend's game against the Browns. Friday's final injury report will determine whether Bowers carries an injury designation for the contest or is fully cleared for Week 12 action.

headline: Bowers (ankle) was on the field for Thursday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Bowers, who was inactive versus Denver in Week 11, logged his third straight limited practice Wednesday, which offers hope that the star TE will be available this weekend against the Browns. Per McFadden, Bowers' right ankle was heavily wrapped up Thursday, which wasn't the case the day before. The Raiders' upcoming injury report will clarify his official participation level in Wednesday' session, in any case.

headline: Head coach Klint Kubiak said that Bowers (ankle) remained a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, but the Raiders are optimistic that the tight end will play Sunday against the Browns, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Bowers was sidelined for this past Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos, but he's now practiced in a limited fashion in each of the Raiders' last three sessions. Though the Raiders have a bye looming in Week 13 that would give Bowers more time to recover from his lower-body injuries, Kubiak indicated that the break in the schedule won't be a factor in Bowers' status for this Sunday's matchup with the Browns, per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com. Still, Bowers may need to advance to full practice participation by Friday in order to gain clearance for the Week 12 game.

headline: Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) was on the field for Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Before sitting out this past Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos, Bowers was a limited participant for the Raiders' final two practices of Week 11. Though it's unclear if Bowers will be upgraded to full participation for the team's first practice of Week 12, McFadden notes that the tight end didn't have any wrapping or tape on his ankle, which seemingly indicates improvement with his condition. Assuming Bowers steers clear of setbacks and is able to practice in some capacity throughout the week, he should have a good shot at returning to action this Sunday at Cleveland.

headline: Raiders coach Klink Kubiak said after Sunday's 38-24 loss to the Broncos that he's optimistic Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) will be available to face the Browns on Nov. 29, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Bowers "was not ready to play" against Denver, per Kubiak, but the head coach believes Vegas' star tight end could be ready to return in Week 12 against the Browns on SNF. Bowers was held to 18 yards by the Seahawks during Fernando Mendoza's first regular-season start in Week 10 after mustering at least 70 receiving yards in each of his seven games with Kirk Cousins.

headline: Bowers (ankle/quad) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: Adam Schefter of ESPN previously reported on Sunday NFL Countdown that there was "not a lot of optimism" that Bowers (who was in and out of last Sunday's loss to the Seahawks before exiting for good after halftime due to an ankle injury) would be available versus Denver. Now that he's been made inactive, Bowers -- who was limited at practice Thursday and Friday -- will target a potential Nov. 29 return, while fellow TE Michael Mayer is poised to step into a key role in the Raiders passing offense Sunday in his notable absence.

headline: Adam Schefter of ESPN reported on Sunday NFL Countdown that "there is not a lot of optimism" that Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) will suit up Sunday at Denver, but the tight end is "pushing to play."
story: Bowers was in and out of last Sunday's loss to the Seahawks before exiting for good after halftime due to an ankle injury. Head coach Klint Kubiak labeled Bowers day-to-day last Monday, and he then missed Wednesday's practice before being limited Thursday and Friday and entering the weekend listed as questionable. It appears Bowers' availability will be subject to a pregame warmup, after which his status will be clarified about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. Fellow TE Michael Mayer will get a boost in standing if Bowers is inhibited or sidelined.

headline: Bowers (ankle) said Friday that his availability for Sunday's game against the Broncos remains up in the air, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: "We still have some conversations to have, so we'll see," Bowers said. With the tight end already slated to carry a questionable tag into the weekend, his own comments don't provide added clarity about whether he'll suit up Sunday. The Raiders may wait until closer to the 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff before making a final call on Bowers' status. Jack Bech was the big winner in terms of playing time and targets after Bowers left last Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

headline: Coach Klint Kubiak said Friday that Bowers (ankle) is slated to be listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Bowers, who was limited at Thursday's practice, was back on the field Friday, but the tight end nonetheless will head into the weekend with a questionable designation. Look for added intel regarding his Week 11 status to arrive late Saturday or early Sunday via the usual assortment of NFL insiders, but if Bowers is limited or ends up out for his team's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff, fellow TE Michael Mayer will merit fantasy lineup consideration while facing 7-2 Denver.

headline: Bowers (ankle) was present for Friday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: After not practicing Wednesday, Bowers logged a limited session Thursday, and the tight end's presence on the field again Friday offers hope that he'll be able to give it a go Sunday against the Broncos. Per Warren, Bowers sported a wrap on his injured right ankle Friday, with his official participation level and game status set to arrive once the Raiders' Week 11 injury report comes out later in the day.

headline: Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Bowers missed Wednesday's practice, but his return a day later, albeit in a limited fashion, is a positive sign as Sunday's game against the Broncos approaches. Head coach Klint Kubiak noted Wednesday that the star tight end doesn't need to practice this week in order to play this weekend, per Sam Warren of The Athletic, but Bowers already has cleared his first hurdle toward that end by virtue of his participation in Thursday's session.

headline: Bowers (ankle) was on the field for the start of Thursday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: After Bowers was a non-participant in Wednesday's session, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak reiterated that the tight end was still being viewed as day-to-day while working through the ankle injury he sustained in a Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. Kubiak added that Bowers didn't necessarily need to practice this week in order to play Sunday in Denver, but Bowers' return to the field Thursday offers some reassurance about his chances of suiting up against the Broncos. The Raiders will reveal the extent of Bowers' practice participation when they post their second Week 11 injury report later Thursday.

headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said Wednesday that Bowers (ankle) doesn't need to practice this week to play Sunday against the Broncos, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. "If he's ready to go, we'll get him out there," Kubiak said.
story: Kubiak added that Bowers -- who was a non-participant in Wednesday's session -- is progressing in his recovery from the ankle injury he sustained in the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. Bowers' ability to practice in any fashion Thursday and/or Friday would assuage some of the concern about his status for Sunday's contest, but even if he fails to get back on the field and carries a questionable tag into the weekend, he looks like he'll still have a shot at playing.

headline: Bowers (ankle) didn't practice Wednesday and is considered day-to-day, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Bowers begins the week as a DNP, but coach Klint Kubiak noted that the star tight end is making progress. He suffered the ankle injury during Sunday's loss to the Seahawks, adding to the litany of lower-body injuries Bowers has battled through this season. It's unclear if he will progress in time to suit up for Sunday's game at the Broncos. If he's out, Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas would be the Raiders' primary tight ends.

headline: Bowers (ankle) wasn't spotted on the field for Wednesday's practice, Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com reports.
story: Bowers will go down as a non-participant in the Raiders' first Week 11 session, after head coach Klint Kubiak deemed the star tight end day-to-day due to the ankle injury he sustained in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks. Though Kubiak suggested that Bowers' injury isn't anything significant, the 23-year-old will still likely need to practice in some fashion Thursday or Friday to have a shot at playing this Sunday in Denver.

headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed Monday that Bowers (ankle) is considered day-to-day after exiting Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. "It's not as bad as we thought, but still a significant injury," Kubiak said.
story: Bowers checked in and out of Sunday's contest as he managed the ankle issue, finishing with two catches for 18 yards on two targets while logging just 11 snaps on offense. Per Ryan McFadden of ESPN.com, Kubiak added that Bowers will continue to be evaluated throughout the week as the Raiders look to determine whether the star tight end will be available for next Sunday's game in Denver. If Bowers is forced to miss his third game of the season, the Raiders would have more targets up for grabs for the likes of tight end Michael Mayer, running back Ashton Jeanty and wideouts Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech.

headline: Bowers, who will undergo additional testing Monday, isn't believed to have suffered a major ankle injury in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Per Rapoport, Bowers is viewed as "more day-to-day" as the Raiders' Week 11 contest against the Broncos approaches. That said, the tight end's practice participation is expected to be affected leading up to next Sunday's game, given that he was in and out the the lineup versus Seattle as he contended with his ankle issue. Bowers ended up playing just 11 snaps on the day and finished with two receptions for 18 yards on two targets.

headline: Bowers (ankle) will be evaluated further Monday, Ryan McFadden of ESPN reports.
story: Bowers was in and out of Sunday's loss to the Seahawks due to an ankle injury before the Raiders eventually ruled him out at the start of the second half. In his minimal work in what was rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza's first career start, Bowers hauled in both of his targets for 18 yards. Monday's testing may provide a firm diagnosis and subsequent prognosis for Bowers.

headline: Bowers (ankle) won't return to Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network and ESPN reports.
story: Bowers had been able to return to the game for a time, but he'll be shut down for the rest of the afternoon, with next Sunday's contest against the Broncos representing his next chance to play. Michael Mayer, Ian Thomas and Carter Runyon are the Raiders' available TE options while Bowers is sidelined.

headline: Bowers headed to the locker room during Sunday's game against the Seahawks due to an ankle issue, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: It remains to be seen if Bowers will re-enter the contest, as he continues to manage his ankle issue Sunday. Prior to his latest exit, the TE had caught both of his targets for 18 yards.

headline: Bowers (ankle) returned to Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Ryan McFadden of ESPN reports.
story: Great news for the Raiders, after Bowers had been listed as questionable to return to the game. Assuming he's able to finish up the contest, it wouldn't surprise to see the tight end's name on next week's injury report, but for now he's working through his ankle issue Sunday.

headline: Bowers (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Paul Gutierrez reports.
story: Bowers had returned to the contest after a brief exit, but now it has been confirmed that the tight end -- who has caught his only target Sunday for six yards -- sustained an ankle injury. In his absence, Michael Mayer will lead the Raiders' TE corps versus Seattle, with Ian Thomas and Carter Runyon in reserve.

headline: Following a brief exit, Bowers (undisclosed) returned to Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Ryan McFadden of ESPN reports.
story: Per Adam Hill of the Las Vegas Review-Journal, Bowers had previously headed to the medical tent after having his leg rolled up on at the end of a play. However, after getting checked out, the Raiders' star TE was able to re-enter the game, which was started by the No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, Fernando Mendoza.

headline: Bowers caught seven of eight targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 loss to the 49ers. He also rushed once for two yards and lost a fumble.
story: Bowers had a 21-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter and came one yard short of scoring again on a 33-yard catch on a fourth-quarter drive that ended with a Kirk Cousins interception in the end zone. The star TE has reached 70 receiving yards in all seven of his appearances this season and is up to six touchdowns. Bowers came five receiving yards shy of his season high and continues to roll, even as the 4-5 Raiders drop out of contention in the AFC. He'll likely face more resistance in Week 10 against the Seahawks, who just held Cardinals TE Trey McBride to 54 yards.

headline: Bowers caught seven of 10 targets for 92 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 38-33 win over the Jets.
story: Bowers scored a 12-yard touchdown in the first quarter and added a two-yard touchdown reception in the third quarter. He came just short of a third touchdown later in the third quarter, getting tackled just outside the goal line to set up a one-yard Kirk Cousins rushing TD. Bowers became the first tight end in NFL history to record at least 70 receiving yards in six consecutive appearances to begin a season. He'll try to extend his historic streak in Week 9 against the 49ers while continuing to work as the top target for Kirk Cousins.

headline: Bowers (calf) was a full practice participant Thursday.
story: Bowers opened Week 8 prep with a limited session Wednesday due to a calf injury, but it didn't deter him from returning to all drills one day later. Since making his season debut in Week 3, he's gone for more than 70 receiving yards in all five of his appearances, sitting on a 34-455-3 line on 52 targets on the campaign.

headline: Bowers (calf) was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Paul Gutierrez of the Raiders' official site reports.
story: Bowers was listed with both hamstring and calf issues on the Raiders' Week 7 injury report, but he appears to have at least put the former injury behind him heading into a Week 8 matchup with the Jets. As long as he's able to make it through the Raiders' next two practices without incident, Bowers will likely head into the weekend without an injury designation.

headline: Bowers secured six of eight targets for 73 yards in the Raiders' 35-21 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
story: The ultra-talented tight end put together another solid performance, finishing second in receptions and receiving yards for the Raiders while also tying for runner-up status in targets. Bowers has at least 70 receiving yards in all five of the games in which he's played, and he's recorded at least six catches in four of those contests. Bowers will undoubtedly remain a critical part of the air attack in a Week 8 road matchup against the Jets next Sunday.

headline: Bowers (hamstring/calf) upgraded to a full practice Thursday, Anthony Galaviz of The Fresno Bee reports.
story: After popping up on the injury report Wednesday as a limited participant with a pair of new "injuries," Bowers was able to get in a full session Thursday and should be ready to roll for Sunday's game with the Rams. The top TE1 play every week, Bowers has 28 grabs for 382 yards and three touchdowns through four appearances.

headline: Bowers (hamstring/calf) was in uniform and warming up ahead of Thursday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: Bowers seems to be trending in the right direction after being added to the injury report with hamstring and calf injuries Wednesday. The Raiders will release their official injury report later Thursday, but it appears Bowers will at least be a limited participant during this session.

headline: Bowers was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to hamstring and calf injuries.
story: Bowers previously missed the first two games of the season while recovering from a meniscus trim, but he's now tending to a pair of new injuries in Week 7. The star tight end's activity will warrant monitoring throughout the week, but he can erase most of the concern about his status heading into Sunday's game against the Rams if he can log a full practice or even another limited practice Thursday.
