headline: Tuipulotu (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: An ankle injury prevented Tuipulotu from practicing all week, yet the Chargers have kept the door open for the fourth-year edge rusher to suit up for Sunday's contest. Akheem Mesidor (ankle) is listed as doubtful, which leaves Khalil Mack, Caleb Murphy and Bud Dupree as the three healthy edge rushers on the Chargers' 53-man roster heading into the weekend.

headline: Tuipulotu (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Tuipulotu appears to have sustained his ankle injury in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. The outside linebacker will need to upgrade his practice participation in Thursday or Friday's session for a chance to suit up for Sunday's contest against the Patriots. If the 24-year-old must miss the game, Akheem Mesidor (ankle) or Caleb Murphy will likely start opposite Khalil Mack.

headline: Tuipulotu recorded six total tackles (three solo), including 0.5 sacks, while intercepting a pass and forcing a fumble during Sunday's 30-23 loss to Seattle.
story: Tuipulotu jumped in front of quarterback Sam Darnold's first pass of the day, notching his first career interception. The linebacker later stripped running back Emanuel Wilson in the third quarter, but Wilson fell on the fumble. Tuipulotu also combined with defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe to sack Darnold in the fourth quarter. The 24-year-old has now compiled 18 total tackles (11 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and added an interception and a forced fumble over four contests this season.

headline: Tuipulotu logged six tackles (five solo), including 1.5 sacks, in the Chargers' 24-16 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
story: Tuipulotu played 82 percent of the Chargers' defensive snaps in Sunday's loss. The outside linebacker sacked Josh Allen once and participated in another sack while the Chargers' defense notched five turnovers in a losing effort. The 24-year-old's 1.5 sacks were his first of the season after he notched a career-high 13.0 over 16 regular-season games in 2025.

headline: Thompson (hamstring) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Patriots, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: Thompson has not played since Week 2 against the Raiders due to a hamstring injury, and it looks like that trend will continue after the rookie fourth-rounder missed all three practices during Week 12 prep. Assuming he doesn't play Sunday, Thompson's next opportunity to play would be Week 13 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Thompson (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Thompson has not played since the Chargers' Week 2 game with the Raiders. The wide receiver initially dealt with a quadriceps injury before sustaining a hamstring injury while still recovering. Thompson's long string of DNPs continues into Week 12 prep, and it appears there may be no end in sight.

headline: Thompson (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Thompson's inactive status doesn't come as much of a surprise, given that he entered the weekend as doubtful due to a hamstring injury. He hasn't played since Week 2 against the Raiders, and his next chance to see the field is Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.

headline: Thompson (hamstring) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Thompson has been sidelined by a hamstring injury and has not seen regular-season action since Week 2 against the Raiders. If he's ruled out for Sunday's game, then the rookie fourth-rounder's next chance to play would be Week 12 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Thompson (hamstring) is inactive for Monday night's game against the Ravens.
story: Thompson will not suit up for Monday's primetime clash after being listed as doubtful following a third consecutive DNP on Saturday, and it's no surprise the fourth-round rookie is unable to play in Monday's game. Derius Davis will take on the role of No. 4 wide receiver in the contest behind starters Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith.

headline: The Chargers list Thompson (hamstring) as doubtful for Monday's game against the Ravens.
story: Though Thompson appears to have moved past the quadriceps injury he sustained Week 2, the Chargers have been listing him with a hamstring issue since returning from their Week 7 bye. The rookie wideout didn't practice in any capacity this week, but he apparently displayed enough progress to avoid being ruled out in advance of Monday's contest. Even so, Thompson isn't expected to play and will likely be included on the Chargers' inactive list, which will be released 90 minutes prior to the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Thompson (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
story: Thompson hasn't played since Week 2 against the Raiders. It appears he will remain on the shelf for Monday's game versus the Ravens unless he shows signs of progress in the next few days.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) is inactive against Houston on Sunday.
story: This doesn't come as a surprise, as Thompson was doubtful heading into the contest after sitting out practice all week. The rookie wideout hasn't logged any game action since Week 2, and it's unclear if he'll be able to return next Monday in Baltimore. Thompson's continued absence will dent the depth of Los Angeles' wideout corps.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) is officially listed as doubtful for Sunday's game versus the Texans.
story: Thompson was not able to practice at all during the week as he continued to nurse quad and hamstring injuries, and it appears likely he'll be absent for his sixth straight game in Week 9. Unless he's able to make a surprise turnaround by Sunday, Derius Davis figures to continue to see a few extra reps at wide receiver.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) is not expected to practice this week, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Thompson recently suffered a setback with his pair of soft-tissue injuries. Another one of OC Mike McDaniel's swings and misses this offseason, Thompson hasn't played since Week 2 and has just one catch for 13 yards on 22 offensive snaps. The fourth-round rookie has been a non-factor.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Rams, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: Thompson didn't play a snap in Week 6 against the Chiefs despite being active for the contest due to a lingering quadriceps injury. He'll be inactive for Sunday's game, so KeAndre Lambert-Smith, Theo Wease and Derius Davis are all candidates for a bump in offensive snaps. Thompson's next chance to play is Week 9 against the Texans on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
story: It was a second consecutive DNP for Thompson, who has been battling multiple injuries for weeks. The 23-year-old was cleared to play in Week 6 versus the Chiefs after missing the three previous games, though he didn't play. It appears Thompson may not be available for the Week 8 meeting with the Rams, especially if he doesn't practice Friday.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps/hamstring) did not participate at practice Wednesday.
story: Thompson was active in Week 6 during the Chargers' last game before their bye, but he ended up not playing any snaps, presumably due to the quad injury that kept him out for the prior three contests. Now his availability for Week 8 is in doubt, and he'll probably have to return to practice Thursday or Friday to have any chance to play Sunday against the Rams.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) was active but didn't play any snaps Sunday in the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
story: After sitting out the Chargers' previous three games due to the quad issue, Thompson was listed as questionable heading into Sunday's contest after three limited practices. Though he got the green light to suit up, Thompson was presumably available only in an emergency since the Chargers' seven-man inactive list consisted of players who were dealing with more significant injuries. Thompson will have added time to get healthy while the Chargers are on bye Week 7, and if he can fully practice at some point during Week 8, he'll have a good chance at seeing his first game action since Week 2 in the team's Nov. 1 matchup with the Rams.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) is active for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Though Thompson is suiting up for the first time since Week 2, it's unclear how extensively he'll be able to play Sunday. The Chargers have a full list of injured players on their seven-man inactive list, so it's conceivable that much like Ladd McConkey a week ago in the team's loss to the Broncos, Thompson could be available only as an emergency option after he was limited in practices Wednesday through Friday. During the Chargers' first two games of the season, Thompson handled a light role on offense, playing just 22 total snaps while recording one reception for 13 yards on three targets.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Thompson earned the questionable tag for Week 6 after logging three consecutive limited practices, giving the rookie fourth-rounder a chance to return from a three-game absence. If he's cleared to play, then Thompson could operate in an elevated role offensively since Tre' Harris (hamstring) has been ruled out.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Thompson has appeared in just two games for the Chargers this season. He practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday and Thursday, though he has some hurdles to clear before getting the green light to play Sunday versus the Chiefs.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Thompson has returned to limited practice after logging consecutive DNPs in the lead-up to the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. The wide receiver did not participate in the contest, and the weekend of rest appears to have boosted his recovery process. Thompson will likely need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's session to dodge an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: Thompson opened Week 5 prep with a limited practice Wednesday, but he followed that up with back-to-back DNPs and will miss a third consecutive game due to a quadriceps injury. Quentin Johnston (chest) has also been ruled out, and with Ladd McConkey (foot) listed as questionable, the Chargers will lean more heavily on Tre' Harris, Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Derius Davis at wide receiver.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) did not participate at the Chargers' practice Thursday.
story: Thompson returned to practice Wednesday for the first time in multiple weeks, logging a limited session. The wide receiver has now taken a step back in his participation, failing to practice Thursday. Thompson expressed some doubt about his availability for Week 5 when he spoke with the media Wednesday, and he appears to be in danger of missing another contest while recovering from a quadriceps injury.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Wednesday's practice was Thompson's first since Week 2 prep, with the rookie fourth-rounder missing the Chargers' last two games due to a quadriceps injury. However, he told reporters after Wednesday's session that he's unsure whether he'll be cleared to return for Sunday's AFC West showdown against the Broncos, per Kris Rhim of ESPN.com. A full practice over the next two days would put Thompson on track to play in Week 6, and his return would be a welcome one for the Chargers, given that top wideout Ladd McConkey is considered week-to-week due to a foot injury.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: Thompson will miss a second consecutive game while working through a quadriceps injury. He was unable to practice during Week 4 prep, so a limited session ahead of Week 5 against the Broncos would indicate that the rookie fourth-rounder is progressing in his recovery. Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Derius Davis will both work in rotational roles behind Ladd McConkey (foot), Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris in Thompson's absence.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Thompson is dealing with a quad injury that already sidelined him for this past Sunday's loss to Buffalo. He's begun Week 4 prep with consecutive DNPs, so his chance of suiting up Sunday versus Seattle is looking quite grim. Prior to getting hurt, Thompson recorded one catch on three targets for 13 yards over his first two games.

headline: Thompson (quadriceps) did not practice Wednesday, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Thompson didn't practice last week and missed Sunday's loss against the Bills. With the rookie sidelined last week, Marquez Valdes-Scantling played three offensive snaps as the lightly-used fourth receiver behind Ladd McConkey, Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris.

headline: Still (ankle) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus the Patriots, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: Still did not practice at all during the week after sitting out the Chargers' contest versus the Jets in Week 11 with an ankle injury, but there's apparently still a chance he'll be able to play in Week 12. Otherwise, Isas Waxter might be in line to see an increased snap count at cornerback Sunday.

headline: Still (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Still did not play in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets due to an ankle injury he sustained in Friday's practice. The cornerback remains sidelined with the issue, leaving Deane Leonard and Genesis Smith as the early options at slot cornerback for Sunday's game against the Patriots.

headline: Still is inactive for Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Jets due to an ankle injury.
story: Still wasn't on the Chargers' practice report until Friday, when he was a limited participant due to an ankle injury. Though he was initially deemed questionable, the third-year cornerback isn't going to be able to suit up against New York. Still's next chance to play will be in Week 12 against New England on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Still (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Still was added to Friday's practice report as a limited participant due to an ankle injury. His late addition to the injury report isn't a great sign ahead of Sunday's game, and if he's unable to play, then Deane Leonard and Genesis Smith would both be in line for more snaps in the Chargers' secondary.

headline: Mesidor (ankle) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game versus the Patriots, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: Mesidor was not able to practice at all during the week because of an ankle injury he sustained in Week 11 versus the Jets, and it looks like he might be trending towards missing his first game of the season in Week 12. If he can't go Sunday, it could mean an uptick in reps on the edge for Caleb Murphy.

headline: Mesidor (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: The rookie first-rounder is working through an ankle injury that he picked up during the first half of the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets in Week 12. Mesidor has two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's contest against the Patriots.

headline: Mesidor (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Jets.
story: Mesidor suffered an ankle injury during the first half, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. In the rookie's absence, Caleb Murphy and Bud Dupree are both candidates to see an increase in opportunities at outside linebacker behind starters Tuli Tuipulotu and Khalil Mack.

headline: Henley (knee) is listed as out for Sunday's game versus New England, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: Henley will spend a second straight game on the sidelines due to a knee injury in Week 12. In his absence, veteran Troy Dye could get a start at linebacker next to fellow veteran Del'Shawn Phillips on Sunday.

headline: Henley (knee) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Henley did not play in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets due to his knee injury. The linebacker has not practiced since sustaining the injury after Week 10. If Henley cannot suit up for Sunday's game, Marlowe Wax and Troy Dye will likely see increased snap shares at inside linebacker next to Del'Shawn Phillips.

headline: Henley (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Henley was unable to practice all week, and head coach Jim Harbaugh said Friday that the fourth-year linebacker has been working through knee soreness since Monday's win against the Ravens, per Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com. Denzel Perryman and Marlowe Wax figure to be the top candidates to start at inside linebacker alongside Del'Shawn Phillips in the absence of Henley, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Patriots on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Henley (knee) didn't participate in the Chargers' practice Wednesday.
story: Henley popped up on the injury report Wednesday after compiling 11 tackles (five solo) during the Week 10 win over the Ravens. Marlowe Wax would be in line to start at inside linebacker during Sunday's matchup versus the Jets if Henley ends up being unable to play.

headline: Henley remains with the Chargers, as the Broncos have backed out of trading for the linebacker, Jeff Legwold of ESPN.com reports.
story: A trade involving Henley was agreed to Tuesday pending a physical, but the Broncos apparently found a red flag concerning his knee during that physical. Denver offered an updated trade to the Chargers with different draft compensation than the originally agreed upon 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 fifth-round pick, but the two sides were unable to agree on an updated framework, so Henley will ultimately remain with the Chargers. Henley has not missed a game this season, so the concern Denver discovered on his physical isn't expected to impact his availability for Monday's game against the Ravens.

headline: The Broncos acquired Henley from the Chargers on Tuesday in exchange for a 2027 fourth-round pick and a 2028 fifth-round pick, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Though Denver will surrender a pair of mid-round picks to bring him aboard, Henley is viewed merely as a depth piece at middle linebacker behind established starters Alex Singleton and Justin Strnad, per Zac Stevens of TheDNVR.com. A full-time player for the Chargers over the past two-plus seasons, Henley had recorded 51 tackles (21 solo), 0.5 sacks, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveries, one forced fumble and one interception through eight games in 2026.

headline: Henley (shoulder) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Henley was dinged up in Sunday's loss to the Rams but was able to return to the contest, and it appears he'll all set for the Week 9 tilt against the Texans. Henley has posted 41 tackles (17 solo), including 0.5 sacks, two fumble recoveries, a forced fumble and one pass breakup across seven starts this season.

headline: Henley (shoulder) was a limited participant in the Chargers' practice Wednesday.
story: Henley is still battling the shoulder injury that briefly sidelined him during the Week 8 loss to the Rams. Marlowe Wax and Troy Dye would likely see increased playing time if Henley ends up being unable to play in Sunday's matchup against the Texans.

headline: Henley (shoulder) has returned to Sunday's matchup versus the Rams, David Droegemeier of Locked On Chargers reports.
story: Henley was briefly sidelined with a shoulder injury early in the first half, but he was able to return to the field before the break. The 26-year-old is back in his starting role at inside linebacker against the Rams.

headline: Henley (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Rams, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Henley suffered a shoulder injury early in the second half, and his availability for the rest of the game is now up in the air. In his absence, Troy Dye and Marlowe Wax will stand to see an increase in workload at inside linebacker.

headline: Henley (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Henley was listed as questionable for Sunday's game due to a knee injury. The linebacker was limited in practice all week due to the injury but has recovered enough to suit up for the Chargers' Sunday divisional contest against the Chiefs.

headline: Henley (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Henley was a limited practice participant all week due to a knee injury, which he likely picked up during the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. Troy Dye would likely start alongside Del'Shawn Phillips at inside linebacker if Henley is not cleared to play against Kansas City.

headline: Uiagalelei will be the Chargers' starting quarterback against the Patriots on Sunday due to the absence of Justin Herbert (concussion), Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Uiagalelei got his first taste of NFL regular-season action in Week 11 against the Jets after Herbert suffered a concussion, with the former completing two of seven passes for 27 yards and a touchdown. With Herbert in the league's protocol for head injuries, Uiagalelei will make his first career start Sunday against a New England defense that ranks 27th in the NFL in passing yards allowed per game (239.0). Jake Browning also is available to serve as Los Angeles' backup.

headline: Uiagalelei completed two of seven passes for 27 yards and a touchdown after replacing Justin Herbert (finger) in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, and head coach Jim Harbaugh said after the game that Herbert could have a fractured finger, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Uiagalelei was inaccurate in his first taste of regular-season NFL action but threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Derius Davis. If Herbert isn't available to face the Ravens on MNF in Week 10 and Trey Lance (groin) isn't ready to return from injured reserve, Uiagalelei would presumably be tabbed for the first regular-season start of the latter's career.

headline: Uiagalelei (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game versus Seattle, though he is listed as the team's emergency quarterback.
story: Trey Lance (groin) is available to suit up in Week 4, meaning Uiagalelei will be a healthy scratch. However, if Lance and Justin Herbert exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection, Uiagalelei will serve as the team's emergency signal-caller.

headline: Herbert (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: At 1-9, the Chargers have zero incentive to rush Herbert back to the field at this stage. His next chance to see game action thus is slated to arrive Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Buccaneers. In Herbet's absence this weekend, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network relays that DJ Uiagalelei is slated to start at QB for the Chargers, with Jake Browning available to back him up.

headline: Herbert (concussion) wasn't present for the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: After Herbert missed practice Thursday and again wasn't spotted Friday, his status for Sunday's game against the Patriots appears to be trending in the wrong direction. If the Chargers' starting quarterback doesn't clear concussion protocol in time, DJ Uiagalelei would be in line to make the first regular-season start of the latter's NFL career against a Patriots team that's set to start backup QB Tommy DeVito.

headline: Herbert (concussion) was officially deemed a non-participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Herbert, who landed in the NFL's concussion protocol in the wake of this past Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets, didn't practice Wednesday, either. He thus is looking iffy, at best, for this weekend's game against the Patriots, especially given the Chargers' 1-9 record. If Herbert is inactive versus New England, DJ Uiagalelei would be in line to start at QB in his place, with Jake Browning available to back him up.

headline: Herbert (concussion) didn't participate during the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Herbert was placed in the concussion protocol following this past Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets, and a likely DNP on Thursday after not practicing Wednesday may put him on the outside looking in to gaining clearance ahead of Week 12 action. If Herbert doesn't suit up Sunday against the Patriots, DJ Uiagalelei is in line to start for the Chargers, with Jake Browning backing him up.

headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said that Herbert (concussion) won't practice Wednesday, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Herbert entered the NFL's concussion protocol following this past Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets, and the QB's pending absence from Wednesday's session gives him two more chances to officially log practice reps before for this weekend's game against New England. In his current absence, DJ Uiagalelei is next up for Los Angeles' signal-caller reps, with practice squad member Jake Browning available for a Week 12 elevation, if needed.

headline: Herbert entered the concussion protocol after Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Herbert completed 15 of 21 passes for 131 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions in Week 11, but he also endured six sacks, fumbled once and added 32 yards and one TD on his eight carries. It's unclear exactly when he picked up the head injury, but he'll be subject to the concussion protocol ahead of further game action. The Chargers take the field next Sunday against the Patriots.

headline: Herbert completed 12 of 18 passes for 129 yards with no touchdowns or interceptions and rushed seven times for 51 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
story: Herbert ironically compiled his second-fewest passing yards of the season in the Chargers' first victory, but the talented signal-caller leaned heavily on both his legs and an effective rushing performance from Omarion Hampton. Herbert made a significant contribution himself to cap off Los Angeles' opening drive of the game, taking off when he couldn't find anyone open and recording a 22-yard rushing touchdown for the first points of the night. The game also marked Herbert's first interception-free performance of the season and gives the beleaguered Chargers' air attack something to hang its collective hat on heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

headline: Herbert (finger) doesn't appear on the the Chargers' injury report ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.
story: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh previously noted that the QB "should be good to go" for Week 10 action after imaging on Herbert's injured left middle finger came back negative for a fracture, per ESPN.com. The fact that Herbert isn't listed in any way on the team's first injury report this week aligns with that and paves the way for him to continue to helm the offense for 0-8 Los Angeles versus Baltimore.

headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said that Herbert "should be good to go" for Monday's game at Baltimore after imaging on the quarterback's injured left middle finger returned negative for a fracture, ESPN.com reports.
story: Herbert may still have to manage some discomfort in the finger during Monday's contest, but since the injury to his non-throwing hand, he shouldn't be too affected while throwing or handing the ball off. That being said, Herbert has become increasingly difficult to justify including in fantasy lineups even when he's been in more optimal health entering games. Heading into the matchup with the Ravens, Herbert has completed a career-low 61.3 percent of his passes for 6.8 yards per attempt and just six touchdowns in eight games. He's tied with New England's Drake Maye for the league lead in interceptions thrown (11) and ranks second behind Cleveland's Deshaun Watson in sacks taken (31).

headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh relayed Monday that Herbert (finger) avoided a fracture in his left middle finger,  Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Herbert sustained the injury in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, but the QB's imaging came back "negative," per Harbaugh. That said, Herbert's status is nonetheless worth monitoring as next Monday's contest against the Ravens approaches. If Herbert's practice participation ends up being impacted in the coming days, DJ Uiagalelei would be be next in line for added QB reps.

headline: Herbert sustained a left middle finger injury in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Coach Jim Harbaugh said after the latest loss that Herbert "could" have a fracture. The quarterback was pulled from the game with the score out of hand in the fourth quarter, but Herbert apparently lobbied to stay in the contest. He'll have an extra day to heal up ahead of next Monday night's date with the Ravens. Herbert has been well off the fantasy radar for much of the season in this broken Los Angeles offense. If he can't face Baltimore, DJ Uiagalelei would likely get the nod under center. He completed two of seven passes for 24 yards and a touchdown in relief of Herbert on Sunday.

headline: Herbert completed 24 of 32 passes for 257 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions while rushing four times for 15 yards in the Chargers' 24-9 loss to the Rams on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that remained with the Chargers.
story: The Chargers declined to move on from offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel during the Week 7 bye, and Herbert did finish with a season-high passing yardage total on a season-best 75.0 percent completion rate. However, Herbert failed to throw a touchdown pass for the second straight game while tossing multiple interceptions for the third time this season. Herbert still has just a 61.8 percent completion rate -- a career low by a fairly wide margin -- and a 5:10 TD:INT through seven games as the winless Bolts try again for their first victory in a Week 9 home matchup against the Texans next Sunday.

headline: Herbert completed 22 of 37 passes for 204 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs. He also rushed five times for 26 yards.
story: Herbert continued to struggle but once again got little help from his teammates. Top wide receiver Ladd McConkey (concussion) exited early, and the Chargers couldn't generate much on the ground, as Herbert led the team in rushing yards. Herbert was held without a touchdown for the first time this season after throwing exactly one touchdown pass in each of the previous five games. The 0-6 Chargers are the first team to six losses this season, as the Titans notched their first win of the season over the Colts on Sunday to improve to 1-5, while the winless Dolphins were on bye. Herbert will be on bye in Week 7 before his next opportunity to snap this season-opening losing streak in a nominal road game against the Rams in Week 8.

headline: Herbert completed 14 of 24 passes for 121 yards, one touchdown and one interception, reeled off 54 yards on six carries and fumbled twice (one lost) during Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos.
story: Herbert's season-low number of pass attempts amounted to by far his lowest yardage total through the air through five contests this season. He also turned over the ball two times, which resulted in two late made field goals for Denver (matching the margin of defeat) and bringing his total on the campaign to nine (seven INTs, two lost fumbles). Granted, Herbert was working without WR Quentin Johnston (chest, inactive), while Ladd McConkey (foot) was active but doesn't appear to have played a snap, so the deck was stacked against him versus a tough defense. Herbert's next chance to get right is next Sunday versus the 4-0 Chiefs.

headline: Njoku (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against New England.
story: Njoku was held out of practice both Wednesday and Thursday due to a shoulder injury that he sustained during the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. He was cleared to return to practice in a limited capacity Friday, which was enough for the veteran tight end to draw the questionable tag for Sunday's contest. Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will maintain expanded roles on offense in the event that Njoku doesn't play, and Patrick Herbert would be a candidate for elevation from the practice squad to give the Chargers more depth at tight end. That said, the Chargers' offensive potential figures to be limited in Week 12 in the absence of Justin Herbert (concussion), with DJ Uiagalelei set to make his first career start.

headline: Njoku (shoulder) was listed as a non-participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Njoku also was deemed a 'DNP' on Wednesday, so the tight end presumably will need to practice Friday, in some capacity, in order to avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Patriots. If Njoku ends up sidelined this weekend, Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will be in line to lead the Chargers' Week 12 TE corps.

headline: Njoku (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
story: The veteran tight end injured his shoulder in last Sunday's loss to the Jets but was able to return to the contest, finishing with two catches for 21 yards on four targets on 41.7 percent of the offensive snaps. It's possible Wednesday was a maintenance day.

headline: Njoku caught two of four passes for 28 yards during the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets on Sunday.
story: Njoku briefly left Sunday's contest after injuring his shoulder at the end of a 13-yard catch in the first quarter. The veteran tight end was cleared to return, and he ended up finishing second on the Chargers in targets behind Ladd McConkey (eight) on a day in which Justin Herbert completed 15 of 21 passes for 131 yards and two touchdowns. Njoku and the Chargers stay home for Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.

headline: Njoku (shoulder) has returned to Sunday's Week 11 matchup against the Jets, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Njoku briefly exited in the first quarter after hurting his shoulder on a 13-yard catch. He was initially deemed questionable to return but has since re-entered the contest. The veteran tight end is playing just his second game after returning from a stint on IR due to a fibula injury.

headline: Njoku (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Njoku appeared to injure his shoulder while being taken down on the tail end of his 13-yard catch early in the first quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. Oronde Gadsden should see a bump in offensive snaps for as long as Njoku is sidelined.

headline: Njoku played 19 offensive snaps but didn't get a target during Monday's 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
story: Njoku's snap count was predictably capped as he returned from a six-game absence due to a fibula injury that he sustained in Week 2 against the Raiders. His 19 offensive snaps were actually ahead of Oronde Gadsden (12), with Charlie Kolar leading all Chargers tight ends with 41 snaps on offense. With another week under his belt to get back up to speed, Njoku could be more involved in the Chargers' passing attack in Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

headline: Njoku (fibula) officially is listed as active for Monday night's game against the Ravens, Omar Navarro of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: Since being designated for return from IR on Nov. 4, Njoku -- who last played in Week 2 -- logged five consecutive limited practice listings before upgrading to full participation Saturday and being deemed questionable for Monday's contest. With his return to the lineup now confirmed, Njoku will bolster a TE corps that also includes Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden. In his only full game with the team this season, Njoku caught all five of his targets for 58 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Cardinals. Now that he's back in the mix, the 2017 first-rounder has an opportunity to reclaim enough of a role in the 0-8 Chargers offense to merit fantasy lineup consideration at his position in deeper fantasy formats going forward.

headline: The Chargers activated Njoku (fibula) from injured reserve ahead of Monday's game against the Ravens.
story: After completing his second week of practice upon being designated for return from IR on Nov. 4, Njoku had been listed as questionable heading into Monday. The Chargers ultimately came away encouraged enough by how Njoku looked during the week of practice to activate him, giving the team a third option at tight end for Monday's game. Due to his blocking prowess, Charlie Kolar likely will lead the position group in snaps Monday, but Njoku could usurp Oronde Gadsden as the Chargers' top pass-catching tight end as he takes the field for the first time since Week 2.

headline: Njoku (fibula) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Ravens.
story: Njoku continues to progress in his recovery from fibula injury that landed him on injured reserve in late September. The veteran tight end turned eight targets into six catches for 67 yards across the first two games of the regular season prior to his injury, and his return would result in a reduced offensive workload for Oronde Gadsden.

headline: Njoku (fibula), who is still on IR, was limited in practice Friday.
story: Njoku's 21-day practice window was opened Nov. 4, so the Chargers still have plenty of time to activate him. The veteran wideout was limited in all three practices last week and has been limited again Thursday and Friday of this week, so he may need to log a full session Saturday to get the all-clear to suit up Monday in Baltimore. Njoku could provide a boost to a struggling Chargers offense whenever he does return -- in his lone full game of the season so far (Week 1 against Arizona), he caught all five of his targets for 58 yards.

headline: Njoku (fibula) was a limited participant at the Chargers' practice Thursday.
story: Njoku remained limited at the team's first practice of the week as he continues to work his way back from a fibula injury that has sidelined him since Week 2. The tight end was a limited participant at the team's three practices last week, and he'll have two more chances to log a full practice prior to Monday night's matchup with the Ravens.

headline: Njoku (fibula) wasn't activated from IR-designated to return ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans, per the NFL's official transaction log.
story: Njoku returned to practice this week but was limited all three days before being deemed doubtful for Week 9 action. The TE's next chance to play will arrive Monday, Nov. 16, when the Chargers face the Ravens.

headline: Njoku (fibula) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Texans.
story: Njoku returned to practice this week but never advanced from limited participation to full. He could have a real shot next week when the Chargers face the Ravens. In the meantime, Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will get most of the TE snaps for Los Angeles.

headline: Njoku (fibula) was limited in Thursday's practice.
story: Njoku had his 21-day practice window opener Wednesday, and he's logged back-to-back limited practice sessions to begin Week 9 work. He's been on the shelf since going down with the lower leg injury in Week 2.

headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Njoku (fibula) has been designated for return from injured reserve, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: The transaction opens up a 21-day window wherein Njoku can be evaluated for a return to the 53-man roster. The veteran tight end has been out of action since sustaining the fibula injury Week 2, but if he's able to turn in a full practice at some point over the next three days, he could have a chance at being activated from IR ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans. Once he's back in the fold, Njoku could push Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden for snaps at tight end.

headline: Coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that the Chargers likely will open the 21-day window for Njoku (fibula) this week, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Njoku landed on IR after sustaining a fibula injury in Week 2, but the tight end's looming return to practice should provide a nice boost to a Chargers' TE corps that also includes Oronde Gadsden and Charlie Kolar. In his only full game with the team (Week 1 versus the Cardinals), Njoku recorded a 55 percent snap share en route to catching all five of his targets for 58 yards. If he can approach that level of production once he's back in the lineup, Njoku could resurface as a fantasy option as the season rolls along.

headline: Mitchell (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Mitchell tweaked his knee during the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets in Week 11. The injury prevented the fourth-year pro from practicing all week, and his absence for Sunday's contest means Kimani Vidal should operate in an expanded role in the backfield behind RB1 Omarion Hampton. Mitchell's next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Buccaneers on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Mitchell (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
story: The running back was injured in last Sunday's loss to the Jets. If Mitchell needs to miss time, it would likely turn this frustrating three-way committee backfield into a more traditional two-man affair, with Omarion Hampton handling early-down work and Kimani Vidal spelling him in passing situations.

headline: Mitchell (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Jets.
story: Mitchell was briefly sidelined with a back injury in the first half before returning to action. The running back is now dealing with an apparent knee issue, placing some doubt on his chances to return to the field Sunday. In his absence, Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal will handle the bulk of the workload in the backfield.

headline: Mitchell (back) has re-entered Sunday's game against the Jets, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Mitchell temporarily exited the contest in the first half due to a back issue. However, he's since returned to the game as part of the kickoff-return unit. Mitchell is thus set to resume his usual role as both a backup RB and special-teams ace.

headline: Mitchell was forced out of Sunday's game against the Jets with a back injury.
story: Prior to that, Mitchell caught his only target for six yards. While he's sidelined Sunday, Kimani Vidal is next in line for the Chargers' carries behind Omarion Hampton.

headline: Mitchell turned three carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned two kickoffs for 30 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
story: One of Mitchell's carries went for 11 yards, but his other two rushes went for minus-five and minus-two yards, and all of those touches came on the same drive in the second quarter. His 13 offensive snaps were third-most among Chargers running backs behind Kimani Vidal (15) and Omarion Hampton (36), and it was Hampton that commanded the majority of backfield touches, finishing with 22 carries for 105 yards and a touchdown. Mitchell has logged four carries or fewer in three of his last four outings, and he'll continue to operate in a rotational role on offense heading into the Chargers' Week 11 home tilt against the Jets on Sunday.

headline: Mitchell (hip) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Ravens.
story: Mitchell's practice reps were limited by a hip injury, but he's been officially cleared to play Monday against the team he spent three seasons with from 2023 to 2025. He turned 10 touches into 67 yards during the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, and Mitchell will continue to operate in a rotational role in the backfield alongside Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal.

headline: Mitchell (hip) remained limited at practice Friday.
story: It's a new injury for Mitchell, who also was limited Thursday when the Chargers filed their first practice report for the upcoming Monday night game at Baltimore. He'll have some extra motivation, facing his former team in primetime as his current team seeks its first win of the season.

headline: Mitchell (hip) was limited at practice Thursday.
story: In this past Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans, Mitchell carried seven times for 33 yards and caught three of his four targets for 34 yards while losing a fumble. The 24-year-old currently is operating in a backfield timeshare with Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal in his first campaign with the Chargers, and Mitchell now has two more chances to upgrade his practice participation level ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.

headline: Mitchell rushed seven times for 33 yards and caught three of four targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He also lost a fumble.
story: Mitchell led LA's three-man backfield rotation with 67 scrimmage yards, while Omarion Hampton had 60 and Kimani Vidal contributed 36. Mitchell's fumble came late in the third quarter, with the Chargers already trailing 31-9 at the time. The winless Chargers are averaging a league-low 15.1 points per game heading into a Week 10 trip to Baltimore, and things could get even worse if QB Justin Herbert (finger) has to miss time after getting injured in the fourth quarter.

headline: Mitchell rushed four times for six yards and caught all three of his targets for 17 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
story: Handpicked by first-year OC Mike McDaniel as a free-agent signing in the offseason, Mitchell has been a total non-factor for much of the first half of the season. With a career 5.7 yards per carry average, Mitchell is averaging just 3.7 yards per rush this season. Involved in a three-way backfield committee with Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal, Mitchell is waiver-wire fodder in normal-sized 12-team fantasy leagues.

headline: Mitchell turned two carries into four yards, failed to haul in his lone target and returned four kickoffs for 87 yards during Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Week 6 was the lowest usage Mitchell has seen this season, and his 17 snaps on offense were third most among Chargers running backs behind Omarion Hampton (34) and Kimani Vidal (25). Through six regular-season games, Mitchell has turned 35 carries into 139 yards and added 12 catches (on 15 targets) for 52 yards and a score, but it's hard to put much trust into any of the Chargers' skill-position players given the team's poor start to the season. Perhaps the Week 7 bye will help the Chargers right the ship, with their next game taking place in Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Mitchell took six carries for 11 yards and caught three of four targets for 18 yards during Sunday's 23-17 loss versus the Broncos.
story: From scrimmage, Sunday was Mitchell's least productive game since Week 1, when he played just 17 offensive snaps. His nine touches in Week 5 tied with 2024 sixth-rounder Kimani Vidal, who managed 56 yards and a touchdown by comparison. Both were outpaced in the touches department by starter Omarion Hampton (15), though both Vidal and Mitchell should continue to be somewhat involved until Hampton is able to demonstrate some explosiveness out of the backfield.

headline: Mitchell tallied 10 carries for 39 yards and five catches (on six targets) for 24 yards during Sunday's 30-23 defeat at Seattle.
story: Mitchell surprisingly led the Chargers backfield in touches with 15, ahead of Omarion Hampton's 11 and Kimani Vidal's seven, but unlike his position mates he didn't reach the end zone. Because Mitchell's touch count has increased in each successive week this season, he's trending in a positive direction, but until one of the trio is handling most of the RB reps, it'll be difficult to trust any of them for fantasy purposes on a weekly basis. He next takes the field next Sunday against the Broncos.

headline: Mitchell (ankle) was a full participant in Friday's practice and does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: After being limited Wednesday and Thursday and wearing a walking boot earlier in the week, Mitchell's good to go against Seattle. At less than 100 percent and facing a stout defense, Mitchell is tough to get behind for fantasy lineups, even after he closed the snaps and touches gap on Omarion Hampton in last Sunday's loss to the Bills. Neither is an overly exciting Week 4 fantasy bet.

headline: Mitchell (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: For the second day in a row, Mitchell had his reps capped while he manages a left ankle injury. So long as he doesn't take a step back in activity during the Chargers' final practice of the week Friday, Mitchell should still be on track to suit up Sunday against the Seahawks. Through the team's first three games, Mitchell has carried 17 times for 85 yards (5.0 YPC) while adding four receptions for 10 yards and a touchdown in a complementary role behind lead back Omarion Hampton.

headline: Mitchell (ankle) was a limited participant at the Chargers' practice Wednesday, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Mitchell was spotted with a walking boot on his left leg, and the Chargers updated their injury report to reflect the running back as limited Wednesday. He may have suffered the left ankle injury during Wednesday's session, but he didn't express much concern about the injury, and the running back will have two more chances this week to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the Seahawks. If Mitchell is unavailable for Week 4, Kimani Vidal would serve as the top reserve option behind starter Omarion Hampton.

headline: The Chargers placed Leonard (groin) on injured reserve Thursday.
story: It's not clear when Leonard was injured, as he logged a season-high 70 percent defensive snap share against the Jets last Sunday. Regardless, he's now required to miss at least four games while on IR. Avery Smith and Isas Waxter may get more opportunities in the secondary during Leonard's absence.

headline: Leonard (concussion) does not have a designation for Monday's matchup against Baltimore.
story: Leonard suffered a concussion at some point between the Chargers' Week 6 loss to Kansas City and the team's Week 7 bye. He missed the club's past two contests but has now passed through the NFL's concussion protocol and has been cleared to return to game action. Leonard should assume a rotational role in Los Angeles' secondary.

headline: Leonard (concussion) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
story: Leonard was upgraded to full participation for Friday's session after being limited Thursday. The cornerback has not yet officially cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol, but a return to full practice means he should be all set to suit up for the Chargers' Monday night contest against the Ravens.

headline: Leonard (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 9 clash against Houston.
story: Leonard is presumably still in concussion protocol, though he was able to log limited practice sessions Thursday and Friday. Donte Jackson (hamstring) is returning from a three-game absence Sunday, so the Chargers will get a boost in their secondary despite Leonard's continued absence.

headline: Leonard (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Rams, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: Leonard is in the league's concussion protocol, though it's not clear when he sustained the injury given that the Chargers were on a bye for Week 7. His absence means the Chargers will have less depth both on special teams and in the secondary. His next chance to play is Week 9 against Houston on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Leonard (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: It is unclear when Leonard sustained his concussion, as the Chargers were on bye in Week 7. The depth cornerback has enterted the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and will not be able to suit up for full-contact activities until he is cleared by an independent neurologist.

headline: The Chargers signed Browning to their active roster Thursday.
story: Browning joined Los Angeles' practice squad Oct. 13 and had been there since before being promoted to the active roster Thursday. The move could be a bad sign for starting QB Justin Herbert, who is in concussion protocol and could miss Sunday's clash against New England. Should Herbert miss that game, rookie DJ Uiagalelei would likely log his first NFL start, with Browning working as his backup.

headline: The Chargers signed Browning to the practice squad Tuesday, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Trey Lance (groin) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, so DJ Uiagalelei served as the Chargers' QB2 role behind Justin Herbert for Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos. The Chargers have opted to bring in a more seasoned veteran in Browning, who appeared in 17 regular-season games (10 starts) with the Bengals between 2023 and 2025, during which he completed 68.5 percent of passes for 2,707 yards, 18 touchdowns and 15 interceptions. Browning will open his Chargers tenure on the practice squad, although he could supplant Uiagalelei as the backup behind Herbert as soon as this Sunday against Kansas City.

headline: Tomlinson (knee) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Tomlinson likely sustained his knee injury in the Chargers' Week 11 loss to the Jets. The defensive tackle will likely need to return to practice by Friday's session for a chance to suit up for Sunday's game against the Patriots.

headline: Tomlinson recorded five tackles (three solo) including 2.0 sacks during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
story: In a game where Ravens quarterback Jacoby Brissett dropped back 51 times, there were no shortage of opportunities for the Chargers to rush the passer, and Tomlinson came away with the best single-game sack total of his nine-plus year career so far. He has taken on a larger role on the defensive line than 2025 third-rounder Jamaree Caldwell in recent weeks, and only Teair Tart played as many snaps on the Chargers' defensive front as Tomlinson did (36) in Week 10.

headline: Tomlinson (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: A hamstring injury has sidelined Tomlinson for the Chargers' last two games, but he avoided an injury tag for Sunday's AFC West tilt after logging a full practice Friday. He'll solidify the Chargers' depth on the defensive line behind Jamaree Caldwell, Teair Tart and Justin Eboigbe.

headline: Tomlinson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: A hamstring injury will cause Tomlinson to miss two consecutive games. The next time he can play is Week 5 against the Broncos, though he would need to log at least a limited practice to have a realistic chance of playing against Denver. Rookie fifth-rounder Nick Barrett will continue to operate in a rotational role on the defensive line in Tomlinson's absence.

headline: Gadsden went without a target while taking the field for 23 of the Chargers' 60 snaps on offense in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
story: Gadsden ranked third in snaps among Chargers tight ends, finishing only slightly behind Charlie Kolar (30) and David Njoku (25). Despite arguably being the most talented pass catcher of the trio, Gadsden was the only one of the three who failed to draw a target in Week 11. The 2025 fifth-round pick has endured a disappointing sophomore campaign, having thus far put together a 20-179-1 receiving line on 30 targets over 10 games while topping 40 receiving yards on just one occasion.

headline: Gadsden hauled in his lone target for seven yards in Monday's 23-20 win over Baltimore.
story: Gadsden went to the locker room during the first half of Monday's game after being poked in the ye, but the second-year tight end was cleared to return for the second quarter. However, his 12 offensive snaps were his lowest since Week 1 against the Cardinals (10), and that lack of playing time coincided with the return of veteran tight end David Njoku, who missed the Chargers' six prior games while on IR due to a fibula injury. Njoku and Charlie Kolar appear to be the Chargers' top options at tight end, squeezing Gadsden out of the game plan ahead of Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

headline: Gadsden (eye) returned to Monday night's game against the Ravens, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Gadsden was poked in the eye in the first quarter and had to go to the locker room before returning early in the second quarter. He wasn't targeted in the passing game prior to sustaining the injury.

headline: Gadsden (eye) is questionable to return to Monday's game against the Ravens.
story: It's unclear when Gadsden suffered the injury, but he went to the locker room midway through the first quarter. He wasn't targeted prior to leaving the contest. David Njoku and Charlie Kolar will handle tight-end duties for the Bolts while Gadsden is sidelined.

headline: Gadsden caught two of three targets for 17 yards during the Chargers' 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday.
story: Gadsden was on the field for 33 of 72 offensive snaps (45.8 percent), which was second-most among Chargers tight ends behind Charlie Kolar (47). Gadsden has caught two passes or fewer in six of eight regular-season games, and his 19-172-1 receiving line (on 29 targets) is well behind pace from his rookie campaign (49 catches on 69 targets for 664 yards and three scores across 15 regular-season contests). The Chargers' offense this season has struggled under quarterback Justin Herbert and coordinator Mike McDaniel, which doesn't bring much confidence ahead of their Week 10 road tilt against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

headline: Gadsden caught all five of his targets for 52 yards during Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
story: Gadsden was able to lead the team in catches while he finished with one fewer target than team leader Ladd McConkey. The tight end has now reeled in at least three passes for the second straight game and third time over the last four contests after having failed to do so in any of the team's first three regular-season games. Gadsden and the rest of the Chargers will face a tough test in Week 9 against the Texans.

headline: Gadsden is active for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Rams.
story: The second-year tight end has had a relatively quiet first season to date in coordinator Mike McDaniel's offense, posting a 12-103-1 line on 21 targets through six games. Gadsden did get back on the Chargers' offense's radar before the Week 7 bye, recording three receptions for 17 yards on five targets over 33 snaps in Week 6 against the Chiefs after being blanked over 39 plays in Week 5 against the Broncos. It remains to be seen if Los Angeles, which declined to make a change at playcaller during the bye, cooked up some improvements during the idle week, and if Gadsden will be more involved moving forward after flashing plenty of upside as a rookie in 2025 with a 49-664-3 line across 15 regular-season contests.

headline: Gadsden secured five of eight targets for 36 yards and recorded a two-yard carry during Sunday's 30-23 defeat in Seattle.
story: With position mates David Njoku (fibula) on IR and Charlie Kolar (forearm) sidelined the last two contests, Gadsden has had uneven results, posting a bagel on three targets in Week 3 at Buffalo before Sunday's season-best performance. Gadsden likely was helped this week by the early exit of No. 1 WR Ladd McConkey (foot), but the former's efficiency (9.5 YPC, 5.7 YPT) has been lacking in a floundering Chargers offense so far this season. In any case, for as long as Njoku and Kolar are out of the lineup, Gadsden shouldn't have a problem leading the team's TEs in most receiving categories.

headline: Gadsden didn't catch any of his three targets in Sunday's loss to the Bills.
story: With Charlie Kolar (forearm) and David Njoku (fibula, IR) both unavailable, Gadsden drew the start Sunday and led Los Angeles' tight ends with a 57 percent offensive snap share. However, Gadsden couldn't do anything with that workload, failing to reel in any of the three targets QB Justin Herbert tossed his way. Gadsden could have another chance to make an impact this coming Sunday against Seattle with both Kolar and Njoku set to remain sidelined, but the Seahawks have given up the third-fewest receiving yards to tight ends so far this season.

headline: Molden recorded eight tackles (four solo) in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
story: The safety has finished with five or more stops in seven of the eight games he's played in this season. Molden has 44 tackles (25 solo), a pass breakup and a fumble recovery in 2026.

headline: Molden (hamstring) is available for Sunday's game against Seattle.
story: Molden has been battling a hamstring injury but will avoid another absence in Week 4. As a result, RJ Mickens and Genesis Smith should see fewer snaps.

headline: Molden (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: A hamstring injury prevented Molden from playing against the Bills in Week 3, but the sixth-year pro has drawn a questionable tag for Week 4 after logging three consecutive limited practices. One or both of Tony Jefferson and Genesis Smith could start at safety Sunday depending on the statuses of both Molden and Derwin James (hamstring).

headline: Phillips finished with four tackles (two solo) in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
story: The linebacker recorded at least four stops for the fourth game in a row and the ninth time in 10 games this season. Phillips has 53 tackles (23 solo) and an interception on the year.

headline: Phillips recorded nine tackles (four solo) and an interception during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
story: Phillips was in the right place at the right time when a Jacoby Brissett pass bounced off the helmet of rookie wideout Ja'Kobi Lane in the second quarter, and the turnover set up a Chargers touchdown that put the team ahead 17-7. His tackle total was also his highest going back to Week 18 of the 2023 season with the Ravens. With that said, his role in the Chargers' defense is still not big enough to warrant IDP consideration in most formats.

headline: Kolar brought in his lone target for eight yards during the Chargers' 27-24 loss to the Jets on Sunday.
story: Kolar was cleared to play Sunday after progressing through the league's concussion protocol, and his 30 offensive snaps were ahead of fellow tight ends David Njoku (25) and Oronde Gadsden (23). Kolar's eight-yard catch midway through the first quarter was the only pass that the fifth-year pro saw from Justin Herbert, but no Chargers pass catcher saw more than five targets other then Ladd McConkey (eight). Kolar has a 16-153-0 line on 24 targets through eight regular-season games heading into Week 12 against the Patriots on Nov. 29.

headline: Kolar (concussion) is active for Sunday's game versus the Jets.
story: Kolar showed up on the Chargers' first Week 11 injury report Wednesday as a non-participant due to a concussion, and thereafter he managed just one limited session Friday before the team tagged him as questionable for Sunday. Despite his inability to practice fully this week and the prospect of gaining clearance from an independent neurologist shaped up as a difficult combination to overcome, he's available to the offense. Kolar will join Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku as L.A.'s active tight ends this weekend.

headline: Kolar (concussion) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: The tight end is still in the concussion protocol, so he'll be up against it to clear the final hurdles, especially after the Chargers played Monday night against Baltimore. If Kolar is ruled out, David Njoku and Oronde Gadsden should handle most of the tight-end duties for the Bolts.

headline: Kolar (concussion) remained sidelined for Thursday's practice.
story: The tight end remains in concussion protocol and looks like he'll miss Sunday's game against the Jets. If so, Oronde Gadsden and David Njoku would step in to handle most of the tight-end duties.

headline: Kolar (concussion) did not participate at practice Wednesday.
story: Kolar led the Chargers in snaps at tight end (41) during Monday's game at Baltimore, but it appears he may have suffered a concussion at some point during the contest. He'll need to progress through the NFL's five-step concussion protocol, which includes gaining clearance from an independent neurologist, before he'll be allowed to return to game action. His level of activity at practice Thursday or Friday could give some indication as to any progress he makes ahead of Sunday's game versus the Jets.

headline: Kolar caught two of three passes for 16 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
story: Kolar's 41 offensive snaps were by far the most among Chargers tight ends, well ahead of a returning David Njoku (19) and Oronde Gadsden (12), although the latter briefly left Monday's game due to an eye injury. That said, Kolar was held to two catches or fewer for the second time in three games, and he has not seen a red zone target from Justin Herbert since Week 6 against Kansas City. Kolar has amassed a 15-145-0 receiving line on 23 targets across seven regular-season games heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

headline: Kolar brought in all three of his targets for 31 yards in a 44-22 loss to the Texans on Sunday.
story: Kolar has recorded three catches in four of his last five outings, although he's cracked 30-plus receiving yards in just two of those contests. The Chargers average a season-low 15.1 points per game, and their 201.9 receiving yards per game is ninth-fewest in the NFL, making pass catchers like Kolar hard to rely on for sustained production. The 0-8 Chargers will look to capture their first win of the season in Week 10 against the Ravens on Monday Night Football.

headline: Kolar caught one of four targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
story: The tight end's four targets tied for third on the team, as he ran 17 routes on Justin Herbert's 37 dropbacks against Los Angeles. More of a blocker than receiver, Kolar has been forced to catch more passes out of necessity at times this season. He has 10 grabs for 98 yards on 17 targets. The catches and targets are both career highs in his fifth season.

headline: Kolar caught three of six targets for 20 yards during the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
story: Kolar finished fifth on the Chargers in receiving yards, but he was also second on the team in both catches and targets behind KeAndre Lambert-Smith (five catches on nine targets for 32 yards). Kolar has a 6-57-0 receiving line in his two outings since returning from a two-game absence due to a fractured forearm, but he's stuck in an offense that is one of the worst units in the league this season. The Chargers will look to regroup during the Week 7 bye before facing the Rams in Week 8 on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Kolar reeled in three of four targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 23-17 loss versus the Broncos. He also lost a fumble.
story: Kolar was fighting for extra yardage after making a 19-yard grab for a first down in the first quarter when safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) jarred the ball loose, creating a turnover to set up a Denver touchdown. Kolar managed two more catches for 18 yards the rest of the way, which was enough to make him the Chargers' most productive pass catcher in a game where quarterback Justin Herbert only threw for 121 yards. Kolar projects to start as a blocking-first tight end again in a Week 6 tilt against the Chiefs.

headline: Kolar (forearm) is active for Sunday's game against Denver, Eric Smith of the team's official site reports.
story: Kolar missed the last two games but will return despite practicing in a limited capacity during the week. With Kolar active in Week 5, Oronde Gadsden is expected to slide back to the No. 2 spot on the tight-end depth chart.

headline: Kolar (forearm) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: Kolar was limited in practice all week due to a fractured forearm, but he's progressed enough in his recovery to draw the questionable tag after missing the Chargers' prior two games. Oronde Gadsden would continue to serve as the Chargers' top tight end if Kolar is unable to return.

headline: Kolar (forearm) remained limited in Thursday's practice.
story: Kolar broke his forearm in Week 2 against the Raiders and has missed the last two games. The block-first tight end's return will be welcomed by Los Angeles once he's cleared. The Chargers offensive line has been a nightmare, and both starting tackles Rashawn Slater (ankle) and Joe Alt (neck) are again dealing with injuries.

headline: Kolar (forearm) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Kolar has missed the Chargers' last two games while recovering from a fractured left forearm that he sustained in Week 2 against the Seahawks. He's progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice Wednesday, and his participation over the next two days will provide clarity on his chances of playing against the Broncos on Sunday. If Kolar is cleared to return, then he would likely split tight end duties with Oronde Gadsden since David Njoku (knee) is on injured reserve.

headline: Kolar (forearm) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: Kolar fractured his forearm during the Chargers' Week 2 loss to the Raiders. He'll miss a second consecutive game due to his injury, but the positive news for the fifth-year tight end is that he ended Week 4 prep with a limited practice Friday. Head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters after Friday's session that Kolar is "doing everything and anything possible" to return to the field, and he could get back as soon as Week 5 against the Broncos on Sunday, Oct. 11. For now, Oronde Gadsden will serve as the Chargers' TE1, with Hayden Rucci also in the mix for offensive snaps.

headline: Kolar (forearm) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Kolar hasn't practiced in any fashion since fracturing his left forearm in a Sept. 20 loss to the Raiders and undergoing surgery two days later. The Chargers have avoided placing Kolar on injured reserve with the expectation that he'll return to action within four games, but he'll almost certainly miss a second straight contest this Sunday in Seattle.

headline: Kolar (forearm) is not practicing Wednesday, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kolar remains unlikely to play Sunday against the Seahawks, as he continues his recovery from a broken forearm, which he suffered in Week 2. Oronde Gadsden, Hayden Rucci and Patrick Herbert handled tight-end duties against the Bills last Sunday.

headline: Dicker made his lone field-goal attempt and all three PATs in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
story: Dicker's field goal was drilled from 52 yards, and he's now 19-for-21 on field-goal tries and 15-for-15 on extra points through 10 games this season. In a Chargers offense struggling mightily to score points, Dicker's fantasy value has tanked this season.

headline: Dicker made all three of his field-goal tries and converted both of his extra-point attempts during Monday's 23-20 win at Baltimore.
story: Dicker's longest field goal on the day was only from 38 yards out, but his accuracy played a big part in the Chargers picking up their first win of the season. He hasn't missed a kick since Week 3, but the team's general inability to move the ball consistently keeps him from projecting as a top-tier fantasy option in most formats going into a Week 11 matchup versus the Jets.

headline: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 44-22 loss to Houston.
story: Dicker was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game and fifth time this season. The kicker did all his damage in the first half, converting field goals from 52, 33 and 43 yards before the break. Dicker has now gone 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Dicker made all three of his field-goal attempts during Sunday's 24-9 loss against the Rams. He did not kick any extra-point tries.
story: The Chargers offense put forth another poor effort in Week 8, with four of their 11 drives ending in punts and another three ending with turnovers. Dicker has mostly been efficient through his first seven games of the season, making 12 of his 14 field-goal attempts, but until the offense demonstrates it can consistently move the ball down the field, he'll be hard to trust as a fantasy option.

headline: Dicker made both of his field-goal attempts in the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
story: Dicker's 23-yard and 30-yard field goals were the only points scored by the Chargers in the team's blowout loss. While the offense could not get going, as has been the theme all season, Dicker remained reliable. The 26-year-old moves to 9-for-11 on field-goal attempts and a perfect 9-for-9 on extra-point attempts over six regular-season games in 2026.

headline: Dicker made his lone field-goal attempt and both of his extra-point tries during the Chargers' 23-17 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
story: Dicker got the Chargers on the board with a 42-yard field goal in the second quarter before adding two PATs in the second half. Dicker has attempted one field goal or zero in three of the first five games of the regular season and has yet to make a field goal from 50-plus yards. He's 7-for-9 on field-goal attempts and 9-for-9 on extra-point tries heading into a Week 6 road matchup Oct. 18 against the Chiefs, who are coming off a bye.

headline: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made both of his PATs during Sunday's 30-23 loss to Seattle.
story: Dicker made field goals from 40 and 39 yards in the first half before converting a 36-yarder late in the fourth quarter. The kicker had missed a field-goal try in each of the last two games entering Week 4, but he was able to get back on track against the Seahawks. Dicker has now gone 6-for-8 on field-goal attempts while making all seven of his extra-point tries over four contests this year.

headline: Johnston caught one of two targets for nine yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets. He added one yard on one rushing attempt.
story: Johnston was targeted on just 9.5 percent of Justin Herbert's 21 pass attempts against New York. The wideout has now caught exactly one pass in three straight games and in five of his last six contests. Johnston is a lightly targeted deep threat who will likely continue to see fewer looks if Ladd McConkey is able to maintain his health for an extended period.

headline: Johnston brought in his sole target for six yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
story: The speedster was poised to see some added involvement with Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, but that never materialized on a night when 86 of Justin Herbert's 129 passing yards went to Tre' Harris. Johnston's yardage total was a season-low figure, and he's now been limited to one reception in four of the last five games. Johnston's often been able to offset the modest catch totals with big plays, but that clearly wasn't the case Monday night. Johnston will remain a hit-or-miss fantasy option in a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday, irrespective of McConkey's availability.

headline: Johnston caught one of four targets for a 58-yard touchdown in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
story: Johnston's long touchdown catch cut the deficit to 38-15 in the fourth quarter. That was the final pass Justin Herbert (finger) completed before exiting the game. If Herbert can't play against the Ravens in Week 10, Johnston would likely find himself catching passes from DJ Uiagalelei. Johnston's 58 receiving yards set a new season high, surpassing his one-catch, 57-yard effort in Week 6, and Sunday's TD was his first of the season.

headline: Johnston caught all four of his targets for 37 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
story: Johnston's four grabs marked a new personal single-game high through six games this season. One of the least efficient wideouts in the league, Johnston entered Sunday with just eight grabs for 165 yards on 22 targets. He hasn't been playable in fantasy football for weeks and will square off with a stingy Houston secondary in Week 9.

headline: Johnston's role in the passing game will shrink slightly in Week 8 against the Rams given that both Ladd McConkey (concussion) and Tre' Harris (hamstring) have been cleared to play, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: Both Johnston and McConkey were sidelined for Week 5, but the latter entered the league's concussion protocol during the Chargers' Week 6 loss to the Chiefs. Johnston logged 17 targets through his first three games of the regular season, although he's seen only five passes from Justin Herbert over his last two outings, which Johnston turned into two catches for 101 yards. The Chargers are averaging only 168.2 passing yards per game this season -- which ranks 28th in the NFL -- and they face a Rams defense that boasts the fourth-best pass defense in the league (186.3 passing yards allowed per game).

headline: Johnston caught one of three targets for 57 yards in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Johnston needed just one catch to set a season high in receiving yards, but he was tackled at the 1-yard line to keep him without a touchdown this season after consecutive eight-touchdown regular seasons. The Chargers proceeded to back up 11 yards from there and settled for a field goal. Johnston has caught a deep pass in each of the past two games, securing a 44-yard catch in the Week 5 loss to Seattle prior to the 57-yard catch against the Chiefs. The 2023 first-round pick has just eight catches through five appearances heading into LA's Week 7 bye.

headline: Johnston (chest) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Ladd McConkey (foot) has also been cleared to play, while Tre' Harris (hamstring) has been ruled out. Harris seemed to be threatening Johnston for the No. 2 receiver job, but for now it'll likely be Johnston's role.

headline: Johnston (chest) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Johnston practiced in a limited fashion for the second day in a row, which offers hope that he'll be able to put an end to a one-game absence and return to action Sunday in Kansas City.
