In order to avoid carrying a designation into the weekend, however, Johnston may need to upgrade to full participation during Friday's practice.

headline: Johnston (chest) was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's injury report.
story: A chest injury kept Johnston off the field for Week 5, but he was able to get some work in Wednesday. Fellow pass catchers Ladd McConkey (foot) and Tre' Harris (hamstring) are also banged up -- the latter did not practice Wednesday -- so it remains to be seen what the Los Angeles receiver room will look like Sunday against the Chiefs.

headline: Johnston (chest) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Denver.
story: With Johnston sidelined and Ladd McConkey (foot) listed as questionable, Tre' Harris may end up being the No. 1 wide receiver for Justin Herbert on Sunday. There was no hint earlier this week of Johnston's chest injury being serious, but he'll apparently miss at least one game.

headline: Johnston (chest) wasn't practicing during the portion of Friday's session open to the media, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: With Johnston having been limited Wednesday and Thursday, this could be more of a rest day for the wideout. The winless Chargers appear set to head into Sunday's game against the Broncos without Ladd McConkey (foot) after he missed practice all week, so Johnston is going to be needed alongside Tre' Harris at wide receiver.

headline: Johnston (chest) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
story: A chest injury has resulted in back-to-back capped sessions for Johnston to kick off Week 5 prep, giving him just one more opportunity to get back to full Friday before the Chargers potentially tag him with a designation for Sunday's game against the Broncos. With Ladd McConkey (foot) not practicing Wednesday or Thursday and potentially trending toward an absence, an active Johnston likely will be the top pass catcher available to QB Justin Herbert this weekend.

headline: Johnston was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a chest injury.
story: The Chargers' receiving corps is banged up at the moment, with all of WR Ladd McConkey (foot, DNP on Wednesday), WR Brenen Thompson (quadriceps, LP) and TE Charlie Kolar (forearm, LP) dealing with health concerns, and WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) and TE David Njoku (fibula) on IR. Johnston has had every opportunity to produce this season, with at least a 75 percent snap share in all four games, but he so far has just nine touches for 111 yards from scrimmage and no TDs. Assuming McConkey isn't able to play Sunday versus the Broncos and Johnston suits up, the latter could be the unquestioned No. 1 pass catcher for QB Justin Herbert.

headline: Johnston caught one of two targets for 44 yards in Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Seahawks. He added one carry for minus-4 yards.
story: Despite Ladd McConkey (foot) playing just 24 of 71 offensive snaps, including zero in the second half, Johnston was a ghost most of the afternoon before hauling in a deep ball in the fourth quarter. Johnston continues to pace the team in snaps and routes at wide receiver, but he has little to show for it this season, posting just seven catches for 108 yards and no touchdowns on 19 targets. Johnston won't be a recommended fantasy play next Sunday against the Broncos, even if Patrick Surtain (ankle) and Riley Moss (ribs) are still banged up.

headline: Vidal carried the ball seven times for 36 yards and caught both his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
story: After handling just four touches last week against the Ravens, Vidal saw his usage increase again as he recorded his most scrimmage yards since Week 5. This time, however, his additional volume came at the expense of Keaton Mitchell (knee), who left the game early. Omarion Hampton has re-established himself as the Chargers' clear No. 1 RB over the last few contests, but if Mitchell's injury proves to be serious, Vidal could have some deeper-league appeal with the No. 2 role all to himself. He'll look to take advantage of whatever opportunities he gets in Week 12 against the Patriots.

headline: Vidal turned two carries into zero yards, brought in both of his targets for 14 yards and returned one kickoff for 32 yards during the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday.
story: Vidal's 15 offensive snaps were just ahead of Keaton Mitchell's 13, but both running backs took a back seat to Omarion Hampton, who was on the field for 36 of the Chargers' 57 snaps on offense and led the backfield with 22 carries for 105 yards and one touchdown. Vidal's two carries were his fewest since Week 3 against the Bills (one), although his 15-yard catch early in the third quarter set the Chargers up just outside the red zone, with Cameron Dicker connecting on a 34-yard field goal four plays later. Vidal and Mitchell appear to be falling into rotational roles behind Hampton heading into Week 11 against the Jets on Sunday.

headline: Vidal rushed seven times for 30 yards in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans. He added one catch for six yards on three targets.
story: The Chargers continue to use a three-man backfield, an unfriendly fantasy situation and one to avoid when making lineup decisions each week. Vidal has been productive when he does get touches, rushing 36 times for 162 yards (4.5 YPC) and one touchdown across eight games. He's also caught 10 passes for 56 yards and an additional score.

headline: Vidal rushed eight times for 23 yards and caught both of his targets for seven yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
story: The Chargers continue to use a fantasy-unfriendly three-man backfield, giving all three of Vidal, Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell meaningful touches and snaps. In a broken Los Angeles offense and crowded group of RBs, Vidal has minimal fantasy appeal outside of deeper formats.

headline: Vidal turned seven carries into 21 yards and caught three of four passes for 19 yards during the Chargers' 22-6 loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
story: The Chargers' run offense struggled Sunday, but Vidal was slightly more efficient than Omarion Hampton (18 yards) on the same number of carries. Vidal has seen more rotational offensive snaps over the Chargers' last three games, and over that span he has logged 20 carries for 103 yards and a touchdown and six catches (on nine targets) for 29 yards and a score. His role may continue to expand following the Week 7 bye, with the Chargers' next game taking place in Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Vidal tallied eight carries for 57 yards and one touchdown, one catch (on two targets) for minus-1 yard and returned three kicks for 75 yards during Sunday's 23-17 defeat to the Broncos.
story: After opening the season with no touches through the first two games -- and just two in Week 3 -- Vidal has taken full advantage of his 16 over the last two contests, turning them into 92 yards from scrimmage and two TDs. All three of the Chargers' running backs got in the mix Sunday, with Omarion Hampton earning 15 touches and Keaton Mitchell getting six, but Vidal was the only one of the trio with an end-zone visit. Considering his recent success, Vidal appears likely to hold on to a regular role next Sunday at Kansas City.

headline: Vidal rushed five times for 25 yards in Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Seahawks. He added two catches for 11 yards and a touchdown on three targets.
story: Vidal, Omarion Hampton and Keaton Mitchell split playing time evenly, as Mitchell logged 26 snaps to 25 each for Vidal and Hampton. The Chargers are looking for answers on offense, and giving Vidal more looks appears to be an avenue the team is willing to explore. Vidal scored on a nine-yard catch in the third quarter after entering Week 4 with just two touches across the first three games. Involved in a three-man backfield committee, he's not yet a viable fantasy starter ahead of next Sunday's date with Denver.

headline: Harris caught both his targets for 28 yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
story: With Ladd McConkey back in the lineup, Harris' role in the passing attack shrank after he'd turned 12 targets over the prior two games into an 8-92-0 line. Harris' fantasy appeal would collapse even further if Justin Herbert (concussion) ends up missing any time. The second-year wideout will at least get a promising matchup in Week 12 against a vulnerable Patriots secondary.

headline: Harris secured all five targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night.
story: With Ladd McConkey (back) sidelined, Harris functioned as a de facto top target for Justin Herbert, and he was responsible for all but 43 of his quarterback's passing yards. The yardage tally also was a career-high figure for Harris, who generated team-high totals with all three components of his receiving line. Harris is up to a career-high 348 receiving yards on 26 catches heading into a favorable Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

headline: Harris (calf) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
story: After being limited the day before, Harris erased any doubt about his availability for Monday's game at Baltimore. He saw a team-high seven targets on a 79 percent route share last week, catching three passes for a mere six yards in the 44-22 loss to Houston. Harris' volume projection for Week 10 partially depends on Ladd McConkey (back), who didn't play any snaps last week and didn't practice Thursday or Friday.

headline: Harris (shoulder) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: With teammate Ladd McConkey sidelined by a back injury in Week 9, Harris played 59 of the Chargers' 68 offensive snaps, drawing a team-high seven targets. It seems like he may have picked up an injury of his own along the way though, which makes his availability for Week 10 worth monitoring. He'll have two more chances to manage a full practice before the Chargers publish their last injury report of the week Saturday.

headline: Harris caught three of seven targets for six yards during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
story: Harris failed to take advantage of Ladd McConkey (back) failing to appear in Sunday's game, registering his fewest receiving yards in a game this season. Harris was able to garner a team-high seven targets, which bodes well for his chances of increased production in Week 10 against the Ravens if McConkey remains sidelined.

headline: Harris caught all three of his targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 24-9 loss to the Rams.
story: After missing Week 6 with a hamstring injury, Harris was healthy coming out of the Week 7 bye but played pretty clearly behind both Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston against the Rams. Harris ran just 20 routes to McConkey's 34 and Johnston's 30. Harris would see a big boost if Johnston gets traded ahead of next week's deadline.

headline: Harris (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Rams.
story: Harris, Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston have all missed time this season, but they're healthy after a Week 7 bye. Prior to the team's onslaught of injuries, Harris actually saw more targets (21) than Johnston (19) over the first four weeks of the season.

headline: Harris (hamstring) remained limited in Thursday's practice.
story: Harris suffered his hamstring injury in Week 5 against Denver and missed Week 6 ahead of last week's bye. With back-to-back limited practices to open Week 8 prep, Harris has a decent chance of suiting up Sunday against the Rams. In a broken Chargers offense, it's difficult to get excited about anyone on the team for fantasy.

headline: Harris (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Wednesday was Harris' first practice since he sustained a hamstring injury during the Chargers' Week 5 loss to the Broncos. He was unable to play in Week 6 against the Chiefs, but the second-year wide receiver had additional time to rest courtesy of the Chargers' Week 7 bye. It's possible he misses only one game, and he'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Rams.

headline: Harris (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Harris didn't practice this week, after making an early exit from the Week 5 loss to Denver. With Ladd McConkey (foot) and Quentin Johnston (chest) now returning from injuries, the team's WR room is in better shape than a week ago even without Harris.

headline: Harris (hamstring) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice.
story: The Chargers have held Harris out of their first two practices of the week, a development that comes as little surprise after head coach Jim Harbaugh described the wideout as "more week-to-week" than day-to-day coming out of this past Sunday's loss to the Broncos, per Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com. Unless Harris is able to make a surprise return to practice Friday, he'll likely miss his first game of the season this Sunday in Kansas City.

headline: Harris (hamstring) was listed as a non-participant on Wednesday's injury report.
story: Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that Harris is week-to-week with the injury he sustained in Sunday's loss to the Broncos, so it comes as little surprise that he did not see any action Wednesday.

headline: Head coach Jim Harbaugh said Monday that Harris is "week-to-week" due to a hamstring injury that he sustained during Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Harris entered Sunday as the Chargers' WR1 due to the absence of Quentin Johnston (chest) while Ladd McConkey (foot) was available only as an emergency option, per Insdorf. Harris caught two of four passes for 16 yards before sustaining a hamstring injury, which was severe enough for him not to return. Given Harbaugh's update, coupled with the Chargers' bye scheduled for Week 7, it seems likely that Harris will be held out for Week 6 against the Chiefs, with an eye toward being available for Week 8 against the Rams on Sunday, Nov. 1. Given the Chargers' injuries to the wide receiver position, the team will need to lean more heavily on Marquez Valdes-Scantling, Theo Wease, Derius Davis and tight ends Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden in the passing game.

headline: Harris (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Broncos.
story: Harris is dealing with an apparent hamstring injury, and his availability for the stretch run of Sunday's matchup is now up in the air. In his absence, Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Derius Davis will likely slot into more prominent roles on offense.

headline: Harris' workload should be larger against the Broncos on Sunday, as Quentin Johnston (chest) has been ruled out, and Ladd McConkey (foot, questionable) may not play, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Rookie fourth-rounder Brenen Thompson (quadriceps) also has been ruled out alongside Johnston. McConkey faces an uphill battle to play Sunday after sitting out of practice all week, and he may operate under a snap count if he's given the green light to suit up. That puts Harris -- who has seen five targets or more in three of four games this season -- in position to work in an elevated role against a Broncos defense that will be without both starting outside cornerbacks Riley Moss (ribs) and Patrick Surtain (ankle).

headline: Harris caught three of five targets for 60 yards during Sunday's 30-23 loss to the Seahawks.
story: Harris led the team in receiving yards for the second straight week, recording at least 53 receiving yards for the third contest in a row. Ladd McConkey (foot) aggravated his pre-existing foot injury in the contest, and he is considered week-to-week for the time being. If McConkey is unavailable in Week 5 versus the Broncos, Harris may have a chance to operate as the team's primary pass catcher.

headline: McConkey caught five of eight targets for 37 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
story: His longest gain went for just 11 yards, but McConkey was deadly in the red zone, connecting with Justin Herbert on scores of 11 and six yards in the fourth quarter as the Chargers tried to mount a late comeback. Herbert was placed in the concussion protocol after the game after taking six sacks, and if he end up missing any time, it would put a big damper on McConkey's fantasy outlook with undrafted rookie DJ Uiagalelei being the Bolts' backup, unless Trey Lance (groin) is able to return from IR. McConkey has had plenty of trouble staying on the field himself this year, of course, and he'll take a 22-323-3 line on 32 targets through seven contests into a Week 12 clash with the Patriots.

headline: McConkey (back) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Though he wasn't among the Chargers' Week 9 inactives, back spasms led to McConkey not recording any snaps during the team's 44-22 loss to the Texans on Nov. 8. After not traveling to Baltimore with his teammates for this past Monday's 23-20 win, the wideout was able to practice in a limited fashion Wednesday through Friday before carrying a 'questionable' designation into the weekend. With no known setbacks since, the 2024 second-rounder will give it a go and is on track to reclaim his key role in Los Angeles' WR corps alongside Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris. In the six games he's taken the field in, McConkey has averaged 2.8 catches (on 4.2 targets) for 47.7 yards with one TD, a pace that the 6-foot, 185-pounder figures to pick up if he can avoid injuries in the coming weeks.

headline: McConkey (back) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Jets, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: McConkey, who didn't record any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms and then was inactive in Week 10, is officially listed as questionable by the Chargers after logging limited practices all week. While the wideout is on track to return to action versus New York, those considering McConkey in Week 11 fantasy lineups are still advised to verify his status once inactives are posted ahead of Sunday's 4:05 pm ET kickoff, given the tricky nature of back spasms.

headline: McConkey (back) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: McConkey, who didn't record any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms and was inactive in Week 10, has been able to practice in a limited fashion thus far this week, but thanks to his official 'questionable' designation, his status will need to be tracked in advance of Sunday's 4:05 ET kickoff. If McConkey is limited or out versus New York, Tre' Harris could maintain a key role in the Chargers' pass-catching corps alongside fellow WR Quentin Johnston.

headline: McConkey (back) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: McConkey, who was inactive in Week 10 and didn't log any snaps during Week 9 action due to back spasms, also was limited Wednesday. Per Noah Furtado of The Athletic, the wideout was seen at Thursday's practice in a non-contact jersey, as he continues to manage his back issue. With that in mind, unless McConkey is able work fully Friday, he'll likely carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

headline: McConkey (back) was spotted at Thursday's practice in a non-contact jersey, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: McConkey was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and the fact that he's in a non-contact jersey a day later suggests that the WR will log another limited listing Thursday. If that's the case, McConkey likely will have to work fully Friday in order to approach Sunday's game against the Jets without an injury designation.

headline: McConkey (back) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: After missing the Chargers' last game with a back issue, McConkey's return to limited work is an encouraging step in his preparation for Week 11 against the Jets. His practice status over the rest of the week should provide more clarity on his availability for Sunday. There's no sugar-coating it that McConkey's season has been a complete disappointment to date, as he's battled multiple injuries that have caused him to miss three entire games and parts of several others. He's difficult to trust for fantasy until he puts something together in the box score and makes it through an entire game healthy.

headline: McConkey (back) won't travel to Baltimore with the Chargers for Monday's game against the Ravens and has been downgraded from questionable to out for Week 10 action.
story: McConkey's next chance to play will thus arrive Nov. 22 against the Jets. In his absence versus Baltimore, Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith will be available to lead Los Angeles' WR corps.

headline: McConkey (back) is listed as questionable for Monday night's game against the Ravens, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Although he was active for the Chargers' Week 9 loss to the Texans, McConkey didn't end up playing a single snap due to back spasms. His practice reps were restricted during Week 10 prep, and the questionable tag means McConkey's official status may not be known until the Chargers announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before Monday's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. If McConkey is ruled out or available only on an emergency basis, then Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith would operate as the Chargers' top wideouts against Baltimore.

headline: McConkey (back) didn't practice Friday.
story: McConkey -- who dealt with back spasms last Sunday and as a result didn't log any snaps in the 0-8 Chargers' loss to the Texans, has now missed back-to-back practices, so what he's able to do Saturday will be pivotal with regard to his status for Monday night's game against the Ravens. If McConkey is unavailable for the contest, Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith would be in line to head Los Angeles' WR corps, as they did versus Houston.

headline: McConkey (back) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com relayed Monday that Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh viewed McConkey as "day to day" with the back spasms that led to the wideout not logging any snaps in this past Sunday's loss to the Texans. With a 'DNP' on the record for Thursday, McConkey now has two more chances to practice ahead of Monday night's game against the Ravens.

headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh noted Monday that McConkey is viewed as "day to day" with back spasms, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: McConkey was not among the Chargers' Week 9 inactives, but he didn't play any snaps in Sunday's loss to the Texans after experiencing back spasms during pregame workouts. Harbaugh's assessment that the wideout is 'day-to-day' offers hope that McConkey will be in the clear ahead of next Monday's game against the Ravens, and a big step toward that outcome would be his full participation in practice no later than Saturday.

headline: McConkey was active but didn't play any snaps in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans after experiencing back spasms during pregame workouts, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Because McConkey sustained the injury after the Chargers had already announced their inactive list, the wideout ended up being active but unavailable for the second time in three games. Back in Week 5, McConkey had been managing a foot injury but still proceeded to suit up for a matchup with Denver, though he didn't see any action and was active only because the Chargers had seven other players dealing with more significant health concerns. McConkey also made early exits in Week 1 due to a rib injury, Week 4 due to the foot issue and in Week 6 due to a concussion. The mounting injuries have made it increasingly difficult for fantasy managers to depend on McConkey, whose lack of availability has been one of many reasons that the 0-8 Chargers have taken a massive step back on offense in 2026.

headline: McConkey (back) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Texans.
story: Prior to his first-quarter exit, McConkey wasn't targeted by QB Justin Herbert. His absence leaves Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris, KeAndre Lambert-Smith and Derius Davis as the Chargers' available WRs versus Houston.

headline: McConkey brought in four of six targets for 86 yards in the Chargers' 24-9 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
story: McConkey finally shook off the concussion that led to his exit from a Week 6 loss to the Chiefs during Week 8 prep, and despite the fact Tre' Harris also was back from a hamstring injury, the former still led the Chargers in receiving yards and targets. The yardage tally was also a season high for McConkey, who is averaging a career-best 16.8 YPC on his 17 catches to date. Los Angeles' air attack showed some improvement Sunday following some retooling during the Week 7 bye, and McConkey figures to remain the top target on the winless Bolts in a Week 9 home matchup against the Texans next Sunday.

headline: McConkey (concussion) is off the injury report and will play in Sunday's game against the Rams, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: After entering the week in concussion protocol, McConkey progressed to full practices Wednesday and Thursday before shedding his injury designation Friday. The Chargers will also get Tre' Harris (hamstring) back in action after a Week 6 absence and Week 7 bye.

headline: McConkey (concussion) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
story: McConkey has back-to-back uncapped practices under his belt this week, but it remains unclear if he's gained clearance from the concussion protocol, which requires getting the all-clear from an independent neurologist. Friday's injury report will reveal if he still needs to pass such an exam ahead of Sunday's game versus the Rams.

headline: McConkey (concussion) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: McConkey was dealing with a foot injury for multiple weeks before suffering a concussion in the Chargers' last game Oct. 18. With the benefit of the team's Week 7 bye, he didn't endure any practice restrictions Wednesday and also ditched his previous foot issue. McConkey thus appears as if he only needs clearance from an independent neurologist in order to play Sunday against the Rams.

headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said McConkey remains in concussion protocol but will practice Wednesday, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: McConkey was knocked out of the Chargers' Oct. 18 loss to the Chiefs after sustaining a concussion but appears to have made some progress through the five-step protocol following the team's Week 7 bye. He was spotted practicing Monday during the Chargers' bonus session coming out of the bye week and looks on track to participate in at least a limited fashion Wednesday in the Chargers' first official practice of Week 8.

headline: McConkey (concussion) was spotted on the field in a no-contact jersey during the Chargers' bonus practice session Monday, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: After a Week 7 bye, the Chargers held an unofficial practice Monday as they begin prepping for a road matchup with the Rams next Sunday. Though the team won't have to release its first Week 8 injury report Wednesday, McConkey appears poised to be listed as at least a limited practice participant, which suggests that he's made some progress through the five-step concussion protocol. The wideout will look to practice fully by the end of the week and receive clearance from an independent neurologist in order to play against the Rams.

headline: McConkey won't return to Sunday's game at Kansas City due to a concussion.
story: McConkey was being evaluated for a possible head injury early in the second quarter before the Chargers quickly ruled him out. This follows a nearly three-week stretch in which he was dealing with a lingering foot issue that didn't allow him to log a snap in Week 4, despite being active. Now that he's subject to the concussion protocol, McConkey's next game action is up in the air.

headline: McConkey (foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chiefs, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: Quentin Johnston (chest) has also been cleared to play, while Tre' Harris (hamstring) has been ruled out. Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh declined to comment on playing-time expectations for Sunday, simply telling reporters, "I don't know," and "we'll see how it goes," when asked about McConkey and Johnston on Friday, per Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com. McConkey has been the No. 1 target when available, but Justin Herbert may not have time to look downfield behind an injury-ravaged offensive line.

headline: McConkey (foot) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: After being active but not playing in this past Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos, McConkey is in a better spot on the health front in Week 6. He's participated on a limited basis in the Chargers' first two practices of the week, and if he can maintain that level of activity of upgrade to full Friday, McConkey could head into Sunday's game against the Chiefs without an injury designation. Much like the other core members of a struggling Chargers offense, McConkey has gotten off to an underwhelming start to 2026 with a 12-183-1 receiving line on 17 targets through his four appearances.

headline: McConkey (foot) was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's injury report.
story: Head coach Jim Harbaugh revealed earlier Wednesday that McConkey would get some work in, and he was officially marked down with a limited tag. It's too early to tell if McConkey will take the field in Week 6, but his participation in Wednesday's session bodes well for his chances of doing so.

headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said McConkey (foot) will practice Wednesday, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: Though he was technically active for this past Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos, McConkey wasn't available after failing to practice in any fashion leading up to the contest. Now that he's poised to get back on the practice field Wednesday, McConkey should be in good position to reclaim his usual role as the team's No. 1 wideout this weekend in Kansas City, provided he has no setbacks in his recovery from the foot injury leading up to Sunday. McConkey's potential return is an important development while the Chargers contend with multiple injuries at receiver, as Tre' Harris (hamstring) exited the Week 5 loss early and Quentin Johnston (chest) and Brenen Thompson (quadriceps) were inactive for the game.

headline: McConkey (foot) was active but didn't play any snaps in Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos.
story: Initially labeled as week-to-week by head coach Jim Harbaugh at the beginning of Week 5 prep, McConkey didn't practice in any fashion Wednesday through Friday but was still listed as questionable heading into Sunday. Though he ultimately suited up against Denver, McConkey looks to have been active only in an emergency since the Chargers had two other wideouts (Quentin Johnston and Brenen Thompson) sitting out with more worrisome injuries. The Chargers' depth was further tested when Tre' Harris (hamstring) left Sunday's game early, resulting in the team finishing with just three healthy receivers. McConkey's practice activity will bear watching this week to determine whether he has a more legitimate chance at playing meaningful snaps next Sunday in Kansas City.

headline: McConkey (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Broncos, Eric Smith of the Chargers' officials site reports.
story: Following an aggravation of a foot injury last Sunday at Seattle, McConkey was held out of drills during Week 5 prep but still entered the weekend listed as questionable to suit up. Adam Schefter of ESPN then reported Sunday morning that McConkey wasn't slated to play, and while the wide receiver actually is in uniform, he isn't expected to have a significant role, per Schefter. If that comes to pass, Tre' Harris likely will serve as the No. 1 WR for QB Justin Herbert, while Marquez Valdes-Scantling, Derius Davis and Theo Wease are the other players available at the position aside from McConkey.

headline: McConkey (foot) isn't expected to play Sunday versus the Broncos, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: McConkey aggravated a foot injury in the third quarter of last Sunday's loss at Seattle and didn't log any on-field work in the meantime, but the Chargers still gave him a chance to suit up in Week 5 by tagging him as questionable. Despite the listing, he's likely to be included among the team's inactives once the list is posted about 90 minutes before a 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff. With fellow WRs Quentin Johnston (chest) and Brenen Thompson (quadriceps) already ruled out, Tre' Harris is expected to be L.A.'s top pass catcher Sunday, with Marquez Valdes-Scantling, Derius Davis and Theo Wease on hand for targets at the position.

headline: McConkey (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Denver, while teammate Quentin Johnston (chest) has been ruled out.
story: McConkey didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday and wasn't spotted by media at the start of Friday's session. The Chargers nonetheless are holding out hope he can play, potentially setting up a game-time decision ahead of a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff Sunday. Tre' Harris figures to play a lot of WR snaps for the Chargers even if McConkey is active, as the team's depth was depleted before the starters got injured.

headline: McConkey (foot) didn't practice Friday, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
story: With McConkey now missing practice throughout the week after coach Jim Harbaugh previously termed him week-to-week, it's looking like the wide receiver will miss Sunday's game against the Broncos. Look for Oronde Gadsden to see more action out of the slot for the Chargers, while Tre' Harris and Quentin Johnston (chest) continue to soak up the bulk of the wideout snaps.

headline: McConkey (foot) didn't practice Thursday.
story: McConkey dealt with a foot injury last week before attempting to play through it this past Sunday in Seattle. He eventually exited for good in the third quarter and hasn't practiced since then. Coach Jim Harbaugh termed McConkey "week-to-week" Monday, according to Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com, so it won't be a surprise if he's ruled out on the Chargers' final Week 5 injury report Friday.

headline: McConkey (foot) was a non-participant at Wednesday's practice.
story: McConkey attempted to play through a foot injury in Week 4, but when he exited this past Sunday's loss at Seattle in the third quarter, he had no catches among his two targets. Coach Jim Harbaugh told Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com on Monday that McConkey is "week-to-week," so his lack of activity to begin Week 5 prep lines up with that assessment. Friday's injury report ultimately may provide clarity on McConkey's status for Sunday's game against the Broncos.

headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said that McConkey (foot) is expected to be at practice Wednesday, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: Harbaugh didn't reveal what the extent of McConkey's participation might be, and it's possible that the wideout is limited to rehab work off to the side. McConkey has battled through a couple of injuries this season, the most recent being a foot issue that flared up in the third quarter of Sunday's loss to the Seahawks. The -0-4 Chargers have a critical game this weekend at home against the Broncos.

headline: McConkey (foot), per head coach Jim Harbaugh, is "week-to-week," Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports.
story: McConkey suited up for Sunday's loss to the Seahawks despite dealing with a foot injury throughout the week, but he was forced from the game with the same issue, and Harbaugh's comment Monday indicates he could miss some time. Another report -- via Kris Rhim of ESPN.com -- indicates McConkey may be more "day-to-day" than "week-to-week," but one way or another more will be known about McConkey's status when the Chargers next release an official injury report Wednesday. Should McConkey wind up sidelined, Quentin Johnston and Tre' Harris would presumably be Justin Herbert's clear top two options at the wideout spots.

headline: McConkey won't return to Sunday's contest at Seattle due to a foot injury.
story: McConkey may have aggravated the foot issue he tended to in advance of this game, but in any case he had no catches (on two targets) at the point of his departure in the third quarter. With the third-year pro ruled out Sunday, Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris, Marquez Valdes-Scantling and Derius Davis represent the Chargers' healthy available wide receivers for the rest of Week 4 action.

headline: McConkey (foot) is active for Sunday's game at Seattle, Eric Smith of the Chargers' official site reports.
story: McConkey had an interesting week, to say the least, which included sitting out Thursday's practice due to a foot injury and then being spotted with a visible limp afterward, according to Kris Rhim of ESPN.com. The third-year wide receiver sandwiched limited sessions around that absence, and after he entered the weekend as questionable for Week 4 action, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Sunday morning that McConkey was likely to play this weekend. Now that that's been confirmed, McConkey will look to build upon his 12-183-1 line on 15 targets in three contests to begin the campaign.

headline: McConkey (foot), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Seattle, is likely to suit up, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: McConkey was limited at Wednesday's session due to a foot injury and then didn't practice at Thursday, after which he was seen exhibiting a limp, per Kris Rhim of ESPN.com. McConkey again was limited Friday before drawing a questionable tag for Week 4 action. The current health concern isn't considered as serious as the rib issue he dealt with earlier this season, per Rapoport, so he should be good for his usual No. 1 WR role in the Chargers offense Sunday, assuming he's active.

headline: McConkey (foot) is questionable for Sunday's game against Seattle, Kris Rhim of ESPN.com reports.
story: McConkey missed practice Thursday but returned for Friday's light session, giving him a chance to suit up versus Seattle. With the Chargers still looking for their first win, having McConkey available would give them significantly better odds of beating the Seahawks. Playing through injuries already to begin the season, McConkey has 12 catches for 183 yards and one touchdown on a disappointing 15 targets. He's a fantasy WR2/3 at less than 100 percent in a struggling offense.

headline: McConkey (foot) is at practice Friday, Kris Rhim of ESPN reports.
story: After failing to practice Thursday and being seen leaving the locker room with a limp, McConkey's presence Friday is a positive sign for his chances of suiting up Sunday against the Seahawks. It's been a disappointing season for the Los Angeles offenses as a whole, and that includes McConkey, who has already dealt with rib and foot issues four weeks into the campaign.

headline: Omarion Hampton's Week 12 fantasy preview
story: Omarion Hampton's Week 12 fantasy preview

headline: Hampton carried the ball 14 times for 89 yards and caught his only target for four yards in Sunday's 27-24 loss to the Jets.
story: While he's still not seeing a consistent bell-cow workload, Hampton has turned his season around over the last three games, racking up 254 rushing yards and a TD while averaging 5.2 yards per carry. Keaton Mitchell left Sunday's game early with a knee injury, but his absence appeared to provide a bigger boost to Kimani Vidal, who wound up logging nine touches and 54 scrimmage yards. Hampton will look to keep rolling in Week 12 against the Patriots.

headline: Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel told reporters Friday that his "expectation" is that Hampton is the lead back for the Chargers, Omar Navarro of the team's official site reports.
story: "Generally, my expecation is [Hampton] is our leading ball carrier every week. ... I knew based on his last two practice weeks, we were feeling like he was going to have a breakout performance at any given time," McDaniel said Friday. That breakout game took place Monday against the Ravens, when Hampton turned 22 carries into a season-high 105 yards and a touchdown in a 23-20 win for the Chargers. With the Chargers getting extra time to rest, Hampton's stock is trending up heading into Week 12 against the Jets, whose defense ranks 30th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (135.3) and 29th in rushing touchdowns allowed (13).

headline: Hampton rushed 22 times for 105 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of two targets for no gain in the Chargers' 23-20 win over the Ravens on Monday night. He also fumbled once but recovered.
story: On the momentous occasion of the Chargers' long-awaited first win of the season, Hampton made a significant contribution with a season-high rushing yardage total. The performance also marked the first time Hampton eclipsed the century mark this season, and he added his fourth rushing touchdown of 2026 on a one-yard power run on fourth down on the first play following the two-minute warning in the first half. Hampton now is up to 474 rushing yards and a 12-63-0 receiving line heading into a Week 11 home matchup against the Jets on Sunday.

headline: Hampton rushed 13 times for 60 yards and wasn't targeted in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans.
story: Hampton worked as the Chargers' primary rushing option ahead of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal, who recorded seven carries apiece. The 0-8 Chargers unsurprisingly faced another negative game script, though, and Hampton wasn't involved in the passing game. The 2025 first-round pick continues to disappoint on a surprisingly awful offense that could get even worse should QB Justin Herbert (finger) miss any additional action after exiting in the fourth quarter. Hampton will try to snap a four-game touchdown drought in Week 10 against the Ravens.

headline: Hampton rushed nine times for 20 yards and brought in two of three targets for seven yards in the Chargers' 24-9 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
story: Hampton logged just one more carry than Kimani Vidal and five more than Keaton Mitchell, as the Chargers' ground game continued to resemble a committee scenario. Hampton now has 45 rushing yards or fewer in four straight games, and he's logged single-digit carries in three of those contests. The second-year back is averaging just 3.5 yards per carry behind an injury-hampered offensive line as well, leaving his outlook bleak for a Week 9 home matchup against an aggressive Texans defense next Sunday.

headline: Hampton rushed seven times for 18 yards and caught all four of his targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
story: The Chargers continued to deloy an ineffective backfield rotation, as Hampton got 11 touches compared to 10 for Kimani Vidal and two for Keaton Mitchell. None of the three running backs exceeded 3.0 yards per carry while QB Justin Herbert led the team with 26 rushing yards. Hampton has been trending in the wrong direction, with his rushing yardage dropping with each subsequent game since a 94-yard performance on the ground in Week 2 against the Raiders. He'll look to reverse that trend in Week 8 against the Rams following a Week 7 bye.

headline: Hampton turned 14 carries into 33 yards and one target into a six-yard catch during Sunday's 23-17 loss to the Broncos.
story: Hampton has found room to run in the Chargers' mostly stagnant offense difficult to come by so far this season, averaging 3.7 YPC through five games after going for 4.4 as a rookie in 2025. On Sunday in particular, he had to contend with fellow RBs Kimani Vidal (nine touches) and Keaton Mitchell (six) mixing into the action a decent amount. Due to ceding those reps to his backfield mates, Hampton's weekly ceiling doesn't appear to be as high as it may have seemed heading into the campaign.

headline: Hampton had nine carries for 45 yards and one touchdown and two catches (on two targets) for eight yards during Sunday's 30-23 loss at Seattle.
story: Hampton failed to reach 10 rushes in a game for the first time in four opportunities this season, and he ceded a number of backfield reps to position mates Keaton Mitchell (15 touches for 63 yards) and Kimani Vidal (seven touches, 36 yards and one TD). It's unclear if the Chargers intend to keep up more of a timeshare between the trio moving forward, but Hampton's lack of targets (five) so far in 2026 inhibit his overall value if he isn't taking on a majority of the rushing workload. His next chance to take the field arrives next Sunday versus the Broncos.

headline: Pipkins (knee) is active for Sunday's matchup against the Jets.
story: Pipkins had been on IR since late September before being activated Saturday. The veteran offensive lineman is now set to give the Chargers' offensive line a boost. Pipkins may work in a rotational role, as Logan Taylor is "locked in" at left guard, per Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com.

headline: The Chargers activated Pipkins (knee) from injured reserve Saturday.
story: Pipkins is still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Jets, but his activation from injured reserve is a good sign for his availability. If he's cleared to play, then he would likely reclaim his starting role at left guard. Pipkins landed on IR in mid-September due to a knee injury.

headline: Pipkins (knee) won't be available for Monday's game against the Ravens after the Chargers didn't activate him from injured reserve.
story: Pipkins has been sidelined since Week 1, but he had his 21-day practice window opened Thursday and was listed as questionable heading into Monday. Assuming he can continue practicing in Week 11 without issue, Pipkins could be activated ahead of the Chargers' next game Nov. 22 versus the Jets. Once reinstated, Pipkins could settle back in as the team's starting left guard.

headline: Pipkins (knee), who is on injured reserve, has been deemed questionable for Monday's matchup against the Ravens.
story: Pipkins hasn't played since Week 1 due to a knee injury. He was placed on IR in late September and had his 21-day practice window opened this past Thursday. The Chargers will need to activate Pipkins from injured reserve in order for him to be eligible to suit up Monday.

headline: The Chargers designated Pipkins (knee) to return from injured reserve Thursday, Omar Navarro of the team's official site reports.
story: Pipkins has been on injured reserve since late September due to a knee injury. He's opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back DNPs, so it's unlikely that he'll be activated from IR ahead of Monday's game against the Ravens.

headline: Klare played 52 snaps (43 on offense, nine on special teams) but didn't show up in the box score otherwise during the Rams' 26-13 win over the Packers on Wednesday.
story: Klare's 43 offensive snaps were second most among Rams tight ends behind Colby Parkinson (65) and ahead of Tyler Higbee (40). Klare, a second-round selection of the Rams in the 2026 NFL Draft, has yet to draw a target this season, although he could see more involvement in the passing game over the coming weeks since Davis Allen is expected to miss multiple games due to a high-ankle sprain.

headline: Klare went without a target while playing four of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
story: Klare has been a healthy inactive on three occasions this season, but he's now suited up in three straight games while the Rams have been short on pass-catching options due to injuries to tight end Terrance Ferguson (hamstring/ankle) and wideouts Puka Nacua (knee), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Jordan Whittington (back). Despite those personnel losses, Klare has still struggled to carve out meaningful playing time, as fellow tight ends Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen are all regarded as superior blockers and have been prioritized ahead of him. The rookie second-round pick out of Ohio State still has yet to draw a target through his first seven NFL games.

headline: Murray suffered a torn Achilles in Wednesday's win over the Packers, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: The 29-year-old offensive lineman made his first career start against Green Bay but was injured in the second half after playing 56 of 75 offensive snaps. Justin Dedich came in to replace Murray at left guard.

headline: Murray (leg) exited the Rams' locker room in a walking boot and on crutches following Wednesday's 26-13 victory over Green Bay, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
story: Murray limped to the locker room early in the fourth quarter and never returned. Head coach Sean McVay didn't mention Murray's status following the win, but it sounds like he may be dealing with a more-than-minor injury. That would further deplete a Los Angeles offensive line that has been without starting left guard Steve Avila (hamstring) since he was hurt Week 9.

headline: Allen is dealing with a high-ankle sprain, according to sources, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Allen was injured in the second quarter of Wednesday's win over the Packers. The Rams are still evaluating the extent of Allen's injury, but Rapoport mentions that high-ankle sprains are typically accompanied by recovery timelines of 4-to-6 weeks, so Allen is looking exceedingly unlikely to be available for the Rams' next game next Thursday against the Chiefs.

headline: Allen (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Wednesday night's game against the Packers.
story: The tight end was injured in the second quarter, so rookie Max Klare will need to play increased snaps as the TE3 in a Rams offense that uses more three-tight end sets than any team in the league. Prior to leaving, Allen caught a pair of passes for 14 yards.

headline: Allen (ankle) is questionable to return to Wednesday's game against the Packers, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: The tight end was rolled up on a run play in the second quarter but was able to stay in the game and finish out the drive, which ended with a Kyren Williams touchdown run. Prior to leaving, Allen caught two passes for 14 yards on a pair of targets. Max Klare will need to step into more snaps behind Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson if Allen can't return.

headline: Allen caught his lone target for a 19-yard touchdown in Sunday's win over the Cardinals.
story: With all three of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) out, the Rams leaned on their tight-end triumvirate of Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Allen, as all three played more offensive snaps than any of the Los Angeles wideouts. Parkinson (53 snaps) led the way, followed by Allen (52) and Higbee (51), and both Allen and Higbee caught touchdowns. Allen, however, ran just six routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks, so it's not enough to warrant consideration in fantasy leagues.

headline: Allen (oblique) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Allen has recovered enough from the oblique injury he suffered during the Rams' Week 9 win over the Commanders to suit up for Week 10. The No. 3 tight end is a key part of the Rams' 13-personnel offense, and he should continue seeing a significant share of offensive snaps for the team.

headline: Allen (oblique) is questionable for Sunday's game against Arizona, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Allen put together an LP-DNP-LP practice log during Week 10 prep while managing an oblique injury, which he likely picked up during the Rams' Week 9 win over the Commanders. If he cannot play Sunday, then Max Klare would operate as the team's TE3 behind Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson. Allen's status may not be officially known until about 90 minutes before the 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff, when the Rams announce their list of inactive players.

headline: Allen (oblique) did not participate at practice Thursday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Allen popped up on the Rams' injury report Wednesday with an oblique issue, and now his availability for Week 10 appears to be in serious jeopardy. With teammates Tyler Higbee (illness), Colby Parkinson (ribs) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) also dealing with health concerns, rookie second-rounder Max Klare currently seems to be the only Rams tight end who is a lock to suit up for Sunday's game at Arizona.

headline: Allen caught four of five targets for 20 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
story: With Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (ankle) sidelined for the Rams, Allen was thrust into an elevated role on offense for Los Angeles. He ended up running just 12 routes on Matthew Stafford's 32 dropbacks but made the most of his chances, particularly in the red zone, where Allen caught three- and five-yard touchdowns in the first half. Allen's volume of routes isn't enough to make him a reliable fantasy option moving forward.

headline: Allen (foot) does not have an injury designation against the Cardinals on Sunday, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
story: A foot injury prevented Allen from practicing Wednesday or Thursday, but his limited participation Friday was enough for him to fade an injury tag for Sunday's NFC West clash. The fourth-year pro has six catches (on nine targets) for 63 yards through five regular-season games.

headline: Allen was listed as a non-participant Wednesday on the Rams' estimated injury report due to a foot injury, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Allen reeled in both of his targets for 24 yards during Monday's 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills, and he may have picked up the foot injury at some point along the way. The 25-year-old will have two more chances to practice prior to Sunday's contest versus Arizona.

headline: Higbee (chest) is considered week-to-week, though it's too early to tell if he may be available Thursday, Dec. 3, against the Chiefs, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports Friday.
story: Higbee and Davis Allen (ankle) were both injured during Wednesday's win over the Packers. Allen likely is facing a multi-week absence due to a high-ankle sprain, but Higbee still has a chance to avoid missing additional action. Colby Parkinson and Max Klare are the only healthy TE options remaining the Rams' active roster.

headline: Higbee exited Wednesday's game against the Packers with a chest injury and will not return, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: With Higbee forced out during the contest after Davis Allen (ankle) was injured earlier in the game, the Rams have only two healthy tight ends left. Colby Parkinson and Max Klare will play virtually every offensive snap the rest of the way for Los Angeles. Prior to leaving, Higbee caught one of three targets for 14 yards.

headline: Higbee caught three of four targets for 17 yards and a touchdown during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Higbee's third and final catch of Sunday's game came late in the second quarter, with the veteran tight end connecting with Matthew Stafford for a five-yard touchdown to give the Rams a 10-6 lead. It was the second touchdown of the season for Higbee, with his first taking place in Week 3 against the Broncos. He's been held to three catches or fewer in each of his last four games, although he's been on the field for at least 50 offensive snaps in three of those contests. The Rams are on bye for Week 11, and Higbee's limited target share will take a hit if Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

headline: Higbee (illness) and Colby Parkinson (rib) have both been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, while fellow tight end Davis Allen (oblique) is listed as questionable, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: With wideout Puka Nacua (knee) placed on injured reserve this week, there's renewed fantasy interest in the Rams' tight ends. Higbee has run a lot of routes without providing production in recent games, but both he and Parkinson could see more targets over the next few weeks, including Sunday in a favorable matchup with Arizona's subpar pass defense.

headline: Higbee didn't practice Wednesday due to an illness, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: With Higbee's addition to the Rams' Week 10 injury report Thursday, the team's top three tight ends on the active roster are dealing with health concerns, as Colby Parkinson has been limited by a rib injury, while Davis Allen downgraded from limited Wednesday to no activity one day later due to an oblique issue. As a result, Friday's practice report will be telling for who among the trio may be available Sunday in Arizona.

headline: Higbee caught one of five targets for 13 yards during Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
story: Higbee was held to just one catch for a second consecutive game, although his 13-yard grab set the Rams up on the Commanders' one yard line and led to a rushing touchdown by Blake Corum on the next play. Higbee has only four catches over his last three games, but he figures to play a larger role in the passing game for at least the next month while Puka Nacua (knee/toe) is on injured reserve. The Rams will hit the road for Week 10 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up six touchdowns to opposing tight ends this season, which ranks 25th in the NFL.

headline: Higbee caught one of two targets for 14 yards against the Chargers in Sunday's 24-9 victory.
story: Higbee logged a hearty 83 percent offensive snap share, most among Rams tight ends. However, he got little attention from quarterback Matthew Stafford, recording just two targets. Higbee had a nice run in Weeks 3-5, when he logged 18 catches for 212 yards across the three-game span. However, since then he's posted just seven receptions for 50 yards across his subsequent three contests. As such, it's hard to trust Higbee on a week-to-week basis right now even with the Rams down multiple pass catchers in Davante Adams (hamstring - IR), Terrance Ferguson (ankle - IR) and Colby Parkinson (ribs).

headline: Higbee caught two of three targets for 14 yards during Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
story: Higbee was expected to have a chance to see an increase in production with wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) unavailable, but the tight end put together a disappointing performance. Fellow tight ends Colby Parkinson (5-48-0) and Davis Allen (4-20-2) had more impressive days, and it may be hard to predict which of the three will be the go-to option any given week until Terrance Ferguson (ankle) returns from injured reserve.

headline: Higbee caught all four of his targets for 22 yards during the Rams' 18-16 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Higbee was not targeted by Matthew Stafford until early in the fourth quarter, but the former fumbled the ball on his first catch of the game, which was recovered by the Cardinals defense. Higbee saw three more passes from Stafford in the quarter, and Sunday's effort snapped his three-game streak of 60-plus yards and five-plus catches. However, the Rams are expected to be without Davante Adams (hamstring) until at least after the Week 11 bye, so Higbee could be Stafford's secondary target in the passing game behind Puka Nacua for the next few games. The Rams hit the road for Week 7 on Oct. 25 against the Raiders, whose defense gives up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to tight ends this season.

headline: Higbee brought in five of six targets for 83 yards in the Rams' 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night.
story: Higbee finished a distant second in receiving yards to Puka Nacua for the Rams on the night, but the figure was a season high for the veteran tight end. After a forgettable two-game stretch to open the season, Higbee has taken the lead in Los Angeles' crowded tight-end room over the last three games by posting an 18-212-1 line on 23 targets. Higbee should have a good chance of retaining a solid complementary role in a Week 6 home divisional clash against the suspect Cardinals defense on Sunday.

headline: Higbee caught five of six targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Eagles.
story: Higbee was the Rams' TE1 for a second consecutive week due to the absence of Colby Parkinson (shoulder/knee). Even with superstar wide receiver Puka Nacua back from a two-game absence, Higbee still finished Sunday's game tied for the second-most receiving yards on the Rams, and his six targets were fourth-most behind Kyren Williams (13), Nacua (12) and Davante Adams (nine). After a quiet start to the season, Higbee has a 13-129-1 line on 17 targets over his last two games. He may have shown enough to warrant an established role in the Rams offense moving forward, even if Parkinson is cleared to return for Week 5 against the Bills.

headline: McManus made all four of his field-goal tries and both of his point-after attempts Thursday in a 26-13 victory over Green Bay.
story: McManus scored the first six points of the game with 43-yard and 41-yard field goals in the first quarter. He added a 40-yarder in the fourth and a 30-yarder just before the end of the game. The veteran kicker has yet to try a field goal from 50-plus yards, but he's been everything the Rams could have asked for since taking over as the team's kicker in Week 7. Through five games, McManus is a perfect 9-for-9 on FG attempts and 16-for-16 on PAT tries.

headline: McManus made both of his field-goal attempts and all four PATs in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: McManus' Sunday performance extends his perfect streak with a Rams' special teams unit that desperately needed consistency at kicker. He's now 5-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 14-for-14 on PATs after five regular-season contests as a Ram in 2026.

headline: McManus made both of his field-goal tries and both PATs in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
story: McManus' field goals were good from 33 and 20 yards, and he's now made all 13 of his kicks through three games with Los Angeles. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) now out for the foreseeable future, this offense figures to struggle to score points, downgrading McManus in the fantasy kicker rankings.

headline: McManus converted his sole field-goal attempt and all three PATs in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: While Joshua Karty handled kickoffs for the Rams, McManus was entrusted with field goals and extra-point tries. The kicker's first field-goal attempt with his new team was a 30-yarder, so the veteran player has not yet been challenged as a Ram.

headline: McManus did not attempt a field goal and went 5-for-5 on extra-point tries during Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
story: McManus signed with Los Angeles this week after Blake Grupe (knee) was placed on injured reserve. The kicker wasn't tested much Sunday, but he was able to avoid making any mistakes. McManus may have a chance to attempt his first field goal as a member of the Rams in Week 8 against the Chargers.

headline: McManus is slated to sign with the Rams, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: With Blake Grupe having landed on IR, the Rams are bringing McManus in to fill the void at kicker ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders. McManus represents an option for those who had rostered Grupe or are otherwise looking for kicking help ahead of Week 7, when four teams will be on bye.

headline: The Rams will work out McManus on Tuesday, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: McManus will compete with fellow veteran kicker Matt Prater for the Rams' placekicker job following the season-ending injury to Blake Grupe (knee) in Week 6. McManus appeared in 14 regular-season games for the Packers in 2025, converting 24 of 30 field-goal attempts and 32 of 33 PATs.

headline: Daniels did not draw a target or log a touch Wednesday in a 26-13 win against the Packers.
story: After posting a career-high 61 percent offensive snap share in Week 10 against Arizona, Daniels logged just a 22 percent share Wednesday. That was still good for third among Rams wideouts behind Konata Mumpfield (90 percent) and Xavier Smith (23 percent), but Daniels didn't get a pass thrown his way. If Davante Adams (hamstring) is able to return to action in Week 13 against the Chiefs on Thursday, Dec. 3, Daniels' prospects for making an impact in the passing game will likely fall even further.

headline: Daniels caught one of two targets for 22 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
story: With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) inactive, Daniels' 46 snaps were two fewer than Konata Mumpfield for the team lead at receiver for the Rams. Mumpfield led the group in targets (four), catches (three) and yards (81), and only Xavier Smith (2-40-1) joined him as wide receivers to catch more than one pass from Matthew Stafford against Arizona while the Rams relied heavily on their tight ends and running backs. Daniels' playing time isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

headline: Head coach Sean McVay said Friday that Daniels "will get an opportunity to play more snaps moving forward," Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
story: Daniels has seen minimal playing time this season, but he'll be thrust into a more prominent role offensively due to both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being on injured reserve. As such, Daniels -- a sixth-round selection of the Rams in the 2026 NFL Draft -- is slated to serve as the team's WR3 behind Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, with Xavier Smith and Brennan Presley also in the mix for snaps on offense. During his final college season in Miami, Daniels recorded 50 catches for 557 yards and seven touchdowns across 13 games.

headline: Atwell didn't log a touch or target Wednesday in a 26-13 victory over Green Bay.
story: Atwell logged just six offensive snaps, behind all of fellow wideouts Konata Mumpfield (70), Xavier Smith (18) and CJ Daniels (17). The Rams also gave more offensive snaps to four different tight ends. Atwell's usage is especially notable given that both Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) didn't play. Nacua is out for the season, but Adams could return as soon as Week 13 versus Kansas City. Atwell is not an advised fantasy play moving forward even if Adams has to miss more contests.

headline: Atwell caught one of two targets for 31 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
story: Despite both Puka Nacua (toe/knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) being sidelined, Atwell still played just 16 of 76 offensive snaps versus Arizona and ran 15 routes on Matthew Stafford's 28 dropbacks. Atwell played behind both Konata Mumpfield and CJ Daniels at receiver for Los Angeles.

headline: Atwell recorded two catches on five targets for 16 yards during the Rams' 20-13 win over the Commanders on Sunday.
story: Atwell ended up finishing second among Rams wide receivers in both targets and offensive snaps behind Puka Nacua. However, the Rams' offense will have to undergo a sizable overhaul in the absence of Nacua, who suffered a sprained PCL/MCL in his knee as well as turf toe during Sunday's win, with the superstar wide receiver expected to be sidelined for at least a month while on injured reserve, per Sarah Bishop of ESPN.com. Davante Adams (hamstring) is also on injured reserve, so that leaves Atwell and Konata Mumpfield as the top healthy wide receivers on the Rams' 53-man roster, and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels is also in position for a larger role on offense. The Rams will face the Cardinals in Week 10, and Arizona's defense has given up 19 passing touchdowns on the year, which is second-most in the league behind Las Vegas' 20.

headline: Atwell wasn't targeted in Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
story: With Davante Adams (hamstring) out, Atwell was active and played 25 offensive snaps. He ran 20 routes on Matthew Stafford's 32 dropbacks, tying Konata Mumpfield for second on the team behind Puka Nacua's 31, but Atwell was just doing cardio out there. He's not a reliable fantasy target, even with Adams injured.

headline: Atwell (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Atwell is a healthy scratch for Sunday's contest. Puka Nacua, Davante Adams, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and Alex Bachman are the five active receivers over Atwell.

headline: Smith gained 11 yards on two carries and caught his only target for four yards in a 26-13 win against Green Bay on Wednesday. He added 15 yards on his lone punt return.
story: Smith was used as a ball carrier for the first time this season and gained a chunk of yards on each of his totes. Aside from that, it was another quiet game for the third-year wideout, who hasn't really been able to take advantage of a wide open WR pecking order in the wake of injuries to star wideouts Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring). In fact, Smith has logged less than a 25 percent offensive snap share over the past two games with the pair of stud WRs absent, so it appears head coach Sean McVay is looking elsewhere to fill the void. As such, Smith doesn't have much fantasy value given that his primary role is in the return game.

headline: Smith caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
story: With the Rams down both Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) for the first time this season, Smith operated as the fourth receiver against Arizona, playing nine of 76 offensive snaps. His 22-yard touchdown in the second quarter was the first of Smith's career. Based on his small amount of playing time and routes run, Smith's 12-point PPR day isn't worth chasing in fantasy.

headline: The Rams signed Smith off the 49ers' practice squad Tuesday.
story: Smith had been with the Rams early in the campaign before being waived Oct. 2. He subsequently signed with San Francisco's practice squad, where he had resided until Los Angeles brought him back into the fold Tuesday. Smith drew just one target (which he didn't catch) across 80 offensive snaps over his three games with the Rams in the early portion of the season, but he could immediately factor into the mix for the next several weeks, as Davante Adams (hamstring) is still on IR, Puka Nacua (knee) is slated to miss several weeks and Jordan Whittington (back) landed on injured reserve Tuesday. Smith could also be used as a returner in Whittington's absence.

headline: The 49ers signed Smith to the practice squad Wednesday.
story: Smith was cut by the Rams on Friday, but the Florida A&M product will stay in the NFC West division with the 49ers as a member of the practice squad. Smith would be a top candidate for an elevation to the active roster if the 49ers needed more depth at wide receiver.

headline: The Rams waived Smith on Friday.
story: Smith played 38 offensive snaps and ran 32 routes last Sunday night against the Broncos but wasn't targeted by Matthew Stafford and has drawn just one target on 60 routes through three weeks. He's also returned seven punts for 69 yards and seven kicks for 144 yards.

headline: Rivers returned four kickoffs for 102 yards and did not log a snap on offense in Wednesday's 26-13 victory over the Packers.
story: The Rams stuffed the ball down the throat of Green Bay's defense, especially late, and ended up with a combined 241 yards on 47 rushes. However, Rivers didn't get a single one of those totes or even a snap on offense. The veteran running back logged season highs with 15 carries and 81 yards against Arizona in Week 10, but all of that work came in garbage time. It appears Rivers isn't going to be a factor outside of his return duties while both Kyren Williams and Blake Corum are healthy.

headline: Rivers rushed 15 times for 81 yards in Sunday's 34-6 win over the Cardinals.
story: Amazingly, all 15 of Rivers' carries came on the Rams' final drive of the game, where they ran 17 plays to kill the final 12 minutes and 15 seconds of the clock. Rivers rushed 15 straight times before Matthew Stafford performed a pair of kneel-downs to end the game. It will be interesting to see if Rivers' efficiency was enough to earn him more carries before garbage time moving forward, especially after Kyren Williams looked stuck in the mud against Arizona, rushing 12 times for just 23 yards. For now, Rivers is simply a name to keep an eye on over the next couple of weeks, with the Rams wanting to lean on the run due to all of their high-profile pass-catching injuries.

headline: The Rams activated Rivers (calf) from injured reserve Saturday.
story: Rivers missed six games while on injured reserve with a calf injury he sustained in the Rams' Week 2 loss to the Giants. The 27-year-old has returned ahead of Sunday's game against the Commanders and has no injury designation headed into the contest. Rivers will likely be a special-teams contributor with no real role in the Rams' offense.

headline: Rivers (calf) does not have a designation for Sunday's clash against the Commanders, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Rivers suffered a calf injury against the Giants in Week 2 and was placed on IR soon thereafter. He was designated to return to practice this Wednesday and logged a trio of full sessions. Rivers' lack of a designation for Sunday's game suggests he has a legitimate chance of playing, but Los Angeles will need to activate him from injured reserve Saturday in order for that to happen.

headline: Rivers (calf) was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
story: Rivers made his return to practice Wednesday, operating as a full participant at the team's first session of the week, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports. The running back has been on injured reserve since late September after suffering a calf injury in Week 2 against the Giants, but he could be back in action as soon as Sunday versus the Commanders.

headline: Parkinson caught both of his targets for minus-1 yard in a 26-13 victory over the Packers on Wednesday.
story: Parkinson logged a hefty 83 percent offensive snap count, highest among Los Angeles tight ends. His two receptions also tied for the team lead among players at the position, but he couldn't do much with those catches, gaining just one yard on the first and losing two yards on the second. However, Parkinson could take on an even more important role moving forward, as Tyler Higbee (chest) and Davis Allen (ankle) both left Wednesday's win early and didn't return. If neither of those players is ready to suit up in Week 13 against Kansas City on Thursday, Dec. 3, Parkinson and untested rookie Max Klare would lead a tight-end corps that quarterback Matthew Stafford typically looks to often.

headline: Parkinson caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Parkinson was able to shed an injury designation for Sunday's game after having his practice reps limited during Week 10 prep due to a lingering rib injury. His second catch of the contest went for 10 yards early in the third quarter and set the Rams up on the 1-yard line, with Blake Corum finding the end zone on the next play. Parkinson was on the field for 53 of the Rams' 76 offensive snaps (69.7 percent), and fellow tight ends Davis Allen (52) and Tyler Higbee (51) were not far behind. The Rams are committed to using their 13-man personnel, although the game plan could be slightly tweaked after the Week 11 bye if wide receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) is activated from injured reserve ahead of Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. Parkinson has caught 20 passes (on 25 targets) for 127 yards and a touchdown through eight regular-season games.

headline: Parkinson (ribs) and Tyler Higbee (illness) have been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Cardinals, while fellow tight end Davis Allen (oblique) is listed as questionable, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Parkinson hasn't shown much hint of matching last year's TD-fueled fantasy production, but he could see more targets in the coming weeks with both Puka Nacua (knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on injured reserve. Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell are the favorites for WR snaps, likely leaving the RBs and TEs to handle a larger-than-usual portion of Matthew Stafford's targets. Of course, the Rams will probably want to run the ball more often while their top receiving weapons are sidelined.

headline: Parkinson (ribs) was limited at Thursday's practice, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: While Parkinson continues to operate with a cap on his practice reps due to the rib issue that sidelined him in Week 8 against the Chargers, fellow TE Tyler Higbee showed up on Thursday's injury report as a DNP due to an illness, and reserve option Davis Allen went from limited Wednesday to no activity one day later. Friday's practice report will unveil the odds of each player to suit up Sunday at Arizona.

headline: Parkinson (ribs) was limited in Wednesday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Parkinson has seemingly been banged up all season, and the ribs are just the latest issue for the tight end. With Puka Nacua (knee/toe), Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (hamstring) vacating more than 45 percent of the Rams' targets, Los Angeles figures to lean heavily on its tight ends to try and get by without its top two receivers and top pass-catching tight end. Parkinson and Tyler Higbee will likely have prominent every-down roles in the coming weeks.

headline: Parkinson notched four catches for 13 yards on four targets in a 20-13 win over Washington on Sunday.
story: Parkinson ranked second on Los Angeles in receptions, though he didn't turn them into many yards. Still, it was his third straight contest with at least four catches, so Parkinson looks to be developing into a favorite target of QB Matthew Stafford. That could come in handy in Week 10 and beyond, as Stafford is going to need to turn to other pass catchers to help make up for the massive production being lost in the absence of Puka Nacua, who is expected to land on IR due to knee and turf-toe injuries.

headline: Parkinson (ribs) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
story: Parkinson, who was inactive in Week 8, managed to log a limited practice Friday, before being listed as questionable for the contest. With Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) -- who was initially slated to return to action this week but subsequently ruled out -- still not in the mix, the return of Parkinson, who has caught five passes in each of the last two games he played, is a welcome boost to a Rams TE corps that also includes Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and Max Klare.

headline: Parkinson (ribs) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: The veteran tight end managed to get in a limited practice Friday, keeping the door open for him to play after missing last Sunday's game against the Chargers. Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was initially slated to return to action this week, but was subsequently ruled out, so the status of Parkinson -- who has caught five passes in each of the last two games he played -- is worth monitoring.
