headline: Parkinson (ribs) remained sidelined for Thursday's practice, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
story: Parkinson hasn't practiced since being injured in Week 7, and he looks headed for a possible second straight absence. With Terrance Ferguson (ankle) looking like he has a chance to return from injured reserve Sunday against the Commanders, it could be Ferguson, Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen handling tight-end duties.

headline: Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Wednesday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Parkinson missed the Week 8 win over the Chargers and remains sidelined for the start of Week 9 prep. Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was back at practice Wednesday and could join Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen at tight end if Parkinson is unable to face the Commanders on Sunday.

headline: Parkinson (ribs) is inactive for Sunday's Week 8 matchup against the Chargers.
story: The veteran tight end has endured an injury-plagued season, and his current ribs issue cost him the first two practices of the week before he managed a limited session Friday. The injury will also lead to Parkinson's second absence of the campaign, and in his stead, Tyler Higbee should be in line for a slight increase in snaps and targets, although fourth-year tight end Davis Allen, who logged a season-high 50 snaps in Week 7 against the Raiders and recorded a pair of touchdown catches, will also stand to be a beneficiary.

headline: Parkinson (ribs) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
story: Parkinson has been banged up seemingly all season, first dealing with shoulder and knee injuries before a ribs issue this week. Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen would be set to handle most of the tight-end duties for the Rams if Parkinson is unable to play, and rookie Max Klare could even see some action on offense.

headline: Parkinson (ribs) didn't practice Thursday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Parkinson has now missed the first two days of Week 8 prep, so his status for Sunday's matchup against the Chargers is looking quite precarious. He'll likely need to practice in some capacity Friday to have a chance of suiting up this weekend. Rams QB Matthew Stafford peppered his tight-end corps with 14 targets in Week 7 in the absence of wideout Davante Adams (hamstring), so Parkinson's absence would be felt by the team's offense if he can't play. Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen could be set for a bump in targets if that's the case.

headline: Parkinson did not participate in Wednesday's practice due to a rib injury, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: Parkinson may have picked up the injury during the Rams' 35-21 win over the Raiders in Week 7, when he caught five of six targets for 48 yards. He'll have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's game against the Chargers. Terrance Ferguson (ankle) will remain on IR for Week 8, so if Parkinson cannot play, then Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen would serve as the Rams' top tight ends.

headline: Parkinson caught five of six targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
story: With Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (ankle) both out and injured for Los Angeles, Parkinson's six targets were second on the team behind Puka Nacua's 10. The tight end ran just 14 routes on Matthew Stafford's 32 dropbacks, but Los Angeles used multiple tight ends, led by Tyler Higbee's 18 routes. Parkinson is more of a touchdown-or-bust fringe TE1/2 headed into Week 8 against the Chargers.

headline: Parkinson caught five of six targets for 31 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Cardinals.
story: The tight end's six targets tied Kyren Williams for second on the team behind Puka Nacua's seven on a day the Rams couldn't move the ball. Parkinson entered Sunday with four catches for 24 yards on seven targets. He can largely be ignored in fantasy football as the Rams' main blocking tight end.

headline: Parkinson (shoulder) doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Parkinson continues to deal with the shoulder injury he originally sustained in Week 3 against Denver. After missing Week 4, the tight end was able to return for last Monday night's overtime loss to the Bills, logging 64.6 percent of the offensive snaps. He secured just one pass for three yards on two targets and isn't in the fantasy football conversation, with Tyler Higbee dominating the pass-game looks.

headline: Parkinson (shoulder) was a limited participant at practice Thursday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Parkinson was able to play through his shoulder injury in Week 5 versus the Bills, but it still appears to be bothering him as Sunday's game versus the Cardinals approaches. He'll now look to repeat what he did a week ago and upgrade to full participation at practice Friday and avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Parkinson (shoulder) was listed as a limited participant on the Rams' estimated injury report Wednesday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Parkinson played 53 snaps on offense during Monday night's 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills, reeling in one of two targets for three yards. The tight end was limited at each of the team's first two practices last week before logging a full session Friday, and he appears to be potentially on track to do the same thing prior to Week 6. Parkinson will have two more opportunities to officially practice before Sunday's matchup with Arizona.

headline: Parkinson (shoulder/knee) practiced fully Friday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Coach Sean McVay told Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site on Thursday that the Rams plan to increase Parkinson's activity level as the week goes on. Indeed, Parkinson followed up a limited session with an uncapped one a day later, meaning he'll miss just one contest as a result of shoulder and knee injuries. Parkinson, Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and Max Klare are the team's current healthy tight ends with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) on injured reserve.

headline: Parkinson (shoulder/knee) was limited in Thursday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: While Parkinson was limited to begin the week, coach Sean McVay said the plan is to ramp the tight end up throughout the week and have him available Monday night against the Bills, according to Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site. Parkinson missed last Sunday's win over the Eagles. With Terrance Ferguson (ankle) still on IR, Parkinson would allow Tyler Higbee to focus on pass-catching duties at the position.

headline: Parkinson (shoulder/knee) is inactive for Sunday's Week 4 matchup against the Eagles.
story: The veteran tight end took a questionable tag into the weekend after missing practice all week, and Parkinson's inactive status has now been confirmed. While he tends to his pair of injuries and targets a return for a Monday night, Oct. 12 home showdown with the Bills in Week 5, Parkinson's snaps and targets are expected to be absorbed by Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and rookie second-round pick Max Klare, the Rams' three remaining healthy tight ends with Terrance Ferguson (ankle, IR) also unavailable.

headline: Parkinson (shoulder/knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
story: Parkinson will not practice Friday and will log three DNPs for the week, but the Rams are leaving the light on for him to play Week 4, especially after Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was already ruled out for the contest. If Parkinson can't go, Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen would be in line for substantial roles, and rookie Max Klare could even see some action on offense.

headline: Parkinson (knee/shoulder) remained sidelined at Thursday's practice, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: In addition to the shoulder injury he suffered last Sunday against Denver, Parkinson is still battling through a knee issue. If neither he nor Terrance Ferguson (ankle) are able to play Sunday against the Eagles, the Rams will need to lean on Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and rookie Max Klare at tight end.

headline: Head coach Sean McVay said Parkinson (shoulder) will not practice Wednesday, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
story: Parkinson is considered day-to-day after injuring his shoulder in last Sunday night's loss to the Broncos. With Terrance Ferguson (ankle) also not practicing Wednesday, the Rams could be looking at Tyler Higbee, Davis Allen and rookie Max Klare handling tight-end duties in Week 4 against the Eagles.

headline: Mumpfield brought in four of five targets for 69 yards in the Rams' 26-13 win over the Packers on Wednesday night.
story: Mumpfield set the pace in receiving yards for the Rams while also sharing the team lead in both receptions and targets. The 2025 seventh-round pick has now posted back-to-back productive games -- he had a 3-81-0 line in the Week 10 win over the Cardinals -- but Wednesday's performance could have been even more rewarding had an apparent two-yard touchdown grab just before the halfway point of the third quarter not been ruled incomplete on replay. Mumpfield should retain a solid No. 2 role even if Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) returns for a Week 13 home matchup against the Chiefs on Thursday, Dec. 3, and the former will retain his No. 1 standing if his star teammate remains sidelined.

headline: The Rams are expected to lean more on Mumpfield and the rest of the team's wide receivers in the absence of Puka Nacua (knee/toe), the latter of whom is expected to be sidelined for the remainder of the regular season, Nate Atkins and Jonathan Jones of The Athletic report.
story: Nacua is expected to miss "a couple of months" after undergoing surgery Tuesday to repair his MCL, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. With Nacua and Davante Adams (hamstring, IR) sidelined for Week 10 against the Cardinals, Mumpfield operated as the Rams' WR1 for that contest and finished with three catches (on four targets) for 81 yards in a 34-6 win for Los Angeles. The Rams are "hopeful" that Adams will return soon, but if he's not activated from injured reserve ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers, then Mumpfield would lead Los Angeles' wide receiver group that also includes Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith.

headline: Mumpfield brought in three of four targets for 81 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: With Puka Nacua (knee/toe) and Davante Adams (hamstring) on injured reserve, Mumpfield operated as the de facto No. 1 receiver for Matthew Stafford. Mumpfield met the moment with a team-high receiving yardage total that more than doubled that of the next-closest pass catcher, Xavier Smith (40 yards). The 2025 seventh-round pick has now cleared the 80-yard mark twice this season, but Mumpfield could slide down to the No. 2 role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25 if Adams is able to finish his recovery over the upcoming Week 11 bye.

headline: Mumpfield will take on an increased role for the Rams while Puka Nacua (knee) and Davante Adams (hamstring) are unavailable, Cameron DaSilva of USA Today reports.
story: Mumpfield and Tutu Atwell have taken most of the WR snaps alongside Nacua since Adams landed on injured reserve. It now sounds like Adams may return in a few weeks, while Nacua is out for at least a month and uncertain beyond that. There's a big opportunity ahead, but Mumpfield has been targeted on just 23 of 168 routes (13.7 percent), which is a low rate even for someone sharing the field with Nacua/Adams. Atwell has an even lower target rate (11.6 percent), so the Rams likely need their RBs and TEs to take on more offensive burden in Nacua's absence. While targets aren't assured, Mumpfield does seem like the safest bet to log a lot of WR snaps over the next few weeks.

headline: Mumpfield caught both of his targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
story: Despite the lack of production, Mumpfield's 20 receiving yards ended up being second-most on the Rams behind Puka Nacua (150). The bigger news from Sunday's game was Nacua sustaining a PCL/MCL sprain in his knee and turf toe, and the superstar wide receiver is expected to miss at least one month while on injured reserve, per Sarah Bishop of ESPN.com. With Davante Adams (hamstring) also on IR until at least Week 11, that leaves the Rams with Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and rookie sixth-rounder CJ Daniels as the top wide receivers for Matthew Stafford. The Rams hit the road for Week 10 against the Cardinals, whose defense has given up 19 passing touchdowns, which is second-most in the NFL behind the Raiders (20).

headline: Mumpfield caught one of two targets for 15 yards during Sunday's 35-21 win at Las Vegas.
story: With Davante Adams (hamstring) on IR and Puka Nacua dealing with a calf injury going into game day, it looked like Mumpfield was going to see his role expand in Week 7. While he was second on the team in snaps (28) at wide receiver Sunday, Mumpfield still lagged far behind Nacua (58). As long as the latter remains available, Mumpfield appears unlikely to draw more than a few targets in any given game.

headline: Mumpfield could get a significant bump in opportunity Sunday in Week 7 against Las Vegas since Davante Adams (hamstring) is on IR and Puka Nacua (calf) is questionable to play, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
story: The Rams have so far suggested that Nacua's injury is minor, but he's officially questionable for Sunday. Meanwhile, Adams is out a minimum of four games. Quarterback Matthew Stafford will therefore likely look for another wideout to step up, and Mumpfield figures to get an opportunity to produce. When Nacua was out Weeks 2 and 3, Mumpfield hovered around a 70 percent offensive snap share, and he had a big performance against Denver, posting a 4-93-1 receiving line on eight targets. With that said, wideouts Jordan Whittington and Tutu Atwell could also be primed for increased roles, and Stafford may give more attention than usual to tight ends Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen.

headline: Mumpfield caught two of three passes for 15 yards during the Rams' 18-16 loss to the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Mumpfield was on the field for only five offensive snaps against the Bills in Week 5, but he was more involved against the Cardinals with 27 offensive snaps. That snap count figures to increase for the Rams' next few games, seeing as Davante Adams is facing a six- to 10-week recovery timeline for a ruptured left hamstring that required surgery, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. The Rams will hit the road for Week 7 against the Raiders, whose defense ranks 25th in fantasy points allowed to opposing wide receivers.

headline: Mumpfield (shoulder) was a full participant in Thursday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Mumpfield suffered a bruised shoulder in last Sunday's win over the Eagles but is fine ahead of Monday night's matchup with the Bills. With Puka Nacua back healthy alongside Davante Adams, Mumpfield has very minimal fantasy appeal.

headline: Mumpfield suffered a rotator cuff contusion during Sunday's 24-20 win over the Eagles, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: Mumpfield briefly exited the game before returning to the field, and head coach Sean McVay and the team don't appear to be overly worried about the injury. With Puka Nacua returning to action Sunday, Mumpfield saw only three targets, reeling in one catch for seven yards in the victory.

headline: Stafford completed 16 of 23 passes for 141 yards with no touchdowns and one interception and rushed once for no gain in the Rams' 26-13 win over the Packers on Wednesday night. He also committed a fumble recovered by Los Angeles.
story: Playing his second game without both Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring), Stafford saw a notable downturn in his numbers and posted a new season low in passing yards. The veteran signal-caller also threw an interception for the fifth straight game, although his pick Wednesday didn't lead to any Packers points since Los Angeles intercepted Jordan Love just two plays later. Stafford also failed to throw a touchdown pass for only the second time this season, and the fact he also lost tight ends Tyler Higbee (chest) and Davis Allen (ankle) to in-game injuries didn't help his cause. On the positive side, there's an outside chance Stafford has Adams back in the fold for a Week 13 home showdown against the Chiefs on Thursday, Dec. 3.

headline: Stafford completed 18 of 26 passes for 249 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed twice for minus-2 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Stafford didn't let the fact he was without top wideouts Puka Nacua (IR, knee/toe) and Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) deter him from a very fantasy-friendly performance, as the reigning NFL MVP tossed at least three TD passes for the fourth time this season. Stafford connected with the unlikely trio of Tyler Higbee (five yards), Xavier Smith (22 yards) and Davis Allen (19 yards) for his scoring strikes, and the quarterback's 9.6 yards per attempt was his second-highest figure of the season. Stafford, who'll have a chance to further build chemistry with his current wideouts during the Week 11 bye, could have Adams back for a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25, as reports earlier Sunday indicated the talented wideout is targeting that game for his return.

headline: Stafford completed 26 of 43 passes for 228 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. He added one yard on his only carry.
story: The veteran QB looked the way of Puka Nacua (knee) early and often, with no other Ram pass catcher managing more than 20 receiving yards, and the star wideout was on the other end of a seven-yard TD toss in the fourth quarter that proved to be the winning score. Stafford has thrown a single touchdown pass in back-to-back games after producing multiple TDs in five of six contests before that, and his options could get even thinner with Nacua headed for an MRI after getting hurt on L.A.'s final possession.

headline: Stafford (right elbow) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN reports.
story: Stafford was seen leaving the locker room with his upper right arm wrapped in ice after this past Sunday's win against the Chargers. Head coach Sean McVay told Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register on Monday that Stafford has been tending to arm soreness, but the quarterback clarified the situation with Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times on Wednesday, stating that he's had his right arm wrapped in ice regularly this season. An uncapped session to begin Week 9 prep puts Stafford in the clear to continue to lead the Ram's offense Sunday in Washington.

headline: Stafford left the locker room after Sunday's 24-9 win over the Chargers with a bag of ice wrapped on his right arm, and Rams coach Sean McVay acknowledged Monday that the quarterback has been dealing with some arm soreness, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: McVay added that he'll defer to Stafford on the topic of how he's feeling ahead of this weekend's game against the Commanders. In any case, the Rams will issue their first injury report of the week Wednesday, at which point it'll become clear if the QB's arm issue impacts his practice reps.

headline: Stafford completed 17 of 25 passes for 157 yards with one touchdown and one interception in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Stafford didn't have to take on too much with his team's defense largely keeping a still-reeling Chargers offense at bay. The veteran signal-caller finished with his second-lowest passing yardage total of the season, while his pass-attempt tally tied the season-low figure he'd generated back in Week 1 in Melbourne, Australia, against the Rams. However, Stafford extended his streak of games with at least one TD pass to four when he connected with Puka Nacua from 18 yards out with 3:41 remaining in the third quarter. Stafford will look to continue successfully weathering the absence of Davante Adams (IR, hamstring) during a Week 9 road matchup against the Commanders next Sunday.

headline: Stafford completed 23 of 29 passes for 195 yards with three touchdowns and one interception and rushed three times for minus-3 yards in the Rams' 35-21 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Stafford was operating with a less-than-100-percent Puka Nacua (calf) and without Davante Adams (IR, hamstring), so his reduced passing yardage total wasn't entirely surprising. The reigning MVP still found a way to deliver a highly useful fantasy performance via a trio of first-half scoring strikes to Davis Allen (three, five yards) and Nacua (11 yards). Stafford also extended a streak of games with better than a 74.0 percent completion rate to three, and his 79.3 percent tally Sunday was a season-high figure. Stafford next takes aim at the Chargers defense in a Week 8 home matchup next Sunday.

headline: Stafford was 25-for-33 passing for 222 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions during Sunday's 18-16 defeat against the Cardinals.
story: Stafford's streak of outings with at least 300 yards passing came to a close at four games, but he offset it with his fourth performance with multiple TD passes through the first six weeks of the season. With the Rams sitting at 2-4 and seeking to right the ship, he does have a get-right game on paper next Sunday in Las Vegas, and he has several talented skill-position players at his disposal, though star wideout Davante Adams exited on the Rams' second-to-last-offensive play of the game Sunday with what may have been a knee injury. However, the team didn't provide any information about Adams' departure or status following the loss, so it's currently very murky as to whether he's in danger of missing any time.

headline: Stafford completed 40 of 54 passes for 383 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions in the Rams' 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night.
story: Stafford's stellar final line underscores he did everything within his power to lead the Rams to victory, as the reigning MVP finished with his second-highest passing yardage total of the season and fourth 300-yard effort of the campaign. The night also marked Stafford's third multi-TD tally over the first five games, with his scoring strikes going to Davante Adams (four and five yards) and Puka Nacua (two yards). Nacua also was on the receiving end of a whopping 17 of Stafford's completions and the intended target on 24 of his pass attempts, but all of those efforts went for naught thanks to the Bills' block of a Harrison Mevis 48-yard field-goal attempt in overtime that would have sealed the victory for Los Angeles. Stafford and the Rams now will look to bounce back in a Week 6 home divisional matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

headline: Williams rushed 12 times for 46 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for 19 yards in the Rams' 26-13 win over the Packers on Wednesday night.
story: Williams had already been losing ground to Blake Corum in recent weeks, but the latter's takeover of the ground attack may have been finalized Wednesday with his career-best 184-yard, one-touchdown effort. Williams logged his final three carries on the Rams' final drive, but Corum was in the clear lead role throughout the majority of the night. Williams did add his seventh rushing touchdown of the campaign on a seven-yard run early in the second quarter, and his backseat role may have been influenced in part by the turf toe injury he's been dealing with for the past month. Nonetheless, Williams could be destined for a true complementary role if McVay opts to center the ground game on Corum moving forward.

headline: Williams is listed as active Wednesday against the Packers, but the running back has been dealing with a turf toe injury for the last month, according to Tom Pelissero of Netflix.
story: In order to play through it, Williams has had a special tape job as well as a carbon fiber insert in his shoe, per Pellissero. Williams' YPC has decreased in each of the past four games, bottoming out at a season-low 1.9 in the Rams' last game in Week 10 at Arizona. During that same four-game span, fellow RB Blake Corum has garnered double-digit touches while taking on a bit more of the backfield snaps. Perhaps the team's Week 11 bye will help Williams look more like himself Wednesday, but his performance has trended downward while dealing with the injury.

headline: Williams (toe) was a full participant in Monday's practice, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: Listed as a limited participant on the Rams' initial Week 12 injury report posted Sunday, Williams quelled any concern about his status for Wednesday's game against the Packers by taking full reps a day later. Though his sore toe isn't expected to affect his workload, Williams nonetheless may find himself in a timeshare with Blake Corum, who has been the more productive option on the ground this season. Williams has totaled seven touchdowns and is averaging 4.4 yards per carry through 10 games, while Corum has scored six times and is averaging 5.3 yards per tote.

headline: Williams (toe) was a limited practice participant Sunday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Head coach Sean McVay relayed to Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com on Saturday that Williams is dealing with a sore toe, so his practice restrictions to begin Week 12 prep aren't a surprise. Williams will have two more chances to put himself in a position to avoid a designation for Wednesday's game against the Packers.

headline: Head coach Sean McVay said Saturday that Williams is tending to a sore toe but is expected to play Wednesday against the Packers, Sarah Barshop of ESPN reports.
story: The Rams are in the midst of their Week 11 bye, but with a Wednesday game on tap in Week 12, the team is getting back on the practice field this weekend. He'll have three more days to work through the new health concern, but considering McVay's comments, Williams should be fine to continue to work in tandem with fellow RB Blake Corum.

headline: Williams rushed 12 times for 23 yards and brought in two of five targets for nine yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Williams was held well under 4.0 yards per carry for the third consecutive game, but Sunday's performance was particularly alarming in that he averaged a minuscule 1.9 yards per carry. In contrast, Blake Corum (17-100-1) and Ronnie Rivers (15-81-0, albeit in garbage time) both had multiple productive runs on the way to efficient afternoons, making Williams' struggles stand out all the more. With Corum particularly playing well in the last several weeks, Williams could be relegated to a clear complementary role in a Week 12 Thanksgiving Eve home showdown with the Packers on Nov. 25, following a Week 11 bye.

headline: Williams carried the ball 15 times for 45 yards and caught three of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over Washington.
story: Blake Corum was the more productive Ram on the ground, turning 11 carries into 58 yards and a touchdown, but the offense mainly flowed through Puka Nacua on the afternoon. Williams failed to find the end zone for only the third time in nine games this season, and the 45 rushing yards were his lowest total since Week 1, although he has yet to reach 100 in any contest. The Los Angeles backfield has become a clear timeshare however, limiting Williams' upside heading into a Week 10 trip to Arizona.

headline: Williams rushed 16 times for 56 yards and a touchdown and brought in his sole target for three yards in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Williams had a difficult time finding running room against a game Chargers defense, but he salvaged his fantasy day with a one-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter. Williams has five of his six rushing scores on the season in the last four games, and he's still averaging a robust 4.9 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Commanders next Sunday.

headline: Williams rushed 16 times for 99 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 22 yards in the Rams' 35-21 win over the Raiders on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Williams logged one fewer carry than Blake Corum but outgained his teammate by six yards, and although the former's lost fumble came at the Rams' 30-yard line, it didn't lead to any Raiders points. Williams scored his fifth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a 17-yard run late in the first half, and he fell a yard short of his first 100-yard effort of the season. Despite the division of labor in a game that yielded a run-friendly game script, Williams should remain the clear leader of the ground attack in a Week 8 home matchup against the Chargers next Sunday.

headline: Williams notched 10 carries for 50 yards and recorded three catches (on six targets) for 17 yards during Sunday's 18-16 defeat to the Cardinals.
story: Williams' rush total represents a season low as he ceded nine carries to reserve RB Blake Corum. Additionally, Williams also didn't reach the end zone for only the second time in six games in 2026, while Corum recorded a TD for the second consecutive contest. Williams is nearly exactly doubling up Corum in terms of touches on the campaign (110 versus 56), so he figures to be the better bet for a fantasy-relevant performance next Sunday in Las Vegas.

headline: Williams rushed 16 times for 49 yards and a touchdown and brought in six of eight targets for 27 yards in the Rams' 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night.
story: Williams operated as the clear lead back while outpacing Blake Corum by 11 carries, three receptions and four targets, but the former found running room at a premium against a Bills defense that's been surprisingly stout up front. Williams was able to add his fourth rushing touchdown on a dramatic one-yard run with five seconds remaining in regulation to help force overtime, and he's now recorded at least six catches in three consecutive games. Williams should remain in a clear lead role when the Rams host the Cardinals in an NFC West matchup Sunday.

headline: Williams rushed 16 times for 80 yards and two touchdowns while catching 10 of 13 targets for 67 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Eagles.
story: Williams led the team in targets and catches, finishing with one more of each than Puka Nacua, though Nacua racked up 125 receiving yards in his return from a hip injury. Nacua also scored the Rams' first touchdown on a two-yard run, but Williams proceeded to score twice in the final four minutes of the fourth quarter, with touchdown runs of one yard and seven yards to complete the Rams' comeback. Backup Blake Corum had just six touches, so Williams is locked in as the primary backfield option for the Rams ahead of a Week 5 home game against the Bills.

headline: Corum rushed 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown and brought in two of three targets for 21 yards in the Rams' 26-13 win over the Packers on Wednesday. He also recovered a fumble.
story: Corum's stock had already been trending firmly up in recent weeks, but Wednesday may ultimately go down as the day he formally took the reins of the ground attack from Kyren Williams. The 2024 third-round pick compiled a career-best rushing total while also becoming the first Rams running back to reach the 30-carry threshold in a game during the Sean McVay era that began in 2017. Corum has now logged double-digit carries in five consecutive games, and he capped off his night with productive runs of seven, nine and 29 yards on Los Angeles' game-sealing drive. Corum's fantasy value naturally skyrocketed with Wednesday's performance, and he'll look to build on the outstanding performance in a Week 13 home matchup against the Chiefs on Thursday, Dec. 3.

headline: Corum rushed 17 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of four targets for 19 yards in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Corum was far more productive than backfield mate Kyren Williams, who he outpaced by five carries and 77 rushing yards. It was the fourth straight game with double-digit rush attempts and a touchdown for Corum, with Sunday's score coming from one yard out early in the third quarter. He has at least 73 rushing yards in three of the last four contests, and it remains to be seen if Sunday's division of labor will have any sticking power when Los Angeles returns to action following a Week 11 bye in a Week 12 home Thanksgiving Eve matchup against the Packers on Nov. 25.

headline: Corum carried the ball 11 times for 58 yards and a touchdown and failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
story: The Rams' backfield has become a full-fledged timeshare, with Corum getting double-digit carries for a third straight game and out-producing Kyren Williams on the ground in Washington. Corum has gotten into the end zone in all three of those contests, punching in a one-yard score in the third quarter Sunday, and over that stretch he's amassed 224 rushing yards and three TDs while averaging 5.7 yards a carry. With Puka Nacua (knee) headed for an MRI, the Rams could lean even more heavily on their ground attack in a Week 10 tilt against the Cardinals.

headline: Corum rushed 11 times for 73 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Rams' 24-9 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Corum led the Rams in rushing yards despite logging five fewer carries than Kyren Williams, and, like the latter, Corum was able to get into the end zone. Corum's score came early in the third quarter on a winding 23-yard run, his second in as many games. The third-year back now has double-digit carries in consecutive games for the second time this season, and he's averaging a career-best 5.2 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road matchup against the Commanders next Sunday.

headline: Corum rushed 17 times for 93 yards and a touchdown and brought in his only target for eight yards in the Rams' 35-21 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Corum led the Rams in rush attempts and was a close runner-up to Kyren Williams in rushing yards. Corum, like Williams, crossed the goal line as well, recording a four-yard touchdown run with 6:34 remaining in the fourth quarter. Corum's carry and yardage totals were also season highs, but given he'd logged single-digit rush attempts in each of the prior four games, he's more likely than not to continue operating in a clear complementary role behind Williams most weeks.

headline: Corum produced 42 yards on nine carries and reeled in both of his targets for 18 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's 18-16 loss against the Cardinals.
story: Corum was only two touches behind the Rams' clear lead RB Kyren Williams, which marked the second-smallest gap between the two in a game this season. Moreover, Corum took advantage of Sunday's slightly expanded workload by reaching the end zone for the second time in as many contests. So far, his 56 touches have equated to 314 yards from scrimmage and two TDs, and he'll aim for another somewhat even split with Williams next Sunday at Las Vegas.

headline: Corum rushed five times for 19 yards and a touchdown and brought in three of four targets for 53 yards in the Rams' 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills on Monday night.
story: Corum was 11 carries behind Kyren Williams, but the former managed to record his first rushing touchdown of the season on a one-yard run early in the second half. Corum also posted a season high in receiving yards with a big boost from a team-high 34-yard catch, making it a serviceable fantasy night overall. Corum is likely to continue in a complementary role during a Week 6 divisional home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

headline: Corum rushed five times for 14 yards in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Eagles. He added one catch for seven yards on two targets.
story: Kyren Williams has greatly outplayed Corum through the first four weeks of the season, and that continued against Philly, as Williams turned 16 carries into 80 yards and two touchdowns. He also caught 10 passes for 67 yards on 13 targets in the passing game. Williams ended up out-snapping Corum 70 to 13, leaving the latter as nothing more than a fantasy bench stash.

headline: Kinchens was ejected from Wednesday night's game against the Packers after being penalized for an illegal hit to the head of Christian Watson in the second quarter, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kinchens put a helmet-to-helmet hit on Watson along the sideline. Watson was injured on the play but was able to the locker room conscious and under his own power. Jaylen McCollough is in the game in the secondary in Kinchens' place.

headline: Kinchens (hamstring) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles.
story: Kinchens has not suited up since sustaining a hamstring injury during the Rams' Week 1 loss to the 49ers in Melbourne, Australia. The 24-year-old upgraded to full practice participation Friday after being limited in the team's Wednesday and Thursday sessions. The free safety is all set to suit up for Sunday's game next to strong safety Kam Curl.

headline: Kinchens (hamstring) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Kinchens has been sidelined for the Rams' last two contests due to a hamstring injury he suffered back in Week 1 versus the 49ers, and his status for Week 4 is now also in doubt. He'll likely need to practice in full Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: The Rams activated Dedich (hand) from injured reserve, and he does not carry an injury designation into Wednesday's game against the Packers.
story: Dedich opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a hand injury. He's been cleared by medical staff to play Wednesday, and his availability gives the Rams more depth on the interior offensive line.

headline: Dedich (hand) was a full participant in Monday's practice.
story: The offensive lineman had his 21-day practice window opened over the weekend and appears ready to return to action Wednesday against the Packers. With all three of Steve Avila (hamstring), Coleman Shelton (hamstring) and Dylan McMahon (knee) injured, Dedich could immediately see snaps on the interior of the Rams' offensive line.

headline: The Rams opened the 21-day practice window for Dedich (undisclosed) on Saturday.
story: Dedich opened the regular season on injured reserve due to an undisclosed injury. He's now been cleared to practice, and his participation over the next few days will factor into whether he's activated from IR ahead of Wednesday's game against Green Bay.

headline: The Rams activated Turner (groin) from injured reserve, and he is active for Wednesday's game against the Packers.
story: Turner has been officially cleared by medical staff to return from a four-game absence due to a groin injury, and his presence gives the Rams additional depth in the pass rush alongside Ty Hamilton, Aaron Donald, Myles Garrett and Byron Young. Prior to his injury, Turner posted 22 tackles (seven solo) and two pass defenses across six regular-season games.

headline: Turner (groin) was a full participant in Monday's practice, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: The Rams opened Turner's 21-day practice window Saturday. The defensive lineman missed the Rams' last four games while on IR due to a groin injury he sustained in Week 6 against the Cardinals. Given his ability to participate in full Monday, there appears to be a good chance he will be activated ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers.

headline: The Rams designated Turner (groin) to return from injured reserve Saturday.
story: Turner has missed the Rams' last four games while on injured reserve due to a groin injury that he sustained in Week 6 against the Cardinals. His practice participation over the coming days will ultimately determine whether he'll be activated from IR ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers.

headline: The Rams placed Turner (groin) on injured reserve Wednesday.
story: Turner suffered a significant groin injury during the Rams' Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, and the health issue is severe enough for him to warrant a stint on injured reserve. The fourth-year pro will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest that Turner can return is Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25. In his absence, Braden Fiske should move into a starting role on the defensive line opposite Aaron Donald, while Tyler Davis and Larrell Murchison work in rotation.

headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Monday that Turner is expected to go on injured reserve after sustaining a groin strain in Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Cardinals, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
story: Adam Schefter of ESPN relays that Turner is facing a projected recovery timeline of 4-to-6 weeks, giving the defensive tackle a chance at returning from IR when first eligible in Week 12 versus Green Bay. Regarded as a strong interior pass rusher, Turner had been held without a sack for the Rams' first six contests of 2026 after racking up 24.0 through his first three seasons in the league. His absence for at least the next four games should open up a full-time starting role for Braden Fiske opposite Aaron Donald.

headline: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback against the Packers on Wednesday, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: As has been the case all season, Simpson will be the Rams' emergency QB3, meaning he is prohibited from playing Wednesday unless both Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett are removed from the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback in Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Simpson continues to be inactive behind Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett. The quarterback will only enter the game if both Stafford and Bennett must exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback in Sunday's game against the Commanders, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
story: Simpson will once again be inactive behind quarterbacks Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett. The first-round rookie will only be eligible to play if both Stafford and Bennett exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Chargers but will serve as the team's emergency quarterback if needed.
story: Simpson will be inactive once again for Week 8. However, he will be eligible to play if Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: The first-round rookie will not enter Sunday's contest unless both Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback against the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: As the inactive emergency third option, Simpson cannot play in Sunday's contest unless both Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Simpson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Rams' emergency third quarterback against the Bills on Monday, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
story: Simpson will continue to operate as the Rams' emergency QB3, which means he cannot play Monday unless both Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Simpson is inactive and serving as the Rams' emergency third quarterback Sunday versus the Eagles.
story: Simpson has now been inactive as Los Angeles' emergency third QB each of the first four weeks to begin the campaign. He'll be eligible to enter Sunday's contest only if both Matthew Stafford and Stetson Bennett become unavailable due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Shelton (hamstring) is set to miss several weeks due to injury, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
story: The starting center is set to miss 4-6 weeks with a hamstring injury. Shelton will likely be placed on injured reserve while he recovers. Dylan McMahon (knee, IR) also sustained an injury in the Rams' Week 10 win over the Cardinals, leaving Beaux Limmer to finish out the contest at center and to likely fill in as the starter for the foreseeable future.

headline: Shelton (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: With both Shelton and backup center Dylan McMahon (knee) ruled out, the Rams' offensive line depth has become razor-thin. David Quessenberry or Beaux Limmer will likely finish the game at center for the team.

headline: Shelton (hamstring) is doubtful to return to Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Shelton exited the first quarter of Sunday's contest with a hamstring injury. The starting center for the Rams will likely not return to the contest, leaving Dylan McMahon to snap the ball to star quarterback Matthew Stafford for the remainder of Sunday's divisional bout with the Cardinals.

headline: Coach Sean McVay said Saturday that Avila (hamstring) will not play in Wednesday's game against the Packers, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: The Rams' left guard was injured in Week 9 against the Commanders and will miss a second straight game. Bill Murray or Justin Dedich (undisclosed) projects to start in Avila's place versus Green Bay.

headline: Avila (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Avila suffered a hamstring injury against the Commanders in Week 9, and it's not clear if a stint on injured reserve is necessary for the fourth-year offensive guard. If he's not placed on IR, then his next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

headline: Coach Sean McVay said Monday that the Rams haven't decided whether Avila will go to injured reserve with the hamstring injury he suffered during Sunday's game at Washington, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
story: McVay said part of the decision whether to place Avila on IR will be influenced by concerns that the team could use up all of its eight injured-reserve slots for players eligible to return later in the season. Either way, for as long as Avila remains sidelined, 2024 sixth rounder Beaux Limmer projects to fill in at left guard.

headline: Avila (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's matchup against the Commanders.
story: Avila dealt with a hamstring issue throughout the week and apparently aggravated the injury in the first half Sunday. Now that he's been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday, Beaux Limmer is slated to finish the contest at left guard.

headline: Avila (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's matchup against Washington.
story: Avila departed in the second quarter and was subsequently deemed questionable to return. He was on the injury report this week due to a hamstring injury, so he may have aggravated the same issue. Beaux Limmer has taken over for Avila at left guard.

headline: Curl has no injury designation for Wednesday night's matchup against the Packers, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
story: Curl posted two limited practices after beginning the week as a nonparticipant. The 27-year-old has started all 10 games for the Rams this season, recording 48 tackles (28 solo) and three pass deflections.

headline: Curl (toe) did not practice Sunday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Curl played through the issue last week against the Cardinals and should be fine for Wednesday's game against the Packers assuming he didn't suffer any setbacks versus Arizona. Curl has started all 10 games this season, recording 48 tackles (28 solo) and three pass breakups.

headline: Curl (toe) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Curl's sole limited practice session Friday was enough to cement his availability for Sunday's contest. The strong safety has started every contest for the Rams in 2026, playing 100 percent of the defensive snaps in six of the Rams' nine games.

headline: Head coach Sean McVay told reporters Friday that he is optimistic that Curl (toe) will be available for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: Curl opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back DNPs due to a toe injury before logging a limited session Friday, per Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com. That was enough for Curl to get the questionable tag for Sunday's game, although McVay's comments suggest that the veteran safety is on the probable side to play in Week 10. If Curl cannot play or operates under a snap count, then Jaylen McCollough would be in line for a larger role in the Rams' secondary.

headline: Curl (toe) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
story: It was the second consecutive DNP for Curl, who is now battling a toe injury after nearly missing the Week 9 meeting with Washington due to a foot issue. The 27-year-old might carry an injury designation heading into Week 10 against the Cardinals, but if he isn't out there, Jaylen McCollough is a candidate to replace him in the starting lineup.

headline: Curl (toe) did not participate in Wednesday's walkthrough practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Curl was cleared to play against the Commanders in Week 9 after recovering from a foot injury, and he finished that contest with eight tackles (four solo). He's now working through a toe issue, and he'll have two more chances to return to practice ahead of Sunday's NFC West showdown against the Cardinals. Curl has accumulated 46 tackles (27 solo) and two pass defenses through the first nine games of the regular season.

headline: Curl (foot) is active for Sunday's game against the Commanders.
story: Curl is set to suit up for Sunday's game despite missing the Rams' Wednesday and Thursday practice sessions. The strong safety will need to anchor the team's secondary due to the absence of starting cornerbacks Jaylen Watson (shoulder, IR) and Trent McDuffie (back).

headline: Curl (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
story: Curl did not participate in practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a foot injury likely suffered at some point in the Rams' Week 9 win over the Chargers. With cornerbacks Trent McDuffie (back) questionable and Jaylen Watson (shoulder) ruled out, Los Angeles' secondary could be short on a few key pieces.

headline: Curl (foot) did not participate at the Rams' practice Wednesday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Curl notched four total tackles (one solo) during the team's 24-9 win over the Chargers in Week 8, but he may have picked up a foot injury during the contest. The safety will have two more chances to return to practice prior to Sunday's game against the Commanders.

headline: Curl logged four tackles (two solo) during the Rams' 35-21 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Curl was on the field for all but one of the Rams' defensive snaps during Sunday's win. The veteran safety has logged four stops or fewer in five of seven regular-season games and is up to 34 tackles (20 solo) and two pass defenses on the year.

headline: Curl finished Sunday's 18-16 loss to the Cardinals with eight tackles (three solo).
story: Curl played every single defensive snap for a third consecutive game and the fourth time this season, and he finished Sunday's contest as the Rams' second-leading tackler behind Nate Landman (10). Curl has registered eight combined tackles in back-to-back outings and is up to 30 tackles (18 solo) and two pass defenses through six regular-season games.

headline: Curl (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Cardinals.
story: Curl injured his ankle in Thursday's practice and was unable to participate in Friday's session. The safety has recovered enough from the injury to suit up for Sunday's divisional contest against the Cardinals as the starting strong safety.

headline: Curl (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
story: Curl injured his ankle during Thursday's practice, and while he was held out of Friday's session, head coach Sean McVay told reporters that the Rams "feel good" about Curl's chances of playing against Arizona. If the veteran safety is not able to play, then Jaylen McCollough would likely step into a starting role next to Kamren Kinchens, with Maximus Pulley providing depth at the position.

headline: Curl was limited in practice Thursday due to an ankle injury, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: The fact Curl showed up on the injury report midweek may be indicative of a health concern that happened in practice. In any case, the status of the Rams' starting strong safety will be monitored to get a sense of his odds to suit up Sunday against the Cardinals.

headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Tuesday that Garrett's absence from Monday's practice was a rest day and had nothing to do with his knee injury, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports.
story: Garrett was limited in practice Sunday and Tuesday due to a knee injury, but it doesn't appear he will be impacted in Wednesday night's matchup against the Packers. The 30-year-old has three tackles (three solo), including 3.0 sacks and a forced fumble in three regular-season games in 2026.

headline: Garrett (knee/rest) did not participate in Monday's practice, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: Garrett downgraded his practice participation in Monday's session. The linebacker started Week 12 prep with a limited session on Sunday, so Monday's lack of participation is likely more due to affording him a day off than any aggravation of his knee issue. Garrett will likely need to log at least a limited session Tuesday to dodge an injury designation ahead of Wednesday's game against the Packers.

headline: Garrett (knee) was limited in practice Sunday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: With the Rams playing the Packers on Wednesday, the team was required to release an injury report Sunday. Garrett is in no danger of missing Week 12. He has 3.0 sacks and a forced fumble across three games this season.

headline: Garrett played 17 defensive snaps but did not show up on the box score otherwise during the Rams' 34-6 win over the Cardinals in Week 10.
story: Garrett was cleared to play in Week 10 after working through a knee injury. The low snap count was more due to the fact that the Cardinals posted only 35 offensive snaps while recording a 17:37 time of possession. The Rams are on a bye for Week 11, so Garrett's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Packers on Wednesday, Nov. 25.

headline: Garrett (knee) is listed as active Sunday at Arizona, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: Garrett was listed as limited on the Rams' first two Week 10 practice reports due to a knee injury and then got a veteran's rest day Friday, heading into the weekend listed as questionable. Head coach Sean McVay told Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com on Friday that Garrett is expected to play Sunday, which now has been confirmed. Garrett will be looking to have a similar impact to the 3.0-sack day he had in Week 9 against the Commanders.

headline: Head coach Sean McVay said Friday that Garrett (knee) will be listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Arizona but is expected to play, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Garrett made his presence felt in his return to the lineup this past Sunday at Washington, sacking Commanders QB Jayden Daniels three times, but the Rams capped his practice reps this week due to a listed knee injury. McVay's comments indicate Garrett isn't in danger of sitting out Week 10, but the pass rusher's status nonetheless will be confirmed about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Garrett (knee) practiced in a limited fashion Thursday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: The Rams are managing Garrett's practice reps after he returned from a seven-game absence this past Sunday at Washington, when he posted 3.0 sacks of Commanders QB Jayden Daniels. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will reveal if Garrett has a designation for Sunday's contest at Arizona.

headline: Garrett (knee) was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: In his first game action this past Sunday at Washington since Week 1, Garrett made his mark with three tackles, all of which went down as sacks of QB Jayden Daniels. Garrett's restrictions to begin Week 10 prep likely are maintenance related more than anything, but his status nonetheless will be monitored ahead of Sunday's contest in Arizona.

headline: Garrett recorded 3.0 sacks and forced a fumble in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders.
story: Making his return from a knee injury that had sidelined him since Week 1, Garrett made an immediate impact and accounted for three of the Rams' four sacks of Jayden Daniels on the afternoon, with Braden Fiske and Shaun Dolac splitting the other. A healthy Garrett's presence in the front seven changes the entire complexion of the defense, and he could continue to make up for lost time in Week 10 against Gardner Minshew and the Cardinals.

headline: Garrett (knee) was activated from injured reserve Saturday and doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Washington.
story: Garrett thus is in the clear for his first game action since Week 1, after which he required arthroscopic surgery on his left knee and an IR stint that sidelined him the last seven contests. Sunday's outing will mark his first working with the out-of-retirement Aaron Donald, and while Garrett may be hard-pressed to extend his streak of 10-plus sack seasons to nine the rest of the way, he should provide a boost to the Rams' fifth-ranked defense (301.1 yards per game).

headline: Garrett (knee) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Garrett didn't practice Friday, but the Rams are planning to activate him from injured reserve Saturday, allowing the veteran edge rusher to play in Week 9. It will be a much-needed boost to the Rams' inferior pass rush.

headline: Garrett (knee) is on track to be activated ahead of Sunday's game against the Commanders, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Since being designated to return from IR, Garrett has logged consecutive limited practices, but it looks like the star pass rusher -- who underwent arthroscopic surgery on his left knee after Week 1 action -- is poised to return to the Rams defense in Week 9. For that to occur, though, he'll need to be officially activated by Saturday afternoon's deadline for the team to do so.

headline: Garrett (knee) remained limited in Thursday's practice, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
story: Garrett's 21-day practice window was opened Wednesday, and he's been limited both days this week. It might be too soon for the star edge rusher to return Sunday against the Commanders, but if not, then Week 10 against Arizona could be a possibility.

headline: Head coach Sean McVay said Garrett (knee) will practice Wednesday, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Garrett has been on injured reserve since aggravating a left knee injury that required arthroscopic surgery in Week 1. In order to be able to practice Wednesday, the Rams designated him for return from IR, per the NFL's transaction log. Garrett's activity level bears watching as the week goes on to get a sense of his odds to play Sunday at Washington.

headline: Coach Sean McVay indicated Monday that Garrett (knee) is on track to practice this week, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.
story: Garrett hasn't practiced since aggravating a left knee injury in the Rams' season opener, a setback that was followed by arthroscopic surgery. Once the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year retakes the practice field, the Rams will have a 21-day window in which to restore Garrett to their active roster. It remains to be seen if this weekend's game against the Commanders is in play, but either way Garrett's looming return to the lineup, whenever it happens, will be a major boost to the Rams defense.

headline: The Rams are optimistic that Garrett (knee) will be able to return to practice in Week 9, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Garrett hasn't practiced since aggravating a left knee injury in the Rams' season-opening loss to the 49ers in Australia and then undergoing arthroscopic surgery. Though head coach Sean McVay has been non-committal on a potential target date for Garrett's return, the star edge rusher will take a notable step toward playing once the Rams officially open his 21-day practice window. Even if he's back on the field for the start of Week 9 prep, Garrett is far from a lock to play next Sunday in Washington versus the Commanders, as the reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year may need more than three practices to get himself back in playing condition following a seven-week layoff from action.

headline: Head coach Sean McVay said Wednesday that the Rams won't open Garrett's (knee) practice window this week, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports.
story: Garrett underwent arthroscopic surgery on his left knee after Week 1 and has been on injured reserve in the meantime. Following McVay's comments, Garrett will miss Sunday's contest against the Chargers, which will mark his seventh consecutive absence. Garrett's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 8, at Washington.

headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Friday that Garrett (knee) could have his 21-day practice window opened next week, Nate Atkins of The Athletic reports.
story: The Rams are in shambles from an injury standpoint headed into Sunday's game against the Raiders, but help may be on the horizon in the form of Garrett. The All-Pro edge rusher hasn't played since Week 1 in Australia.

headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said Monday that Garrett (knee) won't have his 21-day practice window opened this week, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: The Rams haven't indicated that Garrett has experienced any setbacks since undergoing arthroscopic left knee surgery following the team's Week 1 loss to the 49ers in Australia, but he looks like he'll need more time to complete his rehab before getting back on the field for practice. The ongoing absence of Garrett will continue to loom large heading into Sunday's game against the Raiders, especially with one of the Rams' other key pass rushers (defensive tackle Kobie Turner) set to join Garrett on injured reserve after sustaining a groin injury in the Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.

headline: Head coach Sean McVay told reporters Tuesday that Garrett (knee) will not return to practice this week and will not play against the Cardinals on Sunday, Cameron DaSilva of USA Today reports.
story: Garrett underwent knee surgery following the Rams' Week 1 loss to the 49ers in Australia and was subsequently placed on injured reserve. He's eligible to return from IR now that he's missed the four-game minimum, but Garrett has not progressed enough in his recovery to practice, even in a limited capacity. A six-week recovery timeline for the superstar pass rusher's return was reported by Ian Rapoport of NFL Network and ESPN in late September, and if that timeline is accurate, then Garrett could be back in action for Week 7 against the Raiders on Sunday, Oct. 25.

headline: Garrett (knee), per head coach Sean McVay, is "on track" in his recovery but is not expected to return to practice next week, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports.
story: Things seems to be progressing in the right direction for Garrett, but McVay's comments indicate he will not return from injured reserve when first eligible in Week 6. Assuming Garrett remains out of practice next week as anticipated, his next chance to return will arrive in Week 7 against the Raiders.

headline: Pinion (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: He'll miss a second straight game, also Jack Browning should get the nod at punter for Miami. He'll likely be busy Sunday.

headline: Pinion (groin) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Pinion did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions. The punter likely sustained his groin injury in the Dolphins' Week 10 loss to the Colts. Jack Browning is set to be elevated from the practice squad ahead of Sunday's game against the Bills to take over punting duties.

headline: Trader (shoulder/groin) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Jets.
story: Trader was sidelined Week 11 at Buffalo with shoulder and groin injuries, but he's now back to full strength. He projects to start at safety next to rookie fifth-rounder Michael Taaffe against the Jets.

headline: Trader (shoulder/groin) is inactive for Sunday's Week 11 tilt against Buffalo.
story: Trader's inactive status is not surprising given that he didn't practice all week and entered the weekend tagged as doubtful to suit up. Sunday will mark the second-year pro's first career absence. Kyle Louis and/or Zayne Anderson could get a big bump in work at safety in Trader's stead.

headline: Trader (shoulder/groin) is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Bills, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.
story: Trader opened the week as a non-participant in practice after suffering groin and shoulder injuries during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts last Sunday. Kyle Louis and Julius Wood may see more time in his place if Trader does indeed miss Week 11. Trader has 45 tackles (23 solo) and three pass breakups, including one interception, through nine 2026 regular-season games.

headline: Trader (shoulder/groin) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Trader may have picked up the injuries during the Dolphins' 24-22 loss to the Colts in Week 10, when he played every defensive snap and finished with six tackles (four solo). The second-year defensive back will have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Bills.

headline: Trader (shoulder) has returned to Sunday's game against the Jets, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Trader exited Sunday's contest in the third quarter with a shoulder injury. The starting strong safety has been thoroughly vetted and deemed healthy enough to return to the Dolphins' divisional showdown with the Jets.

headline: Trader (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Jets.
story: Trader exited the third quarter of Sunday's game with a shoulder injury. While Trader is absent, Michael Taaffe has taken over at strong safety.

headline: Trader (shin) does not have an injury designation against the Bengals on Sunday, Paul Dehner Jr. of The Athletic reports.
story: Trader opened Week 5 prep with consecutive limited practices, but he avoided an injury tag after logging a full session Friday. The second-year safety has 19 tackles (nine solo) and two pass defenses (one interception) through the first four games of the regular season.

headline: Trader (shin) was limited during Thursday's practice.
story: Trader was originally on the injury report due to a knee issue, which he sustained during the Week 4 loss to Minnesota. However, it appears he is now dealing with a shin injury. The 23-year-old is considered day-to-day, meaning he could be on the field in Week 5 versus the Bengals.

headline: Trader (knee) is considered day-to-day ahead of Week 5, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
story: Trader suffered a knee injury during Sunday's 15-10 loss to Minnesota, and he was briefly sidelined before returning to action. The safety registered five total tackles (three solo) during the contest, and his status at Wednesday's first practice of the week will shed more light on his availability for the team's matchup with the Bengals in Week 5.

headline: Trader (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Minnesota.
story: The 23-year-old has had a quality 2026 campaign, so his absence wouldn't be ideal for the Dolphins defense. While Trader is off the field, it could mean more snaps for rookie Michael Taaffe.

headline: Wayne (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Wayne will end up missing a third consecutive game due to a quadriceps injury, and his next chance to suit up is Week 13 against the Broncos on Sunday, Dec. 6. Kevin Coleman and Jalen Tolbert will continue to operate in slightly expanded roles on offense in Wayne's absence.

headline: Wayne (quadriceps) didn't practice Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Wayne has missed the Dolphins' last two games due to a quadriceps injury. He would need to practice in at least a limited capacity over the next two days to have a realistic chance of being available for Sunday's game against the Jets.

headline: Wayne (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Wayne will miss a second straight game due to a quadriceps injury, and his next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29. In his absence, Kevin Coleman and Jalen Tolbert will serve as the Dolphins' rotational wide receivers behind Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell.

headline: Wayne (quadriceps) did not participate at practice Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Wayne sat out Sunday's game at Indianapolis with a quad injury, and his availability for Week 11 is now in question. If he's not able to get back onto the practice field Thursday or Friday, he'll be trending toward missing Sunday's game at Buffalo.

headline: Wayne (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Colts, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Wayne popped up on Thursday's practice report as a limited participant due to a quadriceps injury, which prevented him from suiting up for Friday's session. He won't be available for Sunday's contest, and it appears the Dolphins will also be without rookie third-rounder Chris Bell (knee), who is listed as doubtful. Wayne's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Bills on Sunday, Nov. 22.

headline: Wayne (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game versus the Patriots.
story: Wayne was limited in Wednesday and Thursday's practice sessions. He was a full participant Friday and didn't carry an injury designation for the Week 8 meeting with New England. However, despite being healthy enough to suit up, the wideout won't be on the field Sunday.

headline: Wayne (knee) does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Patriots, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
story: Wayne was limited in practice both Wednesday and Thursday, but his ability to practice in full Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sundays' AFC East showdown. Wayne made his Dolphins debut against the Jets in Week 7, when he played 16 snaps (10 on offense, six on special teams) without showing up in the box score otherwise.

headline: Wayne (knee) was a limited practice participant Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Wayne was also limited Wednesday, so his status for Sunday's clash against New England is hazy. Unless he's able to upgrade to full participation Friday, the wideout will likely be tagged with a designation heading into the weekend. In his debut with the Dolphins this past Sunday versus the Jets, Wayne didn't draw a target on 10 offensive snaps while also playing six snaps on special teams.

headline: Wayne (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports.
story: Wayne may have picked up the injury during the Dolphins' Week 7 win over the Jets, when he played 16 snaps (10 on offense, six on special teams) without showing up on the box score otherwise. He'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's AFC East showdown against New England. Wayne has not recorded a target in each of his last three outings after turning 12 targets into four catches for 65 yards through the first three games of the regular season as a member of the Texans.

headline: Wayne was claimed off waivers by the Dolphins on Tuesday.
story: Wayne was waived by the Texans on Monday, though he was quickly scooped up by the Dolphins on Tuesday. The 26-year-old appeared in nine regular-season games for Houston across three seasons, totaling six grabs (14 targets) for 65 yards.

headline: Wayne was waived by the Texans on Monday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: Wayne is the odd man out in the wide-receiver room with Houston after the team announced Sunday that they have traded for third-year wideout Marvin Harrison from the Cardinals. Wayne has played in each of the Texans' five regular-season contests to this point, reeling in four of 12 targets for 65 targets. If the 26-year-old clears waivers, there's a strong chance that Wayne returns as a member of Houston's practice squad.

headline: Brents (neck/shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jets, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.
story: Brents did not participate in any of the three Week 12 practices while recovering from neck and shoulder injuries that he sustained in Week 11 against the Bills. Darrell Baker will likely start opposite Jason Marshall at outside cornerback in the absence of Brents, whose next chance to play is Week 13 against the Broncos on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Brents (neck) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Brents was initially diagnosed with a shoulder injury during the Dolphins' Week 12 loss to the Bills. He was tagged with a neck injury on Wednesday's report, and he'll have two more chances to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Jets.

headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said Monday that Brents is day-to-day with a shoulder injury, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports.
story: Brents didn't return to Sunday's loss to the Bills after sustaining a shoulder injury. The 26-year-old is still expected to undergo further tests but appears to have avoided anything serious. Brents has 36 tackles (21 solo) and two pass deflections through 10 regular-season games.

headline: Brents (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's tilt against Buffalo.
story: Brents was hurt in the fourth quarter and is uncertain to re-enter the contest. Darrell Baker has taken over for Brents at outside cornerback.

headline: Brents (neck) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Bills, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Brents' practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday due to a neck injury, but his full session Friday was enough for the fourth-year defensive back to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt. Brents has accumulated 33 tackles (18 solo), one pass defense and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

headline: Brents (neck) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Brents played 42 defensive snaps during Sunday's game at Indianapolis, and it looks like he might have come away from that contest with a neck injury. He'll likely have to upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday to avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Brents (neck/concussion) is active for Sunday's game against New England.
story: Brents was in danger of missing this contest due to multiple injuries. However, he will shed the questionable tag and suit up for the AFC East clash with the Patriots.

headline: Brents (neck/concussion) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots, C. Isaiah Smalls II of the Miami Herald reports.
story: Brents logged a full practice Friday, but he'll need to clear the league's concussion protocol in order to be available for Sunday's AFC East tilt. Marcellas Dial and Jaylin Simpson would be the top candidates to start opposite Jason Marshall at outside cornerback if Brents is not cleared to play.

headline: Brents (neck/concussion) was a limited practice participant Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Brents suffered a concussion this past Sunday versus the Jets and didn't practice at all Wednesday. His ability to upgrade to limited participation Thursday is a good sign of progress, but the cornerback will still need to be cleared by an independent neurologist to be eligible to suit up Sunday against New England. Should Brents not get that clearance in time, Jaylin Simpson could be asked to step into a larger role in the Dolphins' secondary.

headline: Brents (neck/concussion) did not practice Wednesday, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports.
story: Brents reported concussion symptoms following the Dolphins' Week 7 win over the Jets, per Alain Poupart of SI.com. Brents will have two more opportunities to practice this week, but he would not be eligible to play against the Patriots on Sunday unless he's cleared from the league's concussion protocol by an independent neurologist.

headline: Brents (neck) was a full participant at the Dolphins' practice Wednesday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Brents suffered a stinger in the team's Week 5 loss to the Bengals, but he now appears to be back to 100 percent following the team's bye week. The cornerback will be back in his starting role in Miami's secondary versus the Jets on Sunday.

headline: Brents exited in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game against the Bengals due to a stinger and is questionable to return.
story: Brents had initially been labeled as questionable to return after leaving the game in the first half to receive evaluation for a concussion as well as the stinger. He was able to check back into the game to begin the second half, but he appears to have suffered an aggravation of the stinger. Brents tallied six tackles and one pass breakup prior to his most recent exit.
