Coach Kevin O'Connell declined to name a Week 10 starter Wednesday, but Cousins' familiarity with the offense seemingly gives him the edge over Carson Wentz (ankle) after Wentz's Monday night meltdown.

headline: Hockenson recorded four catches for 33 yards on seven targets in a loss to Buffalo on Monday.
story: In addition to leading the Vikings in receptions, Hockenson finished second in receiving yardage and targets in a rough performance by Minnesota's offense. The veteran wideout has hauled in exactly four catches in four straight games, though he snapped a two-game TD streak Monday. It remains to be seen who will be throwing passes for Minnesota next Sunday in Green Bay, as Carson Wentz struggled enormously Monday and Kyler Murray currently is dealing with a Grade 2 hamstring strain.

headline: Hockenson caught four of five targets for 58 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions.
story: Hockenson secured an eight-yard touchdown midway through the fourth quarter to give the Vikings a 15-12 lead, and he's now up to 31 grabs for 295 yards and three touchdowns on 37 targets through seven games this season. Hockenson, though, missed all but two offensive snaps in the Week 5 win over the Saints after suffering a concussion. A favorite target for Kyler Murray in the middle and short areas of the field, Hockenson has settled in as a lower-end TE1 in fantasy. He gets a plus matchup with the Bills next Monday night in another spot the Minnesota offense may be forced to push the gas pedal.

headline: Hockenson caught four of five targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts.
story: The veteran tight end scored Minnesota's only TD of the afternoon, connecting with Kyler Murray on a five-yard score early in the fourth quarter. Hockenson has seen more than five targets just once in six contests this season, and he'll take a 27-237-2 line on 32 targets into a potential revenge game in Week 8 against the Lions.

headline: Hockenson (concussion) practiced fully Friday and doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Colts, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: With the benefit of a Week 6 bye, Hockenson has cleared the concussion protocol after suffering a head injury in the Vikings' last game in Week 5 at New Orleans. He'll be available Sunday along with WRs Justin Jefferson (ankle) and Jordan Addison (hamstring) for QB Kyler Murray.

headline: Hockenson (concussion) was listed as a full participant Thursday.
story: Hockenson is inching closer to clearing the protocol for head injuries after sustaining a concussion during the Vikings' Week 5 win at New Orleans. At the very least, he must gain clearance from an independent neurologist in order to suit up again Sunday against the Colts.

headline: Hockenson (concussion) was a full practice participant Wednesday.
story: In the wake of suffering a concussion during a Week 5 win in New Orleans, Hockenson had the benefit of a Week 6 bye and took advantage of it, but a full practice Wednesday doesn't necessarily mean he's out of the protocol for head injuries just yet. He'll need to gain clearance from an independent neurologist in order to be able to play Sunday against the Colts.

headline: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said that Hockenson (concussion) is expected to practice Wednesday, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
story: Hockenson suffered a concussion on the Vikings' opening possession of a Week 5 win in New Orleans, but with the benefit of an early-season bye in Week 6, the tight end may not miss any additional time due to the injury. Wednesday's activity level will serve as Hockenson's baseline as he works his way through the protocol for head injuries ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts.

headline: The Vikings downgraded Hockenson to out for Sunday's game against the Saints due to a concussion.
story: After recording a seven-yard reception on the Vikings' opening possession, Hockenson immediately headed to the locker room to get checked for a head injury. With Minnesota confirming that he has sustained a concussion, Hockenson will be shut down for the rest of the afternoon and will now be subject to the NFL's five-step protocol. Minnesota is on bye in Week 6, so Hockenson's next chance to play will come against the Colts on Oct. 25.

headline: Hockenson is under evaluation for a possible concussion and is considered questionable to return to Sunday's game at New Orleans.
story: Hockenson remained on the turf at the end of a seven-yard catch in the first quarter and went directly to the sideline tent afterward. If Hockenson isn't able to reenter the contest, Gavin Bartholomew and Ben Yurosek represent the Vikings' remaining available tight ends.

headline: Hockenson caught all 13 of his targets for 119 yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Dolphins.
story: The veteran tight end emerged as Kyler Murray's favorite target in the absence of Justin Jefferson (ankle), and as a result Hockenson produced his first game with 100-plus yards since 2024, when he popped for a 7-114-0 line against the Bears in Week 12. Hockenson came into Sunday with just 76 receiving yards, so he could have trouble repeating the performance even if Jefferson misses another game, but Murray had success feeding the ball to Trey McBride last year with Arizona as well -- McBride posted a 29-275-1 line on 42 targets during the five games they were in the lineup together. Hockenson will look to keep rolling in a Week 5 road trip to New Orleans.

headline: Hockenson could be in line for an increase in targets during Sunday's Week 4 matchup against the Dolphins due to Justin Jefferson being ruled inactive for the contest.
story: Hockenson's 2026 campaign has gotten off to a reasonably productive start, as the veteran tight end has posted a 9-76-1 line on 13 targets through three games. While Hockenson didn't reap any tangible benefit from Jefferson's early exit during the Week 3 win over the Buccaneers -- the former recorded two receptions for 11 yards on four targets -- there's a possibility he's a lot more involved against a Dolphins team that's surrendered 15 receptions for 210 yards and two touchdowns to tight ends, along with an 88.2 percent catch rate.

headline: Hockenson caught two of his four targets for 11 yards in the Vikings' 23-16 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: Hockenson struggled along with the entire Vikings offense in the contest. The team relied on a single explosive rush and a single explosive pass play over the entire 60-minute game. Quarterback Kyler Murray was unable to stoke much of a passing attack against the Buccaneers, relying on a 41-yard touchdown to Jordan Addison for nearly a quarter of his passing yards on the night.

headline: Jennings caught three of six targets for 20 yards during Sunday night's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
story: Jennings made his return to action after missing two games with a calf injury. The 29-year-old reeled in a season-high three passes, while his six targets were also the most he's had in a game this year. The wide receiver has yet to exceed 40 receiving yards in contest, and Jennings hasn't scored a touchdown this season. His next chance to accomplish both feats will come in Week 12 versus the Falcons.

headline: Jennings (calf) practiced in full Wednesday.
story: Jennings sat out the last two games due to a calf injury, but his return to all activity Wednesday gives the Vikings' receiving corps a boost after Jordan Addison was lost for at least a few weeks due to a broken thumb that required surgery. As for Jennings, he'll have a prime opportunity to work opposite No. 1 WR Justin Jefferson as he looks to build upon his 6-54-0 line on 10 targets in his six appearances this season.

headline: Jennings (calf) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Green Bay.
story: Jennings opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back DNP listings due to a calf injury and now will miss his second contest of the campaign. With Jordan Addison (thumb) listed as questionable heading into the weekend, Justin Jefferson, Myles Price and Tai Felton currently are the healthy wide receivers on the Vikings' active roster.

headline: Jennings (calf) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Jennings was estimated as a non-participant on the Vikings' injury report Wednesday after being sidelined in Week 9, and he wasn't able to take the practice field Thursday. Unless he's able to return to practice in some capacity Friday, he'll probably end up missing a second straight game in Week 10, which could leave Myles Price with an expanded role at wideout come Sunday at Green Bay.

headline: Jennings (calf) was estimated as DNP on Wednesday's practice report.
story: The veteran wideout missed last Monday night's loss to the Bills, allowing Myles Price to step in as the No. 3 receiver. Price caught just one of four targets for six yards, and Jennings has just six receptions for 54 yards across six games this year.

headline: Jennings (calf) has been ruled out for Monday's contest versus the Bills.
story: Per head coach Kevin O'Connell, Jennings suffered a calf injury at Thursday's practice that is serious enough to sideline him for at least one game. Jennings' next chance for game action is Sunday, Nov. 15 in Green Bay, while Tai Felton and Myles Price are in for some offensive snaps this week behind the top WR duo of Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.

headline: Jennings (calf) did not participate in Friday's practice.
story: Jennings downgraded his practice participation Friday after being limited in Thursday's session. The wide receiver will likely need to show up in some capacity Saturday for a chance to suit up for Monday night's primetime showdown with the Bills.

headline: Jennings (calf) was limited in Thursday's practice.
story: It's a new injury for Jennings, but he has an extra day to recover this week, as the Vikings play the Bills on Monday night. Jennings has six grabs for 54 yards on 10 targets across six games this season and is nowhere near fantasy relevance in his current role.

headline: Jennings caught both of his targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 19-15 loss to the Lions.
story: The Vikings' third receiver, Jennings ran 20 route on Kyler Murray's 33 dropbacks, playing behind both Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison. Jennings' name has been linked to trade speculation but recently declined a deal to San Francisco after the two teams agreed to trade parameters. Jennings has six grabs for 54 yards on 10 targets across six games this season.

headline: Jennings elected to remain with the Vikings after the team had an agreement in place to move him to the 49ers earlier in the week in a deal that was contingent on the receiver's approval, Jay Glazer reported on "Fox NFL Sunday."
story: According to Glazer, Jennings would have returned to San Francisco if he hopped on a FaceTime call with the 49ers brass to confirm his willingness to rejoin his former squad, but the wideout instead elected to stick around in Minnesota. San Francisco has obvious gaps in its receiving corps due to injuries, and Jennings' familiarity with head coach Kyle Shanahan's system would have made him a natural choice to help strengthen the position group. However, Jennings also left on somewhat acrimonious terms due to his contract situation before becoming a free agent, which may have been a factor in his decision not to sign off on the trade. He'll be active for Sunday's game in Detroit but has struggled to carve out much volume in the passing attack thus far, notching just four receptions for 43 yards on eight targets through his first five appearances with Minnesota.

headline: Jennings caught two of three targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts.
story: The veteran wideout entered Week 7 with just two catches for nine yards across four games, so this counts as a breakout game for Jennings. He's running plenty of routes alongside Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison at receiver, but Jennings is deep down the list for targets in Minnesota. He's not a recommended fantasy play for next Sunday against the Lions' leaky secondary.

headline: Jennings did not reel in his only target during Sunday's 23-13 win at New Orleans.
story: Jennings again got the second most snaps at wide receiver for the Vikings (47) in Week 5 with Jordan Addison (hamstring) out, but it only translated to one target on the afternoon. Jennings has failed to draw more than two targets in any game so far this season, and his role could be further diminished after Minnesota's bye in Week 6 if Addison is able to return to action.

headline: Jennings caught his lone target for eight yards in Sunday's 15-10 win over the Dolphins.
story: Despite Justin Jefferson (ankle) missing Sunday's game, Jennings remained a non-factor on offense, as he took a distant back seat to all three of T.J. Hockenson, Jordan Addison and Aaron Jones. Jennings has two catches for nine yards on four targets across 152 offensive snaps through three games this season. He's well off the fantasy radar.

headline: Jennings is in line to see a boost in targets as the Vikings' No. 2 receiver for Sunday's Week 4 matchup against the Dolphins, due to Justin Jefferson (hamstring) being ruled inactive for the contest.
story: Jennings' Vikings tenure has gotten off to an utterly forgettable start, as the veteran receiver has just one reception for one yard on three targets through two games. While Jennings was unable to capitalize on Jefferson's early exit from a Week 3 win over the Buccaneers, the former did log a season-high 47 snaps and ran 24 routes during the contest. Both numbers -- along with Jennings' target share -- will be in line to increase against Miami with Jefferson out, although the possibility Minnesota eventually has the luxury of turning to a run-heavy approach in the second half also is high considering the generally uncompetitive current state of the Dolphins.

headline: Jennings caught one of two targets for one yard Sunday in a 23-16 win against Tampa Bay.
story: Although Justin Jefferson (ankle) departed in the first half Sunday and didn't return, Jennings didn't see an increase in his production. Jennings did, however, post an 80 percent offensive snap share, and he figures to slide into the No. 2 wideout role alongside Jordan Addison on Sunday versus Miami if Jefferson can't suit up. Even with that in mind, Jennings has produced just one catch (on three targets) through two contests, so expectations should be held in check regardless of Jefferson's status.

headline: Cousins completed 26 of 38 passes for 235 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers. He also rushed once for no gain.
story: After throwing a pick-six among his three interceptions when he faced San Francisco's defense in his final game with the Raiders in Week 9, Cousins had another interception returned for a touchdown by the 49ers in the second quarter of Sunday's loss. The Vikings took a 28-10 deficit into the halftime locker room, and Cousins was unable to orchestrate a comeback before Minnesota waved the white flag and inserted Carson Wentz for its final drive. Cousins is still strengthening his grasp on the offense two games into his reunion with the Vikings ahead of a Week 12 visit from the Falcons, with whom Cousins spent the previous two seasons.

headline: Cousins completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns with one interception in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers. He added 11 rushing yards on three carries.
story: Brought back to Minnesota at the trade deadline to stabilize the offense, Cousins did exactly that, connecting with Myles Price for a 38-yard TD in the first quarter and Gavin Bartholomew on a 20-yard score in the fourth while guiding Justin Jefferson to season highs in catches and targets. The Vikings' passing game didn't need to over-extend itself, however, as the defense sacked Jordan Love eight times in another dominant performance. Cousins may need to find another gear in Week 11 against the 49ers, but he'll have another week of practice to re-familiarize himself with Kevin O'Connell's scheme first.

headline: The Vikings have already gauged Cousins' interest in returning to the team in 2027 since acquiring him Tuesday in a trade with the Raiders, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Cousins -- who will start Sunday's game in Green Bay as he dons a Minnesota uniform for the first time since 2023 -- is set to become a free agent in the spring, but if all goes well over the next several weeks, the Vikings are hoping that the 38-year-old quarterback can be more than just a half-season rental. At the very least, the Vikings are counting on Cousins to provide a short-term upgrade under center from the likes of Kyler Murray (hamstring) and Carson Wentz, both of whom struggled to move the chains while Minnesota raced to a 6-2 start thanks in large part to its blitz-happy, aggressive defense. During his time in Las Vegas, Cousins tossed 20 touchdown passes (second in NFL) and compiled 2,340 passing yards (fifth in NFL), despite playing alongside one of the league's weaker wide-receiver groups.

headline: Head coach Kevin O'Connell announced Friday that Cousins will start Sunday's contest at Green Bay.
story: Cousins was acquired from the Raiders before Tuesday's trade deadline, and after leading the first-team offense during the entirety of Week 10 prep, he'll get the nod under center in his return to Minnesota. In nine starts with Las Vegas this season, he completed 202 of 315 passes (64 percent) for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions while adding two more TDs on the ground.

headline: Cousins is expected to start Sunday's game against the Packers, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: The Vikings acquired Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday, and unsurprisingly he's trending toward being immediately installed as the starter, as his new team is in the midst of a two-game skid. With Kyler Murray (hamstring) viewed as week-to-week, Carson Wentz (ankle, limited at practice Thursday) -- if available -- and Max Brosmer profile as his Week 10 backup options. Prior to being dealt, Cousins was playing well for Las Vegas, and his addition to the Minnesota offense should result in a boost for the team's top pass catchers, Justin Jefferson, T.J. Hockenson and Jordan Addison.

headline: Head coach Kevin O'Connell said Wednesday that he isn't ready to commit to Cousins as the Vikings' Week 10 starting quarterback, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Minnesota acquired Cousins via trade from Las Vegas on Tuesday, but even though he has experience working under O'Connell from his previous stint with the team in 2022 and 2023, the coach will wait to make a decision. It appears Kyler Murray (hamstring) is set to miss another game Sunday at Green Bay, meaning Cousins, Carson Wentz (ankle) and Max Brosmer are the options to get the call this weekend.

headline: Jefferson caught seven of nine targets for 86 yards and lost a fumble in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the 49ers.
story: Jefferson has experienced an uptick in usage since the Vikings reacquired Kirk Cousins. The star WR has 16 catches for 160 yards on 22 targets in two games with Cousins, though Jefferson hasn't scored since Week 8. Jefferson fumbled at the end of a 25-yard catch in the third quarter, turning what would have been one of his best plays of the night into a lowlight. Another heavy dose of targets from Cousins likely awaits Jefferson in Week 12 against the Falcons.

headline: Jefferson caught nine of 13 targets for 74 yards in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers.
story: In Kirk Cousins' return to the Vikings, Jefferson led the team in catches, targets and receiving yards, although Myles Price and Gavin Bartholomew were on the other end of the QB's two touchdown passes. The nine grabs and 13 targets were season highs for Jefferson, while the yardage total was his best showing since Week 5. Despite a disappointing 40-467-4 line on 64 targets through eight games, the star wideout's outlook for the rest of the year is pointed up heading into a Week 11 clash with the 49ers.

headline: Jefferson stands to benefit from Tuesday's acquisition of Kirk Cousins, who is expected to take over as the Vikings' starting quarterback beginning with Sunday's game against the Packers, Michael F. Florio of ESPN.com reports.
story: Jefferson averaged a career-low 56.1 receiving yards per game through the first eight contests while the Vikings had the likes of Kyler Murray (hamstring), Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer under center, but the star receiver looks to be one of the biggest winners in the aftermath of the deadline. He'll be reunited with Cousins, who was at the helm for Jefferson's first four years in the league, when the wideout averaged 98.0 yards per contest and had a 17-game pace of 1,671 yards and 8.5 touchdowns. Though Cousins is three years older than when he last donned a Vikings uniform, he enjoyed a resurgent start to the season in Las Vegas, ranking second in the NFL in passing touchdowns (20) and fifth in passing yards (2,340) despite playing behind a weak offensive line and working with an underwhelming receiver group. Cousins' hot start and history with Jefferson should give Jefferson's fantasy managers added confidence in his rest-of-season outlook.

headline: Jefferson brought in three of 11 targets for 58 yards in the Vikings' 23-6 loss to the Bills on Monday night.
story: Jefferson led the Vikings in receiving yards and targets, but the insertion of Carson Wentz at quarterback in place of Kyler Murray (hamstring) led to a very inefficient night for the star receiver. Jefferson's final catch of the night, which went for a 19-yard gain, came on a pass from Max Brosmer, so Jefferson secured just two of the 10 targets that an ineffective Wentz sent his way. Jefferson has been having a generally quiet season even when working with Murray -- he doesn't have any 100-yard games and has posted Monday night's yardage total or less in five of seven games -- but his outlook would be brighter if Murray can return for Sunday's Week 10 road showdown against the Packers.

headline: Jefferson brought in five of nine targets for 33 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings' 19-15 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
story: Jefferson led the Vikings in receptions with the aid of a team-high target total, and the highlight of the perennial Pro Bowler's afternoon was his touchdown grab. Jefferson stuck his hand up and tapped Kyler Murray's (hamstring) pass to himself while in tight coverage in the left corner of the end zone early in the second quarter, ultimately securing a memorable one-yard score. Jefferson has topped 50 receiving yards just three times and is still in search of his first 100-yard game of the season, but he's found the end zone in two of the last three games heading into a Week 9 home showdown against the Bills on Monday night, Nov. 9.

headline: Jefferson caught four of seven targets for 44 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts.
story: The targets and receiving yards actually led the Vikings in a low-scoring defensive battle, but it was T.J. Hockenson on the other end of Kyler Murray's only TD pass. Jefferson is still looking for his first 100-yard performance of the season, and he's been held under 60 yards in three of his five games. The star wideout could be poised to finally break out in Week 8 against the Lions' struggling secondary.

headline: Jefferson (ankle) practiced in full Thursday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Jefferson's upgrade from limited Wednesday to uncapped one day later indicates that the ankle injury that has bothered him since the middle of a Week 3 win at Tampa Bay is behind him. He'll be taking on a Colts defense Sunday that has allowed the 10th-most yards per target (8.6) to opposing wide receivers this season.

headline: Jefferson (ankle) was limited at Wednesday's practice.
story: Despite having the benefit of a Week 6 bye, Jefferson appears to still be dealing with the ankle injury that he suffered in Week 3 and that forced his inactive status in Week 4 before he suited up in Week 5 at New Orleans, when he hauled in six of seven targets for 79 yards and one touchdown. Meanwhile, fellow WR Jordan Addison (hamstring) practiced fully Wednesday, meaning Jefferson has a bit of work to do to get the top of the Vikings' receiving corps back to 100 percent.

headline: Jefferson (ankle) brought in six of seven targets for 79 yards and a touchdown and rushed once for minus-11 yards in the Vikings' 23-13 win over the Saints on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that remained with Minnesota.
story: Making his return from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury, Jefferson capitalized on an opportunity to perform in front of his home-state crowd. The perennial Pro Bowler was expected to be busy due to Jordan Addison's (hamstring) inactive status, and Jefferson ultimately led the Vikings across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets. The veteran receiver added his first touchdown since Week 1 when he recorded an impressive 15-yard scoring grab in the back corner of the end zone to cap off the first possession of the second half, and Jefferson will next set his sights on a vulnerable Colts defense in a Week 7 home matchup on Sunday, Oct. 25 following a Week 6 bye.

headline: Jefferson (ankle) is listed as active Sunday at New Orleans.
story: Jefferson thus is set for his first in-game action since the second quarter of a Week 3 win in Tampa Bay, when he initially picked up a left ankle injury. After sitting out last Sunday versus the Dolphins, he logged three limited sessions during Week 5 prep, and with his status confirmed for Sunday, there's a good chance he serves as the top pass catcher for QB Kyler Murray with fellow WR Jordan Addison (hamstring) inactive, even if Jefferson can't handle a full workload.

headline: Jefferson (ankle) will go through a pregame workout before the Vikings make a decision on his availability for Sunday's contest at New Orleans, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Jefferson hasn't played a snap since injuring his left ankle in the second quarter of a Week 3 win at Tampa Bay, but he relayed to Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com on Wednesday that he was determined to suit up for a game in his home state of Louisiana. Limited practices Wednesday through Friday left Jefferson questionable for Week 5 action, and the upcoming workout will determine whether or not he's included among Minnesota's inactives about 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. The same can be said for fellow WR Jordan Addison (hamstring), which will leave the receiving corps particularly short-handed if both of them are sidelined.

headline: Jefferson (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at New Orleans.
story: The same can be said for fellow WR Jordan Addison (hamstring). Jefferson himself is looking to miss just one game due to an ankle injury that he picked up in a Week 3 win at Tampa Bay, and his status will be confirmed, one way or another, about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Jefferson (ankle) and Jordan Addison (hamstring) were at practice Friday, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
story: It's unclear if either wide receiver was a full participant, but this does suggest that both have a chance to play Sunday in New Orleans.

headline: Jefferson (ankle) was limited at practice Thursday.
story: Jefferson initially injured his ankle in the middle of a Week 3 win at Tampa Bay and missed this past Sunday's game against the Dolphins. So far this week, he's logged back-to-back capped sessions, and Friday's practice report may provide some clarity regarding whether or not a return to action Sunday in New Orleans is possible. For what it's worth, Jefferson told Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com on Wednesday that he wants to play this weekend as a native of Louisiana, but ultimately it'll be a team decision regarding his status.

headline: Jefferson (ankle) said Wednesday that he's aiming to play Sunday at New Orleans, Kevin Seifert of ESPN reports.
story: Coach Kevin O'Connell provided an update on Jefferson earlier Wednesday, saying the wide receiver "is doing well" and will be limited to begin Week 5 prep. Jefferson's ensuing activity level indeed was limited, but per the player himself he wants to play against the Saints as a native of Louisiana. The Vikings will take the situation "day by day," and his listing on Friday's practice report may be telling for his odds to suit up this weekend.

headline: Coach Kevin O'Connell said Jefferson (ankle) "is doing well" and will be a limited practice participant Wednesday.
story: This will mark Jefferson's first on-field work since he suffered a sprained left ankle in the second quarter of a Week 3 win at Tampa Bay. Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reported Saturday morning that the Vikings are hopeful that Jefferson will return to action in Week 5, and his ability to practice in any capacity Wednesday is a step in that direction.

headline: Jefferson (ankle) has been already been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, but the Vikings are hopeful that the superstar wide receiver will return for Week 5 against the Saints, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
story: Jefferson was removed from the Vikings' Week 3 win over the Buccaneers due to an ankle injury. Additional tests showed a minor ankle sprain for the seventh-year pro, and while he won't play Sunday, a return to practice during Week 5 prep would put Jefferson on track to play against New Orleans. Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings and tight end T.J. Hockenson will be Kyler Murray's top targets against Miami in Jefferson's absence.

headline: Jefferson (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game versus the Dolphins.
story: Jefferson wasn't able to practice this week due to the ankle injury that forced him out of this past Sunday's win at Tampa Bay. His next chance to suit up will be Sunday, Oct. 11 at New Orleans, but considering the Vikings have a Week 6 bye, the team could exercise caution with its top wide receiver with the second half of the campaign in mind. In any case, Jordan Addison is poised to serve as Minnesota's top pass catcher in the short term, with fellow WR Jauan Jennings, TE T.J. Hockenson and RB Aaron Jones likely next up for targets from QB Kyler Murray.

headline: Jefferson (ankle) remained absent from Friday's practice, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
story: Jefferson hasn't practiced at all this week after twisting his ankle seven snaps into last Sunday's game against the Bucs. It's looking likely that Jefferson will now miss Week 4 against Miami. If so, Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings and Tai Felton should see the bulk of the wideout snaps for the Vikings.

headline: Jefferson (ankle) officially didn't participate in Thursday's practice.
story: Jefferson has yet to log any on-field reps since suffering an ankle injury in the first half of this past Sunday's win at Tampa Bay. He thus will have just one more chance to mix into drills Friday, at which point he'll likely receive a game designation ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Dolphins.

headline: Brosmer (coach's decision) is inactive but operating as the Vikings' emergency third QB on Sunday night versus the 49ers.
story: Brosmer will operate as the team's No. 3 option at QB for the second straight week. He will only be eligible to enter the game if both starter Kirk Cousins and primary backup Carson Wentz are forced out of the contest.

headline: Brosmer (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Vikings' emergency third quarterback against the Packers on Sunday.
story: Brosmer was the Vikings' backup for Week 9 against the Bills and ended up seeing the field late in the fourth quarter, when he completed six of seven pass attempts for 58 yards. The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins from the Raiders on Tuesday, and he will serve as Minnesota's starter Sunday while Carson Wentz operates as the backup. With Kyler Murray (hamstring) sidelined, that leaves Brosmer as the emergency QB3, which prohibits the latter from playing unless both Cousins and Wentz leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Brosmer completed six of seven attempts for 58 yards in Monday night's 23-6 loss to the Bills.
story: Brosmer replaced Carson Wentz in the fourth quarter of Monday night's game after the offense failed to produce a touchdown drive. Week 9 was Brosmer's first appearance in a 2026 regular-season game. He will likely play a similar backup role behind newly acquired Kirk Cousins as the season progresses, at least until Kyler Murray returns from a hamstring injury.

headline: Brosmer is set to back up Carson Wentz against the Bills on Monday, as Kyler Murray (hamstring) won't play, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports.
story: It would likely take an injury to Wentz for Brosmer to get into the game, but the latter moves one step closer to getting on the field for the first time in 2026. Brosmer didn't look like an NFL-caliber QB as a rookie in 2025, posting a 0:4 TD:INT across seven appearances, including two starts.

headline: Brosmer (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Vikings' emergency third quarterback against the Lions on Sunday.
story: As the emergency QB3, Brosmer is prohibited from playing Sunday unless both Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Brosmer (coach's decision) is listed as inactive but will serve as the Vikings' third quarterback for Sunday's games versus the Colts.
story: Brosmer remains the emergency reserve quarterback behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz. Brosmer will only enter the game if both Murray and Wentz must depart due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Brosmer (coach's decision) is listed as inactive but will serve as the Vikings' third quarterback for Sunday's games versus the Saints, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
story: Brosmer joined the Vikings' 53-man roster in early October after the team traded away J.J. McCarthy. The 25-year-old is not available to play against the Saints unless both Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz are taken out of the game due to an injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Brosmer (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Vikings' emergency third quarterback against the Dolphins on Sunday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
story: Brosmer was signed to the 53-man roster Tuesday after the Vikings traded J.J. McCarthy to the Giants a day earlier. As the emergency third quarterback, Brosmer is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz are taken out of the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: The Vikings signed Brosmer off their practice squad Tuesday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
story: With the Vikings trading J.J. McCarthy to the Giants on Monday, Brosmer will be awarded a spot on Minnesota's 53-man roster and slot in as the new No. 3 quarterback behind Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz. As an undrafted rookie last season, Brosmer appeared in eight games for the Vikings and completed 47 of 71 pass attempts for 328 yards, zero touchdowns and four interceptions while carrying seven times for 11 yards and also losing a fumble.

headline: Jones (shoulder) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.
story: Jones -- who was managing a shoulder injury during Week 11 prep -- was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. He was signed to the Vikings' 53-man roster Wednesday to give the team more depth at wide receiver while Jordan Addison recovers from a thumb injury. Jones figures to be limited to a rotational role on offense while serving as a contributor on special teams.

headline: The Vikings signed Jones (shoulder) off the practice squad to the active roster Wednesday.
story: Jones was elevated from the Vikings' practice squad to the active roster for both Week 5 and Week 10 against the Saints and Packers, respectively, and he'll now be part of Minnesota's 53-man roster moving forward. He picked up a shoulder injury during Sunday's 30-10 win over Green Bay and was listed as a limited participant during Wednesday's practice, so his reps over the coming days will provide clarity on his chances of playing against the 49ers on Nov. 22. The addition of Jones to the active roster gives the Vikings extra depth at wide receiver in the absence of Jordan Addison (thumb).

headline: Jones (shoulder) reverted to the Vikings' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's official transaction log.
story: Jones was elevated to the active roster to help fill in for Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf) in Sunday's 30-10 win over the Packers, but he didn't record any stats while playing six snaps on offense and 11 with the special-teams unit. The wide receiver also picked up a shoulder injury in the contest, and the severity of the issue is currently unknown. Jones has already been elevated three times, so Minnesota would have to officially sign him to the active roster in order for him to appear in another contest with the team this season.

headline: Jones (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Packers.
story: Jones is being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. He was a practice squad elevation Saturday to give the Vikings more depth at wide receiver due to the absences of both Jordan Addison (thumb) and Jauan Jennings (calf).

headline: The Vikings elevated Jones from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday.
story: Jones has gotten into two games so far this season, catching his lone target for a 32-yard gain over nine offensive snaps. With Jauan Jennings (calf) ruled out for Sunday's battle against Green Bay and Jordan Addison (thumb) deemed questionable, Jones could serve as important depth at wideout for Kirk Cousins in the veteran quarterback's 2026 Minnesota debut.

headline: Jones reverted to Minnesota's practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: Jones was elevated ahead of Sunday's Week 5 win over New Orleans and caught his only target for 32 yards on six offensive snaps. He also logged 11 snaps on special teams and recovered a fumble on kick coverage. Jones' opportunity was partly a result of Jordan Addison (hamstring) being inactive and Odell Beckham being a healthy scratch, so there's no guarantee that Jones will be elevated again Week 7 versus Indianapolis following Minnesota's Week 6 bye.

headline: The Vikings elevated Jones from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
story: The Vikings elevated both Jones and Odell Beckham from the practice squad, giving the team insurance at wide receiver in case one or both of Justin Jefferson (ankle) or Jordan Addison (hamstring) cannot play against the Saints on Sunday. Jones played 14 snaps (three on offense, 11 on special teams) without showing up in the box score otherwise during the Vikings' Week 4 win over the Dolphins.

headline: The Vikings signed Jones to the practice squad Wednesday.
story: Jones was active for Sunday's win over Miami but didn't log a snap. He was waived Monday, though he will remain in Minnesota for now as a member of the practice squad.

headline: The Vikings waived Jones on Monday.
story: Jones served a three-game suspension to begin the 2026 regular season for violating the NFL's substance abuse policy. The wide receiver suited up for the Vikings' Week 4 win over the Dolphins but did not play a single snap in the contest. If Jones clears waivers, he will become a free agent who can sign with any franchise.

headline: Van Ginkel (quadriceps) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the 49ers in Mexico City.
story: Van Ginkel's practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday while managing a quadriceps injury that he sustained in Week 10 against the Packers. He was a full participant in Friday's session, which was enough for the veteran edge rusher to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. In Van Ginkel's four outings since the Vikings' Week 6 bye, he has accumulated 14 tackles (eight solo), including 4.5 sacks, one forced fumble and one fumble recovery.

headline: Van Ginkel (quadriceps) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Van Ginkel sustained a quadriceps injury during the Vikings' 30-10 win over the Packers in Week 10. His ability to practice Wednesday indicates that the injury isn't a serious one, and an increase in participation over the coming days would put Van Ginkel on track to play in Sunday's road game against the 49ers in Mexico City.

headline: Van Ginkel (quadriceps) is expected to practice ahead of a Week 11 road matchup against the 49ers, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reported Monday.
story: Van Ginkel sustained a quad injury late in Sunday's game against Green Bay. The 31-year-old has yet to miss a regular-season game in 2026, recording 28 tackles (16 solo), including 8.5 sacks, and one interception in nine contests.

headline: Van Ginkel (quadriceps) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Packers.
story: It appeared that Van Ginkel sustained his injury during the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest. Blake Cashman (concussion) is inactive, so Jake Golday is in line for more defensive snaps at linebacker for as long as Van Ginkel is being evaluated by medical staff.

headline: Van Ginkel (chest) doesn't have a designation for Monday's matchup against the Bills, Craig Peters of the Vikings' official site reports.
story: Van Ginkel was limited in practice Wednesday and Thursday but was able to upgrade to full participation Saturday. He's thus clear to suit up on Monday Night Football against the Bills. That's a big deal for the Vikings in their quest to slow down Josh Allen, as Van Ginkel leads the team with 6.5 sacks through seven games.

headline: Van Ginkel (chest) was limited in Thursday's practice.
story: Van Ginkel played through the issue last week against the Lions and piled up 2.5 sacks in the loss. The veteran edge rusher has 21 tackles (11 solo), including 6.5 sacks, one interception, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery across seven games this season.

headline: Van Ginkel logged four tackles, including 2.5 sacks, in Sunday's loss to the Lions.
story: The Vikings lost their first game of the campaign, but their defense continued to be ferocious. That was largely due to Van Ginkel, who brought down Jared Goff three times -- two solo and one assisted -- in the first half. That pushed the veteran pass rusher up to 6.5 sacks on the season, tied for fifth-most in the NFL.

headline: Van Noy (calf) is active for Sunday's game against the Packers.
story: Van Noy tweaked his calf during the Vikings' Week 9 loss to the Bills. He earned the questionable tag for Week 10 after logging a limited practice Friday, and he was cleared by medical staff to play in Sunday's NFC North showdown. Van Noy has 15 tackles (nine solo), including 1.5 sacks, through eight regular-season games.

headline: Van Noy (calf) has returned to Monday night's matchup with Buffalo, Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com reports.
story: Van Noy was briefly sidelined with a calf injury in the first quarter, but he has now returned to action. The 35-year-old will continue to operate in his primary reserve role at weak-side linebacker versus the Bills.

headline: Van Noy (calf) is questionable to return to Monday night's contest against the Bills.
story: Van Noy picked up a calf injury early in the first quarter, and his status for the rest of the game is now uncertain. In his absence, Chaz Chambliss and Bo Richter are both candidates to see an increase in opportunities at linebacker versus Buffalo.

headline: The Vikings signed Van Noy from the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday, Craig Peters of the team's official site reports.
story: The Vikings burned through Van Noy's practice-squad elevations by playing the veteran linebacker in each of the team's three wins to start the 2026 regular season. Van Noy logged 59 defensive snaps over the three contests, totaling seven tackles (five solo), including 1.5 sacks. The 35-year-old will now serve as a key rotational edge rusher for the team, this time on the 53-man roster.

headline: Rouse (concussion) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
story: Rouse missed the Patriots' last game before their bye in Week 11 due to a concussion, but after logging a full practice Friday, it looks like there's a chance he could return in Week 12. If he doesn't, Ben Brown could end up being the Patriots' unquestioned top option off the bench on the interior of the offensive line Sunday.

headline: Rouse (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
story: Rouse is in the league's concussion protocol, which prevented him from playing in Week 10 against the Lions in Munich. Despite the extra rest courtesy of the Week 11 bye, the third-year pro has not progressed enough in his recovery to return to practice. Even if he practices over the coming days, an independent neurologist would need to clear Rouse from protocol in order for him to be available for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

headline: Rouse is inactive for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich due to a concussion.
story: Rouse entered concussion protocol following last Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers and was a non-participant in practice to begin Week 10 prep. He was able to close the week with a pair of limited practices en route to taking a questionable tag into Sunday, but Rouse apparently wasn't able to clear the five-step protocol in advance of game day.

headline: Barmore (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
story: Barmore first appeared on the Patriots' Week 12 injury report Friday as a DNP, which indicates that the knee issue is a new one for the sixth-year defensive lineman. A late addition to the injury report typically isn't a good sign, but Barmore's official availability may not be known until the Patriots announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff. DaQuan Jones and Joshua Farmer would both be in line for more snaps on defense if Barmore doesn't play.

headline: Barmore (shoulder) is active Week 5 against the Raiders.
story: Barmore will make his return after missing Week 4 against Buffalo and should resume his regular role in the defensive line rotation.

headline: Barmore (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: A shoulder injury prevented Barmore from playing in the Patriots' Week 4 win over the Bills. He opened Week 5 prep with back-to-back limited practices before logging a full session Friday, but whether he can play Sunday may not be officially known until about 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, when the Patriots announce their list of inactive players. His return would revert Joshua Farmer and DaQuan Jones to rotational roles at defensive end, with Milton Williams being the other starter at the position.

headline: Barmore (shoulder) was a limited participant at the Patriots' practice Thursday.
story: Barmore has logged consecutive limited practices to open the week after failing to practice at all last week before missing the team's Week 4 win over Buffalo. The defensive lineman has been dealing with a shoulder injury since Week 3, and he'll have one more chance to log a full practice Friday prior to Sunday's matchup with Las Vegas.

headline: Barmore (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bills, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Barmore missed the entire week of practice heading into Week 4 after suffering a shoulder injury in the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars. Without the sixth-year veteran in the lineup, Cory Durden and Milton Williams will have to step up.

headline: Barmore (shoulder) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Barmore sustained a shoulder injury during the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars in Week 3, finishing with only two tackles (one solo) while playing a season-low 28 defensive snaps. He'll have two more chances to return to practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Bills. If Barmore is not cleared to play, then Joshua Farmer and Jeremiah Pharms would both be in line for larger roles against Buffalo.

headline: Spillane (illness) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
story: The veteran linebacker exited the Patriots' Week 10 game against the Lions in Germany with an illness but is fine coming out of the team's Week 11 bye. Across 10 starts this season, Spillane has recorded 58 tackles (25 solo), including 0.5 sacks, two pass breakups and a forced fumble.

headline: Spillane (illness) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
story: Spillane went to the locker room in the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's international game. Darius Muasau has taken over for Spillane at inside linebacker.

headline: Gilliam (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
story: Gilliam returned from injured reserve in Week 10 against the Lions and is now coming off the bye week, but he's still dealing with the knee issue. The fullback has touched the ball two times on offense this season, logging 71 snaps and another 56 on special teams.

headline: Gilliam (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
story: Gilliam took a questionable tag into Sunday, but the Patriots' decision to activate him from injured reserve Saturday signaled that he was on track to play for the first time since Week 4. The fullback served almost exclusively as a blocker when he was healthy during the Patriots' first four games of the season, logging no carries and recording a four-yard reception on two targets.

headline: The Patriots activated Gilliam (knee), who remains questionable for Sunday's game against Detroit, from injured reserve Saturday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Gilliam landed on IR on Oct. 10 and had his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday. By coming off injured reserve Saturday, the veteran fullback has a chance to suit up Sunday, though he remains officially questionable. Gilliam was limited in all three of New England's practice this week.

headline: Gilliam (ankle) was designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: The fullback hasn't played since Week 4. He's logged 58 snaps on offense and another 39 on special teams across four appearances this season.

headline: The Patriots placed Gilliam (ankle/knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Gilliam will be sidelined for a minimum of four games. The fullback has logged 58 offensive snaps through the first four weeks of the season, with another 39 on special teams.

headline: Gilliam (ankle/knee) has been ruled out against the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Gilliam was able to play through an ankle injury that he picked up during the Patriots' Week 4 win over the Bills, but he ended Week 5 prep with back-to-back DNPs while dealing with that issue and a new knee injury. The Patriots don't have another fullback on the active roster nor the practice squad, so they could turn to tight ends like Eli Raridon, Cameron Latu and Tanner Arkin to serve as backfield blockers in Gilliam's absence. Gilliam's next chance to suit up is Week 6 against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 18.

headline: Gilliam (ankle) did not participate at the Patriots' practice Thursday.
story: Gilliam opened the week as a limited participant Wednesday, but he took a step backwards one day later. The fullback is nursing an ankle injury that he suffered in the team's Week 4 win over the Bills, and he'll have one more chance to practice before Sunday's contest versus Las Vegas.

headline: Gilliam (ankle) has returned to Sunday's game against the Bills, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Gilliam had to be carted off the field after sustaining an ankle injury. However, the veteran fullback passed the medical staff's tests and was back on the field for the second half.

headline: Gilliam (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bills.
story: Gilliam injured his ankle during the first quarter, and the injury was severe enough for him to be taken to the locker room, where he'll undergo further tests to determine whether he can return. The Patriots don't have another fullback on the roster, so they could turn to tight ends Cameron Latu and Eli Raridon to serve as blockers out of the backfield while Gilliam is out of the game.

headline: Gilliam (knee) is active against the Bills on Sunday.
story: The veteran fullback has been working through a knee injury, but he's been cleared by medical staff to play after going through pregame warmups. Gilliam spent the first six years of his NFL career with the Bills before signing a three-year contract with the Patriots in March.

headline: Gilliam (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Buffalo, Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports.
story: Gilliam has been working through a knee injury the past couple of weeks, but he's drawn the questionable tag for Week 4 after fading such a designation for Week 3 against the Jaguars. He's contributed on special teams and has worked mostly as a blocker on offense, so if Gilliam is not cleared to play against the Bills, then the Patriots may turn to tight ends Cameron Latu or Eli Raridon (thigh) to block out of the backfield.

headline: Gilliam (knee) did not practice Thursday.
story: Gilliam was limited during Wednesday's practice, though he saw a worrisome downgrade Thursday. As a result, he may carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's AFC East showdown with Buffalo, assuming he's not ruled out altogether before then. The 29-year-old appeared in the Patriots' first three games of the 2026 campaign, catching one pass (two targets) for four yards.

headline: Gilliam (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Gilliam was able to play in the Patriots' Week 3 loss to the Jaguars after working through a knee issue during practice prep. He played a total of 19 snaps (eight on offense, 11 on special teams) without showing up on the box score otherwise. Gilliam will have two more opportunities to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation for Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Bills.

headline: Davis (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Despite the extra rest courtesy of the Week 11 bye, Davis was unable to participate in any of the Week 12 practices due to a knee injury and will be sidelined for a second consecutive game. Charles Woods will likely start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback Sunday in the absence of Davis, whose next chance to suit up is Week 13 against the Bills on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Davis (knee) didn't practice Wednesday.
story: Davis didn't travel with the Patriots to Munich for Week 10 against the Lions due to a knee injury that he sustained against the Packers in Week 9. Even with the extra rest courtesy of the bye, Davis has not been cleared by medical staff to return to practice. He would need to log a limited session over the next two days to have a realistic shot of playing Sunday against the Chargers.

headline: Davis (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Davis suffered a knee injury during the Patriots' loss to the Packers this past Sunday. New England already ruled out the veteran defensive back for Week 10, so Charles Woods (hamstring), Channing Canada and Karon Prunty figure to be the top candidates to start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so Davis will have more time to recover for Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Davis (knee) is questionable to return to New England's matchup Sunday versus the Packers.
story: Davis is in danger of missing the remainder of the game after suffering a knee injury in the second half. Channing Canada and Karon Prunty could be in line for an uptick in playing time if Davis is unable to return to the matchup.

headline: Davis (neck) is active against the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Davis has been cleared to return form a three-game absence due to a neck injury he picked up in Week 4 against the Bills. He'll resume his starting role at outside cornerback opposite Christian Gonzalez while Charles Woods provides depth at the position.

headline: Davis (neck) is questionable for Sunday's Week 8 contest in Miami.
story: Davis hasn't played since Week 4 because of a neck injury. It's promising that he logged a trio of full practices this week, but New England isn't yet committing to him returning to action against the Dolphins. Should Davis end up missing the matchup, Charles Woods would likely draw another start.

headline: Davis (neck) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Davis has finally returned to full participation after missing three consecutive games with a neck injury. The starting cornerback should be able to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins as long as he maintains full participation through Friday's practice session.

headline: Davis (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Thursday night's game against the Bears.
story: Davis did not participate in Monday's practice but ended the Patriots' short Week 7 prep with back-to-back limited sessions. Despite the upgrade in practice participation, the cornerback is not quite ready to return to the field and will miss his third consecutive game with a neck injury. Charles Woods should once again start opposite Christian Gonzalez at outside cornerback.

headline: Davis (neck) was a limited participant in Tuesday's practice.
story: Davis has missed the Patriots' last two games due to a neck injury, but it was a promising sign to see him on the field for Tuesday's practice, even in a limited capacity. The Patriots will announce injury designations following Wednesday's practice, at which point Davis' status for Thursday's game against the Bears will be clearer. If he's not cleared to return, then Charles Woods likely will remain the Patriots' second starting outside cornerback opposite Christian Gonzalez.

headline: Davis (neck) did not participate in Monday's estimated practice.
story: Davis has not practiced since sustaining his neck injury, and that remained the case to start Week 7 prep. If the cornerback cannot get on the practice field by Wednesday's session, he'll have almost no chance of suiting up for the Patriots' Thursday night game against the Bears.

headline: Davis (neck) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Davis has not practiced since aggravating a neck injury in the Patriots' Week 4 win over the Bills. The cornerback remains without a set return timeline, and it is unclear how much longer he will be unable to practice.

headline: Davis (neck) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Davis was held out of practice all week due to a neck injury, slimming down a Patriots secondary that will also be without Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), Channing Canada (hamstring) and rookie Karon Prunty (hamstring), with Charles Woods (shoulder) and Craig Woodson (shoulder) listed as questionable. Woods would presumably be one of the starting outside cornerbacks if cleared to play Sunday, but with Davis and Gonzalez both sidelined, the Patriots may have to turn to Marcus Jones, Mike Brown, Jaylen Reed or another defensive back from the practice squad to fill in the second starting spot. Davis' next opportunity to play is Week 6 against the Jets on Sunday, Oct. 18.

headline: Davis (neck) did not participate at the Patriots' practice Thursday.
story: Davis has missed back-to-back practices to open the week with a neck injury that he may have suffered in Week 4 versus Buffalo. The cornerback will have one more chance to return to practice Friday before Sunday's matchup with the Raiders.

headline: Douglas is set to maintain a prominent role Sunday against the Chargers, as A.J. Brown (hamstring) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder, IR) won't play.
story: Douglas had 178 yards and a touchdown in a career-best two-game stretch spanning Weeks 8 and 9, but he was limited to one catch for four yards in his most recent appearance, which QB Drake Maye (lower leg) left early. With Tommy DeVito under center in Week 12, Douglas will try to get back on track in New England's banged-up passing game coming out of a bye week.

headline: Douglas caught one of three passes for four yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
story: The Patriots' offense was effective on the first drive of the game, but that was where the good news ended for New England after Drake Maye was knocked out for the rest of the contest due to an ankle injury. Tommy DeVito took over under center, and the offense struggled to move down the field for the rest of the game. For Douglas, it was the third time this season that he was held to one catch, with the last instance taking place in Week 3 against the Jaguars. A.J. Brown -- who was cleared to return from a two-game absence due to knee and ankle injuries -- also picked up a hamstring injury during Sunday's game, so Douglas could be the New England's WR1 following the Week 11 bye. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Douglas brought in five of nine targets for 102 yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
story: Douglas tied for the team lead in receptions and set the pace in both receiving yards and targets while serving as Drake Maye's top target in the absence of A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder). Douglas also recorded a team-high 36-yard grab among his five catches, and both the yardage and target tallies were season highs. Douglas has at least 76 receiving yards in three of the past four games heading into a Week 10 matchup against the Lions in Germany next Sunday.

headline: Douglas caught all three of his targets for 76 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins.
story: Most of his production came on a nifty 48-yard catch-and-run in the fourth quarter, as Douglas took a strike from Drake Maye along the sideline but then curled back toward the middle of the field and dashed the remaining 30 yards to the end zone while out-racing four Miami defenders. It was the fourth touchdown of the season for the fourth-year wideout, a new career high, and Douglas will take a 26-332-4 line on 37 targets through eight games into a Week 9 tilt against the Packers.

headline: Douglas caught three of his four targets for 23 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
story: Douglas played 35 of the Patriots' 54 offensive snaps in the contest and did not find the end zone. The wide receiver had logged three touchdowns in the prior two contests but has now returned to a role with lower priority as A.J. Brown becomes reacquainted with the offense.

headline: Douglas caught seven of eight targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets.
story: A.J. Brown returned to the lineup from his ankle injury and led the team with 10 targets, but he dropped multiple passes and finished with a 3-27-0 receiving line. After Romeo Doubs left with a shoulder injury early in the first half following a long touchdown grab, Douglas stepped into an increased offensive role. He ran 26 routes on Drake Maye's 35 dropbacks, and Douglas caught a nine-yard touchdown in the second quarter. He's posted back-to-back big box scores after logging 4-65-2 receiving last Sunday against Las Vegas. The Patriots' slot man doesn't have a big fantasy ceiling but looks like a passable WR4 during bye-week crunches headed into Thursday night's game against the Bears.

headline: Douglas caught four of five targets for 65 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders.
story: The fourth-year wideout put together the first two-TD game of his career, connecting with Drake Maye for a 35-yard strike in the first quarter and an eight-yard toss in the fourth to bookend the Patriots' offensive eruption. The scores were Douglas' first of 2026, and through five games he's produced an otherwise modest 13-147-2 line on 22 targets. With Maye regaining his swagger and New England's WR room depleted by injuries, however, there could be more big performances coming for Douglas. He'll carry plenty of momentum into a Week 6 clash with the Jets.

headline: Douglas caught two of three targets for 15 yards during Sunday's 29-26 win over Buffalo.
story: Douglas didn't really make much of a splash in Week 4, but he was able to reel in multiple passes for the first time since Week 1. The wide receiver could step into a more prominent role beginning in Week 5 against the Raiders after Mack Hollins suffered a calf injury in Sunday's victory. Through four contests this season, Douglas has caught nine of 17 targets for 82 yards.

headline: Douglas caught one of his five targets for 38 yards in the Patriots' 35-6 loss to the Jaguars on Sunday.
story: Douglas played 60 percent of the Patriots' offensive snaps in the loss. The sole ball the wide receiver was able to haul in went for a 38-yard gain, marking quarterback Drake Maye's longest pass of the afternoon. Douglas continues to be a threat out of the slot for a struggling Patriots offense.

headline: Hollins is set to work in a starting role Sunday against the Chargers, as A.J. Brown (hamstring) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder, IR) won't play.
story: Hollins led the Patriots with five catches for 48 yards in their 35-10 Week 10 loss to the Lions prior to a Week 11 bye. He showed the best chemistry out of New England's pass catchers with Tommy DeVito, who replaced Drake Maye (lower leg) against Detroit and is expected to start Sunday's game. Hollins has 23 catches for 293 yards and one touchdown in six appearances this season.

headline: Hollins caught five of six targets for 48 yards in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.
story: In his second game back from a calf injury, Hollins led the Patriots in catches and receiving yards, but the entire offense was compromised when Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early. A.J. Brown (hamstring) also didn't last long in his latest return to action. New England gets a bye in Week 11, giving the team's injured stars a chance to recover, so Hollins' role and usage may not become clear until after the break. Over six appearances this season, Hollins has produced a 23-293-1 line on 32 targets.

headline: Hollins caught three of six targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Patriots.
story: After missing four weeks on injured reserve with a calf injury, Hollins returned to the lineup Sunday and immediately became a central part of the offense, tying Kyle Williams for second on the team with 34 routes on 46 dropbacks by New England's quarterbacks. Hollins' six targets also tied Eli Raridon for second on the team behind DeMario Douglas' nine. With A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) still not 100 percent, Hollins figures to remain a big part of the picture next Sunday against the Lions in a potential shootout under the dome at Ford Field.

headline: Hollins (calf) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Packers.
story: Hollins, who had landed on IR prior to Week 5 action, was activated from IR/designated to return Saturday but still carried a 'questionable' designation ahead of the contest. In his first game action since Week 4, Hollins could make an immediate contribution to a WR corps that also includes DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams, but remains without A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder). Prior to his injury, Hollins recorded a 15/209/0 receiving line on 20 targets through four games.

headline: The Patriots activated Hollins (calf) from injured reserve Saturday, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the Packers.
story: Hollins exited a Week 4 win at Buffalo in the third quarter due to a calf injury and eventually landed on IR prior to Week 5 action. He thus has missed the requisite four games while on the list, but his status now bears watching ahead of Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff. With fellow WR A.J. Brown (knee) sidelined, an active Hollins could step into a prominent role in the Patriots passing game alongside position mate DeMario Douglas.

headline: Hollins (calf) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Packers.
story: The Patriots would need to activate Hollins from injured reserve by 4 p.m. ET on Saturday to have him available for Sunday's game against the Packers. The team could certainly use him with A.J. Brown (knee) out again, but Hollins never made it back to full practice participation, instead logging limited sessions Wednesday through Friday.

headline: Hollins (calf) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice after being designated for return from injured reserve.
story: After the Patriots opened up his 21-day evaluation window, Hollins took the field for his first practice since Week 4. Hollins will be eligible for activation from IR at any point, but unless he upgrades to full participation by the end of the week, he could have a tough time gaining clearance for Sunday's matchup with the Packers. Through New England's first four games before he sustained a calf injury, Hollins produced a 15-209-0 receiving line on 20 targets.

headline: The Patriots are expected to designate Hollins (calf) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Hollins' last game appearance came back in Week 4, but with his return to practice on the horizon, he could be an option for the Patriots as soon as this Sunday's game against the Packers. With Romeo Doubs (shoulder) currently on IR and A.J. Brown's (ankle/knee) availability for Week 9 looking cloudy, Hollins could have a chance at claiming a meaningful role right off the bat if he's cleared to play versus Green Bay. Prior to sustaining the calf injury, Hollins logged a 15-209-0 receiving line on 20 targets through New England's first four games.

headline: Hollins (calf), who is eligible to be activated from IR this week, per Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald, could return to practice Wednesday, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Hollins last saw game action in Week 4, but it's possible that his absence could be capped at the minimum mandated four contests. Prior to sustaining his calf injury, Hollins had recorded a 15-209-0 line on 20 targets, and if he's able to return to action Sunday against the Packers, a key role in the offense could await, with A.J. Brown's (ankle/knee) Week 9 status cloudy.

headline: The Patriots placed Hollins (calf) on injured reserve Saturday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Hollins was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders due to a calf injury, which is severe enough for the veteran wide receiver to require a stint on IR. As such, Hollins is prohibited from playing for at least the next four games, so the next time he can play is Week 9 against the Packers on Sunday, Nov. 8. Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will all have expanded roles on offense in Hollins' absence, though the Patriots could have A.J. Brown (ankle) back in the fold over the coming weeks.

headline: Hollins (calf) is ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: With Hollins unavailable, Romeo Doubs looks like New England's clear No. 1 receiver. DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams could all have increased roles in Hollins' absence.

headline: Hollins (calf) wasn't spotted during the portion of Thursday's practice open to media, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Hollins appears to be missing a second consecutive practice ahead of Sunday's tilt against the Raiders. If Hollins is unable to suit up Sunday, Efton Chism could work alongside Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas in three-receiver sets, while Hollins' strong blocking may be missed in the running game.

headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said that he doesn't anticipate Hollins (calf) practicing Wednesday, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Hollins is nursing a calf injury coming out of this past Sunday's win over the Bills, and his availability for the Patriots' Week 5 matchup with the Raiders is in question. If Hollins can't play this weekend, the Patriots will likely turn to Efton Chism to serve as their No. 3 wideout behind Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas.

headline: Head coach Mike Vrabel said that he expects to know more about Hollins' calf injury later Monday, and the Patriots are uncertain if the wideout will be able to practice "for a couple days," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports.
story: Hollins recorded three catches for 53 yards on four targets before exiting in the third quarter of Sunday's 29-26 win over the Bills due to the calf issue. The Patriots listed Hollins as questionable to return at the time of his departure, but he never ended up checking back into the contest. More information on the severity of Hollins' injury should be known in the next day or two, but if he ends up being unavailable for next Sunday's game against the Raiders, more reps would be opened up for Efton Chism, who helped fill in for Hollins in the fourth quarter and made an acrobatic 23-yard touchdown grab with just under two minutes remaining to seal the win over Buffalo.

headline: Hollins (calf) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bills.
story: Hollins hauled in three passes (on four targets) for 53 yards before exiting for the locker room, where he'll have his calf injury evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return to Sunday's game. Romeo Doubs, DeMario Douglas and Hunter Henry are all in line for more targets from Drake Maye while Hollins is out of the game.

headline: Doubs (shoulder), who remains on injured reserve, has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
story: Since the Patriots designated Doubs for return from injured reserve Wednesday, he logged limited listings on injury reports. However, head coach Mike Vrabel told Evan Lazar of the team's official site Friday that Doubs is unlikely to play in Week 12, which now has been confirmed. Doubs will turn his sights to a Week 13 matchup with the Bills on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Head coach Mike Vrabel said Friday that Doubs (shoulder) likely won't play in Sunday's game against the Chargers, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Doubs was designated to return from injured reserve earlier in the week, but Vrabel's comments suggest the wide receiver isn't on track to be activated ahead of Sunday's contest. If Doubs remains sidelined, Sunday would mark his fifth consecutive absence. QB Drake Maye (lower leg) and WR A.J. Brown (hamstring) have both been officially ruled out while Doubs' inactive status has yet to be confirmed.

headline: Doubs (shoulder) was listed as a limited practice participant on Thursday's estimated report.
story: The Patriots didn't hold a practice on Thanksgiving Day, but Doubs has opened Week 12 prep listed as a limited participant in back-to-back sessions. The fifth-year wide receiver was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday, and he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's road game against the Chargers. Doubs' return would bolster a Patriots' wide receiver group that will likely be without A.J. Brown (hamstring) for Week 12.

headline: Doubs (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: According to Mike Reiss of ESPN.com, Doubs did individual drills and ran routes against air, suggesting the wide receiver was especially limited after having his 21-day practice window opened earlier in the day. Doubs looks genuinely questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers.

headline: The Patriots designated Doubs (shoulder) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Doubs has missed the Patriots' last four games while recovering from the shoulder issue, but the team's decision to open his 21-day evaluation window will give him a chance at returning to action as soon as this Sunday versus the Chargers. Coming off a Week 11 bye, the Patriots will post their first Week 12 injury report Wednesday, when it will be known whether Doubs was a limited or full participant in his return to practice. After joining New England on a four-year, $68 million deal, Doubs had gotten off to a disappointing start before going down with the shoulder injury, recording 14 receptions for 261 yards and three touchdowns on 24 targets through the club's first six games.

headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that Doubs (shoulder) may be cleared to return to practice later in the week, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Doubs, who last suited up Week 6, is eligible to return from injured reserve at any point, but Vrabel's comments suggests that the wideout isn't a lock to be reinstated ahead of Sunday's game against the Chargers. With fellow wideout A.J. Brown (hamstring) unlikely to play Week 12 and potentially set to miss additional time beyond that, a prominent role in the passing attack could be available for Doubs once's he ready to play. However, Doubs will eventually make his return to an offense missing Drake Maye (fibula), with Tommy DeVito in line to replace Maye as the team's starting quarterback beginning this Sunday.

headline: Doubs (shoulder) is hopeful to return after the Patriots' Week 11 bye and isn't expected to face a long-term absence, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: With Doubs already on injured reserve, this report offers a more encouraging timeline after Sunday's shoulder injury. He'll still need to miss at least four games, but a possible return after the bye would keep the Patriots from being without one of their key wide receivers for an extended stretch. Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will be in line for increased snaps alongside A.J. Brown and slot man DeMario Douglas with Doubs sidelined.

headline: The Patriots placed Doubs (shoulder) on injured reserve Monday.
story: Just after welcoming A.J. Brown back from IR in Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets, the Patriots will have another starting wideout in Doubs land on the shelf for at least the next four games. Doubs sustained the shoulder injury while making a diving 42-yard touchdown grab in the first quarter, with the Patriots ruling him out for the rest of the game shortly thereafter. Though the extent of his shoulder injury isn't fully known, Doubs won't be eligible for activation until after the team's Week 11 bye as a result of the transaction. Doubs' upcoming absence should open up more playing time for DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams behind Brown.

headline: Doubs (shoulder) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Jets, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
