story: Doubs was injured on his 42-yard TD catch in the first quarter, after which he went to the sideline tent, and eventually, the locker room. A shoulder issue was the cause for his exit and will keep him out for the rest of Week 6. A.J. Brown, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are the Patriots' remaining healthy and available wide receivers.

headline: Doubs (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Jets.
story: Doubs recorded a 42-yard touchdown connection with QB Drake Maye in the first quarter of Week 6 action, but he was shaken up afterward, visited the sideline tent and then went to the locker room before the Patriots deemed the wide receiver questionable to return. For as long as Doubs is off the field, A.J. Brown, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will handle WR reps for New England.

headline: Doubs caught one of three targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders.
story: Six different Patriots caught at least three passes from Drake Maye as the QB tossed four TDs in total, but Doubs wasn't able to secure a share of the bounty. It was a very disappointing follow-up to his 6-58-2 line from last week given the circumstances, but with his quarterback having apparently regained his swagger, Doubs' own arrow is still pointed up. After getting blanked in his New England debut, Doubs has a 13-219-2 line on 20 targets over the last four games. He'll look to get back in the end zone in a Week 6 tilt against the Jets.

headline: Doubs secured six of nine targets for 58 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots' 29-26 win over the Bills on Sunday.
story: Doubs put together a performance befitting his current role as No. 1 receiver in the ongoing absence of A.J. Brown (ankle, IR), recording his first two touchdowns as a member of the Patriots while finishing as the team leader in receptions and targets with figures that also qualified as season highs. Doubs struck from 14 and two yards out in the first and third quarter, respectively, on his pair of scoring grabs, and after a blanking in Week 1 against Seattle, he's bounced back with a 12-203-2 line on 20 targets. Doubs will next try to make inroads against a tough Raiders defense at home in Week 5.

headline: Brown (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: With Brown unavailable following the Patriots' Week 11 bye, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are in line to handle the team's WR duties in Tommy DeVito's first start of 2026. Meanwhile, Romeo Doubs (shoulder) isn't likely to be activated from IR this weekend, so it looks like the earliest either of New England's top two wideouts could be available is Sunday, Dec. 6, against the Bills.

headline: Brown (hamstring) wasn't present for Friday's practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: With Brown set to log three straight practice 'DNPs' this week, there's a solid chance that he'll be officially ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers later Friday. If that ends up being the case, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams would be the Patriots' available WRs on the active roster, though it's possible that Romeo Doubs (shoulder) will be activated from IR ahead of Week 12 action.

headline: Brown (hamstring) was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's practice estimate.
story: Mike Reiss of ESPN.com relayed earlier this week that Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel doesn't anticipate Brown playing Sunday against the Chargers, and the wideout's consecutive 'DNP' listings Wednesday and Thursday haven't changed that narrative. Friday's final injury report will clarify whether Brown has any chance of playing this weekend, but on the plus side for the Patriots, it's possible that fellow WR Romeo Doubs (shoulder) is activated off IR ahead of Week 12 action.

headline: Brown (hamstring) didn't take part in practice Wednesday, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Coming out of a Week 11 bye, Brown didn't take any reps during the two bonus practices the Patriots held Monday and Tuesday, so it comes as little surprise that he was absent from the team's first official practice of Week 12. Head coach Mike Vrabel has already acknowledged that Brown isn't expected to play Sunday versus the Chargers, but the Patriots will likely wait until after Friday's practice before officially ruling the receiver out for that contest.

headline: Brown (hamstring) wasn't spotted on the field for Tuesday's unofficial practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: New England won't publish its next injury report until Wednesday, but Brown seems unlikely to practice in any capacity this week after head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that he didn't anticipate the wideout playing this Sunday against the Chargers. Assuming Brown ends up being ruled out for the Week 12 contest, the Patriots will be left with Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams as their main options at receiver.

headline: Brown (hamstring) wasn't on the field Monday for the Patriots' unofficial practice session, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said earlier Monday that he doesn't anticipate Brown being available for Sunday's game against the Chargers, so the veteran wideout's absence from practice hardly comes as a surprise. The Patriots likely will wait until they post their final Week 12 injury report Friday before formally ruling Brown out in what would mark his seventh missed game of the season. Brown was previously sidelined from Weeks 2 through 5 due to a right high-ankle sprain and Weeks 8 and 9 after a knee issue flared up.

headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said that he doesn't anticipate Brown (hamstring) playing Sunday against the Chargers, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Brown exited the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich on Nov. 15 due to the hamstring injury, and the wideout still needs more time to heal following the team's Week 11 bye. Vrabel noted that Brown won't practice Monday, and unless the 29-year-old receiver is able to get back on the field in some capacity by Friday, he'll likely be formally ruled out for the matchup with the Chargers heading into the weekend. With Brown expected to be out of the mix for Week 12, Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are currently the receivers available for quarterback Tommy DeVito, who will be making his first start of the season in place of the injured Drake Maye (fibula).

headline: Brown (hamstring) is expected to miss multiple weeks, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: New England's trade for Brown is going down as one the team would definitely prefer to reverse. He's shown no chemistry with Drake Maye (ankle) and hasn't looked healthy since injuring his ankle in the first half of the Week 1 game against the Seahawks. Brown also appears to have lost multiple steps with his downfield speed due to the laundry list of lower-body injuries that now includes ankle, knee and hamstring issues in 2026. The Patriots will play out the string on a lost season without Maye and Brown for several more weeks. Look for Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs (shoulder, IR) when healthy, DeMario Douglas, Kyle Williams and Efton Chism to pick up the slack at wideout with Brown on the shelf again.

headline: Brown (hamstring) was spotted walking around with a limp in the locker room following Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Brown returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries to suit up Sunday. However, the veteran wideout sustained a hamstring injury while making a reception in the third quarter and wasn't able to return to the contest. Brown didn't speak to reporters following the loss, and head coach Mike Vrabel said the team would "see what the severity of that [injury] is" once the team returns to the United States. New England is on bye Week 11, but it's far from certain Brown will be able to suit up the next time the team plays Nov. 29 against the Chargers.

headline: Brown (hamstring) won't return to Sunday's game against the Lions, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Brown was initially deemed questionable to return after his exit, but now the WR's next chance to see game action will arrive Nov. 29 versus the Chargers, following the Patriots' bye. In his return from a two-game absence, Brown had caught two of his six targets for 27 yards prior to hurting his hamstring. Mack Hollins, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will handle New England's wide receiver duties for the remainder of Sunday's contest.

headline: Brown (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Lions.
story: After heading for the medical tent during the contest, per Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald, Brown was officially deemed questionable to return versus Detroit. Prior to his exit, the WR caught two of his six targets for 27 yards.

headline: Brown (knee/ankle) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
story: Brown, who hasn't played since Week 7, was able to practice in a limited fashion Wednesday through Friday before being deemed questionable for Sunday's contest. The Patriots' marquee offseason acquisition has had trouble staying on the field to this point, but following a two-game absence, he'll return to bolster a WR corps that also includes DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams. In three games thus far, Brown has compiled a 9/101/0 receiving line on 20 targets, but he's capable of bringing a higher level of productivity to the table going forward, provided he's able to avoid any further injury setbacks.

headline: Brown (ankle/knee) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Brown practiced on a limited basis all week, and it appears that was what he needed to do in order to return from a two-game absence. The Patriots will officially reveal Brown's status for Week 10 when they release their inactives 90 minutes prior to Sunday's 9:30 am ET kickoff.

headline: Brown (knee/ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Lions, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: The same applies to RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee), with coach Mike Vrabel having said "pretty good" when asked before Friday's practice about his view on how the duo was progressing toward playing this weekend. Fortunately for those considering Brown (who was listed as limited at practice Wednesday through Friday) in Week 10 fantasy lineups, his status will be known before the first wave of games Sunday, with a 9:30 am ET kickoff in Munich scheduled.

headline: Brown (ankle/knee) practiced Friday for a third straight day, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Brown was listed as a limited participant on both Wednesday's and Thursday's injury reports, and it appears he is getting at least some work in for a third straight day. The Patriots will reveal his official status for Sunday's matchup with the Lions in Munich when they release their final injury report later Friday.

headline: Brown (knee/ankle) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
story: Brown has been listed as limited on consecutive days to open the Patriots' Week 10 prep in Munich. He would likely need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid carrying a questionable tag into Sunday's game against the Lions, which kicks off at 9:30 a.m. EST. In three appearances for New England, Brown has nine catches for 101 yards.

headline: Brown (knee/ankle) is taking part in Thursday's practice, which Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site describes as a jog-through.
story: Brown's presence at Thursday's session is another positive sign ahead of Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, which will kick off at 9:30 a.m. EST. The wideout was listed as limited at Wednesday's practice, and Brown's participation level Friday will be critical to assessing his likelihood of suiting up following a two-game absence.

headline: Brown (knee/ankle) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Brown last played in Week 7, but the wideout's return to a limited practice Wednesday has him trending in the right direction as Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich approaches. The Patriots' top WR now has two more opportunities to upgrade his practice participation before the team's Week 10 injury designations are assigned Friday.

headline: Brown (knee) returned to practice Wednesday, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Brown's return to practice comes hours after coach Mike Vrabel confirmed to reporters that the wideout will travel to Munich, where the Patriots face the Lions on Sunday. Brown missed the past two games and didn't practice at all last week.

headline: Brown (knee) is traveling with the Patriots to Germany, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Brown missed the past two games and didn't practice last week, but it sounds like he has at least some chance to return for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel did say Wednesday that not all of the injured players traveling for the game will end up playing, per Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald.

headline: Brown (knee) is trending toward traveling with the Patriots for their trip to Munich, where the team will face the Lions this coming weekend, according to Mark Daniels of MassLive.com.
story: Per Mike Reiss of ESPN.com, coach Mike Vrabel indicated that for now the team plans for the wideout to make the trip, but a decision on that front has yet to be locked in. In Brown's second consecutive missed game, Sunday against the Packers, DeMario Douglas, Mack Hollins, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams handled the Patriots' Week 9 WR duties.

headline: Brown (knee) won't be available for Sunday's game against the Packers, Mark Daniels of Masslive.comreports.
story: Following a trio of consecutive DNPs, Brown is slated to sit out a second consecutive contest. In his absence, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams are available to handle Week 9 duties, while Mack Hollins (calf) -- who has been designated to return from IR -- is a candidate to be activated this weekend, and if that occurs he could step into a key role in his return to the lineup. As for Brown's potential availability for the Patriots' Week 10 contest versus the Lions in Munich, coach Mike Vrabel indicated that he doesn't know yet, per Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald.

headline: Brown (knee/ankle) remained sidelined at practice Friday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: With three consecutive DNPs looming, Brown doesn't seem likely to be available Sunday against the Packers. If Brown is ruled out later Friday, the stage would be set for DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, Kyle Williams and potentially Mack Hollins (calf) -- who has been designated to return from IR -- to handle New England's Week 9 WR duties.

headline: Brown (ankle/knee) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice, Rob Demovsky of ESPN.com reports.
story: Thursday's injury report confirms Brown's absence after he wasn't spotted earlier in the day. Brown has missed the team's first two practices leading up to Sunday's game against the Packers, suggesting he's fighting an uphill battle in his effort to avoid missing a second consecutive game. He has dressed for only three of New England's first eight games. DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, Kyle Williams and possibly Mack Hollins (calf) would lead the Patriots' wide receiver room Sunday if Brown sits again.

headline: Brown (ankle/knee) isn't present for the portion of Thursday's practice open to media viewing, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Brown appears set for a second straight missed practice after sitting out Wednesday's session on the heels of his absence during New England's Week 8 win over Miami. He'll have one more chance to practice Friday and will likely have to participate in some capacity to avoid being ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers.

headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said that Brown (knee/ankle) won't practice Wednesday, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Brown was sidelined for New England's Week 8 win over Miami, and with another absence from practice on tap, the wideout's status for Sunday's game against the Packers is cloudy. On the plus side for the Patriots, Mack Hollins (calf) could return from injured reserve this weekend to bolster a wideout corps that also includes DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams.

headline: When asked whether Brown (ankle/knee) might practice at some point this week, coach Mike Vrabel said Monday, "We'll see," Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Brown was inactive for Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins, and Vrabel's comment Monday implies that the wideout's status for this weekend's game against the Packers is uncertain at this stage. In Brown's absence versus Miami, DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams paced the Patriots' Week 8 WR corps.

headline: Brown (knee/ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reports.
story: Brown entered the weekend with the questionable tag despite being held out of practice both Thursday and Friday, and the knee injury that flared up during Wednesday's session is severe enough for the veteran wide receiver to miss Sunday's AFC East tilt. With Brown sidelined, the Patriots' pass-catching group will be led by DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and tight end Hunter Henry. Brown's next opportunity to play is Week 9 against the Packers on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Brown (ankle/knee) is questionable for Sunday's game at Miami, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel deemed Brown questionable after Friday's practice, in which the wideout didn't participate. Vrabel told reporters that Brown's knee flared up during Wednesday's practice and prevented him from finishing the session, per Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald. Brown then missed practice Thursday and Friday, putting his availability in serious doubt ahead of a 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff at Miami on Sunday.

headline: Brown (ankle/knee) was not spotted at Friday's practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Brown was limited Wednesday and missed practice Thursday, with reports confirming a flare-up in his knee. He's managed chronic/degenerative knee problems throughout his career, typically managing to play even when the issue flares up. That said, the back-to-back absences from practice suggest Brown is in danger of missing Sunday's game at Miami, potentially leaving DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams as New England's top three WRs.

headline: Brown (ankle/knee) was officially listed as a non-participant at Thursday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Thursday's injury report confirms earlier reporting from Ian Rapoport of NFL Network that Brown isn't practicing Thursday. According to Rapoport, Brown recently had a knee issue flare up, which has the wide receiver's status for Sunday's game against the Dolphins in doubt. Brown has six catches for 75 yards on 16 targets in two games since returning from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury.

headline: Brown (knee/ankle) is sidelined Thursday by a knee issue that flared up, and the wide receiver's status for Sunday against the Dolphins is up in the air, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Brown is contending with a new knee injury in addition to the ankle injury through which he has played the last two weeks after missing the previous four. The wideout's fantasy managers should start forming contingency plans in case he sits out Sunday against the Dolphins, though Brown could change the narrative by returning to practice Friday.

headline: Brown (ankle/knee) was not present during the media-viewing portion of Thursday's practice, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Brown looks to be trending in the wrong direction after being listed as a limited participant at Wednesday's practice. He has caught just six of 16 targets for 75 yards in two games since returning from a stint on IR due to an ankle injury. Brown's activity level Friday could be pivotal for his availability Sunday against the Dolphins.

headline: Brown was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to knee and ankle injuries.
story: The Patriots are remaining cautious with Brown, who is apparently nursing a knee issue in addition to getting continued maintenance for the high-ankle sprain that kept him out for four games. Brown was limited in two practices ahead of a Thursday night game against the Bears but still played 92 percent of the offensive snaps in the 30-24 loss. A similar rep-management plan could be in place for Brown going into Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

headline: Brown brought in three of six targets for 48 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
story: Brown entered the night looking to put a fairly forgettable Week 6 return from injury behind him, but the veteran wideout could only slightly improve his numbers in the high-scoring loss. He was fairly quiet until the second half, when he had 16- and 14-yard grabs. Brown did finish second in targets on the night for New England, but Drake Maye focused most on tight end Hunter Henry and running back Rhamondre Stevenson, who saw a combined 12 targets. With Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder) out for at least three more games, Brown will have a chance to see elevated volume in a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Stevenson was not listed on the Patriots' practice report Wednesday.
story: Stevenson hurt his knee in Week 9 against Green Bay and initially appeared slated to miss multiple games. However, he surprisingly was able to suit up in Week 10 against Detroit in Munich, Germany, though he logged just a 44 percent offensive snap share and gained only five yards on seven touches. Stevenson is now off the injury report entirely to begin Week 12 prep following New England's Week 11 bye, suggesting that the knee issue is no longer a concern. The veteran running back commented Wednesday on his ability to suit up in Week 10, attributing it to "a bunch of recovery" and sharing, "(The trainers) did a good job of just getting me available again... Leg wasn't feeling 100 percent, but I was well enough to go out there and participate with the team and try to help them out a little bit," per Sophie Weller of Patriots Wire. With no practice restrictions to begin Week 12 prep, Stevenson should be set to suit up this Sunday in Los Angeles against the Chargers, when he'll be taking handoffs from QB Tommy DeVito.

headline: Stevenson carried the ball six times for four yards and caught his only target for one yard in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich.
story: The whole Patriots' offense struggled after Drake Maye (ankle) was knocked out of the game early, but Stevenson also didn't look to be in peak form after dealing with a knee issue during the practice week. Corey Kiner wound up leading the backfield with just 25 rushing yards on 10 totes. Stevenson will get a Week 11 bye to rest up, and if Maye's injury ends up sidelining him for an extended period, New England could lean heavily on its running game in Week 12 against the Chargers.

headline: Stevenson (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
story: Though he initially appeared likely to miss multiple weeks after sustaining a knee tendon injury in last Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers, Stevenson won't end up being sidelined for any game action at all. After being held out of the Patriots' first practice of Week 10, Stevenson proceeded to turn in a pair of limited sessions en route to taking a questionable designation into Sunday. He appears to have made it through a pregame workout no worse for the wear and should be on track to lead the New England backfield once again, with Corey Kiner and Lan Larison on hand as his backup options after TreVeyon Henderson (illness) was moved to injured reserve Saturday.

headline: Stevenson (knee) is expected to play in Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: It initially appeared that the knee injury that forced Stevenson from his team's Week 9 loss to the Packers would cost him a few weeks of action, but it now appears he will not miss any time at all. Stevenson's status for Week 10 will be confirmed when the Patriots release their inactives 90 minutes before Sunday's game kicks off at 9:30 am ET.

headline: Stevenson (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Lions, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Despite a report earlier in the week indicating that Stevenson would likely miss some time, the running back's ability to log limited practices both Thursday and Friday gives him a chance to play this weekend. With a 9:30 am ET kickoff in Munich scheduled, those considering Stevenson or A.J. Brown (knee/ankle, questionable) in Week 10 fantasy lineups will have the duo's statuses clarified before the first wave of games Sunday. Moreover, there's a pretty good chance that NFL insiders such as Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network and Adam Schefter of ESPN will provide some updates on New England's injury situation either late Saturday or early Sunday. If the team ends up holding Stevenson out ahead of a Week 11 bye, Corey Kiner, followed by Lan Larison, would be next in line for backfield work versus Detroit this weekend, with TreVeyon Henderson (illness) still sidelined.

headline: Stevenson (knee) was present but not in uniform for Friday's practice, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: Stevenson was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice, but it's worth noting that Chad Graff of The Athletic described that as a "pad-less, extremely light" session. With the running back presumably in line to log a 'DNP' a day later, Stevenson could be ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions later Friday, and in that scenario, with TreVeyon Henderson (illness) still sidelined, Corey Kiner, followed by Lan Larison, would be next in line for backfield work versus Detroit this weekend, with Terrell Jennings a candidate to be elevated from the team's practice squad.

headline: Stevenson (knee) returned to practice Thursday as a limited participant.
story: Stevenson's participation may come as a surprise after NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday that the running back was likely to miss a few weeks. The Patriots have a Week 11 bye, but first they'll face the Lions in Munich this Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET. Corey Kiner is next up as New England's lead runner if Stevenson doesn't play. Patriots wideout DeMario Douglas told reporters that Stevenson hopes to play, per Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald.

headline: Stevenson (knee) was working off to the side at the start of Thursday's practice, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports.
story: Previous reports suggested that Stevenson, who registered a 'DNP' on Wednesday, is expected to miss time after exiting this past Sunday's loss to the Packers. While it's encouraging to see the running back get some level of work in Thursday, chances are he'll officially be deemed a non-participant on the Patriots' upcoming injury report. The team has a bye in Week 11, which figures to factor into the decision-making process ahead of this weekend's game against the Lions in Munich.

headline: Stevenson (knee) is absent from Wednesday's practice, Evan Lazar of Patriots.com reports.
story: Stevenson is expected to miss time after an early exit from Sunday's loss to the Packers. A Week 11 bye may or may not help him avoid a multi-game absence, but he's unlikely to play this Sunday in Munich against the Lions.

headline: The knee injury that Stevenson sustained late in the third quarter of Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers is expected to keep him out for "the next few weeks," Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Stevenson won't require surgery, but he looks likely to miss at least the Patriots' Week 10 game against the Lions in Munich due to a plantaris tendon issue on the back of his knee. The Patriots will be on bye Week 11 following the contest in Germany, and that extra time off could be enough for Stevenson to avoid a stint on injured reserve, which would require him to miss a minimum of four games. With the status of TreVeyon Henderson (illness) uncertain heading into the matchup with the Lions, the Patriots could be down to their third and fourth options in the backfield, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison, in Week 10.

headline: Stevenson is dealing with a knee tendon issue that isn't slated to require surgery but may require him to miss "a short period of time," Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Stevenson appears to have avoided a worst-case outcome, as surgery is reportedly off the table. However, the issue could cost the Patriots' tailback some time, further depleting an RB room that has been without TreVeyon Henderson (illness) the past two weeks. In the very realistic scenario that both Stevenson and Henderson are out this Sunday against Detroit in Munich, Germany, the Patriots backfield likely will be led by Corey Kiner, with Lan Larison serving as his backup.

headline: Coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that the Patriots are awaiting MRI results on Stevenson's knee, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports.
story: Stevenson was forced out of Sunday's loss to the Packers and didn't return to the contest after sustaining his knee injury. With TreVeyon Henderson (illness) out for an undermined amount of time, Corey Kiner, followed by Lan Larison, would be next up for the Patriots' backfield work in Week 10 if Stevenson is unable to play this coming weekend against the Lions.

headline: Stevenson (knee) won't return to Sunday's game against the Packers, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports.
story: Stevenson went to the locker room in the second half and has been ruled out shortly thereafter. The extent and nature of his knee injury will be clarified in the coming days, with Stevenson's next chance to suit up coming Nov. 15 against the Lions in Munich. Corey Kiner and Lan Larison are New England's remaining healthy running backs, as TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is inactive. Stevenson rushed six times for 32 yards while catching three of four targets for 46 yards and a touchdown prior to exiting.

headline: Stevenson headed to the locker room during Sunday's game against the Packers to be evaluated for an unspecified issue, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Before that, Stevenson carried six times for 32 yards and caught three of his four targets for 46 yards and a TD. With TreVeyon Henderson (illness) sidelined for an undetermined amount of time, Corey Kiner and Lan Larison are available to handle New England's backfield duties Sunday for as long as Stevenson is out of the game.

headline: With TreVeyon Henderson (illness) ruled out for Week 9, Stevenson is set to handle an expanded workload Sunday against the Packers, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports.
story: Henderson will miss a second straight game tending to medical issue. With the second-year running back out last week against Miami, Stevenson logged 76.7 percent of the offensive snaps and handled a season-high 19 carries, turning them into 82 scoreless yards. He also caught three passes on three targets. Stevenson will be a volume-driven, home-favorite RB1/2 for fantasy against Green Bay, while Corey Kiner will step into the RB2 role again.

headline: Stevenson carried the ball 19 times for 82 yards and caught all three of his targets for eight yards in Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins.
story: With TreVeyon Henderson (illness) unavailable, Stevenson led the Patriots in rushing yards and scrimmage yards, although he wasn't able to get into the end zone. His 19 totes and 82 rushing yards were both season highs. The veteran back's workload in Week 9 against the Packers will depend somewhat on Henderson's health, but Stevenson appears to be Mike Vrabel's most trusted option in the backfield, and through eight games he's on pace to top 1,000 scrimmage yards for the first time since 2022.

headline: Stevenson rushed six times for 22 yards and brought in all five targets for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
story: Stevenson had another tough day on the ground, especially considering he gained 13 of his 22 yards on one carry. However, the veteran back had a standout performance as a receiver, leading the Patriots in receiving yards on the night with a big hand from a weaving 48-yard touchdown catch off an end-of-half screen play. Stevenson is now averaging just 3.7 yards per carry across the first seven games of the campaign, but he's up to a 20-204-1 receiving line on 24 targets heading into a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Stevenson rushed 14 times for 36 yards and wasn't targeted in the Patriots' 26-19 win over the Jets on Sunday.
story: Stevenson saw twice the rushing workload of backfield mate TreVeyon Henderson but gained only five more yards. Stevenson also recorded 12 of his yards on one carry, so he ran for next to nothing on his other 13 rush attempts in what was his second-least productive game on the ground this season. Henderson did lose a fumble Sunday and is managing what is reportedly a high-ankle sprain, so Stevenson is likely to remain the lead option during a Week 7 road matchup against the Bears on Thursday night.

headline: Stevenson will be joined by TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) in the backfield Sunday against the Jets, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: After Henderson suffered a right high-ankle sprain last Sunday versus the Raiders, Stevenson had a chance to take on a large workload in the short term, but with the former active, it's unclear if that's a possibility in Week 6. Any number of scenarios are possible for Henderson, from him taking on his normal number of touches to being available in an emergency capacity. Stevenson should be safe for roughly his typical 14.4 touches per game, which so far has amounted to 338 yards from scrimmage and two TDs in five contests this season.

headline: Stevenson's workload against the Jets on Sunday will depend on whether TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is cleared to play, Evan Lazaar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Henderson was expected to miss multiple weeks due to a high-ankle sprain that he sustained against the Raiders in Week 5. However, the second-year running back was able to practice in a limited capacity in all three Week 6 practices, which was enough for him to draw the questionable tag for Sunday's AFC East showdown. If he's ruled out, then Stevenson would be the Patriots' clear RB1 and take on a sizable workload, with Corey Kiner serving in a rotational role.

headline: Stevenson is expected to take on a heavier workload for the next few weeks while TreVeyon Henderson recovers from a high-ankle sprain that he sustained in Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders, per ESPN.
story: The good news for Henderson is that surgery is not required, but whether an stint on injured reserve is necessary remains to be seen. Stevenson has served as the Patriots' RB1 this season, and the veteran's share of the backfield snap count figures to grow even more for as long as Henderson is sidelined, with Corey Kiner slated to take on backup duties. Over his last two games, Stevenson has turned 26 carries into 111 yards (4.3 YPC) and two touchdowns while adding six catches on eight targets for 48 yards.

headline: Stevenson carried the ball 13 times for 64 yards and a touchdown and caught all three of his targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 45-17 rout of the Raiders.
story: There was some question whether Stevenson would even be active for this one after a knee issue limited his practice participation during the week, but the veteran was the clear top option in the Patriots' backfield after TreVeyon Henderson (38 scrimmage yards on five touches) departed with an ankle injury in the second quarter. Stevenson's longest gain went for 20 yards en route to a season high in rushing yards, and he punched in a five-yard TD in the first quarter that put New England in the lead for good at 14-7. Stevenson will look to keep rolling in a Week 6 tilt against the Jets, and he could shoulder a particularly heavy workload if Henderson is unable to suit up in that contest.

headline: Stevenson (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: After a week of limited practice participation, Stevenson was listed as questionable heading into Sunday but will be cleared to play. He'll likely operate as Option 1A in a backfield that includes TreVeyon Henderson while the Patriots take aim at a Raiders defense that has given up 134.5 yards on the ground per game through four contests.

headline: Stevenson (knee) is expected to play in Sunday's game versus the Raiders, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: After coach Mike Vrabel told Taylor Kyles of CLNSMedia.com on Wednesday that Stevenson wouldn't practice due to a leg injury to kick off Week 5 prep, the running back wound up being limited and maintained that activity level through Friday with a listed knee injury. A questionable tag for Sunday followed, but per Rapoport, Stevenson is poised to play through the issue. What that means for the workloads of Stevenson and fellow RB TreVeyon Henderson remains to be seen.

headline: Stevenson (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: After logging limited practice listings throughout the week, Stevenson gets the dreaded questionable tag headed into Sunday. While the running back said himself that he's ready to play, coach Mike Vrabel refused to commit to Stevenson doing so versus Las Vegas. TreVeyon Henderson will be set up for a big increase in snaps and touches if Stevenson is unable to play.

headline: Stevenson (knee) said Friday that he's "ready to go", while Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said the running back "is not out as of yet" for Sunday's game against Las Vegas, according to Mark Daniels of MassLive.com.
story: Stevenson was a limited practice participant Wednesday and Thursday, and he also took part in Friday's session. It sounds like he may get a 'questionable' designation, but he isn't actually worried about missing Sunday's game. Should Stevenson's optimism prove misleading, TreVeyon Henderson would be in line for a large workload after splitting carries the past three weeks.

headline: Stevenson (knee) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: A limited participant in both of the Patriots' first two Week 5 practices, Stevenson still appears to be managing the knee issue he sustained late in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win over the Bills. The fact that he hasn't been held out of practice entirely is a strong sign that Stevenson will be available for this Sunday's matchup with the Raiders, though he might need to upgrade to full participation Friday to head into the weekend without an injury designation.

headline: Stevenson was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice due to a knee injury.
story: Per Mark Daniels of MassLive.com, head coach Mike Vrabel said prior to Wednesday's session that Stevenson had "no chance" of practicing, but the running back ultimately was able to get in enough on-field work to receive a limited listing on the Patriots' first Week 5 injury report. Stevenson is banged up after he appeared to land awkwardly on his right knee after getting tackled on his final carry with 1:05 remaining in this past Sunday's 29-26 win over the Bills. Vrabel noted that Stevenson hasn't been ruled out for this weekend's matchup with the Raiders, though the 28-year-old would likely need to upgrade to full practice participation Thursday or Friday in order to avoid taking a designation into Sunday.

headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said that Stevenson isn't expected to practice Wednesday due to an apparent leg injury, Taylor Kyles of CLNSMedia.com reports.
story: Stevenson looked to have injured his leg or knee near the end of Sunday's win over the Bills, but the Patriots' first Week 5 injury report will be released later Wednesday and provide more clarity on the nature of his health concern. Vrabel expressed some optimism that Stevenson can still play during this Sunday's game against the Raiders, but if Stevenson can't go, TreVeyon Henderson would be set up for a heftier workload as the clear lead back for New England.

headline: Stevenson rushed 13 times for 47 yards and a touchdown while bringing in three of five targets for 27 yards in the Patriots' 29-26 win over the Bills on Sunday. He also caught a two-point conversion pass.
story: Stevenson took one less carry than TreVeyon Henderson but outgained his backfield mate by five yards, and the former was also the only one of the two to get into the end zone. Stevenson scored his rush TD, his first of the season, from one yard out in the second quarter, and his two-point conversion catch extended New England's lead to three following Efton Chism's one-handed go-ahead touchdown grab with 1:50 remaining. Stevenson should remain in a near-even timeshare with Henderson in a Week 5 home matchup against the Raiders next Sunday.

headline: Schooler (hamstring) was not listed on the Patriots' injury report Wednesday.
story: Schooler did not play in Week 10 against the Lions due to hamstring injury, and he missed the Patriots' four prior games while recovering from a back issue. His absence from Wednesday's report indicates that Schooler will be available for Sunday's game against the Chargers. He has four tackles (two solo) across five regular-season games while mostly contributing on special teams.

headline: Schooler (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's contest against the Patriots in Munich.
story: Schooler missed the first four games of the season due to a back injury, and he now will sit out a fifth due to the hamstring issue that forced him out of a Week 9 loss to the Packers. The Patriots likely will turn to some combination of Mike Brown and Jaylen Reed to cover Schooler's typical special-teams duties.

headline: Schooler (hamstring) is questionable to play against the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
story: Schooler was held out of Wednesday's practice due to a hamstring injury he sustained during the Patriots' Week 9 loss to the Packers. He ended Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices, and his absence would deplete the Patriots' depth both in the secondary and on special teams. Starting safety Kevin Byard (chest) is also listed as questionable despite logging a full practice Friday.

headline: Schooler (hamstring) will not return to Sunday's game against the Packers.
story: Strictly a special-teamer for New England, Schooler entered play Sunday with four tackles (two solo) across four games this season. His next chance to play will be next Sunday in Detroit.

headline: Schooler (hamstring) is questionable to return to New England's matchup versus the Packers on Sunday, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Schooler hurt his hamstring in the second half of Sunday's matchup, leaving his status for the remainder of the contest up in the air. If he is unable to return, the team will be left with Jaylen Reed and Mike Brown as its only depth options at safety.

headline: The Patriots activated Schooler (back) from injured reserve Saturday, and he does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Schooler has been cleared to make his regular-season debut Sunday after missing the Patriots' first four games while recovering from a back injury. He should see most of his playing time on special teams, though he could also see some snaps on defense given the Patriots' injuries in the secondary.

headline: Brown (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Brown did not play in the Patriots' Week 10 loss to the Lions in Munich due to a knee injury that he sustained against the Packers in Week 9. With a full practice under his belt, Brown is on track to play against the Chargers on Sunday and should reclaim his starting spot at left guard while Walter Rouse reverts to a depth role on the offensive line.

headline: Brown (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Brown tweaked his knee against the Packers in Week 9, and the injury is severe enough for him to not travel with the team to Munich. In his absence, Walter Rouse is expected to serve as the Patriots' starter at left guard. Since the Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, Brown's next chance to suit up is Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that Brown (knee) likely won't play in Sunday's game versus the Lions, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Brown injured his knee during the first half of New England's loss versus the Packers in Week 9, and it appears he's trending towards being sidelined in Week 10. Should that be the case, 2024 sixth-rounder Walter Rouse projects to start at left guard Sunday.

headline: Brown (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's contest against the Packers.
story: Brown sustained a knee injury in the first half, and he will not return to the contest. If he is forced to miss any action moving forward, Walter Rouse is a top candidate to start in Brown's place at offensive guard.

headline: Brown (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's contest against the Packers, Mark Daniels of MassLive.com reports.
story: Brown suffered a knee injury late in the first half, and his availability for the rest of the game is now up in the air. In his absence, Walter Rouse has taken over at left guard versus Green Bay.

headline: Brown (knee) does not have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports.
story: Brown was unable play against the Bears in Week 7 due to a knee injury. He's faded an injury tag for Sunday's game after logging a full practice Friday, and he should reclaim his starting spot at right guard.

headline: Brown (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Bears.
story: Brown injured his knee during the fourth quarter of Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets. He was held out of all three practices during Week 7 prep, and with both Brown and Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) sidelined Thursday, the Patriots will likely turn to Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse to serve as the starting guards against Chicago. Brown will aim to recover enough to return for Week 8 against Miami on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Coach Mike Vrabel said Tuesday that Brown (knee) probably won't be available for Thursday's game against the Bears, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Vrabel stopped short of ruling out Brown completely, but it seems like it will be an uphill battle for him to try to be ready to play in Week 7. With regular starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) also trending in the wrong direction ahead of Thursday's contest, 2024 sixth-rounder Walter Rouse and veteran Matt Pryor might both be called on to start against a defense that has flashed at times so far this year.

headline: Brown (knee) won't return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Brown suffered a knee injury in the fourth quarter and has since been downgraded to out. Walter Rouse entered the contest and will presumably fill the void for the remainder of the game.

headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that DeVito is the team's starting quarterback, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports. "We're excited about that. He had a good preseason, and Tommy's improved," Vrabel said of DeVito.
story: With Drake Maye (fibula) hurt early in Week 10 against Detroit, DeVito stepped in at quarterback but managed to complete just 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards, a touchdown and an interception. He added 19 yards on four carries. The 28-year-old does have some starting experience -- he helmed the Giants offense for eight starts between 2023 and 2024 -- but he didn't play at all in 2025. For now, the Patriots are at least communicating that they'll stand pat and not look for help at quarterback outside the organization. However, the team is barely hanging on in the AFC playoff race with a 5-5 record, and with only rookie Behren Morton on the active roster as a healthy option to DeVito, the team may still look elsewhere if DeVito is unable to show better production.

headline: Head coach Mike Vrabel said Friday that DeVito will start in Week 12 against the Chargers on Nov. 29, Mike Reiss and Adam Schefter of ESPN.com report.
story: Drake Maye was diagnosed with a fractured right fibula, which he sustained in the first quarter of the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich. DeVito filled in for the rest of that contest and completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards, one touchdown and one interception while turning four carries into 19 yards. DeVito looks like he'll be New England's starter coming out of the bye, with rookie seventh-round pick Behren Morton operating as the backup.

headline: Mike Reiss of ESPN.com notes via ESPN's Adam Schefter that there are fears  DeVito's teammate, Drake Maye, may have sustained a fractured ankle during Week 10 action.
story: Regarding Maye's status going forward, head coach Mike Vrabel indicated that he'll wait for further information before estimating how long his starting QB might be out, but he also acknowledged he "wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the (Week 11) bye," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports. As a result, DeVito is in a position to start Sunday, Nov. 29 against the Chargers and possibly beyond. That said, as NFL reporter Jordan Schultz suggests, New England is expected to explore the QB market in the coming days, be it through a practice squad addition or a veteran free agent such as Jimmy Garoppolo, who previously worked with offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels.

headline: DeVito completed 12 of 24 passes for 81 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich. He added 19 yards on four carries.
story: Drake Maye (ankle) was forced to leave the game early after an Aidan Hutchinson (knee) sack, putting DeVito under center for the third time this season, but the first time with the outcome still in doubt. The 28-year-old QB had little luck moving the ball, and his 10-yard TD toss to Lan Larison in the fourth quarter came when the score was already 28-3. The severity of Maye's ankle injury isn't yet known, but the Patriots fortunately get a bye in Week 11 to give him extra recovery time. If he's still unavailable after that, DeVito could find himself starting in Week 12 against the Chargers.

headline: DeVito is active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich as the Patriots' No. 2 quarterback behind starter Drake Maye.
story: DeVito has now suited up for each of the Patriots' first 10 games of the campaign after securing the top backup job over rookie seventh-round pick Behren Morton coming out of the preseason. With Maye having thus far maintained good health, DeVito's lone two appearances have come at the tail end of blowout losses to the Jaguars in Week 3 and Packers last week. DeVito completed four of eight pass attempts for 51 yards to go with a two-yard carry between those abbreviated outings.

headline: The Patriots designated Vera-Tucker (hamstring) for return from injured reserve Monday.
story: The move opens Vera-Tucker's 21-day practice window. The oft-injured offensive lineman went down in the Patriots' Week 6 win over the Jets. Greg Van Roten started New England's last game at left guard.

headline: Vera-Tucker (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve by the Patriots on Thursday.
story: Vera-Tucker suffered a hamstring injury in the team's Week 6 win over the Jets, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests while recovering. In his absence, Walter Rouse will take over as the team's starting left tackle Thursday night versus the Bears.

headline: Vera-Tucker (hamstring) has been ruled out for Thursday night's game against the Bears.
story: Vera-Tucker suffered a hamstring injury during the Patriots' 26-19 win over the Jets on Sunday. He was unable to practice during the Patriots' short week, and, in his absence, Walter Rouse likely will take over as the starting left guard for New England. Vera-Tucker's next opportunity to play is Week 8 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Coach Mike Vrabel said Tuesday that Vera-Tucker (hamstring) is unlikely to be available for Thursday's game at Chicago, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Vrabel did not rule out Vera-Tucker out completely, but it looks like he's likely in line to sit out his first game of the 2026 season due to the hamstring injury he suffered during Sunday's game versus the Jets. Regular starting right guard Ben Brown (knee) is also looking like a bad bet to suit up in Week 7, and if both he and Vera-Tucker are sidelined, 2024 sixth-rounder Walter Rouse and veteran Matt Pryor would project as the Patriots' starting guards for Thursday.

headline: Vera-Tucker (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Vera-Tucker sustained a hamstring injury in the second quarter of Sunday's contest. The left guard's absence has shifted the Patriots' offensive line around, leaving Ben Brown at left guard and Matt Pryor at right guard.

headline: Vera-Tucker (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Jets.
story: Vera-Tucker exited the second quarter of Sunday's game with a hamstring injury. Ben Brown switched to left guard so Matt Pryor could come into the game at right guard to replace Vera-Tucker.

headline: Maye, who sustained a fractured right fibula in last Sunday's loss to the Lions, is on track to miss at least six weeks, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: The timetable put forth by Rapoport suggests that Maye could make a run at a late-season return, or for the postseason, should New England qualify. Given that the Patriots are already close to the limit of how many players they can designate for return from injured reserve, Maye isn't a lock to land on IR, but he's nonetheless facing an absence longer than the required four games that a placement on IR would mandate. For now, Tommy DeVito has been installed as the team's starter ahead of its Week 12 matchup against the Chargers, with rookie Behren Morton on hand as his backup.

headline: Maye has suffered a fractured right fibula that won't require surgery but is expected to sideline him for some time, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Maye was knocked out of Week 10 action on the first possession of this past Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich. He already was expected to miss multiple games as a result of the injury, but with a diagnosis now available, he's now in rehab mode until further notice. A return at some point down the stretch likely will depend on the Patriots remaining in the playoff race, but for the time being Tommy DeVito will be under center in place of Maye.

headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that he didn't have a definitive diagnosis for the injury Maye (ankle) sustained in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, but indicated that the quarterback will miss time," Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports.  "I wouldn't imagine him being available coming out of the [Week 11] bye," Vrabel said.
story: Adam Schefter of ESPN reported earlier Monday that the Patriots were concerned that Maye fractured his ankle Sunday. That diagnosis has yet to be confirmed, however, and Vrabel suggested that he'll avoid projecting a timeline for Maye until the quarterback returns from Germany to be further evaluated. At the very least, Maye can be expected to miss the Patriots' next game Nov. 29 against the Chargers. In the meantime, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz suggests that the team is expected to explore the quarterback market in the coming days, though top backup Tommy DeVito is currently next in line to start in place of Maye.

headline: The Patriots are concerned that Maye fractured his ankle during Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Per Schefter, Maye remained in Germany to undergo additional testing to determine whether he needs surgery or not. In any case, Maye looks destined to miss some time beyond the Patriots' Week 11 bye, if not the rest of the season. Tommy DeVito came on in relief of Maye in Sunday's contest and would be the next man up at quarterback for the Patriots, while rookie seventh-round pick Behren Morton is also on hand. The Patriots seem likely to add depth to the position group in the coming days, either to the 53-man roster and/or the practice squad.

headline: Maye is believed to have sustained a significant lower-leg injury in Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich that could sideline him for an extended period of time, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Maye, who was forced out of Sunday's game with what the Patriots referred to as an ankle injury, is slated to undergo additional medical tests before a formal diagnosis of his injury is provided. While the Patriots won't have a projected timeline for Maye's recovery until testing is completed, Rapoport suggests that the quarterback could miss the rest of the season. In the event that Maye is sidelined for any length of time following New England's Week 11 bye, Tommy DeVito -- who replaced Maye on Sunday -- and Behren Morton are currently next in line for reps under center. Moreover, while the NFL trade deadline has come and gone, it's still possible that the 5-5 Patriots could explore options at the position via the free-agent market or other teams' practice squads.

headline: Maye is slated to undergo additional testing on his ankle after exiting Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich, but the Patriots are bracing for him to be "out a while," Mike Florio of NBC Sports reports.
story: Maye sustained the injury on the Patriots' first possession of Week 10, when he was sacked by the Lions' Aidan Hutchinson. Though New England has a bye on tap in Week 11, initial evaluations of Maye's injury have left the team skeptical that he'll be ready to play Week 12 against the Chargers. Maye is set to undergo further testing Monday before the Patriots provide an updated diagnosis for his injury and a projected timeline for his return. Backup Tommy DeVito entered in relief of Maye in Sunday's loss and was ineffective while directing the offense, competing just 12 of 24 pass attempts for 81 yards, one touchdown and an interception.

headline: Following Sunday's 35-10 loss to the Lions, coach Mike Vrabel said that Maye will need additional testing to determine the severity of the ankle injury he suffered during the contest, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald.
story: The Patriots have a well-timed Week 11 bye, so Maye has some added healing time ahead of the team's Nov. 29 contest against the Chargers. However, if Maye isn't available by then, Tommy DeVito -- who replaced him Sunday -- would continue to do so in Week 12.

headline: Maye (ankle) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Lions, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: After initially being deemed questionable to return to the contest, Maye will now target a possible return to action Nov. 29 against the Chargers following the Patriots' Week 11 bye. In his absence versus Detroit, Tommy DeVito is in at QB for the team, with Behren Morton on hand as the emergency No. 3 QB. Prior to his exit, Maye completed three of his four pass attempts for 48 yards and ran once for 11 yards.

headline: Maye is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich after sustaining an ankle injury in the first quarter.
story: The injury occurred on the Patriots' first possession of the day, when Maye was taken down by the Lions' Aidan Hutchinson for a third-down sack. After getting checked out on the sideline, Maye made his way to the New England locker room for further evaluation. Tommy DeVito checked in at quarterback for the Patriots' second possession and will be under center for the rest of the game if Maye is unable to return.

headline: Maye completed 21 of 38 passes for 299 yards with three touchdowns and three interceptions while adding one rush for three yards in the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday.
story: Maye was constantly harassed by an aggressive Packers defense that sacked him four times for 27 total yards in losses while also repeatedly getting hands on his throws. Working with a receiving corps that welcomed back Mack Hollins (calf) from injured reserve but was still down A.J. Brown (knee) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder), Maye threw his first interception on the second play of the game on a deep pass intended for Hollins, and his other two picks came during the second quarter. Two of the three INTs led to Green Bay touchdowns, and after throwing just eight interceptions over 17 regular-season games in 2025, Maye is up to 11 over nine contests this season following Sunday's game. The third-year signal-caller's first chance to atone comes in a Week 10 matchup against a seemingly improved Lions defense in Munich, Germany, next Sunday.

headline: Maye completed 16 of 20 passes for 199 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins. He added five rushing yards and a TD on eight carries.
story: While he failed to reach 200 passing yards for the third time in eight games this season, Maye put together a very efficient performance as he produced multiple TDs for a fifth straight game. All three scores came in the second half as the QB rallied the Patriots from a 13-3 deficit, hitting Kyle Williams for a 43-yard score in the third quarter and DeMario Douglas for a 48-yard strike in the fourth, while running for a two-yard TD in between. Maye appears to have gotten his recklessness under control, committing just one turnover in the last four contests, and he'll take a 15:8 TD:INT on the season into a Week 9 clash with the Packers.

headline: Maye completed 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards with two touchdowns and one interception while adding four rushes for 26 yards and another score in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
story: Maye's final line was one that could have easily been generated in victory, but the 2024 first-round pick couldn't quite help the Patriots keep pace with the high-powered Bears offense. Nevertheless, he was able to post his second 300-yard effort in the last three games, while also tossing multiple touchdowns for the fourth straight contest. Maye connected with Rhamondre Stevenson and Eli Raridon from 48 and 30 yards, respectively, for those two scoring strikes, the former coming off a screen pass on the last snap of the first half. Those big plays were preceded by Maye's seven-yard scoring run early in the second quarter, and he also pulled his season completion rate up to 65.9 percent with Thursday's highly efficient effort. The third-year signal-caller should have a good opportunity to stay hot in a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Elliss logged 10 tackles (three solo) during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich.
story: Week 10 was the third time this season that Elliss posted double-digit stops, and he ended up co-leading the Patriots in tackles with safety Kevin Byard. Through 10 regular-season games, Elliss has accumulated 75 tackles (37 solo), including 1.5 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so Elliss's next opportunity to suit up is Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Elliss (chest) is active for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Elliss has been cleared to play Sunday after working through a chest injury during Week 8 prep. He has 51 tackles (29 solo), including 1.0 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble through seven regular-season games.

headline: Elliss (chest) is listed as questionable against the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Elliss's practice reps were not restricted during Week 8 prep, yet the veteran linebacker has been tagged as questionable due to a chest injury. Darius Muasau, Erick Hunter and rookie sixth-rounder Namdi Obiazor would all be candidates for defensive snaps at inside linebacker if Elliss is unable to play Sunday.

headline: Elliss tallied 13 tackles (eight solo) in a Week 7 loss to Chicago on Thursday.
story: Elliss's 13 stops not only led New England, they also tied a career-best mark. The veteran linebacker logged a 100 percent defensive snap share for the fourth time this season and posted his second double-digit tackle performance. Elliss set a career best with 94 regular-season stops over 15 games last season, and he's on pace to easily surpass that mark with 51 tackles (including 1.0 sacks) through seven contests in 2026.

headline: Elliss (chest) is officially active for Thursday's game at Chicago.
story: Elliss was able to practice at full speed during the week despite the chest issue he was tending to, and it won't hold him out of action on gameday, either. He's on the fringe of the IDP radar in some formats for a Week 7 matchup against a run-first Bears offense.

headline: Elliss (chest) is listed as questionable for Thursday night's game against the Bears.
story: Elliss logged three consecutive full practices during Week 7 prep. The linebacker overcame his chest injury in each session and should do the same for Thursday night's game.

headline: Elliss (chest) is active Week 5 against the Raiders.
story: It wasn't a sure thing that Elliss would suit up after only participating in practice in a limited basis all week, but that ended up being enough. The veteran linebacker played through a similar issue last week against Buffalo, where he logged six combined tackles across 58 defensive snaps.

headline: Elliss (chest) is listed as questionable against the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Elliss was able to play through a chest injury against the Bills in Week 4, and he's drawn the questionable tag for Week 5 after stringing together a trio of limited practices. If he cannot play against Las Vegas, then Darius Muasau and Erick Hunter would be the top candidates to start next to Robert Spillane at inside linebacker.

headline: Elliss (chest) is active against the Bills on Sunday.
story: Elliss's practice participation for Week 4 was limited by a chest injury, but he's been cleared to play Sunday after going through pregame warmups. The veteran linebacker has 19 tackles (11 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one forced fumble through three games.

headline: Elliss (chest) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills.
story: A chest injury has limited Elliss's practice participation all week, and if he cannot play Sunday, then Erick Hunter and Darius Muasau would be the top candidates to start at inside linebacker alongside Robert Spillane. Elliss has 19 tackles (11 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one forced fumble through the first three games of the season.

headline: Byard registered 10 tackles (three solo) and two pass defenses (including an interception) during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Week 10 in Munich.
story: Byard picked off a Jared Goff pass intended for Jameson Williams in the end zone late in the second quarter, which halted the Lions' red zone drive in its tracks. It was the first time this season that Byard posted double-digit stops, and each of the veteran safety's two interceptions on the year have come over his last three outings. He enters the Week 11 bye with 53 tackles (26 solo) and five pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

headline: Byard (chest) is active for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
story: The veteran safety was listed as questionable heading into Sunday, but his ability to finish Week 10 prep with a full practice seemingly had him trending toward playing. He'll end up suiting up in Germany and isn't expected to face any limitations while he plays through the chest issue. Through New England's first nine games, Byard has compiled 43 tackles, three pass breakups and an interception.

headline: Following a full practice Friday, Byard (chest) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
story: Byard opened Week 10 prep with back-to-back limited practices before logging a full session Friday. He hasn't progressed enough in his recovery to fade the injury tag for Sunday's international game, so the veteran safety's status may not be officially known until the Patriots announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff. Jaylen Reed would be the top candidate to start alongside Craig Woodson at safety if Byard is not cleared to play against Detroit.

headline: Byard (chest) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Byard was working through a chest injury in October, but it's unclear whether he's dealing with the same issue for the start of Week 10 prep. The veteran safety will have two more chances to increase his practice participation before the Patriots travel to Munich to face the Lions on Sunday. Byard has 43 tackles (23 solo) and three pass defenses (including one interception) through the first nine games of the regular season.

headline: Byard (chest) is officially active for Thursday's game at Chicago.
story: Byard dealt with a minor chest issue during the week that stuck him with a 'questionable' tag Wednesday, but as expected, he'll be available for Week 7. He figures to play a near-every down role against a run-heavy Chicago offense.

headline: Byard (chest) is listed as questionable for Thursday night's game against the Bears.
story: Byard logged three consecutive full practices during Week 7 prep while dealing with a chest injury. The safety will almost certainly suit up for Thursday's contest and play through what appears to be a minor issue.

headline: Williams failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
story: Williams did have a 21-yard carry late in the third quarter, although the play was nullified by offsetting penalties. It was the second straight game that the second-year wide receiver did not record a catch and the fifth time in 10 regular-season contests. New England is on a bye for Week 11, but the offense's outlook looks grim given that franchise quarterback Drake Maye is expected to miss time due to an ankle injury that he sustained in the first quarter of Sunday's game. The Patriots' next game takes place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Williams failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
story: With Mack Hollins (calf) back in the lineup, Williams still held a big snap share, playing 78 percent of the Patriots' offensive snaps against Green Bay. Efton Chism (51 percent) was the biggest loser in terms of playing time. Williams has earned just 15 targets across nine games this season, catching seven passes for 190 yards and two touchdowns.

headline: Williams caught his lone target for a 43-yard touchdown during Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins.
story: Williams made the most of his only touch in Week 8, scoring on a 43-yard deep ball from Drake Maye in the third quarter. The wide receiver had an opportunity to be more involved with A.J. Brown (knee) sidelined Sunday, but Williams saw just one target for the third game in a row. On the year, the wide receiver has now caught seven of 13 targets for 190 yards and two touchdowns over eight regular-season contests.

headline: Williams returned two kickoffs for 47 yards and failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
story: It was the second game in a row in which Williams saw one target from Drake Maye, and the second-year pro's 21 offensive snaps were fourth-most among Patriots wide receivers. He's been surpassed by Efton Chism in the passing game, and with A.J. Brown back in the mix, it seems like most of Williams' impact moving forward will be on kickoffs as a returner. His playing time will take an even greater hit upon the returns of Mack Hollins (calf) and Romeo Doubs (shoulder) from injured reserve. The Patriots will stay on the road for Week 8 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Williams caught all three of his targets for 91 yards and a touchdown while adding three kick returns for 71 yards during Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders.
story: Williams led the team in receiving yards during the victory, most notably reeling in a 34-yard touchdown pass from Drake Maye in the second quarter. The wide receiver has now caught five of 10 targets for 135 yards and a touchdown while also compiling 344 yards as a kick returner over five contests to open the 2026 campaign.

headline: Larison turned his lone carry into two yards and caught two of three targets for 15 yards and a touchdown during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich. He also recorded a tackle on special teams.
story: The Patriots lost starting quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury early in the first quarter, so backup Tommy DeVito was under center for most of contest. New England struggled with DeVito at the helm, but he did connect with Larison for a 10-yard touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter in what was the Patriots' lone trip to the end zone. Even though that score came in garbage time, it was the first touchdown of Larison's NFL career, although he's firmly entrenched as the team's RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner. The Patriots are on a bye for Week 11, so their next game will take place in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Larison recorded a four-yard rush and failed to haul in his lone target during the Patriots' 45-27 loss to the Packers on Sunday. He also recorded two tackles (one solo) on special teams.
story: Both of Larison's tackles came while on kickoff coverage, and his lone touch on offense took place early in the fourth quarter. It was Larison has seen little activity in the Patriots' offense over the team's last two games, but that could change given that Rhamondre Stevenson is expected to be out for "the next few weeks" due to a knee injury he sustained Sudnay, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. TreVeyon Henderson (illness) doesn't have a clear timeline of return, so Larison and Corey Kiner are currently slated to be the Patriots' top backfield options for Week 10 against the Lions in Detroit.

headline: The Patriots signed Larison off the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: The addition of Larison to the 53-man roster gives the Patriots more depth in the backfield, and he could see some offensive snaps against the Dolphins on Sunday due to the absence of TreVeyon Henderson (illness). Larison figures to operate as the RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner.

headline: Chism did not catch his only target during the Patriots' 35-10 loss against the Lions in Munich in Week 10.
story: A.J. Brown (hamstring) returned from a two-game absence caused by ankle and knee injuries in Week 10, and as a result, Chism saw his lowest snap count this season (8) since he was a healthy scratch in Week 1. His role coming out of the Patriots' bye in Week 11 will probably depend heavily on the availability of Brown, who picked up a hamstring issue against the Lions.

headline: Chism caught all five of his targets for 49 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
story: Chism was able to reel in exactly five passes for the second straight week, and he connected with quarterback Drake Maye for an eight-yard touchdown in the second quarter. The score was Chism's second of the year and first since Week 4. With A.J. Brown (knee) potentially set to miss the team's Week 10 matchup against the Lions, Chism may have a chance to operate in a prominent role again against Detroit's underwhelming secondary.

headline: Chism caught all five of his targets for 37 yards during Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins.
story: Chism led the team in targets and receptions, with A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) unavailable. The wide receiver played a season-high 88 percent of the team's offensive snaps, and he has now reeled in 15 of 20 targets for 151 yards and a touchdown over seven regular-season contests with New England so far this year.

headline: Chism caught his sole target for 16 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
story: Chism saw the third most offensive snaps at wide receiver for the Patriots behind A.J. Brown's 49 and DeMario Douglas' 35. The 24-year-old was not given as much attention as in the prior two weeks, with his target share dropping from four targets in Week 5 and six targets in Week 6 to just one in Week 7.

headline: Chism caught five of six targets for 57 yards and added a two-yard rush during Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders.
story: Chism was able to tie tight end Eli Raridon for the team lead in catches, and he set a new career high with 57 receiving yards. The 24-year-old has now reeled in nine of 13 targets for 98 yards and a touchdown over the Patriots' last four contests.

headline: Chism caught two of four targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots' 29-26 win over the Bills on Sunday.
story: Chism ran only 18 routes on Drake Maye's 42 dropbacks as New England's fourth receiver, playing behind all three of Romeo Doubs, Mack Hollins and slot man DeMario Douglas. Chism's 23-yard touchdown with 1:50 left in the fourth quarter proved to be the game-winning score. It was the second touchdown of Chism's regular-season career. He has four grabs for 41 yards and a score through three appearances in 2026.

headline: Raridon caught his only target for six yards in Sunday's loss to the Lions in Munich.
story: The rookie tight end played his normal allotment of plays, seeing 62.7 percent of the offensive snaps, but the offense as a whole was broken after Drake Maye went out with an ankle injury early in the first quarter. The offense bogged down with Tommy DeVito at the controls, and Raridon's one target was his fewest in a game since Week 2. Raridon also has been held to single-digit receiving yards in two of the last three contests. He's averaging a robust 13.6 yards per catch this season but isn't a reliable fantasy option with Hunter Henry healthy.

headline: Raridon caught three passes for 52 yards on six targets in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
story: Even with Hunter Henry (foot) active, Raridon out-targeted the veteran six to three and produced 52 yards to Henry's 35 on the same amount of catches. Raridon has been a big-play threat as a rookie, averaging 14.1 yards per catch on 16 grabs this season, turning his 26 targets into 225 yards and two touchdowns. He's one of the better back-end TE2 options in fantasy.
