headline: Raridon had one reception for five yards on four targets in New England's 24-19 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Raridon's lone reception went for five yards early in the first quarter. He didn't record another catch for the remainder of the contest despite logging a hefty 93 percent offensive snap share, largely due to No .1 tight end Hunter Henry departing in the first half due to a foot injury. Should Henry remain sidelined in Week 9, Raridon will have another big opportunity to produce in a home tilt against Green Bay.

headline: Raridon caught three of four targets for 56 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's Week 7 loss to the Bears.
story: Raridon got open late in the third quarter and hauled in a nicely placed pass from Drake Maye for a 30-yard score. The rookie tight end finished third on the team with 56 receiving yards and tied for third with three receptions. Raridon is clearly behind Hunter Henry, who posted a 7-71-0 receiving line on seven targets, in the tight-end pecking order, but he's shown promise early in his career with 12 catches on 16 targets for 168 yards and two TDs through six games.

headline: Raridon caught all five of his targets for 57 yards during the Patriots' 45-17 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: The rookie third-rounder accumulated three catches (on four targets) for 44 yards and a score in each of his first three games, and he eclipsed those receiving marks (except the score) during Sunday's blowout win. His five catches co-led the Patriots with Efton Chism, and the duo finished tied for the third-most receiving yards behind Kyle Williams (91) and DeMario Douglas (65). Raridon's 43 offensive snaps were only slightly behind top tight end Hunter Henry (48), and the former has played more than 50 percent of New England's offensive snaps in each of the last two weeks. The Patriots will stay home for Week 6 to host the Jets on Oct. 18 in an AFC East divisional showdown.

headline: Raridon (ankle) was not listed in Wednesday's injury report ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Raridon exited Sunday's win over the Bills due to an ankle injury. However, he's not listed on the injury report ahead of the Week 5 meeting with Las Vegas.

headline: Raridon (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Buffalo.
story: Raridon didn't play in Week 3 against the Jaguars due to a hamstring injury. However, an ankle injury could mean he won't be back in Week 4. If Raridon can't return, Cameron Latu could see more work behind Hunter Henry.

headline: Raridon (thigh) is listed as active Sunday at Buffalo.
story: After missing Week 3 due to a thigh injury, Raridon was limited on all three Week 4 practice reports and then listed as questionable for Sunday's contest. Now that the rookie third-rounder is confirmed to be available, he'll hop back in as the No. 2 TE behind Hunter Henry, which so far has equated to a 2-32-1 line on two targets through the first two games of his career.

headline: Raridon (thigh) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills, Phil Perry of NBC Sports Boston reports.
story: Raridon was a limited participant in all three practices during Week 4 prep, which was enough for the rookie third-rounder to draw the questionable tag for Sunday's AFC East showdown. If Raridon is cleared to play, then he would slot behind Hunter Henry on the tight end depth chart ahead of Cameron Latu and Tanner Arkin.

headline: Raridon (thigh) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Raridon has now opened Week 4 prep with consecutive limited practices. If the thigh injury keeps Raridon off the field for Sunday's game against the Bills, Tanner Arkin could see more snaps behind Hunter Henry and Cameron Latu.

headline: Raridon (thigh) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: A thigh injury prevented the rookie third-rounder from playing against the Jaguars in Week 3. He was limited in all three practices prior to New England's loss to Jacksonville, so he may have to log a full practice over the next two days to have a realistic chance of playing Sunday against Buffalo.

headline: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive but available as the emergency third quarterback for Sunday's game against the Lions in Munich.
story: As he has for the first nine games of his career, Morton only will see the field if both starter Drake Maye and backup Tommy DeVito leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback against the Packers on Sunday.
story: As the emergency third quarterback, Morton is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito are removed from the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback against the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: As the emergency third quarterback, Morton is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito are removed from the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive and designated as New England's emergency third quarterback for Thursday's matchup versus Chicago.
story: This has become the routine for Morton, who has worked as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback every week so far this season. The role has yet to land the rookie QB any game reps, and he'll be eligible to enter Thursday's contest only if both quarterbacks ahead of him (Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito) are forced to exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback against the Jets on Sunday.
story: Morton remains the third option at quarterback behind starter Drake Maye and backup Tommy DeVito. The seventh-round rookie will only enter Sunday's contest if both Maye and DeVito cannot return to the game.

headline: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback against the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Effectively, the rookie seventh-rounder is not allowed to play unless both Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Morton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Patriots' emergency third quarterback against the Bills on Sunday.
story: As such, the rookie seventh-rounder is not allowed to play unless both Drake Maye and Tommy DeVito leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Borregales made his sole field-goal attempt and one PAT in the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions in Munich on Sunday.
story: Borregales made a 33-yard field goal on the first drive of the game. The kicker is now 11-for-13 on field-goal attempts and 24-for-25 on PATs through 10 regular-season games in 2026.

headline: Borregales made all three of his PATs in Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
story: Borregales didn't attempt a field goal, and it was the second time this season that he didn't kick any. For the year, the second-year kicker in 10 of 13 on FGAs and has made 23 of 24 extra points. He'll be a fantasy target for next Sunday's potential shootout in Detroit.

headline: Borregales made one of his two field goals and all three PATs in the Patriots' 24-19 win over the Dolphins on Sunday.
story: Borregales missed a 40-yard field goal during the Patriots' last drive of the first half. The kicker continues to struggle in the intermediate range, now sitting at 7-for-10 on field-goal attempts from 30-49 yards during the 2026 regular season.

headline: Borregales made his only field-goal attempt and was successful on all three extra-point tries Thursday in a Week 7 loss to the Bears.
story: Borregales was limited to extra-point tries until the Patriots' final drive of the game, when the kicker nailed a 47-yard field goal with less than a minute remaining to bring his team to within six points ahead of an unsuccessful onside kick. The second-year pro has been held to just four FG attempts -- all of which he has made -- over his past four contests after going 5-for-7 across New England's first three games of the season. The lower volume is largely due to the Patriots' improvement on offense over that four-game stretch, as Borregales has gone 14-for-15 on point-after attempts during that span.

headline: Borregales made both of his field-goal attempts and went 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during the Patriots' 26-19 win over the Jets on Sunday.
story: All of Borregales' kick attempts came from within 35 yards, with his longest field goal coming from 32 yards. He missed his first extra point of the season, and through six games he has gone 8-for-10 on field-goal attempts and 14-for-15 on extra-point tries. The Patriots will operate on a short practice week ahead of Thursday's road tilt against the Bears.

headline: Borregales made his lone field-goal attempt and all six extra-point tries during Sunday's 45-17 win over Las Vegas.
story: Drake Maye and the Patriots offense dominated Sunday's game, so Borregales was mostly limited to extra-point duties outside of a 28-yard chip-shot field goal early in the fourth quarter that gave the Patriots a 38-10 lead. Despite the lack of field-goal attempts over his last two games, Borregales' scoring floor figures to be elevated now that New England's offense has seemingly figured things out. The Patriots will stay at home and host the Jets for Week 6 on Oct. 18.

headline: Borregales did not attempt a field and made all three of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 29-26 win over Buffalo.
story: Borregales went without a field-goal try for the first time in a regular-season contest since Week 10 of the 2025 campaign. The kicker made the three kicks that he was given the opportunity to attempt Sunday, and he figures to get more field-goal chances in Week 5 against the Raiders.

headline: Henry caught two of three passes for 22 yards during the Patriots' 35-10 loss to the Lions on Sunday in Munich.
story: Both of Henry's catches of 10 and 12 yards came on the Patriots' first offensive drive of the game, which ended with a 33-yard field goal by Andy Borregales. Unfortunately for the Patriots, Drake Maye suffered an ankle injury on the play prior to the field goal and was unable to return, and the offense struggled to move down the field with backup Tommy DeVito under center. Maye will undergo more tests once the team has returned to home soil, but the good news for the Patriots is that they are on a bye for Week 11, so the third-year quarterback has more time to heal before New England's next game in Week 12 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 29. Henry's two catches Sunday were his fewest since Week 3 against the Jaguars (one), and the veteran tight end has a 34-383-2 receiving line on 40 targets through 10 regular-season games.

headline: Henry (foot) doesn't carry an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Lions after logging another limited practice Friday.
story: Though Henry was limited at practice all three days leading up to the contest, the Patriots were likely managing his reps in anticipation of having the tight end available this weekend. While it's possible that the team will get top WR A.J. Brown (knee/ankle, questionable) back versus Detroit, RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) is still out and Rhamondre Stevenson (knee, questionable) is banged up, so Henry figures to be a key available option for QB Drake Maye to work with, provided he avoids any setbacks with his foot.

headline: Henry (foot) was a limited practice participant Thursday.
story: Henry played through the injury in last week's loss to Green Bay and has now managed back-to-back limited practices to open Week 10. He'll likely gut it out again Sunday against the Lions in Munich, and while the matchup is favorable, rookie Eli Raridon had been cutting into Henry's snaps and targets even before the veteran injured his foot in a Week 8 win at Miami. Henry played 49.2 percent of snaps in the Week 9 loss to Green Bay, catching each of his three targets for 35 yards.

headline: Henry (foot) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: After injuring his foot in Week 8 against Miami, Henry played through the limited practice reps last week against the Packers and turned three targets into three grabs for 35 yards. Assuming he didn't suffer a setback, Henry should be fine for Sunday's game against the Lions in Germany.

headline: Henry caught all three of his targets for 35 yards during Sunday's 45-27 loss to the Packers.
story: Henry returned to action after suffering a foot injury in the first half of the Patriots' Week 8 win over the Dolphins and missing the majority of that contest. The tight end was held in check versus Green Bay, finishing with three or fewer catches for the sixth time this season. Henry has now reeled in 32 of 37 targets for 361 yards and two touchdowns over nine contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Henry (foot) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Packers, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: After opening the week with back-to-back missed practices, Henry was able to work in a limited fashion Friday before heading into the weekend with a 'questionable' designation. With his active status confirmed, in the absence of any setbacks or limitations Sunday, Henry a" who leads the Patriots with 29 catches and is second in receiving yardage (326), to go with two TDs through eight games -- will have an opportunity to remain a key target for QB Drake Maye in a New England passing offense that continues to be without top WRs A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder).

headline: Henry (foot) "has a realistic chance to play" Sunday against the Packers, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Henry practiced only once all week and it was a limited appearance Friday, but there is reason to believe he will be available Sunday. His status for Week 9 will officially be revealed when the Patriots release their inactives 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Henry (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Packers, Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald reports.
story: After opening the week with back-to-back missed practices, Henry's designation leaves the door open for him to play heading into Sunday. If he can't play, New England would need to lean more heavily on rookie Eli Raridon at tight end against Green Bay.

headline: Henry (foot) is present for the media-access portion of Friday's practice, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: After missing practice both Wednesday and Thursday, Henry's presence for Friday's session is a positive sign ahead of Sunday's game against the Packers. The Patriots' upcoming injury report will reveal both the tight end's official participation level, as well as his Week 9 game status.

headline: Henry (foot) wasn't spotted at Thursday's practice, Evan Lazar of the Patriots' official site reports.
story: Henry has started Week 9 prep with back-to-back absences after exiting during the Patriots' Week 8 win over Miami. If the veteran tight end is unable to practice in at least some capacity Friday, he'll likely be ruled out for Sunday's game against the Packers, paving the way for rookie third-round pick Eli Raridon to take on an expanded role.

headline: Henry (foot) wasn't on the field for the media-access portion of Wednesday's practice, Mike Reiss of ESPN.com reports.
story: Henry was unable to return to Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins after exiting in the second quarter due to the foot issue. The Patriots haven't provided many details regarding the severity of the injury, but Henry will be sidelined as the team begins Week 9 prep. Henry will have two more chances to potentially practice this week before the Patriots decide whether he'll take a designation into Sunday's game against the Packers.

headline: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said Monday that he had no update on Henry's (foot) status heading into Sunday's game against the Packers, Karen Guregian of MassLive.com reports. "I don't have any expectations yet," Vrabel said of Henry. "It's kind of how he responds here. He wasn't able to finish the [Week 8] game. So we'll see where he is, and I know Hunter will do everything he can to get back to help us."
story: Henry recorded three receptions for 30 yards on three targets before exiting in the second quarter of Sunday's 24-19 win over the Dolphins due to the foot issue. The Patriots haven't provided any further word on where exactly Henry stands in his recovery, but more context on that front should arrive when the team releases its first Week 9 injury report Wednesday. Despite his early departure in Week 8, Henry leads the team in receptions (29) and is second to only wideout DeMario Douglas in receiving yards (326) through eight games.

headline: Henry (foot) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game in Miami.
story: Henry exited in the first half of this Week 8 matchup and eventually was ruled out midway through the fourth quarter. He ended with three catches (on three targets) for 30 yards. Eli Raridon will act as the Patriots' top pass-catching tight end for as long as Henry is sidelined.

headline: Henry (foot) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Prior to his departure from the contest, Henry had caught all three of his targets for 30 yards. Next up for the Patriots' TE snaps in his absence is Eli Raridon, with Cameron Latu and Tanner Arkin also on hand versus Miami.

headline: Henry secured all seven targets for 71 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
story: The veteran tight end was a key contributor throughout the night, finishing with team-high figures in receptions and targets while ending second in receiving yards. All three components of Henry's receiving line also were season-high figures, and he now has between 44 and 71 receiving yards in four consecutive games. Henry will take a 26-296-2 line on 31 targets into a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Henry caught four of five targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-19 win over the Jets.
story: Henry's seven-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter proved to be the game-winning score, putting New England ahead 23-16. After not finding the end zone the first four weeks of the season, Henry has scored in back-to-back games. The veteran tight end has been held under 50 yards receiving in five of six contests. He's the definition of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet ahead of Thursday's game with the Bears.

headline: Henry caught three of four targets for 44 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 45-17 win over the Raiders.
story: Henry was able to reel in at least three passes for the fourth time this season, and his biggest moment of the game came in the second quarter when Drake Maye connected with him for an 11-yard score. The tight end has now caught 15 of 19 targets for 177 yards and a touchdown over the first five games of the season.

headline: Henry finished with five receptions for 62 yards on five targets in Sunday's 29-26 win over the Bills.
story: The catch and yardage totals were season-best marks for Henry, who took the field for 49 of the Patriots' 76 offensive snaps (64.5 percent). With fellow tight end Eli Raridon (ankle) making an early exit from the contest and potentially at risk of missing the Patriots' Week 5 game against the Raiders, Henry could be called upon to handle a heftier workload next Sunday.

headline: Richards (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
story: The offensive lineman was injured in Week 10 against the Panthers and was initially expected to miss several weeks. He missed last Sunday's loss to the Bears but appears to have a chance to return following three limited practices. Richards has seen action at both left and right tackle this season.

headline: Richards (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears.
story: Richards suffered a significant knee injury in the Saints' Week 10 loss to the Panthers. The offensive tackle is expected to miss multiple weeks due to the injury, so his absence for Week 11 is no surprise. Mason Murphy is set to start at right tackle while Richards recovers.

headline: Head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that Richards will be sidelined for multiple weeks due to a knee injury that the latter sustained during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday, Matthew Paras of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
story: Richards injured his knee during the fourth quarter of Sunday's game and wasn't cleared by medical staff to return. The injury appears severe enough for him to warrant an extended period of time on the shelf, so Richards is a candidate to be placed on injured reserve. Mason Murphy will likely move into the starting spot at right tackle for as long as Richards is sidelined.

headline: Richards (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Carolina, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
story: Richards suffered a knee injury during the fourth quarter of Sunday's contest. Mason Murphy has taken over at right tackle in Richards' absence.

headline: Fuaga (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Bengals.
story: After missing the previous two games, Fuaga appears to have a chance to return Sunday following a trio of limited practices. Mason Murphy started last Sunday's game against the Bears at right tackle in place of Fuaga.

headline: Fuaga (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears.
story: Fuaga did not participate in any Week 11 prep sessions due to a knee injury he sustained during Week 10 prep. The right tackle will now miss consecutive games due to the issue.

headline: Fuaga (knee) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Fuaga is recovering from a knee strain he sustained a week ago, and his availability for Week 11 is in serious doubt. Unless he's somehow able to return to practice Friday, he'll probably end up on the sidelines during Sunday's game at Chicago.

headline: Fuaga (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: Fuaga is dealing with a knee sprain that he sustained during Thursday's practice, per Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com. However, head coach Kellen Moore indicated Friday that he doesn't expect Fuaga to be sidelined long term, as reported by Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio. Mason Murphy and Asim Richards are the top candidates to start at right tackle in Fuaga's absence.

headline: Fuaga (knee) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: Fuaga was a new addition to the Saints' injury report Thursday, suggesting he may have gotten hurt at practice. In any case, he'll probably need to manage a full practice Friday to avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Emerson (concussion) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game at Cincinnati.
story: Emerson presumably cleared concussion protocol during the week, and he'll return from a one-game absence in Week 12. He figures to start at corner against a pass-happy Bengals offense Sunday.

headline: Emerson (concussion) was a full practice participant Wednesday, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
story: Emerson was held out of practice during Week 11 prep and did not play against the Bears this past Sunday. His full practice participation indicates that he's progressing through the league's concussion protocol, but he would need to pass an evaluation by an independent neurologist in order to be available for Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

headline: Emerson (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bears.
story: Emerson was unable to practice all week while in the league's concussion protocol. The fifth-year defensive back will not suit up for Sunday's contest, so Quincy Riley figures to be the top candidate to start at outside cornerback opposite Kool-Aid McKinstry in the absence of Emerson, whose next chance to play is Week 12 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 29.

headline: Emerson (concussion) didn't practice Wednesday.
story: Emerson entered the league's concussion protocol following the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers in Week 10, and he finished that contest with only one assisted tackle. He'll have two more chances to return to practice, but even if he does get some reps under his belt, he would need to be cleared of the league's protocol in order to play against the Bears on Sunday. Quincy Riley would likely start opposite Kool-Aid McKinstry if Emerson is sidelined for Week 11.

headline: Emerson (shin) is active for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: Emerson drew the questionable tag for Sunday's NFC South tilt due to a nagging shin injury, but the fifth-year pro was given the green light by medical staff to play. He has 20 tackles (18 solo), four pass defenses (including two interceptions) and one forced fumble across seven regular-season games.

headline: Emerson (shin) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.
story: Emerson's practice reps were limited during Week 10 prep due to a shin injury. He was able to play through the injury in Week 9 against the Browns, and he finished that contest with two solo tackles in a 23-22 overtime win for the Saints. Second-year pro Quincy Riley would likely be the next man up at outside cornerback opposite Kool-Aid McKinstry if Emerson is unable to play Sunday.

headline: Emerson is listed as active for Sunday's matchup against the Browns.
story: Emerson didn't participate in Friday's practice after kicking off the week limited Wednesday and Thursday. He appears to be ready to go, as he's not on the Saints' list of inactive players. The 26-year-old has 18 total tackles (16 solo), four pass deflections and two interceptions in six games.

headline: Emerson (shin) is questionable to suit up for Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Browns.
story: Emerson was a limited participant in each of New Orleans' first two practices this week due to a shin injury. However, he downgraded to non-participation Friday and was given a tag of questionable for Sunday. Should Emerson not be able to play against Cleveland, Quincy Riley would likely return to a starting role.

headline: Emerson recorded seven solo tackles and four passes defensed, including two interceptions, during Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
story: Emerson was all over the field in Week 6, finishing second on the team in tackles behind linebacker Pete Werner (11). The cornerback was thrust into a more prominent role in the secondary after Kool-Aid McKinstry was forced out of the game with a migraine, and Emerson definitely didn't disappoint. He was able to reel in a pair of interceptions, picking off Jameis Winston in the third quarter before jumping in front of a pass from J.J. McCarthy one quarter later.

headline: Emerson (shoulder) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Emerson suffered a shoulder injury during the Week 2 win over the Ravens, subsequently resulting in him missing the Week 3 meeting with the Raiders. However, with Emerson logging a full session to begin the practice week ahead of Monday's clash with the Cardinals, it appears he will be back on the field for that one.

headline: Werner (hamstring) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game at Cincinnati.
story: Werner was out Week 11 at Chicago due to a hamstring injury he sustained in Week 10 versus the Panthers, but it now looks like he has put it behind him. He projects to start at linebacker next to veteran Kaden Elliss in Week 12.

headline: Werner (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
story: Werner was held out of the Saints' Week 11 loss to the Bears due to a hamstring injury that he sustained against the Panthers in Week 10. Wednesday was his first practice participation since the injury, and he'll have two more opportunities to log a full session and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Bengals.

headline: Werner (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game against Chicago.
story: Werner injured his hamstring against the Panthers in Week 10, and the injury prevented the sixth-year linebacker from practicing in any capacity during Week 11 prep. He was initially tagged as questionable, but he will observe Sunday's game from the sidelines, and his next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29. Danny Stutsman figures to start alongside Kaden Elliss at inside linebacker in Werner's absence.

headline: Werner (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bears.
story: Werner was held out of practice all week while managing a hamstring injury that he sustained against the Panthers in Week 10. Despite the lack of practice reps, the sixth-year pro has drawn the questionable tag for Sunday's road contest. Danny Stutsman would likely start at inside linebacker next to Kaden Elliss if Werner is unable to play against Chicago.

headline: Werner (hamstring) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Werner suffered a hamstring injury in the first half of the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers in Week 10 and did not return. He'll have two more opportunities to practice in at least a limited capacity, but if he cannot play against the Bears on Sunday, then Danny Stutsman would be the top candidate to start alongside Kaden Elliss at inside linebacker.

headline: Werner (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
story: Werner left in the first half due to a hamstring injury, which medical staff has deemed severe enough for the sixth-year linebacker to be sidelined for the rest of Sunday's contest. Danny Stutsman will work alongside Kaden Elliss at inside linebacker in the absence of Werner, whose status for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, is up in the air.

headline: Werner (hamstring) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Panthers, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
story: Werner sustained the injury in the first half of Sunday's game. He's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return, so Danny Stutsman has entered the game at inside linebacker in Werner's stead.

headline: Werner registered 11 tackles (three solo) during the Saints' 23-22 overtime win over the Browns in Week 9.
story: Werner co-led the Saints in tackles in Week 9, and it was the third time he's reached double-digit stops over his last four outings. Werner is on pace to record his first 100-plus tackle campaign of his six-year NFL career and is up to 65 tackles (29 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass defenses through eight regular-season games.

headline: Werner finished Sunday's loss to the Steelers with eight tackles (three solo).
story: Werner had a two-game streak of double-digit stops snapped, but he was still plenty productive. The veteran linebacker dealt with a neck injury in early October but appears past that issue, as he's played every Saints defensive snap in three straight contests. Werner leads New Orleans with 54 tackles (including 2.0 sacks) through seven games.

headline: Werner recorded 11 total tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding a pass defensed during Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
story: Werner was able to register double-digit stops for the second straight week and third time overall this season. The linebacker was also able to get to the quarterback in Week 6, sacking Jameis Winston in the second quarter. Through six games so far this year, Werner has compiled 46 total tackles (23 solo), including 2.0 sacks, while also producing two passes defensed.

headline: Werner (neck) is active for Monday night's matchup with Atlanta.
story: Werner suffered a neck injury during the team's Week 3 loss to Las Vegas, but he is all set to play Monday. The linebacker has registered 21 total tackles (13 solo), including 1.0 sacks, over three contests so far this season.

headline: Werner (neck) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Falcons, Matthew Paras of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
story: Werner injured his neck during the Saints' 35-27 loss to the Raiders in Week 3, which prevented him from participating in each of New Orleans' first two practices of Week 4 prep. His status may not be officially known until about 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff, when the Saints announce their list of inactive players. Kaden Elliss (calf) has already been ruled out, and if Werner cannot play, then Isaiah Stalbird and Danny Stutsman would be the next men up at inside linebacker.

headline: Werner (neck) did not participate in Friday's practice.
story: Werner has been unable to practice since sustaining a neck injury in the Saints' Week 3 loss to the Raiders. If the linebacker cannot practice in any capacity Saturday, the chances he suits up for Monday night's game against the Falcons will be low.

headline: Werner (neck) did not participate at the Saints' practice Thursday.
story: Werner sustained a neck injury in the first half of the team's Week 3 loss to Las Vegas, and he was unable to return to the contest. The linebacker will have two more chances to practice before Monday night's matchup with the Falcons.

headline: Fant (calf) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Bengals, while Juwan Johnson (hamstring) has been ruled out, Matthew Paras of the New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
story: Fant would be in line to operate as the top TE for the Saints if he gets the green light to suit up against the team for which he played last season. The 29-year-old Fant has scored either three or four touchdowns in six of his eight NFL regular seasons, including three apiece in 2025 with Cincinnati and so far in 2026 with New Orleans. Rookie third-round pick Oscar Delp is the next tight end up if Fant joins Johnson on the sidelines.

headline: Fant caught two of his five targets for 19 yards in the Saints' 21-13 loss to the Bears on Sunday.
story: Fant played 49 offensive snaps in Sunday's contest. The starting tight end was on the field for 69 percent of the team's offensive plays but remains off the same page with quarterback Tyler Shough. The tight end's five targets are the most attention he has seen since Week 1 against the Lions.

headline: Fant failed to haul in his lone target during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
story: Fant didn't connect with Tyler Shough on a short pass late in the first quarter, and that ended up being the only target for the veteran tight end. Fant has a 12-96-3 line on 19 targets through eight regular-season games, although he's logged one reception or zero in four of his last five outings. He doesn't have much fantasy appeal as the Saints' TE2 behind Juwan Johnson heading into Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

headline: Fant Donaldson (back) upgraded to full participation at Thursday's practice.
story: Fant was limited at Wednesday's practice, but the veteran TE faced no limitations Thursday, suggesting that he'll be good to go for Sunday's game against the Panthers. He has worked as the Saints' No. 2 option at the position behind Juwan Johnson.

headline: Fant (back) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Fant may have tweaked his back during the Saints' 23-22 overtime win over the Browns in Week 9, when he finished with one catch on two targets for 12 yards. He'll have two more opportunities to increase his practice participation ahead of Sunday's NFC South tilt against the Panthers. Fant has accumulated 12 catches on 18 targets for 96 yards and three touchdowns through seven regular-season games.

headline: Fant caught one pass for 12 yards on two targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win against Cleveland.
story: The veteran tight end logged 47 percent of the offensive snaps but is mainly a blocker, while Juwan Johnson handles most of the pass-catching duties at the position. Fant has four catches for 30 yards over his last four games and is not even remotely on the fantasy radar.

headline: Fant gathered in all two targets for 11 yards during Sunday's 16-10 defeat against Pittsburgh.
story: After finding the end zone twice in the loss to the Raiders in Week 3, Fant has combined for just three catches in his previous three appearances. While his two receptions Sunday were a small step in the right direction, he is expected to continue to play second fiddle to Juwan Johnson moving forward. It may also be a matter of time before rookie Oscar Delp logs more snaps from week to week.

headline: Fant brought in his lone target for seven yards during the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Fant played 30 of 45 offensive snaps Sunday in his return from a one-game absence due to an abdominal injury, which was one more than fellow tight end Juwan Johnson. Fant saw only one target from Tyler Shough, although the Saints' offense struggled as a whole against the Vikings' defense. Fant has a 9-73-3 receiving line on 13 targets through four games heading into Week 7 against the Giants, whose defense has given up 33 catches to tight ends this season, tied for fifth-most in the NFL.

headline: Fant (abdomen) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Vikings.
story: Fant opened the week with back-to-back limited practices before logging a full session Friday, which was enough for him to shed an injury tag and put himself in a position to return from a one-game absence due to an abdominal injury. He has an 8-66-3 receiving line (on 12 targets) through three regular-season games while operating as the Saints' TE2 behind Juwan Johnson.

headline: Fant (abdomen) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: After sitting out Monday's loss to Atlanta, Fant has had his reps capped for the Saints' first two Week 5 practices while he continues to manage the abdominal injury. He'll likely need to upgrade to full participation Friday to avoid taking a designation into Sunday's matchup with the Vikings. When available this season, Fant has been productive as the Saints' No. 2 tight end behind Juwan Johnson, registering eight receptions for 66 yards and three touchdowns on 12 targets over three appearances.

headline: Fant (abdomen) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: Fant missed Monday night's loss to the Falcons, but his limited start to the week would seem to give the veteran tight end a good shot to return to the field for Week 5 against the Vikings. He's turned 12 targets into eight catches for 66 yards and three touchdowns this season as one of Tyler Shough's favorite options near the end zone.

headline: Fant (abdomen) is listed as inactive for Monday's game against the Falcons.
story: Despite being a limited practice participant during Week 4 prep, Fant will miss his first contest of the campaign due to an abdominal injury. Oscar Delp and Treyton Welch thus will serve as the reserve tight ends behind starter Juwan Johnson on Monday. Fant's next chance to play is this coming Sunday versus the Vikings.

headline: Fant (abdomen) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Falcons, Matthew Paras of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
story: Fant's practice participation was limited all week due to an abdominal injury that he likely picked up in Week 3 against the Raiders. With the questionable tag, the veteran tight end's status for Monday may not be known until the Saints announce their list of inactive players approximately 90 minutes before the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff. Oscar Delp and Treyton Welch would see more rotational snaps at tight end behind Juwan Johnson if Fant is not cleared to play against Atlanta.

headline: Fant (abdomen) practiced in a limited capacity Friday, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: Fant maintained his activity level for a second session in a row, giving him just one more chance to get back to full this week. Saturday's injury report will reveal if he's in danger of missing Monday's game against the Falcons due to his abdominal issue.

headline: Fant was limited in practice Thursday due to an abdominal injury.
story: Fant has taken full advantage of his 12 targets through three games this season, turning them into eight catches for 66 yards and three touchdowns. Now, a health concern is impacting him at the start of Week 4 prep, so his status bears watching as the Saints ramp up for Monday's matchup with the Falcons.

headline: Edwards (knee) does not have an injury designation against the Panthers on Sunday, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.
story: Edwards' practice reps were limited Wednesday and Thursday due to a knee injury, but he avoided an injury tag for Week 10 after logging a full session Friday. He has started in each of the Saints' first eight games of the regular season.

headline: Edwards (knee) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: Edwards popped up on the Saints' injury report Wednesday with a knee injury, and now his status for Week 10 looks uncertain. He might have to practice in full Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Johnson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Cincinnati, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: Johnson suffered a hamstring injury this past Sunday at Chicago, and he then was listed as a DNP on the Saints' first two Week 12 practice reports, despite head coach Kellen Moore calling the tight end "day-to-day" Thursday, according to Terrell. With Johnson missing his first game of the campaign and Noah Fant (calf) questionable for Sunday's matchup, Oscar Delp is the sole healthy player at the position on the active roster.

headline: Coach Kellen Moore said Thursday that Johnson (hamstring/wrist) is considered day-to-day ahead of Sunday's game against the Bengals, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: Per Ross Jackson of WWL-TV, Johnson -- who logged a 'DNP' on Wednesday's practice estimate -- wasn't spotted at Thursday's session. The tight end thus has one more chance to practice before the Saints' Week 12 injury designations are assigned. If Johnson ends up limited or out this weekend, Noah Fant and Oscar Delp would be in line for added snaps in the team's offense this weekendi.

headline: Johnson (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday due to a hamstring/wrist issue, Katherine Terrell of ESPN reports.
story: Johnson was listed as having both hamstring and wrist injuries. He injured the hamstring in Sunday's loss to the Bears, but this is the first report of a wrist issue. Head coach Kellen Moore said that Johnson is "day-to-day," according to Terrell. If Johnson does not progress in time for Sunday's game, Noah Fant and Oscar Delp would be the Saints' primary tight-end options.

headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that Johnson is still undergoing further medical evaluation after injuring his hamstring during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.
story: The Saints expect to have a better feel for Johnson's status Wednesday, when the team holds its first practice of Week 12. Before exiting Sunday in the third quarter, Johnson was targeted just once and failed to record a reception for the second time in 10 appearances on the season. If the hamstring injury prevents Johnson from playing next weekend in Cincinnati, Noah Fant and Oscar Delp would be in line for added snaps at tight end.

headline: Johnson injured his hamstring during Sunday's game in Chicago, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
story: Johnson visited the sideline tent in the third quarter before the Saints deemed him questionable to return. He didn't catch his only target before his departure.

headline: Johnson caught two passes for 28 yards on three targets in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
story: With Jordyn Tyson playing his second game since debuting last week, the rookie wideout was targeted 13 times on Tyler Shough's 35 pass attempts. It didn't leave much for the rest of New Orleans' pass catchers, as Travis Etienne was actually second on the team with five targets. Over his last five games, Johnson has nine catches for 85 yards and a score. He's become a low-end TE2 for fantasy.

headline: Johnson caught both of his targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
story: Johnson made a catch early in the game but wasn't heard from again until overtime, when he caught a 15-yard touchdown to open the extra period. It proved to be the game-winner after the Browns failed on their two-point conversion following their touchdown with one minute left on the clock. After a strong start to the season in which he caught three touchdowns and posted 50-plus yards in each of the first four games, Johnson has been limited to just 57 yards and one score on seven grabs across the last four contests. With rookie wideout Jordyn Tyson back to muddy the picture even further, Johnson is more of a touchdown-or-bust fantasy bet.

headline: Johnson caught one of three targets for seven yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
story: Johnson was held in check yet again in Week 7. The tight end has now gone three straight games without exceeding 16 receiving yards, and he hasn't scored a touchdown since Week 3. Johnson has slowly become an unreliable fantasy option as the season has progressed, but he'll have the opportunity to hit the reset button during the Saints' bye week in Week 8.

headline: Johnson failed to reel in either of his targets during Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
story: Johnson went without a catch in a regular-season contest for the first time since Week 3 of the 2024 campaign. The tight end had reeled in at least three passes in each of the team's first five games of the year. Over the last two weeks, Johnson has caught four of seven targets for 16 yards, and his next chance to get back on track will come in Week 7 against the Steelers in Paris.

headline: Johnson brought in four of five targets for 16 yards in the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
story: The veteran tight end tied Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele for the team lead in receptions, but given Tyler Shough threw for only 96 yards overall, Johnson couldn't generate any meaningful fantasy production with his quartet of catches. Johnson has recorded at least four receptions in four straight games, and despite Sunday's season-low yardage total, he's still compiled a solid 248 receiving yards and has five catches of 20-plus yards heading into a Week 6 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

headline: Johnson secured six of eight targets for 59 yards in the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday night.
story: Johnson tied for second in receptions and also finished as the runner-up in receiving yards on the night for the Saints in the lopsided loss. The veteran tight end has gotten the season off to a productive start, recording at least 53 receiving yards in each contest and posting 14 of his 21 catches of the season in the last two games alone. Johnson also has drawn at least seven targets in three of the first four games, affording him a very appealing fantasy floor going into a Week 5 home matchup against the Vikings on Sunday.

headline: McCoy (biceps) was listed as a full participant during New Orleans' practice estimate Thursday.
story: McCoy was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice but seems to be trending toward making his return after missing the last two weeks due to a biceps injury. The 29-year-old should resume his role as the team's starting center during Sunday's matchup against the Bengals.

headline: McCoy (biceps) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears.
story: McCoy has not practiced since sustaining a biceps injury in the Saints' Week 9 clash with the Browns. The center will now miss consecutive games due to the injury, leaving Cesar Ruiz to start at center against the Bears.

headline: McCoy (biceps) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: The biceps injury McCoy suffered back in Week 9 versus the Browns was expected to keep him out for multiple games, and he seems to be trending toward being out again in Week 11. If he can't return to practice Friday, Cesar Ruiz will likely be in line to start at center Sunday at Chicago, which would leave the starting right guard spot to rookie fourth-rounder Jeremiah Wright.

headline: McCoy (biceps) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.
story: McCoy is expected to miss multiple games while tending to a biceps injury that he sustained in Week 9 against the Browns. Cesar Ruiz is expected to serve as the Saints' starting center for as long as McCoy is sidelined.

headline: Coach Kellen Moore said Monday that McCoy will be out "for a little bit" as he deals with the bicep injury he suffered during Sunday's game versus the Browns, Luke Johnson of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
story: Per Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio New Orleans, Moore also said Monday that McCoy is not tending to a long-term or season-ending injury, and he does not believe it will require surgery. William Sherman filled in for McCoy at center after he exited during the fourth quarter in Week 9, but Cesar Ruiz also has experience at the position, and rookie fourth-rounder Jeremiah Wright is available should the Saints need him at guard.

headline: McCoy (biceps) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Browns.
story: McCoy exited the fourth quarter of Sunday's game with a biceps injury. The 16-16 bout has entered overtime, and it is unclear if the center will return to the contest before it ends. Asim Richards, Jeremiah Wright or William Sherman would be next in line at center.

headline: Sanker recorded seven tackles (four solo) including 1.0 sacks during Sunday's 21-13 loss at Chicago.
story: Sanker was able to wrap up Caleb Williams for the first sack of his career in Week 11, and he collected seven-plus tackles for the fifth time this year. He'll probably be spending more time in coverage against a pass-dependent Bengals offense in Week 12.

headline: Sanker posted nine tackles (seven solo) in Sunday's Week 7 loss to Pittsburgh.
story: Sanker recorded his second-highest tackle tally of the campaign to lead New Orleans in that category. The second-year defender has now tallied six or more stops in five of his seven games this season. With 44 tackles through seven contests, Sanker is easily on pace to surpass the 80 stops he notched in 17 games as a rookie.

headline: Stutsman recorded nine tackles (three solo) and an interception during Sunday's 21-13 loss at Chicago.
story: Stutsman found himself in the right place at the right time when a Caleb Williams pass was batted into the air late in the second quarter, but the Saints weren't able to capitalize after starting in Bears territory. He also logged nine total tackles for a second straight game. His role in Week 12 against the Bengals will likely depend heavily on the status of Pete Werner (hamstring).

headline: Delp hauled in his lone target for a six-yard reception in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
story: The rookie third-round pick out of Georgia has handled a muted role at tight end behind Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant this season, compiling five receptions for 26 yards on five targets through nine appearances. Delp was limited to just 21 of the Saints' 72 offensive snaps in Week 11, but he could see his playing time pick up if the hamstring injury that knocked Johnson out of Sunday's loss early prevents him from suiting up this coming weekend in Cincinnati.

headline: Delp was not targeted during Monday's 45-24 loss versus the Falcons.
story: Delp did record a solo tackle in punt coverage after New Orleans went three-and-out on its first offensive series, but that was his only mark on the stat sheet in Week 4. On a positive note, he was second on the team in snaps at tight end (23) behind veteran Juwan Johnson (53) with Noah Fant (abdomen) sidelined. His involvement in Week 5 versus the Ravens will likely depend on the availability of Fant.

headline: Elliss recorded five tackles (two solo) in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
story: The five tackles were Elliss's fewest in a game this season, and it comes after back-to-back games of double-digit stops. Across seven appearances in 2026, Elliss has produced 61 tackles (31 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass breakups on 100 percent of the defensive snaps in those seven contests.

headline: Elliss recorded 15 tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
story: Elliss was all over the field Sunday with a career-high 15 tackles (11 in the first half), which included an eight-yard sack on Bryce Young on the final play of the third quarter. Elliss has logged 10-plus tackles and a sack in back-to-back games, and the veteran linebacker is up to 56 stops (29 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two pass defenses across six regular-season games.

headline: Elliss recorded 11 tackles (eight solo), including 1.0 sacks, during the Saints' 23-22 overtime victory over the Browns in Week 9.
story: Elliss entered Week 9 without a sack to his name, but he changed that early in the first quarter after taking down Shedeur Sanders for a seven-yard loss. Elliss' 11 stops co-led the Saints, and the veteran linebacker is up to 41 tackles (23 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one pass defense across five regular-season games.

headline: Elliss (calf) doesn't carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Steelers.
story: Elliss was limited earlier in the practice week and will return to the lineup after missing the previous three games. The 31-year-old linebacker has recorded 24 tackles (11 solo) and one pass breakup across three starts this season.

headline: Elliss (calf) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday.
story: Elliss has been sidelined for the Saints' past three games due to a calf injury, but it now seems there's been some progress in his recovery, and he might have a chance to return to game action in Week 7. He'll still probably have to log a full practice Thursday or Friday to avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Elliss (calf) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants, Jeff Nowak of The Big 870 New Orleans reports.
story: Elliss will miss a third consecutive game due to a calf injury. His next chance to play is Week 7 against the Steelers on Sunday, Oct. 25, though Elliss has yet to be cleared to practice. Danny Stutsman will once again start alongside Pete Werner at inside linebacker in Elliss's absence.

headline: Elliss (calf) did not participate at practice Wednesday.
story: Elliss has sat out the Saints' last two games due to a lingering calf injury, and his status for Week 6 now appears to be up in the air, too. He'll likely need to practice in some capacity Thursday or Friday to have a realistic chance of suiting up Sunday against the Giants.

headline: Elliss (calf) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Emily Leiker of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
story: Elliss was unable to practice all week, and his calf injury will cause him to miss a second consecutive game as a result. Second-year pro Danny Stutsman will continue to start next to Pete Werner at inside linebacker due to the absence of Elliss, whose next chance to play is Week 6 against the Giants on Sunday, Oct. 18.

headline: Elliss (calf) did not participate in practice Thursday.
story: Elliss was also deemed DNP on Wednesday's practice estimate. The veteran linebacker didn't practice at all last week due to a calf injury and missed this past Monday's loss to Atlanta. Elliss is looking unlikely to play against Minnesota in Week 5, though there's a chance he can suit up if he's able to practice in some capacity Friday.

headline: Elliss (calf) was estimated as a non-participant at practice Wednesday.
story: The Saints' only started their week of preparation with a walk-through practice, but the estimation signals Elliss is in jeopardy of missing another game because of a nagging calf injury. Unless he returns to practice in some capacity Thursday or Friday, odds are low he'll be available Sunday versus the Vikings.

headline: Elliss (calf) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Falcons, Matthew Paras of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
story: Elliss will miss his first game of the 2026 season due to a calf injury. Pete Werner (neck) is also listed as questionable, so the Saints may have to start Danny Stutsman and Isaiah Stalbird at inside linebacker for Monday's NFC South showdown. Elliss's next opportunity to play is Week 5 against the Vikings on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Elliss (calf) did not participate in Friday's practice.
story: Elliss has now missed consecutive sessions due to a calf injury. The linebacker has one more opportunity to log a limited practice Saturday. If Elliss cannot get on the field for at least one prep session, the odds of the 31-year-old suiting up for Monday night's game against the Falcons are close to zero.

headline: Elliss (calf) did not participate at the Saints' practice Thursday.
story: Elliss is dealing with an apparent calf injury as the team gets ready to face Atlanta on Monday night. The linebacker will have two more chances to log a practice before the team's Week 4 contest.

headline: Lance failed to catch his only target and added 47 yards on kickoff returns during Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
story: Lance was unable to reel in a deep pass from quarterback Tyler Shough in the first quarter, and he didn't get another look the rest of the game. The wide receiver was on the field for 21 offensive snaps, ranking fourth at his position behind Devaughn Vele (64), Chris Olave (62) and Jordyn Tyson (36) in the contest. Lance will continue to primarily serve as a special-teams asset for New Orleans moving forward, making him an unattractive option for fantasy managers.

headline: Lance returned three kickoffs for 55 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
story: The rookie fourth-rounder didn't see a target from Tyler Shough during Sunday's loss, and Lance has not recorded a catch in each of his last two outings, coinciding with the return of 2026 first-round wide receiver Jordyn Tyson. Lance's nine offensive snaps were a season low, and he figures to be limited to return duties now that Tyson is back in the fold. The Saints will hit the road for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

headline: Lance failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
story: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season NFL debut against Cleveland, Lance saw his snaps cut against Cleveland. After playing 79 percent of the offensive snaps in Week 7 against Pittsburgh, Lance logged just 51 percent of the plays versus the Browns. He has nine catches for 78 yards and a touchdown on 23 targets this season.

headline: Lance reeled in all two targets for 12 yards during Sunday's 16-10 loss to Pittsburgh.
story: Lance had two catches for the second consecutive game, though unlike the Week 6 win over the Giants, he didn't find the end zone. The 24-year-old has logged 332 offensive snaps this season, third in the receiving corps behind Chris Olave (387) and Devaughn Vele (438). However, despite being on the field more often than most of the other wideouts on the roster, Lance hasn't been productive thus far in his rookie campaign.

headline: Lance caught two of four passes for nine yards and a touchdown during the Saints' 34-27 win over the Giants on Sunday.
story: Lance's four targets were tied with Alvin Kamara for third most on the Saints behind Chris Olave (seven) and Devaughn Vele (six), with quarterback Tyler Shough completing only 16 of 30 passes. Both of Lance's catches came in the second quarter, the second of which was a two-yard touchdown that tied the game up at 10-10 with five seconds left in the first half. Lance's 36 offensive snaps were third most among New Orleans wide receivers, but his time as the team's WR3 could come to an end as soon as Week 7 against the Steelers on Oct. 25, given that rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR) is traveling with the team to Paris, per NewOrleans.Football.

headline: Lance turned five targets into a seven-yard catch during the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday.
story: Lance finished fifth on the Saints in targets from quarterback Tyler Shough, though each of the four misses between the duo came on deep passes. After catching three of four targets for 42 yards in his NFL debut against the Lions in Week 1, Lance has just two catches (on nine targets) for 15 yards over his last three games. He'll continue to operate as the Saints' WR3 behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. Lance's playing time likely will take a significant hit once fellow rookie Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is cleared to return from injured reserve, though ESPN's Adam Schefter notes that Week 7 against the Steelers is the earliest targeted return for Tyson. The Saints will stay at home for Week 5 against the Vikings and their aggressive defense.

headline: Donaldson logged a five-yard carry and brought in all four of his targets for 12 yards during the Saints' 21-13 loss to the Bears on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
story: Donaldson recorded season highs in both catches and targets, and he finished third on the Saints in both of those categories behind Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. However, Donaldson coughed up the football on his first catch of the game early in the second quarter, which the Bears offense capitalized on with a six-play drive that ended with a three-yard touchdown pass from Caleb Williams to D'Andre Swift. Donaldson's 32 offensive snaps were tied with Travis Etienne for most among Saints running backs Sunday, although Etienne saw a heavier workload with 14 carries for 76 yards while Alvin Kamara, who played only eight offensive snaps, found the end zone on a one-yard touchdown pass from Tyler Shough in the second quarter. Losers of three of their last four games, the Saints will look to reverse their fortunes in Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

headline: Donaldson (shoulder) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Donaldson missed the Saints' last three games due to a shoulder injury, but his full practice Wednesday indicates that he'll be available for Sunday's road game against the Bears. Even if Donaldson does suit up, his role in the backfield figures to be minimal, seeing as Travis Etienne is off injured reserve and Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime are also available for the Saints.

headline: Donaldson (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: Donaldson will miss a third straight game, while Travis Etienne (hamstring) has a chance to return from injured reserve. With Etienne listed as questionable, Audric Estime and Alvin Kamara could have significant roles. Donaldson mostly has played in obvious passing situations this year, often staying in as a blocker.

headline: Donaldson (shoulder) remained a non-participant at Thursday's practice.
story: Donaldson has yet to resume practicing since sustaining a shoulder injury in Week 7, which suggests he's trending for another absence in Sunday's Week 10 matchup with the Panthers. Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime are both expected to be available, while Travis Etienne's (hamstring) status is up in the air as the latter tries to work his way back from a hamstring injury that landed him on IR.

headline: Donaldson (shoulder) did not practice on Wednesday.
story: Donaldson missed last Sunday's overtime win against the Browns. With Audric Estime added to the roster last week and Travis Etienne (hamstring) having his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, Donaldson could have his offensive role disappear once he's healthy. The undrafted rookie running back has rushed 17 times for 81 yards (4.8 YPC) across seven appearances this season. He's also added six tackles (one solo) on special teams.

headline: Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: With Donaldson out and Travis Etienne (hamstring) still on injured reserve, the Saints will roll with a three-man backfield of Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller and Audric Estime. One of the league's least productive backfields doesn't evoke much fantasy excitement.

headline: Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) did not practice Thursday, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: After being limited Wednesday, Donaldson's downgrade to DNP puts him in jeopardy of missing Week 9 against the Browns. With Travis Etienne (hamstring) also looking unlikely to play, the Saints could be rolling with Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller and Audric Estime out of the backfield.

headline: Donaldson (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: The running back went down with the injury in the Saints' pre-Week 8 bye loss to the Steelers in Paris back in Week 7. With Travis Etienne (hamstring) still on injured reserve and looking unlikely to play Sunday against the Browns, New Orleans added Audric Estime to a backfield that also includes Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller.

headline: Donaldson (shoulder) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Steelers in Paris, Jeff Nowak of The Big 870 New Orleans reports.
story: Donaldson sustained a shoulder injury during the first quarter of Sunday's game, and the injury is severe enough for him to be sidelined for the rest of the contest. Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller will be the Saints' two remaining running backs the rest of the way in Donaldson's absence.

headline: Donaldson (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Steelers in Paris.
story: Donaldson picked up the injury during the first quarter and has been taken to the locker room to undergo more tests on his shoulder injury. Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller would be the remaining healthy running backs on the Saints active roster for the rest of Sunday's game if Donaldson is not cleared to return.

headline: Donaldson (shoulder) practiced without limitations Thursday.
story: Donaldson upgraded to full participation Thursday while Alvin Kamara (back) was limited for a second consecutive practice. Heading into Sunday's overseas showdown against the Steelers, Donaldson has been working as the Saints' third option in the backfield behind Kamara and Kendre Miller while Travis Etienne (hamstring) is on IR. Donaldson has accumulated 82 scrimmage yards on 16 touches over the past three games.

headline: Donaldson (shoulder) was listed as a limited practice participant Wednesday, Katherine Terrell of ESPN reports.
story: Fellow RB Alvin Kamara (back) also logged a limited session Wednesday, with added context regarding the duo's Week 7 status slated to arrive via Thursday's practice report. In the Saints' 34-27 win over the Giants in Week 6, Donaldson recorded six carries for 39 yards and lost a fumble while working alongside Kamara (seven carries for 34 yards and two catches for 35 yards with a TD) as well as Kendre Miller (20 carries for 70 yards).

headline: Donaldson logged six carries for 39 yards and lost a fumble during the Saints' 34-27 win over the Giants on Sunday. He also recorded three tackles (one solo) on special teams.
story: It appeared as though Donaldson found the end zone on a one-yard carry midway through the third quarter for what would have been the first touchdown of his NFL career. Unfortunately for the undrafted rookie, the call on the field was reversed, so it was quarterback Tyler Shough who snuck in for the touchdown on the next play. Donaldson proceeded to lose a fumble in the fourth quarter -- leading to a Giants touchdown six plays later -- and he didn't log another carry after that. Travis Etienne (hamstring, IR) has been sidelined for each of the Saints' last three games, and during that span, Donaldson has operated as the team's RB3 behind Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller. The Saints will travel to Paris for a Week 7 tilt against the Steelers on Oct. 25.

headline: Donaldson logged three carries for 18 yards and caught both of his targets for five yards during the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday. He also added a tackle on special teams.
story: All of Donaldson's offensive production came on the Saints' final drive of the contest, when the game was already well out of reach. His 28 offensive snaps ended up being tied with Alvin Kamara for most among Saints running backs, with Kendre Miller (19) not far behind. Donaldson was more efficient with his touches than both Kamara and Miller, but for as much as the Saints' run game struggled in the absence of Travis Etienne (hamstring), it's hard to envision Donaldson as the lead back in New Orleans for the foreseeable future. That said, if Donaldson is trusted by head coach Kellen Moore as a backfield blocker on pass protection, then he could operate in an elevated role in Week 5 against the Vikings and their blitz-happy defense under defensive coordinator Brian Flores.

headline: Smyth made two of three field-goal attempts and his lone PAT in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
story: The Saints didn't have a scoring drive until the second quarter, when Smyth made his season-long, 56-yard field goal to cut the lead going into halftime, his first of two 50-plus-yard FGs in the game. The 25-year-old also continued his perfect PAT percentage for the season, making his singular attempt (5-for-5 in three games). His play on kickoffs stood out Sunday, committing two penalties for kicking the ball out of bounds and giving Chicago excellent field position.

headline: The Saints signed Smyth to a two-year contract Saturday, Michael McQuaid of NFL Ireland reports.
story: Smyth has been elevated from the Saints' practice squad for each of the team's last two games following the release of Daniel Carlson on Nov. 3. Smyth has gone 4-for-5 on field-goal attempts and 4-for-4 on extra-point tries in his two appearances, and his new deal means he'll be the Saints' kicker through the 2027 season.

headline: Smyth reverted to the Saints' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: For a second week in a row, Smyth operated as the Saints' kicker during the team's 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday, when he made both of his extra-point tries and connected on a 55-yard field goal late in the fourth quarter. Daniel Carlson was released by New Orleans on Nov. 3, so Smyth likely will be elevated to the active roster for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22.

headline: The Saints elevated Smyth from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday.
story: Smyth is thus set to serve as the Saints' kicker for the second straight week. In his 2026 debut last Sunday against Cleveland, he went 3-for-4 on field-goal attempts and 2-for-2 on point-after tries. If Smyth performs well Sunday, he'll likely be elevated again for Week 11 in Chicago.

headline: The Saints reverted Smyth to their practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: Smyth was elevated ahead of Sunday's Week 9 overtime win over Cleveland. He served as New Orleans' kicker in the contest and went 3-for-4 on FGAs while making both of his PAT attempts. That performance was likely good enough for Smyth to be elevated again for this Sunday's matchup against the Panthers.

headline: Smyth went 3-for-4 on field-goal tries and made both of his extra-point attempts during Sunday's 23-22 overtime win against Cleveland.
story: Smyth was making his regular-season debut after being elevated to the active roster ahead of the team's Week 9 matchup versus the Browns. The kicker converted field-goal attempts from 30, 27 and 48 yards in the victory. Smyth's lone miss of the day came in the first quarter, when he pushed a 48-yard attempt wide right. The 25-year-old will almost certainly be elevated from the practice squad again ahead of the team's Week 10 contest against Carolina.

headline: The Saints elevated Smyth from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday.
story: Smyth is set to take over as New Orleans' kicker beginning with Sunday's matchup against Cleveland, so the elevation was a necessary move. He'll be replacing Daniel Carlson, who was released Tuesday. The Browns have had 19 field-goal tries against them this season, tied for eighth-most in the NFL, so Smyth could be busy in his 2026 debut.

headline: Coach Kellen Moore announced Wednesday that Smyth will be the Saints' kicker in Week 9, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: Smythe will take over for the recently released Daniel Carlson. A native of Northern Ireland, Smythe went 12-for-16 on field goals over six games for the Saints in 2025.

headline: The Saints plan to elevate or sign Smyth off their practice squad to handle kicking duties in Sunday's game against the Browns, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
story: Daniel Carlson handled kicking duties for the Saints through their first seven games, but after he misfired on four field-goal tries and two extra-point attempts, he was released Monday. The Saints will now give Smyth another look, after he had served as their kicker in the final six games of last season before being cut loose following the preseason. Smyth fared well in his first taste of NFL action in 2025, going 12-for-16 on field goals and 13-for-13 on extra points, with two of his misses coming from beyond 50 yards.

headline: Kamara rushed one time for one yard and caught a one-yard touchdown on two targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
story: The veteran running back played just eight of 72 offensive snaps, while both CJ Donaldson and Travis Etienne played 32 each with Audric Estime a healthy inactive. Kamara has touched the ball just seven times on 24 snaps over the past two weeks, but he's turned three of those touches into short touchdowns. The Saints' three-man backfield continues to be one to try and avoid when making fantasy lineup decisions. Kamara's proverbial gas tank is nearing empty, but the Saints continue to give him high-value touches near the goal line while refusing to play him outside of the red zone.

headline: Kamra rushed two times for four yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added three catches for 10 yards and an additional touchdown on four targets.
story: With Travis Etienne back from his weeks-long hamstring injury that saw him miss five games while on injured reserve, the Saints deployed a three-man backfield committee against Carolina. Kamara scored a couple touchdowns, but it was a fluky performance on just five touches and 16 offensive snaps. Audric Estime logged 27 snaps and handled eight touches, while Etienne played 21 snaps and touched the ball 11 times. This is a backfield to avoid in fantasy while it the trio cancels each other out and caps each others' upside.

headline: Kamara (rest/back) was a full practice participant Thursday.
story: Kamara was listed as a non-participant Wednesday due to the combination of rest and back, but his return to all drills one day later gives him the all-clear ahead of Sunday's contest versus the Panthers. He may be welcoming back fellow RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) in Week 10 after the latter was designated for return from IR and so far has managed a pair of limited sessions, while Audric Estime is coming off a 16-touch showing this past Sunday versus the Browns.

headline: Kamara (back) returned to practice Thursday, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: The veteran returned to practice after resting a back injury in Wednesday's session. His participation level has yet to be released but Kamara is trending in the right direction heading into the Week 10 matchup against the Panthers. Another developing situation for the Saints is a potential return for Travis Etienne (hamstring), who practiced Thursday.

headline: Kamara (rest/back) was a non-participant at Wednesday's practice.
story: The Saints backfield is in a bit of flux at the moment, with Kamara and CJ Donaldson (shoulder) logging DNPs on Wednesday and Travis Etienne (hamstring) closing on a return from injured reserve. At the moment, Audric Estime is the healthiest option at the position, and he and Kamara split the RB reps during this past Sunday's win against the Browns, with Kamara earning a 49 percent offensive target share and turning nine touches into 49 yards from scrimmage, while the former logged 47 percent of the snaps and had 16 touches for 77 total yards and one rushing TD. Kamara was listed with rest and a back injury last Wednesday, so his DNP to start the week likely is more of a veteran rest day than anything.

headline: Kamara rushed six times for 32 yards while catching three of four targets for 17 yards during Sunday's 23-22 overtime win against the Browns.
story: Kamara operated as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind Audric Estime (15-72-1) in Week 9. Estime was claimed off waivers from the Browns on Tuesday, and he immediately supplanted Kamara as the team's lead back. Kamara has yet to exceed 40 rushing yards in a game this season, and he has scored just one touchdown over the team's last four contests combined.

headline: Kamara (rest/back) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Browns.
story: Kamara went from DNP due to rest/back Wednesday to limited Thursday and finally full Friday, paving the way for him to be available to the Saints backfield. With fellow RB CJ Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) sidelined this weekend, it'll be Kamara and Kendre Miller to handle the load Sunday.

headline: Kamara (rest/back) was limited at Thursday's practice, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kamara followed up Wednesday's absence from practice with some activity one day later as he eases into the week due to a lingering back issue. Friday's injury report will reveal if he has a designation for Sunday's game against the Browns.

headline: Kamara (rest/back) returned to practice Thursday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: The veteran RB was back on the field Thursday after getting a rest day to open the practice week. Kamara has also dealt with a back issue that limited his practice participation in recent weeks. The Saints are coming off a bye, so the added time off likely bodes well for Kamara being closer to full strength heading into Week 9 against the Browns. New Orleans' practice report will provide insight on Kamara's participation level, but he seems to be trending in the right direction regardless.

headline: Kamara (rest/back) didn't practice Wednesday.
story: The Saints cited rest and a back injury -- the latter of which impacted his practice reps in each of the three games before the team's Week 8 bye -- as the reasons for Kamara's absence to begin Week 9 prep. During that three-contest stretch, he tallied 27 touches for 137 yards from scrimmage and one receiving TD. Kamara will have two more opportunities to practice this week and put himself in a position to avoid a designation for Sunday's contest against the Browns.
