headline: Kamara carried the ball six times for five yards and caught all seven of his targets for 57 yards in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
story: The Saints' ground game was completely shut down, as quarterback Tyler Shough led the team with a mere seven rushing yards, but Kamara still contributed through the air and led New Orleans in catches while tying Barion Brown for the game high in receiving yards. Since missing the season opener, Kamara has put together 258 scrimmage yards and three total TDs (two rushing, one receiving) over six games, but the backfield could get more crowded after a Week 8 bye if Travis Etienne (hamstring) is cleared to return.

headline: Kamara (back) was limited at Friday's practice but does not have an injury designation for Week 7, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kamara did not get a full practice in all week, but it appears that was simply for management purposes, as he will not head into Week 7 with any sort of injury tag. He shared the backfield duties with Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson each of the last three weeks, and with Travis Etienne (hamstring) spending at least one more game on injured reserve, he figures to do the same Sunday in Paris.

headline: Kamara (back) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kamara now has logged back-to-back capped practices to begin Week 7 prep as he deals with a back concern for a third consecutive week. He's been able to play through it, but his snap shares in Week 5 (27 percent) and Week 6 (26 percent) didn't equate to much work (14 touches for 75 yards from scrimmage and one receiving TD). Friday's injury report will unveil whether or not Kamara enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's contest versus the Steelers in Paris.

headline: Kamara (back) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday, Katherine Terrell of ESPN reports.
story: This now marks three weeks in a row in which Kamara has had practice restrictions due to a back issue, but he's been able to play through it the last two games, accounting for 75 yards from scrimmage and one receiving TD on 14 touches during that stretch. The Saints may limit his on-field work Thursday and/or Friday, but there's been no indication he's in danger of missing Sunday's contest against the Steelers in Paris.

headline: Kamara carried the ball seven times for 34 yards and caught two of four targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
story: The veteran RB left the game in the first half due to an undisclosed injury, but he was cleared to return and connected with Tyler Shough for a 31-yard score in the third quarter. Kamara's seven touches were well behind Kendre Miller's 22, but his 69 scrimmage yards were just one shy of Miller's 70 for the team lead. The duo will split backfield duties for at least one more game in Week 7 against the Steelers, before Travis Etienne (hamstring) will be eligible to come off IR after a Week 8 bye.

headline: Kamara (undisclosed) returned to Sunday's contest at the Giants.
story: Kamara missed some time in the first half after attempting to haul in a pass from QB Tyler Shough down the left sideline, but his return indicates he'll attempt to gut through whatever is affecting him. Having said that, the Saints are continuing to employ a timeshare between Kamara, Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson out of the backfield, so Kamara's current outlook isn't exactly fantasy friendly.

headline: Kamara (undisclosed) walked slowly to the medical tent during Sunday's game at the Giants, Matthew Paras of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
story: While attempting to catch a somewhat errant pass down the left sideline, Kamara landed awkwardly and appeared to be shaken up. The current health concern isn't known, but he has been dealing with a back injury the last two weeks, so it may be an aggravation of that issue. Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson are the Saints' current healthy and available running backs.

headline: Kamara (back) is active for Sunday's game at the Giants, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: Kamara has dealt with a back injury the past two weeks, and three limited listings during Week 6 prep led to a questionable designation for Sunday. On Sunday morning, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Kamara is expected to play, which now has been confirmed. Since Travis Etienne (hamstring) landed on IR after Week 3, Kamara has earned 17 touches, while fellow RBs Kendre Miller (18) and CJ Donaldson (10) also have had regular roles, making it difficult to trust any of the trio for fantasy purposes.

headline: Kamara (back), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest at the Giants, is expected to play, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: For a second week in a row, Kamara's practice reps were impacted by a back issue, resulting in limited listings on all three Week 6 injury reports and a questionable designation for Sunday's matchup. His status will be clarified about 90 minutes before a 1 p.m. ET kickoff, but if he's active, Kamara will be part of a timeshare out of the Saints backfield with Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson.

headline: Kamara (back) practiced on a limited basis Friday is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at the Giants, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kamara was limited at practice all week, but he did get some work in each day from Wednesday through Friday and will have a chance to suit up for Week 6. If Kamara does suit up Sunday he figures to split the backfield work in some fashion with Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson.

headline: Kamara (back) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
story: With back-to-back capped sessions under his belt this week due to a lingering back injury, Kamara has one more chance to get back to full Friday, at which point the Saints may tag him with a designation ahead of Sunday's game at the Giants. Even if he's able to suit up this weekend, though, he's been in a tight timeshare with Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson the last two games, turning his 17 touches into 64 yards from scrimmage and two rushing TDs.

headline: Kamara (back) was a limited practice participant Wednesday.
story: For a second straight week, Kamara is dealing with a back injury, but he was able to play through it this past Sunday against the Vikings, earning a 27 percent snap share and turning five touches into six yards from scrimmage. As for the rest of the backfield, Kendre Miller had a 31 percent offensive snap share and 10 touches, while CJ Donaldson paced the group with 42 percent and logged five touches. None of the trio has stood out since Travis Etienne (hamstring) was placed on IR after Week 3, and Kamara's continued health concerns make him even less reliable for fantasy purposes on top of the current timeshare at the position.

headline: Kamara rushed three times for 12 yards and brought in both targets for minus-6 yards in the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Kamara dealt with a back issue during the practice week, and it's possible that helped lead to Kendre Miller outpacing the veteran back by seven carries. Kamara's minimal opportunity unsurprisingly led to a forgettable fantasy day overall, although the entire Saints offense was underwhelming against the vaunted Vikings defense. Given Sunday's division of labor, Kamara could continue losing some touches to Miller while Travis Etienne (hamstring, IR) remains on injured reserve for a Week 6 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

headline: Kamara (back) is listed as active Sunday against the Vikings.
story: Kamara opened Week 5 prep as a non-participant at Wednesday's walkthrough due to a back injury, but he was able to log back-to-back limited practices to end the week and enter the weekend listed as questionable. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network then reported Sunday morning that Kamara was expected to play, which now has been confirmed. Kamara thus should serve as the Saints' lead runner this weekend, a role which so far has amounted to 36 touches for 121 yards from scrimmage and two rushing TDs in three appearances.

headline: Kamara (back) is expected to play in Sunday's contest against the Vikings, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Kamara sat out Week 1 due to a sprained MCL and then proceeded to suit up the last three games before a back issue threatened his availability for Week 5. He followed up a DNP at Wednesday's walkthrough with limited sessions Thursday and Friday before heading into the weekend listed as questionable. Kamara's status will be clarified about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, and if he's active as anticipated, he'll continue to take on a modest workload out of the Saints backfield, which so far has equated to 36 touches for 121 yards from scrimmage and two rushing TDs this season.

headline: Kamara (back) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: Kamara exited last Monday night's game briefly with a knee injury, and he then popped up on this week's injury report with a back issue, getting in limited practices Thursday and Friday. The veteran doesn't need to practice much in order to play, but if Kamara isn't cleared for Sunday, Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson would be next in line for backfield snaps for New Orleans, as Travis Etienne (hamstring) remains on injured reserve for at least three more weeks.

headline: Kamara (back) practiced in a limited fashion Thursday.
story: Kamara was held out of Wednesday's walkthrough due to a back injury, but his upgrade in activity one day later is a decent sign that he's trending in the right direction for Sunday's game against the Vikings. Friday's practice report will unveil whether or not he enters the weekend with a designation.

headline: Kamara (back) did not participate in Wednesday's walkthrough, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: The veteran was not at practice Wednesday after picking up a back injury during the Monday Night Football loss to the Falcons. Kamara has a couple more days to get back on the practice field before his status for Week 5 comes into question, but the back issue will be one to monitor. With Travis Etienne (hamstring) already out, Kendre Miller or CJ Donaldson may be more involved if Kamara is unable to go Sunday against the Vikings.

headline: Kamara rushed seven times for 23 yards and two touchdowns and brought in five of seven targets for 35 yards in the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday night.
story: With Travis Etienne (hamstring, IR) missing his first game of the season, Kamara was back in the familiar lead role he'd filled with great success previously. While Kamara's rushing opportunities ultimately were limited significantly by game script, the veteran back maximized his time on the field by scoring from three and five yards out in the second and fourth quarters, respectively. Kamara could have more of an opportunity for a normal rushing workload -- albeit in a tough matchup -- in a Week 5 home game against the Vikings on Sunday.

headline: Kamara temporarily exited Monday's game against the Falcons due to a knee issue but has since returned.
story: Kamara appeared to hurt his knee in the third quarter and headed to the medical tent. The veteran running back exited the tent, tested out his knee on the sideline, then briefly returned to the tent, but he was able to re-enter the contest before the end of the period. Kamara is serving as New Orleans' lead running back in the absence of Travis Etienne (ankle) and scored his first touchdown of the campaign earlier in Monday's contest.

headline: Kamara figures to serve as the Saints' top running back for as long as Travis Etienne (hamstring) is on injured reserve, starting with Monday's game against the Falcons, John DeShazier of the team's official site reports.
story: Etienne aggravated a hamstring injury during the Saints' Week 3 loss to the Raiders, and the injury is severe enough for him to require a stint on IR. In Etienne's absence, the veteran Kamara figures to take on RB1 duties for New Orleans, a role he carried through the first nine years of his 10-year NFL career. Kendre Miller will see an uptick in backfield snaps behind Kamara, with CJ Donaldson and practice squad members Zamir White and Ulysses Bentley also in the mix for work on offense for as long as Etienne is on the shelf.

headline: Vele caught seven passes for 76 yards on seven targets in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
story: Vele continues to run virtually every route for New Orleans, and the seven grabs matched his season high from Week 1 against the Lions, while Vele's 76 yards are a new high-water mark for the receiver. It was notable that Jordyn Tyson ran just 22 routes on Tyler Shough's 51 dropbacks against Chicago. The Saints offense has become tough to predict on a week-to-week basis. Vele is more of a low-ceiling fantasy WR4/5 most weeks.

headline: Vele caught both of his targets for 14 yards during the Saints' 20-17 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
story: Vele was on the field for 55 of the Saints' 63 offensive snaps, which was second most among wide receivers behind Chris Olave (56). Despite that playing time, Vele saw only two targets Sunday, although no other Saints pass catcher logged more than three receptions other than rookie first-rounder Jordyn Tyson, who finished with 11 catches on 13 targets for 80 yards. Vele has two receptions in each of his last two outings, and it appears his role in the Saints' passing offense has shrunk due to the return of Tyson. Vele will look to bounce back for Week 11 against the Bears on Nov. 22, and Chicago's defense ranks 15th in the NFL in fantasy points allowed to receivers per game.

headline: Vele caught two passes for 17 yards on four targets in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
story: With Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) making his regular-season debut against Cleveland, Vele's role remained steady, running 44 routes on Tyler Slough's 46 dropbacks. Bryce Lance and Noah Fant appeared to be the bigger losers in terms of playing time and routes. Still, Tyson figures to have an effect on Vele's target potential moving forward, as he's setting in as more of a low-floor WR4/5 in fantasy.

headline: Vele caught all five of his targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
story: The third-year wideout was on the other end of Tyler Shough's only TD pass of the day, hauling in a one-yard toss in the second quarter for the Saints' final points. Vele tied his career high with his third touchdown of the season, and his 33-348-3 line on 48 targets through seven games has him tracking toward a career-best campaign heading into a Week 8 bye. His role could shrink significantly after the bye, however, if rookie Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is cleared to make his NFL debut.

headline: Vele caught three of six targets for 42 yards during the Saints' 34-27 win over the Giants on Sunday.
story: Vele was on the field for 66 of the Saints' 70 offensive snaps (94.3 percent), which was well ahead of fellow wideouts Chris Olave (42) and rookie Bryce Lance (36). Vele has seen at least six targets in each of the first six games of the regular season, and his 28-294-2 line on 43 targets already surpasses his totals across 13 regular-season games in 2025 (25-293-2 on 40 targets). Given his snap count, it wouldn't be surprising if Vele maintains his role in the offense even if Jordyn Tyson (hamstring, IR) returns, which could come as soon as Week 7 against the Steelers on Oct. 25 in Paris.

headline: Vele secured four of six targets for 26 yards in the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Vele finished in a three-way tie with Chris Olave and Juwan Johnson for the team lead in receptions and also drew even with Olave for top slotting in targets. However, that meant little on a day when Tyler Shough was held to 3.8 yards per attempt by an aggressive Vikings defense and finished with just 96 passing yards overall. Vele's quiet afternoon notwithstanding, the third-year wideout has now seen at least six targets in each game and has impressively converted 14 of his 25 receptions into first downs. Vele will take a 25-252-2 line on 37 targets into a Week 6 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

headline: Vele secured six of nine targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday night.
story: Vele tied for second in receptions and checked in as the runner-up in targets for the Saints on the night, and he rounded out a solid fantasy performance by recording a three-yard touchdown reception with 1:13 remaining. The score was ultimately meaningless to the outcome of the lopsided loss, but Vele further cemented his standing as a relatively high-volume No. 2 receiver by tying his season high in targets. Vele will take a 21-226-2 line on 31 targets into a Week 5 home matchup against the Vikings on Sunday.

headline: Vele caught three of six targets for 39 yards Sunday in a loss to Las Vegas.
story: Tyler Shough had another big day at quarterback for the Saints, with 160 of his 255 passing yards going to the combination of No. 1 wideout Chris Olave and top tight end Juwan Johnson. Vele finished third behind that duo in both targets (six) and receiving yards (39). The third-year wideout has been locked into a key role in the Saints' passing game, and through three contests he's registered 15 catches on 22 targets for 172 yards and one touchdown.

headline: Why Field Yates is banking on Jordyn Tyson to bounce back
story: Why Field Yates is banking on Jordyn Tyson to bounce back

headline: Tyson caught one of two targets for six yards and added four rushing yards on his only carry in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
story: One week after logging 13 targets as Tyler Shough's top downfield option, Tyson all but disappeared as Chris Olave instead saw WR1-worthy volume. The Saints' aerial attack simply may not be able to support both wideouts in the same game, which would mark Tyson as a volatile, but high-ceiling, fantasy asset for the rest of the season. The rookie will try to bounce back in Week 12 against the Bengals.

headline: Tyson (chest) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Chicago.
story: Tyson opened Week 11 prep with back-to-back limited sessions due to a chest injury, but his return to a full practice Friday has him in the clear for Sunday's matchup. He'll look to build upon the 11-80-0 line on 13 targets the he compiled against the Panthers in Week 10.

headline: Tyson (chest) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
story: Tyson maintained his activity level from Wednesday as he tends to a chest injury in the wake of his 11-80-0 line on 13 targets from the second game of his career this past Sunday versus the Panthers. Friday's practice report will determine if he has a designation ahead of Sunday's contest at Chicago.

headline: Tyson (chest) took part in the media-access portion of Thursday's practice, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: Tyson was limited at Wednesday's session due to a chest injury, and he at least is maintaining that activity level one day later. Thursday's practice report will reveal if he again was limited or upgraded to full. In the second game of his career this past Sunday against the Panthers, Tyson gathered in 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards.

headline: Head coach Kellen Moore said Tyson was limited at Wednesday's practice due to a chest injury, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: Tyson missed the first seven games of the campaign due to a hamstring issue, but he increased his sway in the Saints offense from Week 9 to 10, upping his snap share (24 to 71 percent) and target count (five to 13). In this past Sunday's loss to the Panthers, he recorded an 11-80-0 line, but he emerged from that contest with a new health concern. As a result, Tyson's status will be monitored in advance of Sunday's contest at Chicago.

headline: Tyson caught 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
story: That bang you just heard was the sound of the window closing on your chances of acquiring Tyson cheaply in your fantasy league. In just his second career NFL game, Tyson dominated looks from Tyler Shough, as no other New Orleans pass catcher handled more than five targets, hauled in more than three passes or topped 30 receiving yards. It may be tough for the team's struggling offense to keep both Tyson and Chris Olave busy at the same time, so the duo may end up trading big games rather than opening things up for each other, but this kind of volume can't be ignored. Tyson will look for his first career touchdown in a Week 11 tilt against the Bears.

headline: Tyson was working with the Saints' first-team offense pregame ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Panthers, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: In his pro debut last Sunday against the Browns, Tyson ranked fourth in snap share (24 percent) among his position mates behind Devaughn Vele (93), Chris Olave (85) and Bryce Lance (51). Tyson still hauled in four of five targets for 30 yards, and head coach Kellen Moore told Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio on Wednesday that the rookie WR should receive "a healthy dose more" of work in his second NFL outing. Considering Tyson has swapped in for Lance with the first-teamers, the former is poised to do just that this Sunday.

headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that Tyson should get "a healthy dose more" of snaps in Sunday's game against the Panthers, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
story: Tyson played just 18 snaps and lost a fumble on his first catch this past Sunday against the Browns, but there were some positives from his regular-season debut, including a strong target rate (five targets on 16 routes). While there's no assurance of a full-time role, Tyson at least figures to take more snaps away from fellow rookie Bryce Lance, if not from veteran Devaughn Vele.

headline: Tyson caught four of five targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns. He also lost a fumble.
story: It wasn't the most dynamic performance from the eighth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, but it was just good to see Tyson on the field after he missed the first seven games of the season due to hamstring trouble, even if his longest gain went for just nine yards. Tyson's role in the offense figures to grow quickly if he can stay healthy, and he has the talent to put together a productive second half as the No. 2 option behind Chris Olave for quarterback Tyler Shough.

headline: Tyson isn't working with the Saints' first-team offense pregame ahead of Sunday's contest against the Browns, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
story: Tyson is active Sunday for the first time in his career, but the rookie first-round pick is getting reps before kickoff behind the WR trio of Chris Olave, Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance. The Saints offense regularly has operated with three wide receivers this season, but it appears Tyson will be mixing in as a reserve rather than taking on a starter-level role in his NFL debut.

headline: Tyson (hamstring) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Browns, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
story: Tyson, the eighth overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, injured his hamstring in August, but now those who held onto to the highly-touted rookie during his absence a" or recently added him to their roster a" will going forward have a player with a high ceiling to consider for fantasy lineups. Given the long layoff, the Saints could choose to proceed deliberately with Tyson in his NFL regular-season debut, but as the season rolls along, the Arizona State product should yield dividends working alongside top pass-catcher Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele, who's been slotting in as the team's WR2 in Tyson's absence.

headline: Tyson (hamstring) was activated from injured reserve Saturday, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns.
story: Tyson thus is one step closer to making his NFL debut after missing the first eight weeks of the campaign due to hamstring issues that have bothered him since the start of training camp. With a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff on tap Sunday, his status will be clarified, one way or another, about 90 minutes before that point.

headline: Tyson (hamstring) intends to make his NFL debut Sunday against the Browns, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports.
story: The Saints opened Tyson's 21-day window in which to practice and potentially return from injured reserve Wednesday, and he managed three consecutive limited listings before getting a questionable tag for Week 9 action. The team still needs to officially activate Tyson from IR by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday in order for him to have a chance to play Sunday, but that appears as if it'll come to pass.

headline: Tyson (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: With Tyson having logged limited practices after the Saints opened his 21-day window to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Friday's designation gives the rookie a chance to make his long-awaited regular-season NFL debut. There's been no indication one way or the other on what the Saints' plans are for Tyson this week. Devaughn Vele and Bryce Lance would be the biggest losers in terms of playing time and targets once Tyson does debut.

headline: Tyson (hamstring) remained a limited participant at Thursday's practice, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: Tyson has logged consecutive limited practices since having his 21-day window to return from IR opened Wednesday. The rookie first-round pick could make his NFL regular-season debut as soon as Sunday against the Browns, though the Saints may want him to log at least one full practice before seeing game action. For his part, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football suggested that from his point of view Tyson didn't look limited Thursday. In any case, the wideout's return to action, be it this week or next, would be proceeded by an official move adding him to the 53-man roster.

headline: Tyson (hamstring) had his 21-day practice window opened and was a limited participant in Wednesday's session.
story: The rookie first-round pick hadn't practiced since Aug. 13 due to a right hamstring strain, but he's closing in on making his NFL debut now that he's officially had his 21-day window opened. Given that he's beginning Week 9 prep with a limited practice following a lengthy layoff, Tyson may not be in play to be activated for this Sunday's game against the Browns. The Saints will see how Tyson looks in practice the next two days before deciding on his availability for the Week 9 game.

headline: Tyson (hamstring) is slated to resume practicing with the Saints on Wednesday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: The Saints are expected to officially open the wide receiver's 21-day evaluation window as they kick off Week 9 prep ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns. Given that the strained right hamstring has kept him off the field since Aug. 13, Tyson may need more than one week of practices to get himself back into playing shape, but the Saints haven't necessarily ruled the rookie first-round pick out from making his NFL debut against Cleveland. Whenever he's deemed ready to play, Tyson could immediately push Devaughn Vele for the Saints' No. 2 receiver job.

headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said that the Saints will decide by Wednesday whether to open Tyson's (hamstring) 21-day practice window this week, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: Adam Schefter of ESPN reported over the weekend that Tyson could have a chance at making his NFL debut as soon as this coming Sunday against the Browns, but until the Saints formally clear the wideout to practice, a target date for him to play will remain somewhat muddled. The No. 8 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Tyson had a checkered medical history during his collegiate career, and the right hamstring strain he sustained in mid-August has only added to the long-term concerns about his durability. However, the 6-foot-2, 203-pound Tyson is undoubtedly talented, and he'll have a fairly clear path to the No. 2 receiver gig if he can get healthy.

headline: Tyson (hamstring) could be reinstated from injured reserve and make his season debut as soon as next Sunday versus the Browns, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: The Saints haven't cleared Tyson to practice since he strained his right hamstring during an Aug. 13 training camp workout, but the rookie first-round pick sounds like he could have his 21-day evaluation window opened in Week 9. Due to the length of his absence, Tyson may not be ready to play against Cleveland even if he checks out well in practice during the upcoming week, but in any case, he doesn't appear far away from making his NFL debut. Whenever he's activated, Tyson could push Devaughn Vele for the No. 2 receiver role behind top target Chris Olave.

headline: Saints general manager Mickey Loomis said Tuesday that Tyson (hamstring) is "getting closer" but won't practice this week, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
story: Tyson made the trip to Paris ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Steelers, but he's not ready to have his 21-day practice window opened just yet. While the Saints haven't provided many specifics regarding where Tyson stands in his recovery from a right hamstring strain beyond noting that he's "improving," the team has a bye coming Week 8, so rookie wideout will be afforded more time to get closer to 100 percent before potentially getting back on the field. If Tyson is able to resume practicing coming out of the bye week, he could be a candidate to make his NFL debut as soon as Nov. 8, when the Saints host the Browns.

headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said that Tyson (hamstring) traveled to Paris in advance of Sunday's game against the Steelers, NewOrleans.football reports.
story: Tyson has been sidelined since mid-August due to a right hamstring strain, but the Saints' decision to include him in their travel party to France could be a sign that his 21-day practice window will be opened this week. While Tyson would have a chance at making his NFL debut against the Steelers if he practices this week, the Saints may prefer to hold him out through their Week 8 bye to give him additional time to heal. Whenever he makes his way back from injured reserve, the No. 8 overall pick in the draft could immediately push Devaughn Vele for the No. 2 spot on the depth chart at receiver behind Chris Olave.

headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that Tyson (hamstring) is "progressing well" but isn't on track to return to practice this week, Jeff Nowak of WWL New Orleans reports.
story: Tyson has resided on injured reserve all season after sustaining a right hamstring strain during an Aug. 13 training camp practice. Though the rookie first-round pick hasn't hit any reported snags in his recovery, the Saints aren't yet ready to open his 21-day practice window. Adam Schefter of ESPN previously reported that Tyson wouldn't make his NFL debut until Week 7, but because the young wideout hasn't resumed practicing yet, a return to game action following the Saints' Week 8 bye is probably more realistic at this point.

headline: Tyson (hamstring) is said to be making progress and feeling good but isn't expected to be activated from injured reserve until Week 7 at the soonest, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: New Orleans placed Tyson on IR with a designation to return back on Aug. 30, making him eligible to resume practicing with the team as soon as Week 3 and playing in Week 5. Saints head coach Kellen Moore previously disclosed Thursday that Tyson wasn't on track to practice during the upcoming week, and Schefter's report further fuels the notion that the team will take a deliberate approach with the rookie first-round draft pick, who is on the mend from a right hamstring strain and had a history of soft-tissue injuries during his time in college. Though a Week 7 return is on the table, the Saints will go on bye in Week 8, which could make a Week 9 home matchup with the Browns a more likely target for Tyson's NFL debut.

headline: Head coach Kellen Moore said Thursday that he doesn't expect Tyson (hamstring) to practice next week, Matthew Paras of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports.
story: At the time his most recent hamstring injury flared up in mid-August, Tyson was given a prognosis of roughly two months, which he's still in the midst of. As a player on injured reserve, his practice window can be opened next week, but that doesn't appear to be a consideration for the Saints at this time. It remains to be seen when the eighth overall pick in the 2026 Draft will be able to make his pro debut.

headline: Etienne carried the ball 14 times for 76 yards and failed to catch his only target in Sunday's 21-13 loss to Chicago.
story: The former Jaguar was the clear No. 1 option in the backfield for the Saints. Alvin Kamara saw just two touches and CJ Donaldson handled five, although Kamara did vulture another red-zone TD on a one-yard reception in the second quarter, Most of Etienne's production came on a 46-yard scamper that saw him tackled just short of the goal line, setting up Kamara's score, but the fact that he was able to produce his first big play as a Saint was still encouraging. Etienne will attempt to build on this performance in Week 12 against the Bengals.

headline: Etienne carried the ball eight times for 14 yards and caught three of five targets for 20 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
story: Seeing his first action since Week 3 after recovering from a hamstring strain, the former Jaguar led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, ahead of Audric Estime's eight and Alvin Kamara's five. Etienne wasn't able to do much with the volume, however, while Kamara scored two short TDs. Etienne still appears to be the top option for the team at RB, but if Estime keeps taking short-yardage work and Kamara is the preferred red-zone back, it would put a real ceiling on Etienne's upside. He'll look to claim a bigger share of the workload in Week 11 against the Bears.

headline: Etienne (hamstring) is active for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: Etienne will play for the first time since Week 3, after the Saints activated him from injured reserve Saturday following a pair of limited practices and one full session this past week. Though his workload could be managed to some degree in his return to the lineup, Etienne will likely step back into a lead role in a New Orleans running game that has struggled throughout the season. The Saints are averaging just 3.8 yards per carry through eight games, with Etienne propping up that mark by carrying 30 times for 128 yards (4.3 average) prior to getting hurt.

headline: The Saints activated Etienne (hamstring) from injured reserve Saturday, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: Etienne thus is poised for his first game action since Week 3, when he strained his left hamstring. His status will be confirmed about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, but assuming he's active, he'll join a backfield currently occupied by Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime.

headline: The Saints are expected to activate Etienne (hamstring) from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's NFC South tilt against the Panthers, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
story: Etienne's 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, and he strung together consecutive limited sessions before practicing in full Friday. That was enough for him to draw the questionable tag for Sunday's game, and it appears the Saints are confident enough in Etienne's recovery to activate the veteran running back from IR. His return would be a welcome one for a New Orleans offense that ranks 26th in the NFL in rushing yards per game (95.3). Etienne's return would result in Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime reverting to rotational roles out of the backfield.

headline: Etienne (hamstring) said Friday that "the week of practice went well," and that he hopes to be active for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Jeff Nowak of WWL Radio reports.
story: Etienne remains on injured reserve and officially is listed as questionable for Week 10, per Ross Jackson of WWL-TV. After the Saints designated Etienne for return from IR on Wednesday, he opened the week with back-to-back limited sessions before logging a full practice Friday, but the team still will need to activate him by Saturday afternoon for him to have a chance to play Sunday. With CJ Donaldson (shoulder) ruled out, Alvin Kamara and Audric Estime will be the other RBs to vie with for touches if Etienne is able to suit up this weekend.

headline: Etienne (hamstring) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Ross Jackson of WWL-TV reports.
story: The Saints designated Etienne for return from injured reserve Wednesday, and he so far has logged back-to-back limited practices during Week 10 prep. He'll have one more opportunity Friday to put himself in a position for his first game action since Week 3, when he suffered a strained left hamstring.

headline: Head coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that the Saints will wait until the end of the week to make a decision whether or not to activate Etienne from injured reserve, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: Considering Etienne went down as a limited practice participant Wednesday, the Saints have officially designated him for return from injured reserve, where he's resided since his last appearance in Week 3 when he suffered a left hamstring strain. He's missed the last five games as a result, but for him to have a chance to play Sunday against the Panthers, the team will need to activate him from IR by Saturday afternoon.

headline: Etienne (hamstring) was back at practice Wednesday, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
story: Etienne's return to practice suggests a return from injured reserve isn't far off. He'd have to be activated by 4:00 p.m. ET on Saturday to play in Sunday's game against the Panthers.

headline: Head coach Kellen Moore said Monday that the Saints haven't yet determined whether Etienne (hamstring) will return from injured reserve ahead of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Luke Johnson of The New Orleans Times-Picayune reports. "We'll see," Moore said. "He's progressing well. We'll gather some more information and make a decision."
story: Moore noted that the Saints are still in the process of "using the time allotted" to let Etienne work out with the training staff before designating him for return from injured reserve and opening his 21-day practice window. Though the 27-year-old back hasn't played since the Saints' Week 3 loss to the Raiders, he's still just 34 yards behind quarterback Tyler Shough for the team lead in rushing yardage (162). Whether he's activated for Week 10 or at some point thereafter, Etienne's eventual return will provide a boost to a New Orleans running game that has struggled mightily through the midway point of the season.

headline: Head coach Kellen Moore said Wednesday that the Saints haven't opened Etienne's (hamstring) practice window just yet, Jeff Nowak of WWL Louisiana reports.
story: Etienne has missed the required four games on IR due to a strained left hamstring, but even with the benefit of a Week 8 bye, he hasn't gained clearance to mix into drills. Moore told Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana on Monday that Etienne has a chance to return to practice this week, but with no on-field work to begin Week 9 prep, he seems to be on the outside looking in to have enough time to be activated for Sunday's contest against the Browns.

headline: Head coach Kellen Moore said that Etienne (hamstring) will be evaluated Monday before the Saints make a determination whether he practices this week, Ross Jackson of WWL Louisiana reports.
story: Sidelined since he sustained a left hamstring strain in a Sept. 27 loss to the Raiders, Etienne will be eligible to play coming out of the Saints' Week 8 bye now that he's missed the required four games while on injured reserve. If Etienne looks good during his upcoming evaluation, he could have his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, when the Saints will begin prepping for Sunday's game against the Browns. Given the time that he's missed, Etienne might need to practice fully at some point this week for the Saints to feel comfortable activating him after a minimum-length stint on IR.

headline: The Saints are placing Etienne (hamstring) on injured reserve, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: Etienne dealt with a hamstring injury during Week 3 prep and then aggravated the issue this past Sunday against the Raiders, leading to head coach Kellen Moore telling Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football on Monday that the running back was expected to miss some time. With his placement on IR, Etienne will sit out at least the next four games, meaning his next chance for game action is Sunday, Nov. 8 versus the Browns. In the meantime, Alvin Kamara figures to take on the lead role in the Saints backfield, but Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson also are on hand for RB reps.

headline: Shough completed 25 of 42 passes for 222 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears. He added 34 rushing yards on three carries.
story: Despite the high volume of attempts, Shough couldn't get much going through the air while dealing with a ferocious Chicago pass rush that sacked him six times, including one for a fourth-quarter safety by Montez Sweat. Shough has gone four straight games without producing multiple TDs, posting a 4:3 TD:INT over that stretch while completing 67.3 percent of his passes with a weak 6.3 YPA. The second-year QB will likely need to be a lot more productive in Week 12 if the Saints are going to keep up with Joe Burrow and the Bengals.

headline: Shough is no longer wearing a protect glove on his left (non-throwing) hand at Thursday's practice, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: The second-year quarterback suffered two broken bones in his left hand back on Oct. 5 and has been playing with the glove ever since. He's also been able to only hand the ball off with his right hand since suffering the injury. Shough has completed 66.8 percent of his passes for 2,173 yards, 15 touchdowns and seven interceptions across nine starts this season. He's averaging one full yard less per pass attempt (6.3) and 1.3 fewer yards per completion (9.5) compared to his 2025 rookie season.

headline: Shough completed 25 of 35 targets for 187 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers. He added 25 rushing yards on six carries and was charged with a lost fumble.
story: The second-year QB had more turnovers than TDs for only the second time this season, although his fumble may have been been more Audric Estime's fault, and Shough fell short of 200 passing yards for the third time. Rookie Jordyn Tyson was his top downfield option, catching 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards in a breakout performance, but no other Saint saw more than five targets or hauled in more than three passes. Shough will take a 15:7 TD:INT into a Week 11 clash with the Bears.

headline: Shough completed 21 of 35 passes for 265 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns.
story: New Orleans got by with three Charlie Smyth field goals and an Audric Estime two-yard TD run in regulation, but Shough connected with Juwan Johnson for a 15-yard touchdown in OT that held up as the winning score when the Browns scored on the subsequent possession but failed on a two-point attempt -- the same way the Saints lost to the Lions in their season opener. Shough will take a 14:6 TD:INT through eight games into a Week 10 clash with the Panthers.

headline: Shough was still wearing a glove on his left hand during pregame warmups ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns, according to Luke Johnson of The New Orleans Times-Picayune.
story: As Johnson notes, Shough wasn't listed on the Saints' Week 9 injury report, as he was (as a full participant) in Week 7, prior to the team's bye. With no reported reported setbacks, Shough -- who sustained two broken bones in his left (non-throwing) hand Oct. 5 -- is presumably simply protecting his hand until it's 100 percent healed. On the plus side from the QB's perspective as he continues to play through the issue is the fact highly-touted rookie WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) -- the eighth overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft -- is making his much-awaited regular-season debut for New Orleans.

headline: Shough completed 30 of 38 passes for 278 yards and one touchdown with one interception in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers. He added seven rushing yards on three carries.
story: With the Saints' ground game getting absolutely nowhere -- Shough actually led the team in rushing yards -- the second-year QB had to air it out frequently once again, but the volume didn't result in much production. Shough will head into a Week 8 bye averaging 39 pass attempts a game -- the fourth-highest mark in the league behind Matthew Stafford, Dak Prescott and Bryce Young -- to go along with a 13:6 TD:INT and 1,721 passing yards.

headline: Shough completed 16 of 30 passes for 144 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants. He added 32 yards and a TD on five carries.
story: While he didn't produce much yardage, Shough kept the Saints' offense humming, connecting with Bryce Lance, Alvin Kamara and Chris Olave for scores through the air while adding a one-yard touchdown on the ground in the third quarter. Shough has been playing through a couple broken bones in his non-throwing hand, which could help explain why he has just 242 passing yards over the last two weeks, but the second-year QB showed he can be plenty productive despite the injury. Shough will take a 12:5 TD:INT through six games into a Week 7 tilt against the Steelers in Paris.

headline: Shough has been playing with two broken bones in his left hand, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Shough has been listed with a left hand injury the past two weeks, but the extent wasn't known until Schefter's report Sunday morning. He had his least productive performance of the season last Sunday versus the Vikings' ferocious defense, when he completed 16 of 25 passes for just 96 yards, no touchdowns and two interceptions. Shough will aim to get back on track in Week 6 against a banged-up Giants defensive unit.

headline: Shough completed 16 of 25 passes for 96 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions in the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Shough's final line underscores the duress he was under throughout the afternoon from an aggressive Vikings defense, even as he took just one sack. Shough nevertheless was intent on getting ball out quickly, leading to him averaging just 3.8 yards per attempt. The second-year quarterback's pair of interceptions didn't lead to any Minnesota points, but they did saddle Shough with his first multi-INT tally since Week 1. Despite Sunday's stumble, Shough and the rest of his teammates on the offensive side of the ball will have a good opportunity to bounce back in a favorable Week 6 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

headline: Shough (left hand) practiced fully Friday and doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Emily Leiker of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports.
story: Shough opened the week with a limited walkthrough Wednesday due to a left hand injury, but he didn't endure any restrictions Thursday and Friday and thus is good to go for Week 5. He currently ranks third in the NFL in passing yards per game with 300.8, which he's supplemented with a 9:3 TD:INT through four contests.

headline: Shough (left hand) practiced in full Thursday.
story: Shough was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough due to an injury to hie left, non-throwing hand, but it didn't impede him whatsoever one day later, indicating he's in the clear for Week 5 action. Through four games this season, he's taken advantage of a pass-heavy offense, completing 121 of 180 throws for 1,203 yards, nine touchdowns and three interceptions.

headline: Shough was limited with a non-throwing hand injury Wednesday, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: Shough had his left hand wrapped during Wednesday's walkthrough, but the team is not overly concerned, according to Triplett. It was a physical game Monday night as the Falcons registered 12 quarterback hits on Shough. As it stands, Shough's status is not in jeopardy for Sunday's game against the Vikings.

headline: Shough completed 30 of 48 passes for 286 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions and rushed twice for five yards in the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday night.
story: Shough's final line was perfectly acceptable from a fantasy standpoint, but Monday night was a case of the numbers being much more aesthetically pleasing than the on-field results. He piled up a significant part of his production in the second half -- including a three-yard touchdown pass to Devaughn Vele with 1:13 remaining -- after the Saints already faced a sizable deficit, as he led a couple of 13-play drives in the fourth quarter when New Orleans was down by 21 and 28 points, respectively. Nevertheless, Shough generated his second interception-free performance of the last three games, and he's up to 1,203 passing yards and a 9:3 TD:INT along with 72 rushing yards and another score heading into a Week 5 home matchup against an aggressive Vikings defense on Sunday.

headline: Olave caught nine of 15 targets for 102 yards in Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Bears.
story: One week after taking a back seat to rookie Jordyn Tyson, Olave re-emerged as Tyler Shough's favorite downfield option, as he set a new season high in targets and topped 100 receiving yards for the fourth time in 2026. Tyson, meanwhile, caught only one pass on two targets, suggesting the Saints' aerial attack may not be able to support both wideouts in the same game. Olave will look to make an impact again in Week 12 against the Bengals.

headline: Olave caught three of four targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to the Panthers.
story: The game wound up being Jordyn Tyson's breakout performance, as the rookie WR hauled in 11 of 13 targets for 80 yards, but that didn't leave much volume for Olave or any other Saint. With Tyler Shough struggling, it's unclear whether the passing game can keep more than one pass catcher fantasy-relevant at a time. Olave sports a 59-774-2 line on 87 targets through nine games, and he'll look to bounce back in a Week 11 tilt against the Bears.

headline: Olave caught seven of 12 targets for 98 yards in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over Cleveland.
story: The fifth-year wideout led the Saints in catches, targets and receiving yards once again, but Juwan Johnson was on the other end of Tyler Shough's only TD of the day. Olave is the clear top option in the New Orleans passing attack, but with Jordyn Tyson finally making his pro debut Sunday, secondaries may have someone else to worry about in the second half of the season. Olave will take a 56-734-2 line on 83 targets into a Week 10 battle against the Panthers.

headline: Olave caught six of 10 targets for 56 yards in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers.
story: While Olave saw a team-high 10 targets, Alvin Kamara caught one more pass and gained one more receiving yard for the team leads in those categories, while Devaughn Vele caught Tyler Shough's only TD. Olave has failed to reach 60 yards in three straight games after topping 100 in three of his first four contests this season, but he'll get a bye week to reset before facing the Browns in Week 9.

headline: Olave caught four of seven targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-27 win over the Giants.
story: While he didn't see his usual volume on an afternoon in which Tyler Shough threw for only 144 yards, Olave was on the other end of one of the QB's three scores, hauling in an 18-yard TD early in the fourth quarter that proved to be crucial after the Giants staged a late, but unsuccessful, rally. Olave got double-digit targets in each of the first four games of the season, but over the last two contests he's been targeted just 13 times, posting an 8-89-1 line. He'll look to regain some steam in Paris for a Week 7 matchup against the Steelers.

headline: Olave (illness) is listed as active Sunday at the Giants, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: An illness afflicted Olave during the entirety of Week 6 prep, holding him to one limited practice Friday, but Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Sunday morning that the wide receiver is expected to suit up. Indeed, that has come to pass, and Olave will continue to operate as the unquestioned top target for QB Tyler Shough, who currently ranks second in the NFL this season with 205 pass attempts.

headline: Olave (illness), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at the Giants, is expected to suit up, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Olave was contained to just one limited session (Friday) during Week 6 prep as he dealt with an illness, but it won't stop him from being available Sunday. His status will be confirmed about 90 minutes before a 1 p.m. ET kickoff, but assuming he's active, he'll be looking to build upon the 39-537-1 line on 54 targets that he's accrued through the first five contests of the campaign.

headline: Olave (illness) was limited at Friday's practice and will be listed as questionable for Week 6.
story: An illness cost Olave the first two practices of the week, but he was able to take the field Friday and get some work in. He isn't in the clear for Sunday's matchup with the Giants just yet, but his participation alone Friday suggests it's more likely than not that he'll be available.

headline: Olave (illness) didn't take part in Thursday's practice, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: With no practice so far this week for Olave due to an illness, he has just one more chance to mix into drills Friday, or else he'll be at risk of heading into the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at the Giants. Through five contests this season, he has three 100-yard efforts to his name en route to cumulative 39-537-1 line on 54 targets.

headline: Olave didn't practice Wednesday due to an illness, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: Olave is coming off a season-worst 4-46-0 line on six targets in this past Sunday's loss to the Vikings, but a stout defense and not a health concern was to blame. As Week 6 prep kicks off, his absence on a Wednesday with an illness isn't as worrisome as it would be if it occurred not long before game day, and he has two more chances to practice Thursday and Friday to prove his health ahead of Sunday's contest at the Giants.

headline: Olave secured four of six targets for 46 yards in the Saints' 23-13 loss to the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Olave found himself in the familiar position of either tying for the team lead or setting the pace for the Saints in receptions, receiving yards and targets, but the numbers he generated in each of those categories left plenty to be desired. His sub-standard production should be taken in context, however, considering Tyler Shough threw for only 96 yards at 3.8 yards per attempt and was picked off twice as well. Olave's numbers were easily season lows across the board, but he should have a good chance to bounce back in a Week 6 road matchup against the Giants next Sunday.

headline: Olave (foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Vikings, Mike Triplett of NewOrleans.Football reports.
story: After being limited Thursday due to a foot issue, Olave's full participation Friday clears up his status for Week 5. The NFL's leader in targets (48) has a tough test against Minnesota's aggressive defense, but the Saints can't run the ball and have been forced to dial up the pass at a high clip through four games. Olave is a lock-and-load WR1 every week.

headline: Olave (rest/foot) appeared to be moving well during the part of Friday's practice open to the media, Jeff Nowak of WWL New Orleans reports.
story: After being rested for Wednesday's walkthrough, Olave was limited at Thursday's session due to a foot injury. His status for Sunday's game against the Vikings may receive some clarity once the Saints post their final Week 5 practice report Friday.

headline: Olave (rest/foot) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
story: The Saints held a walkthrough Wednesday, during which Olave logged a rest day. As of Thursday, he mixed back into drills, but a foot injury was added to the practice report after his capped session. His ability to handle some reps while dealing with a health concern generally is a good sign that his status isn't in question for Week 5, but Friday's injury report will reveal whether or not he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's contest versus the Vikings.

headline: Olave was present and involved throughout Thursday's practice, Ross Jackson of LouisianaSports.net reports.
story: Olave rested Wednesday after catching eight of 12 targets for 116 yards in Monday's loss to the Falcons. The star wide receiver returned to practice Thursday, assuaging any lingering concerns about his health. Olave will look to add to his season totals of 35 catches for 491 yards and one touchdown Sunday against the Vikings.

headline: Olave had a rest day at Wednesday's practice, Katherine Terrell of ESPN.com reports.
story: The Saints had a walkthrough Wednesday after having played Monday night against the Falcons. Olave was given a rest day, and according to Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football, it was unrelated to a hard shot he took during the loss to the Falcons. Olave does not appear to be dealing with an injury, and he should return to practice later in the week.

headline: Olave secured eight of 12 targets for 116 yards in the Saints' 45-24 loss to the Falcons on Monday night.
story: Olave was in the customary position of leading the Saints in receptions, receiving yards and targets, putting together his third 100-yard effort, including his second straight, of 2026. He also extended his season-opening streak of games with double-digit targets to four, and although Jeff Nowak of WWLAM-FM reports the talented receiver took a hit to the knee on New Orleans' final drive and went to the sideline, he never entered the medical tent. Assuming Olave is no worse for wear, he'll once again be slated for a prominent role in a Week 5 home matchup against the Vikings on Sunday.

headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Bears on Sunday.
story: As the emergency QB3, Wilson is not allowed to play Sunday unless starter Tyler Shough and backup Spencer Rattler both leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection. Wilson has yet to appear in a regular-season game in 2026.

headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Panthers on Sunday.
story: Wilson is the No. 3 quarterback behind Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler. The inactive third option will only enter Sunday's game if Shough and Rattler must leave the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Browns on Sunday.
story: The former Jet remains the odd-quarterback out for the Saints. Wilson will not be allowed to play in Sunday's contest unless both Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback against the Giants on Sunday.
story: As the emergency third quarterback, Wilson is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Vikings as the Saints' emergency third quarterback.
story: Wilson remains the No. 3 QB behind Tyler Shough and Spencer Rattler. Wilson can be called upon to enter the contest only if both active quarterbacks are forced out of the game.

headline: Wilson (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Saints' emergency third quarterback for Monday night's contest against the Falcons.
story: Wilson will operate as the team's No. 3 QB for the fourth game in a row to begin the 2026 campaign. Wilson will only be eligible to enter the contest if both starter Tyler Shough and top backup Spencer Rattler are forced out of the game.

headline: Estime (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bears.
story: Estime's role in the offense was reduced in Week 10 against the Panthers, which marked Travis Etienne's return from a five-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Estime is a healthy scratch for Sunday's game, which means Alvin Kamara and CJ Donaldson will operate as the rotational options out of the backfield behind Etienne. Estime's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Bengals on Nov. 29.

headline: Estime carried the ball seven times for six yards and caught his only target for five yards in Sunday's 20-17 loss to Carolina.
story: Travis Etienne returned from IR and led the Saints' backfield with 11 touches, although he managed just 34 scrimmage yards, while Alvin Kamara handled five touches and scored two short TDs. Perhaps worse for Estime's role and future value, he was ineffective in short-yardage situations, getting stuffed on three attempts to pick up a first down from two yards out or less, and a miscommunication with Tyler Shough on a handoff led to a lost fumble in the second quarter, although the giveaway was charged to the QB. Estime will try to maintain some share of the workload in a Week 11 meeting with the Bears.

headline: Estime's role in the backfield will likely be diminished after Travis Etienne (hamstring) was cleared to return for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: Estime -- who the Saints claimed off waivers from the Browns on Nov. 3 -- turned 15 carries into 72 yards and a touchdown while logging a five-yard catch during New Orleans' 23-22 overtime win over Cleveland in Week 9. He split backfield duties with Alvin Kamara in that contest, but both running backs figure to have their snaps reduced due to the return of Etienne on Sunday.

headline: Estime carried the ball 15 times for 72 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-22 overtime win over the Browns. He also caught his only target for five yards.
story: Claimed off waivers by New Orleans earlier in the week to add some depth to a depleted backfield, Estime ended up going up against his former Browns squad in his first game since rejoining the Saints. Since he had played for the Saints in 2025 and didn't need to learn head coach Kellen Moore's playbook, Estime was in prime position to step into a big role right away and capitalized on the opportunity, leading the backfield with 16 touches ahead of Alvin Kamara's nine. Estime capped his big performance with a two-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. While he certainly made a case for a consistent role in the offense, rookie CJ Donaldson (shoulder) could be back next week and Travis Etienne (hamstring) might be close to returning from injured reserve. Estime could still be atop the depth chart, at least temporarily, for a Week 10 clash with the Panthers.

headline: The Saints claimed Estime off waivers from the Browns on Tuesday.
story: New Orleans released kicker Daniel Carlson to clear room on the 53-man roster for Estime, who began the season with the Saints before being cut on an injury settlement Sept. 22. After moving past a thigh injury, Estime caught on with the Browns and made his lone appearance for the team back in Week 6, when he carried nine times for 19 yards and a touchdown in a win over the Ravens. Upon rejoining the Saints, Estime will provide depth to a backfield that also includes Alvin Kamara, Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson (shoulder).

headline: The Browns waived Estime from the active roster Monday.
story: Estime was a healthy scratch in consecutive weeks leading up to Monday's cut. The running back played just one game with the Browns, logging nine carries for 19 yards and a touchdown in the team's Week 6 win over the Ravens. Estime will now be free to sign with another team if he clears waivers.

headline: Estime (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Titans.
story: Estime carried nine times for 19 yards and a touchdown in his 2026 debut during last week's win over the Ravens, but he'll be in street clothes Sunday while the Browns welcome Quinshon Judkins (ankle) and Dylan Sampson (knee) back from injuries. So long as Judkins, Sampson and Jaleel McLaughlin are all available for Cleveland, Estime could remain a fixture on the inactive list in the weeks to come.

headline: Estime turned nine carries into 19 yards and a touchdown during the Browns' 13-10 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
story: The Browns were without Quinshon Judkins (foot), Raheim Sanders (hip, IR) and Dylan Sampson (knee, IR) on Sunday, so Estime and Jaleel McLaughlin were the leaders of Cleveland's backfield. Estime and McLaughlin each had nine carries, but it was the former that logged a two-yard rushing touchdown midway through the fourth quarter to tie the game up at 10-10. Estime's 19 offensive snaps were nearly half of McLaughlin (39), but both of their roles will shrink significantly if Judkins is cleared to return for Week 7 against the Titans on Oct. 25.

headline: The Browns signed Estime to the 53-man roster Tuesday.
story: Estime signed to the Vikings practice squad in late September before signing with Cleveland. The 23-year-old will be behind Jaleel McLaughlin on the depth chart, who is the only other healthy running back on the Browns' roster. Dylan Sampson (knee) remains on injured reserve, and Quinshon Judkins (foot) and Raheim Sanders (hip) are both dealing with injuries after Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets.

headline: The Browns are expected to sign Estime off the Vikings' practice squad to the active roster, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz relays.
story: The Browns are in need of backfield depth, given that Dylan Sampson (knee) is on injured reserve and that both Quinshon Judkins (foot) and Raheim Sanders (hip) sustained their respective injuries during Sunday's 17-12 loss to the Jets. Jaleel McLaughlin is currently the only healthy running back on the Browns' roster, so Estime could have a sizable role in Week 6 against the Ravens on Sunday depending on the practice participation of Judkins, Sanders and Sampson over the coming days.

headline: The Vikings signed Estime to the practice squad Wednesday.
story: Estime worked out for the team Tuesday and will provide backfield depth behind Aaron Jones, Demond Claiborne and special-teamer DeeJay Dallas while Jordan Mason (thumb) remains on injured reserve for at least the next two games. Estime has handled 122 career regular-season carries for 508 yards and three touchdowns.

headline: The Vikings hosted Estime (thigh) for a workout Tuesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: The Saints waived Estime from injured reserve with an injury settlement last Tuesday. The running back suffered a thigh injury in early September and was quickly placed on IR, only to be waived shortly after. Estime played in seven games for New Orleans during the 2025 regular season, rushing 46 times for 198 yards and a touchdown.

headline: Ford (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Vikings.
story: The Saints activated Ford from injured reserve Saturday. The linebacker has recovered from his ankle injury and is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest as a reserve inside linebacker.

headline: The Saints activated Ford (ankle) from injured reserve Saturday.
story: Ford is still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings, but his removal on IR is a positive sign that he'll be available to play. He opened the regular season on injured reserve due to an ankle injury that he sustained during training camp.

headline: The Saints designated Ford (ankle) for return to practice from injured reserve Wednesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
story: The Saints placed Ford on injured reserve Aug. 31 with a designation to return. The linebacker was a full participant in his return to practice Wednesday, signaling he could be ready to return to the active roster shortly. If the Saints fail to add Ford to the 53-man roster by Oct. 28, he will need to remain on IR for the remainder of the 2026 season.

headline: Harris (illness) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Harris was battling an illness that prevented him practicing during Week 12 prep, and he's not progressed enough in his recovery to play in Sunday's contest. Darius Alexander and CJ Okoye are both in line for more rotational snaps on the defensive line in the absence of Harris, whose next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the 49ers on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Phillips (illness) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: An illness prevented Phillips from practicing Wednesday and Thursday. He was a limited participant in Friday's session, which was enough for the Giants to clear the third-year defensive back for Sunday's contest. Phillips has 42 tackles (31 solo), including 2.0 sacks, and five pass defenses through 10 contests this season.

headline: Phillips (illness) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Phillips appears to have come down with an illness, taking him out of Wednesday's prep session. The cornerback has two Week 12 practices remaining to be a healthy participant before he would have an injury designation heading into Sunday's game against the Colts.

headline: Phillips had five total tackles (five solo) and 2.0 sacks in Sunday's 27-27 tie with the Commanders.
story: Phillips hadn't recorded a sack since his rookie campaign. However, the 24-year-old got to Jayden Daniels twice in Week 5, with his second sack resulting in a Commanders punt and eventually a 17-yard touchdown from Malik Nabers to tie the game at the end of the fourth quarter.

headline: Phillips made 11 tackles (eight solo) in the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans.
story: Phillips played 49 defensive snaps in the contest, good for 82 percent of the Giants' total defensive plays. The third-year cornerback had only amassed three tackles over the first two games before Sunday's breakout, making the production difficult to rely on for fantasy purposes for the time being.

headline: Reese (back) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Reese opened Week 12 prep with back-to-back limited practices due to a back issue, but his full session Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag ahead of Sunday's road tilt. The rookie fifth-overall pick is up to 88 tackles (57 solo), including 4.5 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery across 10 games this season.

headline: Reese (back) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Reese likely sustained his back injury in the Giants' Week 11 win over the Jaguars. The linebacker not missing a practice session with the injury is a good sign, but he will likely need to continue stringing sessions together Thursday and Friday to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts.

headline: Reese recorded seven tackles (four solo) in Sunday's 23-18 win over the Jaguars.
story: The seven tackles were the third-lowest total for Reese in a game this season, and he did nothing else in the box score against Jacksonville. Reese is up to 88 tackles (57 solo), including 4.5 sacks, four pass breakups, including an interception, one forced fumble and a fumble recovery across 10 starts in 2026.

headline: Reese logged 13 tackles (four solo) in the Giants' 24-21 loss to the Commanders on Thursday.
story: Reese led the Giants in tackles as a consistent force against the Commanders' run game in the NFC East showdown. Despite the rookie first-rounder's best efforts, the Giants allowed 24 points en route to a meaningful divisional loss.

headline: Reese recorded 12 tackles (10 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and one forced fumble during the Giants' 19-11 win over the Eagles in Week 9.
story: The Giants' pass rush made life miserable for Eagles quarterback Joe Milton, who was making his first start of the season in Week 9. Reese was responsible for three of the Giants' seven sacks, including a strip sack early in the second quarter that caused a takeaway. It was the second time in 2026 that Reese logged double-digit tackles, and he is up to 68 tackles (49 solo), including 4.5 sacks, four pass defenses (including one interception), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through eight regular-season games.

headline: Reese posted seven tackles (five solo), including 0.5 sacks, in Sunday's 27-21 overtime victory against the Texans.
story: Reese continues to produce nice tackle numbers, as he's recorded seven or more stops in five of his seven games this season. The rookie out of Ohio State didn't notch a sack in his first four contests, but he's starting to pick up the pace with 1.5 sacks across his past three games. Reese has logged 100 percent of New York's defensive snaps in all but one of his appearances so far.

headline: Reese logged six tackles (four solo) and a fumble recovery during the Giants' loss to the Saints on Sunday.
story: Reese had another solid outing despite the loss, as he managed to recover the first fumble of his career. The 21-year-old has gotten off to a strong start in his rookie season, racking up 49 tackles (34 solo), including 1.0 sacks, an interception and a fumble recovery across his first six games.

headline: Reese logged nine tackles (nine solo) during the Giants' win over the Cardinals on Sunday.
story: Reese led the team in tackles in addition to recording his first career interception during Sunday's victory. The rookie first-round pick has gotten his career off to a strong start, racking up 34 tackles (27 solo) and an interception across his first four games.

headline: Reese logged 13 tackles (10 solo) and one pass defensed in the Giants' 12-7 win over the Titans.
story: Reese led both teams in tackles, putting together an impressive 10 solo stops in what was a defensive contest that featured 12 total punts and two total turnovers. The second-year linebacker also played all 60 of the Giants' defensive snaps in the contest, consistently assisting the team in shutting down the Titans' offense.

headline: Carter (calf/illness) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Carter was held out of the first two practices of Week 12 prep due to a calf injury and an illness. He was back on the field Friday in a limited capacity, but that was enough for the second-year edge rusher to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's road game. Carter has 26 tackles (10 solo), including 4.0 sacks, and one forced fumble through 10 games.

headline: Carter (calf/illness) did not participate in Thursday's practice, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
story: Carter was a DNP for Wednesday's session due to a calf issue, and the second-year edge rusher is now battling through an illness. His lack of practice reps are concerning, but he has one more opportunity to log at least a limited session ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts. Trace Ford and Dawuane Smoot would both be in line for more defensive snaps in the event that Carter is not cleared to play against Indianapolis.

headline: Carter (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Carter likely sustained his ankle injury in the Giants' Week 11 win over the Jaguars. The linebacker will need to upgrade to at least limited participation by Friday's practice session for a chance to play in Sunday's game against the Colts. Despite starting the week of prep as a DNP, coach John Harbaugh indicated that Carter should be ready to go for Sunday's contest, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.

headline: Carter recorded four total tackles (three solo), including 2.0 sacks, during Sunday's 23-18 win over the Jaguars.
story: Carter was able to notch his first career multi-sack performance, getting to Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence in both the first and second quarters. The edge rusher registered 12 total pressures in the contest according to NFL Next Gen Stats, and he has now compiled 26 total tackles (10 solo), including 4.0 sacks, and a forced fumble over 10 games this season.

headline: Carter (knee/back) doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday night's game against the Commanders.
story: Carter logged limited practices Monday and Tuesday before upgrading to full practice Wednesday. Across eight starts this season, the No. 3 overall pick of the 2025 Draft has produced 19 tackles (six solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a forced fumble. He has yet to develop into a game-wrecking edge rusher.

headline: Carter (illness) returned to practice Thursday, Dan Duggan of The Athletic reports.
story: Carter was absent Wednesday, but his return to the practice field puts the edge rusher on track for Sunday's game against the Eagles. Carter has started all seven games this season, recording 18 tackles (six solo), including 2.0 sacks, and a forced fumble on 88 percent of the defensive snaps.

headline: Carter (calf) is active for Sunday's game against the Saints, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
story: Carter was absent for the first two practices of Week 6 prep before upgrading to a limited participant in Friday's session. The strongside linebacker looked great in practice and has recovered in time to suit up for Sunday's game against the Saints.

headline: Carter (calf), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints, is expected to play, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Carter sat out the Giants' first two Week 6 practices but "looked explosive" while he was on the field as a limited participant for Friday's session, per Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com. The Giants apparently agree with Raanan's assessment, though Carter won't be officially cleared to play until the team releases its inactive list 90 minutes prior to Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff. Through New York's first five games, Carter has accrued 2.0 sacks among his 14 tackles while also forcing a fumble.

headline: Carter (calf) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints.
story: Carter upgraded to limited participation in Friday's practice after missing the earlier sessions of Week 6 prep. He'll try to suit up Sunday and build upon the 2.0 sacks he's logged through five games.

headline: Carter (calf) did not practice Thursday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
