story: Nabers was held out of drills Thursday due to a knee injury, but his return to all activity one day later lines up with head coach John Harbaugh's assessment of the situation Friday, when he told Matt Citak of the Giants' official site that the wide receiver "practiced fully" and is "full go" for Week 9. As a result, Nabers will look to build upon the massive 36-509-2 line on 51 targets that he's accrued over the last four contests.

headline: Head coach John Harbaugh said Nabers (knee) "practiced fully" Friday and will be "full go" for Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Matt Citak of the Giants' official site reports.
story: That's not to say Nabers won't be tagged with a designation once the Giants post their final Week 9 injury report Friday, but it appears his absence from Thursday's practice due to a knee issue was merely a blip on the radar. He's strung together four consecutive 100-yard performances, a stretch in which his receiving line sits at 36-509-2 on 51 targets. Nabers' presence will be key for New York's offense led by J.J. McCarthy, who will be making his second start of the season since assuming the Giants' QB1 role.

headline: Nabers (knee) was catching passes during Friday's walkthrough and should be "good" to go For Sunday's game against the Eagles, Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post reports.
story: After sitting out Thursday's practice due to the knee issue, Nabers appears to be trending in the right direction for Sunday's game at Philadelphia. Still, the Giants' final injury report will provide the clearest indication of whether the wide receiver takes a designation into the weekend.

headline: Nabers didn't practice Thursday due to a knee injury, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Nabers opened Thursday's session working on the side with trainers, and afterward he told Art Stapleton of USA Today, "I'll be good," as it pertains to his status for Week 9. In any case, the reason for Nabers' absence is a knee issue, which could be related to the right ACL tear that ended his 2025 season in Week 4. He'll have one more chance to prove his health Friday, at which point the Giants may tag him with a designation for Sunday's game in Philadelphia.

headline: Nabers (undisclosed) said Thursday, "I'll be good," for Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Art Stapleton of USA Today reports.
story: Nabers was spotted working with the Giants' training staff during the media-access portion of Thursday's practice, one day removed from not being on the team's initial Week 9 injury report. The reason for his likely practice restrictions isn't known but will be revealed once New York posts its second injury report of the week.

headline: Nabers had his jersey and helmet on but worked with the Giants' training staff during the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
story: Nabers may be dealing with an injury ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles, so Thursday's injury report will be worth monitoring, as that will reveal the extent of Nabers' practice participation as well as the nature of any injuries that may be bothering the star wide receiver. He was on a roll prior to the Giants' Week 8 bye, recording at least 111 receiving yards in four consecutive games.

headline: Nabers caught seven of nine targets for 111 yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans.
story: The switch from Jameis Winston to J.J. McCarthy at quarterback for the Giants hasn't slowed Nabers down at all, and the team's No. 1 wideout extended his streak of games with over 100 receiving yards to four. During that surge, Nabers has delivered a 36-509-2 line on 51 targets, as he puts his injury-marred sophomore NFL campaign firmly behind him. He'll try to not to lose his momentum during the bye before facing the Eagles in Week 9.

headline: Nabers caught 12 of 15 targets for 165 yards in Sunday's 34-27 loss to the Saints.
story: Jameis Winston got benched in favor of J.J. McCarthy in the fourth quarter after throwing his second interception of the day, but Nabers stayed busy no matter who was under center for the Giants, leading the team in catches, targets and receiving yards. The third-year wideout topped 100 yards for a third straight game, a stretch in which he's racked up a 29-398-2 line on 42 targets, but a potential full-time switch to McCarthy under center will create a little extra uncertainty for Nabers heading into a Week 7 tilt against the Texans.

headline: Nabers caught 11 of 20 targets for 121 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 27-27 tie against the Commanders.
story: Nabers topped his previous career high of 18 targets, which came in Week 2 of his rookie 2024 season in what was also a road game against the Commanders. He caught a 17-yard touchdown with 1:43 remaining in regulation, and the ensuing PAT tied the game after the Giants had trailed by 14 earlier in the fourth quarter. Nabers also had a few near-misses, including two deep passes that hit his hands on the Giants' final drive of the first half, which ended with one of Dominic Zvada's three missed field goals in a game full of miscues from both teams. After posting just 96 scoreless yards through three games, Nabers has built momentum heading into a Week 6 home game against the Saints, with 233 receiving yards and two touchdown catches across his last two outings.

headline: Nabers (knee) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Washington, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: When Nabers kicked off Week 5 prep with a DNP due to a knee injury, he told Connor Hughes of SNY.tv that he did "as much as I could." Nabers was able to practice in a limited capacity Thursday before head coach John Harbaugh said Friday that the wide receiver will "be ready to play Sunday," per Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News. Now that Nabers has received clearance to do so, he'll continue to act as the top pass catcher for QB Jameis Winston.

headline: Head coach John Harbaugh said Friday that Nabers (knee) will "be ready to play Sunday" at Washington, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports.
story: A knee injury didn't allow Nabers to log any official practice reps Wednesday, but he was back in a limited fashion Thursday and also mixed into drills Friday. Harbaugh's comments indicate Nabers is good to go for Week 5 action, even if the wide receiver ends up going down as questionable on the Giants' final practice report of the week Friday.

headline: Nabers (knee) was on the field for Friday's practice, Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post reports.
story: With Nabers having progressed from a non-participant Wednesday to a limited participant Thursday, his presence and involvement Friday is another positive sign for his status ahead of Sunday's game against the Commanders. The Giants' final injury report will determine whether the wide receiver carries a designation into Week 5, but all signs point to Nabers being available Sunday.

headline: Nabers (knee) was listed as a limited participant at practice Thursday, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: Nabers returned to practice Thursday after sitting out Wednesday's session, but he isn't completely out of the woods yet. An upgrade to full participation Friday could help Nabers avoid an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Commanders.

headline: Nabers (knee) was seen practicing during Thursday's media viewing period, Art Stapleton of USA Today reports.
story: After sitting out Wednesday's practice due to a knee injury, Nabers has taken a step in the right direction by taking part in at least a portion of Thursday's practice. His participation level will be clarified later Thursday as the Giants prepare for Sunday's game against the Commanders. Nabers had six catches for a season-high 112 yards and a touchdown in the Week 4 win over Arizona.

headline: Nabers didn't practice Wednesday due to a knee injury, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.
story: After Wednesday's session, Nabers relayed to Connor Hughes of SNY.tv that he did "as much as I could," and now the nature of that discomfort has been revealed. It's a bit concerning that Nabers went down as a DNP with a knee issue to begin Week 5 prep, especially since he's a year removed from tearing his right ACL. He also told Ralph Vacchiano of FoxSports.com that his shoulder is "a little sore," but the team didn't list that as the reason for his absence. In any case, Nabers' status will be watched as the week goes on to get a sense of his odds to suit up Sunday at Washington.

headline: Nabers said he took on "as much as I could" at Wednesday's practice, after which he noted he's dealing with soreness, Connor Hughes of SNY.tv reports.
story: Nabers also relayed that he'll "see how the week goes" as it pertains to his odds to play Sunday at Washington. He's already on his second signal-caller of the campaign (Jameis Winston) and has a cumulative 18-208-1 line on 26 targets through four games, and whether or not he'll be available in Week 5 remains to be seen.

headline: Nabers caught six of seven targets for 112 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Cardinals.
story: It was Nabers' best effort of the season, as he began to build some chemistry with new starting QB Jameis Winston, The duo connected on a 25-yard TD in the second quarter, Nabers' first trip to the end zone in 2026, and his 39-yard grab on the Giants' first possession helped set up a field goal. The third-year wideout will take an 18-208-1 line on 26 targets through four games, and renewed optimism in his big-play upside without Jaxson Dart (knee) under center, into a Week 5 road clash with the Commanders.

headline: Onyemata (abdomen) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: The veteran defensive lineman was designated for return from injured reserve last week and will look to make his return after logging a trio of full practices this week. Onyemata hasn't played since Week 2.

headline: Onyemata (abdomen) was estimated as a full practice participant on Wednesday's report.
story: Onyemata was designated to return from injured reserve Nov. 18 but was not cleared to play against the Chargers in Week 11. If he can string together full practices over the next two days, then Onyemata would have a good chance of being activated from IR ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Dolphins.

headline: Onyemata (abdomen) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
story: Onyemata was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday and strung together three consecutive limited practice sessions. However, the veteran defensive tackle is not quite ready to come off IR, so his next chance to play is Week 12 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 29. Onyemata has not played since Week 2 against the Packers due to an abdominal injury.

headline: The Jets designated Onyemata (groin) to return from the injured reserve list Wednesday, Eric Allen of the Jets' official site reports.
story: Onyemata's 21-day practice window has been opened. The 34-year-old hasn't played since Week 2 against Green Bay, when he suffered a groin injury. Darrell Jackson, Jowon Briggs and Harrison Phillips have taken most snaps at defensive tackle in his absence.

headline: Phillips (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: The veteran defensive lineman has started all 11 games this season, recording 43 tackles (16 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and a fumble recovery on 55 percent of the defensive snaps. Jack Heflin would be next up for increased snaps alongside Jowon Briggs and Darrell Jackson if Phillips is unable to play. David Onyemata (abdomen) could also be activated from injured reserve.

headline: Phillips (ankle) was listed as a limited participant in the Jets' practice estimate Thursday.
story: Phillips upgraded to limited participation after sitting out Wednesday's practice, and he also managed to play through the ankle injury during the Week 11 win over the Chargers. Jack Heflin would be in line for increased playing time during Sunday's matchup against the Dolphins if Phillips ends up being unable to play.

headline: Phillips (ankle) was listed as a DNP on Wednesday's estimated practice report.
story: Phillips has been working through an ankle injury over the past couple of weeks, so his DNP on Wednesday's report doesn't come as much of a surprise. The veteran defensive tackle will have two more chances to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Dolphins. Phillips has accumulated 42 tackles (16 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and one fumble recovery across 11 regular-season games.

headline: Phillips (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Amanda Vogt of the Jets' official site reports.
story: Phillips played through an ankle issue against the Bills in Week 10, and the veteran defensive tackle has been cleared to suit up for Sunday's contest. He has accumulated 36 tackles (11 solo) and one fumble recovery through 10 regular-season games.

headline: Phillips (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
story: Phillips started Week 11 prep as a DNP before logging consecutive limited sessions to end the week. If the defensive tackle is unable to suit up for Sunday's contest, Jack Heflin and Payton Page may see more rotational defensive snaps behind Darrell Jackson and Jowon Briggs.

headline: Phillips (ankle) was a limited participant in practice Thursday.
story: The defensive tackle missed Wednesday's session. Phillips played on 53 percent of the Jets' defensive snaps in Sunday's loss to the Bills and hasn't missed a game this season. Now that he's back at practice, he looks like he has a good chance to play in Week 11 against the Chargers as well.

headline: Phillips posted 10 tackles (four solo) Sunday in a Week 10 loss to Buffalo.
story: Phillips somewhat improbably led New York in tackles, as he logged just 53 percent of the team's defensive snaps. Prior to Sunday, he had tallied just four stops in his previous two games combined. Phillips has seven or more tackles three times this season, but he hasn't recorded more than four stops in any of his other seven appearances.

headline: Phillips (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Bills.
story: Phillips was trending in the right direction to play Sunday after logging a full practice Friday. The veteran defensive tackle was cleared to suit up after going through pregame warmups, and he'll face the team that drafted him in the third round of the 2018 NFL Draft. Phillips has 26 tackles (seven solo) and one fumble recovery through nine regular-season games.

headline: Phillips (ankle) is questionable against the Bills on Sunday.
story: Phillips missed the first two practices of Week 10 prep while recovering from an ankle injury. He was a full participant in Friday's session, so he may be considered more toward the probable side of playing Sunday. If Phillips cannot play, then both Jack Heflin and Payton Page would be in line for more rotational snaps on the interior defensive line behind Jowon Briggs and Darrell Jackson.

headline: Phillips (ankle) was estimated as a nonparticipant on the Jets' official injury report Wednesday.
story: The Jets only held a walkthrough practice Wednesday, and they projected that Phillips would not have been able to practice at all if a standard session had taken place. He'll likely need to get back on the practice field in a full capacity Thursday or Friday to avoid carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Sweat (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: The defensive tackle remains on injured reserve after having his 21-day practice window opened Wednesday, but he's been fully participating in practice and appears to have a decent chance of being activated Saturday and playing Sunday. Sweat hasn't played since Week 7.

headline: The Jets designated Sweat (knee) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Eric Allen of the Jets' official site reports.
story: The defensive lineman was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. Sweat hasn't played since Week 7 and has logged 17 tackles (five solo) across 229 defensive snaps this season.

headline: The Jets placed Sweat (knee) on injured reserve Saturday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: Sweat was diagnosed with a knee injury during the Jets' Week 7 loss to the Dolphins. The initial diagnosis was week-to-week, and the Jets medical staff has determined that a stint on IR is warranted for the third-year defensive lineman, although he's expected to return this season. Sweat will be required to miss at least four games, so the earliest he can play is Week 12 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 29, although he could be held out until after the Jets' Week 13 bye. Darrell Jackson and Harrison Phillips will both step into more prominent roles on the defensive line in Sweat's absence.

headline: Sweat (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Sweat is considered week-to-week due to a knee injury that he sustained against the Dolphins in Week 7. He was unable to practice during Week 8 prep, and in his absence, the Jets will turn to Jowon Briggs and Darrell Jackson to step into more prominent roles on the interior defensive line. Sweat's next chance to play is Week 9 against the Chiefs on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: Sweat (knee) is week-to-week and is unlikely to suit up for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reported Wednesday.
story: Sweat did not participate in Wednesday's practice as he continues to deal with the knee injury he sustained in the Jets' Week 7 loss to the Dolphins. The defensive tackle will likely miss Week 8 against the Raiders and could miss even longer due to the new injury.

headline: Sweat (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Sweat exited during the third quarter with a knee injury. The starting defensive tackle will likely be replaced by a rotation of Darrell Jackson and Jowon Briggs.

headline: Parham (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Amanda Vogt of the Jets' official site reports.
story: Parham, who is working through a knee issue, has been given the green light to play Sunday after going through pregame warmups. He'll start at left guard while Jordan Meredith provides depth at the position.

headline: Parham (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
story: Parham practiced in all three Week 11 prep sessions, logging consecutive limited practices before upgrading to a full participant Friday. Despite the upgrade to full participation, the offensive guard remains questionable for Sunday's contest, meaning his knee is likely still bothering him.

headline: Head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters that Parham got imaging done for a knee injury that the latter sustained during the Jets' Week 10 loss to the Bills on Sunday, Eric Allen of the Jets' official site reports.
story: Parham sustained the injury in the second quarter of Sunday's game and was not cleared to return. The Jets face the Chargers in Week 11 on Sunday, and if Parham cannot play in that contest, then Jordan Meredith would be the top candidate to fill in at left guard.

headline: Parham (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bills.
story: Parham exited the second quarter of Sunday's game with a knee injury. Jordan Meredith is set to fill in at left guard while Parham is absent.

headline: Parham (knee) is active for Sunday's game against Las Vegas.
story: Parham will be back in action for the first time since Week 3, when he sustained a knee injury in a loss to the Lions. Though he was listed as questionable heading into Sunday, Parham was cleared to play after logging a pair of limited practices and a full session during the week. He should step back in as the Jets' starting left guard, sending Jordan Meredith back to the bench.

headline: Parham (knee) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.
story: Parham will be sidelined for a fourth consecutive game due to a lingering knee injury. The good news for the 2022 third-rounder is that he was able to practice during Week 7 prep, so he's progressing in his recovery and could return for Week 8 against the Raiders on Nov. 1. Jordan Meredith will continue to start at left guard in Parham's absence.

headline: Parham (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Wednesday was Parham's first practice since sustaining a knee injury in Week 3 against the Lions, which prevented him from playing in each of the Jets' three following games. He'll have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Dolphins. If Parham is cleared to return, then he would likely reclaim his starting job at left guard from Jordan Meredith.

headline: Parham (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Patriots, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
story: Parham will miss a third consecutive game due to a knee injury. His next chance to play is Week 7 against the Dolphins on Sunday, Oct. 25, although the fifth-year pro has yet to practice since sustaining his injury. Jordan Meredith will continue to start at left guard in Parham's absence.

headline: Coach Aaron Glenn said Wednesday that Parham (knee) is still week-to-week as the Jets start preparing for Week 6, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
story: Parham has been sidelined for the Jets' last two games with the knee injury he suffered in Week 3 at Detroit, and he appears to be in danger of missing a third straight contest. His activity at practice during the week will be worth monitoring ahead of Sunday's game at New England, but his coach's words don't suggest a ton of optimism he'll be able to play against the division rival.

headline: Parham (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
story: A knee injury prevented Parham from practicing all week. He'll miss a second game in a row as a result of his injury, and his next chance to play is Week 6 against the Patriots on Sunday, Oct. 18. Jordan Meredith figures to once again start at left guard in Parham's absence.

headline: Coach Aaron Glenn said Wednesday that Parham is still week-to-week as he nurses a knee injury, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
story: Parham sat out Sunday's game at Chicago with the knee injury he picked up in Week 3 at Detroit, and it's still bothering him as the Jets begin preparing for Week 5. Barring an unexpected development, he's trending toward missing Sunday's contest versus the Browns.

headline: Parham (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bears, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
story: Parham was unable to finish the Jets' Week 3 loss to the Lions after sustaining a knee injury. He could not participate in any of the Jets' three practice sessions during Week 4 prep, and in his absence, Jordan Meredith will likely start at left guard against Chicago.

headline: Parham is considered week to week due to a knee injury, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
story: Parham is expected to sit out Sunday's matchup versus the Bears after suffering a knee injury during the Week 3 loss to the Lions. In his absence, Jordan Meredith will likely start at left guard.

headline: Ossai (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Bills.
story: Ossai missed the Jets' last four games while recovering from an ankle injury, but the sixth-year pro was cleared by medical staff to return for Sunday's AFC East tilt. He logged nine tackles (five solo) across three regular-season games prior to his injury.

headline: Ossai (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills.
story: Ossai has a chance to return from a four-game absence due to an ankle injury after stringing together a trio of limited practices during Week 10 prep. His return would give the Jets additional depth at defensive end behind Kingsley Enagbare and David Bailey.

headline: Ossai (ankle) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Ossai has missed the Jets' last four games while recovering from an ankle injury. He's been able to practice in a limited capacity, but he may need to log a full session in order to be cleared to play against the Bills on Sunday.

headline: Ossai (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Chiefs.
story: Ossai managed a trio of limited practices this week and was initially deemed questionable to suit up Sunday. However, he's not yet ready to play and is going to miss his fourth straight game. Ossai's next chance to return to action is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Buffalo.

headline: Ossai (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Chiefs.
story: Ossai was a limited participant throughout Week 9 practice as he continues to deal with the ankle injury he sustained in Week 5. The defensive end's upgrade to limited participation this week means he may see the field, but the Jets will likely elect to wait until the 26-year-old is fully healthy to allow him to suit up on game days.

headline: Ossai (ankle) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: It was Ossai's first practice since Week 5 due to a sprained ankle. The offseason pickup has appeared in three games with the Jets this season, recording nine tackles (five solo) on 107 defensive snaps. Ossai will look to provide some more juice to the New York pass rush once cleared to return.

headline: Ossai (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Las Vegas.
story: Ossai will end up missing a third consecutive game while recovering from an ankle injury that he sustained against the Browns in Week 5. He's been unable to practice since picking up the injury, so he would need to return to the practice field to have a realistic chance of returning for Week 9 against the Chiefs on Sunday, Nov. 8. Will McDonald and Nate Lynn will continue to operate in elevated roles defensively while Ossai is on the mend.

headline: Ossai (ankle) didn't participate in the Jets' practice Wednesday, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
story: Ossai is unlikely to play in Sunday's matchup versus the Raiders and is currently considered week-to-week due to an ankle injury he sustained during the Week 5 win over the Browns. Will McDonald and Nate Lynn should continue to see increased playing time in Ossai's absence.

headline: Ossai (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
story: Ossai continues to be held out of practice due to an ankle injury, which will force him to miss a second consecutive game. Will McDonald and Nate Lynn will be the Jets' rotational options at defensive end in the absence of Ossai, whose next chance to play is Week 8 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Ossai (ankle) was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Ossai looks on track to miss a second straight game this Sunday against the Dolphins, with Rich Cimini of ESPN.com relaying that the veteran defensive end is still considered week-to-week due to an ankle injury. While working in a rotational role over three appearances on the season, Ossai has logged nine tackles and no sacks.

headline: Ossai (ankle) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Patriots, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
story: Ossai will be inactive in Sunday's game after suiting up in three consecutive contests. He began the season with a foot injury and made his 2026 debut in Week 3.

headline: Ossai (ankle) was estimated to be a nonparticipant at Wednesday's walkthrough, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
story: Ossai suffered an ankle injury in Sunday's meeting with the Browns. While he managed to return to the contest, it doesn't appear he will be on the field in Week 6 versus the Patriots. Ossai's absence could potentially last longer than that, considering head coach Aaron Glenn classified the 26-year-old as week-to-week.

headline: Ossai (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Browns, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
story: Ossai needed to be helped off the field in the second quarter. Will McDonald is now the sole depth option at defensive end for the Jets' defense.

headline: Head coach Aaron Glenn announced Friday that Cooper (ankle/groin) will remain out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
story: Cooper will miss a second consecutive game Sunday, bringing him up to six total absences as a result of ankle injuries during his rookie campaign. Adonai Mitchell is set to start on the outside opposite Garrett Wilson, with Isaiah Williams manning the slot, though another elevation for practice-squad WR Sterling Shepard could be on the table after Shepard scored twice in the Week 11 win over the Chargers. Cooper's next chance to play will be a Week 14 home game against the Broncos following the Jets' Week 13 bye. Glenn said the timing of the bye played into the decision to keep Cooper out Sunday, per Rich Cimini of ESPN.com, which suggests Cooper has a decent chance to return after the bye.

headline: Cooper (ankle/groin) was listed as a non-participant in practice Thursday.
story: Cooper also logged a 'DNP' on Wednesday's practice estimate, so what -- if anything -- he's able to do Friday will be pivotal with regard to his status for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. If Cooper is sidelined for a second straight time this weekend, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams, in that order, will be next up for added opportunities at WR for the Jets.

headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Cooper (ankle/hip) won't practice Wednesday and is considered day-to-day.
story: The rookie wide receiver will be sidelined for a fourth consecutive practice while he continues to manage a pair of injuries, but the Jets aren't closing the door on Cooper putting an end to a one-game absence and playing this Sunday in Miami. In order to put himself in a position to suit up this weekend, however, Cooper will likely need to put in a full practice either Thursday or Friday. If Cooper ends up missing another game, the likes of Adonai Mitchell, Isaiah Williams (ribs), Tim Patrick and practice-squad member Sterling Shepard could be in line for added snaps and targets.

headline: Coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Cooper (ankle/hip) will be out for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
story: Cooper didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a pair of injuries, and he'll wind up sitting out Week 11. Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will be the primary wideouts for the Jets, and with Isaiah Williams (ribs) joining Cooper on the sidelines, Malik McClain and Tim Patrick will be options when the team wants to get more receivers on the field, and per head coach Aaron Glenn -- via Rich Cimini of ESPN.com -- Sterling Shepard and tight ends Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor could also get involved.

headline: Cooper didn't practice Thursday due to ankle and hip injuries.
story: Cooper made an early exit from this past Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills after injuring his right ankle, and the rookie wideout is also nursing a hip issue as the Jets prepare for a matchup this weekend with the Chargers. With two straight absences from practice to begin the week, Cooper will likely need to get in at least a limited session Friday to have any chance at suiting up Sunday.

headline: Cooper (ankle) isn't practicing Wednesday, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
story: Cooper logged just one snap this past Sunday against the Bills after tweaking the same ankle he hurt in Week 1, which led to an IR stint. The rookie WR will now have two more chances to practice this week, but if he's sidelined this weekend against the Chargers, Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell would likely be busy in Week 11, with Isaiah Williams (seven targets versus Buffalo) also factoring in.

headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Cooper (ankle) will undergo imaging Monday, Eric Allen of the team's official site reports.
story: Cooper played just one snap before exiting Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills after injuring his right ankle. Notably, the rookie first-round pick tweaked the same ankle in the Jets' Week 1 win over the Titans and was diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain, which resulted in a stint on injured reserve. The Jets are hoping that Cooper avoided as significant of an injury this time around, though even if his imaging yields good news, he still could be hard-pressed to suit up next Sunday versus the Chargers.

headline: Cooper (ankle) won't return to Sunday's game against the Bills, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
story: After being deemed questionable to return to the contest earlier Sunday, Cooper has now been ruled out and will target a potential return to action Nov. 22 against the Chargers. In his absence versus Buffalo, Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams are available lead New York's WR corps.

headline: Cooper (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Bills.
story: Cooper approached the contest listed as questionable with an ankle injury but ultimately garnered active status. Per, Connor Hughes of SNY TV, the rookie WR had tweaked the ankle injury he sustained in the opener, and now Cooper is tending to a new issue. In his absence, Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams will lead the Jets WR corps versus Buffalo.

headline: Cooper (ankle) is active for Sunday's contest against the Bills.
story: Cooper opened Week 10 prep listed as limited on back-to-back practice reports due to an ankle injury, but despite logging a full session Friday, the Jets tagged him as questionable for Sunday. Fellow WRs Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Adonai Mitchell (knee) also were listed as questionable, but all three now are available to the Jets offense. Cooper has been hit or miss this season, with two outings of at least 100 yards and exactly one TD, while he combined for a 9-88-0 line on 14 targets in his other three appearances.

headline: Cooper (ankle), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills, is expected to be available, Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports.
story: Cooper was working through an ankle issue during Week 10 prep and drew the questionable tag after logging a full practice Friday. The rookie first-round wide receiver is on track to suit up Sunday, and the same goes for Garrett Wilson (concussion) and Adonai Mitchell (knee). Wilson did not play against the Chiefs in Week 9, and in his absence, Cooper caught a season-high eight passes (on 11 targets) for 58 yards in a 35-12 loss for the Jets.

headline: Cooper (ankle), who was a full participant in Friday's practice, is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Bills.
story: The same goes for top receiver Garrett Wilson (concussion) as well as Adonai Mitchell (knee). The trio's full practice participation Friday suggests that all three players will be available Sunday, but their statuses will nonetheless need to be confirmed ahead of Week 10 action due to their official game designations. Fortunately for fantasy managers who have shares in any of the Jets' top three WRs, the team kicks off at 1:00 pm ET on Sunday.

headline: Cooper (ankle) will be a full practice participant Friday, Eric Allen of the Jets' official site reports.
story: After logging limited practices earlier in the week, Cooper may avoid an injury designation for Sunday's matchup with the Bills. Fellow Jets wideout Garrett Wilson (concussion) also has a chance to be cleared before Sunday, as he's upgrading to full practice participation Friday along with Cooper.

headline: Cooper (ankle) was a limited participant at Thursday's practice.
story: Cooper officially goes down as a limited participant for a second consecutive practice, matching the participation level of Garrett Wilson (concussion). Since returning from an ankle injury that landed him on injured reserve, Cooper has 19 catches for 276 yards and two touchdowns in four games, even with a zero-catch Week 8 performance during that stretch.

headline: Cooper (ankle) is participating in Thursday's practice, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
story: Both Cooper and Garrett Wilson (concussion) were spotted at practice Thursday after logging limited practice sessions Wednesday. It remains to be seen whether either wide receiver will upgrade to full participation Thursday ahead of Sunday's matchup with the Bills.

headline: Cooper (ankle) will be limited in Wednesday's practice, Brian Costello of the New York Post reports.
story: Per Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic,coach Aaron Glenn downplayed Cooper's current ankle injury, noting of the wideout, "I think he'll he just fine." Meanwhile, Connor Hughes of SNY TV relays the that Cooper's current issue is affecting the same ankle that he hurt in Week 1.

headline: Cooper caught eight of 11 targets for 58 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Cooper worked as the clear No.1 receiver for the Jets in the absence of Garrett Wilson (concussion), leading the team in targets, catches and receiving yards while Adonai Mitchell failed to catch any of his seven targets. Prior to finishing without a target in the Week 8 loss to the Raiders, Cooper delivered consecutive performances with at least 103 yards and a touchdown, so he has been effective in three of four games since returning from an IR stint due to a Week 1 ankle injury. Even if Wilson returns in Week 10, Cooper looks likely to remain involved in what could be a pass-heavy game plan against the Bills.

headline: Cooper and Adonai Mitchell will be the Jets' top wide receivers with Garrett Wilson (concussion) unavailable for Sunday's game at Kansas City, ESPN's Rich Cimini reports.
story: After back-to-back 100-yard games in his first two weeks off injured reserve, Cooper ran 26 routes last week without registering a target in the 38-33 loss to Las Vegas. Mitchell caught seven of nine targets for 142 yards and a touchdown, also running 26 routes, and Cimini's report notes that Mitchell "will become the No. 1 receiver" in Wilson's absence. Both Mitchell and Cooper figure to get plenty of snaps and routes, but targets and production aren't as assured.

headline: Cooper did not garner a target during Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.
story: Cooper entered Week 8 having topped 100 receiving yards with a touchdown in back-to-back games, so Sunday's performance was especially disappointing. The rookie wideout was overshadowed by Adonai Mitchell (7-142-1) and Garrett Wilson (6-83-0) in the game, and it'll be hard to predict his workload ahead of the team's Week 9 matchup with the Chiefs.

headline: Cooper caught all five of his targets for 115 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins.
story: Cooper topped 100 receiving yards with a TD for the second time in as many games since returning from an ankle injury sustained in his regular-season debut. The rookie 30th overall pick had a 52-yard catch in the first quarter and a 60-yard catch in the third, then added a three-yard touchdown reception three plays after the second long catch. Cooper has been a big-play machine when healthy, and he'll look to build on his strong start in Week 8 against the Raiders.

headline: Cooper may get fewer looks in the passing game Sunday versus Miami with Adonai Mitchell cleared to return from a finger injury, Amanda Vogt of the Jets' official site reports.
story: Cooper shined in his return from IR this past Sunday against New England, catching six of seven targets for 103 yards and a touchdown. That performance will likely gain him more attention from QB Geno Smith moving forward, but it must also be noted that Cooper's big game came in the absence of Mitchell, who is set to return Sunday following a four-game absence. Both Cooper and Mitchell are likely to remain behind Garrett Wilson in the pecking order, but it will be interesting to see if either Cooper or Mitchell is able to separate himself as the team's No. 2 wideout.

headline: Cooper brought in six of seven targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Making his return from a four-game stint on injured reserve due to an ankle sprain suffered on the opening possession of the season, Cooper hit the ground running and finished as the team leader in receptions, receiving yards and targets. The Indiana product also recorded his first NFL touchdown on a 48-yard strike from Geno Smith early in the third quarter, and his instant production despite the layoff gives his fantasy outlook a significant boost heading into a Week 7 home matchup against the Dolphins.

headline: Cooper (ankle) is active for Sunday's game against the Patriots.
story: Cooper will suit up for the first time since Week 1, when he sustained a high-ankle sprain on the Jets' first offensive possession of the season in an eventual win over the Titans. The rookie first-round pick out of Indiana returned to practice this week, turning in a pair of limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday before upgrading to full participation Friday and getting activated from injured reserve Saturday. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) out for another week, Cooper could potentially settle in as the Jets' No. 2 receiver Sunday, pushing Tim Patrick down a spot on the depth chart.

headline: Cooper (ankle) was activated from injured reserve Saturday.
story: Cooper is still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots, but he's likely to be cleared to play given his activation from IR. The rookie fourth-rounder has missed the Jets' last four games due to an ankle injury, but he could be thrust into a prominent role offensively given the absence of Adonai Mitchell (finger).

headline: Cooper (ankle) is being activated from injured reserve Saturday and is expected to be available for Sunday's AFC East tilt against the Patriots, Connor Hughes of SNY TV reports.
story: Cooper earned the questionable tag for Week 6 after logging a full practice Friday, and it looks like the rookie first-rounder will be back on the field after spending the last four weeks on injured reserve due to an ankle injury he sustained against the Titans in Week 1. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) sidelined, Cooper could slide into the Jets' WR2 role behind Garrett Wilson for Sunday's contest.

headline: Cooper (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at New England.
story: Cooper was a full practice participant Friday, upgrading from limited participation the previous two days. That doesn't necessarily mean he'll play, though the Jets definitely could use the help with Adonai Mitchell (finger) out for another week. They'll need to activate Cooper from injured reserve Friday or Saturday to have him available for Sunday's game against the Patriots at 1:00 p.m. ET.

headline: Cooper (ankle) will be a full participant in Friday's practice, according to the Jets' official X account.
story: After logging limited practices Wednesday and Thursday, the rookie's upgrade to full participation is a positive step in his return from injured reserve. The Jets would need to activate Cooper on Friday or Saturday in order to have him available for Sunday's game at New England. It's not yet clear if the team intends to do that.

headline: Cooper (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Cooper had his reps capped for the second day in a row after the Jets designated him for return from injured reserve Wednesday. The Jets will have just under three weeks to reinstate Cooper, so the rookie wideout may need to upgrade to full participation in Friday's session to have a shot at suiting up this weekend versus the Patriots. Cooper recorded a 30-yard reception and played just five snaps before exiting his NFL debut Week 1 against the Titans in the first quarter due to a high-ankle sprain.

headline: Cooper (ankle) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: After being designated for return from injured reserve earlier Wednesday, Cooper operated with a cap on his reps in his first practice since he exited the Jets' Week 1 win over the Titans due to a high-ankle sprain. The Jets haven't ruled out the possibility of the rookie first-round pick being activated from IR in advance of Sunday's game against the Patriots, but he'll likely need to practice fully Thursday and/or Friday to have a realistic chance at suiting up this weekend.

headline: The Jets designated Cooper (ankle) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
story: Cooper is slated to participate in Wednesday's walk-through practice in some capacity after the Jets opened his 21-day evaluation window. The rookie first-round pick -- who was deactivated after sustaining a high-ankle sprain in the Jets' Week 1 win over the Titans -- could have a chance at returning to action as soon as this Sunday at New England, depending on how he fares in practice this week. With the Jets classifying fellow wideout Adonai Mitchell (finger) as week-to-week, Cooper could have a chance at reclaiming a notable role in the receiving corps once he's activated from IR.

headline: Williams (ribs) practiced fully Thursday, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
story: Williams -- who was inactive in Week 11-- was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's estimated practice report, but his full participation a day later paves the way for him to return to action Sunday against the Dolphins. With fellow wideout Omar Cooper (ankle/groin) in danger of missing his second straight game, Williams could end up working as the Jets' WR3 this weekend behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell in the event that he's active and Cooper isn't.

headline: Williams (ribs) was listed as a limited participant on Wednesday's estimated practice report.
story: Though Williams and fellow wideout Omar Cooper (ankle/groin) were both sidelined for the Jets' Week 11 win over the Chargers, the former appears to be in a better spot on the health front to begin Week 12. Williams was able to take some reps in Wednesday's walkthrough session, while Cooper was a spectator. If he's able to play Sunday in Miami and if Cooper remains out for another game, Williams could end up serving as the Jets' No. 3 wideout behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell.

headline: Williams (ribs) won't play in Sunday's game against the Chargers.
story: With Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) also slated to be unavailable for the contest, Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell will lead the Jets' Week 11 WR corps, with coach Aaron Glenn noting Friday that the team's tight ends, primarily Kenyon Sadiq and Mason Taylor, should have an opportunity to see added opportunities as pass catchers this weekend in the absence of both Cooper and Williams.

headline: Williams (ribs) was a non-participant in Thursday's practice.
story: The Jets' wideout depth could be tested in Sunday's game against the Chargers, as both Williams and Omar Cooper (ankle/hip) have been sidelined for the team's first two Week 11 practices. Both receivers will likely need to practice in some fashion Friday to avoid being ruled out ahead of the weekend. If neither Williams nor Cooper can suit up against the Chargers, Malik McClain and Tim Patrick would be the available backup options behind starting receivers Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell.

headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Williams won't practice Wednesday due to a rib injury, Eric Allen of the Jets' official site reports.
story: New York will be without two of its wideouts to begin Week 11 prep, as rookie Omar Cooper (ankle) is also sidelined for Wednesday's practice. Williams drew a season-high seven targets in this past Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Bills, finishing with four catches for 24 yards across 50 offensive snaps while apparently picking up an injury at some point along the way.

headline: Williams caught four passes on seven targets for 24 yards during the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
story: Williams' seven targets were his most of the season, and most of those looks came after Omar Cooper left early in the first quarter of Sunday's game due to an ankle injury. The injury was to the same foot that Cooper sustained a high-ankle sprain in Week 1 against the Titans, and an extended absence of the rookie first-rounder would result in Williams stepping into the WR3 role behind Garrett Wilson and Adonai Mitchell. The Jets will hit the road for Week 11 against the Chargers on Nov. 22.

headline: Williams did not draw a target in Sunday's Week 9 loss to Kansas City. However, he rushed once for four yards, returned one punt for 18 yards and returned two kickoffs for 55 yards.
story: Williams didn't get a ball thrown his way despite logging a 60 percent offensive snap share. While the Illinois product continues to have a role in multiple facets of the game for New York, he's not making much of an impact as a pass catcher. Williams has one or zero catches in five straight contests and has tallied only 34 receiving yards during that span.

headline: Williams caught an 18-yard touchdown on his lone target in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.
story: Williams ran a total of one route on Geno Smith's 35 dropbacks against Las Vegas, but he made it count with a red-zone touchdown. The Jets' fourth receiver behind Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper, Williams has no fantasy appeal headed into next Sunday's date with the Chiefs.

headline: Williams should continue to serve as the No. 3 wide receiver behind Garrett Wilson and Tim Patrick for Sunday's game against the Patriots due to the absence of Adonai Mitchell (finger).
story: Williams caught one of his two targets for 16 yards and rushed once for three yards in the Jets' Week 5 win over the Browns. The wide receiver should continue to see some attention from Geno Smith, but if Omar Cooper (ankle) is activated from IR for Sunday's game, that could change.

headline: Williams caught one of two targets for 16 yards and added a three-yard carry in Sunday's 17-12 win over the Browns. He also had a 26-yard kickoff return and netted 67 yards on four punt returns.
story: Williams got the ball in his hands in four different ways but was quiet as a pass catcher after getting behind the defense for a 58-yard touchdown in the Week 4 loss to Chicago. The Jets were once again without wide receivers Adonai Mitchell (finger) and Omar Cooper (ankle) against the Browns, but Cooper will be eligible to return from IR ahead of the team's Week 6 trip to New England.

headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns, so Williams should serve as the Jets' WR2 behind Garrett Wilson for a third consecutive week.
story: It'll be the third game in a row that Mitchell will miss while recovering from a finger injury, and the severity around his health concern is not clear, according to Rich Cimini of ESPN.com. Williams has only three catches (on five targets) over his last two games without Mitchell, but the former hauled in two of three targets for 73 yards, including a 58-yard touchdown pass from Geno Smith, in Week 4 against the Bears.

headline: Williams caught two of three targets for 73 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears.
story: The lowly Jets ran a total of 32 offensive plays to Chicago's 89 in this one, and Geno Smith attempted just 15 passes, as the Bears dominated the time of possession. Williams got loose for a meaningless 58-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter. On the season, he has 10 catches for 135 yards and a touchdown on 12 targets. If Adonai Mitchell (finger) is back, Williams won't carry much fantasy appeal into next Sunday's game against the Browns.

headline: Williams will have the opportunity to work as the Jets' WR2 behind Garrett Wilson for Sunday's game against the Bears due to the absence of Adonai Mitchell (finger).
story: Williams has played 80 percent or more of the Jets' offensive snaps in each of the last two games, though he logged only one catch (on two targets) in a Week 3 loss to the Lions. However, with both Mitchell and tight end Mason Taylor (thumb) sidelined and tight end Kenyon Sadiq (back) listed as questionable, Williams should see more targets from Geno Smith in the passing game.

headline: Williams caught one of his two targets for 21 yards and returned four kickoffs for 95 yards over 63 total snaps in the Jets' 31-24 loss to the Lions on Sunday.
story: Williams played 90 percent of the Jets' offensive snaps in the contest alongside an additional eight special-teams snaps as a returner. The wide receiver has seen more playing time lately due to injuries to Adonai Mitchell (finger) and Omar Cooper (ankle). If Mitchell misses another game, Williams should see similar playing time as the No. 2 option in the Week 4 matchup with the Bears.

headline: Wallace (groin) was not listed on Wednesday's estimated practice report.
story: Wallace missed the Jets' last three games due to a groin injury, but his absence from Wednesday's report indicates that he is fully healthy and will return for Week 12 against the Dolphins on Sunday. Wallace has mostly played on special teams in 2026 and has four assisted tackles and a fumble recovery across six regular-season games.

headline: Wallace (groin) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Chargers, Amanda Vogt of the Jets' official site reports.
story: Wallace will end up missing a third consecutive game due to a groin injury, and his next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Dolphins on Nov. 29. He's mostly operated on special teams this season, but his absence means the Jets will have less depth at the edge rusher position for Sunday's contest.

headline: Wallace (groin) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Chargers.
story: A groin injury has prevented Wallace from playing in each of the Jets' last two games. He's questionable for Sunday's road game, but his ability to practice in full Friday indicates that the third-year linebacker is trending in the right direction heading into the weekend.

headline: Wallace (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bills, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
story: Wallace was held out of practice all week while recovering from a groin injury, which will prevent him from playing in a second consecutive game. Most of his snaps this season have come on special teams, but his absence means the Jets will have less depth at linebacker for Sunday's AFC East tilt. Wallace's next chance to play is Week 11 against the Chargers on Sunday, Nov. 22.

headline: Wallace (groin) was estimated to be a nonparticipant on Wednesday.
story: The linebacker missed last Sunday's loss to the Chiefs and has been strictly limited to special teams this season, playing 106 snaps in kick coverage.

headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Friday that Wallace (groin) will not play in Sunday's matchup against the Chiefs.
story: Wallace did not practice on back-to-back days after beginning the week as a limited participant due to a groin injury. The 23-year-old has appeared in six games for the Browns this season, with all of his snaps coming on special teams except for one rep on defense in Week 5.

headline: Ruckert went without a target while logging 16 of the Jets' 60 snaps on offense in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
story: Since recording eight catches for 48 yards and a touchdown over the Jets' first three games, Ruckert has yet to draw a target in any of the team's subsequent eight contests. Ruckert's downturn in involvement in the passing game coincides with the Jets' top two tight ends -- Mason Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq -- getting back to full health after they were either limited or sidelined in the early part of the season.

headline: Ruckert (knee) was a full participant in Friday's practice.
story: Ruckert was limited Wednesday and Thursday but managed to log a full session Friday, clearing the way for his availability for the Week 4 meeting with the Bears. With Mason Taylor (thumb) still sidelined, Ruckert should continue to be more involved. He might see the field even more Sunday if Kenyon Sadiq (back), who is questionable, can't suit up.

headline: Ruckert (knee) was a limited participant in practice Thursday.
story: Ruckert marked his second straight limited practice in preparation for Week 4. The 26-year-old likely suffered the knee injury in the Jets' Week 3 loss to the Lions, when he hauled in five targets for 39 yards and a touchdown. If his status doesn't improve, the fifth-year pro could be in danger of missing Sunday's contest against the Bears.

headline: Ruckert (knee) was limited in Wednesday's practice.
story: Ruckert may have picked up the injury during the Lions' 31-24 loss to the Lions in Week 3, when he hauled in all five of his targets for 39 yards and a touchdown, which was the second score of his five-year NFL career. Ruckert, Mason Taylor (thumb) and Kenyon Sadiq (back) are all dealing with injuries, leaving Jelani Woods and Andrew Beck as the only healthy tight ends to begin Week 4 prep. Ruckert will have two more opportunities to log a full practice and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Bears.

headline: Beck played all but one of his 13 snaps on special teams in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
story: The 30-year-old Beck has been one of the more versatile players in the league this season. In addition to taking snaps as a fullback and tight end, Beck often serves as a short-kickoff specialist for the Jets, while also contributing on the special teams coverage and return units. While the variety of roles he handles makes him valuable from a real-life standpoint, Beck maintains little fantasy relevance. He's carried twice for one yard and has yet to draw a target through the Jets' first 11 games.

headline: Davis registered six tackles (four solo) during Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: It was the second consecutive week in which Davis posted six stops, and he finished Sunday's game tied for the second-most tackles on the Jets behind Jamien Sherwood (11). Davis is up to 74 total tackles through 11 regular-season games, and the 2012 third-rounder is well on pace to record his 10th-straight 100-tackle season.

headline: Davis posted six tackles (three solo) Sunday in a loss to Buffalo.
story: Davis' six tackles tied for third-most on the Jets. The veteran linebacker has been relatively consistent this season with between six and 10 stops in seven of his 10 games so far. Davis has 68 total tackles (including 2.0 sacks) through 10 games, putting him on pace for a 10th consecutive triple-digit tackle campaign.

headline: Davis finished Sunday's Week 7 loss to Miami with three tackles (two solo) and one defensed pass.
story: Davis' tackle tally was his lowest of the campaign, but he did record his first effort of multiple defensed passes. The durable linebacker has played every defensive snap for the Jets so far this season. With 46 stops through seven games, Davis is on pace for a 10th consecutive 100-tackle campaign.

headline: Davis ended with 10 total tackles (five solo) and 1.0 sacks in Sunday's 23-12 loss to Chicago.
story: Davis has been on a roll of late, amassing 10 total tackles and 1.0 sacks in each of his last two games. The 37-year-old veteran has shown no signs of slowing down, and he has a favorable opportunity on the horizon in Week 5 against the Browns, a team that surrendered nearly 3.0 sacks per game in the first month of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Davis recorded 10 tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Sunday's 31-24 loss at Detroit.
story: Davis again led Jets linebackers in snaps in Week 3, but it was his first time registering a double-digit tackle total since Week 12 of the 2025 season. With that said, he remains solidly on the IDP radar in most formats going into a Week 4 matchup against a run-first Chicago offense.

headline: Belton posted six tackles (one solo) during the Jets' 27-24 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Belton played every single defensive snap Sunday and finished tied for the second-most tackles on the Jets behind Jamien Sherwood (11). Belton has recorded at least six stop in 10 of 11 regular-season games and is up to 88 tackles (42 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and five pass defenses. He is well on his way to cracking the tackling century mark for a second consecutive season.

headline: Belton finished Sunday's loss to the Bills with six tackles (one solo) and one defensed pass.
story: Belton tied for third on the Jets with six stops. That's a total he's now reached in every game this season except Week 1. Belton ranks second among NFL safeties with 82 tackles on the campaign.

headline: Belton recorded 12 total tackles (eight solo) and a pass defensed in Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.
story: Belton was able to secure double-digit stops for the second time this season, finishing second on the team behind linebacker Jamien Sherwood (14). Belton is now up to 68 total tackles (37 solo), including 1.0 sacks, while also adding four passes defensed over eight contests to begin the regular season.

headline: Belton registered nine tackles (six solo) in Sunday's loss to the Dolphins.
story: Belton continues to put together a productive season, as he's posted seven or more stops in each of his past five games. The former New York Giant has yet to miss a defensive snap this season in his first campaign as a Jet. After posting a career-high 120 stops across 17 regular-season contests last year, Belton is on pace to challenge that mark with 56 tackles (including 1.0 sacks) through seven games this year. He's also tallied three defensed passes.

headline: Belton recorded nine tackles (four solo) and a pass defensed during Sunday's 26-19 loss at New England.
story: In a game where the Patriots were able to keep the ball on the ground for much of the day, Belton collected six-plus tackles for his fifth straight contest. He's on pace for a career year in that category, and he projects as a solid IDP option in many formats going into a Week 7 matchup versus the Dolphins.

headline: Belton finished with 14 total tackles (six solo) in Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears.
story: Belton finished behind Minkah Fitzpatrick for the game high in total tackles. The 2022 No. 114 overall pick spent his first four seasons with the Giants. In his final campaign with the club in 2025, he amassed a career-high 120 total tackles (60 solo), 2.0 sacks, three forced fumbles and one interception. Belton is on pace for another quality year, giving him plenty of upside for IDP managers moving forward.

headline: Bailey recorded five tackles (two solo), including 2.0 sacks, one pass defense and one forced fumble during the Jets' 27-24 win over the Chargers on Sunday.
story: Week 11 was the third multi-sack performance of the season for Bailey, and his first takedown of Justin Herbert early in the second quarter resulted in a fumble that the Chargers recovered. Bailey is up to 9.5 sacks through 10 regular-season games, which leads all rookies and is tied for third-most in the NFL behind Will Anderson (11.5) and Greg Rousseau (10.0). Bailey also leads the league with six forced fumbles, and the Texas Tech product is living up to his pedigree as the second-overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft.

headline: Bailey tallied nine tackles (five solo), including 2.0 sacks, and two forced fumbles during the Jets' loss to the Chiefs on Sunday.
story: Bailey had a productive outing despite the loss as he was the only Jets defender to record a sack. The 23-year-old has gotten off to a strong start during his rookie campaign, compiling 34 tackles (26 solo), including 7.5 sacks, and five forced fumbles across his first eight games.

headline: Bailey (groin) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
story: After missing Week 8 with the groin injury he suffered the previous week, Bailey appears poised to return after missing just one contest. The No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 Draft, Bailey has piled up 35 tackles (21 solo), including 5.5 sacks, three forced fumbles and one pass breakup across seven starts this season.

headline: Bailey (groin) was a limited participant in practice Wednesday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
story: Bailey was a limited participant in practice Wednesday, which is a step up from last week's three DNPs. The 23-year-old missed Week 8 with a groin injury suffered in Week 7 against Miami. Should the rookie continue to progress well throughout the week, he could have a shot at returning for Week 9.

headline: Bailey (groin) is inactive for Sunday's game against Las Vegas.
story: Bailey suffered a groin injury during the Week 7 meeting with the Dolphins. He didn't practice throughout the week and will now miss his first game of the 2026 campaign. Without Bailey on the field versus the Raiders, Nate Lynn and Will McDonald are candidates for more snaps.

headline: Bailey (groin) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Raiders.
story: Bailey was unable to practice all week due to a groin injury, which he sustained against Miami in Week 7. The Jets haven't shut the door on the rookie second-overall pick playing Sunday, but if he's eventually ruled out, then Nate Lynn and Will McDonald would both take on larger roles on the defensive line against Las Vegas.

headline: Bailey didn't practice Wednesday due to a groin injury.
story: Bailey sustained injury during Sunday's loss to the Dolphins but was able to finish the game, per Rich Cimini of ESPN.com. Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Bailey will be evaluated throughout the week before the team determines his availability for this Sunday's matchup with the Raiders. The No. 2 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, Bailey leads all rookies with 5.5 sacks and is tied with Carl Granderson, Elijah Ponder and T.J. Watt for fifth-most in the NFL.

headline: Bailey recorded seven tackles (five solo), including 3.0 sacks, during the Jets' 17-12 win over the Browns on Sunday.
story: The Browns' offensive line had trouble containing Bailey and the Jets' pass rush Sunday, with New York sacking Deshaun Watson eight times. Three of those sacks were credited to Bailey, two of which were on third down and forced the Browns to punt on the next play. The Week 5 effort was the performance that the Jets were hoping to see out of the second overall pick of the 2026 NFL Draft. Bailey is up to 5.0 sacks through five regular-season games, which leads the Jets and is tied with D.J. Wonnum for fourth most in the NFL behind Will Anderson (7.5), Greg Rousseau (6.0) and Dallas Turner (5.5).

headline: Sherwood recorded 11 tackles (eight solo) and a forced fumble in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
story: It was the linebacker's fourth game this season with double-digit tackles. He also had a fourth-quarter sack wiped off the board by a Jets penalty. Through 11 games this season, Sherwood has recorded 97 tackles (49 solo), four pass breakups, three forced fumbles and a fumble recovery on 97 percent of the defensive snaps.

headline: Sherwood secured nine tackles (four solo) in Sunday's Week 10 loss to the Bills.
story: Sherwood finished second on the Jets in stops Sunday, behind Harrison Phillips (10). Sherwood has notched at least eight tackles in five straight games, and he's hit the double-digit mark three times this season. The veteran linebacker ranks eighth in the NFL with 86 tackles through 10 games.

headline: Sherwood recorded 14 total tackles (five solo) during Sunday's 38-33 loss to the Raiders.
story: Sherwood notched a season-high 14 takedowns in the victory, securing double-digit stops for the third time in the last five contests. The linebacker has now compiled 68 total tackles (32 solo), four passes defensed, two forced fumbles and a fumble recovery over eight games to open the 2026 campaign.

headline: Sherwood totaled eight tackles (four solo) and two defensed passes Sunday in a loss to Miami.
story: Of Sherwood's eight stops, two went for a loss. He also notched multiple defensed passes for the first time this season. Sherwood has been quite disruptive so far in 2026, tallying 54 tackles, four defensed passes, two forced fumbles and a recovered fumble through seven games.

headline: Sherwood recorded 11 tackles (six solo), a forced fumble and a fumble recovery during Sunday's 26-19 loss at New England.
story: Sherwood made a huge hustle play on a third down early in the fourth quarter, punching the ball out of the arms of DeMario Douglas after chasing him down 39 yards beyond the line of scrimmage. He also recovered a fumble in the third quarter, and both turnovers set up Jets field goals. He profiles as a solid IDP option in many formats heading into a Week 7 tilt versus the Dolphins.

headline: Sherwood finished with 13 total tackles (five solo) and one forced fumble in Sunday's 23-12 loss to Chicago.
story: Sherwood finished behind Dane Belton (14) and Minkah Fitzpatrick (16) for the game high in total tackles. He also came up big in the third quarter by forcing a fumble on D'Andre Swift, which ultimately resulted in a 30-yard field goal from Jason Sanders.

headline: Shepard reverted to the Jets' practice squad Monday.
story: Shepard was elevated for Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers due to the absences of fellow wideouts Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs). The veteran receiver answered the call by hauling in both of his targets for 24 yards and two touchdowns in the win. Since Shepard has now been elevated the maximum three times, he'll need to be signed to the 53-man roster in order to suit up again for the Jets this season.

headline: Shepard caught two passes for 24 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
story: With Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) inactive, Shepard was elevated from the practice squad and logged 22 of 60 offensive snaps. He ran 13 routes on Geno Smith's 23 dropbacks and obviously made the most of his two targets. In his 120th career regular-season game, it was Shepard's first career two-touchdown performance. It's unlikely to be indicative of future performance.

headline: The Jets elevated Shepard from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports.
story: The move gives the Jets much-needed depth at wide receiver given the absences of both Omar Cooper (ankle) and Isaiah Williams (ribs) for Sunday's game against the Chargers. It will be the third elevation of the season for Shepard and first since Week 4 against the Bears, so he would need to be signed to the 53-man roster in order to suit up for the Jets beyond Week 11.

headline: Shepard reverted to the Jets' practice squad Monday, per the NFL's transaction log.
story: Shepard was on the field for 17 of the Jets' 32 offensive snaps as the team finished with a time possession of 17:15, and he failed to haul in his lone target from Geno Smith. It was the second time this season that the veteran wide receiver was promoted from the practice squad, and he's eligible for one more elevation before the Jets would be required to sign him to the active roster. Shepard could be brought up for Sunday's Week 5 matchup against the Browns if Adonai Mitchell (finger) is not cleared to play.

headline: The Jets elevated Shepard from their practice squad to their active roster Saturday.
story: Shepard is set to suit up on game day for the second straight week. Last Sunday in Detroit, the veteran wideout logged a healthy workload of 30 offensive snaps -- third-most among New York wideouts -- and caught his only target for three yards. Shepard could also garner a significant role this Sunday due to Adonai Mitchell again being ruled out due to a finger injury.

headline: Brownlee (illness) was a full participant in Wednesday's walkthrough practice, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports.
story: An illness prevented Brownlee from playing in the Jets' Week 10 loss to the Bills. His full practice Wednesday indicates that he is fully healthy and should be available for Sunday's road game against the Chargers.

headline: Brownlee (illness) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Bills.
story: Brownlee developed an illness during Week 10 prep, and he will be an observer for Sunday's contest after not being cleared by medical staff to play. D'Angelo Ponds should take on a larger role in the Jets' secondary in the absence of Brownlee, whose next chance to play is Week 11 against the Chargers on Nov. 22.

headline: Brownlee (illness) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Buffalo.
story: Brownlee was unable to practice Thursday due to an illness, but he was back on the field Friday in a limited capacity. He'll have the weekend to shake off his illness, but his official status may not be known until 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, when the Jets announce their list of inactive players. Rookie second-rounder D'Angelo Ponds would have a larger role in the Jets' secondary if Brownlee is not cleared to play.

headline: Brownlee (concussion) does not have an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Browns, Daniel Oyefusi of ESPN.com reports.
story: Brownlee upgraded his practice participation in each Week 5 prep session, going from a DNP on Wednesday to a full participant Friday. The cornerback has cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol and is all set to suit up for Sunday's contest.

headline: Brownlee (concussion) was limited during practice Thursday.
story: Brownlee didn't return to Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears due to his injury. He didn't practice Wednesday, though his limited participation Thursday keeps the door open regarding his availability for the Week 5 meeting with the Browns. If Brownlee can't suit up for that contest, D'Angelo Ponds may continue to see more snaps.

headline: Brownlee is in concussion protocol as Week 5 approaches, Antwan V. Staley of the New York Daily News reports.
story: Brownlee suffered a head injury during Sunday's loss to the Bears, and he was evaluated for a concussion. The cornerback is officially dealing with a concussion, and he'll have to clear protocol in order to be available for the team's Week 5 matchup with Cleveland.

headline: Brownlee (concussion) did not return to Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears.
story: Brownlee exited the contest to be evaluated for a concussion and was replaced by rookie D'Angelo Ponds. If Brownlee can't suit up in Week 5 against the Browns, Ponds may be needed to fill the void in the slot.

headline: The Jets signed Lynn to the active roster Wednesday.
story: Lynn has yet to start in an NFL regular-season game. The defensive end from William & Mary University will now provide additional support for the Jets' defensive line.

headline: Sanders made both of his field-goal attempts and all three PATs in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Chargers.
story: Sanders got the scoring started with a 50-yard field goal to cap the opening drive of the game. He later made one from 24 yards in the third quarter. Sanders has been a bright spot for the Jets this season, as he entered play Sunday leading the league in field-goal attempts (28) and makes (25), and he further boosted his conversion rate. The Jets have struggled to turn red-zone possessions into touchdowns this season, making Sanders a valuable fantasy kicker.

headline: Sanders made all four of his field-goal attempts in the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday.
story: Sanders knocked in field goals from 41, 27, 22 and 48 yards out in Sunday's contest. The kicker accounted for all 12 of the Jets' points for a second straight week, performing the same feat in the team's Week 9 loss to the Chiefs. Sanders moves to 25-for-28 on field-goal attempts over nine contests so far during the 2026 season.

headline: Sanders went 4-for-5 on field-goal tries during Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs.
story: Sanders provided all the offense for New York in Week 9, making exactly four field goals for the second straight week and third time in the last four contests. The kicker converted attempts from 23, 48, 49 and 54 yards before pulling his lone miss wide left from 53 yards, all of which came in the first half. Sanders has now gone 21-for-24 on field-goal attempts, including 4-for-6 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 season.

headline: Sanders made all four of his field-goal attempts and three PATs in the Jets' 38-33 loss to the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Sanders made four shorter field goals from 21 yards, 36 yards, 39 yards and 31 yards in a perfect outing. The kicker worked to redeem himself after a crucial field-goal miss in a three-point loss to the Dolphins during Week 7. Sanders is 17-for-19 on field goals and 13-for-13 on PATs through eight 2026 regular-season games.

headline: Sanders went 1-for-2 on field-goal tries and made both of his extra-point attempts during Sunday's 28-25 loss to Miami.
story: Sanders hit the right upright on his first field-goal attempt of the day in the third quarter, missing his first kick since Week 1. The kicker later added a 33-yard make in the fourth quarter, but his earlier miss would prove to be the difference in the loss. Sanders has now gone 13-for-15 on field-goal tries, including 3-for-4 from 50-plus yards, over the first seven games of the 2026 season.

headline: Sanders made all four of his field-goal attempts and his sole PAT in the Jets' 26-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday.
story: Sanders had a stellar game, contributing 13 of the Jets' 19 total points in the contest. The kicker made field goals from 42, 36, 40 and 36 yards in the contest, keeping the Jets in the game until the very end.

headline: Sanders made his lone field-goal attempt and both of his extra-point tries during the Jets' 17-12 win over the Browns on Sunday.
story: Both teams battled wind and rain during Sunday's contest at MetLife Stadium, but Sanders managed to extend the Jets' lead to 10-6 early in the fourth quarter on a 54-yard field goal. The veteran kicker has attempted just one field goal in three of the last four games and is 8-for-9 on field-goal tries through five regular-season games, with his lone miss coming from 50-plus yards. The Jets will hit the road for a Week 6 AFC East showdown against the Patriots on Oct. 18.

headline: Sanders made both of his field-goal tries and went 1-for-2 on PATs during Sunday's 23-12 loss to the Bears.
story: Sanders made field goals from 36 and 30 yards in the contest, notching his second game with multiple field-goal makes this season. The kicker did miss an extra-point try in the fourth quarter, and he has now gone 7-for-8 on field-goal attempts and 5-for-6 on PATs over four contests during the 2026 campaign.

headline: The Jets signed Sanders off their practice squad Tuesday, Eric Allen of the team's official site reports.
story: Though New York cut him at the conclusion of the preseason, Sanders re-signed with the organization as a member of the practice squad and was elevated for each of the first three games of the season. He went 5-for-6 on field-goal tries and drilled all five of his point-after attempts during that stretch, with his performance earning him a spot on the 53-man roster.
