story: Moore was held without a catch for the first time since Week 5, failing to take advantage of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) being unavailable. Moore figures to remain an afterthought on offense in Week 9 against the Giants.

headline: Moore caught both of his targets for 16 yards during Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys.
story: Moore had the opportunity to work in an expanded role Monday due to the absences of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). Moore's 22 snaps on offense were fourth-most among Eagles wide receivers and he logged season highs in both catches and receiving yards. However, the Eagles' offense as a whole struggled without its top wide receivers, and Moore would revert to a deep rotational role against the Commanders on Sunday if one or both of Smith and Wicks were cleared to return.

headline: Cooper caught one of his two targets for 14 yards during the Eagles' win over the Cowboys on Thursday.
story: Cooper had a quiet outing despite the win, finishing fourth on the team in both receiving yards and receptions. Across 10 games this season, the 25-year-old has caught 17 passes for 259 yards and four touchdowns, all of which serve as new career highs.

headline: Cooper caught four of his five targets for 59 yards in the Eagles' 19-16 win over the Steelers on Sunday.
story: Cooper played 46 offensive snaps and 15 special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The wide receiver continues to see a significant snap share for the Eagles, drawing two more targets than rookie first-round pick Makai Lemon in the Week 11 win.

headline: Cooper caught just two of eight targets for 25 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
story: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) still out, Cooper played more than 90 percent of the offensive snaps for the third straight game. He's done very little with that playing time, producing five catches for 61 yards during that span. Cooper is well off the fantasy radar until he shows something in the box score, and that's if Smith and Wicks remain sidelined.

headline: Cooper and Makai Lemon are positioned to start again Sunday against the Giants, with fellow wideouts DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) ruled out for a third straight game, per PhiladelphiaEagles.com.
story: Cooper made some big plays earlier this season but hasn't done much with his more recent opportunity, catching just three of nine targets for 36 yards over the past two weeks while playing 94 percent of snaps on offense. He's been targeted on just 13 percent of his routes this year, though that rate could improve some with strong-armed Joe Milton replacing Tanner McKee as the starting QB this week.

headline: Cooper caught two of six targets for 19 yards Sunday in a Week 8 loss to Washington.
story: Both of Cooper's catches came in the first half -- he didn't haul in any of his three targets in the second half. The second-year wideout led Eagles wideouts with 66 offensive snaps and finished second with the six targets, but it didn't amount to much production, as he couldn't form much of a connection with QB Tanner McKee. Despite an elevated role due to injuries to DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) the past two weeks, Cooper has just three catches for 36 yards in that span, making him an unappealing fantasy option.

headline: Cooper caught one of three passes for 17 yards during the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday.
story: With both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) sidelined, the Eagles' wide receiver group was led by Cooper, rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown during Monday's contest. Cooper led the position group with 61 offensive snaps, but he only had a 17-yard catch to show for it, which he logged on the Eagles' final play of the first quarter. He has only two catches on five targets for 26 yards over his last two games, and his profile as a boom-or-bust touchdown option in fantasy is severely hampered with Tanner McKee under center instead of Jalen Hurts (calf, IR). The Eagles will hit the road for Week 8 against the Commanders on Sunday.

headline: Cooper caught one of two targets for nine yards and added 38 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 25-14 loss to the Panthers.
story: Cooper saw his offensive workload decrease with the return of DeVonta Smith in Week 6, and, as a result, this was the first time he's failed to reel in multiple passes since Week 3. With Smith, Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon all active, Cooper's ceiling will be limited from a fantasy perspective moving forward.

headline: Cooper caught two of three targets for 71 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
story: Cooper was able to reach paydirt again Sunday, securing a 62-yard touchdown on a deep pass from quarterback Jalen Hurts in the second quarter. The wide receiver has taken advantage of a larger workload in the last two weeks with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) sidelined, reeling in five of 10 targets for 104 yards and three touchdowns in Smith's absence. On the year, Cooper has caught seven of 13 targets for 137 yards and four scores over five contests.

headline: Cooper caught three of seven targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams.
story: With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dallas Goedert (knee) out versus Los Angeles, Cooper actually led the Eagles in targets and receiving yards while securing both of Jalen Hurts' touchdowns. Each score was of the red-zone variety. Despite carrying a 20-10 lead into halftime, Philly was unable to do anything on the scoreboard after the break. Cooper is unlikely to have much fantasy appeal moving forward if Smith is able to return next Sunday against Jacksonville.

headline: Smith (back) was seen limping badly in the locker room after Thursday's 39-38 win over the Cowboys, Martin Frank of the Delaware News Journal reports.
story: Smith put together a career stat line during the Eagles' Thanksgiving Day win, with the veteran wide receiver hauling in 11 of 14 targets for 200 yards and two touchdowns. He was in and out of the game after landing hard on his tailbone on one of his targets in the fourth quarter and was in noticeable pain when on the field. Smith will have additional time to rest courtesy of the Thursday game, but his status over the coming days will be worth monitoring ahead of the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Smith caught 11 of 14 targets for 200 yards and two touchdowns in Thursday's 39-38 win over the Cowboys.
story: Injuries keep piling up for the Eagles, with both Saquon Barkley (neck) and Dallas Goedert (shoulder) exiting the Thanksgiving contest early, and even Smith was checked for a back injury late in the game after an awkward landing along the sideline. The wideout stayed in the game, however, and he put together a career-best performance while acting as Joe Milton's top downfield option. Both of Smith's TDs came on breakdowns in the Dallas secondary, as he hauled in scores of 50 and 45 yards on plays in which Milton just chucked the ball up and let his No. 1 guy go get it. Smith will take a 42-551-4 line on 67 targets into a Week 13 contest against the Cardinals.

headline: Joe Milton III launches 50-yard TD to DeVonta Smith
story: Joe Milton III launches 50-yard TD to DeVonta Smith

headline: Joe Milton III finds DeVonta Smith for another Eagles TD
story: Joe Milton III finds DeVonta Smith for another Eagles TD

headline: Smith (hamstring) caught five of 12 targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.
story: Smith was targeted on 12 of Joe Milton's 21 passes in the wide receiver's first game since Week 6. Milton has thrown for just 310 yards without a touchdown pass through two starts for the Eagles, so expectations should be tempered for the team's passing game as a whole, but Smith has reclaimed his role as the team's top pass catcher. Smith could make the most of his hefty target share Thursday against the generous Dallas secondary.

headline: Smith (hamstring) practiced fully Thursday.
story: Smith followed up Wednesday's limited showing with an uncapped session one day later, thereby paving the way for his first game action since Week 6. Despite missing five of the last six contests due to a hamstring injury, he put together a 26-310-2 line on 41 targets in his four appearances this season. However, with Jalen Hurts (blood clots) out for the rest of the 2026 campaign, Smith will be on the receiving end of passes from Joe Milton on Sunday against the Steelers.

headline: Smith (hamstring) is taking part in Thursday's practice, Andrew DiCecco of InsideTheBirds.com reports.
story: Smith got back on the practice field Wednesday for the first time since his last game action in Week 6, going down as a limited participant. He has sessions lined up Thursday and Friday to be listed as full, at which point he may be tagged with a designation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Steelers.

headline: Smith (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Smith missed five of the last six games before the Eagles' Week 10 bye due to a hamstring issue, but he was able to get back on the practice field Wednesday, after which he told Eliot Shorr-Parks of Sports Radio 94 WIP Philadelphia that he feels "100 percent healthy." Smith's ensuing activity level may mean the team is easing him back into drills, and how he fares Thursday and Friday likely will determine how he's listed ahead of Sunday's contest against the Steelers.

headline: Smith (hamstring) said Wednesday that he's "100 percent healthy," Eliot Shorr-Parks of Sports Radio 94 WIP Philadelphia reports.
story: That's not to say Smith will go down as a full participant Wednesday, which marked his first on-field work since Week 6 due to a lingering hamstring injury. His activity level will become known once the Eagles post their first Week 11 practice report.

headline: Smith (hamstring) was spotted practicing Wednesday, Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports.
story: The Eagles are getting healthier coming out of the bye, with both Smith and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) present for the media viewing period of practice. That Smith is practicing in any capacity on a Wednesday bodes well for his status going into the Week 11 matchup with Pittsburgh, though practice reports this week will give more detail on how much he's progressing. Regardless, this is a step in the right direction for Smith's return to action.

headline: Coach Nick Sirianni indicated Wednesday that he feels good about Smith (hamstring) returning to action Sunday against the Steelers, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: The same applies to fellow WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), and if the duo is available this weekend, rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon could see decreased opportunities in Week 11. While Sirianni is hopeful that Smith and Wicks are ready to return, per Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia, at this stage he's not ready to make any promises regarding their availability versus Pittsburgh.

headline: Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
story: Smith thus will sit out for the fifth time in six games due to a hamstring injury. Fellow WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) also won't play Sunday, leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore to man the Eagles' receiving corps. Smith's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 22, versus the Steelers.

headline: Smith (hamstring) was not seen at Friday's practice, Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: With Smith now absent from practice again Friday, he's unlikely to play Sunday against the Giants, leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper and Hollywood Brown as the top wide receivers for QB Joe Milton's first start in an Eagles uniform. Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was also absent from practice Friday and figures to join Smith on the gameday inactive list yet again.

headline: Smith (hamstring) officially didn't practice Thursday.
story: Smith has yet to mix into any drills since his last appearance in Week 6 against the Panthers, missing the last two contests due to a hamstring issue. With a Week 10 bye on the horizon, the Eagles may be focusing on getting him healthy for the final eight weeks of the campaign. In any case, Smith's status for Sunday's contest against the Giants may gain some clarity once the team posts its final Week 9 injury report Friday.

headline: Smith (hamstring) wasn't spotted at practice Thursday, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: Smith hasn't practiced or played since he suited up for Philadelphia's Week 6 loss to the Panthers. He's trending toward a third consecutive absence Sunday against the Giants. With Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) also yet to resume practicing, Makai Lemon looks set to lead Philadelphia's receiving corps for a third consecutive game.

headline: Smith (hamstring) didn't practice Wednesday.
story: Smith's lack of activity to kick off Week 9 prep doesn't come as a surprise, as he wasn't present during the media-access portion of Wednesday's session. He hasn't practiced since his last appearance in a Week 6 loss to the Panthers, when he went for seven catches (on 14 targets) for 75 yards and one touchdown. If he's able to put himself in a position to play Sunday against the Giants, Smith will be on the receiving end of passes from QB Joe Milton, who is replacing Tanner McKee as the starter.

headline: Smith (hamstring) wasn't spotted at Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: Smith has missed four of the last five contests due to a lingering hamstring injury, and until he's able to mix into drills again, he may not be a candidate to be active on game days. The Eagles have a Week 10 bye after Sunday's matchup with the Giants, so the team could be focusing on getting him healthy for Week 11 and beyond. In any case, fellow WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) also wasn't seen Wednesday, leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore as the healthy options at the position on the active roster.

headline: Smith (hamstring) is listed as out for Sunday night's game against the Commanders.
story: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) has also been ruled out, so both wideouts will miss a second straight contest. Look for Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore to soak up most of the snaps at wideout for Philadelphia. Smith will thus target a potential return to action Nov. 8 against the Giants.

headline: Smith (hamstring) remains sidelined for Friday's practice, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: Smith has missed practice all week, making him unlikely to play Sunday night against the Commanders. Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was also absent Friday, paving the way for Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore to again handle wideout duties in Week 8.

headline: Smith (hamstring) missed Thursday's practice.
story: Smith so far has sat out Wednesday's walkthrough and Thursday's practice due to a lingering hamstring injury, giving him just one more opportunity to mix into drills this week. The Eagles may make a ruling on Smith's status for Sunday's game in Washington once they post their final Week 8 injury report Friday.

headline: Smith (hamstring) wasn't spotted during the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: Smith was a non-participant at Wednesday's walkthrough, and he doesn't appear ready to rejoin his teammates one day later. He has sat out three of the past four games and will likely need to practice in at least some capacity Friday to have a chance to play Sunday night against the Commanders.

headline: Smith (hamstring) was a non-participant at Wednesday's walkthrough.
story: Smith has missed three of the last four games due to a hamstring injury, and his lack of activity to begin Week 8 prep isn't a great sign for his odds to return to action Sunday in Washington. He likely will need to mix into drills Thursday and/or Friday to have a chance to play this weekend.

headline: Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Cowboys.
story: Smith was unable to practice all week while nursing a hamstring injury, and the Eagles will be without both of their top wide receivers, as Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) has also been ruled out. Rookie Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper and Hollywood Brown figure to be the Eagles' top wideouts for Monday night's game, and tight end Dallas Goedert will be a go-to target for quarterback Tanner McKee due to the absences of both Smith and Wicks. Smith's next opportunity to play is Week 8 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 1.

headline: Smith (hamstring) was not seen at the Eagles' practice Saturday, EJ Smith of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: Smith missed each of the first two practices of Week 7 prep while tending to a hamstring injury that he aggravated against the Panthers in Week 6. His absence for a third consecutive practice doesn't bode well for his chances of playing Monday against the Cowboys, but his status for that contest will be more clear once the Eagles announce their injury designations following Saturday's session. Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was also not on the field, so Dallas Goedert (knee), Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper could be the top targets for quarterback Tanner McKee in Monday's NFC East showdown.

headline: Smith (hamstring) didn't practice Friday.
story: Smith previously sat out Weeks 4 and 5 due to a hamstring issue, but he was able to suit up this past Sunday against the Panthers, logging a 66 percent snap share and reeling in seven of 14 targets for 75 yards and one touchdown. It's unclear if Smith may be in danger of missing Monday's game versus the Cowboys, but Saturday's practice report will unveil his chances to suit up in Week 7.

headline: Smith (hamstring) wasn't spotted at Friday's portion of practice open to the media, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: Smith continues to miss practice with a hamstring injury that cost him two games prior to last Sunday's return against the Panthers. However, he may have aggravated the issue, considering his back-to-back DNPs to begin Week 7 prep. Makai Lemon, Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) and Darius Cooper would be in line for the wideout duties if Smith needs to sit Monday night against Dallas, though Wicks has an injury of his own.

headline: Smith (hamstring) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Smith wasn't present in the media-access portion of Thursday's session, and his previous hamstring issue appears to be the culprit for his absence to begin Week 7 prep. He thus will have two more chances to prove his health before the Eagles potentially tag him with a designation for Monday's game versus the Cowboys.

headline: Smith wasn't spotted at Thursday's practice, Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com reports.
story: Smith sat out Weeks 4 and 5 due to a hamstring injury, but he logged a full practice last Friday before suiting up this past Sunday against the Panthers. His snap share (66 percent) in that contest was below his weekly norm, but he still hauled in seven of 14 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown while working with QB Tanner McKee. Thursday's practice report will reveal if Smith is dealing with a health concern, or is merely getting the day off.

headline: Smith brought in seven of 14 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
story: Smith had an eventful day in his return from a two-game absence, leading the Eagles in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the afternoon. He also worked around getting briefly shaken up following a long incompletion where he appeared to have taken a blow to the chest area, and he added his second touchdown reception of the campaign via a 19-yard grab early in the fourth quarter. Smith displayed solid chemistry with fill-in signal-caller Tanner McKee, which certainly is a welcome development considering Jalen Hurts (IR, calf) is sidelined indefinitely.

headline: Smith (hamstring) practiced in full Friday and doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Panthers.
story: Prior to logging a limited practice Thursday, Smith had been working on a side field for roughly one week, so a return to action seemed possible before the Eagles cleared him outright Friday. He thus will be making his first appearance this weekend since a Week 3 loss at Chicago, looking to build upon his 19-235-1 line on 27 targets through the first three contests. Smith won't be working with Jalen Hurts (calf) due to a blood clot, though, with backup QB Tanner McKee subbing in for Hurts for as long as the latter is sidelined.

headline: Smith (hamstring) said Friday that he is "good" and that his availability for Week 6 is "up to the doctors," Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports.
story: Smith returned to practice Thursday and per reporters also got some work in Friday, so it seems he will have a chance to return to action in Week 6. His status for Sunday's matchup with the Panthers will officially be revealed when the Eagles release their final injury report of the week later Friday.

headline: Smith (hamstring) is practicing Friday, Jimmy Kempski of The Philly Voice reports.
story: Smith returned to practice Thursday as a limited participant, after missing the past two games. If he does play against the Panthers on Sunday, he'll be catching passes from backup QB Tanner McKee.

headline: Smith (hamstring) practiced on a limited basis Thursday.
story: Before he mixed back into drills Thursday, Smith hadn't practiced since logging all 50 offensive snaps during a Week 3 loss at Chicago. On a positive note, he's been working on the side since last Thursday, and his upgrade from DNP this Wednesday to limited one day later gives him a reasonable to chance to return to action Sunday versus the Panthers. Friday's injury report will reveal Smith's odds to play this weekend, and if he's able to do so, he'll be on the receiving end of passes from QB Tanner McKee after Jalen Hurts was ruled out for Week 6 action due to a blood clot.

headline: Smith was not seen with his helmet during the media viewing period Thursday,Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports.
story: Smith is nursing hamstring and toe injuries and it appears he'll be missing his second straight practice Thursday. He has missed back-to-back games and doesn't seem to be trending towards a return in Week 6 against the Panthers. The Eagles will already be missing Jalen Hurts (blood clot) for Sunday's game.

headline: Smith (hamstring/toe) was a non-participant at Wednesday's practice.
story: While Smith remained sidelined from on-field work and now appears to be dealing with a toe injury in addition to his hamstring issue, he was spotted working on a JUGS machine during the open portion of Wednesday's session, per Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer. Smith has missed the last two games and may be trending toward a third absence if he isn't able to get back on the practice field by Friday.

headline: Smith (hamstring) was working on the JUGS machine during Wednesday's practice, Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: Smith thus is unlikely to practice Wednesday after missing the last two games due to a nagging hamstring issue. Head coach Nick Sirianni told Zach Berman of The Athletic on Monday that he's hopeful Smith will return this Sunday versus the Panthers, but he likely will need to mix into some drills this week to have a chance to do so.

headline: Head coach Nick Sirianni expressed hope Monday that Smith (hamstring) will return for this Sunday's game against the Panthers, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports.
story: Smith has missed the Eagles' last two games due to a hamstring injury, and the Eagles also were without Saquon Barkley (hamstring) for their 19-17 Week 5 loss to the Jaguars in London. Smith has been limited to side work over the last couple of weeks, but a return to practice during Week 6 prep, even in a limited capacity, will be a positive step in his rehab program. Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon will continue to be the Eagles' top wide receivers in Smith's absence, though Darius Cooper appears to have been the biggest beneficiary of Smith's injury, with Cooper logging a 5-104-3 line on 10 targets over his last two games.

headline: Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's contest versus the Jaguars in London.
story: Smith was seen running on a side field Thursday before getting in some rehab work Friday, but he was listed as a non-participant on all three of the Eagles' Week 5 injury reports due to a lingering hamstring issue and thus won't play Sunday. With Hollywood Brown (ankle) also sidelined this weekend, Philadelphia's options at wide receiver will be Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey.

headline: Smith (hamstring) is doing rehab work on a side field at Friday's practice, EJ Smith of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: It leaves Smith's status in considerable doubt for Sunday's game against the Jaguars in London, but the Eagles will release official injury designations later Friday. With Smith looking likely to miss Week 5, rookie Makai Lemon and Week 4 standout Darius Cooper once again will be in line to handle prominent pass-catching roles. Neither is particularly exciting in a broken Philadelphia offense.

headline: Smith (hamstring) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice.
story: Per Tim McManus of ESPN.com, Smith was seen running on a side field Thursday, but the activity wasn't enough for him to be considered limited. It could be a sign that Smith is closing in on a return to practice, but until he does he may be trending toward a second straight absence Sunday at Jacksonville due to a hamstring issue. Friday's injury report may provide clarity on that front.

headline: Smith (hamstring) was spotted running on a side field during Thursday's practice, Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports.
story: It's a sign of progress as Smith deals with a hamstring injury that already has sidelined him for one game and didn't allow him to practice Wednesday. In any case, Thursday's injury report will unveil if he was able to upgrade to limited or instead remain a DNP for a second consecutive session.

headline: Elliott converted both of his field-goal attempts and all three of his extra-point attempts during the Eagles' 39-38 win over the Cowboys on Thursday.
story: Elliott had a strong outing in the victory, as he nailed the game-winning field goal from 59 yards out with two seconds left in the game. The 31-year-old has now converted 13 of his 14 field-goal attempts and all 21 of his extra-point tries across 11 games this season.

headline: Eagles make 59-yard FG to stun Cowboys, complete remarkable comeback
story: Eagles make 59-yard FG to stun Cowboys, complete remarkable comeback

headline: Elliott went 4-for-4 on field-goal attempts and made his lone PAT in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.
story: The Eagles kicker accounted for 13 of the team's 19 points, as he was good from 41, 29, 53 and 55 yards on his field goals. It was Elliott's first game with multiple field goals made since Week 4 against the Rams. That's how broken the Philadelphia offense has been for an extended period, and it doesn't project to get any better moving forward with Joe Milton at the controls. Elliott will be a hold-your-nose fantasy play in a theoretically high-scoring environment Thursday against the Cowboys, but it will be a movable force against a stoppable object when the Dallas defense squares off with the Eagles offense.

headline: Elliott made his lone field-goal attempt in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
story: Elliott's kick was good from 45 yards, but with Joe Milton making his first start at quarterback and without DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), the Philly offense struggled to move the ball and score points. Elliott is not an exciting fantasy kicker on a tanking Eagles team.

headline: Elliott (ankle) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game versus the Giants.
story: Elliott was limited at practice Wednesday and Thursday due to an ankle issue, but he managed a full practice Friday and is in line to suit up Sunday. The Eagles have been arguably the most ineffective offense in the league so far in 2026, and there's not much reason to believe they'll turn things around in Week 9 against a solid Giants defense, leaving Elliott as an unappealing fantasy option.

headline: Elliott (ankle) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Elliott was limited for a second consecutive practice. There should be more clarity on his status Friday for the Eagles' Week 9 meeting with the Giants. However, if Elliott is ruled out ahead of that one, the Eagles will presumably hit the open market for a replacement.

headline: Elliott (ankle) was a limited participant at the Eagles' practice Wednesday.
story: Elliott opened the week with a limited session as a result of an apparent ankle issue. The kicker went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT try during the team's 27-10 loss to Washington in Week 8, and he may have picked up the ankle injury during the contest. Elliott will have two more chances to log a full practice before Sunday's matchup with the Giants.

headline: Elliott went 1-for-2 on field-goal tries and hit his only extra-point attempt in Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
story: Elliott clanged a 41-yard attempt off the left upright in the fourth quarter. It was the veteran's first miss of the season, but the Eagles are simply not giving him enough scoring chances to keep him relevant in fantasy football.

headline: Elliott made all three of his PAT attempts and didn't attempt a field goal in Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys.
story: Elliott hasn't missed a kick all season, but he remains stuck on five field-goal attempts for the campaign, as the Eagles aren't moving the ball consistently but have found ways to punch in touchdowns when they get in scoring range. With Philadelphia banged up on offense and in the midst of a five-game losing streak, Elliott is facing some headwinds heading into a favorable Week 8 matchup on paper against the Commanders, who are giving up 28.7 points per game.

headline: Elliott made both of his extra-point attempts during the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday.
story: With Jalen Hurts (calf) out for the year, Sunday was the Eagles' first game with Tanner McKee under center. The offense labored to get up and down the field, and it was the fifth time in six games that Elliott attempted zero or one field goals. Week 7 against the Cowboys on Monday, Oct. 26 could be a better night offensively for the Eagles, given that Dallas' defense ranks 30th in the league in yards allowed per game.

headline: Elliott made his lone field-goal attempt and both of his extra-point tries during Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars in London.
story: Elliott's only field-goal try came late in the fourth quarter, when he knocked through his 48-yard attempt to give the Eagles a 17-16 lead with only eight seconds left to play. He has yet to miss a kick through five regular-season games, though he's made only one field goal or zero in four of those contests. Elliott's scoring floor ceiling figures to be limited given that the Eagles' offense has the second-fewest yards per game (262.2) and ranks in the bottom-5 in points allowed per game (18.4). The Eagles will be home for four of their next five games, starting with Week 6 against the Panthers on Oct. 18.

headline: Elliott converted both field-goal attempts and both PATs in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams.
story: Elliott made field goals from 29 and 56 yards against Los Angeles and remains perfect on the season. He has just four field goals through four games and is 9-for-9 on extra-point attempts. The Eagles aren't currently scoring enough on offense to warrant elite kicker status for Elliott.

headline: Elliott converted his sole PAT and attempted no field goals in the Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Bears on Monday night.
story: Elliott had an uneventful day, kicking through his one extra point on a second-quarter touchdown. The kicker remains 2-for-2 on field-goal attempts and moves to 7-for-7 on extra-point tries through three regular-season games.

headline: Goedert (shoulder) had his right arm in a sling following Thursday's 39-38 victory over the Cowboys, Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com reports.
story: Goedert injured his right shoulder during the first half of Thursday's game and was not cleared to return. He'll undergo further tests to determine the severity of the injury, but the veteran tight end is certainly in jeopardy of not being available for the Eagles' Week 13 road tilt against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6. Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz and rookie second-rounder Eli Stowers would all be in line for larger roles on offense if Goedert were to miss time.

headline: Goedert (shoulder) has been ruled out of Thursday's contest at Dallas.
story: Before he jogged to the locker room and was considered questionable to return to Week 12 action, Goedert hauled in one of two targets for nine yards. With Grant Calcaterra a healthy scratch Thursday, Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz and Eli Stowers are the Eagles' healthy and available tight ends.

headline: Goedert suffered a shoulder injury during Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
story: Goedert jogged to the locker room in the first quarter and was called questionable to return by the Eagles not long afterward. For as long as Goedert remains out of the contest, Johnny Mundt, Zach Ertz and Eli Stowers will handle TE duties for Philadelphia.

headline: The Eagles listed Goedert (shin) as a full participant in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.
story: Philadelphia deemed Goedert a limited participant on Monday's estimated injury report, but had the team held a traditional practice Tuesday, the veteran tight end would have been able to increase his activity. Goedert thus looks on track to play Thursday, when he'll face off against a Cowboys defense that he burned for five receptions for 48 yards on seven targets back in Week 7.

headline: Goedert was listed as a limited participant on Monday's practice estimate due to a shin injury.
story: Philadelphia gauged Goedert as limited to kick off Week 12 prep after he played 47 of 53 snaps while turning his lone target into a 38-yard reception during Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers. Goedert won't have much time to heal up from the shin issue while the Eagles prepare for a Thursday matchup with the Cowboys, but the fact that he avoided being listed as a non-participant on the first injury report of the week is generally a good sign for his chances of being cleared for game day.

headline: Goedert caught his only target for 38 yards in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.
story: Goedert turned his only look from Joe Milton into Philadelphia's longest pass play of the game. This was Goedert's second one-catch performance in eight appearances this season, but he recorded at least four receptions in each of the other six games. He hasn't scored a touchdown since a two-TD performance in the season opener, but perhaps a Thanksgiving matchup with the generous Dallas defense can help Goedert end that drought.

headline: Goedert caught five of six targets for 50 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
story: Goedert finished one catch and 11 yards shy of Makai Lemon's team-leading totals in Joe Milton's first start for the Eagles. Both of Goedert's touchdowns this season came back in Week 1, and the Eagles have since changed QBs twice. Goedert's best result in the three games started by Tanner McKee was a six-catch, 61-yard outing, so the veteran TE has remained consistent even as the offense around him falls apart due to injuries. Milton, McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton are all potential candidates to start in Week 11 against the Steelers after Philadelphia's Week 10 bye.

headline: Goedert caught all four of his targets for 30 yards and added a two-yard run in Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
story: Goedert has 15 catches for 139 receiving yards in three games since Tanner McKee took over as Philadelphia's starting QB, but the veteran TE has now gone five consecutive appearances without a TD after scoring 13 times in the span of 15 regular-season appearances through Week 1 of this season. Goedert had a ball bounce off his hands for an interception in the second half, but the play was negated by a defensive penalty, removing what would have been the lone blemish on Goedert's otherwise clean, though unimpressive, stat sheet. He'll try to snap his touchdown drought in Week 9 against the Giants.

headline: Goedert secured five of seven targets for 48 yards in the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday night.
story: On a night when both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were sidelined, Goedert served as an even more important target than usual. The veteran tight end finished second in all of receptions, receiving yards and targets for the Eagles on the night, and he's now recorded at least five catches in three consecutive games. Goedert has 24 targets over that span as well, and he should remain similarly busy in a Week 8 road matchup against the Commanders on Sunday night.

headline: Goedert (knee) was a full participant in Saturday's practice and does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the Cowboys.
story: After opening the week with two missed practices, the veteran tight end returned to full work Saturday, which was enough for him to fade an injury tag for Monday night's contest. Both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) have been ruled out, so Goedert and rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon should command the majority of targets from quarterback Tanner McKee. Goedert has a 12-99-0 receiving line on 17 targets over his last two games.

headline: Goedert (knee) said he felt good at Saturday's practice after dealing with inflammation earlier in the week, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: Goedert was back on the practice field Saturday after missing the first two sessions of Week 7 prep while dealing with inflammation in his knee. The Eagles still need to submit their injury designations for Monday's game against the Cowboys, but Goedert noted after Saturday's session that he expects to play, per Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer. The veteran tight end's availability is crucial for Philadelphia, given that both of the team's top wide receivers in DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice all week.

headline: Goedert (knee) is on the field for the start of Saturday's practice, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: Goedert missed the first two practices of Week 7 prep while tending to a knee injury, but he's back on the field and in pads for Saturday's session. The Eagles are also dealing with injuries to DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), so Goedert -- if active for Monday night's game against the Cowboys -- would operate in an expanded role in the passing game if either or both of the Eagles' top two wide receivers is sidelined.

headline: Goedert (knee) was a non-participant at Friday's practice.
story: Goedert has yet to mix into drills this week due to a knee injury, which could be related to the right MCL sprain that sidelined him in Weeks 3 and 4. In any case, how he's listed on Saturday's practice report will provide a sense of his chances to play Monday against the Cowboys.

headline: Goedert (knee) was not seen at Friday's portion of practice open to the media, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: With Goedert also having been held out of Thursday's practice, his status will need to be monitored over the weekend ahead of Monday night's game against Dallas. Goedert returned in Week 5 from his MCL injury, and he has 12 catches for 99 yards on 17 targets over the two games since. With back-to-back DNPs to start Week 7 prep, Goedert likely needs to get some work in Saturday in order to play.

headline: Goedert (knee) was held out of Thursday's practice.
story: Goedert previously sat out Weeks 3 and 4 due to a sprained MCL in his right knee, but he's been able to handle 69- and 81-percent snap shares the last two games while compiling a 12-99-0 line on 17 targets. Thursday's DNP may be for maintenance of the previous injury, but his status nonetheless will be monitored as the week continues to get a sense of the tight end's chances to play Monday versus the Cowboys.

headline: Goedert was not seen during the media-access portion of Thursday's practice, Jimmy Kempski of the Philly Voice reports.
story: Goedert joins several other Eagles skill-position players who weren't out with the team during the media-viewing part of the session, including DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks. Thursday's practice report will clarify whether Goedert is dealing with an injury or simply getting a rest day. Goedert missed two games due to a knee injury earlier in the season but has recorded six receptions in back-to-back weeks.

headline: Goedert caught six of eight targets for 61 yards during Sunday's 25-14 loss to the Panthers.
story: Goedert was able to reel in exactly six passes for the second straight week while his eight targets were second only to DeVonta Smith (14). With Jalen Hurts (calf) on injured reserve with a superficial blood clot, Tanner McKee took over at starting quarterback Sunday, logging 45 pass attempts in the defeat. If Philadelphia remains pass-heavy moving forward, Goedert will stand to continue seeing plenty of looks.

headline: Goedert caught six of nine targets for 38 yards in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
story: Back in the lineup after a two-game absence due to a knee injury, Goedert led the Eagles in targets and receptions, although the volume didn't lead to much yardage. With the Philly backfield and wide receiver room depleted by injuries, the veteran tight end could well remain Jalen Hurts' favorite option in the short term. Goedert will take an 11-119-2 line on 16 targets through three contests into a Week 6 clash with the Panthers.

headline: Goedert (knee) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game versus the Jaguars in London.
story: After missing Weeks 3 and 4 due to a sprained MCL in his right knee, Goedert got back on the practice field this week, logging limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday before a full practice Friday gave him the all clear to play again. With both WR DeVonta Smith and RB Saquon Barkley sidelined this weekend due to respective hamstring injuries, Goedert figures to be a featured part of the Eagles' passing attack.

headline: Goedert (knee) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game at Jacksonville.
story: After missing Weeks 3 and 4 due to a sprained MCL in his right knee, Goedert got back on the practice field this week, logging limited sessions Wednesday and Thursday before a full practice Friday gave him the all clear to play again. With both WR DeVonta Smith and RB Saquon Barkley sidelined this weekend due to respective hamstring injuries, Goedert figures to be a featured part of the Eagles' passing attack.

headline: Goedert (knee) was limited at practice Thursday.
story: Goedert maintained his activity level from Wednesday as he looks to put a sprained MCL in his right knee further in the rearview mirror. Friday's practice report will reveal his odds to return to action Sunday in Jacksonville, but if he's inhibited or sidelined again this weekend, Johnny Mundt, E.J. Jenkins and practice-squad member Zach Ertz again will man tight end for the Eagles.

headline: Goedert (knee) practiced on a limited basis Wednesday.
story: Goedert has missed the last two contests due to a sprained MCL in his right knee, but his return to drills this week puts game action back on the table for the ninth-year tight end. He likely will need to string together consecutive days of on-field work to give the Eagles peace of mind and clear him to play Sunday versus the Jaguars in London. For the time being, though, Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins are the healthy TE options on the active roster, and the team can still use one more elevation on Zach Ertz to reinforce the position

headline: Goedert (knee) is practicing Wednesday, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: With Goedert returning to the field after recently being ruled out for Sunday's game against the Rams, this marks his first visible step forward in his recovery from a sprained MCL in his right knee. His participation Wednesday puts the Eagles tight end back on the radar for Week 5, and his practice level and any game designation later in the week will provide more insight about his availability.

headline: Goedert (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Rams.
story: With Goedert set to miss another game while recovering from the sprained MCL in his right knee and DeVonta Smith set to miss due to a hamstring injury, Philadelphia will need to lean heavily on Dontayvion Wicks and first-round rookie Makai Lemon to key the passing game. Goedert has yet to practice since suffering his injury in Week 2 against the Titans and remains week-to-week.

headline: Goedert (knee) officially didn't practice Thursday.
story: Goedert has yet to practice since emerging from Week 2 with an MCL sprain in his right knee, and Friday's injury report may seal his fate for a second straight game after sitting out Monday's loss at Chicago. During that contest, the breakdown of offensive snaps among the Eagles' active tight ends was Johnny Mundt's 26 (of 50), followed by Zach Ertz's 19 and E.J. Jenkins' 13.

headline: Goedert (knee) isn't present for the start of practice Thursday, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: Goedert looks to be on his way to a second consecutive practice absence to kick off Week 4 prep. After sitting out Monday's loss to the Bears due to a sprained MCL in his right knee, Goedert is fighting an uphill battle to return Sunday against the Rams. If Goedert remains sidelined, Zach Ertz would have a chance to step up as the top pass catcher in an Eagles tight end room that was paced in snaps by Johnny Mundt on Monday.

headline: Goedert (knee) didn't take part in Wednesday's walkthrough.
story: Goedert already has missed one game due to an MCL sprain in his right knee and likely will continue to trend toward absences in future weeks until he returns to the practice field in some capacity. In Monday's loss at Chicago, Johnny Mundt started in place of Goedert and logged 26 of 50 offensive snaps, which was followed by Zach Ertz's 19 and E.J. Jenkins' 13. A similar breakdown of TE reps is likely between the trio until Goedert is back in the lineup.

headline: Lemon caught five of six targets for 51 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's 39-38 win over the Cowboys.
story: The Eagles were down 28-10 at the half and watched Saquon Barkley (neck) and Dallas Goedert (shoulder) exit early, leaving Joe Milton with limited tools at his disposal to put together a comeback. DeVonta Smith saw most of the target volume, but Lemon came up big when it counted, connecting with Milton on a 24-yard TD that brought Philly to within two points with about two minutes left. While a two-point conversion attempt to tie the game failed, the stage was set for a game-winning 59-yard field goal by Jake Elliott in the dying seconds. Lemon has topped 50 yards in four of the last five games, producing a 25-249-2 line on 35 targets over that stretch, and the rookie's role could continue to grow in Week 13 against the Cardinals.

headline: Eagles inch closer with late TD, but fail on 2-point conversion
story: Eagles inch closer with late TD, but fail on 2-point conversion

headline: Lemon caught one of three targets for three yards in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.
story: Lemon turned three targets into just three yards while DeVonta Smith (hamstring) paced the Eagles with 12 targets in the latter's return. In five games playing alongside Smith, Lemon has just 11 catches for 60 yards. Opportunities should be available against Dallas' porous secondary on Thanksgiving, but it remains to be seen if the unproven QB-WR combo of Joe Milton and Lemon can capitalize on that favorable matchup.

headline: Lemon will operate as the Eagles' WR2 against the Steelers on Sunday due to the return of DeVonta Smith (hamstring).
story: Smith has missed five of the Eagles' last six games (and each of the last three contests) due to a hamstring injury, but the veteran wide receiver does not carry an injury designation heading into the weekend. Lemon has been the team's WR1 in Smith's absence, but the former still will be heavily involved in the offensive game plan given that Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) has been ruled out for a fourth consecutive game. Joe Milton is getting the start at quarterback for a second straight contest, and the Eagles are facing a Steelers defense that ranks 30th in the NFL in receiving yards allowed per game (260.6). Over his last five outings, Lemon has put together a 27-247-1 line on 39 targets.

headline: Lemon caught six of nine targets for 61 yards in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
story: Lemon showed a nice rapport with QB Joe Milton in Milton's first NFL start, as the rookie first-round pick led the Eagles in catches, receiving yards and targets. Lemon has operated as Philadelphia's de facto No. 1 WR while DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) have both missed the past three games, but the Eagles could get at least one of their top two wideouts back in Week 11 against the Steelers following a Week 10 bye.

headline: Lemon and Darius Cooper profile as the top wide receivers for QB Joe Milton's first start in an Eagles uniform Sunday against the Giants, per PhiladelphiaEagles.com.
story: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) both are out for a third straight game. Lemon led the team in targets the past two weeks, putting up receiving lines of 7-67-1 and 6-57-0 against the Cowboys and Commanders, respectively. He'll likely be a focal point of the passing game again, though Milton may be more inclined to look downfield toward Cooper or Hollywod Brown in situations where Tanner McKee would throw a shorter pass to Lemon or a TE/RB.

headline: Lemon caught six of nine targets for 57 yards in Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
story: Lemon has stepped up as Philadelphia's de facto No. 1 receiver in the ongoing absences of DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). After setting career highs across the board with seven catches for 67 yards and his first NFL touchdown on eight targets in Week 7 against the Cowboys, Lemon led the Eagles in catches, receiving yards and targets Sunday night. The rookie 20th overall pick is building momentum ahead of a Week 9 home game against the Giants, but his target share would likely drop if Smith gains clearance to return.

headline: Lemon will be the Eagles' top wide receiver for a second consecutive game Sunday at Washington due to the absences of both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle).
story: Smith and Wicks have both been held out of practice for the last two weeks while tending to their respective injuries, and they'll both observe Sunday night's NFC East tilt from the sidelines. The Eagles offense has struggled with Tanner McKee under center in place of Jalen Hurts (calf, IR), although Lemon still put together his best game of the season against the Cowboys on Monday, when he caught seven of eight targets for 67 yards and a touchdown. Lemon, Darius Cooper and Hollywood Brown will be the Eagles' top wide receivers against a Commanders defense that ranks 29th in the NFL in passing touchdowns allowed (15) and 28th in passing yards allowed per game (254.0)

headline: Lemon brought in seven of eight targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday night.
story: Lemon operated as the Eagles' de facto No. 1 receiver on a night where both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were sidelined, and the rookie met the moment by posting career- and team-high figures across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets. Lemon rounded out his solid performance by recording his first NFL touchdown catch on a four-yard scoring grab with just under six minutes remaining in the third quarter. Lemon could have another opportunity to spearhead the air attack in a Week 8 road matchup against the Commanders on Sunday night, as both Smith and Wicks may be hard-pressed to get healthy enough to suit up for that contest.

headline: Lemon caught three of six targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 25-14 loss to the Panthers.
story: The rookie wideout briefly exited Week 6 with an undisclosed injury but quickly returned and ended up running a team-high 45 routes on Tanner McKee's 49 dropbcks. It still didn't result in much production, as Lemon's six targets were a distant third on the team. The first-round wide receiver has just 18 catches for 127 yards and no touchdowns on 28 targets through six games. He can't be trusted as a fantasy starter headed into next Monday night's game against the Cowboys.

headline: Lemon (undisclosed) returned to Sunday's contest against the Panthers.
story: Lemon visited the sideline tent in the third quarter but was able to reenter the game in the fourth. With Dontayvion Wicks (undisclosed) leaving the game in the final period, Lemon and DeVonta Smith figure to serve as the top WRs available to fill-in QB Tanner McKee the rest of the way.

headline: Lemon entered the medical tent during the third quarter of Sunday's game against the Panthers due to an unspecified injury.
story: The rookie wide receiver had recorded two catches for six yards on five targets prior to checking into the tent. His status for the remainder of the contest is uncertain.

headline: Lemon caught five of seven targets for 43 yards during Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
story: Lemon was able to set new career highs in receptions and receiving yards Sunday, finishing second on the team in targets behind fellow wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks (eight). The rookie is slowly coming into his own with Philadelphia, and he's had an opportunity to operate in a more prominent role with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) sidelined for the last two games. Lemon has now caught 15 of 22 targets for 108 yards over the first five contests of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Lemon caught three of six targets for 27 yards during Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams.
story: Lemon had a chance to step into a more prominent role on offense in the absence of DeVonta Smith (hamstring), but he didn't really see an increase in production. The wide receiver's six targets are a new career high, but he now has registered three or fewer catches in all four games this season while never exceeding 30 receiving yards. Quarterback Jalen Hurts recorded only 93 total passing yards Sunday, so he'll have to be better for Lemon to see an increase in production in Week 5 versus Jacksonville.

headline: Lemon and Dontayvion Wicks will both operate in larger roles against the Rams on Sunday due to the absence of DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Chris McPherson of the Eagles' official site reports.
story: Lemon, a rookie first-rounder, has seen his receiving yards steadily increase over the first three games of the regular season, and with Smith sidelined for at least one week, the former will have the opportunity to establish himself as a go-to target in the passing game for Jalen Hurts. The Rams will be without starting outside cornerback Jaylen Watson (shoulder), so whomever Los Angeles rolls out as a replacement could be a target that Lemon and the Eagles offense exploits.

headline: Lemon recorded three receptions for 29 yards on four targets in Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears.
story: After taking the field for north of 60 percent of the snaps in both of the Eagles' first two contests, Lemon wasn't a major beneficiary of the absence of tight end Dallas Goedert (knee). Even though the Eagles leaned more heavily on three-wide formations, Lemon saw only a slight uptick in playing time Monday, logging 35 of 50 snaps (70 percent). The rookie first-round pick appears to be little more than a tertiary option in the passing game at this stage of his career, as he's thus far been held to seven catches for 38 yards on nine targets through his first three NFL games.

headline: Shipley carried the ball 10 times for 46 yards and failed to catch his only target in Thursday's 39-38 win over the Cowboys.
story: Saquon Barkley (neck) exited the game early with a stinger, leaving the backfield in the hands of Shipley. The Eagles had to abandon the run game after halftime, however, limiting his usage as Joe Milton engineered an incredible comeback with his arm and legs. Barkley spent most of his time on the sideline trying to talk the coaching and training staffs into letting him back on the field, suggesting his absence was just precautionary, but if he misses additional action, Shipley could be in line for a much bigger workload in Week 13 against the Cardinals.

headline: Shipley (illness/foot) doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
story: Despite being listed as a limited participant throughout the week, Shipley made enough improvement in his recovery from an illness and his lingering plantar fascia injury to get the green light to play Thanksgiving Day. Shipley is expected to contribute as a kickoff returner along with serving as the top backup out of the backfield to Saquon Barkley. In his return from a four-game stint on injured reserve during last week's win over the Steelers, Shipley carried four times for nine yards while playing 19 of 53 snaps on offense.

headline: Shipley (foot/illness) was a limited participant at the Eagles' walkthrough practice Tuesday.
story: Shipley remained limited for a second day in a row while dealing with an illness and a foot injury. The running back returned to action in Week 11 after missing four games with a foot injury, and the illness is likely the more substantial concern at the moment. Shipley will have one more chance to be a full participant at Wednesday's final session ahead of Thursday's matchup with the Cowboys.

headline: Shipley (foot/illness) was estimated as a limited participant on Monday's injury report.
story: Shipley returned Sunday from a four-game absence due to a foot injury, and he finished that contest with four carries for nine yards and returned three kickoffs for 75 yards. He's still working through that foot issue, but he's now battling an illness, so his listed activity level over the next two days will be worth monitoring ahead of the Eagles' Thanksgiving Day contest against the Cowboys in Dallas. Shipley could operate in an elevated role on offense Thursday depending on the status of Saquon Barkley (neck/illness).

headline: Shipley (foot) is active for Sunday's game against Pittsburgh.
story: Shipley was activated from injured reserve Saturday, and the third-year running back has been officially cleared to return from a four-game absence due to a partial plantar fascia tear that he sustained in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Shipley and Jaydon Blue will operate as the Eagles' rotational running backs behind Saquon Barkley for Sunday's game against a Steelers defense that ranks third in the NFL in rushing yards allowed per game (83.2).

headline: The Eagles activated Shipley (foot) from injured reserve Saturday, but he remains questionable for Sunday's game against the Steelers.
story: Shipley logged an LP/LP/DNP practice regimen during Week 11 prep, with Friday's absence attributed to an illness. He appears to be closing in on his first game action since Week 5, when he suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia, but his status for Sunday's matchup won't be confirmed until about 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff. Assuming Shipley returns to action this weekend, he may serve as the direct backup to top RB Saquon Barkley.

headline: Shipley (foot/illness) didn't practice Friday and is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest versus the Steelers.
story: Since the Eagles designated Shipley to return from injured reserve Monday, he managed back-to-back limited practices to begin Week 11 prep before Friday's absence, which seemingly can be attributed to an illness. The team will need to activate Shipley from IR by Saturday afternoon for him to have a chance to play Sunday. If he gets the all clear, Shipley will be joining a backfield that's still led by Saquon Barkley, with Jaydon Blue and potentially practice-squad member Elijah Mitchell also available.

headline: Shipley (foot) remained limited in practice Thursday.
story: Shipley is still on injured reserve but had his 21-day practice window opened this week. With Saquon Barkley healthy right now, Shipley has minimal fantasy appeal in a broken Philadelphia offense that is near the bottom of the league in most categories over the last month.

headline: Shipley (foot) was a limited practice participant Wednesday.
story: Shipley sustained a partial tear of his plantar fascia in Week 5 against the Jaguars in London, resulting in an IR stint. He missed the last four games before a Week 10 bye before the Eagles designated him for return Monday. No. 1 RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) practiced fully Wednesday, so if Shipley gains clearance to play Sunday versus the Steelers, it'll likely be in a complementary role out of the backfield.

headline: The Eagles opened Shipley's (foot) 21-day practice window Monday.
story: Shipley landed on IR after being diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia in the wake of Week 5 action, but he now has a chance to play as soon as Sunday against the Steelers. Meanwhile, fellow RB Tank Bigsby (abdomen) -- who hasn't played since Week 4 -- remains on IR, and the Eagles signed Jaydon Blue to their practice squad Monday. If Shipley is able to suit up this weekend, he'll reclaim a backup role behind Saquon Barkley that isn't likely to result in much volume for the 2024 fourth-rounder.

headline: The Eagles placed Shipley (foot) on injured reserve Friday.
story: After being diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia earlier this week, Shipley was slated for a multi-week absence, and he now will miss at least the next four games while on IR. He'll join Tank Bigsby (abdomen) on the list, and with Saquon Barkley currently tending to a lingering hamstring injury, the Eagles have just two healthy RBs (Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele) on the active roster. Shipley's next chance for game action is Sunday, Nov. 22 against the Steelers.

headline: Shipley (foot) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Considering Shipley suffered a partial tear of his plantar fascia during this past Sunday's defeat to the Jaguars in London and is facing a multi-week absence, his lack of practice reps so far this week is expected. With No. 1 RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) also not practicing Wednesday or Thursday, the Eagles may be preparing to deploy the duo of Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele out of their backfield Sunday against the Panthers.

headline: Shipley (foot) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: It's not much of a surprise to see a DNP next to Shipley's name on the Eagles' first injury report of Week 6 prep given that the third-year running back was diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia following the team's 19-17 Week 5 loss to the Jaguars in London. Shipley is facing a multi-week absence, and with Saquon Barkley (hamstring) also idle for Wednesday's session, the Eagles may have to turn to Dameon Pierce to lead the backfield against the Panthers on Sunday.

headline: Shipley (foot) was diagnosed with a partial tear of his plantar fascia after exiting Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars in London and could be sidelined multiple weeks, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Called upon to make his second career start with Saquon Barkley (hamstring) out for Week 5 and with Tank Bigsby (core) on injured reserve, Shipley played just 13 snaps and accounted for 13 yards and a touchdown on six touches (five carries, one reception) before leaving the game in the second quarter. After his foot injury was revealed to be a plantar fascia tear, Shipley now appears likely to be sidelined for at least next Sunday's game versus Carolina. Barkley is being viewed as week-to-week, and if both he and Shipley end up missing more time, the Eagles could be left with Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele as well as practice-squad member Jaydon Blue as their backfield options for Week 6.

headline: The Eagles ruled out Shipley (foot) for the remainder of Sunday's game versus the Jaguars in London.
story: With Saquon Barkley (hamstring) ruled out for Week 5 and Tank Bigsby (core) landing on injured reserve, Shipley looked poised to handle a featured role out of the Philadelphia backfield. However, Shipley's day came to an end late in the second quarter, when he sustained a foot injury that will ultimately keep him from returning. The Eagles will finish out the contest with Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele as their main options out of the backfield. Shipley finished with five carries for six yards and a touchdown to go with a seven-yard reception on two targets.

headline: Shipley is questionable to return to Sunday's game versus the Jaguars in London due to a foot injury.
story: Shipley was dinged up after a carry in the second quarter and visited the medical tent on the Eagles sideline before going to the locker room. He was getting most of the backfield reps in place of an absent Saquon Barkley (hamstring) before his departure, and if Shipley is unable to re-enter Sunday's contest, the Eagles backfield likely will be paced by Dameon Pierce. Carson Steele is also on hand for reps.

headline: Shipley is slated to lead the Eagles backfield against the Jaguars in Week 5 due to the absences of both Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and Tank Bigsby (abdomen, IR), Chris McPherson of the Eagles' official site reports.
story: Barkley and Bigsby both sustained injuries during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams, and with both running backs sidelined for Week 5, the Eagles may turn to Shipley to handle RB1 duties while Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele provide backfield depth. Shipley is averaging 3.4 yards per carry though four games this season, and his work will be cut out for him against a Jaguars defense that allows the third-fewest rushing yards per game in the NFL (74.3).

headline: Shipley rushed six times for 23 yards and didn't catch his only target in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams. He also returned three kickoffs for 65 yards.
story: Shipley was the last man standing in Philadelphia's backfield after Saquon Barkley (hamstring) exited in the first quarter and Tank Bigsby (undisclosed) left in the fourth quarter. Bigsby had been working ahead of Shipley after Barkley's exit, but if neither of Philadelphia's top two running backs are available in Week 5, Shipley could take on the lead role against the Jaguars in London.

headline: Shipley (foot) practiced in full on Friday and does not carry an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Rams.
story: Shipley has been battling a foot injury. He didn't practice Wednesday and was limited Thursday. However, after logging a full session Friday, the 24-year-old is good to go for the Week 4 meeting with Los Angeles. Shipley is second on the team in snaps at the running back position behind Saquon Barkley, though he hasn't done much, amassing 28 yards on nine carries throughout the first three weeks of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Shipley (foot) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Shipley ended Week 3 prep with back-to-back limited practices and had no injury designation heading into the Eagles' 27-7 loss to the Bears on Monday Night Football. Shipley's downgrade to a non-participant in Wednesday's session could be precautionary or may be a sign the running back aggravated the issue during Monday's game.

headline: Milton completed 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards and three touchdowns with one interception in Thursday's 39-38 win over the Cowboys. He added 15 yards and a TD on three carries.
story: Facing the team who put him on the practice squad to begin the season before he got signed by the Eagles, Milton used his mobility to keep plays alive and find receivers deep against an inept Cowboys secondary. The 26-year-old QB connected with DeVonta Smith for TDs of 50 yards in the second quarter and 45 yards in the third, before a big fourth quarter in which Milton ran in a 15-yard score of his own and then found Makai Lemon for a 15-yard strike as Philly erased a 38-24 deficit. Milton's 331 passing yards weren't just a career high, they were more than he produced in his first two starts this season combined. He'll remain under center against another struggling defense as he faces the Cardinals in Week 13.

headline: Milton completed 11 of 21 passes for 141 yards while rushing five times for seven yards in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.
story: Milton has thrown for just 310 yards without a touchdown pass or interception through two starts. He rushed for just seven yards Sunday after notching 64 rushing yards against the Giants in his first start with the Eagles, but Milton avoided mistakes as the Eagles rode their defense and Saquon Barkley's legs to their third win of the season. Twelve of Milton's 21 passes were directed to DeVonta Smith (hamstring) in their first game together. Milton is poised to start on Thanksgiving against the Cowboys, with whom he appeared in four games last season. He was on Dallas' practice squad prior to signing with the Eagles in October.

headline: Head coach Nick Sirianni confirmed that Milton will remain the Eagles' starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Steelers, according to NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano.
story: While starting in his team debut Week 9 against the Giants, Milton was unable to bring an end to the Eagles' lengthy losing streak, but the third-year quarterback showed enough positives to retain the starting gig coming out of a Week 10 bye. Milton put an intriguing dual-threat skill set on display with 64 yards on nine carries to go with 169 passing yards on 34 attempts in the 19-11 loss to New York, with the rushing output in particular perhaps making him worth a look in superflex leagues or leagues that start two quarterbacks. He lost a fumble and took seven sacks in the loss to the Giants, so Milton may need to show that he can avoid negative plays in Week 11 in order to guarantee himself additional starts.

headline: Milton completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. He also rushed nine times for 64 yards, ran in a two-point conversion and lost a fumble.
story: The big-armed Milton wasn't effective as a passer while working with a depleted receiving corps that was missing DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), but Milton showcased strong mobility and led the Eagles in rushing yards while RBs Saquon Barkley and Elijah Mitchell combined for just 28 rushing yards on 16 carries. The 2024 sixth-round pick of the Patriots played nearly the full game in the 2024 regular-season finale against the Bills and got into four games with Dallas during the 2025 campaign, but this was Milton's first regular-season NFL start. Philadelphia's Week 10 bye will provide an opportunity to evaluate a QB room consisting of Milton, the recently benched Tanner McKee and rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton. Whichever QB gets the starting nod in Week 11 against the Steelers would benefit from the potential return of Smith or Wicks after the bye.

headline: Milton is set to be the Eagles' starting quarterback Sunday against the Giants, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Philadelphia signed Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad Oct. 16, and less than a month later, he's getting the call after the Tanner McKee experience so far has resulted in three consecutive losses. In five appearances (no starts) between New England and Dallas in his career, Milton has competed 37 of 53 passes for 424 yards, two touchdowns and two interceptions while rushing 15 times for 66 yards and one TD and losing both of his fumbles.

headline: Milton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Eagles' emergency third quarterback against the Panthers on Sunday.
story: The Eagles signed Milton off the practice squad to the active roster Friday following the news that Jalen Hurts would be out indefinitely due to a superficial blood clot in his calf, with the latter being placed on injured reserve Saturday. The Eagles will start Tanner McKee on Sunday while rookie fifth-rounder Cole Payton serves as the backup. As the emergency QB3, Milton is prohibited from playing against Carolina unless both McKee and Payton leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: The Eagles are signing Milton off the Cowboys' practice squad, NFL reporter Jordan Schultz reports.
story: With Jalen Hurts recovering from a blood clot on his calf, the Eagles are set to start Tanner McKee this Sunday against the Panthers. Should Hurts miss additional time, Milton could eventually become an option to make starts, though he'll likely be focused on learning the offense and otherwise acclimating for the next few weeks.

headline: Hall (wrist) is questionable to return to the Eagles' matchup against the Cowboys on Sunday.
story: Hall exited the game in the second half, casting doubt on his availability for the remainder of the contest. Ty Robinson could see an uptick in playing time if Hall ends up being unable to return.

headline: Epps (foot) has been ruled out for the remainder of Philadelphia's matchup versus the Cowboys on Thursday, Mike Kaye of ESPN.com reports.
story: Epps is done for the day after suffering a foot injury in the third quarter. In his absence, Kenny Moore has taken over at safety.

headline: Epps (groin) practiced fully Thursday.
story: Epps was held out of Weeks 4 and 5 due to a groin injury, but with a full practice under his belt, he's poised to regain his standing as the Eagles' starting strong safety Sunday against the Panthers. Prior to the recent absence, he tallied 14 tackles in the first three games of the campaign.

headline: Epps (groin) was a limited participant at the Eagles' practice Wednesday.
story: Epps has been forced to miss the team's last two contests while nursing a groin injury, but his return to practice Wednesday is a positive turn of events. The safety will have two more opportunities to log a full practice ahead of Sunday's game against Carolina.

headline: Epps (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.
story: Epps will miss a second consecutive game due to a groin injury. His next chance to play is Week 6 against the Panthers on Sunday, Oct. 18, though he would need to practice in at least a limited capacity to have a realistic shot at returning against Carolina. Michael Carter should once again start next to Andrew Mukuba at safety in Epps' absence.

headline: Epps (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
story: Epps didn't play in Sunday's loss to the Rams. If that trend continues in Week 5 versus Jacksonville, Michael Carter should remain in line to see an uptick in defensive snaps.

headline: Epps (groin) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Rams.
story: Epps practiced in a limited capacity Thursday but was unavailable for Friday's session. With Epps ruled out, Michael Carter is in line for more work.

headline: Barkley suffered a stinger during Thursday's game in Dallas.
story: This marks Barkley's second diagnosed stinger of the campaign, but on the previous occasion in Week 2 against the Titans, he was able to check back in to the contest. The Eagles may opt to exercise caution with Barkley, however, because he tended to a neck issue on a short week following this past Sunday's win against the Steelers.

headline: The Eagles listed Barkley (neck/illness) as a full participant in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.
story: Though Tuesday's injury report was merely an estimate, Barkley would have been able to take every rep had the Eagles held a traditional practice session. Barkley emerged from this past Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers with a neck injury and an illness, but neither health concern looks like it will prevent him from playing Thursday in Dallas.

headline: Barkley was listed as a limited participant on Monday's estimated practice report due to a neck injury and an illness.
story: Barkley appeared to be nursing a left arm injury in the aftermath of Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers, but it was instead two different health concerns that resulted in him being included on the Eagles' first Week 12 injury report. The Eagles are facing a quick turnaround this week with a Thursday matchup against the Cowboys, so Barkley could be in line for only light activity over the next two days as the team aims to keep him as fresh as possible for that contest. Head coach Nick Sirianni hasn't yet offered any indication that Barkley is in jeopardy of sitting out Thanksgiving Day.

headline: Barkley (left arm) said after Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers that he believes he'll play in Thursday's game at Dallas, Johnny McGonigal of PennLive.com reports.
story: Barkley didn't log a touch after the 8:02 mark of the fourth quarter after he had an apparent left arm injury examined by team trainers, according to Olivia Reiner of The Philadelphia Inquirer. While Barkley wouldn't elaborate on the issue to McGonigal, the running back seemed optimistic about his chances to suit up in Week 12. Barkley finished Sunday's matchup with 17 carries for 75 yards and one touchdown and wasn't targeted by QB Joe Milton. Monday's injury report may provide further clarity on Barkley's situation.

headline: Barkley rushed 17 times for 75 yards and a touchdown but wasn't targeted in Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers.
story: Barkley benefited from a week off to heal his nagging hamstring and back injuries during Philadelphia's Week 10 bye. The 29-year-old RB showed off his renewed burst on a 38-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Barkley has scored in four consecutive games, but Sunday's touchdown run alone eclipsed Barkley's rushing yard totals from each of the previous two games. He'll try to extend his touchdown streak Thursday against the struggling Dallas defense, assuming Barkley suits up after getting examined by trainers on the sideline with his helmet off in the fourth quarter of Sunday's win.

headline: Is Saquon Barkley back to must-start status in fantasy?
story: Is Saquon Barkley back to must-start status in fantasy?

headline: Barkley (hamstring) told EJ Smith of PHLY Sports on Friday that he "feels better physically" after the team's Week 10 bye, and the running back doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the Steelers.
story: Barkley was able to put together a full week of drills during Week 11 prep, and while his current state is positive, he added that the time off isn't a "magic pill," indicating that he still has some residual effects from the hamstring injury that has lingered since he picked it up in Week 4.
