In his last appearance in Week 9 against the Giants, he handled a 58 percent snap share and turned his 13 carries into 22 yards and one touchdown. As for the rest of the Eagles backfield, Jaydon Blue is the only other option on the active roster, Elijah Mitchell is a candidate to be elevated from the practice squad, and Will Shipley (foot) may be activated from injured reserve Saturday.

headline: Barkley rushed 13 times for 22 yards and a touchdown while failing to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants.
story: Barkley has mustered a meager 2.0 yards per carry over the past two games while playing through hamstring and back injuries, but he also has both of Philadelphia's touchdowns over that span, including a three-yard rushing score in the second quarter Sunday. It has been a slog offensively for the Eagles, who have tried first Tanner McKee and now Joe Milton under center since losing starting QB Jalen Hurts (IR, calf) likely for the season while also playing without top two wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). It's fair to wonder if Barkley will eventually be shut down as well to get a chance to heal as the 2-7 Eagles drop out of contention, but at least a Week 10 bye will offer him a respite before Philadelphia's Week 11 home game against the Steelers.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game against the Giants.
story: After sitting out Wednesday's session due to lingering hamstring and back injuries, Barkley ended Week 9 prep with back-to-back limited practices, which was enough to get the all-clear ahead of Sunday. He gutted out a 32 percent snap share this past Sunday in Washington en route to 14 touches for 54 yards from scrimmage and one rushing TD while splitting the backfield with Elijah Mitchell (15 touches for 37 total yards).

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) is practicing again Friday, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: After logging a limited practice Thursday, Barkley was back on the field again Friday as he continues to manage hamstring and back issues ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants. His official participation level and final injury designation will provide the clearest read on his Week 9 availability.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
story: Barkley followed up Wednesday's DNP with some activity one day later as he deals with lingering hamstring and back injuries. Friday's practice report will determine if he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game against the Giants. While playing through those health concerns this past Sunday in Washington, Barkley logged a 32 percent snap share and racked up 14 touches for 54 yards from scrimmage and one rushing TD.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) is participating in Thursday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: After sitting out Wednesday's practice due to existing hamstring and back injuries, Barkley is returning to drills one day later, which is one day earlier than a week ago. He thus appears to be a bit healthier this time around, but his activity level will become known once the Eagles post their second Week 9 practice report Thursday.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) officially didn't practice Wednesday.
story: Barkley's DNP to begin Week 9 prep was forecast by his lack of presence during the open portion of Wednesday's session. He continues to deal with the hamstring and back injuries that bothered him last week, but he still was able to play this past Sunday at Washington, log a 32 percent snap share and turn 14 touches into 54 yards from scrimmage and one TD. If he follows a similar practice regimen as last week, Barkley also will sit out Thursday before returning as a limited participant Friday.

headline: Barkley wasn't present for the media-access portion of Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: Barkley may still be tending to the hamstring and back issues that he impacted his practice reps last week, but Wednesday's injury report will reveal if he indeed was a non-participant and also the reason for his absence. Jaydon Blue is the only healthy RB on the Eagles' active roster, though practice-squad member Elijah Mitchell tallied 11 carries for 34 yards and four catches (on six targets) for three yards while splitting the backfield with Barkley this past Sunday at Washington.

headline: Barkley said after Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders that he has received assurances from the Eagles front office that he will remain with the team beyond the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports. "The whole time my mindset was, we have a little issue going on right now and I feel like I'm the type of player and the type of leader that can help us get out of it," Barkley said. "And I want to be one of the reasons why we fix it."
story: After dropping their sixth straight game Sunday, the Eagles now sit at 2-6 on the season and could be motivated to explore moving veteran players for draft capital ahead of the deadline. Barkley -- who is under contract through 2028 -- apparently won't be among the pieces the Eagles consider moving, as the team is counting on re-emerging as a playoff contender next season rather than embracing a long-term rebuilding effort. Though he'll be suiting up for a Week 9 matchup with the division-leading Giants, Barkley could continue to have his playing time managed while he gets ramped back up from hamstring and back injuries. He played just 22 of the Eagles' 68 offensive snaps in the loss to Washington, finishing with 13 carries for 30 yards and a touchdown and a 24-yard reception on his lone target.

headline: Barkley rushed 13 times for 30 yards and a touchdown while catching his only target for 24 yards in Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders.
story: Barkley got to the edge to score a three-yard rushing touchdown out of the wildcat formation and give the Eagles a 10-0 first-quarter lead, but it was all Washington after that. He came into the game averaging 5.7 yards per carry but mustered only 2.3 YPC in this one while playing at less than full health. Barkley didn't sit down when on the sideline in an effort to stay loose and mitigate the effects of the back injury he sustained in Week 7 against Dallas while compensating for a hamstring injury that kept him out of the previous two games. The banged-up Barkley, who didn't notch a touch in the fourth quarter, likely will try to gut it out again in Week 9 against the NFC East-leading Giants.

headline: The Eagles aren't expected to move Barkley ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Philadelphia's roster has been ravaged by injuries this season, and Barkley himself hasn't avoided health concerns, with two contests where he's played above 70 percent of snaps, three appearances in which he made early exits and two missed games to date. He thus has been capped to just 49 touches for 261 yards from scrimmage and one rushing touchdown, but general manager Howie Roseman won't consider trading Barkley ahead of the NFL's trade deadline. As for Barkley's Week 8 prospects, he doesn't have a designation for Sunday night's game at Washington and has only Jaydon Blue and Elijah Mitchell available behind him, so a workhorse role could be in the cards.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Washington.
story: After missing the first two practices of Week 8 prep, Barkley was able to practice in a limited capacity Friday as he deals with a lingering hamstring injury and a new back issue that he sustained Monday against the Cowboys. Earlier Friday, he told Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com, "I would hope so," when asked if he's playing Sunday. With no designation to speak of on the final practice report, Barkley is in the clear ahead of the weekend, and he likely will retain a workhorse role due to the otherwise banged-up nature of the Eagles backfield.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) said Friday that he hopes to play in Sunday night's game against the Commanders, Jimmy Kempski of PhillyVoice.com reports.
story: After returning to practice Friday following absences to begin the week, Barkley at least appears to have a chance to suit up Sunday night. Expect Barkley to get a questionable designation, so fantasy players will need to have a backup plan in place. Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue are waiver-wire options for managers looking for a one-for-one replacement.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) is practicing Friday, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: After sitting out Wednesday and Thursday's practices, Barkley's return to the field Friday at least gives him a chance to suit up Sunday night against the Commanders. His official participation level and any game designation will provide more clarity on his status heading into the weekend. Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue are next in line for snaps and carries for the Eagles if Barkley is unable to play.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) didn't practice Thursday.
story: Barkley has yet to practice this week due to dueling hamstring and back issues, the latter of which knocked him out of Monday's loss to the Cowboys. He relayed to Tim McManus of ESPN.com afterward that he isn't concerned about the most recent injury, but he now has just one more chance to get back on the practice field ahead of Sunday's game at Washington. With all of Tank Bigsby (abdomen), Will Shipley (foot) and Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) on IR, Jaydon Blue currently is the only healthy RB on the Eagles' active roster, though the team also used practice squad member Elijah Mitchell in Monday's loss to the Cowboys.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) wasn't spotted warming up at Thursday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: After being deemed a non-participant in Wednesday's walkthrough, Barkley now appears absent again at the start of Thursday's session. His official participation level will be confirmed by Philadelphia's injury report later Thursday, but Barkley seems to be trending in the wrong direction after sustaining what he described as a compensatory back injury during Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys, which marked his return from a two-game absence. Jaydon Blue is the top healthy alternative on the Eagles' active roster behind Barkley heading into Sunday night's game against the Commanders, with Elijah Mitchell a candidate to be elevated from the team's practice squad ahead of Week 8 action.

headline: Barkley (hamstring/back) was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday's walkthrough.
story: The Eagles are listing Barkley's previous hamstring injury and the back issue that he picked up during Monday's loss to the Cowboys as the reasons for Wednesday's absence. He'll have two more chances to mix into drills this week, but even if he isn't able to, he mentioned of the aforementioned contest that his "hamstring came out great" and that he isn't worried about the new health concern, per Tim McManus of ESPN.com. Ultimately, Friday's injury report will reveal Barkley's odds to suit up Sunday at Washington.

headline: Barkley said after Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys that his "hamstring came out great," and noted that the back issue that kept him out for the entire fourth quarter isn't anything that he expects to prevent him from playing Sunday against the Commanders, Tim McManus of ESPN.com reports.
story: While suiting up for the first time since Week 4 after missing the Eagles' previous two games due to a hamstring strain, Barkley took the field for just 10 snaps on the night but was impactful in his limited playing time. He touched the ball on nine of those snaps, carrying seven times for 62 yards and a touchdown to go with two receptions for nine yards on two targets. Heading into the game, the Eagles had deliberately planned to manage Barkley's workload to some extent, but he ended up seeing fewer snaps than anticipated after his back locked up on him following a 29-yard run in the first quarter. He didn't end up taking any snaps after the third quarter, with the Eagles leaning exclusively on Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) and Elijah Mitchell out of the backfield over the final 15 minutes. Fortunately for Barkley, the back issue doesn't seem to be a major concern, but his activity in practice this week will warrant monitoring as the Eagles assess his availability for Sunday's contest.

headline: Barkley said after Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys that he sustained a compensatory back injury, which he tried to play through after tweaking his injured hamstring on his first run of the game, EJ Smith of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: Coming into Monday, Barkley had been listed as questionable after missing the Eagles' previous two games due to a hamstring strain, but he tried to tough it out and give the offense a much-needed boost out of the backfield. He did just that on the team's first drive, gaining 12 yards on a reception on the first play and immediately following with a 29-yard run. Barkley appeared to pull up a bit lame on the latter play, but he still delivered an eight-yard rushing touchdown less than two minutes later. However, the star running back was used only intermittently for the remainder of the contest, and he sat out the entire fourth quarter while backup Dameon Pierce finished with 14 carries (for 47 yards and a touchdown) to Barkley's seven. Smith relayed that Barkley was on a "pitch count" ahead of Monday's game, so the Eagles may have been motivated to hold him out for the rest of the contest once the back issue cropped up. The Eagles will face a quick turnaround with a Week 8 matchup Sunday versus the Commanders, so it wouldn't be surprising if Barkley's practice activity was affected leading up to that contest.

headline: Barkley is questionable to return to Monday's game against the Cowboys due to a back injury.
story: Barkley entered Monday's contest managing a hamstring injury but was ultimately able to suit up. The star running back looked hobbled throughout much of the game but was able to tally 62 yards and a touchdown on just seven carries along with two catches on two targets for nine yards before being deemed questionable to return early in the fourth period. The Eagles indicated that Barkley is dealing with a back issue when announcing his 'questionable' tag, so it's unclear if the hamstring is also still bothering him.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) is listed as active Monday against the Cowboys.
story: Barkley is available to power the Eagles' backfield for the first time since Week 4, ending a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Considering he practiced fully Saturday, he may be ready to operate as a workhorse as he did in his two healthy games (Weeks 1 and 3) this season. In those games, Barkley combined for 32 touches for 160 yards from scrimmage and no TDs.

headline: Barkley (hamstring), who is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Cowboys, is "trending toward playing," Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Though No. 1 wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for the Week 7 contest, the Eagles are expected to get one of their other top playmakers in Barkley back in action following a two-game absence. Barkley participated in practice throughout the week, turning in limited sessions Thursday and Friday before upgrading to full activity Saturday. Assuming his hamstring checks out fine while warming up Monday, Barkley's availability should be confirmed when the Eagles release their inactive list 90 minutes prior to the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Cowboys.
story: Barkley followed up limited sessions Thursday and Friday with a full practice Saturday, but his status remains up in the air for Week 7 action. He's seeking his first game action since Week 4 as he tends to a lingering hamstring injury, something that'll be confirmed, one way or another, about 90 minutes before Monday's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) was on the field for the start of Saturday's practice, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: Barkley was a limited participant in each of the first two practices of Week 7 prep as the star running back works his way back from a hamstring injury that sidelined him for each of the Eagles' last two games. Saturday's practice report will shed light on Barkley's status ahead of Monday's game against the Cowboys, and a full session would likely be enough for him to avoid an injury designation. His return would result in Dameon Pierce reverting to a rotational role in the backfield.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) was a limited practice participant Friday.
story: Barkley now has logged back-to-back capped practices this week, giving him one more chance to get back to full Saturday, at which point the Eagles may make a ruling on his status for Monday's game against the Cowboys. He's missed the last two games due to a hamstring injury.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) is practicing Friday, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: After practicing in a limited capacity Thursday, Barkley was on the field again Friday as he continues to work back from the hamstring injury that cost him the past two games. His presence at another session keeps him on track for a possible return Monday night against Dallas. Dameon Pierce would then become mostly irrelevant from a fantasy football standpoint.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday.
story: This marks Barkley's first official on-field work since he initially suffered a hamstring injury in Week 4 against the Rams. He consequently sat out Weeks 5 and 6, but his return to drills this week at least gives him a chance to suit up Monday versus the Cowboys. Barkley told Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer on Thursday that he wants to play in Week 7 but still needs to test out his hamstring over the next few days. Ultimately, Saturday's practice report will reveal Barkley's odds to return to action.

headline: Barkley (hamstring) was in uniform for Thursday's practice, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: The Eagles signaled that Barkley was approaching a return to action by moving on from Carson Steele (shoulder, IR) and Jaydon Blue earlier this week. Mike Garafolo of NFL Network then reported Thursday morning that Barkley was expected to practice Thursday with the aim to play Monday against the Cowboys. While Barkley's activity level as he mixes back into drills isn't known yet, he appears to be trending in the right direction for Week 7 action.

headline: DeJean has entered the league's concussion protocol and has been ruled out for the rest of Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
story: DeJean was shaken up on the Eagles' first defensive drive of the first quarter and was taken to the locker room, where medical staff diagnosed the third-year defensive back with a concussion. Michael Carter should see more defensive snaps in the secondary in the absence of DeJean, who will now work through the league's protocol in an effort to be available for Week 13 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: DeJean recorded seven tackles (three solo) during Monday's 38-21 loss versus the Cowboys.
story: DeJean racked up seven-plus tackles for the third time this season in a Week 7 contest that saw Dallas run the ball 38 times. He's on pace for the first 100-tackle season of his career, putting him on the fringe of IDP consideration of some formats ahead of a Week 8 matchup at Washington.

headline: DeJean posted five solo tackles and a pass defense in the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers in Week 6.
story: DeJean has logged at least five tackles in each of the first six games of the regular season and has played every defensive snap in four of those contests. He's up to 39 tackles (23 solo) and five pass defenses (including one interception) on the season, and he's third on the Eagles in combined takcles behind Jihaad Campbell (47) and Zack Baun (42).

headline: DeJean registered five total tackles (three solo) and two passes defensed, including an interception, during Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams.
story: DeJean was able to secure at least five stops for the fourth straight game to open the 2026 campaign, but his biggest moment of the game came as a result of his hands in the second quarter. The 23-year-old jumped in front of a deep ball from quarterback Matthew Stafford for his first interception of the season. DeJean has now compiled 23 total tackles (11 solo) and four passes defensed, including Sunday's interception, over four contests this year.

headline: Payton (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game at Dallas but is available as the Eagles' emergency third quarterback.
story: Payton will only take the field in Week 12 if starter Joe Milton and backup Tanner McKee leave the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Payton (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Eagles' emergency third quarterback against the Steelers on Sunday.
story: As the emergency third quarterback, Payton is not allowed to play Sunday unless both starter Joe Milton and backup Tanner McKee are taken out of the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Payton (coach's decision) is inactive for Monday's game against the Cowboys but will serve as the team's emergency quarterback.
story: Payton will serve as the emergency signal-caller, meaning he won't be able to play unless Tanner McKee and Joe Milton exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Payton is active as the backup to starting quarterback Tanner McKee in Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: A rookie fifth-round pick out of North Dakota State, Payton has yet to make his NFL debut, but he's one step closer to doing so after Jalen Hurts (calf) was placed on injured reserve Saturday. Payton had slotted third or fourth on the depth chart through the first five games of the season, but he'll be dressing as the No. 2 option Sunday while McKee draws his third career NFL start. Since he's set to become a free agent after the season and may not be viewed as the Eagles' long-term plan at the backup quarterback spot, McKee could be in danger of losing his grip on the starting job if he struggles in his extended snaps while Hurts remains out indefinitely. Payton could be someone to keep an eye on if the Eagles decide to give him a look at any point, as he displayed intriguing rushing skills during his collegiate career and gained 45 yards on three carries during his limited preseason action.

headline: The Eagles activated Calcaterra (back) from injured reserve Monday.
story: Calcaterra has been cleared to play Monday night against Dallas, giving Philly another capable tight end behind Dallas Goedert. It's unclear how the playing time will shake out between blocker Johnny Mundt, catch-first rookie Eli Stowers and Calcaterra, but the Eagles could lean into the tight end-heavy sets with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) both ruled out.

headline: Calcaterra, who is on injured reserve due to a back injury, is questionable to suit up Monday versus Dallas.
story: Calcaterra has yet to play this season because of a back injury he suffered during the preseason. Philadelphia opened his 21-day practice window Oct. 14, and the tight end was able to practice in full all three days this week. Since Calcaterra is on IR, he'd need to be activated to the 53-man roster Sunday in order to be eligible to play Monday.

headline: Calcaterra (back) was a full participant at the Eagles' practice Thursday.
story: Calcaterra was able to open the week with a full practice as he remains on injured reserve while recovering from a back injury. The tight end has been sidelined since the beginning of the season, but he could be on track to return to action Monday night against the Cowboys.

headline: The Eagles downgraded Calcaterra (back) to out Saturday for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: Calcaterra remains on injured reserve, though his 21-day practice window was opened earlier in the week. He's nearing a return, though his role is unclear behind Dallas Goedert and potentially even block-first TE Johnny Mundt.

headline: Calcaterra (back) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: The Eagles could significantly bolster their depth at tight end if both Calcaterra and rookie second-rounder Eli Stowers (quadriceps) are activated from injured reserve. If he's cleared to make his 2026 debut Sunday, then Calcaterra would likely slide into the TE2 role behind Dallas Goedert and ahead of Johnny Mundt.

headline: The Eagles opened the 21-day practice window for Calcaterra (back) on Wednesday.
story: Calcaterra has yet to play this season. He will have 21 days to be added to the 53-man roster. If not, Calcaterra will miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Epenesa (back) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against Dallas.
story: Epenesa has been cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a back injury. The veteran linebacker has four tackles (two solo) and one pass defense through four regular-season games and has contributed on both defense and special teams.

headline: Epenesa (back) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: The decision comes as no surprise, given that Epenesa was listed as doubtful for Sunday's contest. He'll miss his first game of the season due to a back injury, and his next opportunity to play is Week 7 against the Cowboys on Monday, Oct. 26.

headline: Epenesa (back) is doubtful for Sunday's game against the Panthers.
story: Epenesa was unable to practice Thursday or Friday due to a back injury, and it looks like he'll miss his first game of the season as a result. With Jalyx Hunt (knee/ankle) sidelined, Arnold Ebiketie would be the lone rotational option at edge rusher if Epenesa is in fact ruled out.

headline: Mondon (ankle) does not carry an injury designation into Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
story: Mondon ended Week 12 prep with back-to-back limited practices, and that was enough for the second-year linebacker to avoid an injury tag ahead of Thanksgiving Day. He's mostly operated on special teams but served in a rotational role on defense in Week 9 against the Giants, and he finished that contest with a season-high five tackles (two solo).

headline: Mondon (ankle) is inactive for Sunday's matchup against Pittsburgh.
story: Mondon was deemed doubtful entering the weekend after not practicing Thursday or Friday following Philadelphia's Week 10 bye. He could have seen more action on defense after Zack Baun (back) landed on IR on Saturday, but Mondon will instead miss his first game of the campaign. Jeremiah Trotter and Jihaad Campbell figure to be the Eagles' starting inside linebackers Sunday.

headline: Ebiketie (oblique) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
story: After his trade to the Bengals fell through two weeks ago, Ebiketie is now dealing with an injury that will sideline him for at least one contest. Jalyx Hunt and A.J. Epenesa should soak up extra snaps off the edge for the Eagles.

headline: Ebiketie (oblique) was estimated as a nonparticipant on the Eagles' injury report Tuesday.
story: It seems like Ebiketie might have suffered the injury during Sunday's game versus the Steelers. Regardless, his availability for Philadelphia's game against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving is now in question. If he's unable to practice Wednesday, his odds of playing Thursday will probably be low.

headline: Ebiketie will remain with the Eagles after his reported trade to the Bengals on Tuesday fell through and won't be completed, according to NFL reporter Jordan Schultz.
story: Earlier Tuesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network relayed that the Eagles agreed to send Ebiketie to the Bengals in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick. The trade wasn't cancelled due to concerns over Ebiketie's physical; instead, the Bengals opted to call it off since they would have lost a third-round compensatory pick if the deal was completed, per Rapoport. The Eagles could still look to move Ebiketie elsewhere prior to Tuesday's deadline, but barring another trade, he'll suit up for Philadelphia in its Week 10 game against Pittsburgh.

headline: The Bengals acquired Ebiketie from the Eagles on Tuesday in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Cincinnati was in need of aid on the edge following Cashius Howell's (wrist) recent placement on IR, and Ebiketie should help fill the void. He was a rotational player for Philadelphia, logging 48 of the team's defensive snaps through the team's first nine games while tallying 25 tackles and no sacks. Ebiketie will likely be the Bengals' first defensive end off the bench behind starters Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy, while his departure should open up more playing time in Philadelphia for rookie seventh-round pick Keyshawn James-Newby.

headline: Jones (ankle) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
story: The cornerback was injured in last Sunday's win over the Steelers. With Jones set to miss Thanksgiving Day against Dallas, Riq Woolen and Kelee Ringo are likely to see increased snaps opposite Quinyon Mitchell.

headline: Jones (ankle) was estimated as a DNP on Monday's injury report.
story: Jones suffered an ankle injury during the Eagles' 19-16 win over the Steelers on Sunday. Philadelphia didn't hold practice Monday, so his participation over the next two sessions will shed light on his chances of playing against Dallas on Thanksgiving Day. Quinyon Mitchell (hamstring) was also injured in Week 11, so the Eagles could very well have Riq Woolen and Kelee Ringo as the outside cornerbacks against a Cowboys offense that scored seven touchdowns (four passing, three rushing) in a 51-30 win over the Titans on Sunday.

headline: Jones (foot) was spotted in a walking boot following Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: Jones is dealing with an apparent right foot injury after recording five total tackles (two solo) and three passes defensed during the team's Week 11 victory. More information on his status will likely come when the Eagles return to practice Wednesday.

headline: Jones (hamstring) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against Pittsburgh.
story: Jones logged a full practice Friday, which was enough for him to avoid an injury designation and return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. He's contributed both on defense and special teams and has six tackles (five solo) and one pass defense across seven regular-season games.

headline: Jones (hamstring) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants.
story: Jones remains sidelined due to a hamstring injury he suffered in the Eagles' Week 8 loss to the Commanders. It is unclear if the cornerback's issue is significant enough to land him a spot on injured reserve.

headline: Mitchell (hamstring) doesn't have an injury designation for Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
story: The star cornerback was injured in last Sunday's win over the Steelers, but the couple days of rest was enough for him to be available for Thanksgiving Day in Dallas. Mitchell has started all 10 games this season, producing 41 tackles (32 solo) and 11 pass breakups, including his first career interception. He should see plenty of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens on Thursday.

headline: Mitchell (hamstring) was a limited participant in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.
story: Mitchell injured his left hamstring during the Eagles' 19-16 win over the Steelers on Sunday. He was held out of Monday's walkthrough practice but was back on the field in a limited capacity Tuesday, and defensive coordinator Vic Fangio told reporters that Mitchell should "be fine" to face the Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day. Riq Woolen would be in line for more defensive snaps in the event that Mitchell cannot play Thursday.

headline: Mitchell (hamstring) has been ruled out for the rest of Sunday's game against the Steelers.
story: Mitchell injured his left hamstring in the second half, and medical staff have determined that the injury is severe enough for the third-year defensive back to be sidelined for the remainder of Sunday's contest. Riq Woolen will take over at cornerback the rest of the way.

headline: Mitchell (knee) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
story: Mitchell suffered a knee injury during the Week 4 loss to the Rams. He was scheduled to undergo imaging Monday. However, Mitchell's availability at practice Thursday suggests things went well, meaning he will likely be on the field in Week 5 versus the Jaguars, barring a setback.

headline: Mitchell (knee) was limited in practice Wednesday.
story: Mitchell exited Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams. He was scheduled to undergo testing Monday, but his limited participation at practice Wednesday seemingly keeps the door open regarding his availability for Week 5 versus Jacksonville.

headline: Mitchell is scheduled to undergo testing on his knee Monday after he was forced out of Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Rams, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Mitchell appeared to hyperextend his knee while tackling the Rams' Blake Corum early in third quarter. According to Rapoport, the Eagles are hopeful that Mitchell isn't dealing with anything more than a bone bruise, but his upcoming tests should clarify the extent of the injury. A first-time All-Pro selection in 2025, Mitchell has notched 19 tackles and two pass breakups through the Eagles' first four games of the season.

headline: Mitchell (knee) is questionable to return against the Rams on Sunday.
story: Mitchell tweaked his knee in the second half of Sunday's game and is being evaluated by medical staff. Kelee Ringo, Jonathan Jones and Kenny Moore are all in line for more defensive snaps while Mitchell is sidelined.

headline: McKee (ribs) was a full participant at the Eagles' walkthrough practice Tuesday.
story: McKee was estimated to be a limited participant on Monday's injury report due to an injury to his ribs. He now looks to be all set to serve as the team's primary reserve option at quarterback behind starter Joe Milton on Thursday against the Cowboys.

headline: McKee (ribs) was estimated as a limited participant on Monday's injury report.
story: It's unclear when McKee picked up the injury, given that he didn't play a single snap during Sunday's 19-16 win over the Steelers while serving as Joe Milton's backup. The Eagles have two more practices on a short week, so McKee's participation in those sessions will determine whether he'll be available against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day. Rookie fifth-rounder Cole Payton would serve as the QB2 behind Milton if McKee cannot play Thursday.

headline: McKee will remain in a backup role for Sunday's game against the Steelers after head coach Nick Sirianni announced Wednesday that Joe Milton will serve as the Eagles' starting quarterback for a second straight game, Jeff McLane of The Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
story: Though the Eagles dropped a seventh straight game while Milton turned the ball over once and took seven sacks in a Week 9 loss to the Giants, Sirianni saw enough from the third-year signal-caller to hand him at least one more start. While it's conceivable that the Eagles could go back to McKee -- who started Weeks 6 through 8 -- at some point if Milton's performance isn't up to par, rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton is also on the roster and may get a look before the season winds down.

headline: McKee (ribs) is active for Sunday's game against the Giants.
story: McKee has overcome his rib injury in time to suit up for Sunday's contest. The quarterback is set to back up Joe Milton against the Giants due to the absence of former starter Jalen Hurts (calf, IR).

headline: McKee (ribs) "is expected to serve as the backup quarterback" Sunday against the Giants, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: McKee is listed as questionable for Week 9 due to what the report notes is "a cracked rib sustained on the first drive" in Week 8, but it appears he is feeling good enough to suit up. Joe Milton is set to start for the Eagles, so even if McKee is in uniform as anticipated, McKee will open the contest in a reserve role.

headline: McKee (ribs) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus the Giants.
story: McKee lost the Eagles' starting quarterback job to 2024 sixth-rounder Joe Milton after Week 8, and now it's up in the air whether McKee will be available at all in Week 9. If he can't suit up, rookie fifth-rounder Cole Payton would figure to slot in as Milton's primary backup Sunday.

headline: McKee (rib) was limited in Thursday's practice.
story: McKee recently lost the starting quarterback job to Joe Milton. As if things couldn't get any worse, the signal-caller appears to be in danger of missing the NFC East showdown with the Giants. If McKee can't suit up for that contest, 2026 fifth-round pick Cole Payton would presumably back up Milton against New York in Week 9.

headline: McKee will shift to a backup role for Sunday's game against the Giants with the Eagles set to move forward with Joe Milton as their starting quarterback in Week 9, Adam Schefter of ESPN and Mike Garafolo of NFL Network report.
story: Just two days after announcing that McKee would draw a fourth straight start this weekend, head coach Nick Sirianni appears to have changed his tune. The Eagles' decision to move forward with Milton comes after McKee went 0-3 as a starter while completing 63.2 percent of his passes for 5.6 yards per attempt and a 2:2 TD:INT since replacing Jalen Hurts (calf) atop the depth chart. Since McKee is set to become a free agent next spring and may not be part of the Eagles' long-term plans, he could end up serving as the No. 3 quarterback if the team wants to give rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton the opportunity to suit up on game days.

headline: Head coach Nick Sirianni said Monday that McKee will remain the Eagles' starting quarterback, Zach Berman of The Athletic reports. "Tanner's our guy. We're not making any changes there," Sirianni said.
story: Since stepping into the starting role Week 6 in place of Jalen Hurts (calf), McKee has led the Eagles to an 0-3 record while completing 72 of 114 pass attempts (63.2 percent) for 638 yards (5.6 YPA), two touchdowns and two interceptions while adding 26 yards on six carries. Despite McKee's mediocre returns, the Eagles will stick with him as their starter for Sunday's matchup with the Giants, but another poor showing could prompt Sirianni to re-evaluate the quarterback situation following a Week 10 bye.

headline: McKee completed 23 of 34 passes for 212 yards, no touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 27-10 loss to the Commanders. He also rushed four times for 25 yards and lost a fumble.
story: McKee operated without top two wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for a second consecutive game and failed to throw a touchdown pass for the first time in his three-game stint as Philadelphia's starting QB. He has thrown for between 211 and 215 yards in each of his three outings since Jalen Hurts (calf) was shut down for the season. Expectations should remain tempered for McKee and Philadelphia's injury-riddled offense in Week 9 against the Giants.

headline: McKee completed 23 of 35 passes for 211 yards with one touchdown and one interception and added one rush for one yard in the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday night.
story: McKee's final numbers weren't poor by any stretch, but the fourth-year signal-caller couldn't come close to keeping pace with Dak Prescott's exploits. McKee was working without both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), so in that context, the quarterback's production was solid, albeit unspectacular. McKee recorded completions to eight different targets overall, and he'll look to boost his overall numbers with a hopefully healthier receiving corps in a Week 8 road matchup against the Commanders on Sunday night.

headline: McKee completed 26 of 45 passes for 215 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions while adding one carry for no gain in the Eagles' 25-14 loss to the Panthers on Sunday. He also recovered a fumble.
story: McKee's completion total was impressive, but he averaged a modest 4.8 yards per attempt on the afternoon despite having DeVonta Smith back from a two-game absence due to a hamstring injury. McKee's longest completion of the day went for 19 yards to Smith on a fourth-quarter scoring strike, which brought Philadelphia to within five at the time. McKee ultimately wasn't able to complete the comeback in the first installment of what figures to be an extended starting assignment in place of Jalen Hurts (IR, calf), and he'll look to be more aggressive during a Week 7 home divisional clash with the Cowboys next Monday night.

headline: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni confirmed Friday that McKee will start Sunday's game against the Panthers, NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: McKee is likely headed for a multi-game run as the Eagles' starter, after Jalen Hurts (calf) was ruled out for Week 6 due to a superficial blood clot before landing on injured reserve Saturday. Rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton is active as the No. 2 quarterback for Sunday's game behind McKee, who will be making the third start of his four-year career. Unlike Hurts, the 6-foot-6, 231-pound McKee is more of a traditional pocket passer who doesn't offer much of a threat as a runner, but he's been serviceable in directing the Philadelphia offense in his limited opportunities. He's completed 54 of 88 career pass attempts (61.4 percent) for 597 yards (6.8 YPA), five touchdowns and one interception.

headline: McKee appears lined up to start Sunday's game against the Panthers after the Eagles announced Wednesday that Jalen Hurts has been ruled out for Week 6 due to a superficial blood clot on his calf, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
story: While the Eagles could look to re-sign the recently released Andy Dalton to give the quarterback room another experienced option in Hurts' absence, McKee looks poised to draw the start after moving ahead of Dalton on the depth chart prior to Week 4. Hurts' availability beyond Week 6 is in flux while the Eagles determine the appropriate course for his treatment, so McKee could be headed for a multi-game run as the team's starter. A 2023 sixth-round pick, McKee has appeared in just six games (two starts) during his four-year career, completing 54 of 88 pass attempts (61.4 percent) for 597 yards (6.8 YPA) and a 5:1 TD:INT. Assuming he starts, McKee may have few weapons at his disposal, as running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring) and wideout DeVonta Smith (hamstring) were absent from practice Wednesday and could be tracking toward sitting out this weekend.

headline: McKee is expected to be active for Sunday's game against the Rams as the top backup to starter Jalen Hurts, while Andy Dalton serves as the Eagles' No. 3 quarterback, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Despite operating as Hurts' primary backup in 2025, McKee slid to third on the depth chart entering the 2026 season after the Eagles acquired Dalton in a trade with the Panthers back in March. Dalton didn't see any snaps on the season until midway through the second quarter of Monday's 27-7 loss to the Bears, when Hurts made a brief exit from the contest to get checked for a concussion. After three consecutive Saquon Barkley carries got the Eagles near the goal line, Dalton proceeded to throw a costly interception in the end zone on his lone pass attempt before Hurts returned for the next possession. The gaffe appears to have resulted in Dalton turning the backup gig over to McKee, at least for one week.

headline: Bernard caught one of two targets for 58 yards during the Steelers' 27-5 win over the Broncos on Friday.
story: Friday was the Steelers' first game with Mason Rudolph under center following a tumultuous few days which saw the team waive veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday. Rudolph threw for only 142 yards on nine of 15 pass attempts, and a big chunk of that came on Bernard's lone reception of the game in the first quarter, when the second-round rookie caught the ball at the Steelers' 20-yard line and scampered into Broncos territory for a 58-yard catch. Pittsburgh's defense did much of the heavy lifting Friday, but the offense will have more time to game plan with Rudolph at the helm ahead of the team's Week 13 home tilt against the Texans on Sunday, Dec. 6. Bernard has a 39-382-1 line on 57 targets through 11 regular-season games.

headline: Bernard caught six passes for 40 yards on 10 targets in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
story: With Michael Pittman (foot) remaining sidelined for Week 11, Bernard retained his every-down role on offense, playing 67 of 71 offensive snaps while leading the team in routes (52) and targets. It was a nice bounce-back game for the rookie after he was held without a catch on three targets against the Bengals in Week 10. Pittman is expected back for Friday's game against the Broncos, but Bernard could keep pacing the team in playing time, especially if DK Metcalf gets disciplined for his latest on-field outburst.

headline: Bernard failed to reel in any of his three targets while notching a 10-yard rush during Sunday night's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
story: Bernard went without a catch for the first time since Week 1, and his three targets were his fewest since the team's Week 4 loss to the Browns. The wide receiver led his position in offensive snaps (58), besting DK Metcalf (50) in that regard. Bernard entered Week 10 having recorded multiple receptions in five straight contests, and he'll have a good shot to get back on track in Week 11 versus the Eagles.

headline: Bernard caught all five of his targets for 30 yards during Sunday's 27-6 win against Cleveland.
story: Bernard led the team in catches, reeling in multiple passes for the fifth straight week and sixth time overall this year. The wide receiver has built a strong rapport with starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers, but it's unclear what Bernard's workload will look like after the Steelers have a chance to regroup and potentially acquire another pass catcher during the team's bye week in Week 9.

headline: Bernard caught three of five targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Saints.
story: It was a big step back in production for the rookie wideout compared to Week 6 against the Bucs, but Bernard still ran a team-high 33 routes on Aaron Rodgers' 34 dropbacks against New Orleans. Bernard's role is secure while Michael Pittman (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) remain sidelined for at least two more games each. Bernard will be a fantasy WR3 for next Sunday's game against the Browns.

headline: Bernard caught 11 of 12 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Bucs.
story: With Michael Pittman (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) out for the Steelers, Bernard was the clear WR2 behind DK Metcalf and actually ran a team-high 54 routes on Aaron Rodgers' 56 dropbacks. Metcalf edged Bernard out in targets 15 to 12, while both players caught 11 passes. Pittman and Wilson are both required to miss at least two and three more games, respectively, so Bernard is locked into an every-down role for the immediate future. Rodgers has sung the rookie wideout's praises early this season, and it's reasonable to expect Bernard to remain a key part of the passing offense moving forward. He should be rostered in all fantasy formats.

headline: Bernard and return specialist Kaden Wetjen are the only wide receivers on Pittsburgh's active roster without injury designations for Week 6.
story: Bernard played 93 percent of snaps in a Week 5 win over Indianapolis, catching six passes for 80 yards on a team-high nine targets. He now projects for a similar workload, at least in terms of playing time, as the Steelers are still without Michael Pittman (IR - foot) and now have Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) ruled out for Week 6. What's more, DK Metcalf is listed as questionable after missing Friday's practice with an illness. Metcalf may not be at his best even if he's able to play, and there's otherwise minimal target competition for Bernard in the WR room. The Steelers figure to deploy multi-TE formations early and often to avoid relying too heavily on practice-squad callups at WR like Brandon Johnson or Isaiah Hodgins.

headline: Bernard caught six of nine targets for 90 yards during Sunday's 34-22 win over the Colts.
story: Bernard led the team in targets while notching six catches and 80 receiving yards, both of which were new career highs. The rookie was operating in a more prominent role with fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) on injured reserve, and Roman Wilson suffered a finger injury Sunday, so Bernard may see even more opportunities moving forward. Through five games this season, he has caught 20 of 33 targets for 278 yards and two touchdowns.

headline: Bernard caught both of his targets for 11 yards during the Steelers' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Thursday.
story: Bernard was not targeted by Aaron Rodgers until late in the fourth quarter, with the duo connecting on passes for six and five yards to help set up a three-yard touchdown catch by Pat Freiermuth after the two-minute warning. The rookie second-rounder was on the field for 29 of the Steelers' 72 offensive snaps (40.3 percent), which was third most among wide receivers behind DK Metcalf (70) and Michael Pittman (52) and ahead of Roman Wilson (22). Bernard has a 7-60-0 line on 11 targets through four regular-season games, though his role in the offense will be limited behind Metcalf, Pittman, Freiermuth, Darnell Washington and Jaylen Warren. The Steelers head back home for Week 5 against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Pittman caught one of two targets for seven yards in Friday's 27-5 win over the Broncos.
story: Seeing his first action since Week 4 after recovering from a left foot injury, Pittman played just 18 snaps on offense and didn't see many looks from new Steelers starting quarterback Mason Rudolph, but neither did anyone else -- DK Metcalf led the team with three catches on four targets, as Rudolph attempted just 15 passes in total. If Pittsburgh sticks with a ground-heavy game plan under Rudolph, it will limit the ceilings of all the team's pass catchers, but Pittman should at least see a bigger snap count in Week 13 against the Texans as he gets back up to game speed.

headline: Pittman (foot), who was activated from IR on Thursday, doesn't carry an injury designation for Friday's game against the Broncos, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
story: Pittman last played in Week 4 but is slated to be back in the lineup versus Denver after logging 'full' practice listings Tuesday through Thursday. In his return, Pittman will bolster a Pittsburgh WR corps that also features DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson, with the veteran pass catcher's Week 12 fantasy upside hinging on how well he connects with newly-installed starting QB Mason Rudolph. Prior to his absence, Pittman recorded a 7-89-0 line on 12 targets through three contests.

headline: The Steelers activated Pittman (foot) from injured reserve Thursday.
story: Pittman has tended to a foot injury for most of the season and spent the last six games on injured reserve. He so far has logged full listings on both of the Steelers' Week 12 practice reports, and Thursday's report will determine if he has a designation for Friday's game against the Broncos. With QB Aaron Rodgers getting waived Wednesday, Mason Rudolph is slated to lead Pittsburgh's offense.

headline: Pittman (foot) was listed as a full participant in Wednesday's practice,Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
story: Pittman also logged a full participation listing one day before, but the Steelers held a walkthrough practice Tuesday, so Wednesday's session is more relevant with regard to the WR's availability for Friday's game against the Broncos. If Pittman -- who last saw game action in Week 4 -- is activated to face Denver, he'll be catching passing in Week 12 from Mason Rudolph, with the Steelers slated to let veteran signal-calller Aaron Rodgers go.

headline: Pittman (foot) was listed as a full participant in Tuesday's walkthrough practice.
story: The Steelers haven't yet brought Pittman back from injured reserve, but he stands a good chance at being activated for Friday's game against the Broncos. Pittman was listed as a full participant Tuesday on a third consecutive practice report as he works to regain conditioning after missing the Steelers' last six games.

headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Monday that he's "very confident" Pittman (foot) will be on the field this week when the Steelers face the Broncos on Friday, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
story: Pittman was designated for return from IR this past Wednesday, but despite being listed as a full participant in practice Thursday and Friday, the Steelers elected to not activate the WR (who had been listed as questionable) for Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles. Added context regarding Pittman's status will arrive via Pittsburgh's next practice report, but barring any setbacks, it appears as though he's approaching his first game action since Week 4.

headline: Pittman (foot) is not expected to be activated from injured reserve for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Brooke Pryor of ESPN reports.
story: Pittman was able to practice fully both Thursday and Friday, but he is not ready to rejoin the mix just yet -- which Pittsburgh confirmed by omitting Pittman from the list of roster moves it made Saturday. Barring an unannounced setback, Pittman figures to continue practicing, and his next chance to take the field will arrive Black Friday, when the Steelers square off against the Broncos.

headline: Pittman (foot) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Mark Kaboly reports.
story: Pittman was designated for return from injured reserve earlier this week and had progressed to full participation Thursday, so his questionable tag keeps him in the mix for a potential activation ahead of Sunday's contest against the Eagles. With both Pittman and Roman Wilson (finger) nearing a return, it's unclear what that will mean for rookie Germie Bernard's role going forward, as the rookie has hit a slow spot in the box score the last couple weeks.

headline: Pittman (foot) was listed as a full participant in Thursday's practice, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
story: After he was designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Pittman practiced for the second day in a row. Pittman took a step forward in activity after he was a limited participant a day earlier, potentially putting him on a path to return from IR ahead of Sunday's game at Philadelphia. In order for Pittman to be eligible to play against the Eagles, the Steelers would have to activate him prior to Saturday's 4 p.m. ET deadline for Week 11 roster moves.

headline: Pittman (foot) participated in practice Thursday, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
story: After being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Pittman was able to return to a limited practice. The WR's presence at Thursday's session implies that there were no setbacks, with the Steelers' upcoming injury report set to reveal his official participation level. In any case, Pittman will need to be activated off IR no later than Saturday afternoon in order to have a chance to play Sunday against the Eagles.

headline: Pittman (foot) was limited in his return to practice Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: The Steelers could be poised to welcome back a pair of their key WRs to the lineup this week, with both Pittman and Roman Wilson (finger, full practice) having been designated to return from IR on Wednesday. Pittman who was placed on IR on Oct. 10, has played in three games so far in his first season with Pittsburgh and has recorded seven receptions for 89 yards on 12 targets in that span.

headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Wednesday that Pittman (foot) has been designated for return from injured reserve, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
story: Pittsburgh opened the 21-day evaluation windows of both Pittman and Roman Wilson (finger), clearing the way for both receivers to resume practicing Wednesday. McCarthy suggested earlier in the week that Pittman has a shot at suiting up Sunday in Philadelphia, though the wideout's availability will likely depend on how he looks in practice over the next three days. Prior to landing on injured reserve Oct. 10 after aggravating a left foot injury, Pittman had gotten off to an underwhelming start to the season, recording seven receptions for 89 yards and no touchdowns on 12 targets through three appearances.

headline: Coach Mike McCarthy said Monday that the Steelers are "hopeful" they can get Pittman -- who last played in Week 4 -- back from his foot injury this week, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
story: The same goes for Roman Wilson (finger), who saw his last game action in Week 5. In the duo's absence, DK Metcalf has led Pittsburgh's WR corps, with Germie Bernard having seen his role expand in the process. Prior to his injury, Pittman caught seven of his 12 targets for 89 yards in three games, but once he rejoins the lineup, the 29-year-old -- who had at least 111 targets in each of his last five seasons with the Colts -- could resurface on the fantasy radar in PPR formats.

headline: Pittman (foot) is warmed up with his teammates Thursday, though he remains on IR and wasn't wearing a helmet, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
story: Pittman is inching toward a return from a foot injury that has sidelined him since Week 4. He won't have his window to return from injured reserve opened prior to Sunday's game in Cincinnati, but a Week 11 return against the Eagles appears to be a realistic possibility.

headline: Pittman (foot) is making progress but won't have his practice window opened this week, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
story: Pittman resumed running in late October and could resume practicing at some point in November. It won't happen this week, however, leaving the Steelers with minimal WR depth beyond DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard.

headline: Pittman (foot) said Monday that he resumed running last week as part of a program to return, but the wideout acknowledged that he's without a clear timeline to be activated from injured reserve, Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports.
story: Pittman has missed the Steelers' last four games and is now eligible to be activated from IR at any point, but based on the receiver's comments, he doesn't appear to be trending toward a return to action following the team's Week 9 bye. The wideout noted that his left foot injury that first cropped up following the season opener was originally plantar fasciitis but has since "morphed into something else." While it's encouraging that he's at least healthy enough to start running again, Pittman didn't indicate when he might be ready to resume practicing with the team.

headline: The Steelers placed Pittman (foot) on injured reserve Saturday.
story: With the expected move now official, Pittman will be required to miss at least the next four games, making Week 10 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15 the earliest that the veteran wide receiver can return. Roman Wilson and Germie Bernard are both in line for more offensive snaps for as long as Pittman is sidelined.

headline: Pittman (foot) is being placed on injured reserve, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
story: Pittman was already ruled out for Sunday's game against the Colts after aggravating a foot injury in practice during Week 5 prep. The team has yet to announce the move, but once it's official, Pittman will be required to miss at least the next four games. With the Steelers on a bye for Week 9, that means the earliest that the veteran wide receiver will be eligible to return is Week 10 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15. Roman Wilson figures to step into the WR2 role behind DK Metcalf in Pittman's absence, and rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard should also be in the mix for more targets from veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

headline: Pittman is expected to miss multiple weeks after aggravating his foot injury, Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports Thursday.
story: Pittman missed Pittsburgh's Week 2 loss to the Patriots due to a foot issue and had just four catches for 31 yards across two subsequent appearances. He's facing a multi-week absence after aggravating that injury in practice leading up to the Steelers' Week 5 matchup against the Colts. The team has yet to decide whether to place Pittman on IR, in which case he would be required to sit out a minimum of four weeks.

headline: Pittman (foot) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
story: Pittman sat out the Steelers' Week 2 loss to the Patriots due to a foot issue, but he proceeded to suit up for the team's subsequent two games, playing north of 70 percent of snaps in both contests while producing a combined 4-31-0 receiving line on nine targets. The Steelers haven't indicated that Pittman is dealing with any major setback coming out of this past Thursday's loss to the Browns, even though he was spotted moving around the locker room Wednesday with a one-legged scooter and no shoe on his left foot, per Mark Kaboly of 93.7 The Fan Pittsburgh. Pittman's ability to practice in some fashion to kick off Week 5 prep suggests that he remains likely to play this Sunday against the Colts.

headline: Pittman was spotted in the Pittsburgh locker room Wednesday using a one-legged scooter with his left foot propped up, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
story: Pittman missed the Steelers' Week 2 loss to the Patriots due to a foot issue, though he was able to play in both of the Steelers' last two contests. The wideout may have just been using the scooter as a precaution, but at the very least, it's an indication that he hasn't yet made a full recovery from the injury. The veteran receiver's participation in practices Wednesday through Friday will ultimately determine whether he suits up this Sunday, when the Steelers will be taking on his former Colts squad.

headline: Pittman caught two of four targets for 15 yards Thursday in a loss to the Browns.
story: Pittman logged a 72 percent offensive snap share, second-most among Pittsburgh wideouts, but he didn't do much with the ample playing time. In fact, Roman Wilson -- who logged a 22 percent offensive snap share -- outproduced Pittman considerably with a 3-74-1 receiving line. In his first season with the Steelers, Pittman has had a tough time connecting with QB Aaron Rodgers, posting just seven catches on 12 targets for 89 yards through three games. He'll look to make more of an impact in Week 5 against Indianapolis next Sunday.

headline: Metcalf caught three of four targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in Friday's 27-5 win over Denver.
story: The targets and catches actually led the Steelers on the afternoon, and Metcalf was on the other end of Mason Rudolph's only TD, a 22-yard strike in the first quarter. Rudolph completed just nine passes in total, and if the offense continues to be ground-heavy following the switch at QB from Aaron Rodgers, it could be tough for Metcalf or any of the team's pass catchers to produce consistent numbers. Metcalf will look to take advantage of what volume he gets in Week 13 against the Texans.

headline: DK Metcalf makes nice TD snag
story: DK Metcalf makes nice TD snag

headline: DK Metcalf's Week 12 fantasy preview
story: DK Metcalf's Week 12 fantasy preview

headline: Metcalf won't receive a suspension after he was ejected from Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles, but the NFL is still reviewing discipline for the receiver that could include a fine, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: Metcalf was disqualified with 4:53 remaining in the third quarter Sunday after he attempted to poke Eagles defensive back Cooper DeJean in the eye. He was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct in what was his second major transgression of the game; Metcalf previously drew an unnecessary roughness penalty in the first half, when he held his block of DeJean well after a play had finished. Though Metcalf won't miss further game action as a result of his ejection, he may have already lost the faith of his fantasy managers heading into a Week 12 matchup with the Broncos on Friday. Metcalf has hauled in just 36 of his 74 targets (48.6 percent catch rate) and has scored just two touchdowns on the season while topping 60 receiving yards in only two of his 10 appearances.

headline: Metcalf will have his actions from Sunday's game against the Eagles reviewed "for potential additional discipline, including a suspension," Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network reports.
story: Metcalf was ejected from Sunday's contest in the third quarter after receiving a second unsportsmanlike conduct penalty, and the NFL will evaluate the situation and determine if he'll face any further penalties. Per the report, the league is expected to make a decision "later" Monday.

headline: Metcalf was ejected in the third quarter of Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports.
story: After accruing his second unsportsmanlike penalty of the contest, Metcalf was tossed from this Week 11 matchup. Prior to his exit with 4:58 remaining in the third quarter, he was having his least productive performance of the season (1-2-0 receiving line on four targets). The Steelers will roll with Germie Bernard, Roman Wilson, Ben Skowronek and Max Hurleman at wide receiver with Metcalf unavailable for the rest of the game.

headline: Metcalf brought in two of six targets for 54 yards and a touchdown and added a two-point conversion catch in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday night.
story: Metcalf's yardage total, modest as it was, led the Steelers on the night. The veteran receiver got there with the help of a team-long 32-yard catch, while his other reception was a 22-yard scoring grab early in the fourth quarter that Metcalf followed up with a two-point conversion. Metcalf has at least Sunday night's yardage total in three of the last four games, but he's still sporting an inefficient 35-432-2 line on 70 targets through nine games heading into a Week 11 road matchup against the Eagles next Sunday.

headline: Metcalf brought in one of six targets for four yards in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.
story: Aaron Rodgers put up a season low in completions, pass attempts, passing yards and completion percentage Sunday, and Metcalf's production was part of the collateral damage. The veteran wideout did see a team high in targets, but the fact he did next to nothing with them led to season lows in catches and receiving yards. Metcalf has had a handful of splash plays over the first half of the season and has two games of more than 90 receiving yards, but he's averaging a career-low 11.5 yards per catch and has just a single touchdown reception heading into the Week 9 bye.

headline: Metcalf two of six targets for 56 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Saints.
story: The Steelers' offense mostly flowed through its backfield, and Metcalf's 56 receiving yards actually led the team despite the fact that his two catches were a season low. The veteran wideout's target volume has been erratic this year, but he remains Aaron Rodgers' top downfield option. Metcalf will take a 32-374-1 line on 58 targets through seven games into a Week 8 clash with the Browns, who he produced a 5-115-0 line against in Week 4.

headline: Metcalf caught 11 of 15 targets for 93 yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers.
story: The targets and catches were season highs for Metcalf, while the veteran WR came up just short of his second 100-yard performance in the last three weeks. Metcalf will take a 30-318-1 line on 52 targets into a Week 7 clash with the Saints in Paris.

headline: The Steelers removed Metcalf (illness) from the injury report Saturday, and the veteran wide receiver will be available for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
story: The wideout popped up on the injury report Friday due to an illness and drew a questionable tag, but Metcalf is apparently feeling better a day later and has been given an early green light to play Sunday. Metcalf saw a season-low four targets in a Week 5 win over the Colts, but he could be in line for more looks Sunday with Roman Wilson (finger) joining fellow receiver Michael Pittman (foot) on injured reserve Saturday and with tight end Pat Freiermuth (calf) listed as questionable for Week 6.

headline: Metcalf is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers after missing Friday's practice due to an illness.
story: Metcalf wasn't listed on the injury report Wednesday or Thursday, which suggests he started feeling sick Thursday evening or Friday morning. He'll have nearly two days to recover before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff Sunday, and the Steelers might want him active even if he isn't at full strength, given their myriad of injury problems at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) are out this week, leaving Germie Bernard and return specialist Kaden Wetjen as the only healthy WRs on the active roster. Brandon Johnson was called up from the practice squad last week.

headline: Metcalf caught three of four targets for 12 yards in Sunday's 34-22 win over the Colts.
story: The veteran wideout didn't make much impact as a pass catcher, but his blocking played a big role on a pair of long Jaylen Warren touchdowns. It was still a disappointing showing from Metcalf after he popped for a 5-115-0 line the week before, but he remains Aaron Rodgers' top downfield threat with a 19-225-1 line on 37 targets through five games. He'll likely be a feast or famine option once again in Week 6 against the Buccaneers.

headline: Metcalf brought in five of nine targets for 115 yards in the Steelers' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Thursday.
story: Metcalf led the Steelers across the stat sheet in receptions, receiving yards and targets, and his production in the first two categories also qualified as new season highs. The veteran wideout started slowly, but he came on with catches of 43, 22 and 28 yards in the fourth quarter. The standout night was a welcome sight for fantasy managers, who'd seen Metcalf post an inefficient and modest 11-98-1 line on 24 targets over his first three games. Metcalf will aim to carry over the momentum into a Week 5 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Dowdle carried the ball 11 times for 71 yards in Friday's 27-5 win over the Broncos.
story: Jaylen Warren led the Steelers backfield with 21 touches, but he turned that volume into just 46 yards while Dowdle led the team in rushing. The 71 rushing yards also were a season high for Dowdle, and if Pittsburgh continues to deploy a ground-heavy game plan with Mason Rudolph under center in place of the exiled Aaron Rodgers, there could be plenty of work for both RBs. Dowdle will try to keep making a case for more of a timeshare with Warren in Week 13 against the Texans.

headline: Dowdle rushed five times for 15 yards and caught four of five targets for 19 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
story: Dowdle finished with 34 scrimmage yards for a second consecutive game after racking up 235 scrimmage yards over his preceding four appearances. He had five more yards than Jaylen Warren on two fewer touches in Sunday's loss. Dowdle is poised to retain his spot as the 1B option alongside Warren in Friday's Week 12 home game against the Broncos.

headline: Dowdle rushed five times for 26 yards and caught both of his targets for eight yards during Sunday's 38-18 defeat at Cincinnati.
story: Dowdle's previous low-water mark in touches was nine in Week 2 at New England, and on the season he averaged 11.8 touches per game entering Week 10 action. As a result, he finished with his second-fewest yards from scrimmage (34) in a contest this season, while backfield mate Jaylen Warren (12 touches for 41 total yards) also found little success in any facet. Dowdle remains the No. 2 RB in Pittsburgh behind Warren and thus is a hit-or-miss option in a Week 11 road matchup with the Eagles next Sunday.

headline: Dowdle rushed 15 times for 56 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday.
story: Dowdle finished just two carries behind Jaylen Warren on the afternoon, and although his backfield mate significantly outpaced him in yardage, the former made his fantasy mark when he opened the scoring on the day with a nine-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Dowdle recorded new season highs in rush attempts and rushing yards as the Steelers had the luxury of leaning heavily on the ground attack, but Warren remains the backfield's clear No. 1 option heading into the Week 9 bye.

headline: Dowdle carried the ball nine times for 41 yards and caught all six of his targets for 45 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over New Orleans.
story: The 15 touches were a season high for Dowdle, but he still took a back seat to Jaylen Warren's 21 touches and 137 scrimmage yards in the Steelers' backfield. Dowdle also led the team in receptions on the day, and his own 86 combined yards were a season high. Pittsburgh could stay with its ground-heavy game plan in Week 8 against Cleveland, giving Dowdle some fantasy appeal even in his backup role.

headline: Dowdle (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
story: After missing three straight games due to a dislocated toe, Dowdle made his return to action in last week's overtime win over the Buccaneers, finishing with 40 yards on seven carries and nine yards on three receptions. However, he seemingly emerged from that contest with a new knee issue, which limited his participation in Week 7 prep and resulted in him being listed as questionable heading into Sunday. The Steelers were apparently encouraged enough by how Dowdle looked in pregame warmups to clear him to play against the Saints, and the 28-year-old should be ready to work in his usual complementary role behind lead back Jaylen Warren.

headline: Dowdle (knee) was a limited participant in Friday's practice and is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris, NFL insider Adam Caplan reports.
story: A limited participant participant all week, Dowdle seems more likely than not to play. He's no longer listed with the toe injury that kept him out for multiple games, instead dealing with a knee issue. Pittsburgh's inactive list will be released around 8:00 a.m. ET on Sunday.

headline: Dowdle (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
story: The Steelers did not practice Friday because of poor weather in Paris, but if they had Dowdle would have been limited with the knee injury -- different than the toe issue he was dealing with previously -- for a third straight day. The Steelers will practice Saturday and could provide an update on Dowdle's status after the session concludes, otherwise his status for Week 7 will be revealed when Pittsburgh releases its inactives 90 minutes before Sunday's 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Dowdle (knee) was listed as a limited participant on Thursday's injury report, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
story: Thursday marked another limited session for Dowdle, who has been dealing with a knee issue in the lead-up to the Steelers' upcoming game against the Saints. He will have a chance to ramp up to a full practice on Friday before the Steelers make a final call on his gameday status.

headline: Dowdle was listed as a limited participant for Wednesday's practice due to a knee injury, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
story: Dowdle had missed three consecutive games due to a dislocated toe on his right foot before returning to action for this past Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers. While playing 21 of the Steelers' 79 offensive snaps, Dowdle finished with seven carries for 40 yards and added three catches for nine yards, but he appears to have emerged from the contest with a new injury. His ability to practice in any capacity to begin Week 7 is generally a good sign, but Dowdle may need to upgrade to full participation by Friday to avoid carrying a designation into Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris.

headline: Dowdle carried the ball seven times for 40 yards and caught three of four targets for nine yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers.
story: Seeing his first action since Week 2 after recovering from a toe issue, Dowdle took a back seat to Jaylen Warren in terms of touches (16 to 10) and scrimmage yards (78 to 49). The volume was still encouraging for Dowdle given how dominant Warren had been during his absence, but the split doesn't help the fantasy value of either RB. Dowdle may need to get into the end zone to make an impact in Week 7 against the Saints in Paris.

headline: Dowdle (toe) is active for Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Buccaneers.
story: Dowdle had teed up his active status by finishing Week 6 prep with consecutive full practices. The veteran offseason addition, who missed the last three games due to a toe dislocation, had been working in a true timeshare with Jaylen Warren over the first two games of the season, but the latter's 321 rushing yards, 169 receiving yards and two total touchdowns during Dowdle's absence will keep him in a clear lead-back role while Dowdle serves as a complementary option against a stout Buccaneers run defense.

headline: Dowdle (toe), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, is slated to play, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: Dowdle has been sidelined exiting a loss to the Patriots in Week 2, when he dislocated the same toe on his right foot twice. After logging back-to-back full practices to cap Week 6 prep, he's expected to put an end to a three-game absence and rejoin Jaylen Warren out of the Steelers backfield. Considering how well Warren has performed as the lead back over the past three weeks, head coach Mike McCarthy has already indicated Dowdle will slide back into a complementary role instead of splitting touches with Warren like he had prior to getting hurt.

headline: Dowdle (toe) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers after being a full participant in practice Thursday and Friday.
story: Steelers offensive coordinator Brian Angelichio said Monday that he was expecting Dowdle to return this week. The team isn't ready to commit to it, but back-to-back full practices suggest he's ready to play unless there's a last-minute setback.
