Steelers coach Mike McCarthy told reporters that Jaylen Warren has earned a larger role even when Dowdle is healthy, which means the two RBs won't alternate drives in a 50/50 split the way they did at the beginning of the season. Pittsburgh's inactive list will be posted at 11:30 a.m. ET on Sunday.

headline: Dowdle (toe) was a full participant at Thursday's practice, Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports.
story: Dowdle upgraded to full participation Thursday after being limited Wednesday, putting him on track to return Sunday against the Buccaneers following a three-game absence. Jaylen Warren seized control of Pittsburgh's backfield with 490 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns during the three games Dowdle sat out, so Warren is expected to continue working in the lead role Sunday, with Dowdle on hand in a complementary capacity.

headline: Dowdle (toe) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
story: The Steelers are optimistic that Dowdle will put an end to a three-game absence and suit up Sunday against the Buccaneers, but he may need to upgrade to full practice participation by Friday in order to avoid taking a designation into the weekend. If Dowdle is cleared to play Sunday, he'll be in store for a lesser role than what he had previously handled, as Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy indicated earlier in the week that Jaylen Warren has earned the right to remain in a bell-cow role out of the backfield.

headline: Steelers offensive coordinator Brian Angelichio said Monday that he anticipates Dowdle (toe) returning to action in Week 6 against the Buccaneers, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
story: Though he managed three limited practices in Week 5, Dowdle ultimately missed a third straight game in Sunday's eventual 34-22 win over the Colts. The Steelers seem optimistic that Dowdle will upgrade to full practice participation at some point this week to put him on a path to play versus Tampa Bay, but if available, the 28-year-old could be ticketed for limited snaps in a backup role. Jaylen Warren has accounted for 490 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns across the past three games, with his performance prompting head coach Mike McCarthy to label him Monday as the featured option out of the backfield, per Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. McCarthy previously suggested that Warren and Dowdle would form a "one-two punch" out of the backfield when both are healthy, but Warren's stellar play has changed that plan.

headline: Dowdle (toe) is inactive for Sunday's Week 5 game against the Colts.
story: The veteran running back will miss a third consecutive game while tending to the toe injury he sustained in a Week 2 loss to the Patriots. Dowdle was able to practice in limited fashion during each session of Week 5 prep, so there appears to be a good chance he manages to gain clearance for a Week 6 road matchup against the Buccaneers next Sunday. Meanwhile, Jaylen Warren, who's logged 23 touches apiece in each of the first two games Dowdle has missed, will continue in a workhorse role out of the Steelers backfield against Indianapolis on Sunday.

headline: Dowdle (toe) is unlikely to play in Sunday's game against the Colts, but the Steelers will make a final decision after pregame warmups, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: While Dowdle was listed as limited during the entirety of Week 5 prep and went into the weekend as questionable to play, he appears destined to miss a third consecutive contest due to a lingering toe injury. If Dowdle is indeed inactive when the Steelers post their list approximately 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, Jaylen Warren again will handle a workhorse role out of the backfield.

headline: Dowdle (toe) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Colts, Mike DeFabo reports.
story: A limited practice participant throughout the week, Dowdle now enters the weekend with a chance to return from a two-game absence. If he's active for Pittsburgh, he won't necessarily jump right back into the 50/50 split that he and Jaylen Warren operated in at the beginning of the year. Warren thrived in Dowdle's absence and isn't on the injury report, so he looks like a solid fantasy start even if Dowdle avoids the inactive list ahead of a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff this Sunday.

headline: Dowdle (toe) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: Dowdle practiced for the second day in a row, albeit with a cap on his reps. Earlier Thursday, head coach Mike McCarthy told Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com that Dowdle's status for Sunday's game against the Colts is still up in the air, though the running back would put himself in good position to play this weekend if he's able to upgrade to full practice participation Friday. If Dowdle ultimately suits up versus the Colts, he'll likely be Option 1B in the backfield behind Jaylen Warren, who has averaged 6.5 yards per carry and 13.7 yards per reception over the past two weeks while Dowdle has been sidelined with a dislocated toe on his right foot.

headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said prior to Thursday's practice that Dowdle's (toe) status for Sunday's game against the Colts is up in the air, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
story: Dowdle was listed as limited at Wednesday's practice after he missed the past two games due to a dislocated toe. Jaylen Warren has functioned as Pittsburgh's lead back in Dowdle's absence, but McCarthy has said that once Dowdle is healthy, he plans to use the two players as part of a "one-two punch" in the backfield. It's unclear if that arrangement will be in place Sunday, however, as Dowdle's availability for that contest will hinge on what he's able to do during practices Thursday and Friday.

headline: Dowdle (toe) was listed as a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
story: Earlier Wednesday, head coach Mike McCarthy told Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette that Dowdle would be part of the rehab group to begin Week 5 prep, but the running back was apparently able to fit in enough work behind the scenes to log his first practice activity since dislocating a toe in the Steelers' Week 2 loss to New England. Given that he's missed the Steelers' past two games, Dowdle may need to upgrade to full practice participation by the end of the week in order to get cleared to play Sunday versus the Colts. If Dowdle is available this weekend, McCarthy has previously indicated that he would likely reclaim his spot in a backfield timeshare with Jaylen Warren, who has thrived while handling an every-down role over the past two games.

headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said that Dowdle (toe) will remain in the rehab group for Wednesday's practice, but the running back is expected to do more on-field work later in the week, Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports.
story: Dowdle has been sidelined for Pittsburgh's last two games due to an injury that he relayed Tuesday was a dislocated toe on his right foot, per Will Graves of the Associated Press. He said that he dislocated the toe twice during the Steelers' Week 2 loss to the Patriots, checking back into the game for a brief spell after popping the toe back in before it popped back out again. He sounds like he's making some progress, but he'll likely need to practice in some fashion Thursday and/or Friday to have a shot at playing Sunday versus the Colts. Jaylen Warren has handled heavy workloads the past two weeks in Dowdle's absence, though McCarthy told Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com on Monday that he envisions the two backs forming a "one-two punch" once Dowdle returns to action.

headline: Head coach Mike McCarthy said that Dowdle (toe) had a positive workout Friday and is "making progress" in his recovery, but the Steelers aren't yet certain if he'll be available to play Week 5 versus the Colts, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
story: Dowdle's right toe injury has kept him out for the past two games, with his consecutive absences enabling Jaylen Warren to take on a heightened role out of the backfield as Pittsburgh's clear top option. Though Warren has ran efficiently (6.5 yards per carry) on heavy volume (34 totes) while chipping in six receptions for 82 yards over the last two weeks, McCarthy emphasized that Dowdle will likely remain part of a "one-two punch" with Warren once he returns. Before sustaining the injury in Week 2, Dowdle had struggled to find open running room, taking his 15 carries for just 37 yards (2.5 average).

headline: The Steelers ruled Dowdle (toe) out for Thursday's game in Cleveland, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
story: Dowdle will miss a second straight game after he was unable to practice in any fashion on a short week. With Dowdle out of the mix again, Jaylen Warren looks primed to handle a workhorse role out of the Pittsburgh backfield, after he logged 56 of 62 snaps and handled 20 touches (17 carries, three receptions) for 176 yards in a 30-27 win over the Bengals last week.

headline: Dowdle (toe) was estimated as a non-participant on Tuesday's injury report, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
story: The Steelers held a walkthrough for the second time in as many days ahead of Thursday's contest against the Browns, and once again Dowdle was unable to get any work in. He was at least present Tuesday after not being spotted during the media-viewing portion of Monday's session, but he will presumably have to practice in some capacity Wednesday in order to have any chance of suiting up.

headline: Dowdle (toe) was present for Tuesday's practice but was a non-participant, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
story: After sitting out Sunday's win over the Bengals due to a right toe injury, Dowdle will go down as a non-participant on the Steelers' first two Week 4 practice reports. Unless he's able to fit in some on-field work during Wednesday's session, he'll likely be ruled out ahead of Thursday's game in Cleveland. Dowdle's absence would set up Jaylen Warren for another heavy workload, after he handled 20 touches in Week 3.

headline: Warren carried the ball 20 times for 46 yards and caught one of two targets for zero yards in Friday's 27-5 win over the Broncos.
story: There wasn't much offense happening in this one -- two of Pittsburgh's three touchdowns came on defense, while the Denver defense chipped in a safety -- but Warren had an especially tough day, as his longest gain went for just six yards, and Rico Dowdle wound up leading the Steelers with 71 rushing yards on just 11 carries. The workload split was still encouraging for Warren, as was the ground-heavy game plan with Mason Rudolph taking over at quarterback for the exiled Aaron Rodgers, but the backfield could be drifting back toward a timeshare. Warren will look to bounce back in Week 13 against the Texans.

headline: Why Mike Clay isn't worried about Jaylen Warren in fantasy
story: Why Mike Clay isn't worried about Jaylen Warren in fantasy

headline: Warren rushed nine times for 28 yards and caught two of three targets for one yard in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
story: Warren finished with 29 yards on 11 touches compared to 34 yards on nine touches for Rico Dowdle, as Pittsburgh's backfield duo was held quiet for a second consecutive game. After recording at least 73 scrimmage yards in eight consecutive games to start the season, Warren has produced just 75 yards without a touchdown over the past two games. Warren and Dowdle should continue to split backfield touches Friday against the Broncos.

headline: Warren rushed seven times for 15 yards and brought in five of six targets for 26 yards in the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday night. He committed a fumble recovered by Pittsburgh.
story: The Steelers were quickly dissuaded from a balanced offensive approach when the Bengals accumulated 24 first-half points, leading to Warren's lowest carry and rushing yardage totals of the season. Warren did tie his second-highest reception total of the campaign thanks in part to how the game unfolded, but it was ultimately a nearly irrelevant fantasy night relative to the lofty standards the versatile back has set this season. Warren will look to get back on track at the expense of the struggling Eagles in a Week 11 intrastate road showdown next Sunday.

headline: Warren rushed 17 times for 143 yards and a touchdown and brought in one of two targets for no gain in the Steelers' 27-6 win over the Browns on Sunday. He also fumbled once but recovered.
story: Warren tied his single-game career high in rushing yards with Sunday's performance, which was partly fueled by a season-long 51-yard run. Warren now has back-to-back 100-yard efforts on the ground for the first time this season, and he snapped a brief two-game rushing TD drought Sunday with a one-yard run early in the third quarter that closed out the scoring for the afternoon. Warren is already up to 704 rushing yards on a career-best 5.9 yards per carry heading into a Week 9 road showdown against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15, following a Week 8 bye.

headline: Warren carried the ball 18 times for 101 yards and caught three of four targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Saints.
story: The 21 touches tied his season high, while Rico Dowdle got 15 as the Steelers went with a ground-heavy game plan. Warren has topped 100 scrimmage yards in four of the last five games, racking up 472 rushing yards and a TD along with a 17-233-1 line on 24 targets during that hot stretch. He'll remain one of the key pieces of the Pittsburgh offense heading into a Week 8 clash at home against a Cleveland defense that Warren recorded 126 combined yards against in Week 4.

headline: Warren carried the ball 14 times for 50 yards and caught two of four targets for 28 yards in Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers.
story: While Warren still led the Steelers' backfield, his touch volume and production took a dip as Rico Dowdle returned from a three-game absence due to a toe injury, with Dowdle turning 10 touches into 49 scrimmage yards. As long as coach Mike McCarthy insists on using a timeshare between the two, Warren will be hard-pressed to repeat the outstanding numbers he compiled while Dowdle was on the shelf. Warren will try to make a bigger impact in Week 7 against the Saints in Paris.

headline: Head coach Mike McCarthy said Monday that he views Warren as "our featured player right now," Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
story: During the offseason, McCarthy said that he viewed the Steelers backfield as a 50-50 split between Warren and Rico Dowdle (toe). However, Warren has solidified his RB1 role over the Steelers' last three games with Dowdle on the sidelines, with the former accumulating 490 yards and two touchdowns on 61 touches (49 carries, 12 catches on 16 targets) in that span. It appears Warren is the clear lead back for the Steelers even when Dowdle returns, which could happen as soon as this Sunday against the Buccaneers.

headline: Warren carried the ball 15 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and caught all six of his targets for 87 yards and another TD in Sunday's 34-22 win over the Colts.
story: The fifth-year back set the tone for the afternoon when he took a checkdown from Aaron Rodgers and turned it into an 80-yard score to begin the Steelers' second possession. Warren then added a 50-yard TD run right after halftime, becoming the first player in Pittsburgh franchise history with rushing and receiving touchdowns of 50-plus yards in the same game. He also become just the sixth player in league history, and the first since Herschel Walker in 1986, with an 80-yard TD catch and a 50-yard TD run in the same game -- a list that includes Hall of Famers Jim Brown and Gale Sayers as well. Warren's 188 scrimmage yards were a career best, and he continues to make the case that he deserves a bell-cow workload, turning 61 touches over the last three games into 490 combined yards, along with Sunday's two touchdowns. Even if Rico Dowdle (toe) returns to the lineup in Week 6 against the Buccaneers, Warren should be locked into the lead role in the backfield.

headline: Warren will remain the Steelers' unquestioned lead back in Sunday's Week 5 matchup against the Colts due to Rico Dowdle (toe) having been declared inactive for the contest.
story: Warren has thrived with the additional opportunity afforded by Dowdle's two-game absence to date, as the former has logged 23 total touches apiece in each contest and compiled 302 scrimmage yards in the process. Warren should be in store for a similar workload Sunday against a Colts defense that's surrendered 4.3 yards per carry and 11.1 yards per reception to running backs through four games.

headline: Warren rushed 17 times for 93 yards and secured three of six targets for 33 yards in the Steelers' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Thursday.
story: Warren once again had near total control of the Steelers' ground attack, as Rico Dowdle (toe) missed a second consecutive contest. As he'd done in the Week 3 win over the Bengals, Warren capitalized on the opportunity to comfortably eclipse the century mark in total yards. Warren compiled 220 rushing yards and another 82 yards through the air over the last two games while serving as the unquestioned lead back, but if Dowdle is able to make it back for a Week 5 matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11, the former will see a hit to his touches.

headline: Rudolph completed nine of 15 passes for 142 yards and a touchdown in Friday's 27-5 win over the Broncos.
story: Making his first start of the season after Aaron Rodgers' abrupt departure from the Steelers, Rudolph avoided committing any turnovers and connected with DK Metcalf on a 22-yard TD in the first quarter. The QB didn't do much else aside from getting sacked for a safety, however, as the defense did most of the scoring for Pittsburgh. Rudolph's 15 pass attempts were less than half of the 31 carries that Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle handled between them, and that could be a strong hint as to how the offense will operate the rest of the way. Rudolph is expected to remain under center in Week 13 against the Texans.

headline: Rudolph will start Friday's game against the Broncos and could remain atop the depth chart for the rest of the season with the Steelers waiving Aaron Rodgers on Wednesday.
story: Late Tuesday, the Steelers opted to make a change under center, naming Rudolph the Week 12 starter and sending Rodgers to the bench on the heels of poor performances by the offense in back-to-back losses to the Bengals and Eagles coming out of a bye week. The Steelers initially planned to make Rodgers inactive for Week 12 but keep him on the roster, but the team now intends to part ways with the four-time MVP after he harshly criticized head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday. The impending departure of Rodgers should thus give Rudolph an extended leash as the Steelers' starter, with a pair of inexperienced quarterbacks in second-year man Will Howard and rookie third-round pick Drew Allar representing the other options behind him on the depth chart. Over 38 career appearances (19 starts), the 31-year-old Rudolph has completed 64.2 percent of his passes for 6.6 yards per attempt and a 30:22 TD:INT.

headline: Rudolph will start Friday's game against the Broncos, Tom Pelissero of The Ringer and Netflix reports.
story: In a stunning move late Tuesday night, the Steelers benched Aaron Rodgers following two straight losses to the Bengals and Eagles, where the offense didn't play well at all, as Rodgers averaged a paltry 5.1 yards per attempt. The Steelers will see if Rudolph can provide a spark for 6-4 Pittsburgh. Rudolph has made 19 career regular-season starts and has averaged 6.6 yards per attempt with a 30:22 TD:INT on 742 pass attempts.

headline: Rudolph completed one of three pass attempts for two yards and rushed once for nine yards in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
story: After the Bengals had built a 20-point lead with five minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, head coach Mike McCarthy opted to remove starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers from the game and turned to Rudolph to direct the offense for the Steelers' final possession. Rudolph led the Steelers on an 11-play drive that concluded in the red zone before time expired. The 31-year-old Rudolph has now made four relief appearances behind Rodgers on the season, playing limited snaps in each of those contests.

headline: Rudolph is active for Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: Rudolph has emerged as the Steelers' preferred backup quarterback behind starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers coming out of the preseason. Through each of Pittsburgh's first seven contests, Rudolph has suited up, while both Will Howard and Drew Allar have been inactive. Howard is the Steelers' emergency No. 3 quarterback and will be called upon to play only in the event that both Rodgers and Rudolph are forced to exit Sunday's game.

headline: Echols (quadriceps) has been ruled out for the rest of Friday's game against the Broncos, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
story: Echols recorded one assisted tackle before leaving the game due to a quad injury that is severe enough for him to not return to Friday's contest. His absence means the Steelers will have less depth both on special teams and in the secondary the rest of the way.

headline: Echols (hamstring) was a full participant at practice Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: Echols missed the last two games before Pittsburgh's bye in Week 9 because of a hamstring injury, but it looks like he's on track to be available in Week 10. Through six games so far in 2026, a substantial majority of his snaps have come on special teams.

headline: Echols (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Browns, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
story: Echols will end up missing a second consecutive game due to a hamstring injury, so the Steelers will have less depth in the secondary for Sunday's contest, although the sixth-year pro has mostly operated on special teams. The Steelers are on a bye for Week 9, so Echols' next opportunity to play is Week 10 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15.

headline: Echols (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's matchup with the Saints, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
story: Echols suffered a hamstring injury in the first half of the team's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers on Sunday, and he will now be forced to miss at least one additional contest as a result. The cornerback plays primarily on special teams, so his absence won't have much of an impact on the Steelers' defensive approach in Week 7.

headline: Echols (hamstring) won't return to Sunday's game against Tampa Bay, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
story: Echols was injured on a Buccaneers punt in the first half. He limped off the field and was eventually ruled out coming out of halftime due to a hamstring injury. With Echols done for the remainder of Week 6, rookie Daylen Everette will need to step up.

headline: Echols (concussion) no longer has an injury designation for Thursday's game against the Browns.
story: A limited practice participant through Week 4 prep, Echols had been listed as questionable heading into Thursday. However, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com relayed Wednesday that the cornerback had cleared the five-step concussion protocol, and the Steelers have now signed off on Echols playing on a short week. Through Pittsburgh's first three games, Echols has accrued two tackles while handling a limited role on defense and serving as a key player on special teams.

headline: Echols (concussion) is listed as questionable ahead of Thursday's game against the Browns, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reported Wednesday.
story: Echols cleared the NFL's five-step concussion protocol Wednesday but remains questionable for Thursday's game. The short turnaround for the divisional clash may prove prohibitive for Echols' chances of suiting up, but his status will be clarified when the Steelers announce their inactives 90 minutes before the game's 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Echols (concussion) was listed as a limited participant in Monday's practice estimate.
story: Echols departed late in Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals to get checked for a concussion, and his appearance on the Steelers' initial Week 4 injury report suggests he's following the NFL's five-step protocol for head injuries. The reserve cornerback will have two more chances to upgrade to full practice participation this week and then potentially gain clearance from an independent neurologist, which would put him on track to play Thursday versus the Browns.

headline: Sawyer (knee) has been ruled out for the rest of Friday's game against the Broncos, Burt Lauten of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: Sawyer tweaked his knee on the final play of the first quarter, and medical staff have determined that the second-year edge rusher's injury is severe enough for him to not return to Friday's contest. With Sawyer done for the day and Alex Highsmith (ankle) inactive, more defensive snaps are available for Nick Herbig and KJ Henry.

headline: Holcomb (heel) is inactive Friday against the Broncos.
story: Holcomb will sit out Friday's game after popping up on Thursday's injury report with a heel injury. His next chance to suit up will come Dec. 6 against the Texans. Carson Bruener and Jacoby Windmon could get more run as rotational inside linebackers in Holcomb's absence.

headline: Holcomb (heel) is questionable for Pittsburgh's matchup versus the Broncos on Friday.
story: Holcomb popped up on the injury report Thursday, leaving his status for Friday's matchup up in the air. Carson Bruener and Jacoby Windmon should be in line for increased playing time if Holcomb ends up being unable to play.

headline: Wetjen (coach's decision) is inactive Friday against the Broncos.
story: With Wetjen scratched, Max Hurleman is next in line to return kickoffs and punts on special teams. Hurleman is one of five active wide receivers for the Steelers on Friday, joining DK Metcalf, Michael Pittman, Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson.

headline: Wetjen (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
story: Wetjen has operated as the Steelers' top returner on both kickoffs and punts this season. However, with Roman Wilson back from injured reserve and Max Hurleman elevated from the practice squad to the active roster, Wetjen will be a healthy scratch Sunday for the first time this season. Wetjen's next opportunity to play is Friday against the Broncos, although the rookie fourth-rounder's chances of suiting up for that contest would be further diminished if Michael Pittman (foot) is activated from IR before that game.

headline: Howard is active and will work as Mason Rudolph's backup Friday against the Broncos, Brian Batko of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: Mason Rudolph will make his first start of the season Friday after the Steelers parted ways with Aaron Rodgers, while Howard moves up to the second spot on the team's quarterback depth chart. Drew Allar (coach's decision) will be Pittsburgh's emergency third QB behind Rudolph and Howard for Friday's game against the Broncos.

headline: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Steelers' emergency quarterback against the Eagles on Sunday.
story: As has been the case all year, Howard will be the emergency QB3 behind starter Aaron Rodgers and backup Mason Rudolph. As such, Howard is not allowed to see the field Sunday unless both Rodgers and Rudolph leave the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive and serving as Pittsburgh's emergency third quarterback Sunday night versus Cincinnati.
story: Howard has regularly worked in the emergency third-quarterback role this season, though it has yet to result in any game action. He'll be eligible to enter the matchup Sunday night only if both Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph exit due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive but will serve as the Steelers' emergency third quarterback against the Browns on Sunday.
story: Howard will continue to operate as the emergency QB3, which means he is not allowed to play Sunday unless both Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph are removed from the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, though he is listed as the team's emergency quarterback.
story: Howard remains in the emergency role, destined only to enter the game if starter Aaron Rodgers and backup Mason Rudolph both must exit the contest.

headline: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against Indianapolis, though he is listed as the team's emergency quarterback.
story: Howard is inactive once again, though he will serve as the Steelers' emergency signal-caller if Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph exit the contest due to injury, illness or ejection.

headline: Howard (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against Cleveland. However, he is listed as the Steelers' emergency quarterback, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
story: Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph occupy the top two spots on the depth chart, though if both of those players exit the game due to injury, illness or ejection, Howard will see the field as the emergency signal-caller.

headline: Allar (coach's decision) is inactive for Friday's game against the Broncos but will serve as Pittsburgh's emergency third QB.
story: Following Aaron Rodgers' departure from Pittsburgh, Allar moves up to the third spot on the depth chart behind Friday's starter Mason Rudolph and Will Howard. Despite the incremental progress, it would take injuries, illnesses and/or ejections to both Rudolph and Howard for Allar to get into Week 12 game action.

headline: Allar (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
story: With Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph as the active quarterbacks and Will Howard inactive as the emergency third option, there is no current place for the third-round rookie in the quarterback room. Allar will likely remain inactive unless one of the other three quarterbacks gets injured.

headline: Allar (coach's decision) is listed as inactive for Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: With Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph available, and Will Howard (coach's decision) serving as the emergency signal-caller, Allar will be inactive once again in Week 5.

headline: Allar (coach's decision) is inactive for Thursday's game against Cleveland, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
story: Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph are active for the AFC North showdown with the Browns, and Will Howard (coach's decision) will serve as the emergency quarterback. As a result, Allar will be a healthy scratch for the fourth consecutive week.

headline: The Steelers signed Murphy-Bunting off the Buccaneers' practice squad Monday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: The Cardinals cut Murphy-Bunting in late August, and the veteran cornerback then found his way to the Buccaneers' practice squad. With Jamel Dean (ankle) hurt and Joey Porter recently traded to the Cowboys, the Steelers needed depth at defensive back. Murphy-Bunting played in 15 regular-season games for the Cardinals during the 2025 season, logging 52 tackles (30 solo), five passes defensed, including three interceptions, and two forced fumbles over 698 defensive snaps and 56 special-teams snaps.

headline: Heidenreich (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
story: The seventh-round rookie continues to be inactive behind Jaylen Warren, Rico Dowdle, Travis Homer and Lew Nichols. It remains unclear what Heidenreich's role is and whether he will remain on the roster throughout the 2026 season.

headline: Heidenreich (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Colts.
story: Even with Rico Dowdle (toe) ruled out once again, Heidenreich won't get on the field in Week 5. As a result, Travis Homer will continue to operate as the No. 2 option on the depth chart behind Jaylen Warren.

headline: Herbig (hip) will play in Pittsburgh's matchup versus Denver on Friday,
story: Herbig is set to make his return after missing the Week 11 loss to the Eagles due to a hip injury. The 2023 fourth-round pick will likely start at outside linebacker alongside T.J. Watt against the Broncos, as Alex Highsmith has been ruled out with an ankle injury.

headline: Herbig (hip) was limited in practice Tuesday.
story: Herbig upgraded his DNP practice status from last week to limited participation Tuesday. The 25-year-old missed Week 11 due to a hip injury. He has two more practice sessions to increase his chances of playing Friday against the Broncos.

headline: Herbig (hip) has been downgraded from questionable to out for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Burt Lauten of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: A hip injury prevented Herbig from participating in any of the Steelers' three practice sessions during Week 11 prep. The door was left ajar for him to play Sunday, but he'll observe the game from the sidelines, and his absence means Jack Sawyer will operate in an elevated role at edge rusher behind starters Alex Highsmith and T.J. Watt. Herbig's next opportunity to play is Week 12 against the Broncos on Friday.

headline: Herbig (hip) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
story: Herbig was held out of practice all week while recovering from a hip injury that he likely picked up during the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals in Week 10. The lack of practice reps is discouraging, but the Steelers have kept the door open for Herbig to play in Sunday's contest. If he's not cleared to suit up against Philadelphia, then second-year pro Jack Sawyer would see a bump in rotational snaps behind starting edge rushers T.J. Watt and Alex Highsmith.

headline: Herbig (hip) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: Herbig likely suffered his hip injury in the Steelers' Week 10 loss to the Bengals. The reserve linebacker will likely need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles.

headline: Herbig recorded six solo tackles, including 2.0 sacks, during the Steelers' 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: Herbig did not record a sack through the first five games of the regular season, but the fourth-year pro got to quarterback Jalon Daniels twice during Sunday's OT victory. Herbig is up to 18 tackles (13 solo) and one forced fumble through six regular-season games while working in a rotational role on defense.

headline: Dunker (knee) has been ruled out for Pittsburgh's matchup versus the Broncos on Friday,
story: Dunker managed to return to practice for the first time since suffering a knee injury in September but will have to wait at least another week before making his return. The rookie sixth-round pick should provide additional depth at guard once healthy.

headline: Dunker (knee) logged a full practice Tuesday.
story: Dunker has put together four consecutive full sessions since being designated to return from injured reserve this past Wednesday. The rookie third-rounder is in the final stages of his recovery from an MCL sprain that he sustained in September. Dunker would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Friday's game against the Broncos.

headline: The Steelers designated Dunker (knee) for return to practice from injured reserve Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
story: Dunker went to IR with a sprained MCL back in late September, but it now looks like he's close to being available again. The move opens a 21-day window during which Pittsburgh can officially activate him before he'd have to go back on the shelf for the remainder of the campaign.

headline: Elliott (knee) does not carry an injury designation into Friday's game against the Broncos, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: Elliott was listed as a full practice participant Thursday, and that was enough for him to avoid an injury tag ahead of Friday's contest. The veteran defensive back has mostly operated in a rotational role in the secondary and has two solo tackles across three regular-season games.

headline: Elliott (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
story: Elliott was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a knee injury to play against the Eagles in Week 11, when he played 22 snaps (14 on defense, eight on special teams) while not showing up in the box score otherwise. Even if he's cleared to play Friday against the Broncos, Elliott would likely operate in a rotational role in the secondary behind Jalen Ramsey, Jaquan Brisker and Robert Spears-Jennings.

headline: Elliott (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
story: Elliott did not play in Week 10 against the Bengals due to a knee injury he sustained during pregame warmups. He drew the questionable tag for Week 11 after logging full practices Thursday and Friday, and he's been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday. Elliott's return means Robert Spears-Jennings will revert to a rotational role in the secondary.

headline: Elliott (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against Philadelphia, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
story: Elliott was able to string together back-to-back full practices to end Week 11 prep, which is an encouraging sign despite the questionable tag. His official status for Sunday's game may not be known until about 90 minutes before the 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, when the Steelers announce their list of inactive players. Robert Spears-Jennings and Brandin Echols would be the top candidates to start alongside Jaquan Brisker at safety if Elliott is not cleared by medical staff to play against the Eagles.

headline: Elliott (knee) was a full participant in practice Thursday, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
story: The safety had to sit out of the Steelers' Week 10 loss to the Bengals after injuring his knee during pregame warmups, but he was able to return to practice on a limited basis Wednesday. Now that he's upgraded to full participation, he looks good to go for Sunday's matchup with the Eagles. Elliott has logged two solo tackles across 43 defensive snaps and five special-teams snaps in two games this season.

headline: Elliott (knee) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: Elliott missed the Steelers' Week 10 loss to the Bengals with a knee injury he suffered in pregame warmups. The strong safety's ability to practice in any capacity after the recent injury is a good sign of his potential eligibility for Week 12 against the Eagles. Elliott will likely need to upgrade to a full participant by Friday's practice to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's contest.

headline: Elliott suffered a pregame knee injury and has been ruled out for Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Bengals.
story: Elliott dealt with an ankle issue during Week 10 prep but was initially cleared to suit up Sunday. However, he's now dealing with a knee injury that occurred during pregame warmups. Elliott's loss is a blow to Pittsburgh's secondary, though he's played in only two games so far this season. Robert Spears-Jennings figures to take on a large defensive snap share Sunday in Elliott's stead.

headline: Elliott was a full participant in practice Thursday, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
story: Elliott had no injury designation in practice Thursday after popping up as a limited participant in practice Wednesday. The 29-year-old has played just two games through nine weeks of the NFL regular season. He returned from injured reserve in Week 7, totaling two tackles (two solo) on the season.

headline: Elliott (ankle) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Elliott ramped up his activity in the Steelers' last game before their bye in Week 9, logging 24 defensive snaps. His attendance of Wednesday's practice session indicates his injury is probably not too serious, but he could still end up carrying an injury designation into the weekend if he doesn't practice in full Thursday or Friday.

headline: Elliott (knee) is active for Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris.
story: Elliott will suit up for his first game action since Oct. 26, 2025, when he sustained a knee injury that kept him out for the remainder of that season as well as the first six games of the 2026 campaign. The 29-year-old was a full participant in practice this week, and after being activated from injured reserve Saturday, he'll likely be ready to handle a full load of snaps against New Orleans. Expect Elliott to unseat rookie Robert Spears-Jennings as one of Pittsburgh's starting safeties.

headline: The Steelers activated Elliott (knee) from injured reserve on Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints.
story: The 29-year-old safety remains questionable for Sunday, but his ability to practice fully throughout the week in addition to the Steelers' decision to activate him implies that he'll be ready to make his 2026 debut. Elliott should reclaim a starting role in the Pittsburgh secondary after turning in 38 tackles, a sack, two pass breakups, an interception and a forced fumble over five games in 2025 before going down with the season-ending knee injury.

headline: Elliott (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: It's the first time Elliott has logged a full practice since his 21-day window to return from injured reserve opened Oct. 8. The Steelers released Rayshawn Jenkins earlier Wednesday, and that's a potential sign that Elliott will be available to make his 2026 debut this Sunday against the Saints in Paris.

headline: Elliott (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Elliott's 21-day return window was opened Oct. 8. The safety did not play in the Steelers' Week 5 game against the Colts and has now been ruled out ahead of Week 6. Elliott was a limited participant in all three practices during Week 6 prep but is still not quite ready to return to the field.

headline: Elliott (knee) has been ruled out ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, Mark Kaboly of 93.7 The Fan Pittsburgh reports.
story: Elliott returned to practice Thursday after the Steelers opened up his 21-day return window. The safety logged two limited sessions in Week 5 as he works through a persistent knee injury. It remains unclear if Elliott will be ready to suit up for Week 6 or if he will need even more time to recover.

headline: Elliott (undisclosed) returned to practice Thursday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
story: Elliott's 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve opened Thursday. While Elliott was only back on the practice field in a limited capacity, it was still a step in the right direction. However, despite his presence at practice Thursday, the team might need to wait a few more weeks before he's ready to suit up, with Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reporting the veteran defensive back's return may not happen until the Steelers play the Saints in Paris on Oct. 25.

headline: Highsmith (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Broncos, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: Highsmith was held out of practice all week due to an ankle injury that he picked up during the Steelers' 19-16 loss to the Eagles this past Sunday, when he logged 2.0 sacks and forced a fumble before his exit. Nick Herbig and Jack Sawyer are the top candidates to start opposite T.J. Watt at the edge rusher position in the absence of Highsmith, whose next opportunity to play is Week 13 against the Texans on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy suggested Monday that Highsmith (ankle) is likely to be sidelined for Friday's game against the Broncos, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports. "It's going to be tough for him to make it this week," McCarthy said.
story: Highsmith recorded a pair of sacks across just six snaps before he was forced out in the first quarter of Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles due to the ankle injury. Per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com, the Steelers' initial belief is that Highsmith's ankle injury isn't serious, but the edge rusher will nonetheless have difficulty getting clearance to play on a short week. If healthy, Nick Herbig (hip/ribs) -- who was inactive for Week 11 -- will be the most likely candidate to start in place of Highsmith on Friday.

headline: Highsmith (ankle) has been ruled out from returning to Sunday's matchup against Philadelphia, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
story: Highsmith began the game with a flourish, recording a pair of sacks in the first quarter. However, he injured his ankle during that opening period and won't be able to re-enter the contest. Jack Sawyer will likely log more defensive snaps with Highsmith sidelined for the rest of the way and with Nick Herbig (hip) inactive.

headline: Highsmith (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Eagles, Burt Lauten of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: Highsmith tweaked his ankle in the first quarter, but he had that foot taped up and was spotted warming up on the sidelines, per Mark Kaboly of 93.7 The Fan Pittsburgh. If Highsmith cannot return or his availability is limited for the rest of Sunday's game, then Jack Sawyer and KJ Henry would both be in line for more defensive snaps.

headline: The Steelers placed Skowronek (calf) on injured reserve Thursday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
story: Skowronek has been working through a calf issue since mid-October, and he appeared to aggravate the injury during the Steelers' Week 11 loss to the Eagles. Now that he's on injured reserve, Skowronek will be required to miss at least the next four games, so the earliest he can return is Week 16 against the Panthers on Sunday, Dec. 27. Max Hurleman was signed off the practice squad to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move.

headline: Skowronek (calf) did not practice Tuesday.
story: The 29-year-old appears to have suffered a setback with his calf injury, as he opened Week 12 as a non-participant in practice Tuesday. Skowronek missed the Steelers' last three games due to the same injury. He will likely need to upgrade his practice status for a chance to play Friday against the Broncos.

headline: Skowronek (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: Skowronek was sidelined by a calf injury for the Steelers' three games prior to the Week 9 bye. His full practice participation Wednesday indicates that he is fully recovered from the injury and will suit up for Sunday's contest against the Browns. Skowronek has three catches on four targets for 32 yards and a touchdown across five regular-season games.

headline: Skowronek (calf) is inactive against the Browns on Sunday.
story: Skowronek will end up missing a third consecutive game due to a calf injury, and with the Steelers on a bye for Week 9, his next chance to play is Week 10 against the Bengals on Sunday, Nov. 15. Kaden Wetjen, Brandon Smith and Brandon Johnson are in line for more snaps on offense in Skowronek's absence.

headline: Skowronek (calf) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Browns, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
story: Skowronek strung together three consecutive limited practices while working through a calf injury that has prevented him from playing in each of the Steelers' last two games. His status for Sunday's AFC North tilt may become more clear depending on whether the Steelers elect to elevate Brandon Johnson from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday.

headline: Skowronek (calf) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: Skowronek has missed each of Pittsburgh's past two games due to the calf issue. His ability to begin Week 8 prep with consecutive limited sessions gives the veteran wideout a chance to return Sunday versus Cleveland, though he'll likely carry a designation into the weekend if he's not able to log a full session Friday. When healthy this season, Skowronek has seen limited opportunities on offense, recording just three catches for 32 yards and a touchdown on four targets through five contests.

headline: Skowronek (calf) was a limited participant at practice Wednesday.
story: Skowronek has missed the Steelers' last two games with a calf injury he sustained back in Week 5 versus the Colts, and now his availability for Week 8 is up in the air. Whether he ends up suiting up Sunday versus the Browns might hinge on whether he's able to upgrade to full participation at practice Thursday or Friday.

headline: The Steelers have ruled Skowronek (calf) out for Sunday's matchup against the Saints, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
story: Skowronek did not participate in Wednesday's practice. He will now miss his second straight week due to a calf injury suffered in the Steelers' Week 5 win against the Colts. Kaden Wetjen may see some extra reps in his place.

headline: Skowronek (calf) did not practice Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: Skowronek was unable to play against the Buccaneers in Week 6 due to a calf injury that he sustained during the Steelers' Week 5 win over the Colts. He'll have two more chances to log at least a limited practice ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints in Paris.

headline: Head coach Mike McCarthy said Monday that Skowronek (calf) will not play against the Buccaneers this Sunday, Alan Saunders of SteelersNow.com reports.
story: Skowronek was diagnosed with a leg injury during the Steelers' 34-22 win over the Colts, which he picked up after a punt return in the first half. He was unable to return to the contest, and his calf issue will cost him at least one game, with his next chance to play being Week 7 against the Saints in Paris on Sunday, Oct. 25. Roman Wilson (finger) has also been ruled out for Week 6, so rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard, Kaden Wetjen and Brandon Smith are all in line for additional snaps on offense against Tampa Bay.

headline: Skowronek (leg) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Colts, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
story: Skowronek exited the game with a leg injury after a punt return and was ruled questionable to return. After further evaluation, it has been determined the wide receiver will not return to Sunday's contest, leaving Brandon Smith as the No. 4 option.

headline: Skowronek (leg) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Colts, Jake Arthur of Roundtable.io reports.
story: Skowronek was injured during a Steelers punt and is now in danger of missing the remainder of the Week 5 meeting with Indianapolis. The 29-year-old logged only eight offensive snaps in the Week 4 loss to the Browns, though his departure from the contest, even if it's brief, will be felt on special teams.

headline: Skowronek hauled in his lone target for a 23-yard touchdown during Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals.
story: Skowronek ranked fifth among Steelers receivers by playing 11 of the team's 62 offensive snaps, but the 29-year-old was able to connect with quarterback Aaron Rodgers on a pass to the end zone during his limited time on the field. Despite coming up with a big play in the Week 3 win, Skowronek remains likely to see most of his field time on special teams moving forward.

headline: The Steelers signed Hurleman off the practice squad to the active roster Thursday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
story: The move corresponds with the Steelers placing Ben Skowronek (calf) on injured reserve. Hurleman was called up from the practice squad and made his NFL regular-season debut against the Eagles in Week 11, when he caught six of seven targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in a 19-16 loss for the Steelers. He also returned three punts for 36 yards and two kickoffs for 32 yards, and with Skowronek on IR, Hurleman figures to take on more return duties moving forward. His production in his NFL debut came after DK Metcalf was ejected from the game, and with Michael Pittman (foot) activated from IR, Hurleman figures to be limited to a return role for Friday's contest against the Broncos.

headline: Hurleman reverted to the Steelers' practice squad Monday.
story: With DK Metcalf ejected in the second half of Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles, Hurleman ended up playing 22 of 71 offensive snaps after getting bumped up from the practice squad to make his NFL debut. The 25-year-old saw seven targets, finishing with six receptions for 61 yards and the Steelers' lone touchdown of the contest. He also displaced Kaden Wetjen on the Steelers' return units, bringing back two kickoffs for 32 yards and three punts for 36 yards. Expect Hurleman to get elevated from the practice squad again in Friday's game against the Broncos.

headline: Hurleman caught six of seven targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles. He also had two kickoff returns for 32 yards and three punt returns for 36 yards.
story: Hurleman unexpectedly emerged as Aaron Rodgers' go-to target during Pittsburgh's fourth-quarter comeback bid after DK Metcalf was disqualified. The practice squad elevation put an exclamation point on his NFL debut with a 20-yard touchdown catch with 1:21 left in the fourth quarter. Metcalf, Germie Bernard and Roman Wilson have all played prominent roles when available, and Michael Pittman (foot) could be back as soon as Friday against the Broncos, but Hurleman may have earned himself another elevation, and possibly even a continued role on offense, after leading the Steelers in receiving yards Sunday.

headline: The Steelers elevated Hurleman from the practice squad Saturday.
story: With Michael Pittman (foot) remaining on injured reserve and Roman Wilson (finger) officially listed as questionable, Hurleman is up as the Steelers' sixth receiver. He's never appeared in a regular-season NFL game.

headline: The Steelers activated Hurleman (undisclosed) from the practice squad injured list Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
story: Hurleman landed on the practice squad IL in mid-September due to an undisclosed injury. The Notre Dame product is now fully healthy, and he would be a candidate for elevation to the Steelers' active roster if the team needs more depth at running back. Hurleman has yet to play in a regular-season game since entering the NFL in May of 2025 as an undrafted free agent.

headline: Steelers get 2nd defensive TD on Ramsey's pick-six
story: Steelers get 2nd defensive TD on Ramsey's pick-six

headline: Ramsey recorded one solo tackle and a pass defensed during Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
story: Ramsey matched his season low in takedowns, but he was able to notch his first pass defensed since Week 5. The 32-year-old will have a chance to bounce back on a short week, taking on the Broncos on Friday at home.

headline: Ramsey tallied 10 tackles (nine solo), including 2.0 sacks, during the Steelers' 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
story: Ramsey was responsible for two of the Steelers' five sacks on Jalon Daniels during Sunday's OT win. Ramsey's first sack came on the third play of the game, and his second sack on Daniels was on a fourth-and-8 in overtime to seal the game for the Steelers. Ramsey has accumulated 19 total tackles over his last two games and is up to 37 stops (23 solo), two pass defenses and one forced fumble through six regular-season games.

headline: Ramsey (wrist) is active for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers.
story: Ramsey played through his wrist injury during the Steelers' Week 5 win over the Colts. The slot cornerback will once again play through the issue, remaining a tough veteran presence for the team's secondary.

headline: Ramsey (wrist) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
story: Ramsey played through his wrist injury in the Steelers' Week 5 win over the Colts. The slot cornerback should suit up despite the injury once again in Week 6 against the Buccaneers after ending the week with consecutive limited sessions.

headline: Ramsey (wrist) is active for Sunday's game against the Colts
story: Ramsey has been battling the wrist issue, but, as was the case in the loss to Cleveland in Week 4, he will play through it versus the Colts.

headline: Ramsey (wrist) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Colts, Mark Kaboly of 93.7 The Fan Pittsburgh reports.
story: Ramsey did not practice on Wednesday but managed to finish the week with two consecutive limited sessions. The slot cornerback played through his wrist injury in the Steelers' loss to the Browns last Thursday and will likely do the same in Sunday's contest against the Colts.

headline: Ramsey (wrist) is active for Thursday's game versus Cleveland, Teresa Varley of the team's official site reports.
story: Ramsey suffered a broken wrist in the Week 3 win over Cincinnati. However, the injury won't keep him off the field, which isn't encouraging news for Cleveland's pass catchers. The 31-year-old appeared in Pittsburgh's first three games of the 2026 campaign, amassing 17 total tackles (nine solo), one forced fumble and one pass defended.

headline: Ramsey (wrist) remains listed as questionable but is expected to play Thursday against the Browns, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
story: Despite breaking his right wrist during the Steelers' Week 3 win over the Bengals, Ramsey looks poised to play through the injury while wearing a cast. Having Ramsey available would help provide some stability to a Steelers secondary that lost cornerback Joey Porter (back), who was traded to the Cowboys on Wednesday.

headline: Ramsey (wrist) is questionable for Thursday night's game against the Browns, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
story: Ramsey was limited in practice all week after suffering the injury last Sunday against the Bengals. Rayshawn Jenkins would become an every-down safety with Daylen Everette and Brandin Echols (concussion) seeing increased reps in the secondary if Ramsey is unable to play.

headline: Ramsey revealed Tuesday that he played through a broken right wrist during Sunday's 30-27 win over the Bengals, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
story: Ramsey was injured on the Steelers' first defensive series, but he powered through and finished with eight tackles (four solo) while playing every single defensive snap. The veteran defensive back's status for Thursday's game against the Browns is dependent on whether he can find a cast that would provide enough protection without being too restrictive. Brandin Echols (concussion) and Asante Samuel would both be in line for more snaps if Jalen Ramsey is unable to play in Thursday's AFC North showdown.

headline: Queen recorded four total tackles (three solo) during Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
story: Queen entered Week 11 having notched double-digit tackles in three straight games, but his streak was snapped versus Philadelphia. The linebacker has now compiled 78 total tackles (28 solo), including 3.5 sacks, four passes defensed, one of which is an interception, and a forced fumble over 10 contests so far during the 2026 season.

headline: Queen (hand) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
story: Queen was working through a hand injury during Week 11 prep, but the veteran linebacker has been given the green light by medical staff to play Sunday. He has logged double-digit tackles in each of his last three outings and is up to 74 tackles (25 solo), including 3.5 sacks, four pass defenses (including an interception) and one forced fumble through nine regular-season games.

headline: Queen (hand) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
story: Queen put together an LP-LP-FP practice log during Week 11 prep, and despite the full session Friday, the veteran linebacker has been given the questionable tag for Sunday's game. If Queen cannot play against Philadelphia, then Cole Holcomb would likely start at inside linebacker alongside Payton Wilson, with Carson Bruener providing depth at the position.

headline: Queen (hand) was a limited practice participant Wednesday, Teresa Varley of the Steelers' official site reports.
story: Queen may have picked up the injury during the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals in Week 10, when he logged 14 tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks. The veteran edge rusher will have two more chances to increase his practice participation and avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's road game against the Eagles. Queen has recorded double-digit tackles in each of his last three outings and has amassed 3.5 sacks in that span.

headline: Queen posted 14 tackles (five solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Sunday's loss to the Bengals.
story: Cincinnati blew out the Steelers on Sunday, but Queen nonetheless managed to put up a hearty IDP fantasy line. The veteran linebacker not only recorded a season-high 14 stops, he also got into the sacks column for the third straight game when he brought down Joe Burrow just before the end of the first quarter. Queen has 3.5 sacks over his past three contests after notching just 2.0 sacks across his previous two regular seasons combined.

headline: Queen compiled 10 tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks, during Pittsburgh's win over the Saints on Sunday.
story: Queen had a strong outing in the victory, leading the team in tackles in addition to registering his first sack of the campaign. The 2020 first-round pick has now logged 48 tackles (17 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception across seven games this season.

headline: Queen made five tackles (three solo) in Thursday night's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
story: Queen played all 62 of the Steelers' defensive snaps in the contest. The linebacker has continued his perfect streak, participating in all 234 defensive plays for the team through four regular-season contests in 2026. Queen's five tackles were middle-of-the-pack on the night, but that total fell well below the linebacker's 13 tackles in Week 3.

headline: Queen logged 13 tackles (four solo) and one pass defensed in the Steelers' 30-27 win over the Bengals on Sunday.
story: Queen once again played all of the Steelers' defensive snaps, logging 56 snaps against the Bengals. The linebacker led both teams in tackles and is now up to 23 total tackles (six solo) and two passes defensed, including one interception, across the first three games.

headline: Wilson recorded just three tackles (one solo) and a pass breakup in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
story: One week after piling up 19 tackles (nine solo) in a loss to the Bengals, Wilson's three tackles Sunday were his fewest in a game this season. His 83 percent snap share on defense was also his lowest since Week 4. Wilson will be in position to rebound against Denver on Friday. He has 91 tackles (46 solo), including 1.0 sacks, four pass breakups, including an interception, and a fumble recovery across 10 games this season.

headline: Wilson recorded 19 tackles (nine solo) in Sunday's 38-18 loss to the Bengals.
story: Wilson not only set a career high with his 19 stops, he also tied the NFL high mark by any player so far this season. The third-year linebacker has jumped up a notch as an IDP asset in 2026, as he's tied for sixth in the league with 88 stops through nine games. Wilson has also added a sack, three defensed passes (including one interception) and a fumble recovery.

headline: Wilson totaled six tackles (three solo) and an interception during Pittsburgh's win over the Saints on Sunday.
story: Wilson had a solid outing in the win, as he recorded the team's lone interception of Tyler Shough. The 26-year-old has now compiled 61 tackles (33 solo), including 1.0 sacks, and an interception across the first seven games of the campaign. He will look to keep producing during next week's matchup against the Browns.

headline: Wilson recorded 11 tackles (seven solo) during Sunday's 26-19 overtime win over the Buccaneers.
story: Payton led the Steelers in tackles Sunday, and it was the third time he's logged double-digit stops this season. The third-year linebacker is up to 55 combined tackles, which leads the Steelers and is eighth-most in the NFL. He should remain busy in Week 7 against the Saints, whose offense, led by QB Tyler Shough, put up 34 points in a win over the Giants in Week 6.

headline: Wilson recorded nine tackles (seven solo), including 1.0 sacks, in Thursday night's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
story: Wilson led the Steelers in tackles, playing 81 percent of the team's defensive snaps in the contest. The inside linebacker also reached Deshaun Watson for a sack, marking his first of the season through four games.

headline: Wilson caught three of six targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles.
story: It was Wilson's first game since suffering a finger injury in Week 5 that landed him on injured reserve. He ended up playing 49 of 71 offensive snaps, 39 of which came out wide. Wilson had primarily operated as the Steelers' slot receiver prior to his injury, but Germie Bernard has emerged in that role for Pittsburgh. While Michael Pittman (foot) is expected back for Friday's game against the Broncos, DK Metcalf might receive some form of team-imposed discipline after he had an on-field meltdown against the Eagles before being ejected from the game.

headline: Wilson (hand/finger) is active for Sunday's game against the Eagles.
story: The third-year wideout was activated from injured reserve Saturday, foreshadowing his availability for Sunday's contest following a four-game absence. Wilson recorded at least three receptions in his first four games of the season on his way to a 14-188-2 line on 25 targets, and he then failed to reel in the only pass thrown his way in Week 5 against the Colts before exiting that game at halftime with his injury. In his return Sunday against Philadelphia, Wilson should slot into the No. 3 receiver role behind DK Metcalf and rookie Germie Bernard, the latter who leapfrogged Wilson on the depth chart over the last several games while filling in for both him and Michael Pittman (IR, foot).

headline: The Steelers activated Wilson (hand) from injured reserve Saturday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Wilson has missed the Steelers' last four games while on injured reserve due to a left hand injury. He's still listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, but his activation from IR indicates that the third-year wide receiver will suit up for the Steelers. Michael Pittman (foot) is staying on IR for at least one more week, so as it stands, Wilson slots in as the team's WR3 behind DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard.

headline: Wilson (finger) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
story: Both Wilson and Michael Pittman (foot) are listed as questionable but remain on injured reserve. The duo could be activated Saturday if cleared to play against Philly. Wilson has been sidelined since injuring his finger in Week 5 against the Colts.

headline: Wilson (finger) was a full participant in Thursday's practice.
story: With a second full practice under his belt since being designated for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Wilson looks poised to get activated ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles. Prior to missing time with a dislocated finger and a fractured digit on his left hand, Wilson had averaged five targets per game over his five appearances, but he could struggle to see that level of volume upon returning. Fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) was also a full participant in Thursday's practice and could be a candidate to return from IR this week, and rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard may have performed well enough over the last handful of games to retain a notable role in the Steelers' receiving corps.

headline: Wilson (finger), who was designated for return from injured reserve earlier Wednesday, was a full participant in his return to practice.
story: Per Mark Kaboly of 93.7 The Fan Pittsburgh, Wilson said after practice that he feels ready to play Sunday against the Eagles, after he dislocated a finger and fractured another digit on his left hand during a Week 5 win over the Colts. So long as Wilson steers clear of setbacks in the Steelers' next two practices, he'll likely be formally reinstated from IR on Saturday.

headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Wednesday that Wilson (finger) has been designated for return from injured reserve, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
story: McCarthy suggested earlier in the week that Wilson could be cleared to play Sunday in Philadelphia, and the Steelers' decision to open the wideout's 21-day practice window is the first step in him potentially playing for the first time since Week 5. Through the Steelers' first five games of the season, Wilson recorded 14 receptions for 188 yards and two touchdowns on 25 targets, but it's not clear where exactly he'll settle in the pecking order at receiver once healthy. Like Wilson, veteran wideout Michael Pittman (foot) had his 21-day window opened Wednesday and could be on a similar timeline for a return. Additionally, rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard has proven to be a reliable target for Aaron Rodgers in the short and intermediate areas of the field over the past few weeks and could maintain a notable role once Wilson and Pittman are back in the fold.

headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said that he's "hopeful" Wilson (finger) will be able to return from injured reserve for Sunday's game against the Eagles, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
story: Now that he's spent the required four games on IR while recovering from a finger injury, Wilson is eligible to have his 21-day practice window opened this week. McCarthy expressed similar optimism that fellow wideout Michael Pittman (foot) will be able to come off IR this week, a development that could result in Wilson settling for a lesser role if both receivers are activated ahead of Sunday's contest. Despite a rough start to the season, Pittman signed a two-year, $35 million extension in March that likely affords him some security as a starter alongside DK Metcalf upon his return, which would leave Wilson to fend with rookie second-round pick Germie Bernard for the No. 3 spot on the depth chart.

headline: Wilson (finger) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports.
story: Wilson already had been ruled out for Sunday's game against Tampa Bay, but the move to IR means that the third-year pro will be required to miss at least four games. Since the Steelers are on a bye for Week 9, the earliest that Wilson can return is Week 11 against the Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 22. He joins Michael Pittman (foot) on injured reserve, which leaves rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard as the Steelers' WR2 behind DK Metcalf for the next few weeks.

headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Monday that Wilson (finger) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Buccaneers, Nick Farabaugh of PennLive.com reports.
story: Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reported earlier Monday that Wilson is expected to miss at least a couple of weeks due to a finger injury that he sustained during the Steelers' 34-22 win over the Colts on Sunday, so the third-year receiver's absence could extend into Week 7. While the Steelers are without Wilson, Ben Skowronek (leg) and Michael Pittman (foot) for at least Sunday's game at Tampa Bay, quarterback Aaron Rodgers is left with wideouts DK Metcalf, rookie Germie Bernard, running back Jaylen Warren and tight ends Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth as his main targets in the passing game.

headline: Wilson (finger) is expected to miss a couple of weeks after exiting Sunday's 34-22 win over the Colts, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: Wilson is still gathering more information about his injury and is seeking a second opinion, so an official timeline for his recovery may not be determined until he decides on a treatment plan. The third-year wideout out of Michigan logged 20 snaps and was unable to haul in his lone target in Sunday's game before leaving the contest just before halftime. After previously moving Michael Pittman (foot) to injured reserve Saturday, Pittsburgh's receiver depth will be further tested with Wilson likely to be sidelined for at least the team's Week 6 game at Tampa Bay.

headline: The Steelers ruled out Wilson (finger) for the rest of Sunday's game against the Colts, Brooke Pryor of ESPN.com reports.
story: With Pittsburgh moving Michael Pittman (foot) to injured reserve Saturday, Wilson appeared headed for a larger role in the receiving corps. Unfortunately for the third-year wideout out of Michigan, he was unable to capitalize in Week 5, as he failed to haul in his lone target before exiting the game late in the second quarter. With Ben Skowronek (leg) also ruled out for the second half, the Steelers will be left with DK Metcalf, Germie Bernard, Kaden Wetjen and Brandon Smith as their available options at receiver.

headline: Wilson was favoring his hand or wrist as he went to the locker room just before halftime of Sunday's game against the Colts, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
story: On a play that initially was an 11-yard catch on the field but overturned following review, Wilson appeared to suffer the injury. Its nature isn't known, but Germie Bernard, Kaden Wetjen and Brandon Smith could be in line for WR reps after halftime behind DK Metcalf if Wilson isn't able to return.

headline: Wilson brought in three of six targets for 74 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers' 27-24 loss to the Browns on Thursday.
story: Wilson capped off a marathon 17-play opening drive for the Steelers by showcasing his speed, as the second-year wideout scored from 12 yards out on a shovel pass from Aaron Rodgers. Wilson has at least three catches in each of his first four games, and Thursday's yardage total established a new season high after he'd also done so with his 60-yard tally in Week 3. Wilson also has exactly six targets in each contest thus far, cementing him as a key complementary component of the air attack heading into a Week 5 home matchup against the Colts on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Pleasants (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against Seattle.
story: Pleasants was designated to return from injured reserve Wednesday and ended Week 12 prep with back-to-back full practices. He would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Saturday's NFC West showdown.

headline: The 49ers designated Pleasants (knee) to return from injured reserve Wednesday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Pleasants opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a knee injury that he sustained in a preseason game against the Chargers in late August. He was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and he would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Seahawks. With Colton McKivitz (ankle) out for the rest of the season, Pleasants would be a candidate to start at right tackle once he's removed from IR.

headline: Greenlaw (neck) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus the Seahawks.
story: Greenlaw was limited at practice all week after sitting out the 49ers' contest versus the Vikings with a neck injury, and now his availability for Week 12 seems like a coin-flip proposition. If he is sidelined again Sunday, Garret Wallow could start in his place at linebacker against a run-first Seattle offense.

headline: Greenlaw (neck) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Greenlaw was not cleared by medical staff to play against the Vikings in Week 11 due to a neck issue. He's opened Week 12 prep with a limited practice, and a full session over the next two days would likely be enough for him to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

headline: Greenlaw (neck) is inactive for Sunday night's contest against the Vikings in Mexico City, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official website reports.
story: Greenlaw will miss Week 11 as a result of a neck injury that forced him to be less than 100 percent at practice throughout the week. In his absence, Garret Wallow and Luke Gifford are both candidates to take over as the team's primary weakside linebacker versus Minnesota.

headline: Greenlaw (neck) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City.
story: Greenlaw was held out of Wednesday's practice due to a neck injury. He was a limited participant both Thursday and Friday, which was enough for him to draw the questionable tag for Sunday's contest. Garret Wallow and Luke Gifford (chest) would be the top candidates to start at linebacker if Greenlaw is not cleared to play against Minnesota.

headline: Greenlaw (neck) was a limited participant at practice Thursday.
story: Greenlaw appeared on the 49ers' injury report with a neck issue Wednesday, but he took a step in the right direction Thursday with a limited practice session. If he can upgrade again Friday to a full practice, he may be able to avoid taking an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Greenlaw (neck) did not participate in practice Wednesday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: Dre Greenlaw played his usual snap count in Week 10 against the Cowboys (71 defensive snaps, two special teams), so it's unclear when the injury occurred. The 29-year-old will likely need to improve his practice availability to have a chance at playing in Week 11. The eight-year pro has 65 tackles (31 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and a forced fumble in eight games in 2026.

headline: Greenlaw logged eight tackles (four solo), including 0.5 sacks, during San Francisco's win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
story: Greenlaw finished second on the 49ers in tackles behind Fred Warner in addition to splitting the team's lone sack of Dak Prescott with Mykel Williams. Greenlaw has now recorded at least eight tackles in six of his eight outings this season and will look to keep producing next week versus the Vikings.

headline: Greenlaw (knee) is active for Sunday's game against Dallas.
story: Greenlaw injured his knee during Thursday's practice session and was deemed questionable for Week 10, but the veteran linebacker has been cleared by medical staff to play in Sunday's contest. He has 57 tackles (27 solo), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery through seven regular-season games.
