headline: Greenlaw (knee) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
story: Greenlaw tweaked his knee during Thursday's practice, but he was cleared to participate in Friday's session in a limited capacity, per Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com. Garret Wallow, Tatum Bethune and Luke Gifford would all be in line to start alongside Fred Warner and Jaden Dugger if Greenlaw is unable to play Sunday.

headline: Greenlaw (knee) was limited during Thursday's practice, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Greenlaw had eight tackles in Sunday's win over the Raiders. While he was limited Thursday, he has more time to get cleared to suit up versus the Cowboys in Week 10. If Greenlaw can't get on the field, Jaden Dugger and Garret Wallow are both in line for more snaps.

headline: Greenlaw registered eight tackles (five solo) and one fumble recovery during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Raiders in Week 9.
story: Greenlaw jumped on the loose ball that was forced out of Brock Bowers' hands by Fred Warner midway through the third quarter. It was the fifth time this season that Greenlow logged at least eight stops, and the 2019 fifth-rounder is up to 57 tackles (27 solo), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery across seven regular-season games.

headline: Greenlaw posted 12 tackles (four solo) in Sunday's loss to the Falcons.
story: Greenlaw missed Week 6 against Washington while on suspension but returned Sunday and logged a season-high 91 percent defensive snap share. The veteran linebacker tied his season high with 12 tackles, finishing one behind Fred Warner for the team lead. Greenlaw is enjoying a productive return to San Francisco with 49 tackles and a forced fumble through six contests.

headline: Greenlaw was reinstated by the NFL on Tuesday after he served a one-game suspension in Week 6, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
story: Greenlaw was back at practice Tuesday after missing the team's 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday Night Football. The 29-year-old will return to his starting role at weakside linebacker in Week 7 against the Falcons.

headline: Greenlaw's appeal of a one-game suspension was denied by the NFL on Tuesday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
story: The suspension stemmed from Greenlaw's actions during the 49ers' Week 5 win over the Seahawks, when he used his helmet to headbutt Ernest Jones during a skirmish on Seattle's sidelines. Greenlaw was unsuccessful in his appeal, so he'll be sidelined for San Francisco's Week 6 home game against the Commanders on Monday. With Garret Wallow (hamstring) facing a multi-game absence, Luke Gifford figures to step into a starting role at linebacker alongside Fred Warner and Jaden Dugger while Greenlaw is sidelined.

headline: Greenlaw was handed a one-game suspension without pay Monday for an act of unsportsmanlike conduct during Sunday's 32-29 win over the Seahawks, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.
story: The suspension stems from an incident that occurred midway through the second quarter, when Greenlaw was involved in a skirmish on the Seattle sideline and used his helmet to headbutt the Seahawks' Ernest Jones, who wasn't wearing a helmet. Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Greenlaw will appeal the suspension, but his history -- with the Broncos last season, he also received a one-game ban for unsportsmanlike conduct -- may work against him in getting the suspension overturned. Barring a successful appeal, the veteran linebacker will miss the 49ers' Week 6 game against the Commanders before returning to action Oct. 25 versus the Falcons.

headline: Greenlaw recorded 12 tackles (seven solo) and forced a fumble during Sunday's 24-14 win versus the Broncos.
story: Greenlaw looked like he was out for revenge against the team that cut him back in March, managing his best tackle total since the 2023 season. He's worth IDP consideration in most formats going into a Week 5 matchup against a run-oriented Seahawks offense.

headline: Greenlaw (quadriceps) is active for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
story: Greenlaw has been officially cleared by medical staff to play Sunday, with the veteran linebacker being limited in practice by a quadriceps injury. He'll start alongside Fred Warner and Jaden Dugger at linebacker while, Luke Gifford and Garret Wallow provide depth at the position.

headline: Greenlaw (quadriceps) is expected to play against the Broncos on Sunday, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
story: Greenlaw drew the questionable tag for Week 4 after logging a DNP-DNP-LP practice week. The veteran linebacker is nursing a quadriceps injury, but it looks like he'll suit up for Sunday's home tilt. Greenlaw has 22 tackles (nine solo) through the first three games of the regular season.

headline: Greenlaw (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against Denver.
story: Greenlaw missed practice Wednesday and Thursday. While he was out there in a limited capacity Friday, he will still carry a questionable tag ahead of the Week 4 meeting with the Broncos. If Greenlaw doesn't suit up Sunday, Garret Wallow should fill most of the void.

headline: Greenlaw (quadriceps) did not practice Thursday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: Greenlaw suffered a quadriceps injury late in the victory over Arizona on Sunday. Since then, he has missed two consecutive practices, so he will have another opportunity Friday to make some progress. If Greenlaw is unavailable versus Denver in Week 4, Garret Wallow may be needed to fill the void in the lineup.

headline: Greenlaw (quadriceps) didn't practice Wednesday, Vic Tafur of The Athletic reports.
story: Greenlaw injured his quad during the fourth quarter of the 49ers' 36-30 win over the Cardinals in Week 3, when he logged eight tackles (three solo). The veteran linebacker will need to return to practice in at least a limited capacity over the coming days to have a realistic chance of playing against the Broncos on Sunday. If Greenlaw is unable to play, then Garret Wallow would likely start alongside Fred Warner and Jaden Dugger at linebacker.

headline: Watkins (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: Warkins was held out of practice all week due to a groin injury, and the second-year wide receiver will end up missing his third game of the season and first since Week 2 against the Dolphins. Keenan Allen, Jacob Cowing and Demarcus Robinson are all candidates for more offensive snaps Sunday in the absence of Watkins, whose next chance to play is Week 13 against the Giants on Sunday, Dec. 6.

headline: Watkins (groin) was estimated as a 'DNP' on Thursday's injury report, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: The 49ers didn't hold a practice for Thanksgiving Day, but Watkins has been listed as a non-participant for the first two sessions of Week 12 prep due to a groin injury. He has one more opportunity to practice in at least a limited capacity ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks. In the event that Watkins is not cleared to play against Seattle, more offensive snaps would be available for the likes of Jacob Cowing, Keenan Allen and Demarcus Robinson.

headline: Watkins (groin) did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
story: Watkins may have injured his groin during the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Vikings in Week 11, when he hauled in his lone target for 19 yards while playing 28 snaps on offense. His practice participation over the next two days will shed light on his status heading into Sunday's NFC West tilt against the Seahawks. If Watkins cannot play in Week 12, then Keenan Allen, Jacob Cowing and Demarcus Robinson would all be in line for larger roles on offense.

headline: Watkins brought in his lone target for 19 yards during the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Watkins' 28 offensive snaps were tied with Deebo Samuel for second most among 49ers wide receivers behind Keenan Allen (31) and ahead of Mike Evans (23). Watkins has played at least 50 percent of San Francisco's offensive snaps in each of the team's last five games, but the second-year pro is stuck in a complementary role on offense behind Evans, Allen, Samuel, tight end George Kittle and running back Christian McCaffrey. The 49ers travel back home for a critical Week 12 tilt against the Seahawks on Nov. 29.

headline: Watkins caught two passes for 49 yards on three targets in Sunday's 46-40 win over the Cowboys.
story: With Deebo Samuel still working his way back to 100 percent off his hamstring injury, Keenan Allen being eased in after his acquisition from the Colts and Mike Evans (Achilles) remaining inactive, Watkins' 44 snaps led San Francisco's wideouts. However, his three targets were a distant fourth on the team and represented just a 10.7 percent share. Allen will likely play more moving forward, and Evans is expected back in the bear future. Watkins doesn't have much fantasy appeal as an ancillary option.

headline: Watkins caught all four of his targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders.
story: Watkins set a new career high in receiving yards, thanks in large part to a 37-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter, which was the first of his NFL career. He has taken on a larger role over the past two games during the absences of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), as Watkins had 56 receiving yards on six targets to lead San Francisco's wide receivers in Week 7 prior to the team's Week 8 bye. If at least one of Evans or Samuel remains sidelined in Week 10, Watkins would be poised to maintain an expanded role against a weak Dallas defense.

headline: Watkins brought in three of six targets for 56 yards in the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday.
story: With the 49ers' receiving corps down all of Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring), De'Zhaun Stribling (IR, ankle) and Demarcus Robinson (IR, ankle), Watkins saw an expanded role and made good use of the opportunity. All three of Watkins' catches went for first downs, and he finished third on the team in receiving yards and targets while also tying for that slotting in receptions. The 2025 fourth-round pick's performance was encouraging, but he's likely to slide back down the depth chart since the wide-receiver room could be much healthier by the time San Francisco returns to action against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8, following the Week 8 bye.

headline: Watkins could take on a significant role Sunday against Atlanta with Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) both sidelined, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site reports.
story: Watkins already saw a big jump in participation this past Monday versus Washington, tallying a season-high 76 percent offensive snap share in Samuel's absence. However, he drew just one target, which he caught for a 22-yard gain. Now that Evans will also be out of action, Watkins seems likely to be deployed often again Sunday, though Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing should also get opportunities to step into larger roles. Finally, Christian Kirk (calf), who is currently on IR, may be activated ahead of the matchup versus Atlanta, and he could also factor into the equation in what would be his 49ers debut.

headline: Watkins caught his lone target for 22 yards during the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday.
story: Watkins connected with Brock Purdy for a big gain early in the second quarter, and all three of wideout's catches this season have gone for 20-plus yards. Watkins' 47 offensive snaps ended up leading all 49ers wide receivers, and the second-year pro's role in the passing game could expand in Week 7 against the Falcons, depending on the availability of Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring).

headline: Watkins recorded two receptions for 60 yards on two targets in Sunday's 36-30 win over the Cardinals.
story: Making his 2026 debut after he was a healthy inactive for the 49ers' first two contests, Watkins took the field for 15 of the team's 54 offensive snaps and was able to make a mark with 34- and 26-yard grabs. He still finished fifth among 49ers receivers in playing time, but he could see an uptick in opportunities if the rib strain Mike Evans suffered Sunday prevents him from playing Week 4 against the Broncos.

headline: Lenoir (foot) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice.
story: Lenoir has been playing through a foot injury since Week 9 against the Raiders, so it's not surprising to see his practice reps limited Wednesday. Unless he suffers a setback, Lenoir should be available for Sunday's NFC West tilt against the Seahawks.

story: Lenoir played in Week 11 despite working through a foot injury that was sustained in Week 9 against Las Vegas. The issue didn't seem to slow the 27-year-old against the Vikings, as he played 81.0 percent of defensive snaps, which was within his usual range.

headline: Lenoir (foot) is active for Sunday's game against Dallas.
story: Lenoir earned the questionable tag for Week 10 after logging a limited practice Friday, and he's been cleared by medical staff to play Sunday after going through pregame warmups. He's been working through a foot injury that he picked up during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Raiders in Week 9.

headline: Lenoir (foot) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.

headline: Lenoir (foot) did not participate in Wednesday's practice, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
story: Lenoir is considered day-to-day due to a foot injury that he picked up in Week 9 against the Raiders. headline: Coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that Lenoir (foot) is considered day-to-day ahead of Sunday's game at Dallas, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
story: Lenoir came away from San Francisco's victory over the Raiders in Week 9 with a foot injury, and now his status for Week 10 is uncertain. It will be worth keeping an eye on whether he's able to practice in full during the week, and the 49ers' first official injury report of the week Wednesday should give more context on his condition.

headline: Lenoir sustained a foot injury during Sunday's 38-17 win against Las Vegas.
story: Lenoir notched three solo tackles, one of which was for a loss, in the contest, but he didn't leave unscathed. Head coach Kyle Shanahan explained after the game that the cornerback hasn't been ruled out for Week 10, suggesting that Lenoir may have avoided a major injury. If he is forced to miss any action moving forward, Ashtyn Davis and Ephesians Prysock are both candidates to see increased workloads in the secondary.

headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan announced that Jones will start in place of Brock Purdy (ankle) on Sunday against the Seahawks.
story: Purdy didn't practice this week and was ruled out for Week 12 on Friday, setting Jones up for his first start of the campaign. In eight starts for an injured Purdy in 2025, Jones went 5-3, completed 201 of 289 passes (69.6 percent) for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions, rushed 28 times for 64 yards and fumbled four times (two lost).

headline: Jones (illness) is active for Sunday night's matchup against Minnesota, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official website reports.

headline: Jones (illness) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City.
story: Jones put together an LP-DNP-LP practice log while working through an illness, which puts him in jeopardy of not being available for Sunday's contest. If Jones is inactive, then Kurtis Rourke would operate as the 49ers' backup to Brock Purdy,

headline: Jones (illness) did not participate at practice Thursday.
story: Jones popped up on the 49ers' injury report with an unspecified illness Wednesday, and now his status for Week 11 is up in the air. If he can't practice in full Friday, there's a decent chance he'll end up carrying an injury designation into the weekend.

headline: Jones (illness) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
story: Jones managed to practice through his illness in a limited fashion Wednesday. It remains to be seen whether the quarterback will overcome the sickness before Sunday's contest against the Vikings. If Jones cannot suit up, Kurtis Rourke would become the backup to Brock Purdy for Week 11.

headline: The 49ers fielded trade inquiries for Jones from the Vikings leading up to Tuesday's deadline, but the quarterback is expected to remain in San Francisco, Dianna Russini of BetUS TV reports.
story: Even though starting quarterback Brock Purdy has been a leading MVP candidate through the halfway point of the season, the 49ers still place a premium value on Jones as an insurance option in the event Purdy misses time due to injury. As such, the 49ers' asking price for Jones was too rich for the Vikings, who have since pivoted their focus to acquiring Kirk Cousins from the Raiders.

headline: Evans (Achilles) is listed as questionable for Sunday's contest against the Seahawks, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Evans didn't practice Wednesday before he was listed as limited on Thursday's injury report as he continues to deal with the right Achilles tendinitis that forced him out of a Week 6 matchup with the Commanders. He returned to action this past Sunday versus the Vikings in Mexico City and gathered in six of seven targets for 109 yards and one touchdown on a 43 percent snap share. Evans' status will be clarified about 90 minutes before Sunday's 4:25 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Evans (Achilles) was listed as limited on Thursday's practice report, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: After not practicing Wednesday, Evans' upgrade in listing one day later generally is a good sign that he has a chance to suit up Sunday versus the Seahawks. In his return from a three-game absence this past Sunday against the Vikings in Mexico City, he logged just 43 percent of the snaps but reeled off six catches (on seven targets) for 109 yards and one touchdown.

headline: Evans (Achilles) won't practice Wednesday, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
story: After a three-game (and four-week) absence due to right Achilles tendinitis, Evans returned to action during Sunday's win against the Vikings in Mexico City, recording a 43 percent offensive snap share and gathering in six of seven targets for 109 yards and one touchdown. The 49ers likely are managing Evans' workload to begin Week 12 prep, but his status nonetheless will be monitored in advance of Sunday's contest against the Seahawks.

headline: Evans (Achilles) caught six of seven targets for 109 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
story: Evans picked up where he left off in his first action since Week 6, leading the team in catches, receiving yards and targets. He has 316 receiving yards in his last three healthy games and has scored four times in seven appearances for the 49ers, including a four-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter of Sunday night's win. Evans will likely have his practice reps managed as usual ahead of a Week 12 home game against the Seahawks, but he looks poised to continue suiting up, barring a setback.

headline: Evans (Achilles) is listed as active Sunday against the Vikings in Mexico City, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
story: Evans thus is poised for his first game action since Week 6 versus the Commanders after missing the 49ers' last three contests due to right Achilles tendinitis. As for Evans' potential workload, Jay Glazer reported on Fox NFL Sunday that the wide receiver likely will avoid a strict "pitch count," but San Francisco also plans to "be smart" with his snaps. Even a limited Evans is viable for fantasy purposes, but he'll have to contend with RB Christian McCaffrey, TE George Kittle and active WRs Deebo Samuel, Keenan Allen, Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing for the attention of QB Brock Purdy.

headline: Evans (Achilles), who is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City, is expected to be active and is likely to avoid a strict "pitch count," though the 49ers plan to "be smart" with his workload, Jay Glazer reported on "Fox NFL Sunday."
story: Evans has been sidelined for the 49ers' previous three contests, but he appears on track to return after logging limited practices Thursday and Friday. Glazer's report suggests that the 49ers plan on giving him meaningful work right off the bat, though Evans may not quite reach the standard snap share he's handled in competitive games when fully healthy this season. Whatever the case, Evans' impending return to action in any capacity should be a boon for quarterback Brock Purdy and the 49ers' passing game.

headline: Evans (Achilles) is reportedly ready to return to action Sunday night against the Vikings, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Evans, who hasn't played since Week 6, logged limited practices Thursday and Friday before heading into the weekend listed as questionable, but in an Instagram post, the wideout's agent relayed that Evans is set to return versus Minnesota on Sunday. This nugget is good news for those considering Evans in Week 11 fantasy lineups, but his status is nonetheless worth verifying ahead of the 49ers' 8:20 pm ET kickoff.

headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that the 49ers will make a decision on Evans' (Achilles) Week 11 status Saturday after listing the wide receiver as questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City, Matt Barrows of ESPN.com reports.
story: Evans got back on the practice field Thursday as a limited participant, marking his first on-field work since aggravating his right Achilles during a Week 6 win versus the Commanders. Shanahan indicated that the team wants to see how Evans reacts to this week's practices before making a call on his availability for Sunday's showdown. In the end, though, San Francisco may not make an official ruling on Evans' status until about 90 minutes before an 8:20 p.m. ET kickoff.

headline: Evans (Achilles) officially was limited at Thursday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.
story: Head coach Kyle Shanahan and GM John Lynch both expressed hope that Evans would return to practice Thursday, and he indeed did enough to receive a limited listing. Evans is aiming for his first game action since a Week 6 win against the Commanders, when he aggravated a right Achilles injury. Friday's practice report will determine if Evans has a chance to play in Sunday's contest against the Vikings in Mexico City.

headline: Evans (Achilles) is suited up for Thursday's practice, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
story: Assuming Evans is able to log at least a limited practice Thursday, it'll officially mark his first on-field work since aggravating a right Achilles injury during a Week 6 win against the Commanders. How he fares in drills Thursday and Friday likely will determine if he's cleared to return to action Sunday versus the Vikings in Mexico City.

headline: San Francisco general manager John Lynch said that "there's a chance" Evans (Achilles) will take part in a padded practice Thursday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Evans joined up with the 49ers in Colorado Springs on Wednesday as the team began prepping for Sunday's matchup with the Vikings in Mexico City, but the wideout was merely a spectator for the first Week 11 practice. The veteran wideout looks as though he could see some involvement in drills Thursday, which would mark his first on-field activity since Week 6. Evans has been sidelined for the 49ers' past three games after aggravating a right Achilles injury in an Oct. 19 win over the Commanders.

headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans (Achilles) won't practice Wednesday, but Shanahan hopes the wide receiver will return to drills Thursday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: If Evans gets back on the field Thursday, it'll mark his first on-field work since Week 6, when he aggravated a right Achilles injury. He's missed the past three games as a result -- benefiting from the 49ers' Week 9 bye -- and it appears how he fares in practice the next two days will determine if game action is possible Sunday against the Vikings in Mexico City.

headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that the 49ers are "hoping to" have Evans (Achilles) back at practice this week, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: Evans missed the 49ers' last three games while recovering from right Achilles tendinitis, but he has a chance at returning to action in Week 11. After staying behind in the Bay Area this past weekend for the team's 46-40 win in Dallas, he's scheduled to meet back up with the 49ers this week in Colorado Springs, where the team will be holding practices at high altitude to get acclimated for Sunday's matchup with the Vikings in Mexico City. If Evans is able to practice in some capacity Wednesday through Friday and if his Achilles responds well, he'll likely be cleared to play for the first time since Week 6.

headline: Evans (Achilles) has a chance to return to action next Sunday against the Vikings, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Evans is missing his third consecutive game this Sunday in Dallas due to right Achilles tendinitis that he suffered during a Week 6 win versus the Commanders. He hasn't practiced in the meantime, and while he's a rare player who doesn't need on-field reps during the week to be available on game days, he would provide confidence in his ability to play again with an appearance in drills at some point this Wednesday through Friday.

headline: Evans (Achilles) has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Dallas, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.
story: Evans thus will miss his third game in a row due to the right Achilles injury that he aggravated during a Week 6 win against the Commanders. Head coach Kyle Shanahan said on KNBR radio Thursday that Evans is "real close" to returning to action and likely would play this weekend if it was a playoff matchup. Instead, the 49ers will continue to exercise caution with their No. 1 WR. With Evans again sidelined Sunday, Deebo Samuel (hamstring), Keenan Allen, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing represent the options at the position available to QB Brock Purdy.

headline: Coach Kyle Shanahan said Thursday that Evans is "real close" to returning from Achilles tendinitis and that he would probably be playing Sunday if it were a playoff game, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
story: Shanahan's comments signal the 49ers are taking an extra cautious approach with the veteran wideout in the hopes that he'll be available down the home stretch of the season. While Evans hasn't officially been ruled out for Sunday's game at Dallas, he isn't expected to suit up in Week 10, per Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site. Until he's fully recovered and ready to go again, his absence should continue to open up additional opportunities outside for 2025 fourth-rounder Jordan Watkins.

headline: Evans (Achilles) didn't practice Thursday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: On Monday, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site reported that Evans isn't expected to return to action Sunday at Dallas, and the wide receiver so far hasn't mixed into any drills during Week 10 prep. The team may make a ruling on Evans' status when it posts its final injury report of the week Friday, but he appears to be trending toward a third missed game in a row due to the right Achilles injury he aggravated during a Week 6 win against the Commanders.

headline: Evans (Achilles) wasn't spotted during the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.
story: Evans appears as if he'll go down as a non-participant for a second straight practice to begin Week 10 prep as he tends to a lingering right Achilles issue. Thursday's injury report will reveal his activity level.

headline: Evans (Achilles) was listed as a non-participant in Wednesday's practice, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
story: The veteran wideout's absence Wednesday isn't surprising, with Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site having previously reported that Evans is not expected to be ready this week, with the caveat that the team will continue to evaluate his status in the coming days. In other 49ers WR news, Deebo Samuel (hamstring) was able to log a limited practice Wednesday, while the team added valuable depth at the trade deadline by acquiring Keenan Allen from the Colts.

headline: Evans (Achilles) isn't expected to be ready to play Sunday at Dallas, though the 49ers will continue to evaluate his status throughout the week, Brooke Evans of the team's official site reports.
story: Per Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com, head coach Kyle Shanahan acknowledged Monday that Evans was unlikely to take part in the 49ers' first practice of the week Wednesday. The veteran wideout appears unlikely to be anything more than a limited participant Thursday or Friday either, so barring dramatic improvement in his recovery from right Achilles tendinitis, he'll miss a third straight game this weekend.

headline: Evans (Achilles) is unlikely to participate in practice Wednesday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.
story: That's not a particularly surprising development, with Mike Garafolo of NFL Network having previously suggested that Evans -- who last played in Week 6 -- appears to be "questionable at best" for this Sunday's game against the Cowboys. On the plus side from the 49ers' perspective is that the team hopes to have fellow WR Deebo Samuel (hamstring) at practice Wednesday.

headline: Evans (Achilles), who won't play in Sunday's game against the Raiders, appears to be "questionable at best" for next Sunday's road matchup with the Cowboys, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports.
story: Evans is missing a second straight contest Sunday after aggravating a right Achilles injury during a Week 6 win against the Commanders. He hasn't been able to practice in the meantime, and while he's the type of player that doesn't require practice reps during the week to be available on game days, even work on the side Wednesday through Friday would be a welcome sign. In any case, with fellow WR Deebo Samuel (hamstring) also sidelined this weekend and Christian Kirk (knee) being placed on IR on Saturday, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, Jacob Cowing and KhaDarel Hodge are the options at the position to be active in Week 9.

headline: Evans (Achilles) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports.
story: GM John Lynch said on KNBR radio Thursday that Evans is unlikely to play in Week 9 due to the right Achilles injury he aggravated in Week 6 against the Commanders, per Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area. After not practicing in any capacity Wednesday and Thursday, Evans indeed will miss a second consecutive contest. Fellow WRs Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Christian Kirk (knee) will join Evans on the sideline Sunday, leaving Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing as the only options at the position on the 49ers' active roster. The team also may activate Demarcus Robinson (ankle) from IR on Saturday after he was listed as questionable.

headline: Evans (Achilles) didn't participate in the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: With Evans now having been absent from the media-viewing portion of practice again Friday, his status for Sunday's game against the Raiders remains in serious doubt. After a round of likely DNPs, Evans' return may have to wait until Week 10, though the veteran wideout has been known to play despite logging DNPs. It could be another patchwork week at wide receiver for the Niners.

headline: Evans (Achilles) didn't participate in Thursday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports.
story: After back-to-back DNPs to open Week 9 prep, Evans technically has one more chance to mix into drills this week, but GM John Lynch said on KNBR radio Thursday that the wide receiver likely won't be available Sunday versus the Raiders due to his lingering right Achilles issue, per Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area. The 49ers may make a ruling on Evans' status as soon as they post Friday's injury report.

headline: Evans (Achilles) didn't participate in the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: Evans' absence Thursday comes as no surprise considering GM John Lynch stated earlier in the day that Evans is unlikely to return Sunday against the Raiders. Barring an unexpectedly quick recovery, Evans will sit out a second consecutive game sandwiched around San Francisco's Week 8 bye before possibly returning in Week 10 at Dallas. At 6-1, the 49ers can afford to take a cautious approach with the top option in their injury-riddled wide receiver room.

headline: Evans (Achilles) isn't expected to play Sunday against the Raiders, 49ers GM John Lynch said on KNBR radio Thursday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: The 49ers were initially optimistic that Evans would return after the team's Week 8 bye following an absence during the Week 7 loss to Atlanta, but the veteran wide receiver apparently needs more time to recover. While official confirmation on Evans' status is unlikely to come prior to game designations being released Friday, Lynch's comments coupled with Evans' inability to practice Wednesday suggest that the wideout's fantasy managers should have an alternative option in place for Week 9.

headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans (Achilles/ribs) won't practice Wednesday, NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano reports.
story: Evans sat out a Week 7 loss in Atlanta after aggravating a right Achilles injury in Week 6 against the Commanders, and while there's an expectation that he'll be back after a Week 8 bye, he'll kick off this week with a DNP. He thus will have two more chances to mix into drills ahead of Sunday's contest versus the Raiders.

headline: Evans (Achilles) is expected to return after San Francisco's Week 8 bye, David Lombardi of SF Standard reports.
story: After missing Sunday's game against the Falcons with the Achilles issue, Evans appears to be trending toward a return for San Francisco's next contest in Week 9 against the Raiders. Working as the Niners' big-play X receiver this season, Evans has been nearly unstoppable when healthy. Maintaining health has been his biggest issue. When on the field, Evans is a fantasy WR2 with WR1 upside.

headline: Evans (Achilles) is out for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
story: This comes as no surprise after Evans was unable to practice all week following Monday night's early departure against the Commanders. The Niners have a Week 8 bye, and the team hopes Evans will be able to be ready to return following that off week. San Francisco should get Christian Kirk (calf) back from injured reserve this Sunday. He'd join Jordan Watkins and Brandin Cooks atop the depth chart this weekend.

headline: Evans (Achilles) wasn't present at the start of Friday's practice, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
story: Evans appears poised to miss every Week 7 practice after he aggravated a right Achilles injury in Monday's win against the Commanders. The 49ers may make a ruling on Evans' availability for Sunday's game in Atlanta once the team posts its final injury report of the week Friday.

headline: Evans (ribs/Achilles) didn't practice Thursday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: Evans officially logged a second consecutive DNP after he made an early exit from Monday's win against the Commanders due to an aggravation of a right Achilles' injury, which head coach Kyle Shanahan has called soreness, per Wagoner. While Evans now has just one more chance to mix into drills this week, he's proved in the past that he doesn't require practice reps to be available on game days. Whether or not he has a chance to play Sunday in Atlanta will become known once the 49ers post their final Week 7 injury report Friday.

headline: Evans (Achilles) wasn't present for the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
story: Evans has yet to practice since aggravating his right Achilles during Monday's win against the Commanders, which forced him out just before halftime of that contest. Coach Kyle Shanahan called the injury "soreness" afterward, per Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com, and at the same time he said he doesn't believe the wide receiver has a long-term injury. Evans doesn't need to practice in order to make himself available on game day, but Friday's injury report will reveal if he has a chance to play Sunday in Atlanta.

headline: Evans (ribs/Achilles) officially didn't practice Wednesday, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
story: As expected, Evans didn't mix into drills just two days removed from exiting Monday's game against the Commanders early due to an Achilles injury. Afterward, coach Kyle Shanahan termed the issue right Achilles soreness, per Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com, which isn't believed to be a long-term concern. Shanahan also expressed hope that Evans will be able to play Sunday in Atlanta, but the 49ers likely will exercise caution with the top wide receiver on the roster.

headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said that Evans (Achilles) isn't expected to practice Wednesday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: Evans exited late in the first half of Monday's game against the Commanders and was quickly ruled out due to an Achilles injury that initially showed up during Week 6 prep. Shanahan told Wagoner afterward that Evans is dealing with right Achilles tendinitis, and while he doesn't believe it's a long-term concern, he also is hopeful the veteran wide receiver will be able to play Sunday in Atlanta. Evans already has proven he doesn't need much, if any, on-field work in a given week to be available on game day, but this particular occasion appears to be different.

headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Friday that Purdy (ankle) has been ruled out for Sunday's game versus the Seahawks, Jennifer Lee Chan of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
story: Purdy wasn't able to practice during Week 12 prep due to an ankle injury, which will sideline him for the first time this season. In place of Purdy, Mac Jones will earn the spot start Sunday, while the former's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 6, at the Giants. Shanahan added that surgery isn't on the table for Purdy and he's optimistic the QB will be OK to return in Week 13, according to Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com.

headline: Purdy (ankle) wasn't spotted during the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
story: Purdy appears poised to be listed as a non-participant for a third consecutive day during Week 12 prep as he tends to an ankle injury. Head coach Kyle Shanahan has yet to speak on Purdy's health concern, but Friday's practice report will reveal if the quarterback is in danger of missing Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

headline: Purdy (ankle) was listed as a non-participant on Thursday's injury report, Eric Branch of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
story: Purdy has kicked off Week 12 prep with back-to-back DNPs due to an ankle injury, giving him just one more chance to mix into drills Friday before the 49ers potentially tag him with a designation for Sunday's showdown with the Seahawks. There's been no indication that Purdy is in danger of missing that contest, but if it comes to pass, Mac Jones is available to start under center.

headline: Purdy didn't practice Wednesday due to an ankle injury, Vic Tafur of The Athletic reports.
story: Purdy put on a master class during this past Sunday's 35-10 win against the Vikings in Mexico City, completing 21 of 26 passes for 255 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. Now with a health concern in tow, his status will be monitored closely to get a sense of his odds to suit up Sunday against the Seahawks. Mac Jones is waiting in the wings in the event Purdy isn't able to play in Week 12.

headline: Purdy completed 21 of 26 pass attempts for 255 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
story: Purdy remained effective despite facing the vaunted Vikings defense, which had allowed just six touchdown passes through nine games. He threw touchdown passes on three of San Francisco's first four drives, connecting with George Kittle for scores of 17 and eight yards before finding Mike Evans for a four-yard touchdown in Evans' first action since Week 6 due to an Achilles injury. Purdy will take a stellar 23:5 TD:INT into another tough matchup on paper in Week 12 against the Seahawks, who held him to a season-low 189 passing yards in Week 5.

headline: Purdy completed 22 of 28 passes for 389 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions and added two carries for 21 yards in the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday. He also threw a two-point conversion pass.
story: As expected, Sunday's showdown between the longtime rivals turned into a complete offensive showcase, and Purdy was right at the center of the fireworks. The veteran quarterback recorded a career-high passing yardage total, with his 66-yard touchdown pass to Christian McCaffrey with just over three minutes remaining putting Purdy over the top. That TD toss was preceded by 11- and 74-yard scoring strikes to Deebo Samuel and McCaffrey, respectively, in the first half, giving Purdy his third tally of at least three touchdown passes this season. Purdy's 78.6 percent completion rate also was his second-highest total of the season, and the fact the star signal-caller seemed to have quick chemistry with trade-deadline acquisition Keenan Allen bodes very well, considering Purdy also may have Mike Evans (Achilles) back for next Sunday night's Week 11 home showdown against the Vikings.

headline: Purdy completed 17 of 25 passes for 232 yards, two touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders. He added seven rushing attempts for 40 yards and a touchdown.
story: Purdy gave the 49ers a 14-0 lead with a one-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter, then added a 12-yard touchdown pass to Christian McCaffrey in the second quarter and a 37-yard touchdown pass to Jordan Watkins in the third. Unfazed by the numerous injuries to San Francisco's wide receivers, Purdy has a 17:5 TD:INT through the air to go with a pair of rushing scores heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Cowboys. Having led the 49ers to a 7-1 record, the fourth-place finisher in the 2023 MVP race is making a strong case for the award at the halfway point of the 2026 campaign.

headline: Purdy completed 27 of 40 passes for 288 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions and added two carries for five yards in the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday.
story: Purdy put together an impressive passing yardage total, especially considering he was down both Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), along with De'Zhaun Stribling (IR, ankle) and Demarcus Robinson (IR, ankle). He also lost Christian McCaffrey for the entirety of the second quarter due to a leg injury that the star back eventually returned from, but the scarcity of his top pass catchers eventually led to a more mistake-filled performance than usual. The multi-interception tally was Purdy's first of the season, and the two picks led to 10 points for the Falcons. Purdy should have a chance to work with a deeper pass-catching corps in a Week 9 home matchup against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8, as the Week 8 bye should offer multiple receivers a chance to recover from their respective injuries.

headline: McKivitz (ankle) was placed on the 49ers' injured reserve list Wednesday.
story: McKivitz was diagnosed with a fractured and dislocated ankle that he sustained in the 49ers' Week 11 win over the Vikings. He's expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, and Vederian Lowe is expected to take over as the starter at right tackle in McKivitz's absence.

headline: San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan said after Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings that McKivitz is believed to have sustained a fractured and dislocated left ankle during the contest, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: McKivitz was carted off the field after going down with the injury during the second quarter, when Vikings linebacker Ivan Pace appeared to roll up on back of McKivitz's left leg at the end of a Christian McCaffrey run. Assuming follow-up tests confirm the injuries, McKivitz will require surgery and will almost certainly miss the remainder of the regular season and playoffs. Vederian Lowe came off the bench to replace McKivitz at right tackle, and Shanahan confirmed that Lowe will be next in line to start at the position beginning with the 49ers' Week 12 matchup with the Seahawks.

headline: McKivitz suffered a season-ending ankle injury in Sunday night's matchup against the Vikings, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: McKivitz is believed to have sustained a fractured and dislocated ankle after being carted off in Sunday's win over the Vikings and is likely out for the season. Vederian Lowe, who filled in at right tackle after McKivitz exited against Minnesota, is expected to start moving forward.

headline: McKivitz (lower leg) was carted off the field Sunday night against the Vikings, Eric Branch of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
story: McKivitz suffered a gruesome lower left leg injury, and he required an air cast before being carted off the field. In his absence, Vederian Lowe has taken over as the 49ers' right tackle on Sunday night.

headline: Stout (shoulder) was only active as an emergency depth option during Sunday's loss to the Falcons, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reported Monday.
story: Coach Kyle Shanahan said that Stout was only going to enter the game in an emergency scenario for the 49ers' secondary. The team hopes the Week 8 bye will allow Stout's shoulder sprain to fully heal ahead of the Week 9 showdown with the Raiders.

headline: Stout (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Falcons, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site reports.
story: Stout is nursing an AC sprain in his shoulder, but the second-year defensive back has been given the green light to play in Sunday's contest. He has 18 tackles (11 solo), including 0.5 sacks, and one pass defense through the first six games of the regular season.

headline: Stout (shoulder) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
story: Stout logged consecutive DNPs to begin Week 7 prep before upgrading to a limited participant in Friday's session. The last-minute practice participation has given the cornerback a chance to recover from his AC joint issue in time for Sunday's contest, but it remains uncertain if the 24-year-old will suit up. If Stout cannot play, Ashtyn Davis will likely start at slot cornerback in his place.

headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said that Stout's removal from Monday's 23-17 win over the Commanders was due to an AC sprain in his shoulder, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
story: Stout's practice reps during Week 6 prep were limited due to his shoulder injury. He was cleared to play Monday but was hampered by his injury, which led to Stout being replaced by Ashtyn Davis in the second half and finishing with two tackles over a season-low 25 snaps. Stout's practice participation over the coming days will provide some clarity on his status for Sunday's road game against the Falcons.

headline: Stout (shoulder) is active for Monday night's game against the Commanders, Brooke Evans reports.
story: Stout was limited throughout Week 6 prep with a shoulder injury he sustained in the 49ers' Week 4 win over the Broncos. The cornerback has recovered enough to suit up for Monday Night Football opposite fellow cornerback Renardo Green.

headline: Stout (shoulder) is questionable for Monday night's game against the Commanders.
story: Stout was limited in practice all week after he initially injured the shoulder in Week 4 against the Broncos. He's yet to miss a game this season. Across five appearances, the cornerback has 16 tackles (nine solo), including 0.5 sacks, and one pass breakup.

headline: Stout (shoulder) is active for Sunday's game against the Seahawks, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official site reports.
story: Stout missed Friday's practice session due to an AC joint sprain the cornerback suffered during the 49ers' Week 4 win over the Broncos. Despite missing the final practice of Week 5 prep, Stout was able to recover enough from the injury to suit up for Sunday's divisional matchup with the Seahawks.

headline: Stout (shoulder) is listed as questionable ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: Stout is day-to-day with an AC joint sprain. The cornerback practiced in a limited capacity Thursday while missing the 49ers' Wednesday and Friday sessions. Stout has an outside chance to play in Sunday's contest, but with one limited practice session during the middle of the week, it is unlikely. If Stout does not play, Ephesians Prysock, Siran Neal or Jack Jones will likely start at slot cornerback against the Seahawks.

headline: San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that Stout is day-to-day with an AC joint sprain in his shoulder, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
story: Stout missed time during the fourth quarter of Sunday's 24-14 win over the Broncos due to the shoulder issue, but he was able to check back into the game after receiving treatment. Though his practice participation could be affected by the injury in Week 5, the expectation is that he'll be ready to play this coming Sunday in Seattle.

headline: Stout (shoulder) returned to Sunday's game against the Broncos, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: Stout briefly missed time in the fourth quarter with the shoulder issue. He has six tackles (four solo) in Sunday's game against Denver.

headline: Stout (shoulder) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Broncos, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: With Stout injured, Jack Jones is the only other healthy cornerback on the roster behind Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir. Prior to exiting Sunday, Stout recorded six tackles (four solo). He handles slot cornerback duties for the Niners.

headline: Kareem (ankle) is inactive for Sunday night's game against the Vikings.
story: Kareem has 12 tackles (six solo) across eight games this season as a rotational lineman and special-teams contributor.

headline: Okuayinonu (foot) was spotted walking without a limp in the 49ers' locker room Wednesday, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
story: Okuayinonu suffered a broken foot in practice ahead of Week 1 and required surgery. He appears to be making progress and could return at some point before the end of the regular season. The 28-year-old appeared in 15 regular-season games last season, and made 12 starts and recorded 23 tackles (16 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and a forced fumble.

headline: The 49ers activated Hobbs (groin) from injured reserve Wednesday.
story: San Francisco needed to make a decision on Hobbs after his 21-day practice window was set to close. The veteran cornerback will be looking to make his 2026 debut Sunday against the Seahawks.

headline: Hobbs (groin) has been downgraded to out for Sunday night's game against the Vikings.
story: The veteran cornerback remains on injured reserve but had been listed as questionable. He had his 21-day practice window opened 17 days ago, so the 49ers will need to make a decision on Hobbs next week. He's yet to play in a game this season.

headline: Hobbs (groin) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City.
story: Hobbs -- who opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a groin injury -- was a full participant in all three practices during Week 11 prep. However, he would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Sunday's contest. His return would give the 49ers extra depth at cornerback behind Deommodore Lenoir and Renardo Green, although Hobbs could easily step into a starting role in the secondary.

headline: The 49ers aren't activating Hobbs (adductor) ahead of Sunday's tilt against Dallas, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
story: Hobbs had his 21-day practice window opened Nov. 4, so the 49ers still have ample time to activate him before he'd need to miss the rest of the season. The veteran cornerback hasn't yet made his regular-season San Francisco debut after signing with the team on a one-year contract last March. Hobbs did manage to log a trio of full practices this week, so he seems to be progressing well toward a return to action.

headline: San Francisco didn't activate Hobbs (groin) from injured reserve Saturday, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
story: Hobbs had his practice window opened Wednesday and logged three limited practices before initially being deemed questionable to face the Raiders on Sunday. Since he wasn't activated Saturday, the veteran cornerback will have to wait at least another week to return to action. Hobbs' next chance to do so is Sunday, Nov. 15, against Dallas.

headline: Hobbs (groin) is officially listed as questionable for Sunday's game versus the Raiders.
story: Hobbs was limited all week after the 49ers allowed him to return to practice Wednesday, and he's still on injured reserve going into the weekend. If he's not activated before Sunday's contest, rookie fourth-rounder Ephesians Prysock could remain a candidate for a few reps at cornerback in Week 9.

headline: The 49ers designated Hobbs (groin) for return to practice from their injured reserve list Wednesday.
story: Hobbs went to IR with a groin injury prior to San Francisco's regular-season debut, but it now looks like he's getting close to returning to action. The 49ers will have 21 days to officially activate him before he'd have to remain on IR for the rest of the campaign.

headline: San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan said Wednesday that Stribling (ankle) is likely at least "a couple weeks away" from returning to practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports. "I don't know. I mean, nothing's changed," Shanahan said, regarding a timeline for the rookie receiver.
story: Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. While Shanahan indicated that Stribling's timeline doesn't appear to have changed, the young wideout will need to get back on the practice field before the 49ers can hone in on a more precise target date for him to resume playing. Given the haziness of his return date along with the fact that he could face limitations with his snaps once activated, Stribling likely isn't worth holding in redraft leagues at this point in the season.

headline: Stribling (ankle) was doing some work on the side at Wednesday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: This is the first time Stribling has participated in on-field work since suffering a significant ankle injury in the Week 1 win over the Rams. The expectation has been that the rookie could be back by December, so Stribling is progressing toward hitting that goal. Once Stribling progresses to full-team drills, his timeline will get more dialed in. The 49ers have two more games in November, leaving the Week 13 matchup against the Giants as his earliest potential return date.

headline: Stribling (ankle) was spotted Monday walking without crutches or a brace on his lower leg, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
story: Stribling, who garnered his share of preseason fantasy buzz, was injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams, but it appears as though the wideout is making solid progress in his recovery. A firm timetable for the 2026 second-rounder's return to practice hasn't been outlined yet, but David Lombardi of SFStandard.com previously noted that Stribling (ankle) remains on track to return at some point in December, a notion supported by Barrows' report.

headline: Stribling (ankle) remains on track to return in December, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports.
story: Stribling was injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and remains on injured reserve. He missed a big opportunity for snaps and targets with the team dealing with so many injuries at the wide receiver position, but all indications are Stribling will be back for the stretch run and a possible trip to the playoffs.

headline: Willis went without a target while logging nine snaps on offense and 21 on special teams in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings in Mexico City.
story: Willis has suited up in each of the 49ers' last nine games but has received little run on offense while the team's top two tight ends -- George Kittle and Luke Farrell -- have remained healthy throughout the season. The 27-year-old has logged single-digit snaps on offense in five straight contests and has yet to draw a target in 2026.

headline: Farrell turned his lone target into a seven-yard reception in Sunday's 35-10 win over the Vikings in Mexico City.
story: Farrell has suited up in each of the 49ers' first 10 games, but despite logging double-digit snaps in each contest, he's produced just four catches for 40 yards on seven targets. He'll continue to serve mainly as a blocking tight end on offense while also serving as a key contributor on the 49ers' special-teams units.

headline: Brown recorded four tackles (three solo) and a pick-six during the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Vikings on Sunday in Mexico City.
story: Brown picked off a pass from Kirk Cousins intended for Tai Felton late in the second quarter, which Brown returned 18 yards to the house to extend the 49ers' lead to 28-10. It was his first interception of 2026 and sixth of his career, and Brown is up to 55 tackles (31 solo) and four pass defenses through 10 regular-season games.

headline: Brown (ankle) does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City.
story: Brown opened the week with back-to-back limited practices due to an ankle issue, but his full session Friday was enough for him to avoid an injury tag for Sunday's contest. The fourth-year safety has 51 tackles (28 solo) and three pass defenses in nine regular-season games.

headline: Brown (ankle) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports.
story: Brown likely suffered his ankle injury in the 49ers' Week 10 win over the Cowboys. The free safety played 74 percent of the team's defensive snaps in the contest. Brown will likely need to upgrade to a full practice participant by Friday to avoid any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Vikings.

headline: Warner recorded eight tackles (four solo) and a pass breakup in Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
story: The four-time First-Team All-Pro linebacker has double-digit tackles in five of 10 games this season and is up to 96 tackles (42 solo), including 0.5 sacks, five forced fumbles, four pass breakups and a fumble recovery on 96 percent of the Niners' defensive snaps.

headline: Warner tallied 11 tackles (two solo) during San Francisco's win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
story: Warner had a strong outing in the victory, leading the team in tackles while playing all 83 defensive snaps. The 29-year-old has now compiled 88 tackles (38 solo), including 0.5 sacks, five forced fumbles and a fumble recovery across nine games this season.

headline: Warner logged five tackles (three solo), one forced fumble and one fumble recovery during the 49ers' 38-17 win over the Raiders in Week 9.
story: Warner's five stops tied a season low, although he did recover the fumble late in the third quarter that the 49ers' offense converted into a 37-yard touchdown pass from Brock Purdy to Jordan Watkins seven plays later. Warner has played every single defensive snap in each of the 49ers' last six games, and the veteran linebacker is up to 77 tackles (36 solo), including 0.5 sacks, three pass defenses, five forced fumbles and one fumble recovery through eight regular-season games.

headline: Warner recorded 13 tackles (six solo) Sunday in a Week 7 loss to Atlanta.
story: Warner led the 49ers in tackles, finishing one ahead of Dre Greenlaw. It was the fourth time through seven games that Warner has notched double-digit stops. The star linebacker ranks second in the NFL with 71 tackles through seven games.

headline: Warner totaled eight tackles (six solo) during the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday.
story: Warner was on the field for every single defensive snap for a fourth consecutive game, and he finished second on the 49ers in tackles behind Jaden Dugger (11). Warner has logged at least seven tackles in five of six regular-season games, and his 58 combined tackles are third-most in the NFL behind Alex Singleton (68) and Ernest Jones (59). The 49ers will hit the road for Week 7 against the Falcons on Sunday.

headline: Warner recorded seven tackles (three solo) and two passes defensed during Sunday's 24-14 win versus the Broncos.
story: Warner took a step back in the tackle department compared to his 17-tackle performance versus the Cardinals in Week 3 but he continued to look sharp in coverage in Week 4. He profiles as an elite IDP option in most formats going into a Week 5 tilt at Seattle.

headline: Warner recorded 17 tackles (eight solo) in Sunday's win over Arizona.
story: The Cardinals ran a whopping 87 offensive plays Sunday, and Warner was on the field for all of them, leading to the inflated tackles number. The 17 tackles were the most Warner has ever recorded in a single game during his nine-year career. Through three games this season, Warner has 33 tackles (14 solo), including 0.5 sacks, two forced fumbles and one pass breakup.

headline: Cowing returned one punt for no gain during San Francisco's win over the Vikings on Sunday.
story: Cowing saw limited action in the win, playing just six snaps on offense and two on special teams. The 25-year-old hasn't been targeted across the last two games and should continue to serve a depth role with Mike Evans now healthy.

headline: Cowing did not draw any targets during Sunday's 46-40 win at Dallas.
story: Cowing was also sent back to receive two punts in Week 10, making a fair catch on one and allowing the other to go into the endzone for a touchback. He has now drawn just one target over the two games following his three-catch performance in Week 7, and his role in the 49ers' offense figures to shrink even further once veteran Mike Evans returns from Achilles tendinitis, which could happen as soon as Sunday versus Minnesota.

headline: Cowing caught three of five passes for 38 yards, added a 10-yard carry and returned one kickoff for 28 yards during Sunday's 29-20 loss to the Falcons.
story: Cowing and the other 49ers pass catchers operated in expanded roles Sunday due to the absences of both Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Cowing was on the field for 26 of the 49ers' 66 offensive snaps (39.4 percent), which was third most behind Jordan Watkins (50) and Brandin Cooks (45). Cowing put up season highs in catches, receiving yards and rushing yards, but his role could shrink significantly following the 49ers' Week 8 bye depending on the statuses of Evans, Samuel, Christian Kirk and Demarcus Robinson (ankle, IR), with rookie second-rounder De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle, IR) not expected back until December, per David Lombardi of SFStandard.com.

headline: Cowing accrued zero targets during Monday's 23-17 win against Washington.
story: Despite the absence of Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and the premature exit of Mike Evans (Achilles), Cowing went without a catch for the fifth time this season. With neither Samuel nor Evans a lock to suit up in Week 7 versus the Falcons, Cowing might see more snaps alongside Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins. However, that may not be the case if Demarcus Robinson (ankle) can manage to get on the field after spending time on injured reserve since the Week 2 win over Miami.

headline: Cowing failed to corral either of his two targets while playing 17 of the 49ers' 54 snaps on offense in Sunday's 36-30 win over the Cardinals.
story: Even though Demarcus Robinson (ankle) was moved to injured reserve following Week 2 and Mike Evans (rib) was unable to finish Sunday's contest, Cowing didn't benefit from much of a spike in playing time. In fact, after logging 24 of the 49ers' 52 offensive snaps (46.2 percent) in Week 2, Cowing saw his snap share drop to 31.5 percent. The biggest beneficiary of Robinson's absence and Evans' early exit was KhaDarel Hodge, who finished second to only Deebo Samuel (39) among 49ers receivers with 30 snaps.

headline: James rushed twice for seven yards during Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
story: James went without a touch on offense for the majority of the game, but he was able to turn the team's final two carries of the game into seven yards late in the fourth quarter. The running back was on the field for five offensive plays, and he'll remain the team's No. 3 option behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black in Week 12 against the Seahawks.

headline: James (calf) is active for Sunday night's matchup with the Vikings, Brooke Evans of the 49ers' official website reports.
story: James is good to go for Week 11 after dealing with a calf injury at practice late in the week. The running back will be available as a depth option in the backfield behind starter Christian McCaffrey and primary backup Kaelon Black versus Minnesota.

headline: James (calf) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Vikings in Mexico City.
story: James' practice reps were limited both Thursday and Friday due to a calf injury. He was limited to kickoff return duties against the Cowboys in Week 10, and that role could be taken over by Deebo Samuel and/or Jacob Cowing if James is unable to play Sunday.

headline: James returned five kickoffs for 101 yards during the 49ers' 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday.
story: James set the tone right out of halftime with a 49-yard kickoff return, although the yards gained were mitigated by a holding penalty by the Niners. All eight of his snaps came on special teams, and it looks like the second-year pro is out of the mix for backfield touches behind RB1 Christian McCaffrey and rookie third-rounder Kaelon Black, the latter of whom found the end zone for the second time in his last three outings. The 49ers will travel to Mexico City for Week 11 to face the Vikings on Nov. 22.

headline: James rushed three times for 11 yards and returned two kickoffs for 31 yards Sunday in a 38-17 victory versus Las Vegas.
story: As has been the case all season, James filled a minor role in San Francisco's backfield behind Christian McCaffrey and Kaelon Black. James' three touches Sunday were his second most this season behind the four touches he logged in Week 2 versus Miami. James likely will be relegated to making most of his impact as a returner unless either McCaffrey or Black misses time.

headline: James logged a six-yard carry, turned his lone target into an 11-yard catch and registered 119 yards on four kickoff returns during the 49ers' 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday.
story: Most of James' on-field work Sunday came on special teams. Both of his touches on offense happened on back-to-back plays in the second quarter, coinciding with the absence of Christian McCaffrey, the latter of whom was playing through a thigh injury during most of Sunday's contest. The only way James would see consistent playing time on offense is if one of McCaffrey or rookie Kaelon Black were to miss time. The 49ers will get some additional rest thanks to the Week 8 bye, and their next game takes place Week 9 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8.

headline: James (coach's decision) is inactive against Denver on Sunday.
story: The second-year pro will observe Sunday's game from the sidelines while the 49ers roll with two active running backs in Christian McCaffrey and rookie Kaelon Black. James' next chance to play is Week 5 against the Seahawks on Sunday, Oct. 11.

headline: Juszczyk caught both of his targets for 13 yards during Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
story: Juszczyk was able to reel in his first two passes since Week 7, notching his fourth multi-catch performance of the year. The fullback has now caught 10 of 13 targets for 89 yards and two touchdowns while also adding a four-yard rush over nine contests to open the 2026 season.

headline: Juszczyk caught all three of his targets for 11 yards and a touchdown during Sunday's 29-20 loss to Atlanta.
story: Juszczyk garnered multiple targets for the fifth straight game that he's played in, and he was able to reach paydirt for the second time this season, reeling in a one-yard touchdown pass from Brock Purdy in the fourth quarter. The fullback has yet to log a carry this season, and he's caught eight of 11 targets for 76 yards and two touchdowns over six contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

headline: Juszczyk (knee) was a full participant in Friday's practice, Harrison Rich of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
story: Juszczyk was cleared to practice without restriction Friday after being limited in Thursday's session. The full practice designation indicates that the veteran fullback has fully recovered from a knee injury and will play against the Commanders on Monday.

headline: Juszczyk (knee) will be limited at Thursday's practice, head coach Kyle Shanahan told reporters Thursday, Cam Inman of Bay Area News Group reports.
story: Juszczyk sat out San Francisco's Week 5 win over the Seahawks after injuring his knee in the Week 4 win over the Broncos. The standout fullback is ramping up in his recovery, but it's too early to say at this point if he will be available for Monday's game against the Commanders.

headline: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that Juszczyk (knee) could return for the Week 6 matchup against the Commanders next Monday night, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
story: Juszczyk's practice participation during Week 6 prep will ultimately determine whether the veteran fullback will return from a one-game absence due to a knee injury he sustained during the 49ers' Week 4 win over the Broncos. The 49ers will continue to rely on tight ends like Brayden Willis for more snaps as blockers in Juszczyk's absence.

headline: San Francisco head coach Kyle Shanahan said Monday that Juszczyk will miss multiple weeks after hyperextending and sustaining a bone bruise to his right knee in Sunday's 24-14 win over the Broncos, Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports.
story: The veteran fullback can be safely ruled out for Sunday's game in Seattle, and while he appears likely to avoid a stint on injured reserve, he could be at risk of missing additional games beyond Week 5. Through the 49ers' first four games, Juszczyk has recorded four receptions for 55 yards and a touchdown on six targets while also filling a key blocking role.

headline: Juszczyk is believed to have sustained a sprained right knee in Sunday's 24-14 win over the Broncos and is likely to miss "several weeks," Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
story: Juszczyk recorded two catches for 28 yards on two targets before exiting early in the fourth quarter with the knee injury. Early evaluations of the fullback's knee have left the 49ers confident that his ACL is intact, but he'll undergo an MRI on Monday to provide more clarity on the extent of his injury. In any case, the 49ers seem to be bracing for Juszczyk to miss multiple weeks, with a stint on injured reserve potentially being on the table. While not typically a major part of the San Francisco passing attack, Juszczyk handles a critical role as a blocker, and his absence for any length of time may have negative consequences on the overall health of the offense.

headline: Juszczyk (knee) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Broncos, Eric Branch of the San Francisco Chronicle reports.
story: Juszczyk was injured at the end of a catch in the second half when he was chopped down at his knees on a tackle. Prior to departing, Juszczyk caught both of his targets for 28 yards.

headline: Juszczyk exited Sunday's contest against the Broncos in the fourth quarter with a leg injury, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports.
story: Juszczyk suffered the injury after reeling in a pass and gaining 16 yards before taking a blow to his right knee area with 14:03 left in the fourth quarter. The fullback's status for the remainder of the game is now uncertain.

headline: Pineiro made all five of his PATs in Sunday night's 35-10 win over the Vikings.
story: It was the veteran kicker's third game this season that he didn't attempt a field goal, but he's now gone three straight games with exactly five extra points. Pineiro now leads the league in both point-after attempts (40) and makes (36), but he's attempted just 11 field goals in a highly efficient San Francisco offense. The lack of field goals certainly keeps him from being a top fantasy kicker.

headline: Pineiro made his only field-goal attempt and went 5-for-5 on PATs during Sunday's 46-40 win over the Cowboys.
story: Pineiro made his only field-goal try from 28 yards in the second quarter. The kicker has now gone eight straight games without making multiple field goals, and his next chance to snap that streak will come in Week 11 against the Vikings' impressive defense.

headline: Pineiro made his lone field-goal attempt and all five of his extra-point tries during San Francisco's win over the Raiders on Sunday.
story: Pineiro continues to see the majority of his action handling extra-point duties, as he's now attempted just two field goals across his last three outings and only 10 total on the season. Sunday's performance also marked just the second time this season that the 31-year-old didn't miss a kick.

headline: Pineiro did not attempt a field goal while going 2-for-3 on PATs in Sunday's 26-20 loss to the Falcons.
story: Pineiro went without a field-goal try for the second time this season, and he hasn't made multiple field goals in a contest since Week 1. To make matters worse, the kicker missed an extra-point try for the second straight week, and he's now 21-for-25 on PATs over the first seven games this season. With the 49ers off next week, Pineiro's next chance to be more involved will come in Week 9 against the Raiders.

headline: Pineiro made his lone field-goal attempt and went 2-for-3 on extra-point tries during the 49ers' 23-17 win over the Commanders on Monday.
story: Pineiro's extra-point try late in the first quarter missed wide to the right, but he connected on a 33-yard field goal late in the third quarter to give the 49ers a 23-3 lead. Through six regular-season games, the veteran kicker has gone 6-for-9 on field-goal attempts and 19-for-22 on extra-point tries. He hasn't been the most accurate kicker, but Pineiro's scoring floor will remain elevated with a 49ers team that ranks third in the NFL in points per game (29.5) and ninth in yards per game (366.7).

headline: Pineiro went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his extra-point tries during the 49ers' 32-29 win over the Seahawks on Sunday.
story: Pineiro's 52-yard field-goal try early in the third quarter went wide left, but he made up for that miss with a 44-yard field goal late in the fourth in what ended up being the game-winning kick for the 49ers. The veteran kicker has gone 5-for-8 on field-goal attempts through the first five games of the regular season, although each of those misses have come from 50-plus yards. Pineiro is also 17-for-19 on extra-point tries, and those 17 made PATs are second-most in the NFL behind Jake Bates (20). The 49ers will head back to San Francisco for Week 6 to host the Commanders on Monday, Oct. 19.

headline: Pineiro went 1-for-2 on field-goal attempts and made all three of his PATs during Sunday's 24-14 win over Denver.
story: Pineiro made his first field-goal try of the day in the second quarter, converting a 24-yard chip shot. The kicker later had a 54-yard attempt blocked by the Broncos, tagging him with his second missed field-goal attempt of the year. Pineiro has now gone 4-for-6 on field-goal tries, including 2-for-4 from 50-plus yards, while also converting 14 of 16 extra-point attempts over four contests so far in 2026.

headline: Rourke (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
story: Rourke is inactive but will not be the emergency third quarterback for the 49ers. The team seems content with Brock Purdy and Mac Jones and does not appear to need the "break-glass" button that the 49ers themselves voted to add during the 2023 offseason.

headline: Bradford (knee) does not carry an official injury designation ahead of Sunday's game at San Francisco.
story: Bradford appeared on the Seahawks' injury report with a knee issue Wednesday, but it doesn't look like it was anything major. With veteran Quenton Nelson (knee) out, Bradford should make another start at guard.

headline: Bradford (knee) was listed as a limited participant in Seattle's practice estimate Thursday, Bob Condotta of The Seattle Times reports.
story: Bradford was listed as limited for the second consecutive day as he continues to deal with a knee injury. The 2023 fourth-round pick should continue to serve as the team's backup right guard behind Grey Zabel during Sunday's matchup against the 49ers.

headline: The Seahawks activated Bradford (knee) from injured reserve Saturday, and he does not carry an injury designation into Sunday's game against the Chiefs, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Bradford has been given the green light to return from a five-game absence due to a knee injury. He should reclaim his starting spot at right guard for Sunday night's game.

headline: Bradford (knee) does not have any injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Chiefs, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports.
story: Bradford remains on IR with a knee injury but has been cleared of any injury tag tied to the issue. The Seahawks will need to decide whether to maintain the 53-man roster spot or bring Bradford back for Sunday's game.

headline: Bradford (knee) was designated to return from injured reserve by the Seahawks on Monday, John Boyle of the team's official website reports.
story: Bradford has been on IR since Sept. 23 while recovering from a knee injury, and he will now have his 21-day practice window opened ahead of Week 7. The offensive lineman is eligible to return to action against the Chiefs on Sunday, and his status at the team's first practice of the week Tuesday will shed more light on his chances to do so.

headline: Reed (toe) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the 49ers.
story: The defensive tackle was injured in the Seahawks' previous contest against the Raiders in Week 10 and will now miss his first game of the season. Reed has 20 tackles (six solo), including 1.0 sacks, on 48 percent of the defensive snaps as a rotational lineman. Rylie Mills and Mike Morris should see more action up front.

headline: Reed is doubtful to return to Sunday's game against Las Vegas due to a toe injury.
